# OHMNI Component Behavior Specification (first research pass)

Companion to PCB_COMPONENT_3D_LIBRARY_SPEC.md. Covers all 180 library entries: what each is, what it is for, how it works, how it connects, how it is modeled and simulated, its limits, how it fails, and how the model was checked. Entry IDs (OHM-001 to OHM-180) match the 3D spec.

**Status of this pass:** 180 entries covered; status counts: {'partial': 144, 'research_required': 18, 'complete': 18}. Every behavior model in it is `behavioural_approximation` or `ideal_components`. No entry claims `vendor_model`, because no vendor SPICE model was attached and run.

## Read this first

1. **What "reliable" means here.** Every model has a runnable ngspice test netlist and an analytical expected value. All 226 netlists were re-run by the coordinator on ngspice 42: 223 exit cleanly; three exit non-zero for explained reasons (one is a template that a script fills in, one is slow, one diverges by design, see the bench section). That shows the models behave as written. It does not show that they match every real part. Many parameters are labeled ASSUMPTION and several benches check a model against the very numbers it was fitted to; each file says which.
2. **Evidence limits.** All datasheets were read through a text-extraction fetch tool that returns summaries, not raw PDF pages. Figures that came from graphs are low confidence. Several standards (IEC 60063, IEC 60384-14, USB-IF USB 2.0 and Type-C, HDMI, IEEE 802.3, SD simplified spec, JEDEC) were not opened; values taken from general engineering knowledge are labeled RECALLED_UNVERIFIED or ASSUMPTION. Rating-critical numbers should be re-verified against the original PDFs before they gate a safety-relevant check.
3. **Packages versus parts.** Entries OHM-103 to OHM-140 are IC packages. They have no electrical behavior alone. The files document package binding (pin map, thermal resistance, parasitics) and a researched set of reference parts (555, op-amps, logic, EEPROM, regulators, MCUs, flash, FPGA interfaces).
4. **Simulation layers.** L1 analog is SPICE-simulable. L2 digital is modeled behaviorally. L3 (USB, HDMI, Ethernet PHY, SD, I2C/SPI peripherals, firmware, LCD and OLED controllers, WS2812B protocol) is NOT simulated by SPICE; each file lists the electrical interface and what a higher layer must provide. Nothing here pretends SPICE can run firmware.
5. **Statuses are honest, not optimistic.** No entry in the resistor, capacitor, diode, LED, connector or frequency groups reached `complete`; they are `partial` because typical parameters, parasitics, or pin maps remain unsourced. The Open Gaps and Conflicts sections below summarize what remains.

## Cross-cutting findings the implementer needs

**Disagreements between the 3D spec, the repo catalog, and electrical reality**

- Bind pins by electrical role (anode/cathode, +/-), not by pin number. The repo's GENERIC_LED_GREEN has pin 1 as the anode; the 3D spec puts the cathode at terminal 1 (R4, R5).
- Polarity stripes differ by family: tantalum stripes mark the anode (+), aluminum, polymer-can and supercapacitor stripes mark the cathode (R2). The checker and renderer must treat them oppositely.
- Bridge rectifier pin functions for OHM-071 and 072 are unconfirmed; the 3D spec's "AC, AC, +, -" label conflicts with a "1=+, 2=AC1, 3=-, 4=AC2" assumption (R4). A reversed DC supply across a bridge's +/- pins shorts through two diodes.
- Common-mode choke winding pairing (OHM-050) has three conflicting readings; default 1-4/2-3 is unverified (R3). Pin maps for OHM-051, 052, 053, 055 are unverified.
- OHM-082 PLCC-4 RGB has two conflicting function maps (Broadcom B/G/R on pins 2/3/4 vs R/G/B) (R5).
- USB-C: the 3D spec has 24 contacts, the repo catalog record is 16-pin (strict subset). No USB record has a shield pin. Mini-HDMI (OHM-168) and RJ11 (OHM-170) pin maps are unresolved (R10A).
- Repo catalog MCP1700T-3302E-TT lists 1=VOUT, 2=GND, 3=VIN; the mirror datasheet reads 1=GND, 2=VOUT, 3=VIN. MCP1700 is SOT-23A, 3 pins, so it is not bound to OHM-120 (R7A). MCP73831 pin 4 is NC in one extract and VDD in the repo annotation; the repo is used.
- The brief's "27C256 in PLCC-28" is false; AT27C256R is PLCC-32 (R7B). W25Q in WSON-8 is 6x5 at 1.27 pitch, nRF52832 QFN48 is 6x6 at 0.4 pitch, RP2040 is QFN-56, and several LQFP parts are 1.4 mm high against the library's 1.0 mm TQFP, so physical dimensions in the 3D spec do not match these reference parts (R7B).
- Datasheet BGA and WLCSP bottom views are mirrored against OHMNI's top-view convention (R7B). XT connector KiCad pad 1 is at +X while OHMNI has pin 1 at -X (R10B).
- Tab connection in power packages depends on the part (collector, drain, output, or ground), so the part binding must supply it (R6). TO-92 BJT pinouts differ by part (E-B-C vs C-B-E); the 78L05 pin order is mirrored between ST and TI (R6).
- Source conflicts remain in the group files for IFSM and IF (1N4148), SS14 Vf, supercapacitor surge and derating, crystal ESR, aluminum vs polymer life rules, Samtec/Molex/Phoenix ratings, PJ-102A voltage, SD supply upper limit, and others.

**ngspice gotchas found by running the models (for the runner and netlist writer)**

- `R=0` silently becomes 1 mOhm. Default `TEMP` and `TNOM` are 27 C; use `.options tnom=25` and `.temp 25` to match datasheet TCR. `temper` works in B-sources, not inside `{}` parameter expressions. A node named `a` printed 0.
- A charge-defined capacitor (`q=`) gives correct DC-bias capacitance, but ngspice 42 ignores `.ic` on it. `meas par('...')` did not parse. Bench netlists use `.include`, so the product netlist writer must inline `.subckt` text; the existing `model_fidelity()` already classifies such decks as `behavioural_approximation`.
- Regulator decks need `.nodeset v(vout)=VNOM`, or `.op` can land on a spurious state (seen: Vout 0.18 V). MOSFET model cards need `IS=0` to avoid a second parasitic body diode.
- A stray capacitor across a crystal's XIN-XOUT kills oscillation; strays must go from each pin to ground. Trapezoidal integration pulled an 8 MHz oscillation 840 ppm low at a 2 ns step.
- A saturating current transformer with an open secondary needs tmax of about 0.5 ns or an analytic check; at a 20 ns step ngspice read 1051 V against 236 V analytic.
- The ngspice 42 build here has no XSPICE. Do not run `ngspice -b -c /dev/null`, it hangs.
- Every capacitor subcircuit in R2 exposes a `flag` bitmask node (1 overvoltage, 2 reverse, 4 peak current, 8 surge/failed) for the rating-check engine.

**Largest open gaps**

- MLCC DC-bias numbers for a specific 10 uF part could not be extracted; the bias knee default is an assumption between two sourced fits that differ by about 2.4x in V0/VR.
- Typical ESR/ESL/leakage, contact resistance, connector thermal resistance, lead inductance (two sources differ about 140x) and package theta-JA for several packages are assumptions.
- No power-MOSFET gate charge match (model 23 % low) and body-diode recovery waveform shape is wrong; the MOSFET Rds(on) is the datasheet maximum, not typical.
- Not obtained: SSD1306 DC table and I2C timing, segment-to-pin maps for 7-segment and 8x8 matrix parts, ATmega328P pin numbers and DC tables, STM32F407 pins, BGA-64 reference part, W25Q electrical and timing, Artix-7 ball map, CD4017.
- OHM-053 flyback transformer and OHM-020 rotary pot (only the PTV09 alternate sourced) are the weakest part-level entries.

Important honesty notes that apply to the whole file:

1. Datasheet numbers were read through a page-fetch tool that returns a model-written extract of each PDF, not the raw PDF. Numbers that are tables of text (power, voltage, TCR, tolerance, revision) are reliable enough for use; numbers that only exist in graphs (derating curve end points, noise plots) are second-hand and are flagged. Anything marked RESEARCH_REQUIRED was not established.

The existing OHMNI runner (`src/ohmni/eda/simulation.py`) derives `model_fidelity` from the deck: a deck without `.model/.subckt` is `ideal_components`; one with them is at best `behavioural_approximation`. It never reports `vendor_model`. Every model here is `ideal_components` (plain R, ideal mode) or `behavioural_approximation` (realistic mode with `.subckt`). ## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-RES-FIXED

Applies to OHM-001 to OHM-013: 01005 to 2512 thick-film chip resistors, axial carbon-film, axial metal-film, cement power, wirewound power.

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
A fixed resistor converts voltage to current (V = I R) and dissipates the difference as heat. Typical jobs: pull-up and pull-down, LED current limit, voltage divider and feedback networks, RC timing and filters, gate resistors, termination and damping, bleeders, current limiting and inrush limiting (power types), dummy loads. Choice of family is driven by tolerance, TCR, noise, power and size.
- Chip thick film (OHM-001..009): the default resistor on any modern board; E24 at 5 %, E24/E96 at 1 % (S1, S2, S3).
- Axial carbon film (OHM-010): cheap through-hole, 5 % E24 (S5, S7), high TCR and noise.
- Axial metal film (OHM-011): through-hole 1 %, E24/E96/E192, 50 to 100 ppm/K (S6).
- Cement power (OHM-012): 2 to 20 W wirewound element in a ceramic case with cement fill, for dummy loads, bleeders, inrush and brake resistors (S9, S10).
- Wirewound power (OHM-013): silicone/coated axial wirewound, tight tolerance and low TCR but inductive unless non-inductive winding (S11).

Value series. E-series are geometric: nominal value of step k in a decade of N values is about 10^(k/N) rounded (E6, E12, E24 have N = 6, 12, 24; E96 and E192 are three-digit). Datasheets opened state E24 and E96 (S1), E24/E96/E192 (S6), E24 (S5). IEC 60063 itself was NOT opened. E12 decade (general practice, basis ASSUMPTION, confidence M): 10 12 15 18 22 27 33 39 47 56 68 82. E24 decade: 10 11 12 13 15 16 18 20 22 24 27 30 33 36 39 43 47 51 56 62 68 75 82 91. The exact E96 and E192 tables are not pure roundings of the formula (for example the E96 step after 110 is 113, not the 112 the formula gives), so the implementer must take them from IEC 60063 or a manufacturer table: RESEARCH_REQUIRED. Tolerance bands that normally go with a series: E24 with 5 % (J) or 2 % (G), E96 with 1 % (F) (S1, S5).

### 2. What it is and how it works
All fixed resistors obey R = rho L / A for the resistive element, with a temperature coefficient and a rating set by how much heat the body and its mounting can remove.
- Thick film: a ruthenium oxide/glass paste screened on an alumina substrate and fired, laser-trimmed to value, overglazed, with wrap-around terminations. Resistance is a percolating network of conducting grains in glass, so it has more current noise, a larger voltage coefficient and a wider TCR than a metal film (S24 gives thin-film noise of -25 to -35 dB class and TCR 2 to 300 ppm/K for Vishay thin-film chips; S1 shows thick-film current noise 0.1 to 10 uV/V from a graph).
- Thin film and metal film: a continuous metal or nitride layer (for example NiCr or tantalum nitride) deposited on a ceramic core or substrate, trimmed by a spiral or laser. Lower noise, tighter TCR (+/-50 ppm/K in S6 and S8), better stability. Vishay RIFAQ states that Power Metal Strip has lower noise than other technologies because it is a continuous metal layer instead of a glass and metal matrix (S22).
- Carbon film: carbon deposited on a ceramic rod and spiraled. Negative TCR (S5: from +/-350 to -500..0 ppm/K depending on value; S7: +350..-450 up to 0..-1300 ppm/K) and the highest noise of the families here.
- Wirewound: resistance alloy wire (CuNi or NiCr) wound on a ceramic or fibreglass core. Excellent TCR (S11: +/-20 ppm/K for 10 ohm and above, +/-50 for 1 to 9.9 ohm, +/-90 for 0.5 to 0.99 ohm), high power, very low current noise, but the winding is an inductor. Vishay offers equivalent non-inductive (Ayrton-Perry) winding, where two counter-wound halves cancel the inductance (S11).
- Cement: a wirewound element inside a ceramic (steatite) case filled with inorganic cement for heat conduction and flame resistance (S9: copper-nickel or nickel-chrome on fibreglass core, steatite case, inorganic potting; S10 Z300: ceramic core, non-flammable cement coating, welded construction).

Key equations.
- Ohm: V = I R. Power: P = V I = I^2 R = V^2 / R.
- Resistance vs temperature (linear TCR): R(T) = R25 (1 + alpha (T - 25 C)), alpha = TCR in ppm/K times 1e-6. Quadratic terms exist but are not tabulated in the datasheets opened.
- Self-heating: Tj = Tamb + P Rth. With resistance depending on Tj, the operating point is a fixed point: R = R0 (1 + alpha (Tamb + Rth V^2 / R - 25)), which gives the quadratic R^2 - R0 (1 + alpha (Tamb - 25)) R - R0 alpha Rth V^2 = 0 (used in benches B2 and B5).
- Power derating: P_allowed(Tamb) = P_rated for Tamb <= T_knee; then falls linearly to P_end at T_end. For Vishay chip thick film the knee is 70 C and the rating goes to zero at the 155 C maximum film temperature (S1 states "linear from P70 at 70 C to zero at 155 C"). Equation: P_allowed = P70 (T_film_max - Tamb) / (T_film_max - 70). Derived thermal resistance from rating (DERIVED, assumes the datasheet test board): Rth_film_to_amb = (T_film_max - 70) / P70. Example 0603: 85 K / 0.125 W = 680 K/W; 2512: 85 K / 1.0 W = 85 K/W.
- Maximum working voltage: V_max = min(U_limit, sqrt(P_rated R)). U_limit is a package-dependent breakdown limit of the element and the body (S1). For wirewound, datasheets give only sqrt(P R) (S11, S9).
- Voltage coefficient of resistance (VCR) is defined as a resistance change in ppm/V measured between full and one tenth voltage (S22 RIFAQ). No VCR number for the families here was found in the documents opened except thin-film PLTU 0.1 ppm/V (S24) and foil <0.1 ppm/V (S23), so VCR is not modeled for them.

Differences that matter for modeling (all sourced values are listed in section 5): TCR sign and size, tolerance, noise (not modeled in L1 ngspice DC; see section 4), power knee and end temperature, parasitic L, and overload.

Pulse and surge: datasheets opened give (a) short-time overload tests: 2.5 x RCWV for 5 s for Yageo CFR and MFR with a stated allowed drift (S5: +/-(0.75 % + 0.05 ohm); S6: +/-(0.25 % + 0.05 ohm)), 5 x rated power for 5 s (3.75 W and below) and 10 x for 4 W and above for Vishay RS (S11), 5 x for 5 s for CPR (S9), 10 x for 5 s for Z300 (S10); (b) Vishay chip graphs for single pulse up to about 2000 V for microsecond pulses on the largest packages (S1, graph, second-hand). No pulse energy table (J vs duration) was extracted, so pulse rating is RESEARCH_REQUIRED beyond those tests.

### 3. How it connects
Two terminals, passive, non-polarized, symmetric. Pin 1 and pin 2 are interchangeable. Typical circuits: divider Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2); RC low-pass with corner 1 / (2 pi R C); LED limit R = (Vs - Vf) / I; pull-ups. Common mistakes: ignoring power derating at hot ambient; using a chip resistor above its limiting element voltage with a high resistance (V_max is the lower of U_limit and sqrt(P R)); using a wirewound resistor as a fast current-limit or damping element without checking its inductance; confusing a zero-ohm jumper with a short in a rating sense (jumper limits in section 5); picking carbon film for a precision divider (TCR sign and size, tolerance 5 %).

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
Layer L1.

Ideal mode (fidelity `ideal_components`):
```
R{ref} {A} {B} {value}
```
Realistic mode (fidelity `behavioural_approximation`, because it needs a `.subckt`):

```
* Series L (wirewound / non-zero ESL), parallel C (optional), TCR and optional self-heating
.options tnom=25
.subckt RES_REAL A B params: R0=1k TOL_OFFSET=0 TCR=100e-6 LS=0 CP=0
Rcore A m {R0*(1+TOL_OFFSET)} tc1={TCR}
* LS > 0 : add  Ls m B {LS}  ; else short with 1u:  Rz m B 1u
* CP > 0 : add  Cp A B {CP}
.ends
```
In ngspice a zero-valued L or C is rejected or clamped, so the generator must omit the element when the parameter is 0 (R=0 is silently turned into 1 mohm; see note 4).

Self-heating subckt (checked in bench res_fixed/B2 and B5):
```
.subckt RTH_SH p n params: R0=1000 TCR=100e-6 RTH=100
Bres p n I=V(p,n)/({R0}*(1+{TCR}*(V(tj)-25)))
Bpw  0 tj I=V(p,n)*V(p,n)/({R0}*(1+{TCR}*(V(tj)-25)))
Rth  tj amb {RTH}
Bamb amb 0 V=temper
* optional thermal capacitance:  Cth tj 0 {CTH}   (seconds of thermal time constant = RTH*CTH)
.ends
```
Node `tj` is in volts that represent degrees C. This is a nonlinear behavioral resistor; it converges in .op for the cases tried. Use for rows in the part spec where the user enables "self-heating".

Parameter mapping.
- R0: nominal resistance (marking). TOL_OFFSET: a draw within +/- tolerance (Monte Carlo or worst-case +/-tol); the simulator picks it, default 0.
- TCR: signed TCR in 1/K (datasheet ppm/K x 1e-6). Carbon film is negative.
- LS: series inductance. Wirewound only unless the non-inductive option is chosen. No wirewound inductance figure was found in S9, S10, S11 (S11 says only that non-inductive winding is available), so LS has no sourced default: ASSUMPTION; recommend a user-supplied value, 0 by default, and a warning in the UI when the resistor is wirewound or cement and the analysis is ac or fast tran.
- CP: parallel capacitance. No sourced value; default 0.
- RTH: from the derating curve (DERIVED, see section 2); this lumps the datasheet test board, so it is only valid for PCBs similar to the datasheet board.

Valid analyses: op, dc, ac, tran, temp. `.noise` in ngspice includes thermal noise 4kTR for plain R only if the instance has `noise=1` default; excess (current) noise of thick film and carbon film is not modeled and should be flagged. The behavioral self-heating subckt is not a plain R and ngspice does not create a thermal noise source for B-sources; add `Rn` in parallel noise model if noise analysis is needed, or say `noise` analysis is invalid in realistic mode.

Valid range: DC to a frequency where LS and CP matter (for chips, unknown without sourced L, C; treat as valid to about 100 MHz only with LS, CP supplied by the user), voltage below V_max, temperature within the part's rated range.

Known limitations:
- No VCR, no excess noise, no thermal EMF, no humidity or aging drift, no power-coefficient of the element beyond the self-heating TCR model.
- Single-pole thermal model (no board spreading).
- Overload recovery drift (the allowed drift after a 5 s overload) is not modeled.
- Parasitic L, C for chips and for leaded types are unsourced.
- Linear TCR only. The TCR datasheet values are bounds over -55 to +155 C; the actual curve is a parabola.

### 6. Ratings and limits
Checks the simulator evaluates after each run (`i`, `v` are from the sim; amplitudes as RMS or DC; P is average):
- Power: `P = v*i` (or `i^2*R`, `v^2/R`); limit `P <= P_allowed(Tamb)`, with `P_allowed = P_rated * clamp((T_end - Tamb)/(T_end - T_knee), 0, 1)` for Vishay chip, `T_knee = 70, T_end = 155` (S1). For Yageo MFR the curve ends at about 20 % of rated at 155 C instead of zero (S6, second-hand graph reading), so `P_allowed = P_rated*(1 - 0.8*(Tamb-70)/85)`; for Vishay RS wirewound `T_end = 250 C` (characteristic U) and the knee is RESEARCH_REQUIRED (ratings are given at 25 C, S11); a conservative linear fall from 25 C to T_end can be used.
- Voltage: `abs(v) <= V_max` with `V_max = min(U_limit, sqrt(P_rated*R))` (S1, S11, S9).
- Overload (short term): not a steady-state check; flag pulses above 2.5 x P_rated per S5/S6 tests only as informational (those are test conditions, not ratings).
- Temperature: operating range per series: -55 to +155 C for the Vishay and Yageo chips and Yageo axial (S1, S5, S6), -55 to +125 C for 01005 (S2), -65 to +250 C for RS (S11), -65 to +275 C for CPR (S9).
- Jumper (0 ohm) current: from S1 and S2, S3 (see per-entry).

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior
Datasheets opened give test conditions and drift limits, not a catalogue of failure modes. The following is physical reasoning (basis ASSUMPTION unless cited) and the simulator responses are proposals.
- Overpower, mild (P above P_allowed): film temperature above its limit; resistance drifts permanently (stability limit +/-1 % after 1000 h at P70, S1). Response: flag WARNING `overpower`; optional drift of R by the datasheet stability limit.
- Overpower, severe (several times rated): thick/thin film resistors normally fail open (the film or trim kerf burns through); carbon film and metal film the same; cement/wirewound may open the winding (S9: CPR "can reliably function as a fuse and as a resistor"; S10 Z300: non-flammable coating but no fusible characteristics noted). Response: flag ERROR `overpower_open`; the simulator re-runs with the part as open (`R=1G`) after the first run reports the violation. Permanent.
- Overvoltage above V_max: flashover or element breakdown, resistance change; response: flag ERROR and treat as failed (open) if V > 2 x V_max (maximum overload voltage in S4, S5, S6 is about 2 x working voltage; not in S1).
- Surge / pulse: see section 2; chip resistors fail open or drift by trim-kerf crack; flag when instantaneous P exceeds 10 x rating, as an informational note only (no sourced pulse table).
- Overtemperature: above T_end: out of rating; flag.
- Reverse polarity: not applicable. ESD: not modeled; thin film is more sensitive than thick film (general practice, ASSUMPTION).
- Short: a resistor does not short on failure; fusible and flameproof variants (CPR; KOA CFP flame retardant, S7) open or burn but do not short. A zero-ohm jumper over its current rating opens (fuse-like).
- Open: permanent for burned elements.

### 8. Thermal behavior
Single-pole: Tj = Tamb + P Rth with Rth from the derating curve (DERIVED). Example: 0603 at 0.1 W: dT = 68 K; 2512 at 1 W: dT = 85 K (both = full rating, film at 155 C). Thermal time constant is not sourced; default Cth gives 10 s (ASSUMPTION L) for chips; power resistors are slower. Bench B2/B5 verify the electrothermal fixed point.

### 9. Appearance summary
Chip entries are small rectangular alumina blocks with a dark overglaze and two silver/tin end terminations; value is printed as a 3 or 4 digit code on 0402 and larger, none on 01005 and 0201 (3D spec OHM-001 to OHM-009). Axial entries are cylinders with color bands, first band next to terminal 1 (OHM-010, OHM-011). Cement and wirewound power resistors are ceramic or coated cylinders or rectangular blocks with the value printed (OHM-012, OHM-013). See the 3D spec for geometry; not re-researched.

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-RES-SENSE

Applies to OHM-014 (SMD metal-strip current-sense resistor, two-terminal and four-terminal Kelvin) and OHM-015 (metal shunt, bolt-on with sense pins).

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
A very low-value resistor (50 uohm to 0.5 ohm in the sources) placed in a current path so that the current is read as a voltage V = I R by an amplifier (high-side or low-side current-sense amp, battery fuel gauge, motor driver, DC/DC converter, BMS). Vishay lists the applications as current sensing, voltage division, pulse, Li-ion battery management and DC/DC converters (S14, S16). OHM-015 is the same function at 100 to 1000 A: a bolt-on battery shunt of 50 to 250 uohm (S15).

### 2. What it is and how it works
A strip of resistance alloy welded to copper terminations ("all welded construction", S14, S15). The Vishay RIFAQ names manganin as a typical alloy, with TCR about +50 ppm/K (-55 to +25 C) and -80 ppm/K (+25 to +125 C) (S22, example), and says Power Metal Strip is a continuous metal layer with lower noise than thick film (S22). Datasheets: very low inductance, 0.5 to 5 nH (S13, S14), < 5 nH for the shunt (S15); thermal EMF < 3 uV/C (S13) and < 1 uV/C for the 50 uohm shunt, < 3 uV/C for others (S15).

The reason for four terminals: at 1 mohm and 10 A the signal is 10 mV, so the 3 mohm of a PCB trace or solder joint on each current lead (6 mohm total) would read as 70 mV, a 600 % error in a 2-wire connection. In a Kelvin (4-terminal) part, the current terminals (I1, I2) carry the load current and the sense terminals (E1, E2) are separate contacts to the element that carry essentially no current, so the lead and joint drops are not in the measurement. The simulation model therefore has two nets per side: a current net (I1 to element end, with terminal resistance Rc) and a sense net (E1 to the same element end, with essentially no current). Datasheet names: "E1 and E2: voltage sense connections; I1 and I2: current connection" (S14).

Key equations: V_sense = I Rs (Kelvin) vs V_2wire = I (Rs + R_lead1 + R_lead2). Current rating from power: I_max = sqrt(P / R) (S15 gives "(P/R)^1/2"). Working voltage V = sqrt(P R) (S13, S14). Self-heating of the element changes R by TCR; the TCR is the dominant error source and varies by resistance value (S13: +/-75 ppm/K for 50 to 500 mohm up to +/-400 ppm/K for 0.5 to 0.99 mohm). Sense accuracy also suffers from thermal EMF at the copper-alloy junction.

### 3. How it connects
2-terminal (WSL type): pins 1 and 2 are both the current path and the measurement point; the PCB must route the sense traces from the inner edge of the pads (Kelvin routing on the board; the part itself gives no help). 4-terminal (WSK, shunt with pins): I1 and I2 in the load path, E1 and E2 to the amplifier inputs; sense traces must not carry load current. Mistakes: swapping sense and current terminals; sharing a sense trace with a high-current trace; using the 2-wire measurement and getting a gain error; omitting the amplifier input filter and picking up inductive spikes (L is only nH but di/dt can be large); ignoring self-heating TCR at full power; exceeding I_max = sqrt(P/R) especially at hot ambient.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
Layer L1. Fidelity: `ideal_components` for a plain resistor; `behavioural_approximation` for the Kelvin subckt below.

```
.options tnom=25
* Two-net Kelvin model: current net I1/I2, sense net E1/E2. For 2-terminal parts E1 is connected to I1 and E2 to I2 at the package level.
.subckt RSENSE4 I1 I2 E1 E2 params: Rs=1m Rc=50u TCR=75e-6 LS=0
Rel   ea eb {Rs} tc1={TCR}
Rc1   I1 ea {Rc}
Rc2   I2 eb {Rc}
Rs1   E1 ea 1u
Rs2   E2 eb 1u
* LS > 0 :  place Ls in series with Rel:  Rel ea em ... Lel em eb {LS}  (generator chooses)
.ends
```
Rc is the terminal-to-element contact resistance on the current side; no sourced value, default 0 for the pure two-net topology (use 1u not 0). Rs is the part value. For the 2-terminal variant the generator ties E1 to I1 and E2 to I2, which collapses the two nets to one.

Realistic extras: TCR (sourced by value range), LS 0.5 to 5 nH (S13, S14, S15), self-heating via the RTH_SH technique in BEH-RES-FIXED (Rth derived from the derating curve (T_end - 70) / P70; for WSL2512 P70 = 1 W, end 170 C, Rth = 100 K / 1 W = 100 K/W, DERIVED, board-dependent). Thermal EMF is not modeled (a series B-source of 3 uV/C x dT could be added, ASSUMPTION).

Valid analyses: op, dc, ac, tran, temp. Valid range: DC to about 1 MHz for the L values above (L = 3 nH vs R = 1 mohm: the impedance doubles in magnitude at 53 kHz, so the realistic model matters for ac and fast tran; bench B3). Limitations: sub-microsecond transients depend on the real layout; no thermal EMF; contact-resistance of the current terminals is not sourced; ngspice clamps exactly-zero resistance to 1 mohm; the TCR is a linear bound, not the real curve.

### 6. Ratings and limits
- Power: `P = i^2 * Rs <= P70 * clamp((T_end - Tamb)/(T_end - 70), 0, 1)` with T_end = 170 C (S13, S15). S14 gives a curve to about 10 % of rated power at 170 C (second-hand reading), which differs from "zero at 170 C" in S13 reading; use the more conservative zero-at-170 C until the curve is read from the PDF.
- Current: `i <= sqrt(P_allowed/Rs)` (S15).
- Voltage: `abs(v) <= sqrt(P * Rs)` (S13, S14), a few volts at most; not a practical limit.
- Sense-terminal current: not specified in the documents opened. Recommendation (ASSUMPTION): treat E1/E2 as a high-impedance measurement port; flag if the sim shows more than 1 percent of the load current in the sense net.
- Short-time overload and pulse: described only by an external calculator link (S13): RESEARCH_REQUIRED.

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior
- Overpower: element overheats, solder joints and PCB degrade; the welded strip normally fails open at gross overload (general knowledge, ASSUMPTION). Response: flag ERROR when P > P_allowed; at P > 5 x P_allowed for 5 s or longer treat as open (assumption, matching 5 x P tests quoted for wirewound in S11, not for this part).
- Drift: TCR times self-heating; flag when temperature rise times TCR exceeds the tolerance (informational).
- Wrong connection (2-wire reading on a Kelvin part, sense pins swapped, sense net carrying load current): the simulator cannot detect this from the part alone; netlist check: if the E1/E2 nodes share a trace with I1/I2 nodes at lead resistance above 10 % of Rs, flag `kelvin_violation` (DRC-style rule, ASSUMPTION).
- Overvoltage, reverse polarity, ESD: not applicable or not sourced.
- Open: permanent. Short: the part cannot short.

### 8. Thermal behavior
dT = P Rth. At 1 W on a WSL2512 the derating curve implies up to 100 K rise (DERIVED); the shunt rated 36 W at 70 C with datasheet mounting (S15). Copper terminals conduct a lot of heat into the board; the real element temperature is higher at the center than at the terminals. Only a single-pole model is provided.

### 9. Appearance summary
OHM-014 is a 2512-sized rectangular body with a visible metal strip between two wide terminal plates, not the dark overglaze of a thick-film chip; the Kelvin variants have four pads (3D spec OHM-014). OHM-015 is a flat copper bar with two bolt holes, a different-colored resistance element in the middle and two small sense pins below (3D spec OHM-015).

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-RES-NETWORK

Applies to OHM-016 (SIP resistor network, bussed or isolated) and OHM-017 (SMD resistor array, isolated elements).

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
Several matched resistors in one package: pull-up/pull-down banks (bussed, one common), series termination of buses (isolated or one per line), LED current limiting banks, resistor ladder building blocks, data-line terminators. They save board area and placement cost and the elements are all of the same technology and value, which gives good ratio tracking. Typical values 10 ohm to 10 Mohm (S17), 10 ohm to 1 Mohm (S18).

### 2. What it is and how it works
Thick-film elements screened on one ceramic substrate with a common value per package (S17: "of equal value"), each with its own rating; the package also has a total power limit. Bussed: n elements, each from the common pin to its own pin. Isolated: each element between two pins of its own. The Bourns 4600X also has a dual-terminator type (S17, circuit 104: pairs of resistors in series between common lines on pins 1 and 8) that this entry set does not model by default.

Equations: each element is an ordinary resistor; element power P_k = V_k^2 / R; package power sum(P_k) <= P_package(Tamb). Ratings (S17, 70 C): bussed 0.20 W per resistor, isolated 0.30 W per resistor, package ratings 0.50 to 1.75 W (4604X to 4614X), max working voltage 100 V, TCR +/-100 ppm/K (50 ohm to 2.2 Mohm), +/-250 below 50 ohm or above 2.2 Mohm, tolerance 10 to 49 ohm +/-1 ohm, 50 ohm to 5 Mohm +/-2 % (+/-1 % with F), above 5 Mohm +/-5 %. SMD array CRA06P (S18, 70 C): 0.063 W per element, 50 V, TCR +/-100 ppm/K, tolerance 1/2/5 %, 10 ohm to 1 Mohm, isolated elements, 4 and 8 terminals, -55 to +125 C, derating linear from 100 % at 70 C to about 0 at 155 C (graph, second-hand). Elements in one package share one substrate, so their temperatures are coupled; the model treats them as thermally independent unless the user enables a shared heat pool (not sourced).

### 3. How it connects
SIP bussed: pin 1 is the common pin; the other pins each go to one element (S17, 3D spec OHM-016 "bussed common = pin 1"). N pins give N-1 resistors. Typical use: pin 1 to VCC, other pins to the signal lines. Mistakes: using a bussed network where isolated resistors are needed (all outputs share one end); reversing the part so the common pin is on the wrong end; exceeding package power when all elements dissipate at once; mixing up the pin 1 marking. SIP isolated: N pins give N/2 resistors, each between two pins. The exact pin pairing for the Bourns isolated type was not established (S17 summary says only "between two pins"): RESEARCH_REQUIRED; the default in this spec (consecutive pairs 1-2, 3-4, ...) is ASSUMPTION confidence L. SMD array: 8 terminals for 4 resistors. The pairing of terminals was not stated in the documents opened; by geometry and by the common array convention each element joins opposite terminals (pin k to pin 9-k for 8-terminal packages, k = 1..4; pin 1 to 4 and 2 to 3 for the 4-terminal 2-element array): basis CONSENSUS, confidence M, flagged for verification against the CRA06P drawing.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
Layer L1. Fidelity: `ideal_components` for plain resistors; models below use `.subckt` so they report `behavioural_approximation` in the OHMNI runner.
```
* Bussed SIP, example N=4 pins (pin 1 common, 3 resistors)
.subckt SIP4_BUSSED p1 p2 p3 p4 params: R=10k TCR=100e-6
R1 p1 p2 {R} tc1={TCR}
R2 p1 p3 {R} tc1={TCR}
R3 p1 p4 {R} tc1={TCR}
.ends
* Isolated 4-element array, 8 terminals (element k between pin k and pin 9-k)
.subckt ARR4_ISO t1 t2 t3 t4 t5 t6 t7 t8 params: R=1k TCR=100e-6
R1 t1 t8 {R} tc1={TCR}
R2 t2 t7 {R} tc1={TCR}
R3 t3 t6 {R} tc1={TCR}
R4 t4 t5 {R} tc1={TCR}
.ends
```
The generator creates N-1 or N/2 elements by pin count. Element-to-element mismatch: each element gets its own tolerance draw plus a correlated common part (matching tolerance is not given in S17 or S18: RESEARCH_REQUIRED; default all elements identical). No inter-element capacitance or leakage is modeled (not sourced). Valid analyses: op, dc, ac, tran, temp. Valid range: below the element and package limits; low frequency (no parasitics).

| R (SIP 4600X) | ohm | 10k | 10 | 10M | +/-2 % (+/-1 % F) | MFR_DATASHEET | H | S17 |
| R (array CRA06P) | ohm | 10k | 10 | 1M | 1/2/5 % | MFR_DATASHEET | H | S18 |
| TCR SIP | ppm/K | 100 | | 250 | | MFR_DATASHEET | H | S17 |

| ratio tracking | ppm/K | RESEARCH_REQUIRED | | | | | | |

### 6. Ratings and limits
- Per-element power `v_k*i_k <= P_elem * derate(Tamb)` with the derating line 100 % at 70 C to 0 % at 155 C for the array (S18) and to the 125 C limit assumed for the SIP (derating curve in S17 not read: ASSUMPTION, zero at 125 C).
- Package power `sum(v_k*i_k) <= P_pkg*derate(Tamb)`; S17 gives 0.50 to 1.75 W by model.
- Voltage per element `abs(v_k) <= V_max` (100 V SIP, 50 V array).

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior
Same physical mechanisms as chip thick film (BEH-RES-FIXED): overpower drifts or opens the element; an open element does not damage its neighbours except by thermal coupling. Sim response: flag per element, open that element only on severe overpower (> 5 x, assumption); flag when the sum exceeds the package power even if every element is below its own limit; flag wrong pin-1 orientation not detectable electrically, but a DRC check is useful: bussed common must not connect to a signal-driven net unless the design intends it (rule suggestion, ASSUMPTION).

### 8. Thermal behavior
Elements share a substrate: use the package rating as the cap and the per-element rating as the individual cap. No sourced Rth. Single-pole per element using Rth = (T_end - 70) / P_pkg for the shared case (DERIVED).

### 9. Appearance summary
OHM-016 is a flat black SIP block with a single row of pins at 2.54 mm pitch and a pin-1 mark; OHM-017 is a small 3.2 x 1.6 mm chip with four terminals per long side and no manufacturer pin-1 mark in the sources (3D spec OHM-016, OHM-017).

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-RES-POT

Applies to OHM-018 (THT multi-turn cermet trimmer, Bourns 3296W as representative), OHM-019 (SMD single-turn trimmer, Bourns 3314G), OHM-020 (rotary potentiometer, RV16 representative, PTV09 as the sourced alternate).

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
A resistive track with a sliding contact (wiper). Used as a variable voltage divider (3 terminals: volume, bias, reference trim, contrast, set-point) or as a variable resistor (rheostat: wiper tied to one end). Trimmers (OHM-018, OHM-019) are set once at calibration with a screwdriver; the rotary pot (OHM-020) is a user control. Common values: 1 k to 1 M (S21), 10 ohm to 2 Mohm for the Bourns trimmers (S19, S20).

### 2. What it is and how it works
A resistive element (cermet for 3296 and 3314, carbon for typical panel pots) between terminals A and B; the wiper terminal W contacts the track at a mechanically set position. The three-terminal model is two resistors from the wiper tap to each end plus a series wiper contact resistance:

R_AW = R_tot * (1 - f(x)), R_WB = R_tot * f(x), with x in [0, 1] the wiper position parameter (mechanical, 0 at the B end by the convention chosen here) and f the taper function. Unloaded divider: V_W = V_AB * f(x). The loaded divider uses R_WB || R_load, as in bench B2. The contact resistance Rw sits in series with the wiper terminal and only matters when wiper current flows.

Taper:
- Linear (B): f(x) = x.
- Audio / logarithmic (A) is not a single formula; real parts use a two-segment or multi-segment resistive curve, and manufacturers publish multiple variants (PTV09 lists A1..A6, B0..B5, C1..C6 series curves, S21). The model offers f(x) = (10^(k x) - 1)/(10^k - 1) with k = 1.505, which gives 15 % of the end-to-end resistance at mid-rotation (bench B3: 15.02 %), an assumed curve (basis ASSUMPTION, confidence L; the exact percentage at mid-travel for a given part is RESEARCH_REQUIRED). The letter code to taper mapping differs by region (a source of user error); S21 defines only that the code letters exist, so the mapping is not stated here.
Trimmer turns and resolution: 3296 is a 25-turn trimmer with "infinite" resolution (S19); 3314 is single turn with 210 degrees nominal adjustment angle (S20); PTV09 rotates 280 +/- 10 degrees (S21). Resolution of a multi-turn trimmer is mechanical (25 turns), so x per degree is tiny; the digital step does not exist, but the contact resistance variation (CRV) is the practical limit: 1.0 % or 3 ohm, whichever is greater, for 3296 (S19); 3 % or 3 ohm for 3314 (S20).
Other sourced electrical facts: end-to-end tolerance +/-10 % (3296) and +/-20 % (3314, PTV09) (S19, S20, S21); TCR +/-100 ppm/K for both Bourns trimmers (S19, S20); power rating 0.5 W at 70 C falling to 0 W at 125 C for 3296 (S19), 0.25 W at 70 C falling to 0 W at 125 C for 3314 (S20); PTV09 20 VDC / 50 VAC maximum, 0.05 W rating derated, -10 to +50 C, sliding noise 100 mV max, 10,000 rotation life (S21; the extraction of the derating value was unclear and is not used). Absolute minimum resistance of 3296: 1 % or 2 ohm, whichever is greater (S19), used as the end-resistance floor Rend.

### 3. How it connects
Terminals 1, 2, 3 with 2 = wiper (S19, S20, 3D spec OHM-018..020). Voltage divider: pin 1 to the high reference, pin 3 to the low reference, pin 2 to the output; the load impedance should be much larger than R_tot (a load of R_tot gives the 4.0 V instead of 5.0 V at mid-travel in bench B2). Rheostat: connect pin 2 to pin 1 or pin 3 (unused end tied to the wiper to avoid an open track during contact bounce). Mistakes: a low-impedance load on the wiper or a wiper current beyond the limit (not specified for the Bourns parts, the wiper is intended as a high-impedance tap); letting the wiper float during adjustment of a rheostat; running the track at full rated power with the wiper near an end (the full power is then concentrated in a short track segment); using a log pot as a linear control; setting a trimmer with a feedback loop whose wiper noise corrupts the loop.

Direction of rotation vs which end: S19 shows "clockwise" diagrams for 3296 but the extraction did not give which terminal pair the resistance decreases toward, and the datasheet for 3314 puts the rotor "within +/-22 degrees of the centerline of terminal 2" (S20) for the factory setting. OHMNI convention (CONSENSUS, flagged): x increases clockwise and moves the wiper toward terminal 1; this should be confirmed against the Bourns drawing.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
Layer L1. Fidelity: `behavioural_approximation` (needs `.subckt`; the three resistor positions are an approximation of a distributed track).

```
.subckt POT3 A W B params: Rtot=10k pos=0.5 Rend=1 Rw=100m taper=0 k=1.505
.param fl={pos}
.param fg={(10**(k*pos)-1)/(10**k-1)}
.param f={taper==0 ? fl : fg}
.param fcl={min(max(f,0),1)}
Rab1 A m {max(Rtot*(1-fcl),Rend)}
Rab2 m B {max(Rtot*fcl,Rend)}
Rwp  m W {Rw}
.ends
```
`pos` is the wiper position parameter (x). Pin order is A (pin 1), W (pin 2, wiper), B (pin 3). `pos = 0` puts the wiper at B, `pos = 1` at A (bench B1 validates V_W = V_AB * pos). For time-varying wiper position (a rotary control animated in a transient run) use behavioral currents, bench B4:
```
Bt A W I=V(A,W)/max({Rtot}*(1-V(pos)),{Rend})
Bb W B I=V(W,B)/max({Rtot}*V(pos),{Rend})
```
with `V(pos)` driven by a PWL or other source.

Parameter mapping: Rtot = end-to-end resistance (marking, tolerance as datasheet); Rend = absolute minimum resistance (1 % or 2 ohm for the 3296, S19; unsourced for 3314 and PTV09); Rw = wiper contact resistance (no sourced value, default 100 mohm is ASSUMPTION; the CRV figures describe variation and noise, not the value); taper from the part's marking code; TCR from section 5. Realistic extras: TCR on both track resistors (tc1 = 100e-6), sliding noise as a random wiper-voltage jitter (S21: up to 100 mV max for the PTV09, not modeled in L1 unless the user adds noise), tolerance draw on Rtot, wiper-position tolerance for the 3314 factory setting (50 % +/-10 %, S20).

Valid analyses: op, dc, ac (with parasitics absent), tran, temp. Valid range: DC to audio and low RF; no parasitic L or C sourced. Limitations: no wiper noise, no end-resistance dependence on position, linear and the one assumed log curve only, no mechanical backlash, no contact bounce, the track is lumped (power and heating in a distributed track are not modeled), and the manufacturer's mid-travel resistance for log tapers is unknown.

### 6. Ratings and limits
- Total track power: `v_AB^2/Rtot <= P70 * clamp((125 - Tamb)/(125 - 70), 0, 1)` (S19, S20; 0.5 W / 0.25 W).
- Segment power (ASSUMPTION): `v_AW^2/R_AW <= P_allowed * (R_AW/Rtot)` and likewise for W-B, so that a wiper near one end does not exceed its share of track.
- Voltage: `abs(v_AB) <= V_max` (300 V for the trimmers listed, 50 V for 3314 style R, 20 V DC for PTV09; S19..S21).
- Wiper current: `abs(i_W)` not specified. Proposed warning threshold (ASSUMPTION L): 1 mA for a trimmer, because the wiper contact is meant as a voltage tap.
- Temperature: -55 to +125 C trimmers, -10 to +50 C PTV09.

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior
Datasheets opened do not describe failure modes. Physical reasoning (ASSUMPTION): overpower or excessive wiper current locally overheats the track under the contact and burns it, which raises the local resistance, then goes open; the wiper can burn the track and lose contact, producing noisy or open-wiper output; cermet tolerates more than carbon. Simulator response: flag `overpower_track` (ERROR) when track or segment power is exceeded; at more than 5 x (assumption) treat the track as open at the wiper location (set Rend to 1G on the overloaded segment). Open wiper (contact lift): model by Rw = 1G (user toggle "wiper open"), useful to expose designs that go to a rail when the wiper is lost (the rheostat-without-tied-end mistake). Overtemperature: out of rating. No reverse polarity or ESD concerns. Wear (S21: 10,000 cycles) and CRV growth: not modeled; the simulator may add a position-dependent jitter in a future version.

### 8. Thermal behavior
Track self-heating: 3296 at full 0.5 W has a rise implied by the derating curve (0 W at 125 C: Rth = (125 - 70)/0.5 = 110 K/W, DERIVED; 3314: 220 K/W). TCR of +/-100 ppm/K applies to the end-to-end value; the divider ratio is nearly insensitive to temperature because both sections move together. Not modeled further.

### 9. Appearance summary
OHM-018 is a blue-or-beige rectangular multi-turn housing with a top or side adjust screw and three round pins in a line; OHM-019 is a 4.5 mm square SMD trimmer with a slotted rotor and three pads (pin 2 = wiper); OHM-020 is a round metal-can rotary pot with a bushing, a shaft and three pins (pin 2 = wiper). See 3D spec entries OHM-018, OHM-019, OHM-020.

```yaml
  - {id: B2, file: bench/pot/B2.cir, expected: [{measure: v(w), value: 4.0, tolerance: 0.1%, basis: "10*(5k||10k)/(5k+5k||10k)"}], measured_in_ngspice: "3.999968", ngspice_version: "42"}
  - {id: B3, file: bench/pot/B3.cir, expected: [{measure: v(w), value: 1.50243, tolerance: 0.1%, basis: "10*(10^(k*0.5)-1)/(10^k-1), k=1.505"}], measured_in_ngspice: "1.502431", ngspice_version: "42"}
  - {id: B4, file: bench/pot/B4.cir, expected: [{measure: v(w)@0.25ms, value: 2.5, tolerance: 0.1%, basis: "10*t/1ms"}, {measure: v(w)@0.75ms, value: 7.5, tolerance: 0.1%, basis: "10*t/1ms"}], measured_in_ngspice: "2.5; 7.5", ngspice_version: "42"}
sources: "S19, S20, S21"
confidence: {parameters: M, ratings: M, model: M, failure: L}
status: partial
```

### 12. Sources
S19 (Bourns 3296), S20 (Bourns 3314), S21 (Bourns PTV09).

### 13. Research confidence
(a) parameters MEDIUM for the trimmers and LOW for the rotary pot because the representative RV16 was not found; (b) ratings MEDIUM; (c) model MEDIUM for linear taper, LOW for log taper; (d) failure LOW.
Unresolved: RV16 (Taiwan Alpha) ratings; wiper current rating (none in S19, S20); wiper contact resistance value; rotation direction vs terminal; tapers A/B/C letter-to-curve map and mid-travel resistance for log curves; PTV09 power derating (extraction unclear); end resistance for 3314 and PTV09.

---

# PER-ENTRY SECTIONS

Pin numbering follows the 3D spec. For all two-terminal entries: pin 1 at -X, pin 2 at +X, A = pin 1, B = pin 2, non-polarized. Chip rating source is Vishay D/CRCW e3 (S1) for 0402 to 2512 unless stated, CRCW0201 (S3) and CRCW01005 (S2). Conflicting rows from the Yageo AC (automotive) datasheet (S4) are shown, not hidden. Derived Rth = (T_end - 70)/P70 (DERIVED, lumps the datasheet test board, L confidence). Common chip defaults: value 10k, tolerance 1 %, TCR 100 ppm/K for 0402 and larger (200 ppm/K for 5 % grade), T_end 155 C, knee 70 C, ls = cp = 0 (unsourced).

Chip table (70 C ratings):

| OHM | size | P70 (Vishay) | U limit (Vishay) | Yageo AC alt. P / U | jumper (Vishay) | TCR options (Vishay) | Rth derived |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 001 | 01005 | 0.031 W (S2) | 15 V (S2) | not listed | 0.5 A, <=50 mohm (S2) | +/-250 or -200/+600 (S2) | (125-70)/0.031 = 1774 K/W if T_end = 125 C |
| 002 | 0201 | 0.05 W (S3) | 30 V (S3) | 1/20 W, 25 V (S4) | 1.0 A, <=50 mohm (S3) | +/-100, +/-200 or -200/+400 (S3) | 1700 K/W |
| 003 | 0402 | 0.10 W (S1) | 75 V (S1) | 1/16 or 1/8 W, 50 V (S4) | 1.5 A (S1) | +/-200, +/-100 (S1) | 850 K/W |
| 004 | 0603 | 0.125 W (S1) | 75 V (S1) | 1/10 or 1/5 W, 75 V (S4) | 2.0 A (S1) | +/-200, +/-100 (S1) | 680 K/W |
| 005 | 0805 | 0.25 W (S1) | 150 V (S1) | 1/8 or 1/4 W, 150 V (S4) | 2.5 A (S1) | +/-200, +/-100 (S1) | 340 K/W |
| 006 | 1206 | 0.25 W (S1) | 200 V (S1) | 1/4 or 1/2 W, 200 V (S4) | 3.5 A (S1) | +/-200, +/-100 (S1) | 340 K/W |
| 007 | 1210 | 0.5 W (S1) | 200 V (S1) | 1/2 or 1 W, 200 V (S4) | 5.0 A (S1) | +/-200, +/-100 (S1) | 170 K/W |
| 008 | 2010 | 0.75 W (S1) | 400 V (S1) | 3/4 or 1.25 W, 200 V (S4) | 6.0 A (S1) | +/-200, +/-100 (S1) | 113 K/W |
| 009 | 2512 | 1.0 W (S1) | 500 V (S1) | 1 or 2 W, 200 V (S4) | 7.0 A (S1) | +/-200, +/-100 (S1) | 85 K/W |

Source conflicts: working voltage for 2010 and 2512 is 400 V and 500 V in Vishay S1 versus 200 V in Yageo AC S4 (a different series and an automotive grade; the standard Yageo RC series datasheet could not be fetched, 404). For 0201: 30 V (Vishay) vs 25 V (Yageo AC). For 0402: 75 V (Vishay, as extracted) vs 50 V (Yageo AC). Default to the lower value when the manufacturer is not specified (conservative): 0201 25 V, 0402 50 V, 2010 200 V, 2512 200 V; use the higher value only when a Vishay part is selected. Power per size also differs for the same size (e.g. 0402 0.10 W vs 1/16 W); the same rule applies: default to the lower of the two.

Common to all chip entries: the zero-ohm jumper variant is a resistor with R <= 50 mohm and a current limit from the table (a jumper that exceeds the limit opens). In ngspice model a jumper as `R 50m`-class or as a 0 V source, never `R=0` (it is replaced by 1 mohm).

## [OHM-001] 01005 SMD resistor -> BEH-RES-FIXED
Values from S2 (rev 28-Oct-13): P70 0.031 W, Umax 15 V, TCR +/-250 or -200/+600 ppm/K, tolerance 1, 2 or 5 %, 10 ohm to 1 Mohm (1 %), E24 and E96, -55 to +125 C. Defaults: value 10k, tolerance 1 %, tcr 250 ppm/K (use the worse bound), t_end 125 C (ASSUMPTION: the datasheet's film-temperature limit was not read; the operating range ends at 125 C). Pin map: A = terminal 1, B = terminal 2. No polarity, no body marking (3D spec). Checks: P <= 0.031 W derated, V <= 15 V. Note the per-size ratings are the lowest in the family; both limits are easy to exceed with a 5 V rail only at low values (P = 25/R: R < 806 ohm exceeds 31 mW at 5 V). Status: partial (L, C unsourced; derating end point assumed).

## [OHM-002] 0201 SMD resistor -> BEH-RES-FIXED
S3 (rev 21-Sep-2022): P70 0.05 W, 30 V, TCR +/-100, +/-200 or -200/+400 ppm/K, 1 or 5 %, 1 ohm to 10 Mohm, E24 and E96, -55 to +155 C; jumper 50 mohm, 1.0 A at 70 C. Yageo AC: 1/20 W, 25 V (S4). Defaults: value 10k, 1 %, 200 ppm/K, T_end 155 C. Pin map: A = 1, B = 2. Status: partial.

## [OHM-003] 0402 SMD resistor -> BEH-RES-FIXED
S1: 0.10 W, 75 V, TCR +/-200 or +/-100, 1 or 5 %, 1 ohm to 10 Mohm. S4: 1/16 W (or 1/8 W high-power), 50 V. Default conservative: 0.0625 W, 50 V unless a Vishay part is chosen. Pin map A = 1, B = 2. Status: partial.

## [OHM-004] 0603 SMD resistor -> BEH-RES-FIXED
S1: 0.125 W, 75 V; S4: 1/10 W (or 1/5 W), 75 V. Default conservative: 0.1 W, 75 V. Jumper 2.0 A. Pin map A = 1, B = 2. Existing OHMNI record GENERIC_RESISTOR lists 0402/0603/0805/1206 with pins 1, 2 passive: compatible. Status: partial.

## [OHM-005] 0805 SMD resistor -> BEH-RES-FIXED
S1: 0.25 W, 150 V; S4: 1/8 W (or 1/4 W), 150 V. Default conservative: 0.125 W, 150 V. Jumper 2.5 A. Pin map A = 1, B = 2. Status: partial.

## [OHM-006] 1206 SMD resistor -> BEH-RES-FIXED
S1: 0.25 W, 200 V; S4: 1/4 W (or 1/2 W), 200 V. Default 0.25 W, 200 V (both agree). Jumper 3.5 A. Pin map A = 1, B = 2. Status: partial.

## [OHM-007] 1210 SMD resistor -> BEH-RES-FIXED
S1: 0.5 W, 200 V; S4: 1/2 W (or 1 W), 200 V. Default 0.5 W, 200 V (agree). Jumper 5.0 A. Pin map A = 1, B = 2. Status: partial.

## [OHM-008] 2010 SMD resistor -> BEH-RES-FIXED
S1: 0.75 W, 400 V; S4: 3/4 W (or 1.25 W), 200 V (conflict on voltage). Default conservative: 0.75 W, 200 V. Jumper 6.0 A. Pin map A = 1, B = 2. Status: partial.

## [OHM-009] 2512 SMD resistor -> BEH-RES-FIXED
S1: 1.0 W, 500 V; S4: 1 W (or 2 W), 200 V (conflict on voltage). Default conservative: 1 W, 200 V. Jumper 7.0 A. Pin map A = 1, B = 2. Note: a 2512 thick film is not a current-sense part (OHM-014), its resistance is 1 ohm and above in S1. Status: partial.

## [OHM-010] Axial carbon-film resistor -> BEH-RES-FIXED
Representative: Yageo CFR (S5, Apr 03, 2024 V.3): CFR-12 1/6 W, CFR-25 1/4 W, CFR-50 1/2 W, CFR-100 1 W, CFR-200 2 W at 70 C; working voltage 150 V (CFR-12) to 500 V (CFR-100, CFR-200); overload voltage 300 V to 1000 V; TCR from +/-350 to -500..0 ppm/K by value; 2 % (G) or 5 % (J), E24, 1 ohm to 10 Mohm; -55 to +155 C; knee 70 C, zero power near 155 C; short-time overload 2.5 x RCWV for 5 s, drift +/-(0.75 % + 0.05 ohm). KOA CF (S7): 0.25 W (CF1/4) and 0.5 W types, TCR +350..-450 up to 0..-1300 ppm/K, working voltage 300 to 700 V by type, CFP flame-retardant variant, knee about 70 C; its document header shows a date of October 28, 2030 beside a September 1, 2020 first page date, an obvious typo, so the revision is unreliable. Conflict shown: Yageo CFR TCR is much smaller in magnitude than KOA's for high values.
Defaults (1/4 W): value 10k, tolerance 5 %, TCR -350 ppm/K (sign negative for carbon), p_rated 0.25 W, u_limit 250 V (ASSUMPTION L: per-type voltage for CFR-25 was not read, only the 150 to 500 V range), t_end 155 C, Rth 340 K/W (DERIVED; lead length and board dependent). The 3D spec lists 1/6, 1/4, 1/2, 1 and 2 W variants: use the S5 power list and set u_limit from the range (150 V for 1/6 W, 500 V for 1 and 2 W, interpolated for others, L).
Pin map: A = pin 1 (-X, first band side), B = pin 2 (+X, tolerance band side). Non-polarized; the band orientation is only a reading convention. Noise: carbon film is the noisiest of the families here but S5 gives no number; not modeled. Status: partial.

## [OHM-011] Axial metal-film resistor -> BEH-RES-FIXED
Representative: Yageo MFR (S6, Apr 03, 2024 V.4): MFR-12 1/6 W, MFR-25 and MFR25S 1/4 W, MFR-50 1/2 W, MFR100 1 W, MFR200 2 W, MFR3WS 3 W at 70 C; working voltage 200 V (MFR-12, MFR-25S) to 500 V (MFR100, MFR2WS, MFR3WS); overload voltage 400 to 1000 V; TCR +/-50 or +/-100 ppm/K; +/-0.5, 1, 2, 5 %; E24, E96, E192; 1 ohm to 4.7 Mohm; -55 to +155 C; derating from 100 % at 70 C to about 20 % at 155 C (graph reading); short overload 2.5 x RCWV for 5 s, drift +/-(0.25 % + 0.05 ohm). Alternative thin-film leaded part (S8, Vishay MRS16/MRS25, rev 07-Mar-16): 0.4 W and 0.6 W, +/-50 ppm/K, 1 %, 200 V / 350 V, 1000 h drift +/-(0.5 % R + 0.05 ohm). Defaults (1/4 W): value 10k, 1 %, TCR 100 ppm/K (50 ppm/K when the +/-50 grade is chosen), p_rated 0.25 W, u_limit 200 V (conservative, the exact 25-size value was not read), power curve end 20 % at 155 C (use `P_allowed = P_rated*(1-0.8*(Tamb-70)/85)`), Rth 340 K/W (derived from the zero-at-155 reading, which is more conservative than 20 % at 155). Pin map: A = pin 1 (-X), B = pin 2 (+X). Status: partial.

## [OHM-012] Cement power resistor -> BEH-RES-FIXED
Representative families: Vishay Dale CPR (S9, doc 30219, rev 21-Dec-10, radial terminals, ceramic case, inorganic potting) and Vishay Draloric Z300 axial cemented wirewound (S10, doc 21007, rev 25-Aug-10). CPR: 3, 5, 7, 10, 15, 20 W at 40 C ambient (CPR03 to CPR20), 0.1 ohm to 2.855 kohm, +/-5 % or +/-10 %, TCR +/-300 ppm/K for 1 ohm and above, +/-600 ppm/K below 1 ohm, -65 to +275 C, V = sqrt(P R), 5 x rated power for 5 s, derating from 40 C to 0 % at 275 C, and "can reliably function as a fuse and as a resistor". Z300: 1 to 10 W, TCR classes -10..-80 ppm/K (class 1) and 100..180 ppm/K (class 3), 10 x rated power for 5 s per IEC 60115-1 as read, non-flammable cement coating; its derating knee was read as about 150 C with a zero-power reference of -55 C, which is not a normal curve reading and is not used (RESEARCH_REQUIRED). Conflict shown: the rating reference temperature is 40 C for CPR (S9), 70 C for chips (S1), 25 C for RS (S11); do not mix them. Defaults (5 W): value 10 ohm, tolerance 5 %, TCR 300 ppm/K, p_rated 5 W with knee 40 C, T_end 275 C, V_max = sqrt(P R), inductance not specified in S9 or S10 (the cement wirewound is inductive: ls default 0 with a UI warning; ASSUMPTION), Rth derived (275 - 40)/5 = 47 K/W (DERIVED; the case becomes very hot, which is why 275 C is permitted). Flameproof / fusible: CPR is stated to function as a fuse; Z300 is not noted as fusible. Pin map: A = pin 1 (-P/2), B = pin 2 (+P/2); non-polar (3D spec). Size variants 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 15 and 20 W in the 3D spec: 2 W is not in CPR (3 to 20 W) and Z300 offers 2 W. Status: partial.

## [OHM-013] Wirewound power resistor -> BEH-RES-FIXED
Representative: Vishay Dale RS (S11, rev 27-Apr-2026): RS1/4 0.4 W, RS1/2 0.75 W, RS01A 1.0 W, RS002 4.0 W (U) or 5.5 W (V), RS02B 3.0 W (U) or 3.75 W (V), RS005 5.0 W (U) or 6.5 W (V), RS010 10 W (U) or 13 W (V), all at 25 C; 0.1 ohm to 273 kohm; tolerance +/-0.05 to +/-10 %; TCR +/-20 ppm/K at 10 ohm and above, +/-50 for 1 to 9.9 ohm, +/-90 for 0.5 to 0.99 ohm; 500 VRMS (RS1/4 to RS01A) or 1000 VRMS dielectric withstanding; V = sqrt(P R); -65 to +250 C (characteristic U) or -65 to +350 C (V); 5 x rated for 5 s (3.75 W and below) and 10 x for 5 s (4 W and above); non-inductive (Ayrton-Perry) winding available as an equivalent-spec part (the NS in the family title is read here as the non-inductive counterpart: inferred, M). Cross-reference RH/NH aluminum housed (S12, 14-Nov-17, ratings at 25 C, TCR +/-20 ppm/K at 10 ohm, 5 x for 5 s) shows the same pattern. The derating knee for RS was read ambiguously (knees at 120 C and 350 C) and is not used: conservative default is a straight line from rated power at 25 C to zero at 250 C (characteristic U). Defaults (RS005 U): value 10 ohm, tolerance 5 %, TCR 20 ppm/K, p_rated 5 W (25 C), ls default 0 with a warning (wirewound is an inductor; use the non-inductive flag to force ls = 0; any numeric ls is user-supplied, ASSUMPTION), V_max sqrt(P R), Rth derived (250 - 25)/5 = 45 K/W (DERIVED). Pin map: A = pin 1 (-P/2), B = pin 2 (+P/2); non-polar. Variants 1 to 10 W in 3D spec: RS1/4 to RS010 match. Status: partial.

## [OHM-014] SMD current-sense resistor -> BEH-RES-SENSE
Representative: Vishay WSL2512 (S13, rev 23-Nov-2023): 1.0 W at 70 C, 0.5 mohm to 0.5 ohm, TCR +/-75 (50 to 500 mohm) to +/-400 (0.5 to 0.99 mohm), 0.5 / 1 / 5 %, -65 to +170 C, L 0.5 to 5 nH, thermal EMF < 3 uV/C; sizes 0603 (0.1 W) to 2816 (2 W) in the same datasheet. Kelvin: WSK2512 (S14, rev 11-Dec-2023): 1.0 W at 70 C, 0.5 mohm to 0.2 ohm, TCR +/-350 (0.5 to 0.99 mohm), +/-250, +/-75, +/-35 ppm/K (5 mohm to 0.2 ohm), tolerance 0.1, 0.5, 1 %, E1/E2 voltage sense and I1/I2 current terminals. The selector guide (S16) lists WSK0612, WSK1206, WSK2512 as four-terminal types. Defaults: Rs 5 mohm, 1 %, tcr 75 ppm/K, 1 W, 170 C end, Rth 100 K/W (DERIVED). Pin map, 2-terminal (default, 3D spec): I1 = E1 = pin 1 (-X), I2 = E2 = pin 2 (+X), no polarity. 4-terminal: the datasheet names E1, E2, I1, I2 but the pin numbers and which pads they are were not established (3D spec also marks it RESEARCH_REQUIRED); do not emit a 4-terminal pin map until it is. Also unresolved: the 3-terminal variant (3D spec says OHMNI treats it as 4-terminal with two sense terminals merged). Status: partial.

## [OHM-015] Metal shunt resistor -> BEH-RES-SENSE
Representative: Vishay WSBS8518 (S15, rev 26-May-2026): 50, 100, 125 and 250 uohm (range to 1000 uohm), 36 W at 70 C, TCR +/-200 (50 uohm), +/-175 (100 and 125 uohm), +/-110 (250 uohm) ppm/K, tolerance +/-5 % (J) or +/-10 % (K), -65 to +170 C, L < 5 nH, thermal EMF < 1 uV/C (50 uohm) or < 3 uV/C, I = sqrt(P/R), derating from 100 % at 70 C to about 10 % at 175 C (note: the 175 C figure is the datasheet's graph reading, versus +170 C operating limit; use the 170 C limit). Defaults: Rs 100 uohm, 5 %, tcr 175 ppm/K, 36 W, rated current sqrt(36/100e-6) = 600 A (125 uohm: 537 A; 250 uohm: 380 A; 50 uohm: 849 A). The 36 W rating holds for the datasheet mounting on a busbar; with no heatsink the real continuous rating is lower: RESEARCH_REQUIRED. Pin map (3D spec): pin 1 = I1 (bolt hole, -X), pin 2 = I2 (bolt hole, +X), pin 3 = E1 (sense pin at -X, nearest I1), pin 4 = E2 (sense pin at +X). Disagreement with the datasheet: S15 lists variants with two or three sense pins and tapped holes; the 3D spec models two sense pins on a 60 mm hole spacing. Status: partial.

## [OHM-016] SIP resistor network -> BEH-RES-NETWORK
Representative: Bourns 4600X (S17, REV. 10/1/20): bussed (4600X-101: 3 to 13 equal thick-film resistors each between the common bus on pin 1 and its own pin), isolated (-102: 2 to 7 isolated resistors each between two pins), dual terminator (-104). 0.20 W per resistor bussed, 0.30 W isolated, package 0.50 to 1.75 W, 10 ohm to 10 Mohm, +/-2 % (+/-1 % F), TCR +/-100 ppm/K (50 ohm to 2.2 Mohm) or +/-250, 100 V, -55 to +125 C, 4 to 14 pins. Defaults: bussed, 8 pins (7 resistors), 10k, 2 %, tcr 100 ppm/K, p_elem 0.20 W, v_max 100 V; the package power for a given pin count is a number in the 0.5 to 1.75 W range that was not extracted per model (RESEARCH_REQUIRED; use sum of element limits only). Pin map (3D spec, N round leads at 2.54 mm, pin 1 at +Y end marked by a dot or notch, bussed common = pin 1): bussed: pin 1 = common; resistor k between pin 1 and pin k+1 (k = 1..N-1). Isolated: resistors between consecutive pairs (pin 1-pin 2, pin 3-pin 4, ...) is ASSUMPTION, confidence L; the true Bourns isolated pairing was not seen and must be checked. Conflict: none between sources; the 3D spec says pin 1 marking form is unspecified. Failure and checks as the class. Status: partial.

## [OHM-017] SMD resistor array -> BEH-RES-NETWORK
Representative: Vishay CRA06P (S18, rev 09-Jan-07, third-party copy): 0.063 W per element at 70 C, 50 V, TCR +/-100 ppm/K, 1, 2, 5 %, 10 ohm to 1 Mohm, isolated resistors, 4 and 8 terminals, -55 to +125 C (155 C film), linear derating to about 0 at 155 C. Defaults: 4-resistor 8-terminal convex array, 10k, 5 %, tcr 100 ppm/K, p_elem 0.063 W, v_max 50 V. Pin map (3D spec dual-row: pins 1 to 4 down the -X side, pins 5 to 8 up the +X side): element k joins pin k and pin 9-k for k = 1..4 (1-8, 2-7, 3-6, 4-5) and, for the 2-element 4-terminal version, 1-4 and 2-3; basis CONSENSUS (opposite terminals of the body), confidence M, not seen in a drawing of the opened sources. No pin-1 mark exists on the real part per the 3D spec; any decal dot is an OHMNI convention. Status: partial.

## [OHM-018] THT trimmer potentiometer -> BEH-RES-POT
Representative: Bourns 3296 (S19, REV. 02/26): 10 ohm to 2 Mohm, +/-10 %, TCR +/-100 ppm/K, 0.5 W at 70 C derating to 0 W at 125 C, 300 V maximum as printed in the rating, -55 to +125 C, 25 turns nominal, infinite resolution, contact resistance variation 1.0 % or 3 ohm max (greater of), absolute minimum resistance 1 % or 2 ohm (greater of), wiper = pin 2. Defaults: 10k, pos 0.5, Rend 2 ohm, Rw 0.1 ohm (ASSUMPTION), linear taper (trimmers are linear). Pin map (3D spec): pin 1 at +Y, pin 2 wiper at center, pin 3 at -Y; A = 1, W = 2, B = 3. No polarity; a printed arrow or "1" near pin 1 is unverified. Rotation direction vs end: not established; OHMNI convention x increases clockwise toward pin 1, to be verified. Wiper current limit: not given in S19. The 3D spec's 3386 (single turn 3/8 in) alias is not covered by S19 (only 3296); a separate datasheet is needed for it. Status: partial.

## [OHM-019] SMD trimmer potentiometer -> BEH-RES-POT
Representative: Bourns 3314 (S20, REV. 07/24): 10 ohm to 2 Mohm, +/-20 %, TCR +/-100 ppm/K, 0.25 W at 70 C derating to 0 W at 125 C, 300 V for styles G, J and H and 50 V for style R, -55 to +125 C, single turn, 210 degrees nominal, contact resistance variation 3 % or 3 ohm, factory wiper position 50 % (actual TR) +/-10 %, rotor within +/-22 degrees of the centerline of terminal 2. Defaults: 10k, pos 0.5, Rend not specified (use 2 ohm as a placeholder ASSUMPTION, L), Rw 0.1 ohm (ASSUMPTION), linear. Pin map (3D spec): pin 1 (+1.15, +2.75), pin 3 (-1.15, +2.75), pin 2 wiper (0, -2.75); A = 1, W = 2, B = 3; no polarity. Wiper current limit not given in S20. Status: partial.

## [OHM-020] Rotary potentiometer -> BEH-RES-POT
The 3D spec uses Taiwan Alpha RV16 (16 mm) as representative with Bourns PTV09 as the alternate. No RV16 datasheet was opened in this research, so RV16 ratings are RESEARCH_REQUIRED. Sourced alternate PTV09 (S21, REV. 01/25): 1 kohm to 1 Mohm, +/-20 %, linear and audio tapers with curve variants A1..A6, B0..B5, C1..C6, 20 VDC / 50 VAC maximum, 280 +/- 10 degrees rotation, -10 to +50 C, 10,000 rotations, sliding noise 100 mV max, residual resistance extracted as "500 ohm or +/-1 % max" (ambiguous); power rating about 0.05 W with a derating (extraction unclear). Defaults: 10k, pos 0.5, linear taper (default B); audio option uses the assumed curve k = 1.505; Rend 20 ohm placeholder (ASSUMPTION L), Rw 0.1 ohm (ASSUMPTION), p_rated 0.05 W (ASSUMPTION L, from PTV09), v_max 20 V DC. Pin map (3D spec): pin 1 at +Y, pin 2 wiper in the middle, pin 3 at -Y; A = 1, W = 2, B = 3. 3D spec pin pitch: 5.0 mm (RV16-style) or 2.5 mm (PTV09). No polarity. Rotation direction vs end unresolved. Status: partial (RV16 research_required).

# R2: Capacitors (OHM-021 to OHM-040) behavior specification

Group R2, 20 entries, 7 behavior classes. Simulator target: ngspice 42 (all benches run with `ngspice -b` here). Fidelity labels use the product vocabulary (`ideal_components`, `behavioural_approximation`, `vendor_model`). Every class in this file is `behavioural_approximation` in realistic mode and `ideal_components` when ESR, ESL, leakage, bias and flags are switched off. No vendor model is attached to any entry, and no class claims `vendor_model`.

## 0. Conventions used by every class in this file

Layer: all seven classes are L1 analog.

Common subcircuit port convention: `p n flag` (ceramic, film, mica: `p n` are the two interchangeable terminals; polarized: `p` = + terminal, `n` = - terminal). The third port `flag` is a behavioral node whose voltage is a bitmask of limit violations, so the simulator's post-processor can read it without re-deriving limits:

| bit value | meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | terminal voltage above the (derated) rating |
| 2 | reverse voltage beyond the allowed reverse value (polarized classes) |
| 4 | peak current above the part limit (`IPK`, inrush/rush) |
| 8 | beyond the surge level; treat the part as failed (tantalum, supercapacitor) |

The flag node is an observation, not a failure model. What the simulator must do on a set bit is stated per class in section 7 of each class. A flag that was never evaluated (analysis not run) is never a pass.

All model parts are written so that setting `ESR` and `ESL` to 0.001 and 1p, `RLK` to 1e12-1e15 and `V0` to 1e6 collapses them to the ideal capacitor (`ideal_components` mode).

Netlist files live in `/home/claude/behavior/bench/cap-<class>/` (`ohm_*.lib` is the subcircuit, `B*.cir` the benches, `results.txt` the captured output). The benches use `.include ohm_xxx.lib`; the product netlist writer must inline the `.subckt` text (the existing `model_fidelity()` in `src/ohmni/eda/simulation.py` already classifies any deck containing `.subckt/.model/.include` as `behavioural_approximation`).

ngspice facts verified while building this group (relevant to the implementer):
- A capacitor defined by charge, `Cb b n q = 'expr(v(b,n))'`, works in op, ac and tran, and its small-signal capacitance is dq/dv (B1 of the ceramic class reproduces it to 1e-6 relative).
- A charge-defined capacitor ignores `.ic` in ngspice 42 (the initial voltage stayed 0). Charge such parts with a source, or use the plain `C` element (which honors `.ic`) when no bias model is needed. All non-ceramic classes here use plain `C` for that reason.
- No XSPICE or special build is needed for anything in this file. Only ordinary B sources, `Cq`, R, L, D, V, I and `.meas` are used.
- `meas ... par('expr')` did not parse in this build for the transient power meas; use a B source that computes the expression and `meas ... avg v(node)`.

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-CAP-CERAMIC

Applies to OHM-021 to OHM-027 (0201, 0402, 0603, 0805, 1206, 1210, 1812 MLCC) and OHM-028 (leaded ceramic disc). One electrical behavior with per-size parasitics.

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
Ceramic capacitors are the default decoupling, bypass, filtering, timing and RF coupling part on a PCB. MLCCs cover about 0.5 pF to tens of uF in chip sizes from 0201 to 1812; Class 1 (C0G/NP0) parts for stable timing, filters and RF, Class 2 (X5R, X7R and, for disc parts, Y5V and similar) for bulk bypass. Typical uses: 100 nF at every IC power pin, 1-22 uF bulk next to regulators, 10-100 pF in oscillators and RF matching, snubbers and EMI filters (1812 for higher voltage). Common series: E6/E12 for Class 1, E3/E6 for Class 2. The leaded disc (OHM-028) is the through-hole equivalent for hand-built boards, ESD and snubber use, and (with a safety rating) line filtering. A disc marked as a Y-class safety capacitor is a mains-safety part and is NOT modeled by this class (see section 7).

### 2. What it is and how it works
An MLCC is a stack of interleaved metal electrodes separated by ceramic dielectric layers, connected in parallel by two end terminations, so C is about eps0*eps_r*A*(n-1)/d. Class 1 dielectric (paraelectric, C0G) has low permittivity and almost no variation with voltage, temperature or time: KEMET quotes 0 +/-30 ppm/C from -55 to 125 C and no aging (S8, S7). Class 2 dielectric is ferroelectric barium titanate: permittivity is 100x higher (more capacitance per volume) but it depends on field, temperature and time (S1, S6). Key behaviors:

- DC bias: as DC field grows, spontaneous polarization saturates and the effective permittivity falls, so capacitance drops with applied voltage; Class 1 does not show this (S1). Loss is larger in smaller parts and at higher fraction of rated voltage (S6). Murata characterizes it from 0 V to rated voltage at 25 C after 60 s (S3) and distributes measured curves (SimSurfing); KEMET K-SIM likewise provides capacitance vs DC voltage plus impedance and ESR vs frequency (S9). Neither publishes a closed-form bias equation in the documents opened, so the equation used here is OHMNI's own fit form (below).
- Temperature: X5R +/-15% over -55 to 85 C (S4, S5), X7R +/-15% over -55 to 125 C (S8). The curve shape inside the envelope is part-specific.
- Aging: Class 2 capacitance decays logarithmically after the last time the part was above the Curie point (about 125 C), -2.5% per decade hour for X5R/X7R, -7% for Y5V, nothing for C0G, and returns after 1.5 h at 150 C, i.e. after reflow (S7). KEMET's high-reliability X7R datasheet quotes about 1.0% per decade hour (S8). Conflict: 2.5 vs 1.0 %/decade hour; the model exposes the rate as a parameter.
- ESR and ESL: ESR is dominated by dielectric loss (DF) and electrode resistance; ESL by the body and terminations, so a chip is a series RLC with a V-shaped impedance curve and a self-resonant frequency (SRF) above which it behaves as an inductor (S6). SRF = 1/(2*pi*sqrt(ESL*C)); at SRF |Z| equals ESR.
- Insulation resistance: very high; KEMET HR rule is 100 Gohm or 1000 Mohm*uF, whichever is less, at 25 C (S8); TDK lists a 50 Mohm minimum for a 10 uF 0805 X5R (S5).
- DF limits (ceilings, not typical values): C0G 0.15% max, X7R 2.5% max (S8); 10% max for the TDK 10 uF X5R (S5).
- Voltage dependence of capacitance also depends on the AC drive level (S10: 64% loss at 500 mVrms versus an additional 4% at 10 mVrms). The model uses a drive-independent small-signal capacitance: a known limitation.
- Piezoelectric effect / microphonics and flex cracking exist for Class 2 parts. No document opened for this group quantifies them, so they are not modeled (RESEARCH_REQUIRED for any acoustic-noise or board-flex feature).

### 3. How it connects
Two interchangeable terminals, non-polarized. In an OHMNI schematic pin 1 and pin 2 are `passive`. Typical circuits: shunt from a supply rail to ground with the part as close to the IC pin as possible; series AC coupling; RC and LC filters; crystal load capacitors. Common mistakes the simulator or checker can catch: using the nameplate capacitance without DC-bias derating on a bulk rail (a 10 uF 10 V 0805 X5R on a 5 V rail keeps only part of its value), choosing a Y5V/Z5U or a 0201 part for a bulk function, putting a high-voltage rail on a low-voltage dielectric (flag bit 1), parallel capacitors of very different values creating an anti-resonance peak (the model reproduces this via ESL), and using a Class 2 part where stability matters (timing, filters).

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
- Layer: L1. Primitives: R, L, charge-defined C (`q=`), B source for the flag. Fidelity: `behavioural_approximation` (ideal_components when parasitics off).
- Subcircuit `ohm_mlcc` in `bench/cap-ceramic/ohm_mlcc.lib` (tested):

```
.subckt ohm_mlcc p n flag params: C0=1u V0=1e6 ESR=5m ESL=0.7n RLK=1e9 VR=10 AGE=0 TCDEV=0
Lesl p a {ESL}
Resr a b {ESR}
Cb b n q = '{C0*(1-AGE)*(1+TCDEV)}*{V0}*atan(v(b,n)/{V0})'
Rlk b n {RLK}
Bflag flag 0 V = 'abs(v(b,n)) > {VR} ? 1 : 0'
.ends
```
- Instance: `X{ref} {pin1} {pin2} {ref}_flag ohm_mlcc C0={value} V0={V0} ESR={esr} ESL={esl} RLK={rlk} VR={vr} AGE={age} TCDEV={tcdev}`
- Bias law: C_eff(V) = C0 / (1 + (V/V0)^2), obtained as the derivative of q = C0*V0*atan(V/V0) (small-signal capacitance in ac, correct charge in tran). V0 is the bias at which capacitance is half the nominal. To fit one datasheet point (bias V1 retains fraction r1 of C0): V0 = V1 / sqrt(1/r1 - 1). This is an OHMNI fit form, not a manufacturer equation; it is smooth and monotonic and is correct near 0 V, but real curves are not exactly this shape (known limitation).
- Fits from the sourced examples (they disagree, and disagree because they are different parts): S2 X5R 100 uF 6.3 V, r1 = 0.90 at 1.8 V gives V0 = 5.4 V (0.86 x VR); S2 Y5V r1 = 0.60 at 1.8 V gives V0 = 2.2 V (0.35 x VR); S10 X5R 1 uF 6.3 V, r1 = 0.36 at 3 V gives V0 = 2.25 V (0.36 x VR). Default for X5R/X7R: V0 = 0.5 x VR (ASSUMPTION, between the two X5R fits). Default for C0G: V0 = 1e6 (no bias). Per-part replacement: read the datasheet or SimSurfing/K-SIM curve and refit.
- Capacitance of a specific 10 uF 0603/0805 X5R part at a given bias: NOT AVAILABLE as numbers from the documents opened (S4 and S5 state that bias graphs exist but do not give text values; the SimSurfing viewer is an interactive tool). RESEARCH_REQUIRED: read the Murata/TDK/Samsung curve for the chosen part and refit V0. Do not present the default as that part's behavior.
- Temperature: `TCDEV` is a fractional deviation applied to C0 and supplied by the simulator per temperature point. Class 1: TCDEV = TC_ppm*1e-6*(T-25). Class 2: use the envelope (+/-0.15) only as a check bound, or the part's curve if available. ngspice `.temp`/`.dc temp` does NOT change it automatically because no temperature parameter is wired to the subcircuit.
- Aging: `AGE` = a * log10(t_hours since last de-aging), a = 0.025 default for X5R/X7R (S7), 0.07 for Y5V (S7), 0.01 as the KEMET HR X7R alternative (S8), 0 for C0G. Default `AGE` = 0 (fresh/reflowed, t about 1 h) for simulations; the realistic-mode UI should expose it.
- ESR: default per entry below (ASSUMPTION L), because the documents opened give DF ceilings only. Conversion from DF: ESR = DF/(2*pi*f*C) at the DF test frequency; this is an upper bound (e.g. 10% DF at 1 kHz on 10 uF is 1.6 ohm, far above real ESR near SRF). Real ESR is frequency dependent (dielectric loss plus skin effect); the constant ESR is a single operating-point approximation. K-SIM/SimSurfing provide measured ESR vs frequency (S9).
- ESL: order-of-magnitude per size (ASSUMPTION L, table in the per-entry sections). SRF = 1/(2*pi*sqrt(ESL*C)); bench B2 verifies that the model reproduces this.
- RLK: R_leak = min(100e9, 1000e6/C_uF) ohm from S8 (high-reliability series rule, M); worst-case floor 50 Mohm from S5.
- Valid analyses: op, dc, ac, tran, noise (ESR thermal noise only). `temp` analysis only if the caller updates TCDEV. Valid range: DC bias magnitude up to VR; frequency up to about 3x SRF (above that the single-L model ignores board/pad parasitics and higher-order modes); small-signal AC drive (the bias law has no AC-amplitude dependence).
- Known limitations: no AC-drive-level dependence of capacitance (S10), no hysteresis or bias history, no piezoelectric noise, no flex-crack failure, constant ESR, one-pole bias law, aging and temperature are scalar inputs, no time evolution of aging during a run.

| RLK | ohm | min(100e9, 1000e6/C_uF) | 50e6 | 100e9 | decades | MFR_DATASHEET (HR series), M | S8, S5 |
| VR | V | per entry | 4 | 3000 | n/a | MFR_DATASHEET | S4, S5, S8 |
| AGE | fraction | 0 | 0 | 0.4 | n/a | MFR_DATASHEET (rate range 1.0-2.5 %/decade h, Y5V 7) | S7, S8 |
| TCDEV | fraction | 0 | -0.82 (Y5V, ASSUMPTION) | +0.22 | n/a | X5R/X7R +/-0.15 sourced (S4, S5, S8); C0G +/-30 ppm/C sourced (S8) | S4, S5, S8 |
| DF (check only) | % | 2.5 (X7R), 10 (X5R TDK), 0.15 (C0G) | | | | MFR_DATASHEET | S5, S8 |

### 6. Ratings and limits
- Rated voltage VR (DC), per part. Check: `abs(v(p,n)) <= VR` (flag bit 1; bench B4). Recommendation (general practice, ASSUMPTION): for Class 2, keep operating voltage to <= 50% of VR on bulk rails because of the bias loss, or use the refit curve.
- Operating temperature: X5R -55 to 85 C (S4, S5); X7R and C0G -55 to 125 C (S8). Check: ambient + self-heating inside range.
- Dielectric withstanding voltage: 250% of VR for 5 s with current limited to 50 mA, a test level for good parts in KEMET's HR series (S8), not a breakdown specification.
- Ripple heating: P = Irms^2 * ESR, with a part-specific temperature-rise-vs-ripple-current graph in TDK/KEMET data (S5, S9). Per-package maximum power is RESEARCH_REQUIRED; check expression: `Irms^2*ESR <= Pmax(size)`.
- Reflow/soldering de-ages the part (S7): after reflow aging restarts at t = 1 h.

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior
| event | physical result | simulator response |
|---|---|---|
| V > VR | dielectric stress rises, life drops; breakdown is a short, sometimes self-clearing at low energy and sometimes permanent | set flag bit 1; report "rating exceeded". For |V| >= 2.5*VR (S8 DWV level; ASSUMPTION that a real part has already failed by here) mark the part failed-short and replace it by a 1 mohm resistor in re-simulation. Permanent |
| Class 2 bias loss | capacitance falls to C_eff(V) | model derating automatically; also post-flag when C_eff/C0 < 0.5 ("bulk capacitance not delivered") |
| temperature outside range | out-of-spec capacitance/ESR, higher failure rate | flag; no state change |
| reverse polarity | not applicable (non-polarized) | none |
| ESD | possible dielectric damage; no sourced value for this group | no model; note only |
| thermal shock or board flex | cracking that can make a short or an intermittent open (general knowledge, not sourced for this group) | not simulated; list as manufacturing/layout rule, RESEARCH_REQUIRED |
| open | cracked termination | not simulated |

### 8. Thermal behavior
Self-heating from ripple: Delta T = Irms^2*ESR*theta, where theta (junction-to-ambient) is size and board dependent and not sourced here. The TDK datasheet carries ripple temperature-rise curves at 100 kHz, 500 kHz and 1 MHz for the 10 uF 0805 part (S5) but with no values in the text. Simple model for the implementer: Delta T = P/(k*A) with A the body area; leave as RESEARCH_REQUIRED and report only P.

### 9. Appearance summary
See the 3D spec entries OHM-021 to OHM-027 and OHM-028. MLCCs are plain unmarked tan to brown blocks with two wrap-around silver/tin end caps; gray ceramic is an OHMNI default for C0G. There is no polarity marking. The disc is a round ceramic disc with two straight tinned leads (spec: Class A, THT, lead diameter 0.5 mm, disc axis along Y).
