## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-CAP-ALEL

Applies to OHM-029 (radial), OHM-030 (SMD can), OHM-031 (snap-in): polarized wet-electrolyte aluminum electrolytic capacitors. Polymer aluminum (OHM-032) is a separate class, BEH-CAP-ALPOLY.

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
High capacitance per volume at low cost for bulk energy storage and low-frequency filtering: input and output bulk capacitors on power supplies and regulators, mains-rectifier reservoir capacitors (snap-in, 200-450 V families), motor-drive and audio coupling. Typical values 1 uF to 100 mF, 6.3 V to 450 V. Radial through-hole (OHM-029) for general boards, SMD V-chip can (OHM-030) for reflow boards, snap-in (OHM-031) for large power boards.

### 2. What it is and how it works
An etched aluminum anode foil carries a thin aluminum-oxide dielectric formed anodically, a paper spacer carries liquid electrolyte, and the cathode foil completes the pair; the wound element sits in an aluminum can with a pressure-relief vent. Equivalent circuit (S12): C, a series resistance ESR (foils, electrolyte, leads), a series inductance L (wound foils and leads), and a parallel resistance r representing the oxide film (leakage). Behaviors with sources:

- Polarity and reverse voltage: the part is polarized; "no reverse voltage or AC voltage" may be applied, and even bipolar types cannot take AC (S11). Physically (S12): low reverse voltage forms an oxide on the cathode foil and the current falls over time; high reverse voltage makes the current rise quickly and generates gas that opens the pressure vent. The cathode foil's own oxide withstands about 1 V (S12).
- Temperature: capacitance rises with temperature and falls when cold; the electrolyte conductivity falls when cold so ESR and tan(delta) rise at low temperature (S12). The extract of S12 was internally inconsistent in wording (it said "decrease sharply at lower temperatures" and "ESR increases significantly" at -25 C); the physics (conductivity falls when cold, ESR rises) is the correct one and is what the model uses. A numeric low-temperature impedance ratio was NOT obtained: the model default of 2x per 20 C below 25 C is an ASSUMPTION (L).
- Leakage: temperature coefficient about 2-3x at 65 C and 3-5x at 85 C relative to 20 C (S12). Leakage rises after storage of more than 2 years; a voltage treatment through a 1 kohm resistor is recommended to restore it (S11). The formula for the maximum leakage current (commonly 0.01*C*V or a few uA) was not found in an opened document, so the default RLK is an ASSUMPTION (L).
- Ripple current and heating: dissipation W = Irms^2 * ESR; temperature rise grows with the square of ripple current (S12). Rating is frequency and temperature dependent: for one 450 V series the 105 C rating of 950 mA at 120 Hz scales to 760 mA at 60 Hz, 1188 mA at 500 Hz, 1330 mA at 1 kHz and 1425 mA at or above 10 kHz, and 1615 mA at 85 C and 1995 mA at 65 C for the same 10,000 h load life (S14). These multipliers are series-specific, not universal.
- Lifetime: Arrhenius; life doubles for each 10 C reduction below the maximum rated temperature (S12), the "10-degree rule": Lx = Lo * 2^((To - Tx)/10) (S13, Bt about 2). Ripple self-heating: dT = (Ix/Io)^2 * dTo, and the combined estimate Lx = Lo * 2^((To-Tx)/10) * 2^(-dT/5) (S13). Example: Lo = 2000 h at 105 C, Tx = 65 C, Ix = Io, dTo = 5 C gives 2000 * 16 * 0.5 = 16000 h.
- Vent: the pressure-relief vent must keep clear space above it: 2 mm for diameters 8-16 mm, 3 mm for 18-35 mm and 5 mm for 40 mm and above (S11 as extracted).
- Series connection needs a balancing resistor across each part (S11).
- Wet electrolytic wear-out is by electrolyte loss: capacitance falls and ESR rises over life (general knowledge; the polymer document S15 states the same for polymer). End-of-life drift is not modeled.

### 3. How it connects
Two pins: + (anode) and - (cathode). In the 3D spec terminal 1 is + at -X, terminal 2 is - at +X for all three entries; the negative side carries a stripe or black band (see 3D spec). Typical circuits: bulk capacitor across a supply rail, + to the more positive rail; output capacitor of a regulator (ESR can matter for regulator stability); RC snubber and coupling only when DC bias can never reverse. Common mistakes: placing it backwards (the footprint's stripe is on the negative lead), exceeding voltage or ripple rating, using it near heat sources (life), forgetting the vent keep-out, using it on an AC node, and paralleling a small ceramic and expecting the electrolytic to filter MHz noise (ESL/ESR limit it).

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
- Layer L1. Primitives: R, L, C, D, V (current sense), B. Fidelity: `behavioural_approximation` (ideal when ESR, ESL, RLK, reverse diode off).
- Subcircuit `ohm_alel` in `bench/cap-alel/ohm_alel.lib` (tested):

```
.subckt ohm_alel p n flag params: C0=100u ESR=0.3 ESL=15n RLK=1meg VR=25 TA=25 TESRK=20 VREVMAX=1 IPK=1e9 DIS=1e-9 DN=4
.param ESRT={ESR*max(1,pow(2,(25-TA)/TESRK))}
Lesl p a {ESL}
Resr a c {ESRT}
Vsns c b 0
Cb b n {C0}
Rlk b n {RLK}
Drev n b dmod
.model dmod D(Is={DIS} N={DN})
Bflag flag 0 V = '(v(b,n) > {VR} ? 1 : 0) + (v(b,n) < -{VREVMAX} ? 2 : 0) + (abs(i(Vsns)) > {IPK} ? 4 : 0)'
.ends
```
- Instance: `X{ref} {p} {n} {ref}_flag ohm_alel C0={value} ESR={esr} ESL={esl} RLK={rleak} VR={vr} TA={tamb} IPK={ipk}`
- ESR(T): ESR*2^((25-TA)/20) for TA below 25 C (ASSUMPTION, L; qualitative direction sourced S12); no reduction is applied above 25 C (conservative; real ESR falls when warm).
- Reverse conduction: diode `dmod` (anode on `n`, cathode on `p`) with Is = 1 nA, N = 4: about 16 uA at 1 V reverse and 0.24 A at 2 V (shape ASSUMED; sourced fact is only that the cathode oxide withstands about 1 V and current then rises quickly, S12). Flag bit 2 sets when reverse voltage exceeds `VREVMAX` = 1 V.
- Leakage: RLK default = 1e8/C_uF ohm (equivalent to a 0.01*C[uF]*V[V] uA rule, ASSUMPTION L). Temperature multiplier from S12 (2-3x at 65 C, 3-5x at 85 C): divide RLK by 2.5 at 65 C and by 4 at 85 C (simulator-side scalar).
- Ripple/life post-check (not in the netlist): `P = Irms^2*ESR`, `dT = (Irms/Irated)^2*dTo`, `L = L0*2^((To-Ta)/10)*2^(-dT/5)`. Rated ripple current Irated, dTo and L0 are datasheet values per part; none are sourced for the generic entry (RESEARCH_REQUIRED per part).
- Valid analyses: op, dc, ac, tran, noise (ESR thermal noise only). Valid range: 0 to VR forward bias, TA -40 to +105 C, f up to about SRF*3. The SRF of the series RLC is typically in the 10 kHz to 1 MHz range for these sizes (computed from the assumed ESL).
- Known limitations: capacitance versus temperature and frequency not modeled (S12 gives direction only); ESR frequency dependence not modeled (ESR is single value); no wear-out drift; ESL assumed; the reverse-conduction diode is a shape, not a measurement; no electrolyte dry-out and venting dynamics.

### 6. Ratings and limits
- Voltage: `v(p,n) <= VR` (flag bit 1); no reverse above 1 V; no AC (S11, S12). Surge rating per part is RESEARCH_REQUIRED.
- Ripple: `Irms(f,T) <= Irated(f,T)`; example scaling in S14 (series-specific).
- Temperature: `Tamb + dT <= To` (105 C common but not universal; per part).
- Life: 10-degree rule with ripple term (S13); example above.
- Vent clearance by can diameter (S11).
- Surge/inrush: not sourced for this wet class; the 10 A rush limit in S11 is for conductive polymer types only and must not be applied here.

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior
| event | physical result | simulator response |
|---|---|---|
| reverse > 1 V | gas generation, vent opens, possible rupture (S11, S12) | flag bit 2; if reverse voltage persists above 1 V for more than the user-set time, mark failed (vent open: treat as open circuit after the event, may short beforehand). Permanent |
| V > VR | oxide degradation, rising leakage, possible vent | flag bit 1; leakage in the diode-free branch is not increased by the model |
| ripple above rating | overheating, life loss | post-check; flag |
| cold temperature | ESR rises (assumed 2x per 20 C below 25 C), capacitance falls | scale ESR via TA |
| stored more than 2 years | leakage up (S11) | note; no automatic action |
| open / dry-out | capacitance falls, ESR rises over life | not modeled |

### 8. Thermal behavior
Self-heating dT = (Irms/Irated)^2 * dTo with dTo from the datasheet (S13); P = Irms^2*ESR (S12). Life accelerates 2x per 10 C and an additional 2x per 5 C of ripple rise (S13, formula 17 weights core rise double). Because heating is concentrated in the core, the simulator should report both P and the computed life.

### 9. Appearance summary
See 3D spec OHM-029, OHM-030, OHM-031. Cylindrical aluminum can in a colored sleeve with a negative stripe band and a scored top vent. Radial: two leads, + at -X; SMD: base plate with flat terminals and chamfered corners marking +; snap-in: two pins on 10 mm pitch (2-pin default), minus band on the +X side.

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-CAP-ALPOLY

Applies to OHM-032 (polymer electrolytic: Style A SMD can default, Style B radial through-hole). Aluminum conductive-polymer and hybrid capacitors. Molded polymer tantalum (POSCAP/SP-Cap, T543-type) are NOT this entry (3D spec note) and are covered by BEH-CAP-TANT parameters only if the user selects the polymer type.

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
Low-ESR bulk capacitance for switching-regulator outputs, CPU/FPGA core rails, point-of-load filtering and long-life power rails; replaces wet electrolytic where ESR, ripple current and life matter. Common 2.5-25 V, 10-1000 uF. Style A (SMD can, same outline as OHM-030) and Style B (radial OS-CON-like leaded can).

### 2. What it is and how it works
Same wound or stacked aluminum foil structure as OHM-029/030 but with a solid conductive polymer (or polymer plus a little liquid in hybrids) as cathode in place of liquid electrolyte. Consequences with sources:
- Life rule differs: Lx = Lo * 10^((To - Tx)/20), i.e. 10x per 20 C, and the Vishay OS-CON document says polymer life can be calculated without ripple self-heating (S15). This conflicts with the wet-electrolyte rule (2x per 10 C, ripple term), so the model carries the two rules separately. Example from S15: 105 C / 2000 h converts to about 63,245 h at 75 C (10^(30/20) = 31.6; 2000*31.6 = 63,245). The estimate is capped at 15 years (S15).
- Failure mode: wear-out is open mode; capacitance decreases (S15).
- Rush current: Nichicon cautions that conductive-polymer types subjected to drastic charge and discharge may short or leak and says not to apply rush current above 10 A (S11).
- Polarity: polarized; Panasonic radial OS-CON shows a negative marking (3D spec gap-fill; that document was not opened for this task, so treat as from the 3D spec only).
- ESR is low (tens of mohm); a numeric ESR for aluminum polymer was not found in an opened document (the 9-100 mohm at 100 kHz in S19 is for tantalum polymer T543). ESR and ESL defaults are ASSUMPTIONS.
- Voltage derating: S17 gives 20% (above 10 V) and 10% (at or below 10 V) derating for tantalum polymer and covers "Al-Polymer" in its title, but the Al-polymer specifics were not captured in the extract. Use 20%/10% as a conservative assumption (L) until a polymer-aluminum datasheet is read.
- Reverse voltage: not sourced for aluminum polymer; treated as zero allowance (flag any reverse above 0.1 V; ASSUMPTION, conservative).

### 3. How it connects
Two pins, + and -. 3D spec Style A: pin 1 (+) at -X, pin 2 (-) at +X; Style B: pin 1 (+) at (-1.25, 0), pin 2 (-) at +1.25 mm (2.5 mm pitch). Used on regulator outputs/inputs next to ceramic caps. Mistakes: reverse polarity; large inrush into an uncharged polymer cap from a stiff source (limit rush to about 10 A per S11 guidance or the datasheet); exceeding derated voltage; assuming the same 10-degree life rule as a wet electrolytic.

### 4. Electrical model
- Layer L1; primitives R, L, C, V (sense), B; fidelity `behavioural_approximation`.
- Subcircuit `ohm_alpoly` in `bench/cap-alpoly/ohm_alpoly.lib` (tested):

```
.subckt ohm_alpoly p n flag params: C0=100u ESR=20m ESL=5n RLK=1meg VR=16 DER=0.8 VREVMAX=0.1 IPK=10
Lesl p a {ESL}
Resr a c {ESR}
Vsns c b 0
Cb b n {C0}
Rlk b n {RLK}
Bflag flag 0 V = '(v(b,n) > {VR*DER} ? 1 : 0) + (v(b,n) < -{VREVMAX} ? 2 : 0) + (abs(i(Vsns)) > {IPK} ? 4 : 0)'
.ends
```
- Instance: `X{ref} {p} {n} {ref}_flag ohm_alpoly C0={value} ESR={esr} ESL={esl} RLK={rleak} VR={vr} DER={der} IPK={ipk}`
- Post-checks (outside netlist): life `Lx = Lo*10^((To-Tx)/20)` (S15), capped at 15 years (S15); ripple `P = Irms^2*ESR`.
- Valid analyses: op, dc, ac, tran, noise. Valid range: 0 to VR*DER forward, TA about -55 to +105 C (per part).
- Limitations: all numeric defaults are assumptions; no ESR(T); no wear-out drift; inrush limit is a guideline, not a physical limit of the part model.

### 5. Parameters table
| name | unit | default | min | max | tolerance | basis | source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C0 | F | 100 uF | 10 uF | 1000 uF | +/-20% typ. (not sourced) | ASSUMPTION, L | none |
| ESR | ohm | 0.02 | 0.005 | 0.1 | factor 2 | ASSUMPTION, L | S19 (tantalum polymer range as context only) |
| ESL | H | 5 nH | 2 nH | 15 nH | factor 2 | ASSUMPTION, L | none |
| RLK | ohm | 1e6 | 1e4 | 1e9 | decades | ASSUMPTION, L | none |
| VR | V | 16 | 2.5 | 25 | n/a | MFR_DATASHEET per part | none opened |
| DER | fraction | 0.8 (VR > 10 V), 0.9 (VR <= 10 V) | 0.5 | 1.0 | n/a | CONSENSUS (S17 20%/10%, S19 80%/90% for tantalum polymer) | S17, S19 |
| VREVMAX | V | 0.1 | 0 | 0.5 | n/a | ASSUMPTION, L | none |
| IPK | A | 10 | 1 | 100 | n/a | MFR (Nichicon guideline for polymer) | S11 |

### 6. Ratings and limits
`v(p,n) <= VR*DER`; `v(p,n) >= -VREVMAX`; `|i| <= IPK` (rush, peak, from S11); life `Lx = Lo*10^((To-Tx)/20)`, at most 15 years (S15); `P = Irms^2*ESR <= Pmax` (Pmax per part, RESEARCH_REQUIRED).

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior
| event | physical result | simulator response |
|---|---|---|
| rush current > 10 A | short or leakage rise (S11) | flag bit 4; recommend series resistance or soft start |
| V above derated voltage | accelerated failure; polymer failure is benign compared to MnO2 in tantalum (S19), not stated for Al polymer | flag bit 1 |
| reverse voltage | not sourced; assume damage | flag bit 2; permanent |
| wear-out | open mode, capacitance decrease (S15) | not modeled; life estimate only |
| over-temperature | life loss (10x per 20 C) | post-check |

### 8. Thermal behavior
Power P = Irms^2*ESR; per S15 the polymer life estimate ignores ripple self-heating, but a conservative implementer may still report P and the computed temperature rise if the part's thermal resistance is known (not sourced).

### 9. Appearance summary
See 3D spec OHM-032. Style A (default): aluminum can on a flat base plate with chamfered + corners and a dark negative band; Style B: radial can with a negative stripe. OHMNI default marks negative at +X.

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-CAP-TANT

Applies to OHM-033, OHM-034, OHM-035, OHM-036 (tantalum molded chip cases A, B, C, D). A `type` parameter selects MnO2 cathode (default, conservative) or conductive-polymer cathode.

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
Compact, stable bulk capacitance with moderate ESR in a small SMD body: rail bypass, hold-up, filtering where ceramic DC-bias loss or wet-electrolytic size is a problem; common in industrial and medical designs. Typical 1-470 uF, 4-50 V. Case A to D = EIA 3216-18, 3528-21, 6032-28, 7343-31 (3D spec).

### 2. What it is and how it works
Sintered tantalum powder anode with a Ta2O5 dielectric formed on it, a cathode of manganese dioxide (MnO2) or conductive polymer, carbon/silver counter electrode, molded epoxy body, anode marked by a stripe and bevel. Behaviors with sources:
- Derating: KEMET recommends 50% derating (operate at most half of rated voltage) for MnO2 and 20% for polymer, i.e. 80% of VR (S16); S17 refines polymer to 20% for VR above 10 V and 10% for VR at or below 10 V; the T543 datasheet states steady-state 90% (VR <= 10 V) and 80% (VR > 10 V) (S19). Sourced numbers: MnO2 at 50% VR 13 ppm mean failure rate (S16), polymer at 80% VR 11 ppm (S16); in surge testing MnO2 reaches 100 ppm at 68% VR (S17).
- Failure mechanism: stress-induced cracking of the dielectric (wedge areas where tantalum particles converge); MnO2 is hard and brittle, polymer is soft and elastic and absorbs thermal-expansion mismatch (S16, S17).
- Ignition: with MnO2, a fault site heats and the MnO2 converts to a higher-resistance compound (self-healing); when current is not limited the process runs away, a "catastrophic, or ignition type of failure" (S18). Polymer parts have a "benign failure mode which eliminates the ignition failures" (S19).
- Surge/inrush: power-on failures dominate; surge voltage tests at 1.32 x VR, larger cases are surge-current tested at 75% of VR (commercial) or 100% of VR (power-supply grade) (S18). A series resistance or soft start is the usual mitigation (S18 recommends a safety margin on first power application).
- Reflow stress: dielectric cracks form when cooling after soldering (S18; time above 180 C should stay below 90 s).
- Reverse voltage: polarized; "may be permanently damaged or destroyed" if connected with wrong polarity; the T543 transient reverse allowance is 15% of VR at 25 C down to 3% of VR at 105 C (S19, as extracted; verify). This allowance is for transient reverse spikes, not for operation.
- ESR: T543 polymer 9-100 mohm at 100 kHz depending on rating (S19). MnO2 ESR numbers were not found in an opened document (typically higher; RESEARCH_REQUIRED). Leakage max <= 0.1 CV (uA with C in uF and V in volts) after 5 min at VR for T543 (S19).
- Ripple: I(max) = sqrt(Pmax/ESR) (S19), with power multipliers 1.0 up to 45 C falling to 0.25 above 85 C (S19). Per-case Pmax values were not captured: RESEARCH_REQUIRED.

### 3. How it connects
Two pins: anode (+) and cathode (-). 3D spec: pin 1 anode at -X marked with a stripe and bevel; pin 2 cathode at +X. IMPORTANT: on tantalum chips the stripe marks the ANODE (+), the opposite of aluminum cans. Some EDA footprints mark the cathode instead (3D spec warning): the checker must verify the footprint stripe corresponds to pin 1 (+). Typical use: rail bypass at a regulator, with the capacitor on a rail whose voltage is below the derated limit and whose source has current limiting or soft start. Mistakes: placing it backward (it can fail short and ignite for MnO2), operating at 100% of VR, hot-plugging a low-impedance supply, and using MnO2 parts across a stiff battery without a series resistor.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
- Layer L1; primitives R, L, C, V (sense), B; fidelity `behavioural_approximation`.
- Subcircuit `ohm_tant` in `bench/cap-tant/ohm_tant.lib` (tested):

```
.subckt ohm_tant p n flag params: C0=100u ESR=0.1 ESL=2.5n RLK=100k VR=16 DER=0.5 VREVFR=0.03 IPK=1e9
Lesl p a {ESL}
Resr a c {ESR}
Vsns c b 0
Cb b n {C0}
Rlk b n {RLK}
Bflag flag 0 V = '(v(b,n) > {VR*DER} ? 1 : 0) + (v(b,n) < -{VREVFR*VR} ? 2 : 0) + (abs(i(Vsns)) > {IPK} ? 4 : 0) + (v(b,n) > {1.32*VR} ? 8 : 0)'
.ends
```
- Instance: `X{ref} {anode} {cathode} {ref}_flag ohm_tant C0={value} ESR={esr} ESL={esl} RLK={rleak} VR={vr} DER={der} VREVFR=0.03 IPK={ipk}`
- RLK: RLK = 1/(LKF*1e-6*C_uF) with LKF = 0.1 (T543 maximum leakage, S19) gives the conservative (leaky) upper bound; typical parts leak far less, so offer LKF 0.1 (max, default), lower values as user input. Bench B1 verifies the mapping (5 V on 100 uF: 50 uA).
- Flag semantics: bit 1 = V above DER*VR (MnO2 0.5, polymer 0.8 above 10 V or 0.9 at or below 10 V); bit 2 = reverse above 3% of VR (the lowest allowance in S19, conservative); bit 4 = peak current above `IPK` (user-set; the default is disabled because no sourced inrush limit exists for the generic entry); bit 8 = V above 1.32*VR, the KEMET surge-test level (S18); the part must be treated as failed.
- Valid analyses: op, dc, ac, tran, noise. Valid range: 0 to DER*VR forward, -55 to +105 C (T543; MnO2 range per part).
- Known limitations: no MnO2 ignition dynamics (flag only); no capacitance vs temperature or frequency; ESR(f) not modeled (single value); ESR defaults for MnO2 are assumptions; reverse allowance is conservative (not a rated operating condition); surge failure is statistical and not reproduced.

### 5. Parameters table
| name | unit | default | min | max | tolerance | basis | source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C0 | F | per entry | 1 uF | 1000 uF | +/-20% typical (not sourced) | ASSUMPTION, L | none |
| ESR | ohm | per entry (MnO2); 0.009-0.1 at 100 kHz (polymer) | 0.009 | 5 | factor 2 | ASSUMPTION (MnO2), MFR_DATASHEET (polymer range) | S19 |
| ESL | H | 2.5 nH | 1 nH | 5 nH | factor 2 | ASSUMPTION, L | none |
| RLK | ohm | 1e7/C_uF (LKF 0.1) | 1e3 | 1e9 | decades | MFR_DATASHEET (max leakage T543), M | S19 |
| VR | V | 16 | 4 | 50 | n/a | MFR_DATASHEET per part | S19 |
| DER | fraction | 0.5 (MnO2); 0.8 (polymer VR>10 V); 0.9 (polymer VR<=10 V) | 0.5 | 0.9 | n/a | CONSENSUS (S16, S17, S19) | S16, S17, S19 |
| VREVFR | fraction of VR | 0.03 | 0.0 | 0.15 | n/a | MFR_DATASHEET (T543 transient reverse 3-15%) | S19 |
| surge level | x VR | 1.32 | | | n/a | MFR_DATASHEET (KEMET surge test) | S18 |

### 6. Ratings and limits
- Voltage: `v(p,n) <= DER*VR` operating; `v(p,n) <= 1.32*VR` is the surge test level and not an operating allowance.
- Reverse: transient only, at most 3-15% of VR depending on temperature (S19); steady reverse is not allowed.
- Inrush: `|i| <= Isurge(part)`; the surge-current test levels are 75% or 100% of VR with defined source resistance (S18); per-part limit RESEARCH_REQUIRED.
- Ripple: `Irms <= sqrt(Pmax*k(T)/ESR)`, k from S19 (1.0 at or below 45 C, 0.25 above 85 C; intermediate values not captured).
- Temperature: -55 to +105 C for T543 polymer (S19).

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior
| event | physical result | simulator response |
|---|---|---|
| V above derated (but below VR) | rising failure rate (13 ppm at 50% VR MnO2 baseline, S16) | flag bit 1 |
| V above 1.32*VR | beyond KEMET surge test | flag bit 8; mark failed short (replace with 10 mohm); if type = MnO2 and the source can supply more than the self-healing current, raise "ignition risk: yes" (S18; permanent) |
| inrush from stiff source | power-on dielectric failure, short; MnO2 may ignite (S18) | flag bit 4 (when IPK set); permanent |
| reverse polarity | permanent damage, short (S19) | flag bit 2; mark failed short (10 mohm) and raise ignition risk for MnO2; permanent |
| polymer type failure | benign, no ignition (S19) | no ignition flag |
| over-temperature | derate power, life loss | post-check against S19 multipliers |
| open | rare | not modeled |

### 8. Thermal behavior
P = Irms^2*ESR; allowed dissipation scales with ambient temperature as 1.0 up to 45 C and 0.25 above 85 C (S19 multipliers). Self-heating beyond P is not modeled.

### 9. Appearance summary
See 3D spec OHM-033 to OHM-036. Rectangular molded epoxy body (3.2x1.6, 3.5x2.8, 6.0x3.2, 7.3x4.3 mm per case), flat tin terminals wrapping the ends, anode end marked with a stripe and bevel at -X.

| B2 | B2.cir | derating and surge flags, VR=16, DER=0.5, ramp 1 V/s | bit 1 edge at 8 V; bit 8 edge at 1.32*16 = 21.12 V; value 9 above both | 0.05 V | flag 0 at 7 V, 1 at 10 V, 9 at 23 V; edges at 7.998 V and 21.122 V: match |
| B3 | B3.cir | reverse flag, VREVFR = 0.03 of VR=16 | bit 2 at v < -0.48 V | 0.02 V | flag 0 at 0.2 V, 2 at 1 V reverse; edge at 0.4799 V: match |

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-CAP-FILM

Applies to OHM-037 (film box capacitor) and OHM-038 (X2 safety capacitor). Metallized film, non-polarized. X2 uses the same electrical model with a mains-rated peak-voltage check and an extra safety section.

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
Stable, low-loss, self-healing capacitors for audio coupling and timing (MKT/MKS polyester, polypropylene), filters, snubbers, motor-run and power-factor duties, and for across-the-line EMI suppression (X2). X2 capacitors sit across line and neutral behind a mains input to attenuate differential-mode noise. Typical values: 1 nF to 10 uF (box), 1 nF to a few uF (X2), pitch 7.5 to 27.5 mm.

### 2. What it is and how it works
Plastic film dielectric (polyester/PET, polypropylene/PP, PPS in SMD) with a vacuum-deposited metal layer as electrode ("metallized"), wound or stacked, leaded and resin-encapsulated in a box. Behaviors with sources:
- Self-healing: a local dielectric breakdown vaporizes the thin metal around the fault and clears it, with only a tiny capacitance loss (S20, S21). Not modeled as an event beyond the flag.
- Loss: tan(delta) for WIMA MKP-X2 at 20 C is 10-30e-4 at 1 kHz, 20-60e-4 at 10 kHz and 90e-4 at 100 kHz depending on capacitance (S20), so ESR = tan(delta)/(2*pi*f*C) falls with frequency (for 1 uF with 20e-4 at 1 kHz: 0.318 ohm; with 90e-4 at 100 kHz: 14 mohm). A single ESR equals the 1 kHz value and over-estimates loss at high frequency: a known limitation.
- Insulation resistance: 15,000 Mohm for C of 0.33 uF or less, and 5000 s (as extracted: MOhm times uF) above (S20).
- Voltage: MKP-X2 rated 275 VAC (250 VAC certified), 305 VAC version available; test voltages 1800 VDC for 2 s (C of 1.0 uF or less) and 2260 VDC for 2 s (C above 1.0 uF) per the extract (S20). Operating range -55 to +105 C (S20). Reliability: 2 fit, 300,000 h at the conditions stated in the datasheet (S20, S21 0.5 x Ur at 40 C for the SMD series).
- Temperature coefficient: PPS is "very constant" (S21); PET and PP coefficients were not captured, so no TC is modeled (RESEARCH_REQUIRED).
- Pulse rating: S20 gives a pulse rise-time limit for 2 x 275 VAC = 390 V pulses; the unit in the extract was garbled ("100 V/msec"), so it is not used. RESEARCH_REQUIRED.
- X2 classification: WIMA labels this part Class X2 (S20). The definition of the X2 class and its test voltages and overvoltage categories come from IEC 60384-14, which was not opened for this group, so the class definition is not reproduced here (RESEARCH_REQUIRED). Do not treat the OHMNI X2 entry as certified.
- Z/lead inductance: through-hole leads and a long body add inductance that grows with pitch (assumed here at 15 nH default, ASSUMPTION L).

### 3. How it connects
Two interchangeable terminals, non-polarized. Typical: audio coupling, decoupling in power-electronics (with ceramic), snubber across a switch, and for X2: line to neutral across the mains input after the fuse and before or inside the EMI filter (a standard filter topology; use with a bleeder, see section 7). Mistakes: using a non-safety box capacitor across mains, exceeding AC rating (X2 275 VAC is rms; the peak is 389 V), using a high-dV/dt duty without checking the pulse rating, leaving X2 without a discharge path.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
- Layer L1; primitives R, L, C, B; fidelity `behavioural_approximation`.
- Subcircuit `ohm_film` in `bench/cap-film/ohm_film.lib` (tested):

```
.subckt ohm_film p n flag params: C0=1u TAND=20e-4 FREF=1k ESL=15n RLK=15g VRPK=388.9
.param ESRV={TAND/(2*3.14159265358979*FREF*C0)}
Lesl p a {ESL}
Resr a b {ESRV}
Cb b n {C0}
Rlk b n {RLK}
Bflag flag 0 V = 'abs(v(b,n)) > {VRPK} ? 1 : 0'
.ends
```
- Instance: `X{ref} {pin1} {pin2} {ref}_flag ohm_film C0={value} TAND={tand} FREF=1k ESL={esl} RLK={rleak} VRPK={vrpk}`
- X2 defaults: `VRPK = 275*sqrt(2) = 388.9 V` (peak of 275 VAC rms, conservative for AC use; the DC rating of an X2 part is RESEARCH_REQUIRED). The AC rating is an rms value; a DC-biased X2 must use the datasheet's DC rating, not this peak.
- RLK default: IR = 15,000 Mohm for C of 0.33 uF or less; for larger C use 5000 Mohm*uF / C_uF (S20 as extracted).
- Valid analyses: op, dc, ac, tran, noise. Valid range: |V| below VRPK, f up to 3x SRF, -55 to +105 C (S20 range).
- Known limitations: constant ESR (tan(delta) rises with frequency in reality), no temperature or voltage dependence of C, no self-healing event, no dV/dt limit, ESL assumed, no humidity effects.

### 5. Parameters table
| name | unit | default | min | max | tolerance | basis | source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C0 | F | 100 nF | 1 nF | 10 uF | +/-5%, +/-10%, +/-20% by code (not sourced) | ASSUMPTION, L | S20 range as context |
| TAND (at FREF) | none | 20e-4 at 1 kHz | 10e-4 | 60e-4 | per part | MFR_DATASHEET | S20 |
| ESL | H | 15 nH (pitch 15 mm), 10 nH (pitch 10 mm) | 5 nH | 40 nH | factor 2 | ASSUMPTION, L | none |
| RLK | ohm | 15e9 | 1e9 | 1e12 | decades | MFR_DATASHEET (IR) | S20 |
| VRPK | V | box: 100 V peak (ASSUMPTION); X2: 388.9 | 63 | 1000 (S21 SMD range 63-1000 VDC) | n/a | MFR_DATASHEET (X2), ASSUMPTION (box) | S20, S21 |
| temperature range | C | -55..+105 (X2 PP) | | | n/a | MFR_DATASHEET | S20 |

### 6. Ratings and limits
- Peak voltage: `abs(v(p,n)) <= VRPK` (flag bit 1; bench B3). For X2: `Vrms <= 275` and `Vpeak <= 389` for AC; combined AC plus DC limits per datasheet.
- Test voltage (production): 1800 VDC or 2260 VDC for 2 s (S20): not an operating rating.
- Temperature: `Tamb <= 105 C` (X2 PP, S20).
- Pulse/dV-dt: RESEARCH_REQUIRED.

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior
| event | physical result | simulator response |
|---|---|---|
| overvoltage | dielectric breakdown, self-heals at small energy; large energy or repeated events cause permanent capacitance loss or a short | flag bit 1; no capacitance degradation in the model |
| X2 across mains with no bleeder | stored charge up to 0.5*C*Vpeak^2 (75.6 mJ for 1 uF at 389 V) remains on the terminals after unplugging; the required discharge rules come from the safety standard that was not opened for this group (RESEARCH_REQUIRED). Hazard statement: do not assume an X2 capacitor is discharged | when an X2 is across a mains source, require a discharge path in the checker (design rule) |
| non-safety box capacitor across mains | failure may be unsafe (short or fire), no safety approval | checker rule: forbid OHM-037 across mains |
| X2 end-of-life | self-healing capacitance loss (S20); failure behavior in the standard is not summarized here | note only |
| high dV/dt | local heating, internal contact damage | RESEARCH_REQUIRED |

### 8. Thermal behavior
P = Irms^2*ESR with ESR from tan(delta) at the working frequency (the model's single ESR will mis-estimate it). Per-part rise vs ripple current not sourced.

### 9. Appearance summary
See 3D spec OHM-037 and OHM-038. Rectangular resin-filled plastic box, two straight round leads (pitch 10 mm default for box, 15 mm default for X2), no polarity marking.

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-CAP-MICA

Applies to OHM-039 (dipped silver mica, CD15 row).

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
Very stable, low-loss, low-drift small capacitors for RF tuning, oscillators, filters, high-voltage coupling and timing. Values from about 1 pF to a few nF, voltage ratings from 100 Vdc to 2500 Vdc across CDE types (S22).

### 2. What it is and how it works
Thin mica sheets coated with silver electrodes, dipped in epoxy; the mica dielectric has stable permittivity, so capacitance changes only by tens of ppm per degree and does not age like Class 2 ceramic. CDE's dipped mica characteristic codes (S22): code C: -200 to +200 ppm/C for 1-18 pF; code E: -20 to +100 ppm/C for 20-82 pF; code F: 0 to +70 ppm/C for 91 pF and up (with tolerance bands on capacitance drift of +/-(0.5% + 0.1 pF), +/-(0.1% + 0.1 pF), +/-(0.05% + 0.1 pF) respectively). Tolerance codes from +/-1/2 pF (D) to +/-5% (J) (S22). Temperature range -55 to +125 C, with a +150 C option for the CD10/15/19/30/42 types (S22). Dielectric withstand test 200% of rated voltage (S22). Q, dissipation factor and insulation resistance values are NOT in the opened document (RESEARCH_REQUIRED); the CDE web page only calls mica "high Q" with no numbers. Mica has no DC-bias derating (a general property of Class-1-like dielectrics; not shown by a number in the opened documents, S22 gives no voltage dependence).

### 3. How it connects
Two interchangeable leads, non-polarized (3D spec: pin 1 at -X). Typical circuits: LC tank and oscillator tuning, RF coupling/bypass, HV snubbing. Mistakes: ignoring the rated voltage (DC plus RF peak) and the RF current limit (heating); assuming mica has Class 2 behavior; ignoring lead inductance at VHF.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
- Layer L1; primitives R, L, C, B; fidelity `behavioural_approximation`.
- Subcircuit `ohm_mica` in `bench/cap-mica/ohm_mica.lib` (tested):

```
.subckt ohm_mica p n flag params: C0=100p TCPPM=0 TEMP=25 Q=1000 FQ=1meg ESL=8n RLK=1e12 VR=500
.param CT={C0*(1+TCPPM*1e-6*(TEMP-25))}
.param ESRV={1/(Q*2*3.14159265358979*FQ*C0)}
Lesl p a {ESL}
Resr a b {ESRV}
Cb b n {CT}
Rlk b n {RLK}
Bflag flag 0 V = 'abs(v(b,n)) > {VR} ? 1 : 0'
.ends
```
- Instance: `X{ref} {pin1} {pin2} {ref}_flag ohm_mica C0={value} TCPPM={tc} TEMP={temp} Q=1000 FQ=1meg ESL={esl} RLK={rleak} VR={vr}`
- TCPPM default: +35 ppm/C (DERIVED, midpoint of the CDE code F band 0 to +70); use code C/E bands for small values. The tolerance and the code-specific drift term are kept as user inputs.
- Q: default 1000 at 1 MHz (ASSUMPTION L; only qualitative "high Q" sourced). ESL default 8 nH (ASSUMPTION L, dipped lead length).
- Valid analyses: op, dc, ac, tran, noise. Valid range: |V| below VR, -55 to +125 C, f up to 3x SRF (above about 100 MHz for the defaults).
- Known limitations: Q frequency dependence not modeled; temperature coefficient assumed linear; no voltage dependence; no failure other than the flag.

| C0 | F | 100 pF | 1 pF | 5 nF | +/-5% (J) default; D, C, E, F, G codes | MFR_DATASHEET (code table) | S22 |

### 6. Ratings and limits
`abs(v(p,n)) <= VR` (flag bit 1, DC plus AC peak); temperature -55 to +125 C (+150 C only for options P on CD10/15/19/30/42, S22); DWV test 200% of VR (a production test). RF current rating: RESEARCH_REQUIRED.

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior

| out of temperature range | drift beyond coefficient; solder or epoxy stress | flag |

### 8. Thermal behavior
P = Irms^2*ESR with ESR from Q; no thermal resistance sourced.

### 9. Appearance summary
See 3D spec OHM-039. A flat, rounded epoxy-dipped slab (CD15 row) with two straight leads exiting the bottom edge; no polarity.

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-CAP-EDLC

Applies to OHM-040 (supercapacitor, electric double-layer capacitor, radial can default; PB stacked pack and coin variants noted in the 3D spec are not electrically characterized here).

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
Energy storage between capacitors and batteries: memory/RTC backup, ride-through of short outages, peak-current assist for pulse loads (radio bursts, motors), energy harvesting buffers. Cells are rated about 2.5-3 V (S23, S24); higher voltages need series strings with balancing. Capacitance spans millifarads to hundreds of farads (S24 shows 3 F, 10 F, 110 F HB parts).

### 2. What it is and how it works
Two activated-carbon electrodes in an organic electrolyte store charge in the electric double layer; capacitance is large but the cell voltage is limited by electrolyte stability (2.5 V standard, S23/S24). Behaviors with sources:
- ESR: DC ESR 0.020 to 0.160 ohm for Eaton HB 3-110 F parts (S24), measured per IEC 62391-1 at 20 C. ESR rises with age (end-of-life ESR increase) and rises temporarily when cold (viscosity), and permanently at high temperature (S23).
- Leakage and self-discharge: 7 to 180 uA nominal for HB parts after a 72 h charge (S24); realistic leakage measurement needs more than 100 hours of charging, and leakage rises with temperature (S23). Leakage decays with time (exponential charging tail) and varies strongly between nominally identical cells (S25).
- Voltage: 2.5 V maximum working, 2.8 V surge (S24), 3 V surge in the guidelines (S23); conflicting surge numbers (2.8 V HB datasheet vs 3 V application note), the conservative 2.8 V is used.
- Temperature and life: standard range -25 to +70 C; +85 C with derating to 2.3 V (S24, HB, linear) versus 1.8 V per capacitor at +85 C (S23); these conflict, so the model uses the lower value until the series is known. Life is halved by each +10 C rise (S23), and HB life limits are at most 30% capacitance change and 200% ESR increase after 1000 h at 70 C, 2.5 V (S24).
- Capacitance tolerance -10% to +30% at 20 C for HB (S24).
- Series connection: because capacitance tolerance and leakage differ, voltages divide unequally. S23 gives the example of two 1 F capacitors with +/-20% spread at 5 V total, one receiving 3 V. Passive balancing resistors should carry at least 50x the worst-case leakage current (S23), typical 3.3-22 kohm; active balancing is preferred for frequent cycling (S23, S25). Overcharge damages cells (S23, S25).
- Hazard: venting or rupture if overcharged, reverse-charged or heated above 150 C; high case temperature (S23). Stored energy E = 0.5*C*V^2 and short-circuit current V/ESR are large (e.g. 31 J and 119 A for a 10 F, 2.5 V, 20 mohm cell into 1 mohm).

### 3. How it connects
Polarized: + and -. 3D spec: pin 1 (+) at -X, pin 2 (-) at +X; the negative lead carries the vent/polarity indicator for AVX SCC and, per the 3D spec, a stripe; the longer lead is positive per Eaton (S24). Typical circuits: across a 2.5 V rail through a charge-limiting resistor or current-limited source; diode-OR backup for RTC; series strings with balancing resistors or active balancers. Mistakes: charging from a stiff source (inrush limited only by ESR), series strings without balancing, operating above rated voltage, reversing polarity, using at +85 C without derating, and ignoring that a shorted terminal can deliver a large current.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
- Layer L1; primitives R, C, B; fidelity `behavioural_approximation`.
- Subcircuit `ohm_edlc` in `bench/cap-edlc/ohm_edlc.lib` (tested):

```
.subckt ohm_edlc p n flag params: C0=10 ESR=0.02 RLK=125k VR=2.5 VSURGE=2.8
Resr p b {ESR}
Cb b n {C0}
Rlk b n {RLK}
Bflag flag 0 V = '(v(b,n) > {VR} ? 1 : 0) + (v(b,n) < -0.01 ? 2 : 0) + (v(b,n) > {VSURGE} ? 8 : 0)'
.ends
```
- Instance: `X{ref} {p} {n} {ref}_flag ohm_edlc C0={value} ESR={esr} RLK={rleak} VR={vr} VSURGE={vsurge}`
- RLK: from the datasheet leakage at rated voltage: RLK = VR / I_leak (per part). Default I_leak = 20 uA at 2.5 V gives 125 kohm (ASSUMPTION L, inside the 7-180 uA range of S24), time constant 10 F * 125 kohm = 1.25e6 s (14.5 days). Leakage is not constant in reality (decays with charging time and rises with temperature); the single resistor represents a settled value.
- Valid analyses: op, dc, ac, tran. Valid range: 0 to VR, -25 to +70 C (HB standard). Charging-redistribution and frequency-dependent capacitance (real EDLC capacitance falls at high frequency) are not modeled.
- Known limitations: no multi-branch (redistribution) model, no C(f), no C(T), no ESR(T), no aging; leakage is a single resistor.

### 6. Ratings and limits
- Voltage: `v(p,n) <= VR`; surge `v(p,n) <= VSURGE` (momentary); strings: each cell `<= VR` (balancing check).
- Reverse: not allowed (S23, S24); flag at -10 mV.
- Temperature and derating: `V <= 2.5 V` up to 70 C; at 85 C `V <= 1.8 V` (S23, conservative) or 2.3 V (HB, S24).
- Life: halves per +10 C (S23).
- Balancing: `I_balance >= 50 * I_leak_worst` (S23), with `R_balance` about 3.3-22 kohm in S23's guidance for the example product.

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior
| event | physical result | simulator response |
|---|---|---|
| V above VR | accelerated degradation, gas generation | flag bit 1 |
| V above surge | damage, vent or rupture possible (S23) | flag bit 8; mark failed |
| reverse voltage | venting or rupture (S23) | flag bit 2; permanent |
| hard short | peak current V/ESR; stored energy 0.5*C*V^2 | report peak and energy; hazard note (high current, burn, arcing) |
| temperature above 150 C | venting or rupture (S23) | flag |
| end of life | ESR up (up to 200% in S24 limits) and C down (30%) | not modeled; ESR and C0 multipliers available as user parameters |
| series imbalance | one cell over voltage | flag bit 1 or 8 on the weak cell (bench B2) |

### 8. Thermal behavior
Self-heating P = Irms^2*ESR is small except in pulse duty; the life model (half per +10 C, S23) is evaluated at ambient plus rise.

### 9. Appearance summary
See 3D spec OHM-040. A radial cylindrical can (OHMNI default placeholder) with two leads, 5.0 mm pitch for 10 mm diameter, the negative lead carrying a vent/polarity mark and a stripe on the negative side.

# Per-entry sections

All defaults below are OHMNI placeholders (basis ASSUMPTION, confidence L) unless stated; they exist so a freshly placed part simulates sensibly, and the user value always overrides them. Where a default names a real part number, the number is one of the two datasheets opened for this task (S4, S5) and only for the 0805 10 uF case. SRF values are computed from the assumed ESL and the default capacitance (1/(2*pi*sqrt(ESL*C))); they are not measured.

Electrical pin names for the two-terminal passive classes are "1" and "2", both `passive`, matching the existing GENERIC_CAPACITOR record in the product repo (`src/ohmni/catalog/data/parts/GENERIC_CAPACITOR.json`, pins "1" and "2"). That record lists MLCC packages 0402, 0603, 0805 and 1206 only; the other sizes in this group (0201, 1210, 1812) and every non-ceramic entry have no part record yet.

## [OHM-021] 0201 MLCC capacitor
- Class: BEH-CAP-CERAMIC. Terminals (3D spec OHM-021): terminal 1 at -X (pad center x = -0.225 mm), terminal 2 at +X (+0.225 mm); non-polarized, no marking. Pin map: pin "1" -> terminal 1, pin "2" -> terminal 2.
- Defaults: 100 nF, 6.3 V, X5R, V0 = 3.15 V, ESR 50 mohm, ESL 0.3 nH (SRF about 29 MHz), RLK = 1e10 ohm.
- Package notes: the smallest size has the thinnest dielectric layers and, per TDK (S6), the largest relative DC-bias loss; use a refit V0 from the datasheet curve for any bulk use. Disclaimer: this default does not describe a real 0201 part.
- Status: partial (parasitics and bias knee assumed).

## [OHM-022] 0402 MLCC capacitor
- Class: BEH-CAP-CERAMIC. Terminals (3D spec OHM-022): terminal 1 at -X (-0.375 mm), terminal 2 at +X; non-polarized. Pin map as OHM-021.
- Defaults: 100 nF, 16 V, X7R, V0 = 8 V, ESR 30 mohm, ESL 0.4 nH (SRF about 25 MHz), RLK = 1e10 ohm.
- Notes: product repo already carries a 0402 package in GENERIC_CAPACITOR (KiCad footprint C_0402_1005Metric, not hand-solderable).
- Status: partial.

## [OHM-028] Ceramic disc capacitor
- Class: BEH-CAP-CERAMIC (with leaded ESL). Terminals (3D spec OHM-028): two round tinned leads d 0.5 mm at (-S/2, 0) and (+S/2, 0); pin 1 at -X; non-polarized; Class A, THT. Pin map: pin "1" -> lead 1 (-X), pin "2" -> lead 2 (+X).
- Defaults: 100 nF, 50 V, treated as a high-permittivity (Y5V-like) disc: V0 = 0.35*VR = 17.5 V (derived from the Y5V point in S2; ASSUMPTION), aging rate 0.07 per decade hour (S7), ESR 0.1 ohm, ESL 10 nH (lead length, ASSUMPTION; SRF about 5 MHz), RLK = 1e10 ohm.
- Safety warning: a disc may be a safety (Y-class, line-to-earth) capacitor, aliased in the 3D spec. The Y-class rating definitions and tests come from a safety standard that was not opened here, so this entry must not be used as a mains-rated part: set `safety_class = none` and treat any mains application as a checker error until a safety-rated variant is researched (RESEARCH_REQUIRED).
- Class 1 option (C0G disc): V0 = 1e6, tolerance and TC from the user; the default is the high-K disc because that is the common 100 nF disc.
- Status: partial.

## [OHM-029] Radial electrolytic capacitor
- Class: BEH-CAP-ALEL. Terminals (3D spec OHM-029): two round tinned leads, lead 1 = + at -X (-F/2), lead 2 = - at +X (+F/2); negative stripe band on the +X side; the longer lead is positive on new parts (visual only, 3D spec). Pin map: pin "+" -> terminal 1, pin "-" -> terminal 2. Electrical convention matches the marked stripe: stripe side = negative.
- Defaults (default member 10x16): 220 uF, 25 V, ESR 0.15 ohm, ESL 15 nH (SRF about 88 kHz), RLK = 1e8/220 = 4.5e5 ohm, VREVMAX 1 V. Vent clearance above the can: 2 mm for diameters 8-16 mm (S11 as extracted; the 10 mm can falls in that band).
- Ratings: rated ripple Irated, dTo, L0 (life at 105 C) are RESEARCH_REQUIRED per part; use the post-check formulas in the class.
- Status: partial.

## [OHM-030] SMD aluminum electrolytic capacitor
- Class: BEH-CAP-ALEL. Terminals (3D spec OHM-030): two flat tin terminals, pin 1 (+) at (-2.4, 0) and pin 2 (-) at (+2.4, 0) for the default D8 member (6.3 x 7.7); negative side (+X) has a black top segment and a '-' band; positive side has chamfered base-plate corners (3D spec confidence M). Pin map: "+" -> pin 1, "-" -> pin 2.
- Defaults: 47 uF, 25 V, ESR 0.8 ohm, ESL 10 nH (SRF about 232 kHz), RLK = 1e8/47 = 2.1e6 ohm.
- Notes: vent clearance for a 6.3 mm diameter can is not covered by the three bands in S11 (2/3/5 mm for 8-16, 18-35, 40+ mm): RESEARCH_REQUIRED. SMD cans are reflow-soldered; reflow stress is not modeled.
- Status: partial.

## [OHM-031] Snap-in electrolytic capacitor
- Class: BEH-CAP-ALEL. Terminals (3D spec OHM-031): 2-pin default: pins at (-5, 0) (+) and (+5, 0) (-), 10 mm pitch; minus-pole band on the +X side. 3-pin variant: one + pin and two electrically connected - pins; the third hole geometry and the 3-pin numbering are unresolved in the 3D spec (RESEARCH_REQUIRED). Pin map (2-pin): "+" -> pin 1 at -X, "-" -> pin 2 at +X. For a 3-pin variant, tie the two negative pins to the same net and flag a numbering question to the user.
- Defaults (25x40): 2200 uF, 35 V, ESR 0.03 ohm, ESL 20 nH (SRF about 24 kHz), RLK = 1e8/2200 = 4.5e4 ohm. Vent clearance for a 25 mm diameter: 3 mm (S11 band 18-35 mm).
- Notes: large ripple currents and long life lines: use the life formula with the part's dTo (S13). High-voltage snap-in types (200-450 V, S14 example) need a creepage check and a discharge path; bleeder resistors are a design rule, not part of this model.
- Status: partial.

## [OHM-032] Polymer electrolytic capacitor
- Class: BEH-CAP-ALPOLY. Terminals (3D spec OHM-032): Style A (default, SMD can, same outline as OHM-030): pin 1 (+) at (-2.4, 0), pin 2 (-) at (+2.4, 0). Style B (radial leaded OS-CON-like): pin 1 (+) at (-1.25, 0), pin 2 (-) at (+1.25, 0), 2.5 mm pitch; lead diameter 0.5 mm assumed in the 3D spec. Negative side marked at +X (OHMNI default); other makers' molded polymer chips mark the positive end (not this entry). Pin map: "+" -> pin 1, "-" -> pin 2.

The polarity-marking conflict among makers (negative band on cans vs positive stripe on molded polymer chips) is a footprint-checking risk; the checker must verify stripe polarity against the selected style.

- Status: partial.

## [OHM-038] X2 safety capacitor
- Class: BEH-CAP-FILM with the X2 profile. Terminals (3D spec OHM-038): same box geometry as OHM-037 with default pitch 15.0 mm; pin 1 at -X; non-polarized. Pin map as OHM-037.
- Defaults: 100 nF, tan(delta) 20e-4 at 1 kHz (S20 range 10-30e-4), ESL 15 nH (SRF about 4.1 MHz), RLK 15e9 ohm, VRPK = 388.9 V (275 Vrms x sqrt(2); S20), temperature -55 to 105 C (S20), pitch 7.5-27.5 mm (S20).
- Safety: the entry is a mains-connected capacitor; hazard is stored charge after unplugging (0.5*C*Vpk^2 = 7.6 mJ for 100 nF at 389 V) and fire if a non-safety part is used. The X2 class definition and the discharge-time requirement come from IEC 60384-14 and the equipment safety standards, which were not opened; the checker should (a) require a discharge path across any X2 capacitor on a mains net, (b) forbid OHM-037 and OHM-028 in the same position, (c) not claim safety approval for the placed part. Statements about the class are RESEARCH_REQUIRED beyond WIMA's own label "Class X2".
- Status: partial.

## [OHM-039] Silver mica capacitor
- Class: BEH-CAP-MICA. Terminals (3D spec OHM-039): two round leads d 0.6 mm (CD15) at (-S/2, 0), (+S/2, 0), exiting the bottom edge; non-polarized, pin 1 at -X; lead plating not verified in the 3D spec. Pin map: pin "1" -> -X, "2" -> +X.
- Defaults: 100 pF, +/-5% (code J), characteristic F (0 to +70 ppm/C for 91 pF and up; default +35), Q 1000 at 1 MHz (assumed), ESL 8 nH (SRF about 178 MHz), RLK = 1e12 ohm, VR = 500 V (assumed; CDE range 100-2500 Vdc by type, S22).
- Status: partial.

## [OHM-040] Supercapacitor
- Class: BEH-CAP-EDLC. Terminals (3D spec OHM-040): two leads d 0.6 mm (AVX SCC, D at or below 12.5 mm), 5.0 mm pitch for D 10 mm; pin 1 (+) at (-2.5, 0), pin 2 (-) at (+2.5, 0); negative lead carries the 'Vent (-)' indicator for AVX SCC; the longer lead is positive per Eaton PB (not stated for AVX); stripe on the negative side at +X. Pin map: "+" -> pin 1, "-" -> pin 2. The 3D spec lists three styles (radial can default placeholder, stacked-cell PB pack, coin with pins); only the radial-can style has an electrical default.
- Defaults: 10 F, 2.5 V, ESR 0.02 ohm, leakage 20 uA at 2.5 V (RLK 125 kohm), surge 2.8 V (these come from the Eaton HB data ranges, S24; the 3D spec's default style is an AVX SCC that was not opened, so a 10 mm radial can in reality holds far less than 10 F: treat the default as an Eaton HB-like cell, not as the 10 mm can; RESEARCH_REQUIRED).
- Hazard: stored energy and short-circuit current are large for high-capacitance cells (31 J and 119 A for the default into 1 mohm). Series strings need balancing (bench B2/B2b).
- Status: partial.

# Group notes for the coordinator and implementer

- Layer decisions: all 20 entries are L1. No L2/L3 content.
- 3D spec versus electrical reality checks:
  - Polarity is consistent for polarized parts (pin 1 = + at -X). Tantalum stripe marks the anode while aluminum, polymer-can and supercapacitor stripes mark the cathode: the footprint/3D renderer and the DRC must treat these oppositely. The 3D spec itself already warns about EDA footprints that mark the tantalum cathode.
  - OHM-026 and OHM-025 share pad centers (+/-1.35 mm) in the 3D spec although their lengths (3.2 vs 3.2 mm) are the same and only width differs; not an electrical issue.
  - OHM-032: polymer capacitors have two body styles with opposite marking conventions across manufacturers (3D spec records this); keep the style as a parameter.
  - OHM-040 default style (AVX SCC radial 10 mm) was not electrically sourced; the electrical default is an Eaton HB-like cell (S24).
  - OHM-031 3-pin numbering is unresolved in the 3D spec.
- Source conflicts recorded: MLCC aging 2.5 vs 1.0 percent per decade hour (S7 vs S8); supercapacitor surge 2.8 V vs 3 V and +85 C derating 2.3 V vs 1.8 V (S24 vs S23); polymer life rule (10x per 20 C, no ripple term, S15) vs wet electrolytic (2x per 10 C with ripple term, S13); MLCC bias fits from three sources differ by a factor of about 2.4 in V0/VR (S2 vs S10, different parts).
- Simulation flag convention (section 0) should be mirrored by the behavior layer's check engine: flag bits 1, 2, 4, 8.

# GROUP R3: Inductors, chokes, transformers (OHM-041 to OHM-055)

Output of the R3 research agent. Bench netlists live in `/home/claude/behavior/bench/mag_inductor/`, `mag_xfmr/`, `mag_cmc/`, `mag_flyback/`, `mag_ct/`, `mag_ethmag/`. Every benchmark number below was produced by running `ngspice -b` (ngspice-42, KLU build, no XSPICE needed) in this environment.

## 0. Group overview and conventions

Six behavior classes cover the 15 entries.

| Class | Entries | Layer | Core idea |
|---|---|---|---|
| BEH-MAG-INDUCTOR | OHM-041..049 | L1 | L(i) saturating inductor + Rdc + Cp + loss + self heating |
| BEH-MAG-CMC | OHM-050, OHM-051 | L1 | two coupled windings, DM = leakage, CM = coupled; CM flux saturation |
| BEH-MAG-XFMR-SIGNAL | OHM-052 | L1 | linear coupled pair or T-model with saturable magnetizing branch |
| BEH-MAG-XFMR-FLYBACK | OHM-053 | L1 | same T-model, used as gapped energy-storage element, leakage spike |
| BEH-MAG-XFMR-CT | OHM-054 | L1 | T-model, current source behaviour, burden, open-secondary hazard |
| BEH-MAG-ETHMAG | OHM-055 | L1 (+ L3 note) | 1CT:1CT transformers + line CMC, isolation barrier |

Fidelity label for every class: **behavioural_approximation**. No vendor SPICE model is attached anywhere in this group (no vendor model was opened). Conforms to `src/ohmni/eda/simulation.py`: a deck is `behavioural_approximation` as soon as it carries `.model/.subckt/.include`, and `ideal_components` only when it holds bare R/L/C/K. A plain `L` + `K` deck with no `.subckt` is `ideal_components`; the saturating and parasitic subcircuits below are `behavioural_approximation`. A simulation that did not run is never a pass.

Shared mechanisms (verified by running ngspice 42):

1. **Saturating inductor.** `L1 a b L='expr'` with `i(L1)` inside the expression is a *differential* inductance: v = L(i)*di/dt. Verified: for L(i)=1u/(1+(i/2)^2) at 4000 A/s the measured v was 2.000 mV at 2 A (expected 2.000 mV). This is dlambda/dt for lambda(i)=integral of L(i), so energy is consistent. The model used everywhere is lambda(i) = LR*L0*i + (1-LR)*L0*Ia*tanh(i/Ia), hence L(i) = L0*(LR + (1-LR)*sech^2(i/Ia)). Constants: Ia = Isat / atanh( sqrt( DROP/(1-LR) ) ), where Isat is the DC current at which the small-signal inductance has fallen by the fraction DROP (0.1, 0.2 or 0.3, as the datasheet defines it) and LR = L_sat/L0 is the residual (air-core) fraction (default 0.05, ASSUMPTION).
2. **The `flux='expr'` form was tested and rejected** (`bench/mag_inductor/X1_flux_form_disagrees.cir`): for flux = L0*Ia*tanh(i/Ia) ngspice 42 gave 6.09 mV and 7.57 mV where 1.68 mV and 0.414 mV are the analytic values. Do not use `flux=` for this model.
3. **Small-signal AC at a DC bias works with `L='expr'`.** `.ac` linearizes at the operating point, so L(i_bias) is what AC sees (bench B1: 1.54 uH at Isat for a 30 % part, exact). This is how a datasheet "L vs DC bias" curve is reproduced.
4. **DC operating point trap.** At t=0 the DC solution shorts every inductor. A transient that starts with a source at nonzero value (e.g. a cosine) therefore starts with a huge fictitious current. Use `.tran ... uic` or start sources from zero. Without this the volt-second bench read 200 kA.
5. **Overflow guard.** `cosh(x)` overflows during Newton iterations; the expression clamps its argument: `1/cosh(max(min(i/ia,20),-20))`. Without it ngspice printed "out of range for cosh" and failed to converge.
6. **Name collisions.** A `.param` named `lm` clashes with an inductor instance `Lm` referenced as `i(Lm)` (the circuit silently misbehaved). Inductor instance names starting with `B` are parsed as behavioral sources (`LB1` not `B1`). Parameters in the shipped libs use `lmag`, `lleak`, `ia`.
7. **Ideal transformer by dependent sources.** v(sx,s2) = N*v(pb,p2) by `E`, and current by `F` from a zero-volt sense source: verified against the K-element version (output 1.7809 vs 1.7883 V, 0.4 %).
8. **Time-step sensitivity of saturation spikes.** For the CT open-secondary case the spike is about 30 ns wide; `.tran 20n` read 1051 V, 5 ns read 227 to 237 V, 1 ns read 182 V, 0.5 ns with reltol 1e-5 read 237.7 V (analytic 235.6 V). The behavior layer must either bound tmax by the spike width or compute the open-secondary peak analytically (see BEH-MAG-XFMR-CT section 6).

The existing part records (`src/ohmni/catalog/data/parts/*.json`) use `electrical_type: passive` for two-terminal passives. Inductors keep it; windings of transformers are also `passive` (galvanically separate windings are different nets). There is no `magnetic` type in the repo; this document uses `passive` and keeps the winding grouping in `package_terminal_rule`.

Source IDs are global to this file (S1..S27 at the end). Many values were relayed by the WebFetch summarizer rather than read by eye from the PDF; where a number is load-bearing and the summarizer was inconsistent between fetches, that is stated.

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-MAG-INDUCTOR

Applies to OHM-041, 042, 043 (multilayer chip), 044 (wirewound ceramic chip), 045 (shielded power), 046 (unshielded power), 047 (axial), 048 (radial drum), 049 (toroidal). Layer L1.

### 1. Purpose and real-world use

An inductor stores energy in a magnetic field, opposes changes of current, and is the energy element of switch-mode converters and the series element of LC filters and RF matching networks. Typical uses by family:

- Power inductors (045, 046, 048, 049): buck/boost/SEPIC energy storage, output and EMI filter chokes. Values from about 0.1 uH to 1 mH (SRP7028A series spans 0.15 uH to 10 uH and beyond; RLB0914 reaches 1 mH in distributor listings; S4, S19).
- RF and signal chip inductors (041, 044): impedance matching, bias tees, LC filters, from about 1 nH (wirewound ceramic) to some uH (multilayer ferrite).
- Multilayer ferrite chips (041, 042, 043): small-signal filtering and low-current power (Murata LQM18DN 6.8 uH: Isat 120 mA, S6).
- Axial and radial leaded (047, 048): through-hole filters and low-frequency chokes (Bourns 78F 3.3 uH, 575 mA, S18; RLB0914-101KL 100 uH, Irms 1.1 A, S19).
- Toroids (049): DC/DC converters and EMI filters (Bourns 2107-V-RC 33 uH, 5 A, S20).

### 2. What it is and how it works

Construction: a winding of N turns (DCR = wire resistance, "based strictly on the wire diameter and length", S1) around a magnetic path. The inductance of a gapped or powder core follows L = N^2 / R_m, with the reluctance R_m dominated by the gap (distributed gap in powder cores). The flux linkage is lambda = L*i until the core flux density approaches B_sat, after which permeability collapses and L falls.

- **Isat and the percent-drop definition.** "Definition of where saturation begins is therefore somewhat arbitrary and must be defined. ... Definitions in the range of 10-20% are common, but ... some inductor catalogs may use figures of 50% inductance drop." (Coilcraft Doc 469, S1). Coilcraft XAL40xx: "DC current at 25 C that causes an inductance drop of 30% (typ)" (S2). Bourns SRP7028A: "Inductance drops 20 % at Isat" (S4). Murata LQM18DN gives "Rated current (Isat)" based on inductance change without stating the percentage in the extracted text (S6). Bourns RLB0914 and SDR0604 listings give Isat values without a stated percentage (S19, S21). **The percentage is a mandatory parameter (`drop`), not a constant.**
- **Irms (heating current).** "The RMS current is used to give a measure of how much average current can continuously flow through the part while producing less than some specified temperature rise" and "should include the ambient temperature at which it was measured" (S1). XAL40xx gives both a 20 C and a 40 C rise from 25 C ambient (S2). SRP7028A: 40 C rise at Irms (S4).
- **Isat versus Irms are independent ratings.** The usable DC current is the smaller of the two. For SRP7028A-100M, Isat = 6 A but Irms = 3.5 A, so heat limits first; for XAL4020-222ME Isat 5.6 A (30 % drop) and Irms 5.5 A (40 C) are close (S2, S4).
- **Core materials and saturation shape.** Ferrite (gapped) saturates hard: "inductance drops sharply as current approaches saturation limits"; pressed powder or composite saturates softly ("inductance degrades gradually"), has higher core loss at high flux density, and a fully molded powder body gives "full shielding for low EMI" (Coilcraft Doc 1733, S7). Bourns SRP7028A uses a carbonyl-powder core (S4); XAL40xx a composite (S2); Bourns 78F is listed with "Ferrite DR" (drum) core (S18). The tanh model captures the soft case; a hard-saturating ferrite corresponds to a smaller `LR` and (optionally) a larger exponent, which is not modeled (known limitation).
- **Shielded versus unshielded.** Shielded (molded powder, 045) keeps most flux inside: low radiated field and low coupling to neighbours. Unshielded open drums (046, 048) and toroids (049, closed path but with leakage flux), axial rods (047) radiate more. This is an EMI and layout effect that SPICE does not see; the behavior layer carries it as a metadata field `shielding: full|semi|none` for DRC (keep-out, orientation of adjacent inductors), not as an electrical element. Mutual coupling between two inductors can be added by a `K` statement with a small `k` (ASSUMPTION; no source quantifies it for these parts).
- **SRF, Q and parasitic capacitance.** The winding distributed capacitance resonates with L: SRF = 1/(2 pi sqrt(L*Cp)) (S1 defines SRF as the frequency at which the winding "resonates naturally with the distributed capacitance"). Above SRF the part is capacitive. Q = omega*L / R_series(f) rises with frequency until copper skin/proximity loss and core loss dominate; datasheets quote a minimum Q at a test frequency (Murata LQW18AN15NJ10D: Q min 42, S5; Bourns 78F3R3J: Q min 50, S18).
- **Temperature.** Copper resistance rises about 0.393 %/K (general physics, alpha_Cu = 0.00393 /K near 20 C; basis CONSENSUS). Datasheet DCR is at 25 C (assumption, standard practice).

Key equations used by the model:

- L(i) = L0 * (LR + (1-LR) * sech^2(i / Ia)), Ia = Isat / atanh( sqrt(drop / (1-LR)) )
- lambda(i) = LR*L0*i + (1-LR)*L0*Ia*tanh(i/Ia)  (volt-seconds to reach a current: V*t = lambda)
- Cp = 1 / ((2 pi SRF)^2 * L0)
- Rp (loss branch) from Q at the test frequency fq: 1/Q = Rdc/(omega_q*L0) + omega_q*L0/Rp, so Rp = omega_q*L0 / (1/Q - Rdc/(omega_q*L0))
- Rth = dT_rated / ( Irms^2 * Rdc25 * (1 + alpha*dT_rated) ) [degC/W, DERIVED, assumes the rating test is self-consistent]
- P = i_rms^2 * Rdc(T), Rdc(T) = Rdc25 * (1 + alpha*(T-25))

### 3. How it connects

Two terminals, no polarity (all nine entries are non-polarized in the 3D spec; the Coilcraft color dot on 044 is value coding, not polarity). Electrical pins `A` and `B`. Typical circuits: series with a switch node and output capacitor (buck), series LC low-pass, shunt-to-ground RF choke, ferrite bead replacement for small currents.

Common mistakes the layer should flag:
- Choosing by L alone and ignoring Isat: the real inductance at peak current can be 20 to 30 % low (or far lower if peak exceeds Isat), which raises ripple current and can make a converter run away.
- Ignoring Irms heating at high ambient (derating below).
- Using a part above its SRF (it behaves as a capacitor).
- Placing unshielded inductors next to sensitive nodes or other inductors.
- Parallel inductors for current: no current sharing guarantee.
- Using a DC-op shortcut: a DC solve treats the inductor as a short, so a hard voltage source across an ideal inductor gives infinite current.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation

**Layer**: L1. **Primitives**: R, C, L with `L='expr'`, B-source for self-heating. **Fidelity**: ideal mode `ideal_components` (a bare `L` with tolerance); realistic mode `behavioural_approximation`. No XSPICE needed; ngspice 42 behavioral inductor expressions only. `.include bench/mag_inductor/ind_sat.lib` (file shipped in this repo output).

```spice
* ideal mode (fidelity ideal_components)
L{ref} {A} {B} {L0}

* realistic mode (fidelity behavioural_approximation)
.subckt IND_SAT a b L0=1u Isat=5 DROP=0.3 LR=0.05 RDC=10m CP=1p RP=1e9
.param ia={Isat/atanh(sqrt(DROP/(1-LR)))}
Rdc a x {RDC}
Lnl x b L='L0*(LR+(1-LR)*(1/cosh(max(min(i(Lnl)/ia,20),-20)))**2)'
Cp a b {CP}
Rp a b {RP}
.ends
X{ref} {A} {B} IND_SAT L0={L0} Isat={Isat} DROP={drop} LR={lr} RDC={rdc} CP={cp} RP={rp}

* with self heating: node th carries the temperature rise in degC (1 V = 1 degC)
.subckt IND_SAT_TH a b th L0=1u Isat=5 DROP=0.3 LR=0.05 RDC=10m CP=1p RP=1e9 RTH=40 CTH=0.05 TC=3.93m
.param ia={Isat/atanh(sqrt(DROP/(1-LR)))}
Rdc a x R='RDC*(1+TC*v(th))'
Lnl x b L='L0*(LR+(1-LR)*(1/cosh(max(min(i(Lnl)/ia,20),-20)))**2)'
Cp a b {CP}
Rp a b {RP}
Bpw 0 th I='v(a,x)*v(a,x)/(RDC*(1+TC*v(th)))'
Rth th 0 {RTH}
Cth th 0 {CTH}
.ends
```

Parameter to datasheet mapping:
- `L0` = nominal inductance at the datasheet test frequency, zero bias. Tolerance (+-5 % RF, +-10/20 % power, up to +-30/40 % chokes) applied as a Monte Carlo or corner multiplier on L0.
- `Isat`, `drop` = the saturation-current row and the percentage stated next to it. If the percentage is not stated, use `drop=0.3` and mark the instance `assumed_drop=true` (basis ASSUMPTION).
- `RDC` = DCR typical (use maximum for worst-case); `TC` = 3.93e-3.
- `CP` from SRF (formula above). When the datasheet gives only a "min SRF", `CP` is an upper bound.
- `RP` from Q at `fq`; where Q or its frequency is not given (most power inductors) use `RP=1e9` (off). Murata Q test frequency was not stated in the opened text (S5); the bench assumes 100 MHz and says so.
- `RTH` from Irms and rise as in section 2.

Valid analyses: `op`, `dc` (L is a short), `ac` (small-signal L at the DC operating point, including saturation), `tran` (full nonlinear; needs `uic` or zero-start sources), `temp` (via TC). `noise` not meaningful. Valid range: DC to about 0.5 * SRF (ASSUMPTION; the model has one parasitic C and one loss resistor, so it is trustworthy near and below SRF only within a few percent), current magnitude up to about 2 * Isat before the tanh shape (not the real roll-off) dominates the error.

Known limitations (where the model is wrong):
- Saturation shape is a single-parameter tanh fitted to one datasheet point (Isat at drop %). Real curves (ferrite hard knee, powder soft) differ between that point and the extremes. Datasheets seldom give a second point, so a second point cannot be fitted without the L-vs-I curve (RESEARCH_REQUIRED per part).
- No frequency dependence of L (permeability roll-off) and no AC resistance (skin, proximity); Q holds only at the fit frequency. The CMC bench (BEH-MAG-CMC) shows the effect: an inductance fit to 100 kHz fails at 2.5 to 100 MHz unless re-fit.
- Core loss is not a function of flux swing (no Steinmetz). Heating uses I^2*Rdc only, so ripple core loss is ignored and the model underestimates rise in high-ripple converters.
- No hysteresis or remanence. No magnetostriction, no audible noise.
- No temperature dependence of L0 or Isat (ferrite Isat falls hot; Coilcraft Isat is stated at 25 C, S2).
- No mutual coupling to neighbours unless the user adds a `K`.

| rating | symbol | value | condition | check expression | source |

| heating current | Irms | per part | specified rise at 25 C ambient | `rms(i_L) <= Irms_allowed(Ta)` | S1,S2 |
| derated heating current | Irms(Ta) | Irms for Ta <= 25 C; Irms*sqrt((Tmax-Ta)/dT_rated) above | assumes dT proportional to I^2*R (DERIVED; ignores R(T)); rating tests are at 25 C ambient (S2) | `rms(i) <= (Irms if Ta<=25 else Irms*sqrt((Tmax-Ta)/dT_rated))` | S2 (Tmax 165 C), S4 (150 C) |
| part temperature | Tpart | Ta + dT <= Tmax | XAL 165 C, SRP7028A 150 C, Murata 125 C, Bourns leaded 105 C | `T = Ta + v(th) <= Tmax` | S2,S4,S5,S18,S20 |
| frequency | f | f <= 0.5*SRF | ASSUMPTION | WARN above 0.5*SRF, ERROR above SRF | S1 (SRF definition) |
| voltage | V | not rated for power inductors | insulation of enamel wire; no value in opened docs | no check (RESEARCH_REQUIRED) | n/a |

Example of the derating rule: XAL4020-222ME (Tmax 165 C, dT_rated 40 K) at Ta = 125 C allows Irms*sqrt(40/40) = 5.5 A; at Ta = 140 C it allows 5.5*sqrt(25/40) = 4.35 A. This is a DERIVED rule, not a manufacturer curve.

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior

| id | trigger | effect (physical) | sim_response | permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| saturation | abs(i) approaches or exceeds Isat | L collapses to LR*L0; current spikes limited only by resistance and source; switch stress, converter fault | model already does it (L(i)); flag WARN at 0.9*Isat, ERROR at 1.5*Isat | recoverable (ferrite core returns); if overheated, see below |
| overheat | Tpart > Tmax | enamel insulation degrades, turn-to-turn short or open winding, solder reflow, core material change | flag ERROR at Tmax; if Tpart > Tmax + 20 K for > 1 s of sim time replace the element by a 1 Gohm resistor (open) | permanent |
| overcurrent far beyond Irms | I > ~2*Irms for seconds | wire fuses open | same as above (open) | permanent |
| above SRF | f > SRF | capacitive; filter stops filtering, resonance peaking | model shows it via Cp; flag WARN above 0.5*SRF | recoverable |
| overvoltage | no source value | turn-to-turn flash, insulation breakdown | RESEARCH_REQUIRED, no automatic action | permanent |
| reverse polarity | n/a | none (non-polarized) | none | n/a |
| ESD | negligible | none | none | n/a |
| short winding | manufacturing defect | not a user fault | not modeled | n/a |
| mechanical (cracked ferrite) | board flex, soldering shock (multilayer chip) | inductance drop or open | not modeled; DRC note: chip inductors near board edges (RESEARCH_REQUIRED) | permanent |

### 8. Thermal behavior

Model: steady-state rise dT = Rth*P with Rdc(T) feedback (bench B4). `RTH` derived from Irms and its rise (section 2). `CTH` default 0.05 J/K for chip-to-power sizes (ASSUMPTION; typical thermal time constants of seconds to minutes; no source). Ambient temperature is a simulation-level scalar Ta; Tpart = Ta + dT. Core loss from ripple is not included (underestimates dT; note it in the check output).

### 9. Appearance summary

Appearance is defined in the 3D spec: 041, 042, 043 dark ferrite chip with two silver caps and no marking; 044 beige ceramic chip with a color dot; 045 dark molded block with two tin lead-frame ends; 046 exposed ferrite drum with winding; 047 colored lacquer cylinder with bands and axial leads; 048 upright sleeved cylinder with two leads; 049 coated torus with two leads. No polarity marks anywhere; the 3D spec's pin 1 is -X (chips, power SMD), or the end near the first band (axial). No re-research was done.

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-MAG-CMC

Applies to OHM-050 (SMD, 4 pads) and OHM-051 (THT, 4 pins). Layer L1.

### 1. Purpose and real-world use

A common-mode choke (line filter, CMC) is two windings on one core. It gives a high impedance to currents that flow the same way in both conductors (common-mode noise, usually the radiated-emission culprit) and almost none to the wanted differential current, which cancels its flux. Uses: mains-input EMI filters (051, Wurth 744821240 rated 250 V ac, 1.5 A in distributor listings, S17), DC and low-speed data lines (050, WE-SL5 744272222, 2.2 mH, 80 V, S9), USB/Ethernet/CAN line filters (small variants like TDK ACM4520 are only named in the 3D spec).

### 2. What it is and how it works

Two windings A (A1 to A2) and B (B1 to B2) wound on a ferrite core with dots at A1 and B1.

- **Differential mode**: current enters A1, leaves A2, returns through B2 to B1. The two fluxes oppose, the core sees almost no net MMF, and the only impedance is the **leakage inductance** (Wurth: "residual inductance when one winding is short-circuited", S8). WE-SL5 744272222: LS = 130 nH typ at 1 MHz / 1 mA (S9).
- **Common mode**: current enters A1 and B1 (or leaves A2 and B2), fluxes add, impedance is high. With k = M/sqrt(L1*L2) (typical CMC k = 0.80 to 0.95 for deliberately leaky chokes, S8), each winding in the CM loop sees L*(1+k).
- Equations (windings identical, self-inductance L each): k = sqrt(1 - LS/L). CM inductance per winding L_cm,w = L*(1+k). With both windings paralleled as in an impedance analyzer CM test, L_cm = L*(1+k)/2. DM inductance seen through the loop of both windings L_dm = 2*L*(1-k) (about LS for k near 1: L_dm = 2*LS/(1+k)).
- **Impedance versus frequency**: ferrite permeability falls with frequency and the winding capacitance C0 resonates it: WE-SL5 744272222 data: Zmax = 7500 Ohm typ at 2.5 MHz, 4000 Ohm at 10 MHz, 400 Ohm at 100 MHz (S9). L = 2200 uH is only valid at the test point 100 kHz/100 mV, tolerance +-40 %.
- **Saturation**: the core flux is set by the net MMF, i.e. by the *common-mode* (or imbalance) current. A DC differential current ideally produces no flux, so it does not saturate the core. A large CM DC or a surge saturates it and the CM inductance collapses; leakage (DM) inductance stays because it is an air path. No Isat for either entry was found in the opened documents (WE-SL5 gives IR for a 40 K rise, S9).
- **Parasitics**: winding capacitance C0 (ferrite loss resistor R0 and DC resistance, S8 lists exactly these equivalent-circuit elements), interwinding capacitance, DCR (WE-SL5: 0.3 Ohm max).

### 3. How it connects

Four terminals. In-line use: line conductor 1 passes through winding A, conductor 2 through winding B; the choke is placed in series with both conductors (not across them). Differential signals see only the leakage inductance. Most common errors: using it as a shunt element; swapping one winding (reverses the sense so the choke becomes a differential inductor and saturates on signal current; DM then drives flux additively); assuming it filters DM noise (it only does so through the small leakage); exceeding rated current (heating, not saturation, is usually first).

**Pin-pairing warning.** The 3D spec numbers WE-SL5 pins CCW with windings 1-2 and 4-3 (each winding on one side), but an opened Wurth datasheet read says pins 1 and 3 belong to one winding and 2 and 4 to the other (S9, schematic text via summarizer). Neither was visually confirmed, and a through-passing choke normally pairs a left pin with a right pin. Consequently the winding-to-pin map is **RESEARCH_REQUIRED**; the DRC layer should not trust it for polarity checks. The electrical class is symmetric in the windings, so the simulation is unaffected as long as the user wires each conductor through one winding.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation

Layer L1, fidelity `behavioural_approximation` (or `ideal_components` if only two inductors and a `K` are written without parasitics). Library: `bench/mag_cmc/cmc.lib`.

```spice
* Linear K-coupled model (fidelity ideal_components when parasitics are zero)
.subckt CMC_K a1 a2 b1 b2 L=2.2m LS=130n RDC=0.3 C0=1p RPAR=1e9
.param kk={sqrt(1-LS/L)}
Ra a1 ax {RDC}
La ax a2 {L}
Rb b1 bx {RDC}
Lb bx b2 {L}
K1 La Lb {kk}
Ca a1 a2 {C0}
Cb b1 b2 {C0}
Rpa a1 a2 {RPAR}
Rpb b1 b2 {RPAR}
.ends

* Saturating model: symmetric T, common flux driven by iA_in + iB_in
.subckt CMC_SAT a1 a2 b1 b2 L=2.2m LS=130n RDC=0.3 C0=1p RPAR=1e9 ISATM=2 DROP=0.3 LR=0.05
.param kk={sqrt(1-LS/L)}
.param lmag={kk*L}
.param lleak={L*(1-kk)}
.param ia={ISATM/atanh(sqrt(DROP/(1-LR)))}
Ra a1 ax {RDC}
Lla ax am {lleak}
Lm am a2 L='lmag*(LR+(1-LR)*(1/cosh(max(min(i(Lm)/ia,20),-20)))**2)'
Es bm b2 am a2 1
Vs bm bs 0
Fp am a2 Vs 1
Llb bs bx {lleak}
Rb bx b1 {RDC}
Ca a1 a2 {C0}
Cb b1 b2 {C0}
Rpa a1 a2 {RPAR}
Rpb b1 b2 {RPAR}
.ends
```

Parameter mapping: `L` = datasheet inductance (the self-inductance of one winding at the test frequency); `LS` = leakage inductance with the other winding shorted; `RDC` = DCR (per winding); `C0`, `RPAR` from the impedance curve (see below); `ISATM` = common-mode current (sum iA+iB) at which L_cm has dropped by `DROP`: **not given by any opened datasheet, ASSUMPTION, confidence L** (a default of 2*IR, i.e. about 1.6 A for the 744272222, is a placeholder and must be flagged).

Two parameter sets are needed because L falls with frequency: a low-frequency set (L = 2.2 mH at 100 kHz) and a high-frequency EMI set fitted to the impedance table. Fit used (derived, bench B2): L = 1.02 mH, C0 = 1.99 pF per winding (3.98 pF total CM), RPAR = 15 kOhm per winding (7.5 kOhm paralleled), which reproduces 7500 Ohm at 2.5 MHz, 3707 Ohm at 10 MHz (datasheet 4000, -7.3 %), 400 Ohm at 100 MHz (400). The fit assumes the datasheet impedance is the paralleled CM impedance of the 744272222 (not stated in the opened text).

Valid analyses: `op`, `dc`, `ac`, `tran` (CMC_SAT), `noise` no. Valid range: DM operation up to the frequency where the leakage inductance resonates with C0; CM operation per the fitted band (100 kHz to 100 MHz for the HF set).

Known limitations: single resonance, no frequency-dependent loss (the 10 MHz point is off by 7 %); no CM-to-DM conversion due to winding asymmetry (real chokes have a few percent unbalance, so some CM converts to DM); saturation shape is a tanh fitted to an assumed point; the leakage path is linear (real leakage also saturates at very high DM current); the T-model forces both windings identical.

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior

| id | trigger | effect | sim_response | permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| cm_saturation | abs(iA+iB) beyond ISATM (surge, imbalance, asymmetric winding) | CM inductance falls, filtering lost; DM leakage unchanged | CMC_SAT handles it; WARN at 0.9*ISATM | recoverable |
| overcurrent heating | rms current > IR | winding insulation damage, opens | flag ERROR at IR*1.0 (WARN 0.9); open the winding after Tmax+20 K | permanent |
| overvoltage | v > VR (>> Vtest) | winding-to-winding flashover, enamel breakdown | flag ERROR; short A-B windings (insulation failure) above 2*Vtest peak; no sourced limit beyond Vtest | permanent |
| winding wired as DM inductor (one winding reversed) | user wiring error | fluxes add for signal current: large inductance in the signal path, saturation, signal lost | DRC: require one winding per conductor and dot-consistent in-to-out; sim shows it automatically (CMC_SAT) | recoverable |
| above SRF | f > resonance | capacitive, no filtering | model includes C0 | recoverable |
| ESD | n/a | negligible | none | n/a |

### 8. Thermal behavior

Same as BEH-MAG-INDUCTOR with P = iA_rms^2*RDC + iB_rms^2*RDC and Rth from IR: Rth = 40/(IR^2*2*RDC*(1+0.00393*40)) assuming IR is the current through each winding with both windings carrying it at once (ASSUMPTION; for 744272222: 40/(0.83^2*2*0.3*1.157) = 83.6 K/W). Core loss from the line frequency is not modeled.

### 9. Appearance summary

See the 3D spec (OHM-050, OHM-051): 050 is a dark flat-top block with four corner terminals and a pin-1 dot; 051 is a tall black or blue rectangular case with four pins in a 2 by 2 rectangle (4.5 mm by 10 mm pitch). The winding pairing is not visible on the part.
