## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-MAG-XFMR-SIGNAL

Applies to OHM-052 (small signal / audio transformer). Layer L1. This class also defines the generic transformer building blocks (`XFMR_K`, `XFMR_SAT`) that BEH-MAG-XFMR-FLYBACK, BEH-MAG-XFMR-CT and BEH-MAG-ETHMAG reuse. Library: `bench/mag_xfmr/xfmr.lib` (identical copies in `mag_flyback/` and `mag_ct/`).

### 1. Purpose and real-world use

A small signal transformer transfers an AC signal between two windings with galvanic isolation and impedance or voltage transformation, and blocks DC. Uses: audio line and microphone coupling (600 Ohm to 600 Ohm lines, Triad TY-145P "600CT : 600CT", response 200 Hz to 15 kHz, S22), telephone/modem interfaces, ground-loop isolation, gate-drive and pulse coupling at higher frequencies. Impedance ratio = turns ratio squared.

### 2. What it is and how it works

Two (or more) windings on a common core. Ideal transformer: v2 = n*v1 (n = Ns/Np), i1 = n*i2 into the dot, no losses, passes AC from DC to infinity. Real transformer differences:

- **Magnetizing inductance** Lm (primary open-circuit inductance minus leakage) in parallel with the ideal transformer on the primary side: it limits the **low-frequency** response: f_L = Req/(2 pi Lm), Req = (Rs + Rp) || ((Rsec + RL)/n^2), all referred to the primary. With Rs = RL = 600 Ohm and winding resistances 40 Ohm, Req = 320 Ohm.
- **Leakage inductance** Llk in series: limits the **high-frequency** response with winding capacitance. The mapping used: Llk = primary-referred inductance measured with the secondary shorted; the coupled-inductor equivalent has k = sqrt(1 - Llk/Lp), L1 = Lp, L2 = n^2*Lp.
- **Winding resistances** Rp, Rs (insertion loss), **interwinding capacitance** Ciw (couples common-mode noise, limits isolation at HF).
- **Saturation (volt-seconds)**: flux = integral of v dt / N. A transformer driven at low frequency, or with a DC offset, saturates: magnetizing current rises sharply. The limit is a **volt-second product**, not a current. With a magnetizing branch lambda(i) = LR*Lm*i + (1-LR)*Lm*Ia*tanh(i/Ia), a sinusoid of peak V at frequency f needs peak flux linkage V/(2 pi f); the peak magnetizing current follows by inverting lambda(i) (bench B3).
- **DC through a winding** magnetizes the core (no gap in a typical audio unit): DC current adds a flux offset and reduces the AC headroom. Not modeled except through the saturating Lm if the user places DC current in it.
- **Polarity (dots)**: the dotted terminals are in phase. Dots matter for series/parallel wiring of windings and for center-taps.

### 3. How it connects

Six terminals on OHM-052 in two rows of three (Triad numbering 1-3 and 4-6 by rows per the 3D spec). The documented electrical rating is "600CT : 600CT": each side has a center tap, so the natural mapping is **pins 1-2-3 = primary A, CT, B** and **pins 4-5-6 = secondary A, CT, B**, with the dots at pins 1 and 4. **That assignment is a DEFAULT-ASSUMPTION; the pin-to-winding table was not read from the Triad datasheet** (RESEARCH_REQUIRED). Typical circuits: line in on 1-3, line out on 4-6, CTs floating or used for DC feed (phantom or loop current). Mistakes: driving with DC bias; using a transformer below its low-frequency corner; wiring windings out of phase; assuming isolation rating (the opened listing gives none).

### 4. Electrical model

Layer L1. Fidelity: ideal mode (`ideal_components`) is `L`+`L`+`K` with k = 1 or an ideal `E`/`F` pair; realistic mode is `behavioural_approximation`.

```spice
* linear coupled-inductor version
.subckt XFMR_K p1 p2 s1 s2 LP=1m N=1 LLK=1u RP=1m RS=1m CIW=1p
.param kk={sqrt(1-LLK/LP)}
Rp1 p1 pa {RP}
L1 pa p2 {LP}
L2 sa s2 {LP*N*N}
Rs1 s1 sa {RS}
K12 L1 L2 {kk}
Ciw1 p1 s1 {CIW/2}
Ciw2 p2 s2 {CIW/2}
.ends

* saturating T-model: leakage in series, nonlinear magnetizing branch across an ideal transformer
.subckt XFMR_SAT p1 p2 s1 s2 LP=1m N=1 LLK=1u RP=1m RS=1m CIW=1p ISATM=1 DROP=0.3 LR=0.05
.param lmag={LP-LLK}
.param ia={ISATM/atanh(sqrt(DROP/(1-LR)))}
Rp1 p1 pa {RP}
Llk pa pb {LLK}
Lm pb p2 L='lmag*(LR+(1-LR)*(1/cosh(max(min(i(Lm)/ia,20),-20)))**2)'
Es sx s2 pb p2 {N}
Vs sx sb 0
Fp pb p2 Vs {N}
Rs1 s1 sb {RS}
Ciw1 p1 s1 {CIW/2}
Ciw2 p2 s2 {CIW/2}
.ends
```

For center-tapped windings (OHM-052 and the Ethernet magnetics) use four coupled half-windings with a `K` between every pair, as in `bench/mag_ethmag/ethmag.lib` (tested there; the half-windings have L = Lp/4 each so a full winding series-aids to Lp). That multi-winding form is linear only (no saturation).

Parameter mapping: `LP` primary open-circuit inductance (datasheet "OCL" or "primary inductance"); `N` = Ns/Np; `LLK` leakage with secondary shorted; `RP`, `RS` DCR; `CIW` interwinding capacitance; `ISATM` primary-referred magnetizing current at `DROP` fall of Lm. **For TY-145P only the impedance (600CT:600CT, 1:1) and response band (200 Hz to 15 kHz) were found (S22); LP = 1 H, RP = RS = 40 Ohm, LLK = 5 mH, CIW = 100 pF are ASSUMPTIONS with confidence L.** The band implies LP >= about 0.25 H if "200 Hz" is a -3 dB point with 600 Ohm source and load (DERIVED, Req = 320 Ohm), which the 1 H default satisfies.

Valid analyses: `op`, `ac`, `tran` (XFMR_SAT, use `uic` or start-from-zero sources, see section 0 item 4), `dc` (DC is blocked: the K model shorts DC through the windings, so DC paths must be provided by the user circuit). Valid range: from the Lm corner to roughly 1/(2 pi sqrt(Llk*Cw)) (not computed; Cw unknown).

Known limitations: single-pole leakage/capacitance model; no frequency-dependent core loss; no distortion from non-sinusoidal B-H beyond the tanh; leakage split is all on the primary side (the K model and the T model differ by 0.4 % in a loaded test, section 0 item 7); center-tap form has no saturation; no winding self-resonance; DC bias headroom not derived.

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior

| id | trigger | effect | sim_response | permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| core saturation | volt-seconds beyond lambda_max (low f, high V, DC offset) | magnetizing current spikes, distortion, overheating, primary overcurrent | XFMR_SAT behaves; WARN at 0.9*ISATM | recoverable |
| winding overcurrent | I beyond wire rating | overheat, open | ERROR; open | permanent |
| isolation breakdown | Vbarrier above the (unknown) rating | flashover | not modeled; no rating known | permanent |
| DC bias | DC current in a winding | core offset and early saturation | flag if DC component of winding current exceeds 10 % of ISATM (ASSUMPTION) | recoverable |
| open secondary | normal for a voltage transformer | no hazard | none | n/a |

### 8. Thermal behavior

Copper loss only: P = Ip^2*RP + Is^2*RS; no thermal rating found for TY-145P. Use the same Rth derivation as BEH-MAG-INDUCTOR when a rating exists, else no thermal model (flag RESEARCH_REQUIRED).

### 9. Appearance summary

See OHM-052 in the 3D spec: rectangular plastic box with a 2 by 3 grid of square pins on 4.75 mm pitch, 10.67 mm row spacing. Color and any pin-1 mark were not found in the datasheet; the 3D spec uses the OHMNI convention.

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-MAG-XFMR-FLYBACK

Applies to OHM-053 (flyback transformer on EE/EFD core, Wurth WE-FB 750311595 representative). Layer L1. Library: `bench/mag_flyback/xfmr.lib` (same `XFMR_SAT` as BEH-MAG-XFMR-SIGNAL).

### 1. Purpose and real-world use

A flyback "transformer" is a coupled inductor: it stores energy in the core gap while the primary switch is on, and releases it to the secondary (and auxiliary) windings when the switch turns off. It provides isolation and voltage conversion in low-power isolated SMPS (about 1 to 100 W): phone chargers, auxiliary supplies, PoE and offline controllers, gate-drive supplies. Typical parts: EE, EFD or RM cores with a bobbin and 8 to 14 pins; windings: primary Np, one or more secondaries Ns, an auxiliary winding for the controller supply. A distributor listing for a WE-FB part (750311691, not the OHM-053 part) shows the order of magnitude: turns ratio 1:5, 60 uH primary inductance, 0.315 Ohm primary DCR, 1 uH leakage, 2.5 kV isolation, 6 pins (S23).

### 2. What it is and how it works

- **Energy storage in the gap.** A ferrite core without a gap would saturate at a tiny current; an air gap reduces the effective permeability so the same flux needs more MMF: "The transformer stores energy in its core. ... Add an air gap to core to reduce the equivalent permeability" and "Max. Energy ~ 1/2 * L * Isat^2", with the design requirement I_sat,prim >> I_pri,peak (S10). Energy per cycle is E = 1/2*Lp*Ipk^2, power P = E*f/efficiency.
- **Polarity matters**: with primary dot at the supply side and the secondary dot at the output return, the diode is on the non-dot secondary terminal; the diode conducts only while the switch is off. Reversing the secondary makes the converter a forward-type connection and it will not work as a flyback (the diode conducts during the on-time, shorting the primary through the secondary).
- **DCM (discontinuous) operation, lossless**: Ipk = Vin*D/(Lp*f); Vout = Vin*D*sqrt(R/(2*Lp*f)) independent of the turns ratio; the reflected output voltage Vor = (Vout + Vf)/N (N = Ns/Np). The demagnetizing time is t_dem = Lp*Ipk/Vor and must be below (1-D)/f for DCM.
- **Leakage inductance and the spike**: Llk is not coupled to the secondary. At turn-off its current has nowhere to go, so the drain voltage rises above Vin + Vor until a snubber or the switch absorbs the energy 1/2*Llk*Ipk^2. A WE presentation gives the spike as V = Ipk*Llk/(Cp+Cds) (S10); as extracted this is dimensionally inconsistent (H*A/F is not a voltage), so the simulation uses the energy balance V_spike = Ipk*sqrt(Llk/C) (resonant bound) which the bench confirms. An RCD clamp dissipates P_clamp = 1/2*Llk*Ipk^2*f*Vc/(Vc-Vor) in the textbook form; the bench shows this holds to 8 % with minimal parasitic capacitances and overpredicts by a factor of two when the realistic Cds, diode and interwinding capacitances absorb part of the leakage energy.
- **Saturation is catastrophic in a flyback**: when Ipk exceeds Isat the inductance collapses to LR*Lp and the current rises at about Vin/(LR*Lp) until the MOSFET fails or the controller's cycle-by-cycle limit trips.
- **Isolation**: the winding-to-winding barrier (the 750311691 listing says 2.5 kV; the OHM-053 part's value was not found). Creepage, safety class and insulation system are RESEARCH_REQUIRED; do not claim reinforced insulation.

### 3. How it connects

Windings: primary (Vin+ to switch drain), secondary (output rectifier and capacitor), auxiliary (controller VCC), possibly bias/feedback. The 3D spec reports that the WE-FB 750311595 has 12 pins with windings N1, N2, N3 on pins 1-6 and 7-12 but says "exact pin lists unreliable" (the WE-OLSTM 750871111 is a different 14-position part with different populated pins). **The winding-to-pin map is RESEARCH_REQUIRED.** In the behavior layer a flyback transformer is a user-assigned set of windings: PRI(dot, end), SEC(dot, end) and optional AUX(dot, end), with the dot on pin 1 of each winding by the OHMNI default (no source).

Typical circuit: Vin+ -> primary dot ... end -> switch drain; secondary dot to output return; secondary end -> diode anode -> cathode -> output; RCD clamp across the primary; snubber capacitor across the diode. Mistakes: wrong polarity of the secondary, insufficient gap/core (saturation), no clamp (switch avalanche), too large a leakage, forgetting that primary and secondary inductances scale with N squared.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation

Layer L1, fidelity `behavioural_approximation`. Same subcircuit `XFMR_SAT` as BEH-MAG-XFMR-SIGNAL (text there) with these mappings:

- `LP` = primary inductance (the gapped inductance, datasheet "inductance" in the primary winding), `LLK` = leakage inductance (datasheet "leakage inductance", primary referred, secondary shorted), `N` = Ns/Np, `RP`, `RS` = DCR, `CIW` = interwinding capacitance, `ISATM` = primary current at which the *inductance* has fallen by `DROP` (the datasheet "saturation current", the percentage must be read from the datasheet; default 0.3 with `assumed_drop=true` if not stated).
- Additional windings (aux): one more `Es/Vs/Fp` triple per winding referenced to the same magnetizing node (pb, p2) with the winding's own turns ratio. **This multi-winding extension was not benched** and is documented here as a recipe only.
- Switch: `S` with `.model SW SW(Ron=5m Roff=1G Vt=2.5 Vh=0.1)`; diode `.model DSCH D(IS=1e-7 N=1.05 RS=20m CJO=50p)`; these are bench models, not part data.

Valid analyses: `tran` (the converter), `ac` (small-signal around the operating point of the magnetics only; switching converters need averaged models, not provided), `op` (DC: inductors short, useful only for bias). Valid range: the magnetizing branch is valid up to saturation; the model has no frequency-dependent core loss and no winding resonance, so ring-down after a clamp event is qualitative.

Known limitations: tanh saturation from one point; no fringing-flux copper loss, no core loss, no proximity effect (these dominate efficiency in practice: the benches show 4.5 W in, 4.26 W out, 0.17 W clamp, about 0.1 W other, and have no core loss at all); leakage placed all on the primary; ring-down depends on Cds and Cj; multi-winding extension untested; timing of the switch is behavioural (no gate drive).

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior

| id | trigger | effect | sim_response | permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| core saturation | Ipk > ISATM (overload, startup, short on output, too long on-time) | current runaway, switch overstress | XFMR_SAT does it; ERROR flag at 1.0*ISATM | recoverable if the switch survives; switch failure is permanent |
| leakage spike | switch turn-off with no or undersized clamp | drain over-voltage, MOSFET avalanche | flag ERROR if `v_drain` exceeds `0.9*Vds_max`; open or short the switch model only if the user supplied its Vds rating | permanent (switch) |
| output short | secondary short | Ipk climbs until limit; reflected leakage energy bigger | WARN; relies on controller model (not provided) | recoverable |
| reversed secondary polarity | wrong dot wiring | no flyback action, forward conduction through diode | automatic in the netlist (circuit does not deliver) plus DRC polarity check once pin map is verified | recoverable |
| isolation breakdown | barrier voltage above rating | hazardous: loss of isolation | ERROR; this is a **safety** event | permanent |
| overheating | copper and core loss exceed rise rating | insulation damage | flag; core loss unmodeled so only copper | permanent |

### 8. Thermal behavior

Copper loss only: P = Ip_rms^2*RP + Is_rms^2*RS with Rth from a datasheet rise rating when one exists. No rating was found for OHM-053; core loss (Steinmetz) is missing and is the main loss in a real flyback, so the simulator must say "thermal estimate excludes core loss".

### 9. Appearance summary

See OHM-053: two ferrite E halves clamped on a bobbin with flanges, yellow tape wrap, 12 pins in two rows (about 29 mm by 32 mm by 13.7 mm). Pin 1 is marked on the bobbin flange. The pin function table is unreliable in the 3D spec.

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-MAG-XFMR-CT

Applies to OHM-054 (PCB current-sense transformer, Talema AS series, AS-103 representative). Layer L1. Library: `bench/mag_ct/xfmr.lib` (same `XFMR_SAT`).

### 1. Purpose and real-world use

A current transformer (CT) senses AC current with galvanic isolation. The primary carries the current to be measured (one or a few turns); the secondary has N turns and delivers a proportional current Is = Ip/N into a **burden resistor** that converts it to a voltage. Uses: switch-mode power supply current sensing for current-mode control and overload protection, AC current monitoring, motor and inverter current feedback (Talema: "low cost method of controlling, monitoring or measuring AC currents" for SMPS at 20 to 200 kHz, S14). It cannot measure DC.

### 2. What it is and how it works

- Ideal CT: Is = Ip/N, Vburden = Ip*Rb/N. Example from the AS-103 datasheet copy: 1:200, 100 Ohm termination, maximum secondary current 75 mA (S14), so 15 A primary peak gives 75 mA and 7.5 V across 100 Ohm. The AS series datasheet states "the output Voltage/Ampere ... can be increased or decreased linearly over a restricted temperature range by adjusting the terminating resistance" (S13).
- Real CT: secondary magnetizing inductance Lsec in parallel with the burden (set the low-frequency corner fL = (Rsec+Rb)/(2 pi Lsec)), winding resistance Rsec (voltage drop, accuracy), leakage (high frequency), capacitance. AS-103-class: 20 kHz to 200 kHz specified (S13, S14).
- **Core saturation**: the secondary can only generate a limited flux; Vsec*t beyond the core volt-second capacity (which depends on core area, turns and Bsat) saturates the core and the waveform clips. A large burden raises Vsec and so saturates sooner.
- **Open secondary hazard.** The primary current is imposed by the external circuit and cannot be reduced by the CT. With the secondary open, all of the (secondary-referred) current has to flow through the magnetizing branch: "Secondary Voltage = Primary Current x Magnetizing Impedance" and the core saturates, giving sharp voltage spikes (an engineering article, S16, says never to operate a CT open-circuit and mentions protection by MOVs or back-to-back zeners). The simulated spike height at the primary-current zero crossing equals Lsec*omega*Is_peak: bench B3 with Lsec = 10 mH, Ip = 15 A pk (Is = 75 mA pk) at 50 kHz gives 237.7 V peak versus 235.6 V analytic, versus 7.1 V with a 100 Ohm burden. With the 250 mH inductance in one distributor listing (S15, conflicting) the same formula gives about 5.9 kV, which exceeds the 2500 VAC isolation rating of the datasheet copy (S14): insulation breakdown and a shock hazard are realistic.
- A saturated core also retains remanence (accuracy shift after an open event; general practice, no source opened, confidence L).

### 3. How it connects

OHM-054 in the 3D spec has **three in-line pins** (1, 2, 3) with pin 2 present only on center-tapped versions (consistent with the AS datasheet: "Standard Type A has 3 pins; center-tapped versions add pin #2", S13). The datasheet copy dated 06-06 states pin 1 = primary sense current input, pin 2 = center tap (CT versions only), pin 3 = primary return / secondary ground, with the schematic labeled "Prim./Sec. Ratio" and isolation 2500 VAC (S14, summarizer reading). That description does not give an isolated primary a separate pair of pins, so **either the 3D spec's 3 pins do not include the primary connection, or the pin function in S14 was mis-summarized. The primary/secondary pin assignment is RESEARCH_REQUIRED** and the behavior layer treats the part as an abstract four-terminal CT (P1, P2, S1, S2) with an optional S_CT. The coordinator should reconcile the 3D spec (3 pins) with the electrical reality (an isolated CT needs a primary connection).

Typical circuit: primary in series with the load or switch current; secondary across a burden resistor (plus a rectifier diode and filter for peak or average sensing); burden always connected. Mistakes: leaving the secondary open (even briefly, e.g. a probe lifted or the burden resistor unsoldered), using at 50/60 Hz or DC (the lower corner of the AS series is 20 kHz), too large a burden (saturation), burden below the minimum (accuracy), forgetting that polarity (dots) matters for a rectified output.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation

Layer L1, `behavioural_approximation`. Use `XFMR_SAT` (text in BEH-MAG-XFMR-SIGNAL): primary winding P1 (dot) to P2, secondary S1 (dot) to S2.

```spice
* AS-103-class defaults (CONFLICTING sources, see below)
X{ref} {P1} {P2} {S1} {S2} XFMR_SAT LP={lsec/(N*N)} N={N} LLK={llk} RP=1u RS={rsec} CIW=1p ISATM={isatm_pri} DROP=0.3 LR=0.05
Rburden {S1} {S2} {Rb}
```

Mapping: `N` = turns ratio Ns/Np; `lsec` = datasheet secondary inductance; the model takes the primary-referred value LP = Lsec/N^2 (bench: 10 mH / 200^2 = 250 nH); `rsec` = secondary DCR; `ISATM` (primary referred) = N * (secondary magnetizing current at which Lsec has fallen 30 %): **no datasheet value was found, ASSUMPTION confidence L**; `llk` default 0.1 % of LP. **Source conflict for AS-103** (all LOW confidence):

| source | turns ratio | Lsec | DCR sec | termination | Isec max | primary current |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DigiKey listing (S15, Talema/Amgis) | 1:300 | 250 mH | 10 Ohm max | 10 Ohm secondary? ("10Ohm Secondary") | not shown | 15 A |
| Talema AS datasheet copy 06-06 via aggregator, AS-103 page (S14a) | 1:200 | 1 mH min (10 kHz, 10 mV) | 3 Ohm nom | 100 Ohm | 75 mA | 15 A (implied 75 mA*200) |
| same datasheet via the AS-211 aggregator page (S14b) | 1:200 | 10.0 mH min | 300 Ohm nom | 100 Ohm | 75 mA | |
| Talema AS series datasheet 07/18 (S13) | family 1:50 to 1:750 | 5 mH min (1:50) to 560 mH min (1:500) | 0.3 to 25 Ohm max | 25 to 500 Ohm | 300 mA (1:50) to 30 mA (1:500) | to 30 A (1:750) |

The simulator defaults chosen: N = 200, Lsec = 10 mH, Rsec = 3 Ohm (the lower of the two DCR readings), Rb = 100 Ohm, Ip max 15 A pk. Each is flagged `conflict=true`. The 15 A and 75 mA are mutually consistent for 1:200 (15/200 = 0.075), which weakly favors the 1:200 reading over DigiKey's 1:300.

Valid analyses: `tran` (waveform, saturation, open-secondary), `ac` (burden gain and corner), `op`. Valid range: 20 kHz to 200 kHz per datasheet; below that the corner at 1.6 kHz (for Lsec 10 mH, Rsec+Rb 103 Ohm) is a model value.

Known limitations: no measured Lsec(f); remanence is not modeled (the tanh branch has no memory); the open-secondary peak is a numerical stiffness problem (section 0 item 8): use `tmax <= 0.5 ns` for a 50 kHz, 15 A case or compute the peak analytically; no capacitive load of the secondary winding; the 1 uOhm primary resistance is a placeholder (primary DCR not given).

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior

| id | trigger | effect | sim_response | permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| open secondary | burden missing or open while primary carries current | secondary voltage spikes (hundreds of V here, kV for large Lsec), core saturates, insulation breakdown, shock; remanence offsets later accuracy | ERROR flag with the predicted peak; if predicted V_open_pk exceeds 0.7*Visolation peak (2.5 kVac -> 3.5 kV) mark the part failed (short primary-secondary insulation model) | permanent (insulation), remanence recoverable only by demagnetizing |
| core saturation by overload or large burden | Ip too large or Rb too large | output clips, ratio error | XFMR_SAT; WARN at Isec_max | recoverable |
| DC or very low frequency in primary | DC component | core walks into saturation, output near zero | model shows it (droop at fL) | recoverable |
| burden too small or shorted | Rb << nominal | output tiny, no hazard (secondary is the safe state) | none | recoverable |
| overcurrent heating | Ip above rating for long | primary and secondary heat | WARN; no thermal rating found | permanent if sustained |
| isolation breakdown | barrier voltage above 2500 Vac | shock hazard | ERROR | permanent |

### 8. Thermal behavior

Primary conductor loss and the secondary I^2*(Rsec+Rb) are small; the datasheet rise rating was not found. Skip detailed thermal modeling; carry the "Ta + 20 K <= 120 C" check as a placeholder (ASSUMPTION).

### 9. Appearance summary

See OHM-054: black encapsulated box about 17.2 by 9.5 by 20.4 mm with 3 in-line pins on 6.35 mm pitch (rectangular 0.66 x 0.45 mm). The 3D spec itself notes unresolved dimensions and unresolved primary/secondary assignment.

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-MAG-ETHMAG

Applies to OHM-055 (Ethernet 10/100 magnetics, 16-terminal SMD, Pulse H1102NL family representative). Layer L1 for the magnetics; the PHY/MAC and link protocol are L2/L3 and are not SPICE-simulable here. Library: `bench/mag_ethmag/ethmag.lib` (+ `cmc.lib`).

### 1. Purpose and real-world use

Ethernet magnetics sit between the PHY transceiver and the RJ45 connector of 10BASE-T and 100BASE-TX links. They (a) galvanically isolate the board from the cable (datasheet hipot 1500 Vrms minimum, S11), (b) AC-couple the differential signal, (c) match impedances, (d) provide a center tap on each winding through which the PHY's current-mode driver is biased, and (e) contain common-mode chokes that suppress common-mode noise and emissions on the cable side. A single-port part contains the transmit (TX) and receive (RX) channels. The Pulse H325.Q sheet describes "10/100BASE-T single port surface mount magnetics with various turns ratios": H1102NL, H1183NL, H1199NL, HX1188NL, HX1198NL and H1302NL are 1:1 TX / 1:1 RX; H1100NL is 2:1 TX; H1101NL 1.25:1 TX; H1121NL 1:1.414 TX (S11).

### 2. What it is and how it works

Per channel: a transformer with a center tap on both the PHY side and the cable (line) side ("1CT:1CT" for TX), followed on the line side by a two-winding common-mode choke. Differential 100BASE-TX or 10BASE-T signal passes the transformer 1:1 (insertion loss about 1 dB at worst across 100 kHz to 100 MHz, S11); common-mode current is blocked by the CMC and by the center-tap structure (CMRR 30 to 42 dB typical at 30 to 100 MHz, S11); DC is blocked completely by the transformer.

Datasheet figures found (Pulse H325.Q, 9/09, S11), all at 25 C:

| parameter | value |
|---|---|
| insertion loss 100 kHz to 100 MHz | -0.9 to -1.1 dB max |
| return loss at 30/60/80 MHz | -10 to -20 dB typ |
| common-mode rejection 30 to 100 MHz | -30 to -42 dB typ |
| crosstalk 30 to 100 MHz | -30 to -45 dB typ |
| hipot isolation | 1500 Vrms min |
| not given in that sheet | OCL and DC-bias spec, leakage inductance, interwinding capacitance, DCR |

The related Pulse H315.D sheet (H1038NL and H1094NL, 2:1 TX ratio, an older family) gives "350 uH OCL with 8 mA bias" guaranteed over 0 to 70 C and 1500 Vrms minimum isolation (S12), which is the only OCL figure obtained; it is a different part and is used here as the order of magnitude.

Why the center tap and the 8 mA DC bias spec: in 100BASE-TX the PHY drives currents through each half of the TX winding toward the center tap rail; those DC components flow in opposite halves and cancel their flux (balanced); the OCL-with-DC-bias spec therefore guards against small imbalance, not the full drive current.

**How a PHY connects** (general practice, not read from an opened document, confidence L): the PHY's TD+/TD- (and RD+/RD-) go to the PHY-side pins; the PHY-side TX center tap is tied to the supply rail the PHY datasheet requires (for current-mode drivers with 49.9 Ohm pull-ups to the same rail it is a decoupled supply node; some PHYs want it grounded through a capacitor); the line-side pins go to the RJ45 TX pair (RJ45 pins 1, 2) and RX pair (pins 3, 6); line-side center taps are commonly terminated with 75 Ohm resistors and a high-voltage capacitor to chassis. The PHY datasheet decides the PHY-side CT network, which is why the entry cannot be fully specified here.

### 3. How it connects

16 terminals, 8 per long side. The 3D spec numbers pin 1 at top-left, counter-clockwise to pin 16, rows 10.16 mm apart (UNCERTAIN). A TX channel needs 3 PHY-side and 3 line-side terminals, an RX channel the same: 12 signal terminals; the remaining 4 were not identified. **The assignment of the 16 package terminals to TD+, TD-, TDCT, RD+, RD-, RDCT and the line-side pins is RESEARCH_REQUIRED** (the H325.Q schematic is a drawing that the text extraction cannot read). The behavior layer exposes named functional pins, and the library part binds them to terminals after the datasheet pinout has been read from the drawing.

Mistakes: putting the PHY on the cable side; leaving a center tap floating when the PHY expects bias; routing signal traces across the isolation gap (creepage); using 10/100 magnetics for gigabit (different part); ignoring that a 2:1 TX ratio part (H1100NL) needs a PHY designed for it.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation

Layer L1, fidelity `behavioural_approximation`, linear (no saturation; the 8 mA imbalance spec is carried only as a check). Per channel `ETH_CH` (library `ethmag.lib`):

```spice
.subckt ETH_CH tdp tdm tdct lp lm lct OCL=350u LLK=0.4u RW=0.5 CIW=15p CMC_L=100u CMC_LS=0.1u CMC_RDC=0.1 CMC_C0=1p CMC_RPAR=1e9
.param lh={OCL/4}
.param kk={sqrt(1-LLK/OCL)}
Ra1 tdp a1x {RW/2}
LA1 a1x tdct {lh}
Ra2 tdct a2x {RW/2}
LA2 a2x tdm {lh}
Rb1 lxp b1x {RW/2}
LB1 b1x lct {lh}
Rb2 lct b2x {RW/2}
LB2 b2x lxm {lh}
K1 LA1 LA2 {kk}
K2 LA1 LB1 {kk}
K3 LA1 LB2 {kk}
K4 LA2 LB1 {kk}
K5 LA2 LB2 {kk}
K6 LB1 LB2 {kk}
Ciw1 tdp lxp {CIW/2}
Ciw2 tdm lxm {CIW/2}
Xcmc lxp lp lxm lm CMC_K L={CMC_L} LS={CMC_LS} RDC={CMC_RDC} C0={CMC_C0} RPAR={CMC_RPAR}
.ends
```

(Windings named `LA1..LB2`: a name starting with `B` is a behavioral source in ngspice.) Instantiate twice for TX and RX; a turns ratio other than 1:1 needs the line-side half-windings scaled by N^2 (not exercised by any bench).

Parameter mapping: `OCL` total open-circuit inductance of a full winding (S12: 350 uH min at 8 mA bias for the related family); `LLK` and `CMC_LS` leakage: **DERIVED by fitting** so that insertion loss at 100 MHz equals the datasheet limit (-1.1 dB max): LLK = 0.1 uH and CMC_LS = 0.1 uH give -1.03 dB (bench B1); these are therefore conservative worst-case values, not measured ones (a sweep of LLK/CMC_LS: 0.4/0.1 uH gave -4.3 dB; 0.2/0.05 uH gave -1.18 dB; 0.1/0.03 uH gave -0.36 dB; 0.05/0.02 uH gave -0.15 dB at 100 MHz); `RW` = 0.5 Ohm per full winding, `CIW` = 15 pF, `CMC_L` = 100 uH, `CMC_RDC` = 0.1 Ohm: ASSUMPTIONS confidence L (not in any opened document).

Valid analyses: `ac`, `tran`, `op`. Valid range: 100 kHz to 100 MHz (the datasheet band). Known limitations: linear only; return loss, crosstalk between channels and the CMRR figures were not fitted or benched; CMC symmetric; no center-tap termination network; not valid for gigabit or PoE bias currents; no PHY model: the driver is whatever the user connects (the bench uses ideal current sources with 49.9 Ohm terminations).

**L3 note.** Auto-negotiation, link pulses, MLT-3/NRZI coding, MAC framing and the PHY registers are not electrical behavior of this part. The magnetics model passes the waveform; a higher layer must provide the PHY.

### 6. Ratings and limits

| rating | check | source |
|---|---|---|
| isolation (hipot) | `abs(V_barrier) <= 1500*sqrt(2) = 2121 V peak`; test duration not stated, so this is a production-test limit, not a working-voltage rating; continuous working voltage RESEARCH_REQUIRED | S11, S12 |
| DC imbalance in a center-tapped half | `abs(DC(iA1) - DC(iA2)) <= 8 mA` WARN (the OCL test condition; DERIVED) | S12 |
| insertion loss | informational: model must show <= 1.1 dB at 100 MHz (fit) | S11 |
| frequency | 100 kHz to 100 MHz | S11 |
| temperature | 0 to 70 C guaranteed OCL in H315.D; H325.Q at 25 C | S11,S12 |
| PoE / high DC | not rated in the opened sheets: flag ERROR if a DC current above 8 mA imbalance flows (ASSUMPTION) | |

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior

| id | trigger | effect | sim_response | permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| isolation breakdown | barrier voltage above hipot rating (surge, ESD, lightning, mains fault on the cable) | loss of isolation: PHY and board exposed, hazard to users and equipment | ERROR; model the failed barrier as 100 Ohm from tdct to lct (ASSUMPTION) | permanent (safety event) |
| DC imbalance / PoE bias | DC current imbalance beyond 8 mA or PoE current through center taps | OCL falls, link errors; with PoE overheating | WARN/ERROR; saturation is not modeled in ETH_CH, so the check is by expression only | recoverable (saturation) or permanent (heat) |
| wrong orientation | PHY side and line side swapped | isolation barrier and CT bias mis-applied; link may still pass signals | DRC (needs verified pin map) | recoverable |
| common-mode surge | large CM energy | CMC saturates (not modeled here) | no response | recoverable |
| over-temperature | not rated in opened docs | | none | |

### 8. Thermal behavior

Negligible at signal currents: none modeled (no rating found).

### 9. Appearance summary

See OHM-055: wide black plastic case about 12.7 by 9.5 by 6.8 mm with 8 gull terminals on each long side (1.27 mm pitch), white print, pin-1 marking not documented. W and H conflict between two readings of the datasheet.

### 10. Validation benches

`/home/claude/behavior/bench/mag_ethmag/`.

| id | file | check | expected | measured | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | `B1_insertion_loss.cir` | insertion loss, 100 Ohm source and load, relative to a matched direct connection | mid-band IL = 20 log((Rs+RL)/(Rs+RL+Rw)), Rw = 0.5+0.5+2*0.1 = 1.2 Ohm: -0.052 dB (tol 0.01); at 100 MHz must meet >= -1.1 dB (fit) | 1 MHz: -0.0553 dB; 10 MHz: -0.0625 dB; 100 MHz: -1.033 dB | match at mid-band; the 100 MHz value is meeting the datasheet limit by construction of the fit |
| B2 | `B2_isolation_leakage.cir` | AC leakage through the barrier at 50 Hz | I = 2 pi f Ciw V = 4.712 nA/V (Ciw 15 pF assumed); 7.07 uA at 1500 Vrms | 4.7153 nA/V | match |
| B3 | `B3_tx_drive.cir` | 100BASE-TX style current-mode drive, 49.9 Ohm terminations to a 3.3 V CT, 100 Ohm line, 1 MHz square | per pin 49.9 in parallel with 50 = 24.97 Ohm, +-20 mA DM gives 0.9988 V (2.0 Vpp) before loss and droop; tol 5 % | -0.988 V and +1.045 V at the two plateaus (average magnitude 1.017 V, +1.8 %) | match within tol; the 4.6 % asymmetry of the +1.045 V sample is flux offset from the unbalanced start of the square wave (physical for a transformer), not a sign error |

Note: the first version of B3 started from a DC operating point with one pin sinking 40 mA; the resulting flux offset gave -1.8 V (a 1.8x error). That was a test-setup error (section 0 item 4), fixed by starting with both pins at 20 mA (zero net flux).

Return loss, crosstalk and CMR figures from the datasheet were not benched.

# PER-ENTRY SECTIONS

Conventions: "default instance" is what the library should place when the user drops the entry without choosing a value. `placeholder=true` means the number is not sourced and the UI must show the part as "value required". Pin numbering follows the 3D spec. Representative part numbers are only the ones named in the 3D spec or opened here.

## [OHM-041] 0603 chip inductor -> BEH-MAG-INDUCTOR

- Variants (from the 3D spec): multilayer ferrite (default), multilayer ceramic (HF), wirewound ceramic (larger envelope).
- Default instance (multilayer ferrite, reference Murata LQM18DN6R8M70#, 1608M = 0603, S6): L = 6.8 uH +-20 %, DCR 0.74 Ohm typ (0.96 max), Isat 120 mA (inductance-change rating, drop percentage not stated: use `drop=0.3`, `assumed_drop=true`), Itemp 330 mA (temperature rise not stated: use `dT_rated=40`, assumed), SRF 40 MHz min, ferrite core, -55 to +125 C. Cp upper bound = 1/((2 pi 40 MHz)^2*6.8 uH) = 2.33 pF. Q not stated (use `RP=1e9`). Rth derived = 40/(0.33^2*0.74*1.157) = 429 K/W (DERIVED from the assumed rise; ASSUMPTION confidence L).
- Wirewound ceramic variant (reference Murata LQW18AN15NJ10D, 0603, S5): L = 15 nH +-5 %, Q min 42 (test frequency not stated; bench assumes 100 MHz), SRF 4.5 GHz (listing says "max"; Murata convention is a minimum), DCR 85 mOhm max, Idc 700 mA, -55 to +125 C. Cp = 83.4 fF, RP = 637 Ohm (bench B3).
- Pin map: electrical A -> terminal 1 (-X, x = -0.65 mm), B -> terminal 2 (+X). Non-polarized; no marking.
- Package parasitics: Cp 0.08 to 2.3 pF by type (above); ESL is inside L (no separate ESL).
- Ratings: Isat 0.12 A, Irms 0.33 A (multilayer ferrite default); 125 C maximum.
- Notes: 0603 multilayer power-rated parts have very low saturation current; the layer must warn when a user places one in a DC supply path above Isat.
- Status: complete for the multilayer ferrite default (one real part opened); the multilayer ceramic variant has no values (RESEARCH_REQUIRED).

# R4: Diodes, rectifiers, bridges (OHM-056 to OHM-072)

Group R4 covers 17 library entries and 5 behavior classes. Layer for every class: **L1 analog** (ngspice D model plus R and B sources). Fidelity label for every netlist in this document: `behavioural_approximation` (each deck carries its own `.model`/`.subckt`, none is a vendor model). Two vendor SPICE files were opened as cross-checks (Nexperia 1N4148 and BAT54, S12 and S14 below) but are NOT attached to any OHMNI part, so no entry may claim `vendor_model`.

Evidence caveat (applies to every number below): datasheets were read through a web fetch tool that returns a model-written extraction of each PDF, not the PDF pages. Tabulated values were cross-checked against each other where two documents exist (conflicts are listed, not hidden), but graphs (VF vs IF, capacitance vs VR, derating curves) were NOT readable, so no number here comes from a datasheet graph. Where a value needed a graph it is marked ASSUMPTION.

Class index

| Class | Entries | One line |
|---|---|---|
| BEH-DIO-PN | OHM-056..066, OHM-070 | silicon pn junction diode: signal, rectifier, dual (SOT-23) |
| BEH-DIO-SCHOTTKY | OHM-067 | metal-semiconductor diode, low VF, high leakage |
| BEH-DIO-ZENER | OHM-068 | reference/regulator diode used in breakdown |

## Cross-cutting: pin convention reconciliation (read first)

* Electrical convention (SPICE `D name anode cathode model`, and the existing OHMNI roles `PinRole.ANODE` / `PinRole.CATHODE` in `src/ohmni/domain/component.py`): current flows anode to cathode.
* 3D spec convention for every two-lead diode package in this group: **terminal 1 = cathode (marked end, band/bar at -X), terminal 2 = anode (+X)**. The spec itself notes EDA libraries differ.
* Pin-to-package-terminal map used by the behavior layer for all two-lead entries: `K -> terminal 1`, `A -> terminal 2`. The SPICE instance line is therefore `D{ref} {net_of_terminal_2} {net_of_terminal_1} {model}`. Never write `D{ref} {t1} {t2}`: that mounts the diode backwards.
* Conflict in the repo: `src/ohmni/catalog/data/parts/GENERIC_LED_GREEN.json` numbers the LED pin 1 = A, pin 2 = K. The 3D spec numbers diode terminal 1 = K. Both can coexist only if the behavior layer binds by pin ROLE (anode/cathode) and each part record carries its own number-to-role table. Do not infer polarity from pin number. The existing verifier (`verifier/rules/led.py`) already resolves by role, which is the right pattern.
* Three-lead SOT-23 dual diodes (OHM-070) and four-lead bridges (OHM-071/072) use their own tables below.
* Spec inconsistency found: OHM-069 (and the generator note near spec line 8359) put SMB terminal centers at X = +/-2.425, while OHM-065 and PKG-SMX.SMB give +/-2.15 (span 5.4 and foot 1.1 give 2.7 - 0.55 = 2.15). 2.15 is the arithmetic result; 2.425 appears to be an error. SMA +/-2.0 and SMC +/-3.42 are consistent.

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-DIO-PN

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
A silicon pn junction diode passes current in one direction and blocks it in the other. Uses: rectification of AC (mains-frequency with 1N400x/1N540x/S1x, high-frequency with fast types), polarity protection, freewheeling/flyback across inductive loads (relays, motors), signal steering and clamping to rails (1N4148, BAV99), wired-OR, small-signal detection. Common values and series: 1N4148/1N914 (100 V, 200-300 mA, fast), 1N4001-1N4007 (50-1000 V, 1 A, slow), 1N5400-1N5408 (50-1000 V, 3 A), S1A-S1M (SMA 1 A), BAV99/BAV70/BAW56 (dual 100 V SOT-23), 1N4148W/WS (SOD-123/SOD-323).

### 2. What it is and how it works
A pn junction. Forward bias lowers the built-in barrier and injects minority carriers; current follows the Shockley equation

    I = IS * (exp(V_j / (N * Vt)) - 1),   Vt = kT/q = 25.86 mV at 27 C,   V_j = V_D - I*RS

where IS is saturation current, N the emission coefficient (1 for ideal diffusion current, approaching 2 when recombination dominates, as in small silicon signal diodes), and RS the ohmic series resistance of bulk and leads. At high current RS dominates and the curve goes linear. In reverse the current is about -IS (plus generation and surface leakage that grows with voltage and temperature), until avalanche/breakdown near BV.

Capacitance has two parts. Depletion (junction) capacitance Cj(V) = CJO / (1 - V/VJ)^M for reverse and small forward bias (linearised above FC*VJ). Diffusion capacitance is the stored charge Q = TT * I, which is what makes the diode keep conducting after the voltage reverses.

Reverse recovery: forward current stores charge Qs = TT * IF in the neutral regions. When the external circuit forces the current to reverse, the diode stays on (acts like a short) for a storage time ts until Qs is removed, then the junction depletes and reverse current decays over tt. Simple storage model: ts ~ TT * ln(1 + IF/IRM), IRM being the reverse current the circuit allows (set by VR and RL). Signal diodes (gold-doped or small die) have TT of a few ns; general-purpose rectifiers (1N400x, S1M) are "standard recovery", microseconds. The ngspice parameter TT is exactly this storage time constant.

Temperature: IS rises with temperature (ngspice: IS(T) = IS * (T/T0)^(XTI/N) * exp(EG*q*(T-T0)/(N*k*T*T0))), so at constant current VF falls about 1.5 to 2 mV/K. Leakage roughly doubles every 8 to 10 K in silicon (consensus; the 1N4007 sheets quote 5 uA at 25 C and 50 uA at 125 C max, S6).

### 3. How it connects
Two terminals, anode (A) and cathode (K, the banded end). Forward when V(A) > V(K) by about 0.6 to 0.9 V at small currents (more at amps). Typical circuits: half-wave rectifier into R||C; four of them as a bridge (see BEH-DIO-BRIDGE); reverse-polarity protection in series with the supply (costs one VF and VF*I of heat); flyback diode across a coil (cathode to the positive side); clamp to rail pair (BAV99: pin 3 to signal, pin 1 to GND, pin 2 to +V). Common mistakes: mounting backwards (band is the only cue); using a signal diode where amps flow (1N4148 is 300 mA); using a 1N400x as a fast switching rectifier above ~50 kHz (reverse recovery microseconds, large shoot-through in a buck converter); no series resistor on a clamp; ignoring reverse voltage with an inductive kick; putting a 1N4007 in series with a Zener for temperature compensation and expecting exact figures.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
**Layer:** L1. **Fidelity label:** `behavioural_approximation` (own `.model`, not a vendor model).

**ngspice primitive:** `D` with `.model ... D (...)`. Realistic mode adds nothing structural for the junction itself; optional extras: a parallel leakage resistor (only if leakage at a voltage below breakdown must match a datasheet figure, because the D model's reverse current is a flat -IS), and a thermal node for self-heating (Section 8).

Netlist template (2-lead; `{A}` is package terminal 2, `{K}` is package terminal 1):

```
D{ref} {A} {K} DMOD_{part}
.model DMOD_{part} D (IS={IS} N={N} RS={RS} CJO={CJO} VJ={VJ} M={M} TT={TT} BV={BV} IBV={IBV} EG={EG} XTI={XTI})
```

Ideal mode: `.model DIDEAL D (IS=1e-14 N=1 RS=0)` is the ngspice default diode (IS=1e-14 A, N=1, RS=0, CJO=0, VJ=0.8, M=0.5, TT=0, BV=infinity, IBV=1 mA; defaults read from the ngspice manual parameter table, S23). Use only for "does the topology work" checks.

**Parameter to datasheet mapping**

| Model parameter | Datasheet quantity | Extraction rule |
|---|---|---|
| IS, N, RS | VF vs IF | two anchor points (I1,V1), (I2,V2); see fit method below |
| CJO, VJ, M | Cd or CJ at a stated VR and f | CJO = Cd(VR) * (1 + VR/VJ)^M with VJ, M assumed (0.7, 0.4 to 0.5) unless a curve is read |
| TT | trr with test condition | TT ~ trr / ln(1 + IF/IRM) then trim in simulation to reproduce the datasheet trr condition |
| BV, IBV | V(BR) at stated IR | BV = V(BR); IBV = the IR quoted with it; subtract IBV*RS if the V(BR) is a terminal voltage |
| EG, XTI | VF tempco, IR vs T | keep EG=1.11, XTI=3 (ngspice defaults) for silicon; fit only if a tempco is given |

**Fit method (worked, all four numbers verified in ngspice):**
Two-point extraction. With anchors at I1 << I2, in the exponential region V = N*Vt*ln(I/IS + 1) + I*RS. Choose RS (or N) from knowledge of the part, then N = ((V2 - I2*RS) - (V1 - I1*RS)) / (Vt*ln(I2/I1)) and IS = I1 / (exp((V1 - I1*RS)/(N*Vt)) - 1). Datasheets usually give only MAXIMUM VF at one current, so a "max-corner" fit (all of VF max, IR max, Cd max, trr max) is conservative for losses, and a "typical" fit needs either a typical table entry or a graph. The brief forbids inventing graph values, so each fit below states where its anchors came from.

*Fit A: 1N4148 (typical anchors from vendor model, constrained by datasheet limits).*
Datasheet limits (S1 Vishay 81857, S2 Nexperia, S3 Fairchild): VF <= 1.0 V at 10 mA (max, only tabulated forward point for 1N4148), IR 25 nA at 20 V typ/max at 25 C and 50 uA at 150 C, V(BR) 100 V at 100 uA, Cd <= 4 pF at 0 V 1 MHz, trr <= 4 ns (IF = 10 mA, VR = 6 V, iR = 0.1*IR, RL = 100 ohm), Vishay alternate trr 8 ns (IF = IR = 10 mA, iR = 1 mA). No typical VF is tabulated, so the typical anchors are evaluated from the Nexperia 1N4148 PSPICE model (S4: IS 4.352e-9, N 1.906, RS 0.6458, CJO 0.705 pF, VJ 0.869, M 0.03, TT 3.48 ns, BV 110, IBV 100 uA): VF(1 mA) = 0.609 V, VF(10 mA) = 0.729 V, VF(100 mA) = 0.900 V (these three are OUR evaluation of the vendor model, not datasheet table entries). Fix RS = 0.6 ohm, fit on 1 mA and 100 mA: **IS = 5.537e-9 A, N = 1.944, RS = 0.600 ohm** (VF(10 mA) check 0.7304 V vs vendor-model 0.7286 V, 1.8 mV apart, and well under the 1.0 V max). CJO: datasheet Cd max 4 pF at 0 V (a ceiling, the vendor model's 0.7 pF is typical); default **CJO = 2 pF** (ASSUMPTION midpoint, L) with VJ 0.7, M 0.4 (ASSUMPTION). **TT = 23 ns** was trimmed in ngspice: with TT 20 ns the Vishay trr test (IF = 10 mA, VR = 6 V via RL = 100 ohm, trr measured from i = 0 to i = -1 mA) gives 3.41 ns, with TT 23 ns it gives 3.83 ns, just inside the 4 ns datasheet maximum (bench B2). The vendor model's TT 3.48 ns would give about 0.6 ns, i.e. a "typical", not max, corner. BV 100 V / IBV 100 uA from S1.

*Fit B: 1N4007 (typical anchor from onsemi, max anchor from Vishay).*
Anchors: VF typ 0.93 V at 1 A, max 1.1 V at 1 A (S7 onsemi Rev 12 Aug 2005 typ and max; S6 Vishay 1.1 V max). A second, low-current anchor is not tabulated, so N and RS cannot both be found: **N = 1.8 and RS = 0.03 ohm are ASSUMPTIONS (L)**, giving **IS = 4.02e-9 A (typical corner)** and IS = 1.04e-10 A (max-VF corner). The assumed N,RS imply VF(10 mA) about 0.69 V and VF(100 mA) about 0.80 V on the typical corner, which is plausible for a rectifier die but is not a datasheet number. CJ: 15 pF at VR = 4 V (S6); with VJ 0.7, M 0.5 assumed, **CJO = 38.9 pF** (bench B4 reproduces 15.0 pF at 4 V). trr is NOT listed in S6 or S7. Vishay S1M, a comparable 1000 V standard-recovery rectifier, lists trr typ 1.8 us (S9, test condition not in extraction). Default **TT = 3 us (ASSUMPTION, L)**. BV: datasheets give no breakdown figure for 1N4007; reverse current is specified only up to VRRM. Default BV = 1100 V, IBV = 5 uA (ASSUMPTION, L): the avalanche point is above 1000 V by margin; do not show breakdown below VRRM.

*Other rectifier corners (max-corner fits, N = 1.8, RS assumed):* 1N5400-1N5408 VF max 1.2 V at 3 A (S8): RS 0.015, IS = 5.05e-11, CJ typ 30 pF at 4 V gives CJO 77.7 pF. S1M: VF max 1.1 V at 1 A, CJ typ 12 pF at 4 V gives CJO 31.1 pF (S9). These carry L confidence for RS and N.

**Ideal vs realistic:** ideal = `IS=1e-14 N=1 RS=0` (0.7 V-ish knee, no capacitance, instantaneous). Realistic = fitted IS/N/RS, CJO/VJ/M, TT, BV/IBV, EG/XTI, optional leakage resistor and self-heating. Tolerance: VF is a max-limited quantity with unit-to-unit spread of at least +/-50 mV (consensus, ASSUMPTION), so Monte-Carlo should perturb IS by a log-normal factor rather than ngspice parameters like N. Temperature: IS(T) and VJ(T) via EG/XTI; default valid -55 to +150 C (S1 allows 175 C junction).

**Valid analyses:** op, dc, tran (including reverse recovery), ac (junction capacitance and small-signal rd = N*Vt/I), temp (via `.temp` or `set temp=`), noise (shot + thermal RS; flicker KF/AF default 0). Valid range: |I| below IFSM-related damage limits, VR below BV, junction below TJmax.

**Known limitations:** (1) The ngspice D model has a flat reverse current of -IS, so datasheet leakage at a rated VR needs an explicit parallel resistor (R = VR/IR) or the Nexperia trick of a large parallel resistor; leakage does not rise with temperature unless you add a temperature-dependent source. (2) One exponential cannot fit high-injection roll-off and low-current recombination knee over eight decades; accept +/-30 mV outside the anchor window. (3) TT models storage only; real recovery softness (snappiness) is not modelled. (4) Forward recovery (VFR overshoot at fast di/dt, Nexperia 2.5 V max for 1N4148) needs conductivity-modulation modelling the D model does not have. (5) Avalanche energy (EAS) is not modelled. (6) Package inductance (axial leads about 5 to 10 nH per lead pair, ASSUMPTION) matters only above tens of MHz and is not included.

| repetitive peak reverse | VRRM | 100 V | 1000 V (type dependent 50-1000) | 50-1000 V | by type | `max(vr) <= VRRM` | S1,S6,S8,S9 |
| continuous / average forward | IF / IF(AV) | 300 mA (S1), 200 mA (S3 avg, S4 header), IFRM 450 mA (S2) | 1.0 A at TA 75 C, 0.375 in leads | 3.0 A at TL 105 C, 0.5 in leads | 1.0 A | `mean(i_f) <= IF(AV)(Ta)` | S1,S2,S3,S6,S8,S9 |
| non-repetitive surge | IFSM | 2 A, 1 us (S1) vs 4 A, 1 us (S2) CONFLICT | 30 A (8.3 ms half sine), 45 A (1 ms square) | 200 A (8.3 ms) | 40 A (S1A-J), 30 A (S1K-M) | `i_peak*sqrt(t) <= IFSM*sqrt(t_ref)` see below | S1,S2,S6,S8,S9 |
| forward voltage max | VF | 1.0 V at 10 mA | 1.1 V at 1 A | 1.2 V at 3 A | 1.1 V at 1 A | info only | |
| reverse current | IR | 25 nA at 20 V, 25 C; 5 uA at 75 V (S1 typ); 50 uA at 20 V, 150 C | 5 uA (25 C), 50 uA (125 C) at VRRM | 5 uA (25 C), 500 uA (150 C) | 1 uA (25 C), 5 uA (125 C) | info | S1,S6,S8,S9 |
| power dissipation | Ptot | 500 mW at TL <= 25 C, 440 mW at 45 C (S1) | (RthJA 50 C/W PCB mounted) | (RthJA 20 C/W) | (RthJA 75 C/W, S1A-J; 85 for S1K-M) | `Tj = Ta + RthJA*(VF*IF_avg + other) <= TJmax` | S1,S6,S8,S9 |
| junction temp | TJmax | 175 C (S1,S3) | 175 C (S7 range), 150 C absolute not stated by S6 | | 150 C | `Tj <= TJmax` | |

Surge rule for the simulator: IFSM is quoted for a single 8.3 ms half sine (or 1 us for signal diodes). For other pulse widths use I^2*t-like scaling, `I_allowed(t) = IFSM * sqrt(t_ref / t)` for t between 1 ms and 100 ms (CONSENSUS engineering rule of thumb, ASSUMPTION L, not from an opened document); repeated surges count as repetitive and must obey IF(AV) and thermal limits. Derating: `IF(AV)(Ta) = IF(AV)_rated * (TJmax - Ta) / (TJmax - Ta_rated)` (linear to zero at TJmax, DERIVED, conservative; the Vishay 1N4007 curve extraction was ambiguous: one reading "1 A at 25 C falling to about 0.2 A at 150 C" conflicts with the table's 1.0 A at TA = 75 C, so use the table).

Source conflicts for 1N4148: IFSM 2 A (Vishay, 1 us) vs 4 A (Nexperia, 1 us); continuous IF 300 mA (Vishay) vs 200 mA (Fairchild and the Nexperia SPICE header; Nexperia datasheet IFRM 450 mA, a repetitive figure); trr 4 ns max under the same test condition in all three, Vishay adds 8 ns for the IF = IR = 10 mA condition. Use the conservative value (2 A, 200 mA) as default and let the part record override.

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior

| id | trigger | effect | sim_response | permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| overcurrent_avg | mean forward current > IF(AV)(Ta) or Tj > TJmax | silicon overheats, solder/lead heat, die cracks | flag WARN at 100% of rating, FAIL at 120%; after sustained FAIL mark part `failed_short` | permanent |
| surge | single pulse above IFSM(t) | die/bond wire melts; rectifier diodes most often end SHORT (alloy through junction), at extreme energy the bond wire fuses OPEN (CONSENSUS, not from an opened document; ASSUMPTION L) | flag FAIL; replace by 1 mOhm resistor (`failed_short`) as default, option `failed_open` (1 Gohm) | permanent |
| reverse_overvoltage | VR > VRRM | for NON-avalanche-rated rectifier types (the 1N400x/1N540x/S1x sheets opened give no avalanche energy), avalanche above BV concentrates in a hot spot and the diode shorts; type may survive a single microsecond transient only if avalanche-rated (rating not present in sources) | flag WARN at 0.8*VRRM, FAIL above VRRM; the model conducts above BV (IBV model) so the simulation shows the physical clamp but the verdict is FAIL; set `failed_short` after FAIL | permanent |
| reverse_polarity | installed backwards | blocks; downstream circuit sees no supply; or, as a protection diode, nothing conducts | no special action; the netlist is correct by polarity | recoverable |
| thermal | Ta high | VF falls (-1.57 mV/K at 10 mA verified, bench B7), leakage rises | temperature via `.temp`; check Tj | recoverable |
| esd | not specified in opened sheets | n/a | not modeled | n/a |
| short / open | external | none for the part | n/a | |

### 8. Thermal behavior
Self-heating `Pd = VF*IF_avg + VR*IR_leak`. Simple model: `Tj = Ta + RthJA * Pd`, one resistor to ambient (add Cth for transients): node `tj` in degC, `Rth tj ta {RthJA}`, current source into `tj` equal to power. Per-package RthJA (junction to ambient, datasheet-quoted, mounting-dependent): DO-35 350 K/W (4 mm leads, S1, S2); DO-41 50 C/W PCB mounted (S6, RthJL 25); DO-201AD 20 C/W (S8); SMA 75 C/W for S1A-S1J, 85 for S1K-S1M, RthJL 27/30 (S9); SMB and SMC rectifier values: see per-entry sections. Power limits at 25 C ambient from (TJmax - Ta)/RthJA with TJmax 150 C: SMA 1.7 W (using 75), see entries for the others. Leads dominate for axial parts: shorter leads or copper area lowers RthJA; the sheets quote specific lead lengths and pad areas, which OHMNI does not model, so use the quoted values as DEFAULT with the mounting note and expose `rth_ja` as an override.

### 9. Appearance summary
Glass or black epoxy cylinders with a single band at the cathode end (OHM-056 to OHM-058, MELF OHM-059/060) and small flat-lead rectangular SMD bodies with a cathode bar at the -X end (OHM-061 to OHM-066), per 3D spec entries of the same IDs. SOT-23 dual diodes (OHM-070) have no band and are identified by pin position only. The band or bar is the only polarity cue and must be visible at every LOD.

model:
  fidelity: behavioural_approximation
  spice_primitives: [D]
  netlist_template: |
    D{ref} {A} {K} DMOD_{ref}
    .model DMOD_{ref} D (IS={IS} N={N} RS={RS} CJO={CJO} VJ={VJ} M={M} TT={TT} BV={BV} IBV={IBV} EG={EG} XTI={XTI})
  valid_analyses: [op, dc, ac, tran, noise, temp]

  known_limitations:
    - "reverse current is flat -IS in ngspice D model; add R=VR/IR for datasheet leakage"

  - {name: junction_temperature, symbol: TJmax, value: 175, unit: C, condition: "signal types", check: "Ta + RthJA*Pd <= TJmax", source_ref: S1}

---

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-DIO-SCHOTTKY

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
A Schottky diode is a metal-semiconductor junction with a much lower forward drop (about 0.3 to 0.5 V) and no minority-carrier storage, hence almost no reverse recovery. Uses: output rectifiers in switch-mode supplies (SS14/SS34), reverse-polarity and OR-ing diodes, freewheel diodes in low-voltage buck converters, RF/detector and clamp duty for small-signal parts (BAT54/BAT42W). Series seen in sources: BAT42W (30 V, 200 mA, SOD-123), BAT54 (30 V, SOT-23), SS12-SS16 (20-60 V, 1 A, SMA), SS22-SS26 (2 A, SMB), SS32-SS36 (3 A, SMC).

### 2. What it is and how it works
Conduction is majority-carrier thermionic emission over a metal-semiconductor barrier of height phi_B: IS = A*A**·T^2·exp(-q·phi_B/kT) (textbook). A low barrier gives low VF but a larger IS, hence (1) much higher reverse leakage than a pn diode, (2) leakage that rises steeply with temperature, and (3) a lower breakdown voltage (rated 20 to 100 V in the sheets opened). The same Shockley form applies with N close to 1 (1.0 to 1.1 typical) and a small RS. Junction capacitance is relatively large (tens to hundreds of pF) and, with no stored charge, TT is zero: switching is limited by capacitance only.
Thermal runaway: leakage power P = VR*IR(T) heats the die, raising IR, raising P. If Rth*dP/dT >= 1 there is no stable operating point and the device destroys itself. Quantitatively (this class, bench B3): with IR doubling roughly every 16 K (datasheet 25x from 25 to 100 C, i.e. a = ln(25)/75 = 0.0429 /K), Tj = Ta + Rth*VR*IR25*exp(a*(Tj-25)); no solution exists when Rth*VR*IR25*a*e*exp(a*(Ta-25)) > 1.

### 3. How it connects
Two pins, A and K, same polarity convention as BEH-DIO-PN. Typical: freewheel diode across the switch node (K to the switch node's high side), output rectifier, OR-ing of two supplies, solar/battery reverse blocking. Mistakes: using a 40 V part with ringing above 40 V (no avalanche rating in the sheets), running hot with reverse voltage near rating (runaway, see above), assuming the VF at 1 A holds at 25 mA, using 1 A parts for 3 A peaks (surge only), ignoring that leakage at 85 C can be milliamps (it matters in battery standby).

### 4. Electrical model
**Layer:** L1. **Fidelity:** `behavioural_approximation`.
Primitives: `D` (forward and capacitance), `B` source for reverse leakage with temperature.

```
D{ref} {A} {K} DSCH_{ref}
.model DSCH_{ref} D (IS={IS} N={N} RS={RS} CJO={CJO} VJ={VJ} M={M} TT=0 BV={BV} IBV={IBV} EG={EG} XTI={XTI})
Bleak_{ref} {A} {K} I = {IR_ref/VR_ref} * v({A},{K}) * exp({aT}*(temper-25))
```
(`aT = ln(IR_hot/IR_cold)/(T_hot-T_cold)`; the B source is a linear conductance between A and K; for V(A,K) > 0 it adds a tiny forward error, negligible at VF levels, and in reverse it gives the datasheet leakage at VR_ref scaled linearly with voltage; real leakage grows faster than linearly near rated voltage, ASSUMPTION flagged.) The `temper` variable in ngspice B-source expressions follows `.temp`/`set temp=` (verified in bench B2).

**Fit (SS14, max-corner), worked:**
Sources: Vishay SS12-SS16, doc 88746, 23-Apr-2020: VRRM 40 V, IF(AV) 1 A, IFSM 40 A, IR 0.2 mA (25 C) and 5.0 mA (100 C) at rated VDC, RthJA 88 C/W, RthJL 28 C/W, TJ 150 C (S10). VF max: the 88746 extraction reported 0.75 V at 1 A, the Fairchild/onsemi SS14 page 0.50 V (S11), and the Vishay SS22-SS26 sheet gives 0.5 V (SS22-SS24) and 0.7 V (SS25-SS26) at 2 A (S12) and SS32-SS36 gives "0.5 V, 0.75 V by type" (S13). CONFLICT: the 0.75 V value almost certainly belongs to the SS15/SS16 columns, not SS14. **Decision: SS14 VF max = 0.50 V at 1 A** (M confidence). No typical VF is tabulated and the VF graph is unreadable, so a single anchor exists; N = 1.05 and RS = 0.05 ohm are ASSUMPTIONS (L) and IS = 6.37e-8 A follows from the anchor, giving VF(10 mA) = 0.325 V (not a datasheet number). Leakage: Gleak = (0.2 mA / 40 V) * exp(0.0429*(T - 25)), which reproduces both datasheet points (B2). EG for the D-model IS tempco chosen so IS rises 25x from 27 to 100 C with XTI = 2: **EG = 0.296 eV** (DERIVED, ASSUMPTION L; only affects forward VF tempco). CJO: Vishay quotes a capacitance curve only in the extraction (not numerically readable); default **CJO = 110 pF at 0 V (ASSUMPTION, L)** with VJ 0.4, M 0.45. BV = 45 V (just above VRRM 40, ASSUMPTION), IBV = 1 mA.

**Small-signal Schottky (BAT54 class):** the Nexperia BAT54 SPICE file (S14) gives IS 2.117e-7, N 1, RS 2.7, CJO 8 pF, BV 56 V, with datasheet maxima VF 0.8 V at 100 mA, IR 2 uA at 25 V, VR 30 V. Evaluating the vendor model gives VF(100 mA) = 0.608 V, which satisfies the 0.8 V max. Use these as the default parameters for OHM-067 in SOD-123 and SOD-323 (they come from a Nexperia model, so they are DERIVED/vendor-extracted, M confidence, and the file's license terms are not known: do not redistribute the file, store only the numbers).

**Ideal vs realistic:** ideal = `D(IS=1e-14 N=1 RS=0)`. Realistic adds RS, CJO, leakage B source, temperature. **Valid analyses:** op, dc, tran, ac, temp. The thermal loop (Section 8) needs `tran` or a nonlinear `op` with the B-source reading the thermal node. **Valid range:** VR < VRRM, Tj <= 150 C (leakage fit is anchored at 25 and 100 C only).
**Known limitations:** reverse leakage vs voltage shape is linear (real is superlinear); VF tempco poorly constrained (no sourced tempco); no Schottky barrier lowering; no avalanche energy (Vishay SS32-SS36 quotes EAS 20 mJ non-repetitive avalanche energy, S13, which the sim does not use).

| VRRM | 40 V | 40 V | 40 V | 30 V | `max(vr) <= VRRM` |
| IF(AV) | 1.0 A | 2.0 A | 3.0 A | (IF not extracted) | `mean(if) <= IF(AV)(Ta)` |
| IFSM | 40 A | 75 A | 100 A | n/a | surge rule as BEH-DIO-PN |
| VF max | 0.50 V at 1 A (S11; see conflict) | 0.5 V at 2 A | 0.5 V (SS32-SS34 by type, at 3 A) | 0.8 V at 100 mA | info |
| IR max | 0.2 mA (25 C), 5 mA (100 C) | 0.4 mA (25 C), 10 mA (100 C) | not extracted | 2 uA at 25 V | `Ta + Rth*(VR*IR(Tj)+VF*IF) <= TJmax` and runaway check |
| RthJA / RthJL | 88 / 28 C/W | 75 / 17 C/W | RESEARCH_REQUIRED (the 88746-family SMC value not retrieved; TVS SMC is 75 / 15 C/W, S18, use as proxy) | | |
| TJmax | 150 C | 150 C | 150 C | | |

Runaway check the simulator evaluates each thermal step: `unstable if Rth * VR * IR_ref * aT * exp(aT*(Tj - 25)) * (VR/VR_ref)^0 >= 1` (using the linear leakage model; derivation in Section 2 and bench B3).

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior

| id | trigger | effect | sim_response | permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| reverse_overvoltage | VR > VRRM | Schottky has no controlled avalanche except where EAS is quoted (SS32-SS36: 20 mJ); beyond that junction damage, usually leakage rises then short | WARN above 0.8*VRRM, FAIL above VRRM, `failed_short` | permanent |
| thermal_runaway | Rth*VR*IR*a >= 1 (hot ambient, high VR, small copper) | leakage power heats the die until it shorts | FAIL when Tj reaches TJmax in `tran`, or when the stability inequality is violated in `op`; `failed_short` | permanent |
| overcurrent / surge | as BEH-DIO-PN | as BEH-DIO-PN | as BEH-DIO-PN | permanent |
| reverse_polarity | backwards | leaks (up to mA at hot) rather than blocks fully | model includes leakage; no extra action | recoverable |

### 8. Thermal behavior
Same single-node model as BEH-DIO-PN. Package RthJA in the table above. Add the leakage term `Pd_rev = VR*IR(Tj)` (usually negligible at 25 C, 8 mW at 40 V max for SS14 and dominant near 85 C). Bench B3 implements the electrothermal loop: node `tj` (V = degC), power B-source `I = G(Tj)*VR^2` into `tj`, `Rth` to an ambient source and `Cth` for dynamics.

### 9. Appearance summary
Default package SOD-123 per OHM-067 (matte black body, silver cathode bar at -X, two flat gull-wing leads); alternates SMA/DO-41/DO-201AD/SOD-323 follow their own 3D entries. Polarity is shown only by the bar or band.

### 10. Validation benches (`/home/claude/behavior/bench/beh-dio-schottky/`)

| id | file | what | expected | measured |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | B1_fwd_iv.cir | SS14 forward V at 1 A and 10 mA | 0.500 V at 1 A (fit anchor); 0.325 V at 10 mA (formula) | 0.49986 V, 0.32529 V MATCH |
| B2 | B2_leak_temp.cir | leakage at 40 V, 25 C and 100 C via `set temp` | 0.2 mA and 5.0 mA | 0.200059 mA, 5.00082 mA (residual from the diode's own IS) MATCH |
| B3 | B3_thermal_runaway.cir | electrothermal loop, Rth 88 K/W, 40 V, IR25 0.2 mA | stable Ta = 60 C: Tj = 63.7072 C from solving Tj = Ta + Rth*P(Tj); runaway ambient 83.24 C so Ta = 95 C must diverge | Tj = 63.7072 C at 40 s (MATCH to 4 digits); at Ta = 95 C Tj peaks above 773 C within 1 s, i.e. diverges as predicted MATCH |

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-DIO-ZENER

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
A Zener (or avalanche reference) diode is operated in reverse breakdown to hold a nearly constant voltage VZ. Uses: simple shunt regulators and references (with a series resistor), over-voltage clamps on logic and ADC inputs, level shifting, bias strings. Series: BZX55 (DO-35, 500 mW, 2.4 to 75 V), BZV55 (MiniMELF, 500 mW), BZX85 (DO-41, 1.3 W), BZX384/MMSZ (SOD-323/SOD-123), 1N52xx (DO-35), 1N47xx (DO-41 1 W). Values follow E24 (e.g. 3.3, 3.6, 3.9, 4.3, 4.7, 5.1 ... 10 V).

### 2. What it is and how it works
Heavily doped junctions have a thin depletion region. Below about 5 V the breakdown is quantum tunnelling (Zener effect) with a NEGATIVE temperature coefficient; above about 6 V it is avalanche multiplication with a POSITIVE coefficient; near 5 to 6 V the two cancel (TC near zero), which is why 5.1 V parts are the usual reference choice (Vishay data in the next paragraph shows this directly). The breakdown I-V is a steep exponential plus the ohmic RS, giving a dynamic impedance rZ = dV/dI that is smallest at moderate current and large at the knee (low current).

Data for BZX55 (S15, Vishay doc 85604 Rev. 2.0, 07-Nov-2024, via extraction): BZX55C5V1: VZ 4.8 to 5.4 V at 5 mA, rZ < 35 ohm at 5 mA and < 550 ohm at 1 mA, TC -0.02 to +0.02 %/K, IR < 0.1 uA at 25 C and < 2 uA at 150 C. BZX55C10: VZ 9.4 to 10.6 V at 5 mA, rZ < 15 ohm at 5 mA and < 70 ohm at 1 mA, TC +0.03 to +0.1 %/K. Ptot 500 mW at 25 C, RthJA 300 K/W (4 mm leads), DO-35.

Forward bias behaves as an ordinary silicon diode (about 0.7 V).

### 3. How it connects
Two pins. The CATHODE goes to the more positive node: in regulation the cathode is positive and current flows cathode to anode (reverse through the junction). Typical circuit: Vin -> Rs -> node (cathode) -> load in parallel with the Zener to ground (anode at ground); Rs = (Vin_min - VZ) / (IZ_min + IL_max) and the dissipation must stay under the derated power at Vin_max, no load. Mistakes: installing backwards (it then clamps at 0.7 V, "regulates" nothing); no series resistor; too little IZ so it sits at the knee (rZ explodes, VZ drops); power derating ignored; paralleling Zeners expecting current sharing; relying on the tolerance bin (E24 5 % or 2 %) for accuracy; expecting low noise.

### 4. Electrical model
**Layer:** L1. **Fidelity:** `behavioural_approximation`.

```
.subckt DZ A K
DF A K DFWD_{ref}            * forward conduction (ordinary diode)
DR A K DZB_{ref}             * breakdown branch, conducts for V(K) > V(A) + BVeff
RLK K A {RLEAK}              * leakage at sub-breakdown voltages
.ends
.model DFWD_{ref} D (IS=5e-9 N=1.9 RS=1.0 CJO={CJ} VJ=0.7 M=0.4 TT=50n)
.model DZB_{ref}  D (IS=1e-15 N=1 RS={RSZ} BV={BVeff} IBV={IZT} NBV={NBV})
```
Mapping (fit, verified): rZ(IZT) = NBV*Vt/IZT + RSZ (the slope of the model's exponential plus RS; bench B1 shows ngspice agrees to +/-1 ohm). Because RS also adds the drop IBV*RSZ, the breakdown parameter must be `BVeff = VZ - IZT*RSZ` so the terminal voltage at IZT equals VZ. Worked fit, **BZX55C5V1:** VZ = 5.1 V at 5 mA (the range 4.8 to 5.4 V is the bin), rZ = 35 ohm at 5 mA (datasheet MAXIMUM, conservative for regulation): choose RSZ = 19.5 ohm and NBV = 2.7, so BVeff = 5.1 - 0.005*19.5 = 5.0025 V, producing VZ = 5.1000 V and rZ = 35.0 ohm (bench B1). Realistic mode uses the max rZ; ideal mode uses the nominal VZ with `RSZ = 1`, `NBV = 1`.

**Known fit limitation:** the datasheet also gives rZ < 550 ohm at 1 mA (a soft knee). A single exponential cannot match both: with these parameters rZ(1 mA) is about 100 ohm, so the model regulates BETTER than the part at low current. Operating below about 1 mA must be flagged as "outside model validity" and VZ there is optimistic. Temperature coefficient (TC) is not in the netlist (ngspice's TBV1 is not used): apply `VZ(T) = VZ*(1 + TC*(T-25))` by editing BVeff per `.temp` step, with TC from the sheet (+/-0.02 %/K for 5.1 V, +0.03 to +0.1 %/K for 10 V); implement as a parameterised BV expression in the template. **Valid analyses:** op, dc, tran, ac, temp (with TC parameter). Valid range: IZ from about 1 mA to Ptot/VZ, Tj <= TJmax.
Leakage RLEAK: datasheet IR < 0.1 uA at 25 C at a test VR not captured in the extraction; default `RLEAK = 100 Meg` (50 nA at 5 V, ASSUMPTION L).
Forward diode: IS/N/RS above are generic silicon-diode ASSUMPTIONS (L); VF at IF is not extracted from the Zener sheets.

### 6. Ratings and limits
Power: `Pz = VZ_actual * IZ`; derated `Pmax(Ta) = (TJmax - Ta)/RthJA` = 0.5 W at 25 C, 0 W at 175 C (check `Pz <= Pmax(Ta)`). Package alternatives (from the 3D spec variant list): 500 mW glass (DO-35, MiniMELF), 1 W and 1.3 W molded DO-41 (power figures for those two are NOT from an opened document and need research; the opened Vishay sheet is BZX55 and BZV55 is cited only by the spec). Forward: treat like a signal diode (IF about 200 mA, ASSUMPTION). Surge: not in extraction; RESEARCH_REQUIRED.

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior

| id | trigger | effect | sim_response | permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| overpower | Pz > Pmax(Ta) | junction overheats; Zener usually fails SHORT, can open at extreme (CONSENSUS, ASSUMPTION L) | WARN at 80% of Pmax, FAIL above 100%; `failed_short` | permanent |
| knee_operation | IZ < 1 mA | VZ droops, rZ large; regulation lost | flag "outside validity", model optimistic | recoverable |
| reverse_polarity | installed backwards | acts as 0.7 V diode, supply is clamped to a diode drop | none needed; netlist is right | recoverable |
| overcurrent_forward | IF above diode rating | as BEH-DIO-PN | as BEH-DIO-PN | permanent |
| zener_with_no_series_R | source stiff, IZ unlimited | immediate overpower | detected by Pz check | permanent |

### 8. Thermal behavior
`Tj = Ta + RthJA * Pz`, with VZ tempco feeding back (positive TC above about 6 V reduces regulation margin and tends toward thermal instability only with constant-voltage drive). Self-heating shifts VZ by `TC * (Tj - 25)`; for the 10 V part a 100 K rise moves VZ by +3 to +10 %.

### 9. Appearance summary
Default package SOD-123 (OHM-068) with a cathode bar at -X; DO-35 glass body for 1N52xx/BZX55 types, MiniMELF for BZV55 (blue cathode marking documented by Vishay for that series in the 3D spec), DO-41 molded for 1 W types. Cathode marked at the -X end, and unlike the other diodes the marked end is the one that goes positive in regulation.

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-DIO-TVS

### 1. Purpose and real-world use and HAZARD
A transient voltage suppressor (TVS) avalanche diode clamps surges (ESD, EFT, inductive kick, lightning-induced pulses) to a voltage the downstream circuit survives, by shunting the surge current to ground. Placed across a supply rail or I/O line. Series: SMAJ (400 W, SMA), SMBJ (600 W, SMB), SMCJ (1500 W, SMC), all with 10/1000 us peak pulse power ratings. HAZARD: a TVS that is too weak, under-rated for the surge, or fed from a source that can supply sustained current will fail. The common failure mode is a SHORT circuit (CONSENSUS; see failure table), so the protected supply is then shorted and the source (battery, supply, cable) must be fused or current-limited; a shorted TVS across a lithium or high-current source can overheat. Treat every clamp as safety-relevant and keep to the datasheet limits below, derated.

### 2. What it is and how it works
A large-area silicon junction designed to avalanche at a defined breakdown voltage VBR and to carry large pulse current. Terms (from S16 and the SMAJ/SMCJ sheets):
* VWM (reverse standoff voltage): the working voltage at which leakage ID is specified (SMBJ15A: VWM 15 V, ID 1 uA max). Operate at or below VWM.
* VBR (breakdown voltage) at test current IT: minimum guaranteed (SMBJ15A: 16.7 V min at 1 mA; SMAJ15A lists a window of 16.7 to 18.5 V).
* VC (clamping voltage) at the peak pulse current IPP: the maximum voltage across the part during the surge (SMBJ15A: 24.4 V at 24.6 A).
* PPPM = VC * IPP, the peak pulse power for a 10/1000 us exponential pulse (10 us rise to peak, decay to half value at 1000 us), at 25 C: SMAJ 400 W, SMBJ 600 W, SMCJ 1500 W. Checks: 24.4 V * 24.6 A = 600 W (SMBJ15A); 24.4 V * 16.4 A = 400 W (SMAJ15A); 26.9 V * 55.8 A = 1501 W (SMCJ15A uni, S18).
* Dynamic resistance rdyn = (VC - VBR) / IPP; for SMBJ15A with VBR near 17.6 V: (24.4 - 17.6) / 24.6 = 0.28 ohm.
* Unidirectional (band = cathode): clamps positive surges in reverse avalanche and conducts about 0.7 to 2 V in forward for negative surges. Bidirectional (suffix C or CA, no band): two opposed junctions clamp both polarities symmetrically.
* Response time is "very fast" per Vishay (picosecond-class junction), so the clamp is limited by lead inductance and the surge source, not the diode.
* Surge current IFSM of the forward junction (unidirectional only): SMAJ 40 A, SMBJ 100 A, SMCJ 200 A (8.3 ms half sine, S16, S17, S18).
* Temperature coefficient of VBR: SMBJ5.0A 0.057 %/C, SMBJ15A 0.088 %/C, SMBJ24A 0.096 %/C (S16).

### 3. How it connects
Two pins. Unidirectional: cathode to the protected rail (positive), anode to ground (or return); the part must be reverse-biased in normal operation, so VWM >= max working rail voltage with margin. Bidirectional: either orientation, use on AC lines, differential data lines and signals swinging both sides of ground. Place as close as possible to the connector with a short low-inductance return. Mistakes: VWM below the working voltage (it conducts continuously and overheats); choosing VBR above the absolute max of the protected IC (VC is what the IC sees); no fuse or current limit upstream; placing it after a long inductive trace; using a unidirectional part on a bipolar signal; ignoring TVS capacitance on high-speed lines (hundreds of pF to nF for large parts).

### 4. Electrical model
**Layer:** L1. **Fidelity:** `behavioural_approximation`. Pulse clamping is real avalanche behavior and is well modelled by the D model's breakdown branch; temperature, energy and failure are not.

```
.subckt TVSU A K              * unidirectional: A anode, K cathode
DF A K DFWD_{ref}             * forward junction (low drop)
DR A K DTVS_{ref}             * avalanche branch
RLK K A {VWM/ID}              * leakage at standoff
.ends
.model DFWD_{ref} D (IS=1e-9 N=1.5 RS=0.05 CJO={CJ})
.model DTVS_{ref} D (IS=1e-15 N=1 RS={RDYN} BV={VBRnom} IBV=1m NBV=1)
```
Fit (SMBJ15A, worked, bench B1): VBR nominal 17.6 V (ASSUMPTION: midpoint of the 16.7 to 18.5 V window the SMAJ15A sheet gives; SMBJ sheets give only the min 16.7 V), IPP 24.6 A, VC 24.4 V: with NBV = 1 the exponential adds Vt*ln(IPP/IBV) = 0.26 V between 1 mA and 24.6 A, so RS = (24.4 - 17.6 - 0.26)/24.6 = **0.266 ohm**; simulated 24.416 V at 24.6 A and 17.61 V at 1 mA. To use the guaranteed MINIMUM VBR instead (a more pessimistic standoff margin, optimistic for VC), set BV = 16.7 V and RS from the same VC point. Leakage at VWM: RLK = VWM/ID, 15 V / 1 uA = 15 Meg.
Bidirectional model (bench B3): two TVSU cells in anti-series (A - cell1 - m - cell2 - B). Each cell's forward junction must be low-drop (IS = 1e-6, RS = 5 mohm, about 0.56 V at 24.6 A) so the avalanche branch is trimmed (BV = 17.42 V, RS = 0.25 ohm) for the same 24.4 V total; this is symmetric by construction.
**Valid analyses:** op, dc, tran (surge waveforms), ac. **Valid range:** pulse peak at or below IPP at the rated pulse; ambient 25 C.
**Known limitations:** (1) no pulse-width derating curve (Vishay Fig. 1/Fig. 3 were not readable); the simulator therefore uses PPPM only for a 10/1000 us pulse and a rule-of-thumb scaling for other widths (peak power allowed ~ (1000 us / tp)^0.5 for 10 us to 1 ms; ASSUMPTION L, not from an opened document); (2) the temperature derating extraction ("100% at 25 C falling to about 60% at 150 C") is suspicious (the Vishay curve normally reaches zero at TJmax); use linear derating to zero at TJmax 150 C as the conservative default; (3) capacitance not extracted (default CJ is an assumption); (4) VBR temperature coefficient applied by parameter edit per step; (5) the clamp can overshoot above VC by lead inductance L*di/dt in the real world, not modelled; (6) energy dissipation over repeated pulses (repetition rate 0.01 percent duty in sheet footnotes) not modelled.

### 5. Parameters (SMBJ15A default; SMAJ and SMCJ per entry section)

| name | unit | value | tolerance | basis | conf | source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| VWM | V | 15 | | MFR_DATASHEET | H | S16 |
| VBR (min / nominal) | V | 16.7 at 1 mA / 17.6 | window 16.7-18.5 (SMAJ15A) | MFR_DATASHEET / ASSUMPTION | M / L | S16,S17 |
| VC at IPP | V | 24.4 | max | MFR_DATASHEET | H | S16 |
| IPP | A | 24.6 | | MFR_DATASHEET | H | S16 |

### 6. Ratings and limits
Per package at 25 C and 10/1000 us: SMA 400 W (SMAJ, S17, doc 88390 08-May-07), SMB 600 W (SMBJ, S16, doc 88392 09-Jan-2024), SMC 1500 W (SMCJ, S18, doc 88394 07-May-07). Checks:
* `P_pulse_peak = max(v*i) <= PPPM(tp) * derate(Tj)` for a 10/1000 us-like pulse; for other tp use the Ppk scaling above.
* `I_pulse_peak <= IPP`; `V_clamped <= VC` (report as info; VC is what the downstream part sees; compare with the protected part's absolute maximum).
* `V_rail_max <= VWM` (continuous).
* `average power` over repetition: TVS is rated for pulses, not continuous power; continuous dissipation is limited by `(TJmax - Ta)/RthJA`, about 1.25 W for SMB at 25 C (100 C/W), 1.0 W for SMA (120 C/W), 1.67 W for SMC (75 C/W); the leakage + conduction power in normal use should be well below 10 percent of that.
* Forward surge (unidirectional negative excursions): `i_forward_pk <= IFSM`.

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior

| id | trigger | effect | sim_response | permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| pulse_overpower | pulse peak power > PPPM(tp) | junction melts through; the part fails SHORT-circuit (CONSENSUS engineering practice for silicon TVS, intended as a fail-safe; no opened document states it, so ASSUMPTION L; treat a TVS that has been stressed beyond rating as shorted and the rail as dead) | FAIL, replace the part with 10 mohm (`failed_short`); the downstream sim then shows a collapsed rail | permanent |
| continuous_overvoltage | VR > VWM continuously, sustained above VBR | continuous avalanche heats the die, thermal runaway, short | WARN above VWM, FAIL if sustained current * V > the continuous limit or Tj > TJmax | permanent |
| source_not_limited | upstream source can deliver more than the rail rating after a short | wire, PCB trace, connector or battery overheats; possible fire | the safety check must require a series fuse or limit when a TVS is on an energy-rich rail; flag HAZARD when none is present | n/a |
| repetitive_surge | many surges | degradation (VBR drift, leakage rise) | count pulses; WARN beyond a configured count | permanent |
| reverse_orientation (unidirectional) | installed backwards | conducts as a forward diode (about 0.7 V) on the normal rail, rail is clamped to a diode drop, large current | simulated by the netlist; flag as miswire | recoverable if current-limited |

### 8. Thermal behavior
Pulse heating is adiabatic (a 1 ms pulse is shorter than the thermal time constant of the package); use the power-versus-pulse-width rating. For continuous leakage dissipation use `Tj = Ta + RthJA*P` with RthJA SMA 120, SMB 100, SMC 75 C/W (S17, S16, S18). VBR rises with temperature by TC (0.088 %/C for SMBJ15A, so +5.5 % at 100 C above 25 C), which raises VC by about the same proportion.

### 9. Appearance summary
Default package SMB (OHM-069); SMA and SMC alternates. Unidirectional parts have a cathode band at -X; bidirectional parts (suffix C/CA) have NO band, per the 3D spec entry (and Vishay's marking statement). Terminal 1 = cathode for the unidirectional part; for a bidirectional part the two terminals are electrically interchangeable.

The B2 clamp-power check reproduces `P = VC*IPP` as the rating check the simulator will evaluate; it validates the model plumbing only, not the real pulse energy rating.
