## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-DIO-BRIDGE

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
A bridge rectifier is four rectifier diodes in one package, giving full-wave rectification of single-phase AC into DC with only two diode drops in the path, and tolerant of any AC polarity. Used at the front of every linear and switch-mode supply from a transformer or mains. Series: DB101-DB107 and DF005M-DF10M (DIP-4, 1 A), W005G-W10G / W02M-W10M (round WOG/WOM, 1.5 A), voltages from 50 V (suffix 005) through 1000 V (suffix 10).

### 2. What it is and how it works
Four junction diodes in a diamond: D1 from AC1 to +, D2 from AC2 to +, D3 from - to AC1, D4 from - to AC2. During a positive half cycle at AC1 (relative to AC2) D1 and D4 conduct; in the negative half D2 and D3 conduct. The output is the rectified waveform minus two diode drops: Vout,peak = Vpk - 2*VF(I). Output ripple with a reservoir capacitor C and load current I: ΔV about I/(2*f*C) for full-wave (an upper bound, since the diode conducts for part of each half cycle). Ratings in the sheets are per bridge (IF(AV), IFSM) with VF specified per diode (per element) at a stated current.
Real figures (S19 Vishay DFM, S20 Vishay WOG, S21 MCC WOM; extraction, caveats in header): DF005M-DF10M: VRRM 50 to 1000 V, IF(AV) 1.0 A at TA = 40 C, IFSM 50 A, VF max 1.1 V per diode at 1.0 A, IR 5 uA (25 C) and 500 uA (125 C) per diode, CJ typ 25 pF at 4 V 1 MHz, RthJA 40 C/W, RthJL 15 C/W, doc 88571 10-Oct-06 (the RS-hosted copy of the same family printed no doc number). W005G-W10G: IF(AV) 1.5 A at TA 25 C, 0.375 in lead length, IFSM 50 A, VF 1.0 V at 1.0 A per diode, IR 5 uA / 500 uA at 125 C, CJ 14 pF, RthJA 36 C/W, case WOG. MCC W06M-W10M (April 2016): IO 1.5 A, IFSM 50 A, VRRM 600 to 1000 V, VF 1.0 V per element, TJ -65 to 125 C. Important: Vishay quotes IF(AV) for the DFM at 40 C ambient on copper pads; derating curve not readable.

### 3. How it connects (pins and polarity)
Four terminals: AC1, AC2 (the two inputs, interchangeable), PLUS (+ DC output), MINUS (- DC output). Typical: transformer secondary across AC1/AC2, reservoir capacitor across +/-, load. Mistakes: (1) connecting the DC supply to the AC pins and reading the DC pins as the output (works but is a different circuit); (2) wiring a DC source across the DC (+/-) pins with polarity reversed: this is NOT blocked, because each of AC1 and AC2 forms a diode path from the - pin to the + pin through two diodes in series; the supply sees a short through two diode drops (bench B3 reproduces this: 35.7 mA through a 100 ohm resistor from a 5 V source, versus 8 nA blocked in the correct sense); (3) grounding one AC pin and expecting the DC output to be ground-referenced (output is floating unless you tie the MINUS or one AC node to ground; two diode drops are always in the path); (4) forgetting the reservoir capacitor's inrush current (surge rated IFSM 50 A for a 8.3 ms half sine, but inrush into an uncharged cap can exceed it); (5) using a bridge as a 4-diode cheap diode OR gate.
**Pin identity (physical positions):** the sources opened confirm only that the polarity marks are printed on the body ("Polarity: As marked on body", Vishay DFM) and that the two AC leads are diagonally opposite to each other in the case drawing, with + and - at the other two corners (extraction of the Vishay DFM and WOG case drawings; low-resolution reading, M-L confidence). Which numbered lead is + and which is AC is NOT stated in any opened document (the MCC document says "terminal configuration" is marked on the product; the KiCad DIP-4 footprint has no function labels). Default map used by OHMNI, an ASSUMPTION (L) consistent with the diagonal AC rule and with the 3D spec's placeholder that pin 1 is +: counter-clockwise numbering from the top-left, **pin 1 = PLUS, pin 2 = AC1, pin 3 = MINUS, pin 4 = AC2** (the AC pair is pins 2 and 4, diagonal). Electrical results do not depend on which AC pin is AC1 or AC2. Behavior layer must bind by FUNCTION (PLUS, MINUS, AC1, AC2) and the part record must carry the number-to-function table, so a corrected pin order only changes the table, not the model. RESEARCH_REQUIRED: confirm the physical lead functions from a manufacturer dimension drawing (Vishay DFM, MCC DB-1, Vishay WOG/MCC WOM) before treating the 3D marking as authoritative.

### 4. Electrical model
**Layer:** L1. **Fidelity:** `behavioural_approximation`.

```
.subckt BRIDGE AC1 AC2 PLUS MINUS
D1 AC1 PLUS DBR_{ref}
D2 AC2 PLUS DBR_{ref}
D3 MINUS AC1 DBR_{ref}
D4 MINUS AC2 DBR_{ref}
.ends
.model DBR_{ref} D (IS={IS} N={N} RS={RS} CJO={CJO} VJ=0.7 M=0.5 TT={TT} BV={BV} IBV={IBV})
```
Per-diode model: same class as BEH-DIO-PN standard-recovery rectifier. Default (1N4007-class typical fit, bench-verified) IS = 4.02e-9, N = 1.8, RS = 0.03; **DFM/WOG are different silicon**: the datasheets give VF max 1.1 V (DFM) and 1.0 V (WOG) at 1.0 A per diode; the max-corner fit for DFM is the S1M-style IS = 1.04e-10 (N 1.8, RS 0.03); the WOG max-corner point (1.0 V at 1 A) gives IS = 8.9e-10 with the same N and RS (computed, not benched). CJO from CJ: DFM 25 pF at 4 V gives CJO about 65 pF (VJ 0.7, M 0.5, ASSUMPTION), WOG 14 pF gives about 36 pF. TT = 3 us (ASSUMPTION L). BV = 1.1*VRRM (ASSUMPTION L); IBV = 5 uA. Note: bridge sheets quote VF at 25 C junction per element; during use two elements are in series, so the loss is `2*VF*I`.
Ideal mode: four `IS=1e-14 N=1` diodes. **Valid analyses:** op, dc, tran, ac, temp. **Limitations:** (1) all four elements are identical in the model (real elements match within a few percent on one die set); (2) isolation: AC to DC path exists only through diodes (no galvanic isolation, no creepage modelling); (3) package-level thermal coupling between the four diodes is not modelled: use package RthJA with the total dissipation `2*VF*I` (2.2 W at 1 A and VF 1.1 V is a 88 K rise at 40 C/W; see the Section 6 check); (4) reverse recovery uses TT ASSUMPTION.

### 5. Parameters (per diode)

| name | unit | DFM (1 A DIP) | WOG/WOM (1.5 A round) | basis | conf | source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| VRRM | V | 50 to 1000 by type (default 1000 for DF10M, 100 for DB101-class) | 50 to 1000 | MFR_DATASHEET | M | S19,S20 |
| IF(AV) | A | 1.0 at TA 40 C | 1.5 at 25 C, 0.375 in leads (S20); 1.5 (S21) | MFR_DATASHEET | M | S19,S20,S21 |
| IFSM | A | 50 (8.3 ms half sine) | 50 | MFR_DATASHEET | M | S19,S20,S21 |
| VF max per diode | V | 1.1 at 1 A | 1.0 at 1 A (S20,S21) | MFR_DATASHEET | M | S19,S20,S21 |
| IR | A | 5e-6 (25 C), 500e-6 (125 C) | 5e-6, 500e-6 | MFR_DATASHEET | M | S19,S20 |
| CJ | F | 25e-12 typ at 4 V | 14e-12 at 4 V | MFR_DATASHEET | M | S19,S20 |
| RthJA | C/W | 40 (13 x 13 mm copper pads) | 36 | MFR_DATASHEET | M | S19,S20 |
| TJmax | C | 150 (WOG sheet operating range -55 to +150; MCC WOM -65 to 125) | | MFR_DATASHEET | M | S20,S21 |

### 6. Ratings and limits
Checks: `mean(i_out) <= IF(AV)(Ta)` (bridge total), `i_peak_in_cap_charge <= IFSM` for the first half cycle (inrush), `max(vr_each_diode) <= VRRM` where each diode sees the peak AC input voltage (not the DC), `Tj = Ta + RthJA * (2*VF*I_avg)`. Worked check for DF10M at 1 A with VF 1.1 V: Pd = 2.2 W, with RthJA 40 C/W the rise is 88 K, so at 40 C ambient Tj = 128 C (below 150 C), consistent with the sheet's 1.0 A at 40 C rating (the rating assumes the quoted copper pads). At higher ambient the allowed current falls by `(TJmax - Ta)/(TJmax - Ta_rated)`.

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior

| id | trigger | effect | sim_response | permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| overcurrent | mean current above IF(AV)(Ta) or Tj > TJmax | package overheats, one or more diodes short; epoxy burns | WARN 100%, FAIL 120%; one diode `failed_short` (default D1) which produces a half-wave plus a line short on alternate half cycles | permanent |
| inrush_surge | cap charge peak above IFSM | element(s) short | FAIL, `failed_short` | permanent |
| reverse_overvoltage | AC peak above VRRM (each diode blocks the peak) | avalanche, short | FAIL above VRRM, WARN above 0.8*VRRM | permanent |
| dc_reverse_connection | DC source on the +/- pins reversed | conducts through two diodes in series (see B3), no blocking | netlist reproduces; flag as miswire if the + pin is more negative than the - pin by more than 2*VF | permanent if unlimited |
| ac_shorted_to_dc | AC pin tied to a DC rail | defeats rectification, shorts one diode path each half cycle | netlist reproduces | permanent if unlimited |
| open_element | one diode fails open | half-wave behavior, doubled ripple, output voltage falls | optional `failed_open` parameter per diode | permanent |

### 8. Thermal behavior
All four diodes share the package: dissipation `P = 2*VF(I)*I_avg` plus leakage; `Tj = Ta + RthJA*P`. Default RthJA 40 C/W (DFM, pads of 13 x 13 mm per sheet), 36 C/W (WOG). Heat leaves via the leads into the board copper, which is not modelled; expose `rth_ja` as an override.

### 9. Appearance summary
OHM-071 is a square-ish black epoxy 4-lead DIP body with row spacing 7.62 and pin pitch 5.08 (Vishay DFM / DB-1), printed polarity marks. OHM-072 is a round black epoxy puck 9.1 mm diameter with four straight leads on a 5.08 square pitch and a printed + mark. Polarity marks are printed text and are the only function cue; both rows of leads look alike.

```yaml
    D1 AC1 PLUS DBR_{ref}
    D2 AC2 PLUS DBR_{ref}
    D3 MINUS AC1 DBR_{ref}
    D4 MINUS AC2 DBR_{ref}
    .ends
    .model DBR_{ref} D (IS={IS} N={N} RS={RS} CJO={CJO} VJ=0.7 M=0.5 TT={TT} BV={VRRM*1.1} IBV=5u)
    X{ref} {AC1} {AC2} {PLUS} {MINUS} BRIDGE_{ref}
  valid_analyses: [op, dc, ac, tran, temp]
  valid_range: "AC peak < VRRM, mean current < IF(AV)(Ta)"
  known_limitations:
    - "four identical diodes, no thermal coupling or lead heat flow"
    - "lead functions of the physical pins are not confirmed by an opened drawing"
    - "TT, N, RS assumed"
ratings:
  - {name: average_forward, symbol: IF(AV), value: 1.0, unit: A, condition: "DFM, TA 40 C, pads 13x13 mm", check: "mean(i_out) <= IF_AV*(150-Ta)/(150-40)", source_ref: S19}
  - {name: surge, symbol: IFSM, value: 50, unit: A, condition: "8.3 ms half sine", check: "i_pk <= IFSM", source_ref: S19}
  - {name: reverse_voltage, symbol: VRRM, value: 1000, unit: V, condition: "DF10M", check: "max(v_ac_pk) <= VRRM", source_ref: S19}
failure_modes:
  - {id: overcurrent, trigger: "mean current above rating", effect: "overheat, element shorts", sim_response: "WARN, FAIL 120%, failed_short on D1", permanence: permanent}
  - {id: dc_reverse_connection, trigger: "DC supply across +/- pins reversed", effect: "two-diode short path", sim_response: "netlist reproduces; miswire flag", permanence: permanent}
bench:
  - {id: B1, file: bench/beh-dio-bridge/B1_fullwave_load.cir, expected: [{measure: Vpk, value: 8.4253, tolerance: "0.5%", basis: "solve"}, {measure: Vavg, value: 4.9287, tolerance: "0.5%", basis: "numerical integral"}], measured_in_ngspice: "8.42528 / 4.93004", ngspice_version: "42"}
  - {id: B2, file: bench/beh-dio-bridge/B2_filtered.cir, expected: [{measure: ripple, value: "<= 0.677 V", tolerance: "bound", basis: "I/(2fC)"}], measured_in_ngspice: "0.571 V", ngspice_version: "42"}
  - {id: B3, file: bench/beh-dio-bridge/B3_polarity.cir, expected: [{measure: "reverse DC current", value: 0.0357368, tolerance: "0.5%", basis: "solve"}, {measure: "blocked current", value: "< 1e-6", tolerance: n/a, basis: leakage}], measured_in_ngspice: "35.7368 mA / 8.06 nA", ngspice_version: "42"}
sources: [{id: S19, org: Vishay, title: "DF005M thru DF10M Single-Phase Bridge Rectifier doc 88571", url: "https://hallaweb.jlab.org/tech/Detectors/public_html/manuals/chip_specs/M-Z/vishay_siliconix/dfm.pdf", date: "10-Oct-06", used_for: "VRRM, IF(AV), IFSM, VF, IR, CJ, RthJA, polarity statement"}]
confidence: {parameters: L, ratings: M, model: M, failure: L}
status: partial
```

### 12. Sources
S19 Vishay, "DF005M thru DF10M Single-Phase Bridge Rectifier", case DFM, doc 88571, 10-Oct-06 (hallaweb.jlab.org mirror: https://hallaweb.jlab.org/tech/Detectors/public_html/manuals/chip_specs/M-Z/vishay_siliconix/dfm.pdf; also read the RS-hosted copy https://assets.rs-online.com/v1698967676/Datasheets/dbe1f46eafa0fbcc3ab04df05f71e4c2.pdf, which shows no doc number). Used: ratings, "Polarity: As marked on body", package drawing labels (~, +, -, AC pair on diagonal corners).
S20 Vishay, "W005G thru W10G Single-Phase Bridge Rectifier", case WOG (RS-hosted copy https://assets.rs-online.com/v1698969169/Datasheets/5fb12707834ec63d778ad2aac6b6d4ee.pdf; also the Radiolocman page https://www.radiolocman.com/datasheet/data.html?di=97445); no doc number or revision in the extractions. Used: IF(AV) 1.5 A, IFSM 50 A, VF 1.0 V, IR, CJ 14 pF, RthJA 36, case WOG, marked +, -, ~, ~.
S21 Micro Commercial Components, "W06M thru W10M", Apr 2016 (Mouser copy https://www.mouser.com/datasheet/2/169/w06m_thru_w10m-1133520.pdf). Used: IO 1.5 A, IFSM 50 A, VF 1.0 V per element, TJ -65 to 125 C, statement that terminal configuration is marked on the product; the drawing itself was not readable.
KiCad `Diode_Bridge_DIP-4_W7.62mm_P5.08mm` footprint (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KiCad/kicad-footprints/master/Diode_THT.pretty/Diode_Bridge_DIP-4_W7.62mm_P5.08mm.kicad_mod): pads 1 at (0, 0), 2 at (0, 5.08), 3 at (7.62, 5.08), 4 at (7.62, 0): geometry only, no function labels, consistent with the 3D spec's dimensions.

### 13. Research confidence
(a) parameters LOW-MEDIUM (diode model assumed), (b) ratings MEDIUM (consistent across Vishay and MCC), (c) model MEDIUM (verified in ngspice; four identical diodes), (d) failure LOW.
Unresolved (RESEARCH_REQUIRED): the physical function of each numbered lead for DIP-4 (DFM/DB-1) and round (WOG/WOM) bridges; derating curves; IFSM for a single-diode view; SMD bridges (MBS-style) proposed in the 3D spec are not covered.

# Per-entry sections

Common rule for OHM-056 to OHM-068 (two-lead packages): electrical pin K maps to package terminal 1 (cathode, band/bar at -X), pin A maps to package terminal 2 (anode, +X). SPICE line: `D{ref} {net_of_terminal_2} {net_of_terminal_1} model`. Geometry and dimensions are in the 3D spec entry of the same ID and are not repeated. "Package thermal" figures are datasheet values for a representative part; none of them is a property of the package alone, they depend on the lead length or copper area stated in the source.

## [OHM-056] DO-35 signal diode -> BEH-DIO-PN
* Reference functional part: 1N4148 (Vishay doc 81857, S1). Package DO-204AH glass, cathode band black (3D spec).
* Defaults (fit A): IS 5.537e-9, N 1.944, RS 0.6, CJO 2 pF, VJ 0.7, M 0.4, TT 23 ns, BV 100 V, IBV 100 uA.
* Ratings: VRRM 100 V, IF 200 mA (conservative; Vishay 300 mA, Nexperia IFRM 450 mA), IFSM 2 A for 1 us (Vishay) / 4 A (Nexperia), Ptot 500 mW at TL <= 25 C (440 mW at 45 C), RthJA 350 K/W with 4 mm leads, TJmax 175 C.
* Pin map: K to terminal 1 (band end, -X, hole at X = -3.81), A to terminal 2 (+X).
* Other DO-35 contents (Zener 1N52xx/BZX55, small Schottky) belong to BEH-DIO-ZENER and BEH-DIO-SCHOTTKY via the part's `behavior_class` field.
* Notes: glass package; mechanical shock and lead stress crack the glass. Status: complete for the 1N4148 reference (partial for max-corner trr and no typical VF graph); partial overall.

## [OHM-057] DO-41 rectifier diode -> BEH-DIO-PN (rectifier variant)
* Reference part: 1N4007 (Vishay doc 88503, onsemi Rev 12), family 1N4001-1N4007 (50-1000 V).
* Defaults (fit B, typical): IS 4.02e-9, N 1.8 (assumed), RS 0.03 (assumed), CJO 38.9 pF, VJ 0.7, M 0.5, TT 3 us (assumed), BV 1100 V (assumed), IBV 5 uA.
* Ratings: VRRM per type (1N4007 1000 V), IF(AV) 1.0 A at TA 75 C 0.375 in leads, IFSM 30 A (8.3 ms) and 45 A (1 ms), VF max 1.1 V at 1 A (typ 0.93 V), IR 5 uA (25 C) / 50 uA (125 C), CJ 15 pF at 4 V, RthJA 50 C/W, RthJL 25 C/W (PCB mounted, 0.375 in), TJmax 175 C (onsemi operating range).
* Thermal power limit at 25 C: (175 - 25)/50 = 3.0 W junction limit; the 1 A rating gives about 1.0 W (0.93 V * 1 A), margin is the lead length.
* Pin map: K to terminal 1 (band end, -X), A to terminal 2. Vishay: "color band denotes cathode end".
* Notes: standard recovery (trr not specified): unsuitable above about 50 kHz in switchers. Status: partial.

## [OHM-058] DO-201 power diode (DO-201AD) -> BEH-DIO-PN (rectifier variant)
* Reference part: 1N5400-1N5408 (Vishay doc 88516, 3 A).
* Defaults (max-corner fit): IS 5.05e-11, N 1.8, RS 0.015 (assumed), CJO 77.7 pF, TT 3 us (assumed), BV 1.1*VRRM.
* Ratings: VRRM 50-1000 V, IF(AV) 3.0 A at TL 105 C with 0.5 in leads, IFSM 200 A (8.3 ms), VF max 1.2 V at 3 A, IR 5 uA (25 C) / 500 uA (150 C), CJ typ 30 pF at 4 V, RthJA 20 C/W typical (PCB, 0.375 in), no trr.
* Pin map: K to terminal 1 (band, -X, X = -7.62), A to terminal 2.
* Notes: dissipation at 3 A: about 1.2 V * 3 A = 3.6 W max-corner; with 20 C/W the rise is 72 K. Status: partial.

## [OHM-059] MiniMELF diode -> BEH-DIO-PN (also BEH-DIO-ZENER and BEH-DIO-SCHOTTKY via part)
* Reference parts named by the 3D spec: BZV55 Zener (blue band, Vishay doc 88315, cited by the spec, NOT opened in this research), LL4148-type switching diodes. No MiniMELF datasheet was opened here.
* Defaults: use the 1N4148 fit (fit A) for a switching diode; Zener use BEH-DIO-ZENER with the BZX55-derived fit (the SOD-80 BZV55 sheet may differ, RESEARCH_REQUIRED). Power for MiniMELF Zeners is typically 500 mW (assumed from the BZV55 series name in the spec, not opened).
* Pin map: K to terminal 1 (cathode end cap, band, -X, X = -1.56), A to terminal 2.
* Notes: lower thermal mass than DO-35; RthJA higher on board, not sourced. Status: partial (no ratings sourced for the package itself).

## [OHM-060] MELF diode -> BEH-DIO-PN
* Reference part named by the spec: GL41 plastic MELF rectifiers (Vishay doc 88548, cited by the spec, NOT opened here). Use the BEH-DIO-PN rectifier class with ratings of a 1 A rectifier family as a placeholder (1N4007 data S6) and mark `rating_source: assumed`.
* Pin map: K to terminal 1 (band end cap, -X, X = -2.245), A to terminal 2.
* Notes: MELF cylinders have no polarity cue besides the band; cylindrical body can roll in assembly. Status: partial (research_required for GL41 ratings).

## [OHM-061] SOD-123 diode -> BEH-DIO-PN
* Reference parts: 1N4148W-class switching diode (use fit A with CJO and ratings per its datasheet; no SOD-123 datasheet was opened). Schottky (BAT42W/BAT54 type) uses BEH-DIO-SCHOTTKY, Zener (BZT52/MMSZ) BEH-DIO-ZENER.
* Pin map: K to terminal 1 (-X bar side, X = -1.425), A to terminal 2.
* Notes: SOD-123F/FL flat-power variants are a different package and are not covered by this entry. Package RthJA not sourced; Nexperia SOT-23 devices quote 500 K/W (BAV99, S22) as a lower-power reference. Status: partial.

## [OHM-062] SOD-323 diode -> BEH-DIO-PN
* Reference: 1N4148WS / BAS16WS / BAT54WS class (no datasheet opened). Use fit A with CJO 1.5 pF (ASSUMPTION), ratings from the 1N4148 family scaled down: IF 150 mA assumed.
* Pin map: K to terminal 1 (-X, X = -1.05), A to terminal 2.
* Status: partial (ratings research_required).

## [OHM-063] SOD-523 diode -> BEH-DIO-PN
* Reference: BAS16-type in SOD-523 (no datasheet opened). Same placeholder as OHM-062 with lower power.
* Pin map: K to terminal 1 (-X, X = -0.625), A to terminal 2.
* Status: partial (ratings research_required).

## [OHM-064] SMA diode -> BEH-DIO-PN (rectifier), also BEH-DIO-SCHOTTKY and BEH-DIO-TVS via part
* Rectifier reference: S1A-S1M (Vishay, S9): IF(AV) 1.0 A, IFSM 40 A (S1A-S1J) / 30 A (S1K-S1M), VF max 1.1 V at 1 A, IR 1 uA (25 C) / 5 uA (125 C), CJ typ 12 pF at 4 V, trr typ 1.8 us, RthJA 75 C/W (S1A-S1J) / 85 (S1K-S1M), RthJL 27/30 C/W, TJ -55 to +150 C. Fit: IS 1.04e-10 (max corner), N 1.8, RS 0.03, CJO 31.1 pF, TT 3 us (assumed; datasheet trr 1.8 us typ with unknown test condition).
* Schottky: SS14 (S10) 1 A, 40 V, RthJA 88 C/W. TVS: SMAJ 400 W, RthJA 120 C/W (S17).
* Pin map: K to terminal 1 (-X, J-lead, contact center -2.0), A to terminal 2 (+2.0).
* Power handling: (150 - 25)/75 = 1.67 W junction limit at 25 C for the rectifier with the quoted pads; SS14 (150 - 25)/88 = 1.42 W; SMAJ TVS continuous 1.04 W. Status: partial.

## [OHM-065] SMB diode -> BEH-DIO-PN, BEH-DIO-SCHOTTKY, BEH-DIO-TVS
* Schottky reference: SS24 (Vishay SS22-SS26, S12): 2 A, 40 V, IFSM 75 A, VF max 0.5 V (SS22-SS24) at 2 A, IR 0.4 mA / 10 mA (25 / 100 C), RthJA 75 C/W, RthJL 17 C/W. TVS: SMBJ (S16) 600 W, RthJA 100 C/W. Rectifier S2x (spec-named, no datasheet opened): RESEARCH_REQUIRED, use S1x scaling with IF(AV) 2.0 A.
* Pin map: K to terminal 1 (-X, contact center -2.15 per this entry; OHM-069 states 2.425, which is inconsistent, see header), A to terminal 2 (+2.15).
* Power handling at 25 C: Schottky 1.67 W, TVS continuous 1.25 W. Status: partial.

## [OHM-066] SMC diode -> BEH-DIO-PN, BEH-DIO-SCHOTTKY, BEH-DIO-TVS
* Schottky reference: SS34 (Vishay SS32-SS36, S13): 3 A, 40 V, IFSM 100 A, VF 0.5 V (SS32-SS34) / 0.75 V (SS35-SS36), EAS 20 mJ, TJ 150 C; IR and RthJA not in the extraction. TVS: SMCJ (S18) 1500 W, IFSM 200 A, RthJA 75 C/W, RthJL 15 C/W. Rectifier MURS-type (spec-named, not opened): RESEARCH_REQUIRED.
* Pin map: K to terminal 1 (-X, contact center -3.42), A to terminal 2 (+3.42).
* Power handling at 25 C (RthJA 75 proxy): 1.67 W. SMC is the largest of the three bodies and has the highest continuous and pulse capability: SMA 400 W TVS, SMB 600 W, SMC 1500 W. Status: partial.

## [OHM-067] Schottky diode -> BEH-DIO-SCHOTTKY
* Default package SOD-123 (small-signal): defaults from the Nexperia BAT54 vendor numbers (S14): IS 2.117e-7, N 1, RS 2.7, CJO 8 pF, BV 56 V, IR 2 uA at 25 V, VR 30 V, VF max 0.8 V at 100 mA. Power variants (SMA SS14, DO-41, DO-201AD): SS14 fit.
* Alternates: SMA, DO-41, DO-201AD, SOD-323 (per 3D spec `package_member`).
* Pin map: K to terminal 1 (bar, -X), A to terminal 2, for every member.
* Notes: leakage rises steeply with temperature; thermal runaway check is mandatory for power parts above about 60 C ambient at high VR (bench B3, Ta threshold 83 C for SS14 max leakage at 40 V). Status: partial.

## [OHM-068] Zener diode -> BEH-DIO-ZENER
* Default package SOD-123; alternates DO-35 (1N52xx), DO-41 (1 W), MiniMELF (BZV55), SOD-323. The Zener VZ is a part parameter (E24), default 5.1 V from the BZX55C5V1 fit; BZX55C10 (9.4-10.6 V at 5 mA, rZ < 15 ohm at 5 mA) shows the form for other voltages.
* Pin map: K to terminal 1 (band/bar, -X) which is the end that goes positive in regulation; A to terminal 2. For DO-35 glass the cathode is at X = -3.81.
* Power: 500 mW at 25 C for DO-35, derating (175 - Ta)/300; SOD-123 and DO-41 values are RESEARCH_REQUIRED.
* Status: partial.

## [OHM-069] TVS diode -> BEH-DIO-TVS
* Default package SMB (SMBJ), alternates SMA (SMAJ, 400 W) and SMC (SMCJ, 1500 W). Default part SMBJ15A: VWM 15 V, VBR min 16.7 V at 1 mA, VC 24.4 V at 24.6 A, 600 W (10/1000 us).
* Unidirectional: K to terminal 1 (band at -X), A to terminal 2. Bidirectional (`bidirectional: true`): no band; terminals 1 and 2 interchangeable, model BEH-DIO-TVS bidirectional cell pair.
* Notes: terminal center X is stated as +/-2.425 here but +/-2.15 for the same package in OHM-065 and PKG-SMX.SMB; 2.15 is arithmetically correct (see header). HAZARD: short-circuit failure mode, see class section 1 and 7. Status: partial.

## [OHM-070] Dual diode SOT-23 -> BEH-DIO-PN (two diodes per instance)
* Three configurations (3D spec pin usage; BAV99 confirmed by opened Nexperia datasheet S22, BAV70 and BAW56 from the spec's own sourcing, not re-opened here). Parameter `config`.
* Defaults per diode: 1N4148-class fit A (CJO 1.5 pF used by Nexperia max Cd 1.5 pF for BAV99, S22; IS/N/RS from fit A as a proxy because the BAV99 sheet extraction gives only VF 855 mV at 10 mA, min/typ/max unlabeled). Ratings per BAV99 (S22): VRRM 100 V, IF 215 mA per diode, IFSM 4 A (1 us), IR 0.5 uA max at 80 V, trr 4 ns max, Ptot 250 mW total, Rth(j-a) 500 K/W. Fit A VF(10 mA) = 0.730 V, below the BAV99 855 mV figure, so the fit is a typical-to-low corner here; for max-VF behavior scale IS by exp(-(0.855-0.730)/(1.944*0.02586)) = 0.083.
* Pin map (package terminals, per 3D spec numbering: pin 1 (-0.95, -1.0), pin 2 (+0.95, -1.0), pin 3 (0, +1.0)):

| config | pin 1 | pin 2 | pin 3 | SPICE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| series (BAV99) | A1 | K2 | K1 and A2 | `D1 {p1} {p3} M` , `D2 {p3} {p2} M` |
| common cathode (BAV70) | A1 | A2 | K1 and K2 | `D1 {p1} {p3} M` , `D2 {p2} {p3} M` |
| common anode (BAW56) | K1 | K2 | A1 and A2 | `D1 {p3} {p1} M` , `D2 {p3} {p2} M` |

* Convention note: unlike the two-lead packages, pin 1 is not always the cathode here; polarity is carried by this table only. Bench B6 ran the BAV99 series config as a rail clamp (clamps to 5.685 V and -0.726 V, matching the closed form).
* Status: partial (BAV70 and BAW56 sheets not opened in this session).

## [OHM-071] DIP bridge rectifier -> BEH-DIO-BRIDGE
* Reference parts: DB101-DB107 (DB-1 outline) and DF005M-DF10M (Vishay case DFM, doc 88571). Defaults: DF10M-class ratings: VRRM 1000 V, IF(AV) 1.0 A at TA 40 C, IFSM 50 A, VF 1.1 V max per diode at 1 A, IR 5 uA / 500 uA (25 / 125 C), CJ 25 pF, RthJA 40 C/W.
* Pin map (3D spec numbering: pin 1 (-3.81, +2.54), pin 2 (-3.81, -2.54), pin 3 (+3.81, -2.54), pin 4 (+3.81, +2.54)): electrical PLUS to pin 1, AC1 to pin 2, MINUS to pin 3, AC2 to pin 4. ASSUMPTION (L), consistent with the 3D spec placeholder (pin 1 = +) and with the diagonal AC rule from the Vishay drawing, but NOT confirmed from a dimension drawing. The part record must hold this as a function table so a correction changes only data.
* Notes: bridge polarity is printed on the body; the modelling is correct for any permutation of AC pins. Status: partial (pin functions research_required).

## [OHM-072] Round bridge rectifier -> BEH-DIO-BRIDGE
* Reference parts: W005G-W10G (Vishay WOG, S20), W02M-W10M (MCC WOM, S21). Defaults: IF(AV) 1.5 A (0.375 in leads, 25 C), IFSM 50 A, VF 1.0 V at 1 A per diode, IR 5 uA / 500 uA, CJ 14 pF, RthJA 36 C/W, VRRM 50 to 1000 V, TJ -55 to +150 C (Vishay), -65 to +125 C (MCC).
* Pin map (3D spec: pin 1 (-2.54, +2.54), pin 2 (-2.54, -2.54), pin 3 (+2.54, -2.54), pin 4 (+2.54, +2.54)): electrical PLUS to pin 1, AC1 to pin 2, MINUS to pin 3, AC2 to pin 4. ASSUMPTION (L). The 3D spec states MCC WOM labels as AC, AC, +, -, which suggests a different numbering order than the assumed one (AC at pins 1 and 2); that statement is not resolved by any opened drawing. RESEARCH_REQUIRED before use for any visual or layout checking.
* Status: partial.

# R5: LEDs and displays (OHM-073 to OHM-092)

Group R5 covers 20 library entries in 8 behavior classes.

| Class | Entries | Layer | One line |
|---|---|---|---|
| BEH-LED-INDICATOR | OHM-073..081 | L1 | single-die LED (THT lamps, chip LEDs, PLCC-2), series-resistor driven |
| BEH-LED-RGB | OHM-082, 083 | L1 | three independent dies in one package (PLCC-4 RGB, 5050 6-pin RGB) |
| BEH-LED-POWER | OHM-085, 086 | L1 + thermal | 1 W-class emitter and its MCPCB star, current-source driven |
| BEH-LED-ADDRESSABLE | OHM-084 | L1 supply + L2/L3 protocol | WS2812B-style RGB LED with built-in driver, single-wire NRZ |
| BEH-DISP-LEDARRAY | OHM-087..090 | L1 (+L2 drive pattern) | 7-segment digits and 8x8 matrix: LED groups with common anode/cathode, multiplexed |
| BEH-DISP-LCD1602 | OHM-091 | L3 (+L1 supply, backlight) | HD44780/ST7066 character LCD module |
| BEH-DISP-OLED-I2C | OHM-092 | L3 (+L1 supply, I2C pull-ups) | SSD1306 128x64 OLED breakout |

Fidelity label for every netlist here: `behavioural_approximation` (every deck carries its own `.model` or behavioural source). No vendor SPICE model was opened or attached, so no entry may claim `vendor_model`. A simulation that did not run is never a pass.

## Evidence caveat (applies to every number below)

The datasheet fetch tool returns a model-written extraction of each PDF, not the PDF pages. Tables were read through it and cross-checked between documents where two exist. Graph values (VF vs IF, intensity vs current, flux vs current) are the extractor's reading of figures and are LOW confidence. The Vishay figures behave inconsistently in places (see the blue LED point at 1 mA, below), and that is reported rather than hidden. Where a number needed a graph and I could not obtain it, it is marked ASSUMPTION or RESEARCH_REQUIRED. Documents that could not be opened (Kingbright direct, Raystar OLED, SSD1306 DC table) are not cited for numbers.

Two things were NOT obtained and are open for every class that needs them:
* Per-MPN segment-to-pin maps for 7-segment displays and the 8x8 matrix (the Kingbright PDFs opened here do not carry the pin table in the extracted text).
* The SSD1306 DC characteristics table (IDD, ICC) and I2C timing numbers.

## Cross-cutting: pin convention and ground rules

* Electrical convention: SPICE `D name anode cathode model`. For every two-lead LED in this group (OHM-073..081, 3D spec "Terminals"), **terminal 1 = cathode, terminal 2 = anode**. The SPICE line is `D{ref} {net_of_terminal_2} {net_of_terminal_1} {model}`. The existing repo part record `src/ohmni/catalog/data/parts/GENERIC_LED_GREEN.json` numbers pin 1 = A, pin 2 = K. This is the same conflict R4 found for diodes. The behavior layer must bind by pin ROLE (anode/cathode) and each part record carries its own number-to-role table. Do not infer polarity from pin number.
* The existing verifier rule (`verifier/rules/led.py`) computes `(Vdrive - Vf_low)/R` against `max_forward_current` using the part's `led` record (forward_voltage min/typ/max, max_forward_current, test_current). The class parameters below map onto those fields: `vf_min/typ/max` -> forward_voltage, `if_max` -> max_forward_current, `if_test` -> test_current.
* The repo's GENERIC_LED_GREEN record assumes Vf 1.8/2.1/2.4 V and 20 mA max, labelled ASSUMED. Section "Datasheet conflicts" shows how that compares with real data.

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-LED-INDICATOR

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
Indicator and signalling LEDs: power-on lights, status, backlighting of switches, optocoupler-style optical links, simple lamps. Driven from a rail through a series resistor (or a constant-current sink). Common values: 20 mA at 2 V (red/yellow/green GaP, AlInGaP), 20 mA at 3.0 to 3.4 V (InGaN green, blue, white); typical drive 2 to 20 mA; modern high-efficiency chip LEDs are bright at 1 to 2 mA. Forms in this class: 3 mm and 5 mm THT lamps (T-1, T-1 3/4), 10 mm lamp, rectangular lamp, chip LEDs 0402/0603/0805/1206, PLCC-2 (3528).

### 2. What it is and how it works
A pn (or heterojunction) diode in a direct-bandgap semiconductor. Forward bias injects electrons and holes into the active region, where radiative recombination emits photons of energy about equal to the bandgap Eg, so wavelength (nm) ~ 1240 / Eg(eV). The material fixes the colour and the forward voltage:

| Colour | Material (as printed in the opened datasheets) | VF at 20 mA typ / max | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| deep red | GaAlAs on GaAs (DH) | 1.8 / 2.2 V | S1 |
| super red, orange, yellow, yellow-green | AlInGaP | 2.0 / 2.4 V | S6 |
| red/yellow/green GaAsP or GaP on GaP | GaAsP/GaP | 2.4 / 3.0 V (yellow, green); red 2.0 typ | S3, S4 |
| true green (InGaN) | InGaN | 3.2 / 3.6 V | S6 |
| blue | GaN on SiC (TLHB5800) | 3.9 / 4.5 V | S2 |
| blue | InGaN (VLMB13xx) | max 3.8 V | S6 |
| blue / green | InGaN (Broadcom ASMB-MTB0) | typ 3.1, 2.8 to 3.6 V | S7 |
| white | InGaN die + phosphor converter | 3.2 typ (2.8 to 3.6) V | S5 |

Conflict kept: blue VF typ is 3.9 V (Vishay TLHB5800, GaN on SiC) and 3.1 V (Broadcom, InGaN). Both are real products; the model must be selected per MPN, with 3.1 V the more common modern value.

Current-voltage law (Shockley with series resistance), used by the SPICE diode:

    I = IS * (exp(Vj / (N*Vt)) - 1),   Vj = V - I*RS,   Vt = kT/q = 25.86 mV at 27 C

N for LEDs is 1.5 to 3 or more (recombination in the depletion region and in quantum wells), not 1. RS (bond wire, contact, bulk) sets the linear region: from the datasheet 20 mA to 50 mA points, RS is about 6 to 20 ohm in these small lamps.

Light output is roughly proportional to current at moderate current: Iv = Iv_ref * (If/If_ref)^k with k about 1.0. From S1 (TLDR4400): Iv = 2 mcd at 1 mA and 45 mcd at 20 mA, so k = ln(45/2)/ln(20) = 1.039. The same document gives about 0.1 relative at 0.1 mA and 1.0 at 10 mA (chart, extractor reading). Intensity falls with junction temperature (AlInGaP red/amber strongly, about 1 percent per K; InGaN blue/white much less; the only sourced figure is XP-E2 white falling about 20 percent from 25 to 150 C, S8, which is 0.16 percent per K average). Peak wavelength drifts with temperature and current (a few nm), and phosphor white shifts chromaticity weakly (S5 states chromaticity moves little over 10 to 60 mA).

Temperature dependence of VF: at constant current VF falls with temperature. The usual figure is -2 to -3 mV/K per junction (general LED physics, ASSUMPTION, no opened datasheet quoted it). The ngspice D model reproduces this through EG and XTI (see B5, B6).

Reverse behaviour: LEDs are poor reverse blockers. Datasheets give VR = 5 V (InGaN: S2, S5, S6; Broadcom: "not recommended for reverse bias", S7) or 6 V (GaP/GaAlAs: S1, S3, S4) as a rating at IR = 10 uA. Above that the junction avalanches or tunnels; the current is limited only by the circuit and the die can be damaged. Typical VR on GaP parts is 6 to 15 V (S3, S4).

### 3. How it connects
Two terminals: anode (long lead, +) and cathode (flat side, short lead; for chip LEDs a mark on the cathode end). Forward when V(A) > V(K) by about VF. Standard circuit: rail - resistor - LED - GND, with R = (Vs - VF)/IF. A constant-current sink gives a defined current regardless of rail. Common mistakes: no series resistor (current limited only by RS and the source, destroys the die within microseconds to milliseconds); reversed polarity (blue/white may be damaged at 5 V reverse); sizing R with a typical VF and ignoring that VF max is 0.4 to 0.7 V higher so current drops 10 to 30 percent; running a 3.3 V rail into a blue LED with a 3.9 V VF (it will barely glow or not at all, because 3.3 V is below the knee); paralleling LEDs on one resistor (VF mismatch gives current hogging); using PWM peak current above the pulsed rating.

Series resistor sizing: R = (Vs - VF(IF)) / IF, with VF taken at the worst corner for the current of concern: minimum VF for the maximum current (safety), maximum VF for the minimum current (visibility).

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
Layer: **L1**. Fidelity label: `behavioural_approximation` (own `.model`).

ngspice primitives: `D` with `.model ... D(IS N RS CJO VJ M TT BV IBV EG XTI)`. Optional behavioural source `B` for a luminous-intensity output node. No XSPICE or special build needed.

Netlist template (A is package terminal 2, K is package terminal 1):

```
D{ref} {A} {K} LED_{colour}
.model LED_{colour} D (IS={IS} N={N} RS={RS} CJO={CJO} VJ=1.0 M=0.33 TT=0 BV={BV} IBV=10u EG={EG} XTI=3)
* optional output quantity: luminous intensity in mcd on node iv_{ref} (1 V = 1 mcd)
* B{ref}iv iv_{ref} 0 V = {iv_ref}*pow(max(i(V{ref}s),1e-12)/{if_ref},{k_exp})*(1+{k_temp}*(temp-25))
```
`V{ref}s` is a zero-volt sense source in series with the anode. VJ is limited to 2 by ngspice (value above 2 triggers a warning); use 1.0. TT=0 is acceptable for indicator service (LED lifetime of minority carriers is ns, far below any realistic drive).

#### 4.1 D-model fits (how IS, N, RS were obtained)
Fit script: `/home/claude/behavior/tmp_R5_fit.py` (scipy least squares, Vt at 27 C = 25.86 mV; V = N*Vt*ln(I/IS + 1) + I*RS). Input points are the datasheet table value VF typ at 20 mA where available, plus chart points where available. Each fit is shown with its inputs.

| Card | Input points (I, V) | N | Result IS (A), RS (ohm) | Residual (V) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LED_RED (TLDR4400, S1) | chart: (10 mA, 1.8 V), (20 mA, 2.0 V) | 2.0 fixed | IS = 1.846e-16, RS = 16.4 | 0, 0 (2 points, 2 unknowns) | Table says VF typ 1.8 V @ 20 mA, max 2.2 V. Chart reading says 2.0 V @ 20 mA. Conflict kept; card sits at 2.0 V, between typ and max. A card anchored on table typ (1.8 V @ 20 mA) would need IS = 1.07e-16, RS = 5 ohm (assuming 1.55 V at 1 mA, which is an assumption). |
| LED_GREEN (TLHG5800, S3) | (0.1 mA, 1.9 V), (20 mA, 2.4 V table typ), (100 mA, 3.2 V) | free: 2.38 | IS = 3.793e-18, RS = 8.76 | 0, 0, 0 (3 points, 3 unknowns) | Fit with N fixed at 2 leaves residuals up to 23 mV; N = 2.38 is exact. |
| LED_BLUE (TLHB5800, S2) | chart: (10 mA, 3.8), (20 mA, 4.0), (50 mA, 4.2) | 3.0 fixed | IS = 7.641e-24, RS = 6.28 | +36, -48, +12 mV | The chart also gives (1 mA, 3.0 V). The 1 mA point needs N about 12 (unphysical) and is NOT reproduced: model gives 3.60 V at 1 mA, 0.6 V above the extracted point. Treat low-current blue behaviour as wrong (see limitations). Table typ is 3.9 V at 20 mA; card gives 3.95 V. |
| LED_WHITE (VLHW5100, S5) | table typ (20 mA, 3.2 V) only | 3.0, RS = 6.3 assumed (copied from the blue fit) | IS = 1.247e-19 | exact at 20 mA | Only one datasheet point; N and RS are ASSUMPTIONs. |
| LED_RGB_R (Broadcom ASMB-MTB0 red, S7) | table typ (20 mA, 2.1 V) | 2.0, RS = 12 assumed | IS = 4.848e-18 | exact at 20 mA | N and RS are ASSUMPTIONs. |
| LED_RGB_GB (Broadcom green/blue, S7) | table typ (20 mA, 3.1 V) | 3.0, RS = 6.3 assumed | IS = 4.526e-19 | exact at 20 mA | N and RS are ASSUMPTIONs. |

Card values as used (file `/home/claude/behavior/bench/beh-led-indicator/models.inc`):

```
.model LED_RED   D (IS=1.846e-16 N=2.0  RS=16.4 CJO=30p VJ=1.0 M=0.33 TT=0 BV=15  IBV=10u EG=2.2 XTI=3)
.model LED_GREEN D (IS=3.793e-18 N=2.38 RS=8.76 CJO=50p VJ=1.0 M=0.33 TT=0 BV=15  IBV=10u EG=2.8 XTI=3)
.model LED_BLUE  D (IS=7.641e-24 N=3.0  RS=6.28 CJO=60p VJ=1.0 M=0.33 TT=0 BV=5.5 IBV=10u EG=4.6 XTI=3)
.model LED_WHITE D (IS=1.247e-19 N=3.0  RS=6.3  CJO=60p VJ=1.0 M=0.33 TT=0 BV=5.5 IBV=10u EG=3.9 XTI=3)
```
CJO: red 30 pF is the TLDR4400 table (Cj at 0 V, 1 MHz), green 50 pF the TLHG5800 table; blue/white 60 pF are ASSUMPTIONs (S2 and S5 do not state Cj). BV and IBV encode the reverse rating: blue/white BV = 5.5 V at IBV = 10 uA (S2: VR min 5 V at 10 uA, so the card clamps just above the rating), red/green BV = 15 V (S3 says VR 6 to 15 V; 15 V is the upper end and is ASSUMPTION; the rating check flags at 6 V regardless). EG is NOT a bandgap here: it is tuned so the card's dVF/dT at 20 mA is about -2 mV/K (red, green) or -3 mV/K (blue, white), measured in bench B6 (-2.03, -2.17, -2.85, -3.02 mV/K). The tempco targets are ASSUMPTIONs.

Model results at the fit points (bench B1, 27 C): red 1.80 V at 10 mA and 2.00 V at 20 mA (inputs 1.8 and 2.0); green 2.40 V at 20 mA (input 2.4) and 3.20 V at 100 mA (input 3.2); blue 3.84, 3.95, 4.21 V at 10, 20, 50 mA (inputs 3.8, 4.0, 4.2); white 3.20 V at 20 mA (input 3.2).

Ideal vs realistic mode:
* Ideal: single D card, RS and N from the table, no tempco handling beyond `.temp`.
* Realistic: add `CJO`, reverse BV/IBV, temperature via `.temp` (global in ngspice, so electro-thermal feedback needs an iteration loop; see BEH-LED-POWER), the luminous-intensity B-source with temperature factor, and a VF grade offset: to move the whole curve to a worse-case VF corner, scale IS by exp(-dV/(N*Vt)) (for dV = +0.4 V on red N = 2: IS x 0.0000044).

Valid analyses: `op`, `dc`, `tran`, `temp` sweep. `ac` works (CJO, junction conductance) but LED small-signal use is rare. `noise` runs but is not validated.

Valid range: forward 0.1 mA to the rated IF (the card is tuned for 10 to 100 mA; below 1 mA VF is unreliable, red within about 0.1 V, blue up to 0.6 V wrong); -40 to +85 C.

Known limitations:
* The D model has no thermal feedback. Self-heating must be iterated by the caller.
* Low-current VF of blue/white is wrong (see fit table).
* No wavelength shift, no efficiency droop at high current (matters for BEH-LED-POWER only).
* Reverse breakdown is a clamp, not a failure; the destruction logic lives in the rating checks (Section 7).
* Capacitance is a constant CJO model; real capacitance varies with bias and is only sourced for red and green.

### 6. Ratings and limits
All checks use the quantities of the part record.

| Name | Symbol | Value | Check expression | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| continuous forward current | IF | per package, derated with temperature | `if_avg <= if_max_derated(Tamb)` | S1..S6 |
| derating | IF(Tamb) | Tamb <= T_knee: if_max; above: limited by dissipation | `p_max(Tamb) = (Tj_max - Tamb)/Rth_ja; if_max(Tamb) = min(if_max, p_max(Tamb)/vf)` | S1, S2, S3 (see consistency check) |
| power | PV | 75 to 100 mW | `vf*if <= p_max(Tamb)` | S1..S6 |
| pulsed current | IFM | tp <= 10 us: 1 A (S1, S3, S4), 0.1 A (S2, S5); tp = 0.1 ms: 80 mA (AlInGaP chip), 100 mA (InGaN chip) (S6) | `i_peak <= ifsm(tp)` and `i_avg <= if_max` | S1..S6 |
| reverse voltage | VR | 5 V or 6 V | `v_reverse <= vr_max` | S1..S6 |
| junction temperature | Tj | 100 C (lamps) | `Tamb + Rth*vf*if <= tj_max` | S1..S5 |

Consistency check made: for S1, S2 and S3 the stated PV equals (Tj_max - T_knee)/RthJA: (100 - 60)/400 = 0.100 W (S1), (100 - 65)/350 = 0.100 W (S2, S3). So the dissipation rating is just the thermal limit at the knee temperature and the linear derating rule above is consistent with the datasheet tables.

Scanning/PWM rule: both `i_peak <= IFM(tp, duty)` and `i_avg <= if_max` must hold. The Kingbright displays (S14, S15) quote peak 150 to 160 mA at 1/10 duty and 0.1 ms pulse with DC 30 mA; Broadcom (S7) quotes 100 mA at 10 percent duty and 1 kHz.

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior

| id | Trigger | Physical effect | sim_response | Permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| overcurrent_cont | IF above if_max_derated, sustained | die and bond-wire overheating, accelerated lumen depreciation, ultimately open or short | flag at `if > if_max`; severity error at `> 1.5*if_max`; mark "degraded" (no simulation change) | permanent (cumulative) |
| overcurrent_pulse | `i_peak` above IFM/IFSM | bond wire fusing, die cracking | flag; at `> 2*IFSM` set part to open after the pulse (replace card with 1 Gohm) | permanent |
| no_resistor | LED across a stiff source (no R) | current limited by RS; destroys within us to ms | the simulation runs (the D model conducts); flag `NO_CURRENT_LIMIT`; the verifier rule already catches this in the repo | permanent |
| reverse_over_rating | `v_reverse > vr_max` (5 or 6 V) | leakage rises; InGaN junction may avalanche; sustained reverse current degrades or kills the die | flag `REVERSE_OVER_RATING`; BV clamp in the card keeps the simulation convergent (card conducts 10 uA at 5.5 V, 4.4 mA at 6.0 V for blue, bench B4) | recoverable below damage; permanent if current exceeds a few mA (ASSUMPTION) |
| overtemperature | Tj > tj_max (100 C lamps) | package yellowing, die damage | flag; use `Tamb + Rth*P` | permanent |
| esd | HBM events | latent or immediate junction damage; InGaN parts are most sensitive. Only XP-E2 white gives a number (8 kV HBM, S8); Broadcom (S7) warns the parts are ESD sensitive without a number | not simulated | permanent |
| open | bond wire broken | no conduction | model as open (Gohm) | permanent |
| short | rare die short | low-resistance conduction | model as RS only (about 5 ohm) | permanent |

### 8. Thermal behavior
Self-heating: P = VF*IF and Tj = Tamb + Rth_ja*P_heat. For a 5 mm lamp at 20 mA and 2 V: 40 mW * 350 K/W = 14 K. Blue at 20 mA and 3.9 V: 78 mW * 350 = 27 K. At the Vishay PV limit (100 mW) the rise is 35 to 40 K, which is exactly why Tj_max = 100 C and the knee is 60 to 65 C. VF falls about 2 to 3 mV/K, so on a voltage-ish drive the current rises with temperature; with a resistor the effect is small (resistor drop dominates). For chip LEDs there is no opened Rth; use ASSUMPTION 400 to 500 K/W for 0603 and larger board-dependent values, flagged L.

### 9. Appearance summary
Round or rectangular epoxy lamps with a flange, flat cathode side and two leads of unequal length, or small rectangular chips with a cathode mark. See 3D spec entries OHM-073 to OHM-081 (flange flat at -X, terminal 1 cathode). Lens tint follows led_color.

Result summary: 6 of 6 benches in this class agree with the analytical expectation; B1's blue 1 mA mismatch is a documented model limitation, not an unexplained disagreement (the extracted datasheet point implies N about 12).

### 11. Canonical YAML
```yaml
behavior_id: BEH-LED-INDICATOR
applies_to: [OHM-073, OHM-074, OHM-075, OHM-076, OHM-077, OHM-078, OHM-079, OHM-080, OHM-081]
layer: L1
category: diode
pins:
  - {name: A, role: anode, electrical_type: passive, package_terminal_rule: "terminal 2 (+X, long lead / unmarked end)"}
  - {name: K, role: cathode, electrical_type: passive, package_terminal_rule: "terminal 1 (-X, flat side / marked end)"}
parameters:
  colour: {unit: enum, default: red}
  vf_typ: {unit: V, default: 2.0, min: 1.8, max: 4.5, tolerance: "typ to max +0.4..+0.7 V", basis: MFR_DATASHEET, confidence: M, source_ref: S1}
  if_test: {unit: A, default: 0.020, basis: MFR_DATASHEET, confidence: H, source_ref: S1}
  if_max: {unit: A, default: 0.020, min: 0.020, max: 0.050, basis: MFR_DATASHEET, confidence: M, source_ref: S1}
  p_max: {unit: W, default: 0.100, basis: MFR_DATASHEET, confidence: M, source_ref: S1}
  tj_max: {unit: C, default: 100, basis: MFR_DATASHEET, confidence: M, source_ref: S1}
  rth_ja: {unit: K/W, default: 350, min: 350, max: 400, basis: MFR_DATASHEET, confidence: M, source_ref: S1}
  vr_max: {unit: V, default: 5, min: 5, max: 6, basis: MFR_DATASHEET, confidence: H, source_ref: S2}
  IS: {unit: A, default: 1.846e-16, basis: DERIVED, confidence: L, source_ref: S1}
  N: {unit: 1, default: 2.0, basis: ASSUMPTION, confidence: L}
  RS: {unit: ohm, default: 16.4, basis: DERIVED, confidence: L, source_ref: S1}
  CJO: {unit: F, default: 30e-12, basis: MFR_DATASHEET, confidence: M, source_ref: S1}
model:
  fidelity: behavioural_approximation
  spice_primitives: [D, B]
  netlist_template: |
    D{ref} {A} {K} LED_{colour}
    .model LED_{colour} D (IS={IS} N={N} RS={RS} CJO={CJO} VJ=1.0 M=0.33 TT=0 BV={BV} IBV=10u EG={EG} XTI=3)
  valid_analyses: [op, dc, tran, temp]
  valid_range: "0.1 mA to rated IF, -40..+85 C; blue/white below 1 mA unreliable"
  known_limitations: ["no thermal feedback in the D model", "blue/white low-current VF wrong by up to 0.6 V", "no wavelength shift or droop", "chip LED Rth unsourced"]
ratings:
  - {name: forward_current, symbol: IF, value: 0.020, unit: A, condition: "default, package specific", check: "if_avg <= if_max_derated", source_ref: S1}
  - {name: power, symbol: PV, value: 0.100, unit: W, condition: "Tamb <= 60..65 C", check: "vf*if <= (tj_max - tamb)/rth_ja", source_ref: S1}
  - {name: reverse_voltage, symbol: VR, value: 5, unit: V, condition: "IR = 10 uA", check: "v_reverse <= vr_max", source_ref: S2}
  - {name: surge, symbol: IFSM, value: 0.1, unit: A, condition: "tp <= 10 us (blue/white), 1 A GaP/GaAlAs", check: "i_peak <= ifsm", source_ref: S2}
failure_modes:
  - {id: overcurrent_cont, trigger: "IF > if_max_derated", effect: "degradation, eventual open", sim_response: "flag; error at 1.5x", permanence: permanent}
  - {id: reverse_over_rating, trigger: "VR > vr_max", effect: "avalanche, possible damage", sim_response: "flag; BV clamp in card", permanence: permanent}
  - {id: no_resistor, trigger: "LED on stiff source", effect: "destruction", sim_response: "flag NO_CURRENT_LIMIT", permanence: permanent}
```

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-LED-RGB

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
Colour mixing indicators and decorative lighting: three independent LED dies (red, green, blue) in one package, driven by three PWM channels. Typical use: status LEDs with colour coding, mood lighting, UI feedback. Forms here: PLCC-4 3528 (4 pins) and 5050 (6 pins).

### 2. What it is and how it works
Three separate LED junctions: red is AlInGaP (VF about 2.1 V), green and blue are InGaN (VF about 3.1 V; Broadcom ASMB-MTB0-0A3A2 typical, S7). Each behaves as the BEH-LED-INDICATOR model. The 4-pin package ties one electrode of all three (common anode in the Broadcom part, S7) to save pins; the 6-pin package brings out all six electrodes. Colour is set by the three currents; perceived colour depends on the relative intensities. Per-die ratings differ (S7): red 25 mA, green/blue 25 mA DC, power 65 mW red and 90 mW green/blue, peak 100 mA at 10 percent duty at 1 kHz, Tj 110 C.

### 3. How it connects
4-pin common-anode part (Broadcom pin map S7): pin 1 = common anode to the positive rail, pins 2, 3, 4 = blue, green, red cathodes each through its own resistor to the sinking driver (low-side GPIO or MOSFET). Common-cathode parts reverse this. Because VF differs (2.1 V red vs 3.1 V green/blue), each channel needs its own resistor value: at 5 V and 20 mA, red 145 ohm and green/blue 95 ohm (bench B7). Mistakes: one shared resistor (colour and current shift); wiring a 3.3 V logic high directly onto a common-anode cathode without checking that the green/blue die has headroom (3.3 V rail minus 3.1 V VF leaves 0.2 V and an unusable current); assuming the 3D-spec pin numbers imply function (they do not, see conflict below).

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
Layer L1. Fidelity `behavioural_approximation`. Three `D` instances sharing one common node.

```
* common anode (Broadcom ASMB-MTB0 map): pin1 = CA, pin2 = B-, pin3 = G-, pin4 = R-
D{ref}R {CA} {Rk} LED_RGB_R
D{ref}G {CA} {Gk} LED_RGB_GB
D{ref}B {CA} {Bk} LED_RGB_GB
.model LED_RGB_R  D (IS=4.848e-18 N=2.0 RS=12  CJO=30p VJ=1.0 M=0.33 BV=5.5 IBV=10u EG=2.2 XTI=3)
.model LED_RGB_GB D (IS=4.526e-19 N=3.0 RS=6.3 CJO=60p VJ=1.0 M=0.33 BV=5.5 IBV=10u EG=4.0 XTI=3)
```
For common-cathode parts swap anode and cathode of the three diodes and take `{CA}` as the cathode node. Parameter derivation: IS from VF typ at 20 mA (S7); N and RS are ASSUMPTIONs (marked L). Valid analyses op, dc, tran, temp. Limitations: no colour model (the simulator outputs three currents; mixing is a display-layer calculation); per-die thermal coupling is not modeled (dies share a package, so the real part has about 3 times the dissipation on one Rth_ja); Cj values assumed.

| vf_r @ 20 mA | V | 2.1 | 1.8 | 2.6 | MFR_DATASHEET | S7 |
| vf_g, vf_b @ 20 mA | V | 3.1 | 2.8 | 3.6 | MFR_DATASHEET | S7 |
| if_max per die | A | 0.025 | | | MFR_DATASHEET (Broadcom part) | S7 |
| ifm per die (10 percent duty, 1 kHz) | A | 0.100 | | | MFR_DATASHEET | S7 |

### 6. Ratings and limits
Checks per die: `if_die <= 0.025`, `v_die*if_die <= p_max_die`, `i_peak <= 0.100 at duty <= 0.10 and f = 1 kHz`; package: `sum(v_die*if_die) <= 0.2` W (sum of die powers, ASSUMPTION: no package-level figure was extracted); reverse: none above 0 V recommended (flag any reverse bias on a die); `Tj <= 110 C`.

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior
Same pattern as indicator LED, per die: overcurrent flag at 25 mA, open-die on gross overload; reverse bias flagged; wrong resistor per colour flagged when `vf_die` mismatch causes `if_die > if_max`. A shared-resistor topology is flagged `RGB_SHARED_RESISTOR` (design rule, not physical). ESD: S7 warns LEDs are ESD sensitive without a figure.

### 8. Thermal behavior
Package dissipation is the sum of three dies; Tj = Tamb + Rth_ja*P_total (Rth not extracted; RESEARCH_REQUIRED). At 20 mA each: P = 42 mW + 62 mW + 62 mW = 166 mW, above any single-die figure but split over three dies; check per-die PD and the package total.

### 9. Appearance summary
See OHM-082 (3528 body with four terminals and a pin-1 chamfer or dot) and OHM-083 (5050 body with six terminals, chamfer at pin 1). Both have a clear or diffused lens over three dies.

### 10. Validation benches
`/home/claude/behavior/bench/beh-led-indicator/B7_rgb_common_anode.cir` (RGB common-anode 5 V rail with per-colour cathode resistors 145, 95, 95 ohm). Expected: each die 20.000 mA by solving Vs = I*(R+RS) + N*Vt*ln(I/IS+1) (Python brentq: 20.00003 mA red, 20.00005 mA green/blue). Measured: 20.00003, 20.00006, 20.00006 mA. PASS.
Second bench: B2 and B3 of BEH-LED-INDICATOR apply to each die unchanged (same D card equations).
Result: 1 of 1 dedicated bench matched, plus shared-equation benches B2 and B3 of the indicator class.

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-LED-POWER

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
Illumination: flashlights, work lights, grow lights, automotive and architectural lighting, projectors, machine-vision strobes. A 1 W to 3 W class emitter (default 3535 package, Cree XLamp XP-E2 class) driven at 350 mA to 1 A from a constant-current driver, mounted on a heat-spreading board. The star module (OHM-086) is the same emitter pre-mounted on a 20 mm aluminium MCPCB with two or four solder pads, to be bolted to a heat sink.

### 2. What it is and how it works
An InGaN blue die with phosphor (white), or a coloured die, on a ceramic or plastic substrate with a thermal pad. The forward voltage is about 2.9 to 3.25 V at 350 mA and 3.05 to 3.15 V at 700 to 1000 mA for the white parts (Tj = 85 C, S8). Efficiency is below 50 percent, so most of the electrical power becomes heat that must leave through the thermal pad and board.

Key physics:
* Thermal: Tj = Ts + Rth_js*P_heat, where Rth_js is the junction-to-solder-point resistance. XP-E2 (S8): white/royal blue/blue 9 C/W, green 15, PC amber 9, amber 7, red/red-orange 5 C/W. Tj max 150 C. A sink adds Rth_sa; with the board and sink the junction can easily reach 100 to 150 C.
* Efficiency droop: light output rises less than linearly with current. S8 (white, Tj = 85 C): flux roughly doubles from 350 mA to 1000 mA (a 2.86x current increase), so the local exponent is about ln2/ln2.86 = 0.66 (extractor reading of a graph, confidence L).
* Temperature: white flux falls about 20 percent from Tj = 25 C to 150 C at 350 mA (S8), 0.16 percent per K on average. Red, amber fall much faster (not extracted).
* Why a current source is needed: VF falls about 2 to 3 mV/K and the I-V curve is steep (dynamic resistance about 0.2 ohm; N*Vt/I = 0.1 ohm at 0.9 A). On a voltage-ish drive a 10 K rise at fixed voltage raises current by 3 mV/K*10K/(N*Vt = 0.093 V) = 32 percent, more heat, more current: thermal runaway (positive feedback). A series resistor stabilises only if its drop is at least comparable to the LED's tempco swing (about 0.3 V over 100 K). Constant-current sinks/buck drivers remove the feedback. Bench B2 shows 0.143 A cold (25 C) rising to 0.223 A after three electro-thermal iterations from a fixed 3.0 V source and 0.1 ohm, a 56 percent increase from a 17 K rise.
* Pulsed operation: S8 gives no pulsed rating in the extraction; pulse limits must come from the chosen MPN.

### 3. How it connects
Two electrical terminals (anode +, cathode -) plus a thermal pad. XP-E2 bottom view marks the anode with "+" in a circle (S8). The 3D spec entry OHM-085 numbers pad 1 = cathode, pad 2 = anode, pad 3 = thermal (KiCad XP convention). Whether the thermal pad is electrically isolated from the anode and cathode was NOT established from the opened document: treat as RESEARCH_REQUIRED, default to isolated (no conduction in the model, ERC warning if tied to a net other than copper heat-spreading area). Typical circuit: buck or linear constant-current driver (LM3406-class, ASSUMPTION, no document opened) with the LED in series with a sense resistor; low-side PWM dimming at 200 Hz to 20 kHz for brightness. Mistakes: driving from a voltage source with a small resistor (runaway); leaving the thermal pad unsoldered or on an insulating board (Tj exceeds 150 C in seconds at 1 A); using FR4 with no copper pour; reverse-polarity at the driver (VR 5 V, S8).

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
Layer: **L1 plus a thermal sub-model**. Fidelity: `behavioural_approximation`.

```
D{ref} {A} {K} LED_XPE2
.model LED_XPE2 D (IS=1.87e-14 N=3.0 RS=0.2233 CJO=300p VJ=1.0 M=0.33 BV=5 IBV=10u EG=3.9 XTI=3 TNOM=85)
* thermal (electro-thermal fixed point, ngspice .temp is global): Tj = Ta + (Rth_js + Rth_sa)*(1 - eta)*Vf*If
* behavioural flux:  phi_rel = (If/If_ref)^0.66 * (1 + k_T*(Tj - 25))
```
Fit (script `/home/claude/behavior/tmp_R5_fit.py` and the inline solve): N = 3 assumed, points (700 mA, 3.05 V), (1.0 A, 3.15 V) at Tj = 85 C from S8; solved IS = 1.87e-14 A, RS = 0.223 ohm using Vt at 85 C (30.86 mV). Cross-check against a point not used in the fit: 350 mA gives 2.91 V, inside the S8 range 2.9 to 3.25 V (lower end). TNOM = 85 so the card equals the datasheet points at Tj = 85 C. EG = 3.9 gives dVF/dT about -3 mV/K (ASSUMPTION). CJO = 300 pF, M, VJ are ASSUMPTIONs.

The thermal model uses the fixed-point loop in `B1_cc_selfheat.cir`: set `option temp = Tj`, run `op`, compute heat = (1 - eta)*Vf*If, update Tj. eta = 0.30 and Rth_sa = 30 K/W are ASSUMPTIONs (S8 gives Rth_js only). The loop converged in under 12 iterations in all cases tried. Valid analyses: `op` with the loop, `dc`, `tran` with a thermal RC if needed (thermal time constants of die/board are seconds, not modeled; the model is steady-state).

Known limitations: no ngspice-native per-instance self-heating (temperature is global in a deck unless the `temp`/`dtemp` instance parameters are used); droop, flux and wavelength shift are post-processing, not part of the electrical solution; no pulsed derating; thermal pad assumed isolated; star MCPCB Rth unknown.

### 6. Ratings and limits
`if <= 1.0 A` (absolute maximum drive current); `Tj = Ta + (Rth_js + Rth_sa)*P_heat <= 150 C` (derate current so this holds: `if_max(Ta) = min(1.0, (150 - Ta)/((Rth_js+Rth_sa)*(1-eta)*vf))`); `v_reverse <= 5 V`; ESD 8 kV HBM white; no pulsed rating available (RESEARCH_REQUIRED). Recommended operating: keep Tj below about 100 C for lifetime (general practice, ASSUMPTION; lumen maintenance tables not opened).

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior
| id | Trigger | Effect | sim_response | Permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| overtemp | Tj > 150 C | phosphor/lens degradation, die and bond failure | flag at 150 C; error and open the part at `Tj > 175 C` (ASSUMPTION) | permanent |
| overcurrent | if > 1 A | thermal and electromigration damage | flag; open the part at 1.5 A sustained (ASSUMPTION) | permanent |
| thermal_runaway | voltage drive, no limit | current rises with Tj, positive feedback | the iterative loop detects `Tj` diverging or `if > 1 A` and reports `THERMAL_RUNAWAY` | permanent |
| reverse | v_reverse > 5 V | avalanche, die damage | flag; BV clamp | permanent |
| no_heatsink | Rth_sa unknown or very high | overtemp | flag `NO_THERMAL_PATH` when pad not tied to copper | permanent |
| esd | HBM above 8 kV | damage | not simulated | permanent |

### 8. Thermal behavior
See Sections 2 and 4. Worked case, bench B1: 700 mA, Rth_js 9 + Rth_sa 30 K/W, eta 0.30, Ta = 25 C: P_el = 0.7*3.055 = 2.14 W, heat 1.50 W, Tj = 83.4 C; at the same Tj the VF is 3.055 V. Independent calculation with a 3 mV/K slope: Tj = 83.378 C, VF = 3.0549 V. With Rth_sa = 40 K/W Tj would reach 25 + 49*1.5 = 98.5 C; with no sink (Rth_sa = 60 K/W) Tj = 25 + 69*1.5 = 128.5 C (arithmetic from the same formula, not simulated).

### 9. Appearance summary
OHM-085: 3.45 mm square ceramic/plastic package with a yellow phosphor dome and three underside pads (cathode, anode, thermal). OHM-086: a 20 mm MCPCB star carrying one such emitter with wire pads. See 3D spec entries OHM-085 and OHM-086.

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-LED-ADDRESSABLE

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
WS2812B-style integrated LED: a red, green and blue LED plus a small control IC in one 5050 package. A microcontroller sends one serial stream on one wire; each pixel takes its 24 bits, latches them, and forwards the rest. Used in LED strips, matrices, wearables, status bars. Each pixel can draw up to tens of mA per colour, so a strip is a power distribution problem as much as a data problem.

### 2. What it is and how it works
Contents: three constant-current drivers with 8-bit PWM greyscale per colour (the exact PWM frequency is not in the opened extract; commonly stated around 400 Hz to 2 kHz, unverified), a signal reshaper and a data latch. Interface: DIN receives the stream, DOUT re-transmits after the pixel has consumed its own 24 bits. Pins (S9, matches the 3D spec): 1 VDD, 2 DOUT, 3 VSS, 4 DIN.

Data format (S9): 24 bits per pixel in GRB order, MSB first: G7..G0, R7..R0, B7..B0. A bit is one high pulse then low pulse within a period of 1.25 us (TH + TL = 1.25 us +- 600 ns); code 0: T0H = 0.4 us, T0L = 0.85 us; code 1: T1H = 0.8 us, T1L = 0.45 us; each +-150 ns; reset (latch) = low for at least 50 us (this revision). The stream is passed through: the first 24 bits are taken by pixel 1, the rest shaped and sent on DOUT. After the reset low period, all pixels latch and display.

Electrical characteristics (S9): VDD 3.5 to 5.3 V as printed in the maximum ratings table (the electrical-characteristics table is stated for VDD 4.5 to 5.5 V; this is internally inconsistent in the document and is reported, not resolved); input VIH >= 0.7*VDD, VIL <= 0.3*VDD, hysteresis 0.35 V typical, input current +-1 uA; Vin absolute range -0.5 V to VDD + 0.5 V; operating junction -25 to +80 C; storage -40 to +105 C. LED die characteristics: red 620 to 625 nm, 390 to 420 mcd, 2.0 to 2.2 V; green 522 to 525 nm, 660 to 720 mcd, 3.0 to 3.4 V; blue 465 to 467 nm, 180 to 200 mcd, 3.0 to 3.4 V (these are the LED forward voltages per colour; a constant-current driver sits in series, so the pin supply must exceed the highest VF plus the driver dropout, hence the 3.5 V minimum VDD).

### 3. How it connects
VDD (pin 1) to a 5 V rail with a 100 nF decoupling capacitor close to each pixel (common practice, ASSUMPTION), VSS (pin 3) to ground, DIN (pin 4) from the previous pixel's DOUT or from the microcontroller, DOUT (pin 2) to the next DIN. Ground must be common to the data source. Mistakes: driving DIN from a 3.3 V GPIO when VDD = 5 V (VIH = 0.7*5 V = 3.5 V is above 3.3 V, so the 3.3 V high level does not meet the specification; use a level shifter or lower VDD to 4.5 V or below, giving VIH = 3.15 V); long data line without series resistor (ringing); feeding power only at one end of a long strip (voltage drop dims or colour-shifts the far pixels, see bench B2); reset time too short between frames (pixels never latch; newer revisions reportedly require a longer reset than 50 us, which this opened datasheet does not show, RESEARCH_REQUIRED); VDD above 5.3 V (rating).

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
Layers: **L1 supply, L2 input thresholds, L3 protocol and pixel state.** The part is NOT simulable by SPICE alone.

**L1 (SPICE).** Model each pixel as a supply load (constant-current with brown-out) and a high-impedance data input:
```
* L1 supply load: static + three constant-current channels scaled by a brown-out factor (ASSUMPTION values)
B{ref}load {VDD} {VSS} I = {iq} + {ich}*({r_duty}+{g_duty}+{b_duty})*min(max((v({VDD},{VSS})-3.0)/0.5,0),1)
* DIN: high-impedance CMOS input, Cin ASSUMPTION
RIN{ref} {DIN} {VSS} 100Meg
CIN{ref} {DIN} {VSS} 5p
* DOUT: push-pull output, driven by the L3 model (see below), Rout ASSUMPTION 50 ohm
```
Parameters (basis in brackets): iq = 1 mA (ASSUMPTION), ich = 20 mA per colour at 100 percent (ASSUMPTION: 60 mA per pixel at full white, widely quoted but not in the opened extract; datasheet current per channel RESEARCH_REQUIRED), brown-out knee 3.0 to 3.5 V (ASSUMPTION; the datasheet minimum VDD of 3.5 V is the sourced anchor). Duty values r_duty, g_duty, b_duty come from the L3 state (value/255; PWM average, not simulated per cycle unless a PWM stimulus is used).

**L2 (digital).** Input thresholds VIH = 0.7*VDD, VIL = 0.3*VDD, hysteresis 0.35 V (S9); a Schmitt-trigger with these values can be an XSPICE `d_*` or B-source comparator with hysteresis. Bit decode: the pixel classifies each high pulse by width using an internal reference; the datasheet nominal windows are T0H = 0.4 us +-150 ns and T1H = 0.8 us +-150 ns, so a pulse is code 0 for T_high < about 0.6 us and code 1 for T_high > about 0.6 us (decision boundary derived as the midpoint, ASSUMPTION; the datasheet gives only the nominal windows).

**L3 (what a higher-layer model must implement).**
1. Bit decoder: sample the DIN waveform; on each rising edge start timing the high pulse; at the falling edge classify as 0 or 1 using the windows above; fail (frame error) if a full bit period T_bit is outside 1.25 us +-600 ns (S9).
2. 24-bit shift register per pixel in GRB order, MSB first. The first complete 24 bits after a reset belong to the first pixel; later bits are forwarded to DOUT (with re-shaping: DOUT edges delayed by a small propagation delay, value unspecified in the opened extract, RESEARCH_REQUIRED).
3. Reset detect: DIN low for >= 50 us (S9). On reset: latch the shift registers to the PWM stage, ready for the next frame. A frame with fewer bits than the chain needs leaves later pixels unchanged.
4. PWM output stage: three channels at value/255 duty (greyscale); average LED current = ich*value/255 per colour (L1 bridge).
5. Power-up state: undefined/dark until the first data; no data retention across power loss.
Not simulated at SPICE level: the datasheet-level waveform shaping, the internal oscillator, PWM frequency.

Fidelity: `behavioural_approximation` for L1 numbers; protocol layer has no fidelity label, it is a software model of the documented protocol (S9). No vendor model is attached.

### 6. Ratings and limits
`3.5 <= VDD <= 5.3` (flag `VDD_OUT_OF_RANGE`; the stricter reading of the document); `V(DIN) in [VSS - 0.5, VDD + 0.5]` (flag overstress); `V(DIN, high) >= 0.7*VDD` for guaranteed level detection (flag `LOGIC_LEVEL_MARGIN` when a 3.3 V source drives a 5 V pixel); `Tj <= 80 C` operating junction, `-25 C` minimum; total chain current check: `sum(i_pixel) <= feed_current_rating` of the supply path (design rule).

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior
VDD above 5.3 V: exceeds the maximum ratings; the sim flags it and treats the part as damaged (LED stays dark, pixel stops forwarding) when `VDD > 6 V` (ASSUMPTION; the rating margin is not quantified). Reverse VDD: no reverse protection stated for WS2812B; treat as damaging (ASSUMPTION). DIN above VDD + 0.5 V or below VSS - 0.5 V: overstress flag (input ESD structure conducts; permanent damage possible). Data timing out of window: the L3 decoder reports `BIT_TIMING_VIOLATION` and the pixel state becomes undefined (the real part misreads bits, producing wrong colours). Broken chain (a dead pixel): all downstream pixels receive no data. Over-temperature: flag at 80 C junction. ESD: not quantified in the opened text.

### 8. Thermal behavior
Per-pixel dissipation at 5 V and 60 mA is about 0.3 W (ASSUMPTION from the current figure); Rth is not given, so a package-level thermal model is RESEARCH_REQUIRED; rule of thumb: derate brightness on dense matrices, check board copper.

### 9. Appearance summary
5050 body with four terminals and a chamfer at pin 1 (VDD top-left per the 3D spec, though the corner is not verified from the datasheet drawing). See OHM-084.

T0H = 400 ns + 5 ns (edge asymmetry), etc. | datasheet window +-150 ns | T0H 405 ns, T0L 845 ns, T1H 805 ns, T1L 445 ns, T_bit 1.250 us. PASS (all inside windows) |
| B2 | B2_chain_supply_droop.cir | 10 pixels at 61 mA each (60 mA + 1 mA), 0.05 ohm per segment; V_end = 5 - Rseg*Ipix*N(N+1)/2 = 4.83225 V | 1 mV | V(n10) = 4.83225 V, V(n1) = 4.9695 V. PASS |

Honest limits: B1 verifies the stimulus (timing numbers of the datasheet) only; it does not test a device model. B2 verifies the L1 constant-current load model and the supply droop arithmetic with ASSUMPTION current numbers. Result: 2 of 2 match, with those scope limits.

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-DISP-LEDARRAY

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
Numeric and dot-matrix LED displays: clocks, meters, appliance panels, scoreboards, simple graphics. Entries: single, dual and four-digit 7-segment displays (OHM-087, 088, 089) and the 8x8 LED matrix (OHM-090). They are groups of LEDs wired with shared anodes or cathodes to cut pin count, driven by multiplexing (time-sharing) from a microcontroller or a driver IC (MAX7219-class, TM1637-class: not opened here, so not specified).

### 2. What it is and how it works
**7-segment digit.** Eight LEDs: segments a (top), b (upper right), c (lower right), d (bottom), e (lower left), f (upper left), g (middle) and dp (decimal point, right-hand for the opened Kingbright part, S14 "Rt Hand Decimal"). Common-cathode: all cathodes joined, drive segments high; common-anode: all anodes joined, drive segments low. The Kingbright SC56-11EWA (digit 0.56 in, red) is common cathode with VF 2.0 V typ and 2.5 V max at 20 mA, DC 30 mA, peak 160 mA at 1/10 duty and 0.1 ms pulse, VR 5 V, PD 105 mW per segment (S14, DSAA5198 V.2, 9 Jan 2003; the digikey page for the part says common cathode, 2 V, 20 mA, S17).

Digit patterns (standard font, bits a..g; used by the L2 drive model): 0 = abcdef, 1 = bc, 2 = abdeg, 3 = abcdg, 4 = bcfg, 5 = acdfg, 6 = acdefg, 7 = abc, 8 = abcdefg, 9 = abcdfg.

**Multi-digit displays.** Segment pins are shared across digits (all digits' "a" segments joined, etc.) and each digit has its own common pin. The driver turns on one digit at a time (digit select) while presenting that digit's segment pattern on the segment lines, cycling fast. The eye integrates the light (persistence of vision): if the whole frame repeats faster than about 60 to 100 Hz (general vision physics; flicker visibility depends on brightness and eye movement, ASSUMPTION), the display looks steady. Each digit is on for 1/N of the time (N = digits), so its average current is Ipk/N and its average brightness is about 1/N of continuous drive at the same peak current. To get the same perceived brightness as steady drive the peak current is raised by about N (within the pulsed rating).

**8x8 matrix.** 64 LEDs arranged as 8 rows by 8 columns; each LED anode on a row line and cathode on a column line (or the reverse for "column anode" parts). One row is enabled at a time (all columns are driven with that row's pixel pattern). Single-row current: up to 8 LEDs lit, each with its own column current limit; per-LED average current is Ipk/8. The Kingbright TC23-11 family (8x8, 58 mm, S15) is offered in column-cathode and column-anode versions, VF 2.1 V typ (2.5 V max) at 20 mA, DC 30 mA, peak 150 mA at 1/10 duty and 0.1 ms. The OHM-090 default is a 32 mm "1588BS-style" matrix for which NO datasheet was opened (3D spec); the TC23-11 data is used only as a class reference.

Multiplexing physics: ghosting (a faint image of the wrong pixel) appears when a row/column line is not fully deselected before the next one is enabled (capacitance CJO, driver slow turn-off); real designs add a dead time. In the model, the simulation of ghosting needs CJO and the driver Ron/Roff; the benches use a 1 us dead time.

### 3. How it connects
* Each LED group is a diode; the common pin (cathode for common-cathode parts) goes to a low-side switch (digit select), and every segment pin goes to a driver output through a current-limiting resistor (about 100 to 330 ohm at 5 V, from (Vs - VF)/IF; bench B2 uses 150 ohm) or to a constant-current driver IC.
* Multiplex timing: choose frame rate >= 100 Hz and a duty of about 1/N; peak current <= the pulsed rating, average current per LED <= DC rating.
* Mistakes: one resistor for all segments on the common pin (brightness changes with the number of lit segments); peak current above the pulsed rating after raising it to compensate for duty; confusing common anode with common cathode (nothing lights); connecting the display directly to a microcontroller pin without a resistor; forgetting that a digit select pin sinks the sum of all lit segments (8 segments x 20 mA = 160 mA, above a 20 mA GPIO limit, so use a transistor).

Pin maps (segment to pin) vary by MPN and are NOT available from the opened documents. Unverified conventional layouts are given in the per-entry sections, flagged ASSUMPTION; the behavior layer must take the map from the chosen MPN's datasheet.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
Layer: **L1** (each LED a D card) plus **L2** drive pattern (which segments/rows conduct when, supplied by a stimulus or a higher-layer scan engine). Fidelity `behavioural_approximation`.

Netlist templates:
```
* 7-segment digit, common cathode (pin order is MPN specific)
D{ref}_a {SEG_a} {COM} LED_RED ...  (one D per segment a..g and dp; SEG_x are package terminals from the pin map)
* common anode: D{ref}_a {COM} {SEG_a} LED_RED
* digit select: S{ref}_d {COM_d} {GND} {gate_d} 0 SWMUX  (low-side switch, Ron 10 ohm ASSUMPTION)
* 8x8 matrix, column cathode: D{ref}_{r}_{c} {ROW_r} {COL_c} LED_RED (64 diodes)
```
The `.model LED_RED` card is the BEH-LED-INDICATOR card (the same card works for amber/orange segments with a different IS; the VF of the opened displays, 2.0 to 2.1 V typ, matches the LED_RED card's 2.0 V at 20 mA). Switch model: `.model SWMUX SW(Ron=10 Roff=1G Vt=2.5 Vh=0.1)`. Valid analyses: `tran` (scan), `op` (one static pattern). Limitations: no light model (brightness is average current x efficiency); no ghosting beyond CJO; driver ICs not modeled (their constant-current set resistors would need the IC datasheet).

Luminous output quantity: average segment current Iavg gives relative brightness `Iavg/Iavg_ref` (Talbot-Plateau: perceived brightness of a repeated pulse train equals the time-averaged luminance for rates above flicker fusion, general vision physics; ASSUMPTION for numerical use).

### 5. Parameters
| Name | Unit | Default | Min | Max | Basis | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| vf_seg @ 20 mA | V | 2.0 (red 7-seg), 2.1 (green matrix) | | 2.5 | MFR_DATASHEET | S14, S15 |
| if_dc_seg | A | 0.030 | | | MFR_DATASHEET | S14, S15 |
| if_peak_seg | A | 0.160 (SC56-11EWA), 0.150 (TC23-11) at 1/10 duty, 0.1 ms | | | MFR_DATASHEET | S14, S15 |
| pd_seg | W | 0.105 | | | MFR_DATASHEET | S14 |
| vr_max | V | 5 | | | MFR_DATASHEET | S14, S15 |
| common_type | enum | cathode | | | per MPN | S14, S15, S17 |
| n_digits / rows | | 1, 2, 4 / 8 | | | spec | 3D spec |
| frame_rate | Hz | 100 | 60 | | ASSUMPTION | |
| duty per digit | | 1/N | | | derived | |
| seg R | ohm | 150 (5 V, 20 mA) | | | DERIVED | |

### 6. Ratings and limits
Per segment/LED: `i_avg <= 0.030`, `i_peak <= 0.160 at duty <= 0.10 and tp <= 0.1 ms` (SC56) / `0.150` (TC23), `v_reverse <= 5 V`, `vf*i <= 0.105 W`. Scan rule: for N digits, `i_peak = i_avg_target * N` must satisfy both limits; `1/N` duty and tp = frame/N: at 100 Hz and N = 4, tp = 2.5 ms, longer than the 0.1 ms test pulse of the peak rating, so the 160 mA figure does not apply as written; the safe sizing is `i_peak <= 0.030` for long slots (ASSUMPTION; the datasheet quotes the peak rating only for 0.1 ms pulses). Common-pin sum: `i_com = sum of lit segments` must not exceed the switch/driver rating (design rule).

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior
| id | Trigger | Effect | sim_response | Permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| seg_overcurrent | i_avg > 30 mA or i_peak outside the pulse rating | segment degrade/open | flag per segment; open the segment above 2x rating | permanent |
| scan_stall | scan stops with a digit on | a single digit gets full DC current (about N times average), over rating | flag `SCAN_STALL` when one digit conducts > 100 ms at `i > if_dc` | permanent |
| common_mismatch | wrong common type | no light, or reverse bias on LEDs | reverse bias flagged against 5 V | recoverable |
| reverse | v_reverse > 5 V | segment damage | flag; BV clamp in card | permanent |
| ghosting | late deselect | faint extra segment | model through CJO and switch times (qualitative) | n/a |

### 8. Thermal behavior
A digit at 8 segments x 20 mA x 2.0 V = 0.32 W continuous; the module's package Rth is not given (RESEARCH_REQUIRED); use per-segment PD 105 mW as the limit and derate by ambient (no derating curve extracted).

### 9. Appearance summary
Rectangular black or gray plastic bodies with 0.56 in digit windows (7-seg) in a dual-row DIP-like pin layout; matrices are square plates with a dot grid. See 3D spec OHM-087 to OHM-090 (pin 1 at the -X,+Y corner in the OHMNI layout, which corresponds to bottom-left in the upright datasheet view).

### 10. Validation benches
Files in `/home/claude/behavior/bench/beh-led-mux/`.

| Bench | File | Expected | Tolerance | Measured |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | B1_matrix_scan.cir | 64 LEDs, 8 row slots of 124 us in 1 ms, column R = 150 ohm. Per-LED average = 0.124*Ion = 0.124*20.0017 mA = 2.4802 mA; column average = 0.992*Ion = 19.84 mA | 1 percent | LED avg 2.4804 mA, column avg 19.843 mA. PASS. The reported steady peak was 154 mA: this is a capacitive transient (the lit LED charges its own 30 pF and the seven other LED capacitances on the same column, roughly 240 pF, through an ideal 1 ns row edge, order of C*dV/dt), not a conduction current. A re-run with 10 ns row edges gave a peak of 77 mA and an unchanged average (LED avg 2.4807 mA), so the peak scales with edge rate but not 1:10 exactly (not analysed further). The rating check must therefore average over at least 1 us before testing `i_peak`. |
| B2 | B2_digit_mux4.cir | 4 digits, one lit segment each, 4 slots of 249 us, total series R = 160 ohm (150 + switch 10). Ion = 18.8846 mA (Python brentq). Per-digit average = 0.249*Ion = 4.7023 mA; shared segment line average = 0.996*Ion = 18.809 mA | 1 percent | digit avg 4.7023 mA, segment line avg 18.810 mA. PASS |

Result: 2 of 2 benches match.
