## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-DISP-LCD1602

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
A 16-character by 2-line text display module (1602). Used for instruments, prototypes, appliance panels, hobby electronics. It is a glass LCD with an on-module controller (HD44780-compatible; the WH1602B uses ST7066U, S13), an LED backlight and a 16-pin 0.1 in header. Power: logic 5 V (some variants 3.3 V), a separate contrast voltage, and a backlight LED string that is the largest single load.

### 2. What it is and how it works
Twisted-nematic or STN LCD glass driven by a controller that holds a character ROM (5x8 font, ROM version A00/A02, not opened), an 80-byte display-data RAM (DDRAM) and 64-byte character-generator RAM (CGRAM, 8 custom characters). LCD segments are AC-driven at a bias voltage VLCD = VDD - V0 (contrast): too low and the glass is clear, too high and all pixels darken. WH1602B table (S13): logic supply 4.5 to 5.5 V (typ 5 V), LCD supply 3.2 to 5.2 V (temperature dependent), IDD 1.0 to 1.5 mA at 5 V, input high 0.7*VDD to VDD, output high 3.9 V to VDD. The backlight is a separate LED array on A (anode) and K (cathode); the WH1602B extraction gave no backlight current, VF or resistor value, and the chip datasheets do not cover the backlight.

Controller (HD44780U per S10, ST7066 V1.2 per S11): supply 2.7 to 5.5 V; supply current 150 to 600 uA over 3 to 5 V (S10) or 0.3 mA typ and 0.6 mA max at 270 kHz oscillator and 5 V (S11); LCD driver voltage 3.0 to 11 V; internal oscillator 190 to 350 kHz (S10), 270 kHz typ (S11). Conflict kept: module IDD 1.0 to 1.5 mA (S13) exceeds the chip's 0.3 to 0.6 mA (S11), which can be explained by the module's other components (bias network, LCD driver load) and is not resolved from documents.

Display RAM map (S10, S11): two-line mode, line 1 = 0x00 to 0x27, line 2 = 0x40 to 0x67 (40 positions each, 16 visible).

### 3. How it connects
16-pin header (S13 WH1602B; consistent with the 3D spec, which places pins 15 and 16 at A/K): 1 VSS (GND), 2 VDD (+5 V), 3 V0 (contrast, from a 10 k pot between VDD and VSS or a divider), 4 RS (0 = instruction, 1 = data), 5 R/W (0 = write, 1 = read; tie to GND if the host never reads), 6 E (enable strobe), 7 to 14 DB0 to DB7, 15 A (backlight +), 16 K (backlight -). 4-bit mode uses DB4 to DB7 only (DB0 to DB3 unused/left open or tied low), with RS, E (and optionally R/W) from the host: 6 GPIO lines total. Typical wiring mistakes: contrast pin floating or tied wrongly (blank or all-black display; bench B2: with the pot at 80 percent VLCD = 4.0 V); backlight without a series resistor when the module has none (backlight chain burns; many modules include one, which a part record must state); 3.3 V logic on a 5 V module (input high needs 0.7*VDD = 3.5 V); sending data before the 15 ms power-up wait (S10); skipping busy-flag or delay timing.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
Layers: **L1** supply, V0 contrast input and backlight; **L2** logic thresholds; **L3** controller behaviour. The display content is NOT SPICE-simulable.

**L1.**
```
* logic supply: constant-current load (ASSUMPTION value, module sheet gives 1.0..1.5 mA at 5 V, S13)
B{ref}idd {VDD} {VSS} I = {idd}
* contrast input V0: CMOS-class high-impedance
RV0{ref} {V0} {VSS} 100Meg
* backlight: effective diode (Vf, N, RS ASSUMPTIONs; see B1) between A and K
D{ref}bl {A} {K} BL
.model BL D (IS=1.2188e-12 N=6 RS=2 CJO=500p VJ=1.0 BV=5 IBV=10u)
```
Backlight card anchor: Vf = 4.1 V at 100 mA, N = 6 (about two InGaN junctions in series), RS = 2 ohm. These numbers are ASSUMPTIONs for a typical white backlight: no opened document gave them. The part record MUST replace them from the chosen MPN's datasheet.

**L2.** Inputs RS, R/W, E, DB0..DB7: VIH = 0.7*VDD (S13), VIL assumed 0.3*VDD for the controller family (S13 extraction did not give VIL; ASSUMPTION, not in S10/S11 extractions either); DB lines are bidirectional when R/W = 1 (output high 3.9 V to VDD, S13).

**L3 (what a higher-layer model must implement).** Cite S10 (HD44780U) and S11 (ST7066 V1.2):
1. Bus protocol: 4-bit mode: each byte is two E cycles, high nibble first on DB7..DB4, then low nibble; 8-bit mode: one E cycle on DB7..DB0. Data is latched on the falling edge of E.
2. E timing: ST7066 (S11, VCC = 5 V): E cycle >= 400 ns, E pulse width >= 150 ns, address setup (RS/RW before E) >= 30 ns, address hold >= 10 ns, write-data setup >= 40 ns, data hold >= 10 ns, read data delay <= 100 ns. HD44780U (S10 extraction): E cycle >= 500 ns, address setup 40 ns, address hold 10 ns, write-data setup 80 ns, read-data delay <= 160 ns (pulse width not in extraction). Conflict kept: use the stricter combination (500 ns cycle, 80 ns data setup) unless the module's controller is identified.
3. Registers: IR (instruction), DR (data), busy flag BF (read with RS = 0, R/W = 1, DB7), address counter AC (7 bits), shift state, cursor and blink flags.
4. Instruction set (codes from S11; execution times from S10/S11):
   * Clear display 0000 0001, 1.52 ms (clears DDRAM to 0x20, AC = 0)
   * Return home 0000 001x, 1.52 ms
   * Entry mode set 0000 01(I/D)(S), 37 us
   * Display on/off control 0000 1(D)(C)(B), 37 us
   * Cursor or display shift 0001 (S/C)(R/L)xx, 37 us
   * Function set 001(DL)(N)(F)xx, 37 us (DL = 1 for 8-bit, N = 1 for 2 lines, F = 1 for 5x10 dots)
   * Set CGRAM address 01(AC5..AC0), 37 us
   * Set DDRAM address 1(AC6..AC0), 37 us
   * Read busy flag and address 0 us
   * Write data to RAM 43 us (S11) or 37 + 4 us (S10, about 41 us)
   * Read data from RAM 43 us
   (The S11 extraction printed some codes (function set, set CGRAM, set DDRAM) in a way that disagrees with the standard HD44780 table; the codes above follow the standard HD44780 encoding: function set 001 DL N F, CGRAM 01 AAAAAA, DDRAM 1 AAAAAAA. Execution times at 270 kHz are consistent: 37 us = 10 cycles, 1.52 ms = 410 cycles. The behavior layer must still check the standard codes against S10 when implemented.)
5. Initialization by instruction (4-bit), S10/S11: wait more than 15 ms after VCC > 4.5 V; write function set 0x3 (high nibble only, DB7..DB4 = 0011); wait more than 4.1 ms; write 0x3 again; wait more than 100 us; write 0x3 a third time; write 0x2 (switch to 4-bit); then function set (N, F), display off, display clear, entry mode set, display on. Power-on reset (S10): needs supply rise time 0.1 to 10 ms; otherwise the internal reset fails and the manual sequence is required.
6. Busy: after each instruction, either poll BF or wait the execution time; while BF = 1 further instructions are ignored (real behaviour); the simulator should drop or flag instructions sent while BF = 1.
7. DDRAM/CGRAM semantics: auto-increment/decrement of AC after each write (entry mode I/D), display shift (S), CGRAM 5x8 patterns at 0x00..0x3F for characters 0..7, line 2 offset 0x40, hidden DDRAM positions beyond 16 (up to 0x27 and 0x67) that scroll into view with display shift.
8. Display on/off, cursor and blink, contrast (analog: VLCD vs V0, not a command).
9. Backlight: independent of the controller (L1 only).

Fidelity: L1 pieces `behavioural_approximation` with assumed backlight numbers; L2/L3 software behaviour has no fidelity label.

### 6. Ratings and limits
`4.5 <= VDD <= 5.5` for the 5 V module (flag `VDD_RANGE`); `3.2 <= VDD - V0 <= 5.2` for readable contrast (flag `CONTRAST_RANGE` outside); logic inputs `<= VDD + 0.3 V`, `>= -0.3 V` (general CMOS practice, ASSUMPTION; absolute maxima not extracted); backlight `If <= its rated current` (MPN specific; 100 mA default assumption flagged); controller protocol checks (setup/hold, E width) at L3.

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior
Contrast outside range: display blank or all dark (L3 visual flag, not electrical damage). Backlight over current: LED string damage (flag `BACKLIGHT_OVERCURRENT`; permanent). VDD high: damage above about 7 V (ASSUMPTION; not extracted). Early commands or wrong init: undefined display state; the L3 model should enter a "not initialised" state, shows garbage or blank. 3.3 V host drive of a 5 V module: `LOGIC_LEVEL_MARGIN` flag (VIH = 3.5 V). Timing violations of E: unreliable latching; flag and corrupt the nibble.

### 8. Thermal behavior
Controller negligible (about 6 mW). Backlight dissipates about 0.4 W at 100 mA and 4.1 V (Section 4 assumption). Temperature shifts the required LCD voltage (S13 says LCD supply is temperature dependent); contrast drifts with temperature (qualitative).

### 9. Appearance summary
80 x 36 mm PCB with a rectangular window, 16-pin header at the top edge, 4 corner mounting holes, backlight behind the glass. See OHM-091.

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-DISP-OLED-I2C

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
A 0.96 in 128x64 monochrome OLED module with I2C, driven by the Solomon Systech SSD1306 controller. Used for status screens, sensor read-outs, small UIs. Four-pin form: GND, VCC, SCL, SDA (pin order varies by vendor, see 3D spec OHM-092).

### 2. What it is and how it works
Self-emitting pixels (organic LED), no backlight. Each lit pixel draws current from the panel supply, so supply current depends on how many pixels are on (all-white draws several times more than blank). The SSD1306 contains a 128x64-bit graphic RAM (GDDRAM) organised as 8 pages of 8 rows by 128 columns, a contrast control (256 levels), a charge pump that can generate the panel supply VCC (7 to 15 V in S12) from a low supply, and an I2C interface.

Supply (S12, Rev 1.1 April 2008): VDD (logic) 1.65 to 3.3 V; VCC (panel) 7 to 15 V; the extraction listed VBAT as reserved/connect to VDD, which does not agree with the usual description of VBAT as the charge-pump input and is therefore marked unresolved. The DC characteristics table (IDD, ICC, sleep currents) was not obtainable from any opened copy.

Modules add an on-board regulator and charge-pump capacitors so that the 4-pin module accepts about 3.3 to 5 V (module level, not from an opened source: ASSUMPTION).

### 3. How it connects
I2C: SDA and SCL are open-drain lines needing pull-up resistors to the logic rail (4.7 kohm is typical; the module may already carry them: per-MPN fact, unknown). Slave address (S12): 0111100 or 0111101 selected by SA0, i.e. 0x3C or 0x3D (7-bit). Most 4-pin modules fix SA0 with a solder jumper or resistor (ASSUMPTION). Control byte (S12): Co bit and D/C# bit followed by six zeros; D/C# = 0 selects command, 1 selects data; Co = 0 means the rest of the transfer is data-only. Pin order differs between vendors (GND/VCC/SCL/SDA vs VCC/GND/SCL/SDA, 3D spec OHM-092); reversed VCC/GND on the header kills the board (module has no reverse protection, ASSUMPTION). Mistakes: 5 V logic on a 3.3 V-only module without regulator (check the module); missing pull-ups; wrong address; not sending the charge-pump enable and display-on commands.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
Layers: **L1** supply and pull-ups; **L3** controller and display.
**L1.**
```
* module supply: static + pixel-proportional current (ASSUMPTION: 1 mA idle, 20 mA all-white at 3.3 V, SSD1306 DC table not obtained)
B{ref}idd {VCC} {GND} I = {iidle} + ({ion}-{iidle})*{pixel_fraction}
* I2C lines: open-drain inputs from the module side, pull-ups (module or host)
RPU_SDA {VCC} {SDA} {rpu}      ; 4.7k default
RPU_SCL {VCC} {SCL} {rpu}
CSDA {SDA} {GND} {cbus}        ; 50 pF default
```
Pull-up rise time: bench B1 (30 to 70 percent, 4.7 kohm, 50 pF): tr = 0.8473*R*C = 199.1 ns.

**L3 (what a higher-layer model must implement; S12).**
1. I2C slave at 0x3C (SA0 = 0) or 0x3D (SA0 = 1): ACK on address match; ignore other addresses; support write transactions with control bytes (Co/D/C#) and repeated data bytes; reads (status register) are rarely used.
2. GDDRAM: 128 columns x 8 pages x 8 bits; data writes fill whole 8-bit column segments; addressing modes (set memory addressing mode 0x20: horizontal, vertical, page), column address (0x21) and page address (0x22) windows, auto-increment and wrap.
3. Commands (S12 list): display off 0xAE, display on 0xAF, set contrast 0x81 (+ value), entire display on 0xA4 (follows RAM) / 0xA5 (all pixels on), normal/inverse 0xA6/0xA7, set multiplex ratio 0xA8, memory mode 0x20. Charge pump (0x8D with 0x14 to enable) and the other timing commands (0xD5, 0xD9, 0xDA, 0xDB) are widely used in initialization sequences but were not present in the opened extraction: verify against the PDF before implementing (RESEARCH_REQUIRED).
4. Reset: RES# low for at least 3 us then high; power-on sequence: VDD stable, RES# pulse, wait, VCC on, then display on (S12). On modules RES# is generated on board (ASSUMPTION).
5. Display state: after reset the display is off and RAM undefined; pixels render only after display on (0xAF) and (for module-powered panels) charge pump enable.
6. Current model (L1 bridge): supply current as a function of lit-pixel fraction and contrast; numbers must come from the MPN/panel datasheet.
7. I2C timing: S12 references the timing table (Table 13-6) but the numbers were not extracted (RESEARCH_REQUIRED); the model should enforce standard-mode and fast-mode limits from the I2C specification (not opened here).

Fidelity: L1 `behavioural_approximation` with assumed currents; L3 has no fidelity label.

| VDD (controller) | V | 3.3 | 1.65 | 3.3 | MFR_DATASHEET | S12 |
| VCC (panel) | V | 12 (or internal charge pump) | 7 | 15 | MFR_DATASHEET | S12 |
| module VCC | V | 3.3 | 3.3 | 5 | ASSUMPTION | |

### 6. Ratings and limits
`1.65 <= VDD <= 3.3` for the bare controller (flag `VDD_RANGE`); module supply limit is MPN specific (default 3.3 to 5 V, ASSUMPTION flagged); `7 <= VCC <= 15` for an external panel supply; I2C bus voltage must not exceed the module rail; pixel-fraction x ion current vs supply capability (design rule).

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior
Wrong supply polarity: board damage (flag `REVERSE_SUPPLY`). Overvoltage on the module rail beyond the regulator (flag). Logic level 5 V on SDA/SCL of a 3.3 V part: flag `I2C_OVERVOLT` (current through pull-ups into the ESD structures; permanent damage possible, ASSUMPTION). Burn-in: static high-contrast images dim the lit pixels over time (OLED aging); not modeled. Missing init: black screen (L3 state).

### 8. Thermal behavior
Negligible at about 20 to 70 mW (ASSUMPTION): all-white raises panel temperature slightly; OLED lifetime falls with brightness and temperature (qualitative).

### 9. Appearance summary
27 mm square PCB (default) with a black glass panel and a 4-pin header at the bottom edge (see OHM-092); the active area is a small rectangle on the panel.

### 10. Validation benches
Files in `/home/claude/behavior/bench/beh-oled-ssd1306/`.

| Bench | File | Expected | Tolerance | Measured |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | B1_i2c_pullup_rise.cir | tr(30 to 70 percent) = 0.8473*4.7k*50 pF = 199.1 ns | 2 percent | 199.12 ns. PASS (generic RC check; confirms the pull-up/bus-capacitance model arithmetic) |
| B2 | B2_supply_load_step.cir | 3.3 V through 1 ohm with load 1 + 19*0.5 = 10.5 mA: V = 3.3 - 0.0105 = 3.2895 V | 0.1 percent | 3.2895 V. PASS (arithmetic of the assumed load) |

Result: 2 of 2 match. Neither tests a datasheet number for the SSD1306 (DC table not available); both check the L1 model structure.

# Per-entry sections

Common note for OHM-073..081: pin map `K -> terminal 1`, `A -> terminal 2`; SPICE line `D{ref} {net_t2} {net_t1} LED_{colour}`. Package-level defaults below are the generic part; selecting an MPN replaces them with datasheet values. Parasitics (lead inductance of THT lamps, pad capacitance) are not modeled and are below the resolution of the L1 model at indicator frequencies. Default `if_max` is set conservatively to 20 mA for generic parts (the repo GENERIC_LED_GREEN record also uses 20 mA); sourced higher values are listed per entry for use when the MPN matches.

## [OHM-073] 3 mm THT LED -> BEH-LED-INDICATOR
* Package: T-1 lamp, lead pitch 2.54 mm (3D spec). Pin map: terminal 1 = cathode (-X, flat side, short lead), terminal 2 = anode (+X, long lead).
* Sourced reference part: Vishay TLDR4400 (deep red GaAlAs, 3 mm tinted diffused), S1: IF 50 mA at Tamb <= 60 C, PV 100 mW, Tj 100 C, RthJA 400 K/W, VR 6 V, IFSM 1 A (tp <= 10 us), VF 1.8 typ / 2.2 max at 20 mA, Cj 30 pF, Iv 45 mcd typ at 20 mA (25 mcd min), 2 mcd typ at 1 mA. Model card LED_RED is fitted to this part.
* Defaults: colour red, if_test 20 mA, if_max 20 mA (generic; 50 mA only for TLDR4400-class at <= 60 C), rth_ja 400 K/W, vr_max 6 V (red/GaP) or 5 V (blue/white).
* Polarity: flat on flange = cathode. Mounting the lamp backwards means reverse bias; flag against vr_max.
* Status: complete for the reference part; generic colours partial.

## [OHM-074] 5 mm THT LED -> BEH-LED-INDICATOR
* Package: T-1 3/4 lamp, pitch 2.54 mm. Pin map as OHM-073 (terminal 1 cathode, terminal 2 anode).
* Sourced reference parts (S2..S5): blue TLHB5800 (IF 20 mA at <= 65 C, PV 100 mW, RthJA 350 K/W, VR 5 V, IFSM 0.1 A, VF 3.9 typ / 4.5 max, Tj 100 C); yellow/green/pure-green TLHY/G/P5800 (IF 30 mA, VR 6 V, IFSM 1 A, RthJA 350 K/W, VF 2.4 typ / 3.0 max, Cj 50 pF); white VLHW5100 (IF 30 mA, VR 5 V, IFSM 0.1 A, RthJA 400 K/W, VF 2.8 to 3.6 V, IR <= 50 uA at 5 V, intensity 5600 to 11200 mcd, narrow +-10 degree beam); red/yellow/green TLH x 520x (IF 30 mA at <= 65 C, VF 2 to 3 V).
* Defaults: red, 20 mA. Model cards: LED_GREEN (TLHG5800 fit), LED_BLUE (TLHB5800 fit), LED_WHITE (VLHW5100 single-point fit).
* Notes: the largest evidence base in the group. Blue VF: Vishay GaN-on-SiC 3.9 V vs modern InGaN 3.1 V (S7), so the part record must pick a variant; a 3.3 V rail cannot light a 3.9 V blue.
* Status: complete for the listed reference parts.

## [OHM-075] 10 mm THT LED -> BEH-LED-INDICATOR
* Package: 10 mm lamp, pitch 2.54 mm; same pin map and polarity as OHM-073.
* No datasheet opened for a 10 mm part. Defaults are ASSUMPTION: if_max 20 mA (generic conservative; many 10 mm lamps run at the same 20 to 30 mA or use several dies, not verified), rth_ja 350 K/W (copied from 5 mm, flagged L), vr_max 5 V.
* Status: partial; ratings RESEARCH_REQUIRED per MPN.

* Package: rectangular lamp (about 5 x 2 mm), pitch 2.54 mm. Pin map: terminal 1 = cathode (-X, chamfer/flat), terminal 2 = anode (+X).
* No datasheet opened. Defaults: ASSUMPTION as OHM-075 (20 mA).
* Notes: stackable bar LEDs are often red/green dual-die variants: that is a different circuit (two dies) and is not in this entry.

* Package: 18 pins, 2.54 pitch, pins 1-9 down the -X row, 10-18 up the +X row (3D spec).

Pin-count arithmetic: 18 pins = 2 digits x (8 segment pins + 1 common) would mean each digit has its own segment pins (non-multiplexed); a multiplexed dual would need only 10 pins, so 18 pins suggests separate segment pins per digit (DERIVED, L; not verified). Bind from the MPN datasheet.
* Electrical: same per-segment limits as OHM-087 for the red 0.56 in class (S14).
* Status: research_required for pin map and wiring; class model applies.

## [OHM-089] Four-digit 7-segment display -> BEH-DISP-LEDARRAY
* Package: 12 pins, 2.54 pitch, pins 1-6 down the -X row, 7-12 up the +X row (3D spec).
* Pin map: NOT in the opened documents. 12 pins = 8 segment lines + 4 digit commons, i.e. a multiplexed display (DERIVED from pin count). Conventional 0.56 in four-digit layout, UNVERIFIED (ASSUMPTION, L): 1 = E, 2 = D, 3 = DP, 4 = C, 5 = G, 6 = digit 4, 7 = B, 8 = digit 3, 9 = digit 2, 10 = F, 11 = A, 12 = digit 1. Common type per MPN.

* Package: 16 pins (2 rows of 8, 2.54 pitch), pins 1-8 down the -X row, 9-16 up the +X row (3D spec; placeholder dimensions, status partial there as well). 16 pins = 8 row lines + 8 column lines (DERIVED).

* Defaults: VDD 5 V, IDD 1.2 mA, VLCD 4.0 V, 4-bit mode on DB4..DB7, backlight assumed 4.1 V at 100 mA (ASSUMPTION; replace per MPN).

Pin map is therefore per MPN; default GND, VCC, SCL, SDA (ASSUMPTION, most common; verify silkscreen).

# Group-level findings

* Pin/polarity conflicts: (1) the repo GENERIC_LED_GREEN record has pin 1 = anode while the 3D spec has terminal 1 = cathode for every two-lead LED; bind by role. (2) OHM-082 has two different pin function maps (Broadcom 2 = B, 3 = G, 4 = R; RND 2 = R, 3 = G, 4 = B); there is no universal PLCC-4 RGB map. (3) OHM-083 pin map unknown. (4) OHM-092 module pin order varies (VCC/GND swap). (5) OHM-085: Cree datasheet marks the anode with "+"; the 3D spec uses the KiCad convention with pad 1 = cathode; consistent in function but check silkscreen.
* Datasheet conflicts kept: red 3 mm VF typ 1.8 V (table) vs about 2.0 V at 20 mA (chart); blue VF typ 3.9 V (GaN on SiC) vs 3.1 V (InGaN); blue 1 mA chart point (3.0 V) inconsistent with a physical diode fit; ST7066 vs HD44780U bus timing (400 vs 500 ns cycle, 40 vs 80 ns data setup); WS2812B VDD printed as 3.5 to 5.3 V in maximum ratings but 4.5 to 5.5 V in the electrical table; LCD module IDD 1.0 to 1.5 mA vs controller 0.3 to 0.6 mA; 0603 height 0.55 mm (3D spec) vs 0.8 mm (Vishay VLM x 1300).
* Layer decisions: LED parts are L1; LED arrays L1 with L2 drive patterns; WS2812B has L1 supply, L2 thresholds, L3 protocol; LCD1602 and OLED are L3 with L1 supply, backlight and pull-ups. L3 requirements are listed in each class.
* Honesty notes: no vendor SPICE models were opened; every deck is `behavioural_approximation`. All datasheets were read through an extraction tool; graph readings are LOW confidence. Not opened or not available: SSD1306 DC table, I2C timing, 7-segment and matrix pin maps, 5050 passive RGB pin map, 10 mm, rectangular, 0402, 0805, 1206 and PLCC-2 datasheets, backlight data of the 1602 module.
* Benches: 17 netlists run in ngspice 42 under `/home/claude/behavior/bench/beh-led-indicator`, `beh-led-mux`, `beh-led-power`, `beh-led-ws2812`, `beh-lcd1602`, `beh-oled-ssd1306` with `results.txt` files. All matched their analytical expectation within the stated tolerance. Scope limits are stated per bench (several verify model arithmetic with assumed parameters, not a datasheet number).

# GROUP R6: Transistor and power packages (BJT, MOSFET, linear regulator) (OHM-093 to OHM-102)

Author: research agent R6. ngspice 42 run locally; every bench file is under `/home/claude/behavior/bench/<class>/`, with the raw results of the last full run in `results_ngspice42.txt` in each class directory.

## 0. Reading guide

These ten entries are PACKAGES, not parts. A package has no electrical behavior by itself. What a user places on the board is "a TO-220", and the behavior is whatever functional device the part binding puts in it. This file therefore defines four behavior classes and then, per entry, a binding table that says which reference parts live in the package, how their pins map to the package terminals (the order differs between parts in the same package), and what the package contributes (thermal resistance, tab connection, parasitics, power rating).

| Class | What it models | Entries it applies to |
|---|---|---|
| BEH-TRN-BJT | NPN/PNP bipolar transistors (Gummel-Poon, `Q` device) | 093, 094, 095, 096, 097 (and TO-220 power BJTs, not researched) |
| BEH-TRN-MOSFET | N-channel enhancement MOSFETs (level 1 / level 3 core plus behavioural dynamic parts) | 093, 094, 098, 099, 100, 101, 102 (096 and 095 possible, not researched) |
| BEH-REG-LINEAR | Three-terminal linear regulators (behavioural subcircuit) | 093, 094, 095, 096, 098, 100, 101 |
| BEH-PWR-PKGTHERMAL | Package thermal resistance, derating and the power-rating check shared by the three classes above | all ten |

Layer: all four classes are L1 (analog, ngspice primitives, B sources). Nothing here needs L2 or L3 and nothing needs XSPICE. Everything below ran on the stock ngspice 42 build found on this machine.

### Honesty notes that apply to the whole file

1. The page-fetch tool used for datasheets returns a model-written extract of each PDF, not the raw PDF. Tables of numbers (limits, thermal resistance, hFE bands, pinouts) are usually reliable and several were cross-checked against each other (see BEH-PWR-PKGTHERMAL bench B2, where 12 of 15 datasheet power ratings are reproduced by `(Tjmax-25)/Rth` to better than 1.5 %, the other three are listed as conflicts). Test conditions, typical (not min/max) columns, curves, SOA charts and revision dates are often missing from the extracts. Where the extract looked self-inconsistent it is flagged below as a suspected extraction error and not silently used. Revision/date strings are quoted as the extract reported them; some Infineon documents were reported with 2026 revision stamps that I cannot confirm.
2. No vendor SPICE model was opened or attached. Every model in this file is `behavioural_approximation` (a fit to datasheet numbers or a behavioural subcircuit). Nothing here may be labelled `vendor_model`. The existing runner (`src/ohmni/eda/simulation.py`) labels any deck that contains `.model`/`.subckt` as `behavioural_approximation` and any other deck as `ideal_components`; a bare `Q`/`M` with no model card would be `ideal_components` in that vocabulary and would not even simulate usefully, so every binding in this file ships a model card or subcircuit.
3. The runner only parses `.op` node tables. All DC models below converge in `.op`. The regulator subcircuit needs a `.nodeset v(vout)=VNOM` in the deck (without it ngspice 42 `.op` landed on a spurious state, e.g. Vout = 0.18 V with the pass element at its current limit). The runner does not add nodesets today, so whoever wires this in must emit one per regulator instance.
4. ngspice 42 gotchas found by running (they matter for the implementer):
   - The first line of a netlist is the title; a `.model` card placed first is silently ignored.
   - `ac lin 1 f f` works for a single frequency; `ac dec 10 f f` (start = stop) produces zero rows.
   - The level-1/3 MOS model has its own bulk-junction diodes with default `IS = 1e-14`. With bulk tied to source they act as a second, parasitic body diode and clamp the body-diode drop at about 0.95 V at 25 A. Every MOSFET model card below sets `IS=0`.
   - A charge-based capacitor `Cx n1 n2 q='expr'` takes q as a function of `v(n1)-v(n2)`. A sign slip makes a negative capacitance and a blow-up (seen, 1e33 A), and a `B` source with `ddt()` oscillated in the Miller transition; the charge form with correct sign converged.
   - `meas ... integ` needs a vector that exists in the current plot; boolean-masked `let` vectors were not found, `(x-abs(x))/2` was.
   - Control-language vectors from `op` are lost after a following `ac`/`tran`; store scalars with `set` if they are needed later, or compute within the same plot.
   - `alter` followed by a second `op` can start from the previous state and fail or pick another solution for the bistable regulator deck; use `dc` sweeps or separate decks.
5. The brief asks for pin maps "per package, tab = drain or output". The surprise of this group is how little is fixed by the package: the same TO-220 is G-D-S with tab = drain (IRFZ44N), IN-GND-OUT with tab = GND (L7805) or ADJ-OUT-IN with tab = OUT (LM317). Only one structural fact held across everything opened: in the 3-lead power packages (SOT-89, SOT-223, TO-126, TO-220, DPAK, D2PAK) the tab is electrically the middle terminal (pin 2), which agrees with the 3D spec's "pin 2 tied to tab". What the tab IS (collector, drain, output, ground) depends on the part.

## 1. BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-TRN-BJT

Applies to: OHM-093 (TO-92), OHM-094 (SOT-23), OHM-095 (SOT-89), OHM-096 (SOT-223), OHM-097 (TO-126), OHM-098 (TO-220, power BJT variants, not researched). Reference parts with datasheets actually opened: 2N3904 (S1), PN2222A (S2), BC546/547/548 (S3), BC817 series (S4), BCP56 series (S5), BCX56 series (S6), BD135/137/139 (S7).

### 1.1 Purpose and real-world use
A bipolar junction transistor (BJT) is a current-controlled current source: a small base current controls a collector current about hFE times larger. On boards it is used as (a) a switch driving LEDs, relays, buzzers and level shifters from logic pins (saturated, forced beta about 10 or less), (b) a small-signal amplifier (common emitter, emitter follower), (c) a current source or mirror, (d) the pass element in discrete linear regulators, (e) a driver for power MOSFET gates. Typical values: general-purpose 40-60 V, 100-800 mA parts in TO-92/SOT-23 (2N3904, 2N2222/PN2222A, BC547, BC817); medium-power 1-1.5 A parts in SOT-223/SOT-89/TO-126 (BCP56, BCX56, BD139).

### 1.2 What it is and how it works
Construction: two back-to-back junctions in an NPN (or PNP) sandwich. In the forward-active region the base-emitter junction is forward biased and the base-collector junction reverse biased; emitter electrons diffuse across the thin base and are swept into the collector.

Key equations (textbook Ebers-Moll/Gummel-Poon, as implemented in the ngspice `Q` model, S31):
- Forward active: Ic = IS (exp(Vbe/(NF Vt)) - 1)(1 + Vce/VAF), Ib = Ic/BF + ISE (exp(Vbe/(NE Vt)) - 1). Vt = kT/q = 25.865 mV at the ngspice default of 27 C.
- hFE = Ic/Ib is not constant: it rises with Ic while the ISE (recombination) current fades, peaks, then falls at high injection (IKF knee) and with series resistances. Datasheets give bands (S1: 2N3904 hFE at Vce = 1 V: 40-300 at 0.1 mA, 70-300 at 1 mA, 100-300 at 10 mA, 60-300 at 50 mA, 30-300 at 100 mA).
- Early effect: output conductance 1/ro = Ic/(VAF + Vce).
- gm = Ic/Vt; small-signal emitter resistance re = Vt/Ic.
- Regions: cutoff (both junctions off), forward active, saturation (both forward biased, Vce(sat) 0.06-0.3 V, charge storage makes turn-off slow), reverse active (poor gain, BR).
- Vbe temperature coefficient about -1.8 mV/K at constant Ic; Ic at constant Vbe roughly doubles every 8-10 K. With a stiff base voltage, power dissipation therefore feeds back on itself (thermal runaway, below). An emitter resistor gives negative feedback.
- Second breakdown (S30): at high Vce a local current crowding makes the usable power fall faster than the thermal limit; forward-biased SOA is derated with temperature, reverse-biased SOA is not. The practical rule in S30: if the maximum bus voltage is below 0.75 VCEO(sus), second-breakdown stress is normally acceptable. Neither the 2N3904 nor 2N2222A extract contained an SOA chart.

### 1.3 How it connects
Three terminals. Pin function is determined by the part, not the package (section 1.10 and the per-entry sections):
- 2N3904 and PN2222A in TO-92: pin 1 emitter, pin 2 base, pin 3 collector (E-B-C) (S1, S2).
- BC546/547/548 in TO-92: pin 1 collector, pin 2 base, pin 3 emitter (C-B-E) (S3). The reverse order of the 2N3904 in the same package.
- BC817 in SOT-23: pin 1 B, pin 2 E, pin 3 C (S4).
- BCP56 in SOT-223: pin 1 B, pin 2 C, pin 3 E, pin 4 (tab) C (S5).
- BCX56 in SOT-89: pin 1 E, pin 2 C (tab), pin 3 B (S6). Different order from BC817 and BCP56.
- BD135/139 in SOT-32/TO-126: pin 1 E, pin 2 C, pin 3 B; the mounting plate is the collector (S7).
Typical circuits: low-side switch (emitter to ground, load in the collector, base resistor from the logic pin; choose Rb so that Ib is Ic/10 for hard saturation), emitter follower (collector to supply), common-emitter amplifier with divider bias and emitter degeneration.
Common mistakes: rotating a TO-92 by 180 degrees (EBC vs CBE parts), no base resistor, forgetting that the BE junction breaks down at only 5-6 V reverse (VEBO 6 V for 2N3904/PN2222A, 5 V for BC817), switching inductive loads with no flyback diode, driving 3.3 V logic through a base resistor chosen for 5 V, and putting a small-signal part on a power load.

### 1.4 Electrical model for simulation
Layer L1. Primitive: `Q` with a Gummel-Poon `.model`. Fidelity label: `behavioural_approximation` (fit to datasheet numbers; NOT a vendor model).

Netlist template (device name and node order follow ngspice: collector, base, emitter):
```
.include models_bjt_r6fit.lib        * Q2N3904_R6FIT, Q2N2222A_R6FIT
Q{ref} {C} {B} {E} Q2N3904_R6FIT [area] [temp={Tj}]
```
Library: `/home/claude/behavior/bench/trn_bjt/models_bjt_r6fit.lib`. Model cards (fitted, not vendor):
```
.model Q2N3904_R6FIT NPN(IS=1.4693e-14 BF=325.03 NF=1 VAF=100 IKF=0.061592 ISE=2.5511e-14 NE=1.331 BR=4 NR=1 RB=12.769 RE=1.1905 RC=1 CJE=9.4e-12 VJE=0.75 MJE=0.33 CJC=6.7e-12 VJC=0.75 MJC=0.33 TF=4.775e-10 XTF=2 ITF=0.4 VTF=4 TR=5e-08 XTB=1.5 EG=1.11 XTI=3)
.model Q2N2222A_R6FIT NPN(IS=3.2019e-14 BF=558.78 NF=1 VAF=100 IKF=0.21803 ISE=2.7068e-14 NE=1.2366 BR=4 NR=1 RB=6.6976 RE=0.097874 RC=0.56613 CJE=29e-12 VJE=0.75 MJE=0.33 CJC=17e-12 VJC=0.75 MJC=0.33 TF=4.608e-10 XTF=2 ITF=0.5 VTF=4 TR=6e-8 XTB=1.5 EG=1.11 XTI=3)
```

How the fit was done (so it can be redone, script names `tmp_R6_bjt_fit.py`, `tmp_R6_fit_run.py` in /home/claude/behavior):
1. Free parameters IS, BF, ISE, NE (clipped 1.2-2.0), IKF, RB, RE, RC, fitted by non-linear least squares (scipy `least_squares`) using ngspice DC runs.
2. Targets for hFE: the datasheet gives only min and max bands. The target typical value was set to the geometric mean of the band (2N3904: 108, 150, 173, 131, 96 at 0.1, 1, 10, 50, 100 mA). For PN2222A, where only minimums are given below 150 mA, the target was 2x the minimum (basis ASSUMPTION). This is a guess of the typical curve, not a datasheet value.
3. Vce(sat) targets were half of the datasheet maximum (typical not captured); Vbe(sat) targets were the band midpoints.
4. Capacitances: CJC and CJE chosen so that Cjc at the test Vcb and Cje at 0.5 V reverse approach the datasheet Cobo/Cibo maxima (2N3904: Cobo 4 pF, Cibo 8 pF; PN2222A 8 pF, 25 pF).
5. TF tuned until the simulated unity-current-gain frequency was 305 MHz (datasheet fT 300 MHz at Ic = 10 mA for the 2N3904; for PN2222A the 300 MHz number was taken at about 25 mA, conditions not in the extract, ASSUMPTION). TR tuned so that the simulated storage time stays under the datasheet limit (2N3904 ts < 200 ns; PN2222A ts < 225 ns) with an ASSUMED drive circuit.
6. Not in the datasheets opened and therefore assumptions: VAF = 100 V, BR = 4, NF = NR = 1, XTB = 1.5, EG = 1.11, XTI = 3, VJE = VJC = 0.75, MJE = MJC = 0.33, XTF, ITF, VTF.

Fit result (measured, benches B3, B3b, B4, B7; limits are the datasheet values from S1, S2):

| Quantity | Datasheet | Model |
|---|---|---|
| 2N3904 hFE at 0.1 mA | 40-300 | 107.7 |
| at 1 mA | 70-300 | 150.1 |
| at 10 mA | 100-300 | 173.0 |
| at 50 mA | 60-300 | 131.0 |
| at 100 mA | 30-300 | 96.3 |
| 2N3904 Vce(sat) 10 mA/1 mA | <= 0.2 V | 0.063 V |

Ideal vs realistic mode:
- Ideal mode: `IS`, `BF` only (`.model Q NPN(IS=1e-14 BF=hFE_typ)`), no parasitics. Fidelity label stays `behavioural_approximation` because a model card is present; the label `ideal_components` is for decks with no model card at all.
- Realistic mode: the fitted cards above (hFE roll-off, saturation, junction capacitance, charge storage, temperature).
- hFE spread (tolerance): corner rule, verified in bench B3c: scale BF by k and ISE by 1/k. With k = 0.58 the 2N3904 reads 100.4 at 10 mA (datasheet minimum 100), with k = 1.73 it reads 299.4 (datasheet maximum 300); all ten corner points stay inside the datasheet bands.
- Self-heating: ngspice 42 has no self-heating on `Q`. Pass `temp=Tj` on the instance and close the loop outside the solver (iteration as in bench B8) or with the thermal network of BEH-PWR-PKGTHERMAL.
- Pass-through of tolerance: `area` multiplies IS, ISE, IKF and divides RB/RE/RC (use for parallel devices).

Valid analyses: op, dc, ac, tran, noise (thermal and shot noise only, no KF/AF fitted), temp. Valid range: Ic from 10 uA to the datasheet maximum, Vce up to Vceo, Tj -55 to 150 C. Known limitations (measured or by construction):
- The hFE curve is inside the datasheet band by construction but its exact shape is a guess; the typical curve was not in the extract. Do not use it to claim accurate gain at a bias point.
- No breakdown model: BVCEO/BVEBO are not in the model; the simulator must evaluate the rating checks in section 1.6.
- No SOA, no second breakdown, no thermal runaway inside the solver.
- VAF = 100 V is an assumption (bench B5: ro measured 63.5 kohm vs 63.9 kohm expected from the assumed VAF; the check is of the model against itself).
- Quasi-saturation and the real Vce(sat) at forced beta other than the datasheet's are not fitted.
- PNP models were not fitted (no PNP datasheet opened).

### 1.6 Ratings and limits and the check expressions
For every placed BJT the simulator should evaluate (all values from the binding's record):
- `vce_ok: |Vce| <= VCEO` (2N3904 40 V, PN2222A 40 V, BC547 45 V, BC817 45 V, BCP56/BCX56/BD139 80 V). Source S1-S7.
- `vbe_rev_ok: -Vbe <= VEBO` (6 V for 2N3904/PN2222A, 5 V BC817). BE-junction reverse breakdown is the usual casualty of a bipolar used as a bidirectional switch.
- `ic_ok: |Ic| <= IC_max` (continuous), and pulse `|Ic| <= ICM` for tp <= 1 ms where given (BC817 1 A, BCP56/BCX56 2 A).
- `power_ok: P = Vce*Ic + Vbe*Ib <= PD(Ta)`, with `PD(Ta) = (Tjmax - Ta)/RthJA` for the board condition. This formula reproduces the datasheet powers: 2N3904 125/200 = 0.625 W, BC817 125/500 = 0.25 W and 125/362 = 0.345 W, BCP56 125/93 = 1.344 W (datasheet 1.35), BD139 125/10 = 12.5 W at Tc = 25 C (bench B2 of BEH-PWR-PKGTHERMAL).
- `tj_ok: Tj = Ta + RthJA*P <= Tjmax` (150 C for all parts above; 175 C is not a BJT number here).
- Derating: 5 mW/K above 25 C for the TO-92 parts of S1-S3 (equals 1/RthJA = 1/200).
- Forward-bias SOA: not available for the small-signal parts (no chart in the extracts); for power BJTs use the second-breakdown rule `Vce <= 0.75 * VCEO` as a flag threshold (S30), basis ASSUMPTION for parts with no SOA chart opened (low confidence).

### 1.7 Failure and misuse behavior
| Trigger | Physical effect | Simulator response | Permanence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vce above VCEO | collector-emitter avalanche; with enough current, hot spots | flag `VCEO_EXCEEDED`; model keeps conducting; no clamp (the model has no breakdown) | recoverable if current limited, otherwise destructive |
| Vbe reverse above VEBO | BE junction avalanche; hFE degrades with repeated stress | flag `VEBO_EXCEEDED`; degrade: lower BF by the user-set factor on repeated violations (policy, not a datasheet fact) | gradual degradation |
| Ic above rating | bond wire and metallisation limit; hFE falls; Vce(sat) rises | flag; no model change | permanent if long |
| P above PD(Ta) or Tj above 150 C | thermal overstress, plus thermal runaway when the base is voltage driven | flag `TJ_EXCEEDED`; at Tj > 150 C mark part failed and replace by a short C-E (typical failure is a C-E short) or open (bond wire fuse): choose short for power parts, open for small-signal parts, flagged as ASSUMPTION | permanent |
| Second breakdown (high Vce and Ic with the junction at constant voltage) | current crowding, local melt, C-E short | flag only when SOA data are available; otherwise the `0.75 VCEO` rule above | permanent |
| Reverse supply (collector more negative than emitter) | reverse-active region, BR = 4 | model conducts with low gain; flag if Vcb < -VEBO of the collector junction (no number opened) | recoverable |
| ESD | junction damage, leakage rises | not simulated; document only | permanent |
| Base open or collector open | cutoff or no current | model handles | n/a |
Bench B8 shows the thermal-runaway criterion: with a stiff Vbe = 0.84 V the junction temperature iteration diverges (Tj hits the 300 C clamp in 25 iterations) because the loop gain G = Rth * Vce * dIc/dT = 200 * 5 * 0.056 * 0.045 = 2.5 > 1; with a 2 ohm emitter resistor it converges at 92 C.

### 1.8 Thermal behavior
Self-heating Tj = Ta + Rth*P. Use RthJA from the binding (BEH-PWR-PKGTHERMAL). Thermal runaway criterion for a constant-Vbe drive: loop gain G = Rth * Vce * Ic * alpha, alpha = (Eg - Vbe)/(Vt T) + XTI/T per kelvin, must be below 1 (bench B8). Ballast resistor lowers G by about 1/(1 + gm Re).

### 1.9 Appearance summary
See 3D spec entries OHM-093 (TO-92: black D-shaped body with a flat marked face, three tin leads), OHM-094 (SOT-23: three gull-wing leads, two on one side), OHM-095 (SOT-89: flat body with three leads and a wide centre tab), OHM-096 (SOT-223: wide tab plus three leads) and OHM-097 (TO-126: plastic slab with metal back plate and mounting hole). The package alone says nothing about what the part is: the marking code identifies the type.

## 2. BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-TRN-MOSFET

Applies to: N-channel enhancement MOSFETs in OHM-093 (TO-92: 2N7000), OHM-094 (SOT-23: 2N7002), OHM-098 (TO-220: IRFZ44N, IRF540N, IRLB8721), OHM-099 (TO-247: IRFP260N), OHM-100 (DPAK: IRLR8721, IRLR3410), OHM-101 (D2PAK: same silicon families, no D2PAK MOSFET datasheet opened), OHM-102 (PowerPAK SO-8: Si7898DP). P-channel and depletion devices are not covered (nothing opened).

### 2.1 Purpose and real-world use
A power MOSFET is a voltage-controlled switch (or variable resistor). On boards: low-side and high-side load switches, motor and solenoid drivers, synchronous buck rectifiers, battery protection, reverse-polarity protection, hot-swap and inrush limiters, linear pass elements (rare, dangerous, see SOA), logic-level shifters (2N7000/2N7002/BSS138 class). Typical series: 2N7000/2N7002 (60 V, a few ohms, 200-300 mA), IRLB8721 (30 V logic level, 8.7 mohm), IRFZ44N (55 V, 17.5 mohm), IRF540N (100 V, 44 mohm), IRFP260N (200 V, 40 mohm), Si7898DP (150 V, 85 mohm).

### 2.2 What it is and how it works
Vertical DMOS (power) or lateral small-signal MOSFET: a gate electrode over a thin oxide inverts a channel between source and drain when Vgs exceeds the threshold Vgs(th). Body diode: the source-body short and the drift region form a parasitic P-N diode from source to drain (anode = source for N-channel).
Level-1 (Shichman-Hodges, S31): saturation Id = (KP/2)(Vgs - VTO)^2 (1 + LAMBDA Vds); triode Id = KP [(Vgs - VTO) Vds - Vds^2/2]. On-resistance in triode at small Vds: Rds(on) ~ R0 + 1/(KP (Vgs - VTO)) where R0 = RD + RS (bond wires, drift region).
Level-3 (semi-empirical, S31) adds mobility degradation THETA: the effective KP falls as KP/(1 + THETA (Vgs - Vth)), which is what lets a model reproduce a flat Rds(on) vs Vgs. Bench B2 shows the consequence for IRLB8721: level 1 cannot reproduce both datasheet points (8.7 mohm at 10 V and 16 mohm at 4.5 V) with a plausible VTO; the level-1 card gives 25.0 mohm at 4.5 V (56 % high), the level-3 card gives 16.0 mohm.
Real power-MOSFET features not in a level-1/3 core:
- Vgs(th) spread: datasheet min/max (2.0-4.0 V for IRFZ44N/IRF540N/IRFP260N and Si7898DP, 1.35-2.35 V for IRLB8721/IRLR8721, 0.8-3.0 V for 2N7000, 1.0-2.5 V for 2N7002). The spread is part to part, not a tolerance on a nominal. Bench B9: the same 2N7000 card with Vto 0.8 V gives 47.2 mA and with Vto 3.0 V only 7.7 mA from 3.3 V logic into a 100 ohm load at 5 V (ratio 6.1).
- Rds(on) temperature coefficient positive; level-1 scales KP with (T/Tnom)^-1.5, bench B7: 17.5 mohm at 27 C becomes 27.3 mohm at 150 C (ratio 1.56) as the analytic estimate predicts. The real datasheet Rds-vs-Tj curve was not captured, so the ratio is an assumption-level check (typical power MOSFETs are 1.6 to 2.0 at 150 C, general practice, not sourced).
- Vgs(th) tempco negative; at low Vgs and high Vds this makes Id rise with temperature (thermal instability, S28 and S29). The level-1 card does not model this.
- Gate charge and capacitances Ciss, Coss, Crss: voltage dependent. Crss (Cgd) is strongly nonlinear: tens of pF at high Vds, several nF when Vds is near zero. This is the Miller plateau. A model with constant capacitors gets the switching losses wrong by a large factor (bench B3).
- Body diode: forward drop VSD (1.0-1.3 V at rated current for the parts opened), reverse recovery Qrr, trr.
- Avalanche: single-pulse EAS (IRFZ44N 530 mJ, IAR 25 A), repetitive EAR.
- Gate oxide: Vgs max +/-20 V for all power parts opened (30 V for the 2N7002, 20 V for 2N7000). Exceeding it ruptures the oxide permanently (short G-S or G-D).
- Safe operating area: thermal limit P = (Tjmax - Tmb)/Zth(t) at high Vds and short pulse; below that the Spirito (hot-spot) region where the allowed current collapses (S28: for Vds = 20 V the allowed current falls from a theoretical 60 A to about 15 A; DC operation is unstable at any voltage in the Spirito region; the inflexion point sits near 5 V for 1 ms and 3 V for 10 ms in the example in S28).

### 2.3 How it connects
Three electrical terminals G, D, S (plus the tab = D in most power packages). N-channel low-side switch: S to ground, D to load, G driven from logic with a series resistor 10-100 ohm and a pulldown 10-100 k. Logic-level parts (IRLB8721, IRLR8721, 2N7002) can be driven from 5 V (and the best of them from 3.3 V), standard parts (IRFZ44N, IRF540N, IRFP260N, Si7898DP) need 8-10 V drive (the datasheet Rds(on) is quoted at Vgs = 10 V). Pin order per package/part is in section 2.10.
Common mistakes: using a standard-threshold MOSFET with 3.3 V logic (bench B9: the part may not turn on), leaving the gate floating, driving the gate from a high impedance so that the Miller cap turns the device on or slows switching, ignoring the body diode in half-bridges and reverse-polarity protection, exceeding Vgs 20 V (for example 24 V drive), inductive turn-off without clamp (avalanche), and operating in the linear region at high Vds (SOA).

### 2.4 Electrical model for simulation
Layer L1. Fidelity label: `behavioural_approximation` (fitted card plus behavioural dynamic elements, NOT a vendor model).
Library: `/home/claude/behavior/bench/trn_mosfet/models_mosfet_r6fit.lib`, subcircuits `IRFZ44N_R6`, `IRF540N_R6`, `IRLB8721_R6`, `IRFP260N_R6`, `SI7898DP_R6`, `2N7000_R6`, `2N7002_R6`, pins `d g s`, parameter `BVDSS`. Generator script `tmp_R6_mos_fit.py` and `tmp_R6_mos_lib.py` in /home/claude/behavior (fits the card from the datasheet numbers, then writes the library).
Netlist template:
```
.include models_mosfet_r6fit.lib
X{ref} {D} {G} {S} IRFZ44N_R6 BVDSS=55
```
Subcircuit contents (what each element stands for):
- `Rg` gate resistance (3 ohm TO-220/TO-247 parts, 1.5-2 ohm others, 10 ohm small signal): ASSUMPTION, not in extracts.
- `M1` core MOSFET (level 1 for single Rds(on) point devices; level 3 with THETA for devices with two Rds(on) points), `IS=0` to disable the parasitic bulk diodes, `RD = RS = R0/2` with R0 = 3 mohm (TO-220/TO-247 class), 1.5 mohm (IRLB8721), 5 mohm (Si7898DP), 50 mohm (small signal): ASSUMPTION.
- `Cgs` = Ciss - Crss (constant) at the datasheet test point (assumed Vds = 25 V).
- `Cgd` nonlinear charge capacitor, Cgd = Cmin + (Cmax - Cmin)/(1 + exp(-Vgd/0.9)): Cmin = Crss, Cmax sized so that the gate charge across the Miller plateau equals the datasheet Qgd (only IRFZ44N has Qgd in the extract; other parts use a constant Cgd = Crss; IRFP260N and Si7898DP have no Crss/Coss and carry only a lumped Cgs).
- `Dbody` body diode (anode s, cathode d): N = 1.2 and RS assumed, IS solved from the datasheet VSD at the datasheet current, `CJO` from Coss - Crss at 25 V with M = 0.5, VJ = 0.8 (abrupt-junction assumption), `BV = BVDSS` so that unclamped inductive turn-off is limited to the rated voltage (the model clamps but is never destroyed), `TT` only for IRFZ44N (14 ns, tuned in bench B6).
Fit method (closed form then refined with ngspice):
1. VTO = midpoint of the datasheet Vgs(th) min/max (IRFZ44N 3.0 V, IRLB8721 1.85 V, 2N7000 1.9 V, ...): the typical threshold was not in the extracts, so this is a DERIVED guess (confidence L).
2. KP (level 1) from the datasheet MAXIMUM Rds(on): KP = 1/((Rds - R0)(Vgs - VTO)), then refined by least squares against ngspice `.op` (Id forced, Vds measured). The model is therefore a worst-case Rds(on) card, not a typical one. Multiply KP by about 1.2-1.3 (typ/max ratio, not in the extracts) if typical behavior is wanted: ASSUMPTION.
3. Two-point devices (IRLB8721: 8.7 mohm at 10 V, 16 mohm at 4.5 V; Si7898DP 85/95 mohm at 10/6 V; 2N7000 5/6 ohm at 10/4.5 V; 2N7002 5.0/5.3 ohm) use level 3 with THETA solved with KP from the two points.
Fitted values (measured by the fit script; `check` equals the datasheet value to 4 digits):

| Device | Level | VTO V | KP A/V^2 | THETA 1/V | Rds(on) points used (max) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| IRFZ44N | 1 | 3.0 | 10.17 | | 17.5 mohm at 10 V, 25 A |
| IRF540N | 1 | 3.0 | 3.669 | | 44 mohm at 10 V, 16 A |
| IRLB8721 | 3 | 1.85 | 37.23 | 0.1434 | 8.7 mohm at 10 V, 16 mohm at 4.5 V |
| IRFP260N | 1 | 3.0 | 4.197 | | 40 mohm at 10 V, 28 A |
| Si7898DP | 3 | 3.0 | 25.34 | 1.844 | 85 mohm at 10 V, 95 mohm at 6 V |
| 2N7000 | 3 | 1.9 | 0.2096 | 0.7551 | 5 ohm at 10 V, 6 ohm at 4.5 V |
| 2N7002 | 3 | 1.75 | 0.3633 | 1.407 | 5 ohm at 10 V, 5.3 ohm at 4.5 V (maxima; typ 2.8/3.8 ohm) |
Note that THETA = 1.84 for the Si7898DP exists only because the two datasheet points (10 V and 6 V) are nearly equal; below 6 V the card is unfitted and will overstate conduction.
What the fits reproduce and what they do not (benches B1-B9, all measured):
- Rds(on) at the datasheet points: exact by construction (B2: 8.700 and 16.000 mohm for the level-3 IRLB8721 card). At other currents the level-1 triode term moves it by a few percent (B1: Vds = 0.1020 V at 5.95 A, 2.0 % below the 17.5 mohm hand value).
- Transconductance: IRFZ44N gfs at Id = 25 A, Vds = 25 V is 21.8 S against the datasheet 19 S (+15 %); level-1 has no mobility roll-off at the datasheet point (B4).
- Gate charge (B3): Qgd = 23.2 nC against 23 nC (fitted), but total Qg(10 V) = 48.8 nC against the datasheet 63 nC (-23 %) because Cgs is a constant Ciss - Crss. With constant Cgd = Crss = 88 pF the Miller charge is 4.8 nC (about 5 times too small) and Qg 14.6 nC.
- Body diode (B5, B6): VSD at 25 A = 1.300 V (by construction, B5). Reverse-recovery charge integrated over 0.4-0.8 us is 165 nC against the datasheet 170 nC after tuning TT = 14 ns; with TT = 0 the same integral is 115 nC (junction-capacitance ringing). The reverse peak current is 2.2 A against the roughly 5.4 A implied by trr = 63 ns and Qrr = 170 nC: the recovery shape is wrong even though the integral is tuned.
- Avalanche (B8): the clamp holds Vds at BVDSS; E_av integral = 0.239 J against the analytic 0.5 L I^2 BV/(BV - Vdd) = 0.240 J with I = 24.7 A. The device is not destroyed in the simulation; the simulator must compare E_av with EAS.
- Vendor subcircuits: manufacturers publish level-1-core subcircuits with nonlinear Cgd, Rds(on)-vs-temperature and Vth tempco tweaks, thermal ports and sometimes avalanche. None was opened here. The cards above are what a datasheet-only flow can produce.
Ideal vs realistic mode:
- Ideal: one `M` with a level-1 card from Rds(on) only (no capacitances, no body diode, `IS=0` would also remove the diode: add an explicit `D` if it is wanted).
- Realistic: the subcircuit above.
Valid analyses: op, dc, tran, ac (small-signal capacitances are the linearisation of the charge capacitor), temp (Rds(on) and KP only). Not modelled: Vth tempco, hot-spot instability, avalanche energy limit, gate-oxide breakdown, quasi-saturation, Rds(on) vs drain current in saturation edge effects.
Convergence notes: charge-capacitor `Cgd` form converged in all benches (op, dc, tran); the `B`-source `ddt()` form did not and should not be used.

### 2.6 Ratings and limits and the check expressions
- `vds_ok: Vds <= VDS(max)` (55, 100, 30, 200, 150, 60 V per part); avalanche exception below.
- `vgs_ok: abs(Vgs) <= VGS(max)`: 20 V for every power part opened and the 2N7000, 30 V for the 2N7002. This is a hard check; the model has no gate clamp.
- `id_ok: Id <= ID(Tc)` with `ID(Tc) = sqrt((Tjmax - Tc)/(Rth * Rds(on,Tj)))` limited by the package and by IDM for pulses. Datasheet currents are the lower of the silicon and package limits.
- `power_ok: Vds*Id <= (Tjmax - Tref)/Rth` with the Rth that matches the mounting (RthJC with a heat sink, RthJA free air, DPAK 1 in2 copper 50 K/W vs minimum footprint 110 K/W). Bench B2 of BEH-PWR-PKGTHERMAL: IRF540N 150/1.15 = 130 W (datasheet 130 W), IRLB8721 65.2 W (65 W), IRFP260N 300 W (300 W), IRLR3410 78.9 W (79 W).
- `avalanche_ok: E_av <= EAS(Tj)` where `E_av = integral(Vds*Id dt)` during the clamp (bench B8 gives 0.239 J for 0.5 mH at 24.7 A), and `Iav <= IAR`. EAS is specified at 25 C start; derate roughly linearly to zero at Tjmax (general practice, ASSUMPTION).
- `dvdt`: IRFZ44N 5 V/ns (S10).
- SOA: no SOA curves in the extracts. Use the thermal-limit expression above for pulses with `Zth(t)` from BEH-PWR-PKGTHERMAL and, for linear-mode operation (Vgs below about 6-8 V and Vds above a few volts), flag as SOA RISK (Spirito, S28). Basis: S28 for the mechanism only.
- Vgs overdrive: with Vgs below Vgs(th)max the part may be off (bench B9). Flag logic-level mismatch when `Vgs_drive < Vgs(th)max + 1 V`, per part.

### 2.7 Failure and misuse behavior
| Trigger | Physical effect | Simulator response | Permanence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vgs beyond +/-20 V | gate-oxide rupture, gate shorts to source (or to drain) | flag `VGS_EXCEEDED`; mark failed: Rgs = 100 ohm to 1 kohm short; device behaves as permanently on or off with a leaky gate (basis: general engineering knowledge, no source opened, confidence L) | permanent |
| Vds above BVDSS with energy below EAS | avalanche, device clamps at BVDSS | clamp (the body diode BV does it), flag if `E_av > EAS` | recoverable if within EAS |
| Avalanche energy above EAS or high repetition | hot spot, melted metal, drain-source short (S29 states the electrical signature of an overstress filament is a low-ohmic drain-source-gate short) | mark failed: Rds = 1 mohm D-S short (and G short to S/D) | permanent |
| Linear mode in the Spirito region (high Vds, low Vgs, DC or ms pulses) | thermal runaway of a hot spot below the ZTC point (S28, S29) | flag `SOA_RISK` (no model of hot-spot) | permanent when it triggers |
| Overcurrent above ID/IDM | bond wire fusing, die overheat | flag; fail open for bond wire or short for die (policy; unknown) | permanent |
| Body diode current above IS, or dv/dt above 5 V/ns (IRFZ44N) | parasitic bipolar turn-on, shoot-through in bridges | flag only | possibly permanent |
| Gate floating | gate charges by leakage and coupling through Cgd, part turns on partially | model has no leakage: user must tie to a source; DRC rule (no gate net without a driver) | recoverable |
| ESD | oxide damage on small signal parts | not simulated | permanent |
| Overtemperature Tj above 175 C (150 C Si7898DP, 2N7000 150 C implied) | thermal runaway of Rds(on) loop with a constant-current load, or a destroyed die | flag `TJ_EXCEEDED`; the Rds(on) positive tempco is stable for switching loads | permanent |

### 2.8 Thermal behavior
Self-heating Tj = Tref + Rth P with the package-specific Rth (BEH-PWR-PKGTHERMAL). Conduction loss P = Id^2 Rds(on)(Tj), switching loss approx 0.5 Vds Id (tr + tf) f (Qgd and the gate drive resistance set tr, tf; a model with constant Cgd underestimates this several times, bench B3), body-diode loss VSD Id plus Qrr Vds f. The Rds(on) fixed point in Tj is solved with `temp=Tj` iterations as for the BJT.

### 2.9 Appearance summary
OHM-098 (TO-220): black slab with metal tab and mounting hole, three leads, marking on the front. OHM-099 (TO-247): the same idea at 15.9 mm wide with leads at 5.45 mm. OHM-100/OHM-101 (DPAK/D2PAK): surface mount black block with an exposed tab at one end and a cropped middle lead. OHM-102 (PowerPAK SO-8): SO-8-sized flat body only 1.04 mm high with flush leads and a large exposed drain pad underneath. OHM-093/094 hold the small-signal parts.

## 3. BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-REG-LINEAR

Applies to: three-terminal linear regulators in OHM-093 (TO-92: 78L05 class), OHM-094 (SOT-23: MCP1700-type, existing record), OHM-095 (SOT-89: 78L05 class), OHM-096 (SOT-223: AMS1117, LM1117, LM317), OHM-098 (TO-220: L7805, LM317, LM1117, LM2940), OHM-100 (DPAK: L78 series, LM1117), OHM-101 (D2PAK: L78, LM317, LM2940). Reference parts opened: AMS1117 (S17), LM1117 (S18), L78 series (S19), LM317 (S20), LM2940 (S21), L78L (S22), LM78L (S23).

### 3.1 Purpose and real-world use
A linear regulator turns a higher, poorly controlled input into a lower, stable output by dropping the difference across a pass transistor. It is used for 3.3 V and 5 V logic rails from 5-12 V inputs, analog supplies (low noise, no switching ripple), post-regulation after a switcher, and as a current-limited adjustable supply (LM317). Three families matter:
- Standard NPN-Darlington-type (78xx, 78Lxx): about 2 V dropout, fixed output, tolerant of any output capacitor of at least 0.1 uF, input up to 35 V (L7805) or 20-30 V (78L05).
- Low-dropout NPN/PNP-hybrid (LM1117, AMS1117, LM2940): 1.1-1.3 V (1117 at 0.8 A) or 0.5 V typ/1 V max (LM2940 at 1 A) dropout; need an output capacitor with ESR in a window.
- Adjustable (LM317): 1.25 V reference, output set by two resistors, needs a minimum load current.

### 3.2 What it is and how it works
Error amplifier compares the output (through a divider, internal for fixed parts) with a bandgap reference and drives the pass element (NPN Darlington, PNP, or PMOS). Loop gain sets load and line regulation, the output capacitor and the pass-element output impedance set the loop poles, and the output capacitor ESR places a zero that stabilises the loop for the bipolar types.
Key quantities and equations:
- Dropout: smallest Vin - Vout at which regulation holds. In deep dropout the pass device is a resistor, Vout = Vin - Rdo Iout with Rdo = VDO/IDO. AMS1117: 1.1 V typ, 1.3 V max at 0.8 A (S17); LM1117: 1.3 V max at 0.8 A, 0-125 C (S18); L7805: 2 V at 1 A, 25 C (S19); LM2940: 0.5 V typ, 1 V max at 1 A (S21); LM317 needs at least 3 V differential (S20).
- Line regulation: dVout/dVin. L7805: 50 mV typ over 7.5-25 V (S19), i.e. 2.86 mV/V. AMS1117: 0.5-1.0 mV typ across its input range (S17).
- Load regulation: Rout = dVout/dIout. L7805: 100 mV typ from 5 mA to 1.5 A (66.9 mohm); AMS1117: 3-7 mV for 0-0.8 A (about 6 mohm); LM1117 0.4 % max (adjustable); LM317 0.1 % typ.
- Quiescent (ground) current: L7805 4.3-6 mA (S19); LM1117 5 mA typ, up to 10 mA (S18); AMS1117 5-11 mA max (S17); LM2940 30 mA typ at 1 A with Vin - Vout = 5 V, 10-20 mA at 5 mA load (S21); L78L05 6 mA at 25 C (S22) vs 3.6-4.7 mA typ (S23, new chip).
- Dissipation: P = (Vin - Vout) Iout + Vin Iq. The junction temperature is Tj = Ta + Rth P (BEH-PWR-PKGTHERMAL); thermal shutdown is a protection, not an operating mode.
- Minimum load: LM317 3.5-10 mA (S20); LM1117 adjustable 1.7 mA typ, 5 mA across temperature (S18); AMS1117 5-10 mA (S17). Below it the output may drift upward.
- Output capacitor: AMS1117 22 uF solid tantalum minimum (S17); LM1117 at least 10 uF tantalum with ESR 0.3-22 ohm (S18); LM2940 at least 22 uF with ESR 0.1-1 ohm (S21); L78xx input 0.33 uF, output 0.1 uF (S19); L78L the same (S22). A ceramic capacitor (ESR typically 5-20 mohm) is outside the ESR window of LM1117/LM2940/AMS1117 and can make them oscillate: a famous real-world failure.
- Current limit and thermal shutdown: LM1117 800-1200-1500 mA (min-typ-max) at 5 V dropout (S18); AMS1117 current limit 900-1500 mA (S17), shutdown at 165 C at the sense point, 125 C maximum continuous junction temperature; L7805 short-circuit current 0.2 A sustained and 2.2 A peak (S19). Thermal-shutdown temperature of the L78 and LM1117 families was not captured.
- Input limits: L7805 35 V (5-18 V outputs), 40 V (20-24 V); LM1117 20 V; AMS1117 15 V; LM2940 26 V continuous, 60 V transient for 100 ms, reverse polarity withstand -45 to -75 V for 1 ms (S21); L78L05 20 V (S22) vs 30 V (S23).

### 3.3 How it connects
Three terminals IN, OUT, GND (ADJ for LM317 and adjustable LM1117). The package never fixes the order:
- L7805 TO-220: pin 1 IN, pin 2 GND, pin 3 OUT; tab = GND (S19). L78 in DPAK and D2PAK: input-ground-output (same ordering; tab not stated, assumed GND).
- LM317 TO-220 / TO-263 / SOT-223: pin 1 ADJ, pin 2 OUT, pin 3 IN (S20). The tab is OUT (not stated explicitly in the extract; consistent with pin 2 = tab).
- LM1117 SOT-223: pin 1 ADJ/GND, pin 2 OUT, pin 3 IN, pin 4 OUT (tab); TO-252: pin 2 OUT = tab; TO-220: pin 1 GND, pin 2 OUT, pin 3 IN (S18).
- AMS1117 SOT-223 and TO-252: pin 1 GND/ADJ, pin 2 OUT, pin 3 IN, tab = OUT (S17).
- LM2940 TO-263 and TO-220: pin 1 IN, pin 2 GND, pin 3 OUT (S21).
- 78L05 TO-92: ST L78L: pin 1 IN, pin 2 GND, pin 3 OUT (S22); TI LM78L: pin 1 OUT, pin 2 GND, pin 3 IN (S23). The two vendors use mirrored orders for the same function. SOT-89 likewise: ST pin 1 GND, pin 2 VI, pin 3 VO; TI pin 1 VOUT, pin 2 GND, pin 3 VIN.
Typical circuit: input capacitor (0.1-0.33 uF or 10 uF) close to the part, output capacitor in the window above, a protection diode from OUT to IN where the output can be held above the input (recommended for the LM317 and 78xx families; the extracts did not capture the figure). Common mistakes: mirrored pins (SOT-223 AMS1117 versus a part with IN-GND-OUT), a ceramic output capacitor on a part that requires ESR, feeding 12 V into a 3.3 V regulator that must dissipate 8.7 V * 0.8 A = 7 W in a SOT-223, omitting the minimum load on LM317/LM1117, and back-feeding the output from a second supply.

### 3.4 Electrical model for simulation
Layer L1. Fidelity: `behavioural_approximation` (behavioural B-source subcircuit; NOT a vendor model; no datasheet or vendor loop model was opened). Library: `/home/claude/behavior/bench/reg_linear/reg_behavioural_r6.lib`, subcircuit `LDO_R6 vin vout gnd` with parameters.
Netlist template:
```
.include reg_behavioural_r6.lib
X{ref} {IN} {OUT} {GND} LDO_R6 VNOM=3.3 VINREF=5 KLINE=0.0005 ROUTDC=0.006 VDO=1.1 IDO=0.8 IQ=5m IQ1=0 ILIM=1.2 GM=40 FP1=200k FP2=2meg TSD=165 RTH=61.6 CTH=0.05 TA=25
.nodeset v(OUT)=3.3            * REQUIRED for .op, see honesty note 3
```
Structure of the subcircuit:
- Reference: `Vreg = VNOM + KLINE (Vin - VINREF) - (ROUTDC - 1/GM) Ipass`. The finite loop transconductance GM adds 1/GM of output resistance, so the term is corrected; the net DC output resistance is ROUTDC. When 1/GM > ROUTDC the coefficient is negative (a mild static positive feedback of gain GM (1/GM - ROUTDC) < 1); keep GM ROUTDC at or above 0.2.
- Demand current `GM (Vreg - Vout)` filtered through two lag poles FP1, FP2 (the loop dynamics).
- Pass current = soft-min(demand, ILIM, (Vin - Vout)/Rdo), Rdo = VDO/IDO, soft-max with IFLOOR, times a thermal gate 0.5(1 - tanh((Tj - TSD)/1 C)). Soft widths are 2 mA. A 1 mA residual remains at zero load (soft floor).
- Ground current `IQ + IQ1 Ipass` drawn from Vin to GND.
- Thermal node: power into an RC (RTH, CTH) to ambient TA; Tj is the node voltage (1 V = 1 C).
- `Dbody` from OUT to IN with IS = 1e-12, N = 1.5, RS = 0.3 ohm models a reverse-current path (ASSUMPTION; real parts differ and the datasheets opened did not state their reverse-current behavior).
Parameter sets (every number is from the cited extract unless marked ASSUMPTION; values the extracts did not give are marked):

| Part | VNOM V | VDO V at IDO A | KLINE mV/V | ROUTDC mohm | IQ mA | ILIM A | TSD C | RTH K/W | Output cap rule | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AMS1117-3.3 | 3.3 | 1.1 typ (1.3 max) at 0.8 | 0.5 (ASSUMPTION per V; datasheet gives 0.5-1 mV over its range) | 6 (5 mV/0.8 A, typ of 3-7 mV) | 5 (typ; extract printed "5 11 mA" max) | 1.2 (ASSUMPTION, datasheet 0.9-1.5) | 165 | 61.6 (TI LM1117 SOT-223 value used as stand-in; AMS gives 45-80) | >= 22 uF tantalum | S17, S18 |
| LM1117-3.3 | 3.3 | 1.3 max at 0.8 (typ not captured) | 0.2 % max total (adjustable version) | 0.4 % max over load (adj) | 5 typ, 10 max | 1.2 typ (0.8-1.5) | not captured (150 C is the absolute maximum junction temperature) | SOT-223 61.6, TO-252 45.1, TO-220 23.8 | >= 10 uF tantalum, ESR 0.3-22 ohm | S18 |
| L7805 | 5.0 | 2 at 1 | 2.86 (50 mV over 17.5 V) | 66.9 (100 mV over 1.495 A) | 4.3-6 | 2.2 peak (0.2 A sustained short circuit) | not captured (150 ASSUMPTION, L) | TO-220 50, D2PAK 62.5, DPAK 100 (RthJC 5, 3, 8) | 0.33 uF in, 0.1 uF out | S19 |
| LM317 (fixed 5 V example) | 1.25 (1 + R2/R1) + IADJ R2 | 3 V minimum differential | 0.01 %/V typ | 0.1 % typ | 3.5-10 mA minimum load, IADJ 50-100 uA | 1.5 | not captured | TO-220 23.5, TO-263 41, SOT-223 59.6 (new chip, TI JEDEC board) | datasheet figure not captured | S20 |
| LM2940-5.0 | 5.0 | 0.5 typ, 1 max at 1 | 20-150 mV over its line range (extract) | 35-200 mV over 50 mA-1 A (extract) | 10-20 mA at 5 mA load; 30 mA at 1 A (IQ1 = 0.03 A/A over the offset) | not captured | 150 stated as the maximum junction temperature | TO-220 23.3, TO-263 40.9, SOT-223 59.3 | >= 22 uF, ESR 0.1-1 ohm | S21 |
| L78L05 / LM78L05 | 5.0 | 2 typ (ST) vs 1.4-1.8 at 40 mA (TI): conflict | 19-29 mV over 7-20 V (TI) | 5.5-15 mV over 1-100 mA (TI) | 6 (ST) vs 3.6-4.7 (TI): conflict | 0.1 rated | "automatic shutdown" (temperature not captured) | TO-92 200 (ST, RthJC 15) vs 158.7 (TI); SOT-89 55 (ST, 6 cm2 Cu) vs 54.7 (TI) | 0.33 uF in, 0.1 uF out (ST) | S22, S23 |

Ideal vs realistic mode: ideal = `Vout = VNOM` voltage source with a dropout limit (use ROUTDC = 0, KLINE = 0, GM = 200, no Cth); realistic = the subcircuit above with poles, ILIM, thermal gate and quiescent current.
Valid analyses: op (with nodeset), dc (line and load sweeps work: bench B2), tran (load steps, thermal cycling), ac only around a converged op point. Not modelled: PSRR vs frequency, noise, startup ramp and soft start, true minimum-load behavior (only IFLOOR), foldback, thermal-shutdown hysteresis (the gate is a soft threshold with no latch), output-capacitor ESR window (see limitation).
Known limitations measured in this session:
- The transient and stability behavior depends on GM, FP1, FP2, which are ASSUMPTIONS (no datasheet gave a loop bandwidth). Bench B5: with GM = 40 S, 2.2 uF and 10 mohm ESR the model sustains an oscillation (peak 3.4056 V, unchanged between 36 us and 150 us); 22 uF with 10 mohm and 22 uF with 0.3 ohm settle. That is qualitatively the trend of the real parts but it does NOT reproduce the datasheet windows (for example 22 uF with 10 mohm is outside the LM2940 window of 0.1-1 ohm yet stable in the model). The simulator must therefore flag the output capacitor by the datasheet RULE (`cout_ok` below) and must not infer stability from a transient run.
- The DC operating point of the subcircuit can land on a spurious state without a nodeset (observed Vout 0.18 V).
- No input-to-output reverse conduction model from a datasheet.

### 3.6 Ratings and limits and the check expressions
- `vin_ok: Vin <= Vin_max` (AMS1117 15 V, LM1117 20 V, L7805 35 V, LM2940 26 V continuous). Transients: LM2940 60 V for at most 100 ms and -45..-75 V for at most 1 ms.
- `dropout_ok: Vin - Vout >= VDO(Iout)` else the output is not regulated: flag `OUT_OF_REGULATION` (and report the actual Vout from the model).
- `p_ok: P = (Vin - Vout) Iout + Vin Iq` and `Tj = Ta + Rth P <= Tj_max` (125 C for AMS1117 continuous and for the new-chip LM317; 150 C absolute for LM1117 and LM2940; 125 C for the L78 'C' versions in S19: "0 to 125 C").
- `iout_ok: Iout <= Imax` (1 A AMS1117, 0.8 A guaranteed for LM1117, 1.5 A L7805/LM317, 1 A LM2940, 0.1 A L78L).
- `iload_min_ok: Iout >= Imin` for LM317 (3.5-10 mA), LM1117 adjustable (5 mA worst), AMS1117 (5-10 mA). If violated, flag `MIN_LOAD`.
- `cout_ok: Cout >= Cmin and ESRmin <= ESR(Cout) <= ESRmax` (rule per part from 3.4). A ceramic output capacitor with ESR below the window must raise `COUT_ESR_TOO_LOW` for the families that state an ESR window. This is a rule, not a simulated result.
- `rev_ok: Vout <= Vin + 0.3 V` unless an external diode is present; otherwise flag `REVERSE_CURRENT` (no datasheet number found; the check is conservative).

### 3.7 Failure and misuse behavior
| Trigger | Physical effect | Simulator response | Permanence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tj above shutdown temperature | internal thermal shutdown reduces/stops the pass current, output collapses, then cycles as the die cools | model: soft thermal gate throttles current near TSD; bench B4 overload (15 V, 1 A load): Tj peaks at 151.2 C, Vout falls to 0.86 V, and recovers to 5.01 V when the load is removed (Tj 43.5 C) | recoverable |
| Output short | current limit (ILIM, or foldback for some parts): L7805 0.2 A sustained short | soft limit in the model (hard 1 mA-wide knee); heating rises through (Vin - 0) * ILIM so the thermal gate engages | recoverable unless the thermal limit is bypassed (high Vin) |
| Vin above abs max | pass transistor/die breakdown | flag; mark part failed: short IN to OUT (typical, ASSUMPTION L) or open | permanent |
| Reverse polarity at input | for LM2940 survives -45 to -75 V for 1 ms (S21); for other families no number opened | flag; for parts without a stated rating mark failed | LM2940 recoverable within the pulse; others unknown |
| Output held above input (back-feed, input collapses) | current flows from OUT to IN through the pass device or its body diode; can damage the regulator | model: Dbody conducts; flag `REVERSE_CURRENT` | potentially permanent |
| Output cap ESR outside the window | loop oscillates, often a 100 kHz-1 MHz ring on the output | flag by rule; model may show an oscillation but is not calibrated (bench B5) | recoverable |
| Dissipation above rating but below shutdown | long-term die heating, reduced life | flag `P_EXCEEDED` | gradual |
| Light load below the minimum | output rises (LM317/LM1117) | IFLOOR model only; flag | recoverable |
| ESD | not simulated | document only | permanent |
Thermal shutdown is a recoverable protection; destruction happens when the junction exceeds the absolute maximum before shutdown acts (short pulse above the abs-max input voltage, fast thermal transient from a hard short at high Vin) or when other absolute maxima are violated.

### 3.8 Thermal behavior
`Tj = Ta + Rth P` with Rth from the package (BEH-PWR-PKGTHERMAL). Example from the benches: L7805 at 9 V in, 0.5 A, TO-220 RthJA 50 K/W: P = 4 x 0.5 + 9 x 0.005 = 2.045 W, Tj = 25 + 50 x 2.045 = 127.25 C (bench B4: 128.16 C, +0.7 %). At 12 V in and 1.5 A the same part would need 10.5 W, which at 50 K/W (free air) exceeds any junction limit: a heat sink is mandatory. A SOT-223 AMS1117 dropping 8.7 V at 0.8 A needs 6.96 W; at 61.6 K/W that is a 429 C rise, so the part is in thermal shutdown in practice: the regulator behavior class makes this visible through the `p_ok` check.

### 3.9 Appearance summary
Packages as in the 3D spec entries OHM-093, 094, 095, 096, 098, 100, 101. A regulator and a transistor in the same package look identical; only the marking and the connection distinguish them. SOT-223 and DPAK/D2PAK regulators show the tab, which in the opened parts is OUT (AMS1117, LM1117, LM317) or GND (L78).

### 3.12 Research confidence
- Parameters: MEDIUM (headline numbers from extracts; typical columns and some conditions missing).
- Ratings: MEDIUM (conflicts: L78L between ST and TI, thermal resistance depends on the test board).
- Model fidelity: LOW-MEDIUM: DC behavior matches datasheet numbers by construction; dynamics, stability, reverse current are assumptions.
- Failure behavior: MEDIUM for thermal shutdown (recoverable) and input ratings; LOW for reverse current and for destruction states.
- Unresolved: thermal-shutdown temperature of L78/LM1117/LM317/LM2940; reverse-current and protection-diode requirements per part; PSRR curves; startup; MCP1700 pins (the repo record says pin 1 VOUT, 2 GND, 3 VIN with empty evidence, and the Microchip datasheet could not be opened to check); tab connection of TO-220 LM317/LM1117/LM2940 (inferred from pin 2); the full LM317 and LM1117 adjustable circuits.

## 4. BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-PWR-PKGTHERMAL

Applies to: all ten entries. This class carries what the PACKAGE contributes to behavior: thermal resistance, how copper area changes it, derating, transient thermal impedance and the power-rating check shared by BEH-TRN-BJT, BEH-TRN-MOSFET and BEH-REG-LINEAR.

### 4.1 Purpose and real-world use
Power rating is a package-and-board property as much as a die property. A 2N3904 in TO-92 can dissipate 0.625 W because (150 - 25)/200 K/W = 0.625 W; the same silicon in SOT-23 is limited to 0.25 W by a 500 K/W footprint (S1, S4). A TO-220 MOSFET with a heat sink can handle 100+ W while the same package free in air is limited to 62 K/W (2 W at 125 K of rise). Users pick DPAK/D2PAK for surface-mount power and size the copper pour; the rating changes by a factor of two with copper area (S24).

### 4.2 What it is and how it works
Heat flows from the junction to the case or mounting base (`Rth(j-c)` or `Rth(j-mb)`, intrinsic to the package and die, independent of the board; S25), then through the board or heat sink to ambient (`Rth(c-a)`). `Rth(j-a)` is the series sum and is dominated by the PCB for small packages (S25: "RthJA is dominated by PCB effects while RthJC is just a small part of the overall system"; S27: the FR4 PCB itself sets a floor of 50-60 K/W). Larger copper lowers `Rth` with diminishing returns (S25, S27). Two parallel paths exist (case-to-air and PCB). The steady-state rule is `Tj = Ta + Rth(j-a) P` and the rating `P_max = (Tj_max - Ta)/Rth(j-a)` (S24 and datasheets); with a heat sink `Tj = Tamb + P (Rth(j-c) + Rth(c-s) + Rth(s-a))`, where `Rth(c-s)` is 0.5 K/W greased for the TO-220 IRFZ44N and 0.24 K/W for the TO-247 IRFP260N (S10, S13). In the transient regime thermal capacitance makes the junction temperature rise as a charging RC (Foster or Cauer network); shorter pulses permit higher peak power because Zth falls with pulse width, `P = (Tj_max - Tmb)/Zth(t) = Id Vds` (S28).
The datasheet values depend on the test board and the way the document states them: TI quotes TO-220 at 23-24 K/W (a JEDEC high-K board mounted via the tab), ST quotes L7805 in TO-220 at 50 K/W free air (S19), Infineon quotes 62 K/W for the TO-220 MOSFETs (S10-S12). These are different conditions for the same package, not inconsistent measurements.

### 4.3 How it connects
No electrical pins. In the netlist the thermal network is a ground-referenced RC ladder: power in watts is a current source into the junction node, temperature in degrees Celsius is the node voltage (1 V = 1 C), ambient is a DC source. In the layout tool, the user's copper pour area under the tab (DPAK/D2PAK/SOT-223/PowerPAK) selects the `Rth(j-a)` row. Common mistakes: using the free-air RthJA with a heat sink, using RthJC alone without a sink (junction at the case temperature only if the case is held), adding the junction-to-case rating of a datasheet test with an infinite sink, forgetting the interface thermal resistance, and using DC `Rth` for short pulses.

### 4.4 Electrical model for simulation
Layer L1 (thermal analogy). Fidelity: `behavioural_approximation`.
Netlist template (two-stage Foster, defaults for a TO-220 MOSFET on a heat sink):
```
Ip   0 tj dc {P}            * P in W is a current in A
R1 tj tc {RTHJC}
C1 tj 0 {C1}  ic={TA}
R2 tc ta {RTHCA}            * RTHCA = RTHCS + RTHSA, or RTHJA - RTHJC for a bare package
C2 tc 0 {C2}  ic={TA}
Vta ta 0 {TA}
```
In the regulators the same network is inside `LDO_R6` (RTH, CTH). For the BJT and MOSFET classes the power is `Vce Ic` or `Vds Id` taken from the solution, and `Tj` returns as `temp=Tj` on the instance in a fixed-point loop (bench B8 of BEH-TRN-BJT).
Copper-area dependence: only published points were captured, so use a table with linear interpolation of Rth versus log(area), and refuse to extrapolate outside the published range (interpolation rule is an ASSUMPTION):
- DPAK: 62 K/W at 0.45 cm2 (minimum footprint) and 50 K/W at 6 cm2, 2 oz copper, FR-4 (S24: "RTHJ-PCB"; junction-to-PCB, close to junction-to-ambient). Datasheet S14 gives 110 K/W minimum footprint and 50 K/W for 1 in2 (6.45 cm2) for the IRLR8721. The two sources conflict on the minimum footprint (62 vs 110 K/W): different boards and definitions. Keep both as per-part rows.
- D2PAK: 42 K/W at 1.2 cm2 and 34 K/W at 6 cm2 (S24).
- PowerSO-8 (not a PowerPAK, context only): 56.6 K/W at 0.23 cm2, 42 K/W at 6 cm2 (S24).
- LFPAK (context only, S27): 3.2 W (single layer, LFPAK56) vs 6.3 W (four layers with vias) at 80 C ambient.
- SOT-223 and SOT-89 collector pad (BJTs): BCP56 192/125/93 K/W for standard footprint, 1 cm2, 6 cm2 (S5); BCX56 250/132/93 K/W (S6). SOT-23 BC817: 500/362 K/W for standard footprint and 1 cm2 (S4).
Transient: no manufacturer Zth curve or Foster coefficients were captured. The capacitor values in bench B1 (C1 = 0.02 J/K, C2 = 0.5 J/K) are ASSUMPTIONS and only the DC end value is checked. RESEARCH_REQUIRED: per-package Zth(t) curves (DPAK, D2PAK, TO-220, SOT-223) from datasheets (Infineon, Vishay normalised thermal response) before pulse-power checks can be promised.
Known limitations: no lateral coupling between devices on a shared copper pour, no board stack-up or via model, no convection or airflow dependence, no radiation, the Tj-dependent Rth of a package is not modelled.

### 4.6 Ratings and limits and the check expression
- `pmax(Ta) = (Tj_max - Ta)/Rth(j-a)` for the declared mounting; `pmax(Tc) = (Tj_max - Tc)/Rth(j-c)` when a heat sink holds the case. Tj_max is 150 C (BJTs, 2N7000 implied, Si7898DP) or 175 C (IRFZ44N, IRF540N, IRLB8721, IRFP260N, IRLR8721). Bench B2 reproduces 12 of 15 datasheet power numbers to better than 1.5 %.
- `tj = Ta + Rth*P <= Tj_max` evaluated for each placed device with the selected mounting; the DRC output carries the margin.
- Power in a SOA check at short pulses: `P_pulse <= (Tj_max - Tmb)/Zth(t)`; unavailable without Zth data, so the checker reports `ZTH_UNKNOWN` instead of a pass.
- Derating: linear from the 25 C rating to zero at Tj_max (5 mW/K for the 625 mW TO-92 BJTs; 0.63 W/K IRFZ44N; 0.87 W/K IRF540N; 2.8 mW/K 2N7000).
- Rule of thumb from S28 for linear-mode pulses outside the Spirito region: a triangular pulse is equivalent to a rectangular one of the same width and half the peak (an empirical design margin).

### 4.7 Failure and misuse behavior
| Trigger | Effect | Simulator response | Permanence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tj above Tj_max (150 or 175 C) | bond-wire and die damage, solder fatigue, parametric drift | flag `TJ_EXCEEDED`; the device class decides short/open policy | permanent |
| Rth(j-a) assumed from the wrong row (sink vs free air vs copper area) | rating off by factors of 2-10 | flag `RTH_CONTEXT`: the binding must state mounting; default to the worst published value for that package | n/a |
| Copper area below the table minimum | Rth above published | refuse to extrapolate; use the minimum-footprint row | n/a |
| Thermal runaway (loop gain above 1) | see BEH-TRN-BJT 1.7, BEH-TRN-MOSFET 2.7 | flag | permanent |
| Cycling (repeated shutdown) | solder fatigue | document only | cumulative |

### 4.8 Thermal behavior
This class is the thermal behavior. Bench B1 reproduces `Tj = Ta + P (R1 + R2)` for a 2 W step: 148.999 C against 149.0 C analytic.

### 4.9 Appearance summary
See the 3D spec entries of each package; copper area, tab and exposed pads are the visible thermal features: TO-220 tab with hole (OHM-098), TO-247 (OHM-099), DPAK and D2PAK exposed tabs and undersides (OHM-100, OHM-101), PowerPAK drain pad (OHM-102), SOT-223 tab (OHM-096).

### 4.12 Research confidence
- Parameters: MEDIUM (many published rows, board conditions differ by source).
- Ratings: HIGH where B2 reproduces the datasheet number; the three failed rows are flagged.
- Model fidelity: MEDIUM for steady state, LOW for transient (no Zth data).
- Failure behavior: MEDIUM.
- Unresolved: Zth(t) per package; JEDEC board definitions (JESD51) were not opened; thermal vias; the exact meaning of S24 "RTHJ-PCB" (junction to PCB, not ambient).
