# PER-ENTRY SECTIONS

Convention: each entry is a package. The "binding" table says which functional part lives in the package and how its electrical pins map to the package terminal numbers of the 3D spec (terminal numbering as in the 3D spec Terminals section of each entry). "Default" is the functional part the inventory should place when the user picks the package without choosing a part; it is a recommendation, not a library fact. Every entry also inherits BEH-PWR-PKGTHERMAL.

## [OHM-093] TO-92 transistor -> BEH-TRN-BJT, BEH-TRN-MOSFET, BEH-REG-LINEAR

Package facts (3D spec OHM-093): THT, 3 straight leads at 1.27 mm spacing (2.54 outer to outer), body 4.6 x 3.7 x 4.8 mm, flat marked face, pin 1 leftmost looking at the flat face, no pin-1 dot. No tab. Aliases TO-92, TO-226, SOT54, SC-43A.
Binding (pin order is part dependent):

| Functional part | Class | Pin 1 | Pin 2 | Pin 3 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2N3904 | BJT NPN | E | B | C | S1 |
| PN2222A | BJT NPN | E | B | C | S2 |
| BC546/547/548 | BJT NPN | C | B | E | S3 |
| 2N7000 | N-MOSFET | S | G | D | S8 |
| L78L05 (ST) | regulator | IN | GND | OUT | S22 |
| LM78L05 (TI) | regulator | OUT | GND | IN | S23 |
Electrical-type mapping: BJT C and E bidirectional, B input; MOSFET D and S bidirectional, G input; regulator IN power_in, GND power_in, OUT power_out.
Package-specific values: RthJA 200 K/W and RthJC 83.3 K/W (2N3904, PN2222A, BC547, derating 5 mW/K from 625 mW, Tj max 150 C); RthJA 357 K/W for the 2N7000 (350 mW, 2.8 mW/K); ST L78L05 TO-92 RthJA 200 K/W, RthJC 15 K/W vs TI LM78L 158.7 K/W (conflict). Pad: three-hole in-line footprint, the same for all functions, so a wrongly oriented part is electrically wrong but mechanically plausible.
Defaults: 2N3904 (`Q2N3904_R6FIT`), pin map E-B-C. Polarity: the flat face is the only orientation feature; the schematic symbol must carry the part's pin order (E-B-C vs C-B-E) so that a part swap cannot silently reorder pins.
Parasitics: lead inductance and capacitance not researched (THT lead 0.45 x 0.40 mm, about 14 mm uncut); the fT of 300 MHz parts is limited by the die, not the package.
Notes: 2N7000 is also sold with other pin orders by other makers (BS170 is drain-gate-source; not opened, so only mentioned as a known risk, no data). The 78L05 vendor orders mirror each other (S22 vs S23).
Status: partial (2N3904, PN2222A, BC547 pin maps verified; BC547 has no fitted card; 78L05 vendor conflict; regulators in TO-92 other than 78L05 not researched).

## [OHM-094] SOT-23 transistor -> BEH-TRN-BJT, BEH-TRN-MOSFET, BEH-REG-LINEAR

Package facts (3D spec OHM-094): SMD, 3 gull-wing leads, pins 1 and 2 on one side (pitch 1.9 mm), pin 3 on the opposite side, counter-clockwise numbering seen from the top, pin 1 bottom-left. Aliases SOT-23, TO-236AB, SOT23-3.
Binding:

| Functional part | Class | Pin 1 | Pin 2 | Pin 3 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BC817 | BJT NPN | B | E | C | S4 |
| MMBT3904 (SMD 2N3904) | BJT NPN | B | E | C (industry norm, NOT verified: datasheet blocked) | none opened |
| 2N7002 | N-MOSFET | G | S | D | S9 |
| MCP1700-3302E/TT (existing repo record) | regulator | VOUT | GND | VIN as recorded in the repo (evidence list empty; not verified against Microchip) | repo |
Package-specific values: RthJA 500 K/W (standard footprint) and 362 K/W (1 cm2 collector pad) for the BC817 (Ptot 250 mW and 345 mW, Tj max 150 C); 2N7002 350 K/W, Ptot 0.83 W (conflict with its own Rth: 125/350 = 0.357 W; the 0.83 W is probably referenced to another condition and was not resolved). Land pattern per the 3D spec (0.8 x 0.9 pads).
Defaults: MMBT3904 modelled with the 2N3904 fit (`Q2N3904_R6FIT`): ASSUMPTION that the SMD part has the same die, status partial. Polarity: pin 1 bottom-left; for SOT-23 the single pin on the top edge is pin 3 (collector or drain or VIN depending on the part).
Notes: A SOT-23 sits at 250 mW for a BC817 on a minimum footprint, an order of magnitude below a TO-92 power rating of the 2N7000, so the power check will be the common DRC hit. Pin 1/2/3 functions of the three bindings differ: BC817 B-E-C, 2N7002 G-S-D, MCP1700 as recorded VOUT-GND-VIN. The repo record for MCP1700 may disagree with the datasheet (not opened here): treat as RESEARCH_REQUIRED.
Status: partial (BC817 and 2N7002 verified; MMBT3904 and MCP1700 pin maps unverified).

Package facts (3D spec OHM-095): SMD, body 4.5 x 2.5 x 1.5 mm, three leads at 1.5 mm pitch on one side, the centre lead widens into a tab on the opposite end, pin 2 = tab. Aliases SOT89, TO-243, SC-62.

| Functional part | Class | Pin 1 | Pin 2 (tab) | Pin 3 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BCX56 | BJT NPN | E | C | B | S6 |
| L78L05 (ST) | regulator | GND | VI | VO (extract says the tab is connected to GND: contradicts "tab = pin 2 = VI" in the same extract) | S22 |
| LM78L05 (TI) | regulator | VOUT | GND | VIN | S23 |
Package-specific values: BCX56 RthJA 250 K/W (standard footprint), 132 K/W (1 cm2 collector pad), 93 K/W (6 cm2), Ptot 0.5 to 1.35 W, Tj max 150 C; L78L05 SOT-89 55 K/W with 6 cm2 copper (ST) and 54.7 K/W (TI).

Notes: The BCX56 is E-C-B while the BC817 and BCP56 are B-E-C and B-C-E, so SOT-89 BJT footprints cannot be freely swapped. In the L78L SOT-89 extract the tab is GND while pin 2 is VI: either the extract is garbled or the ST part's tab is not pin 2. This is UNRESOLVED and affects the rule "pin 2 = tab" from the 3D spec for regulators; keep the 3D spec's pin 2 = tab and mark the L78L SOT-89 binding research_required.

## [OHM-096] SOT-223 transistor/regulator -> BEH-TRN-BJT, BEH-REG-LINEAR

Package facts (3D spec OHM-096): SMD, body 6.5 x 3.5 x 1.65 mm, three leads at 2.3 mm pitch, pin 4 = wide tab (3.0 mm) opposite the leads, pin 4 electrically tied to pin 2. Aliases SOT223, SC-73, TO-261 (not seen in the opened documents).
Binding:

| Functional part | Class | Pin 1 | Pin 2 | Pin 3 | Pin 4 (tab) | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BCP56 | BJT NPN | B | C | E | C | S5 |
| AMS1117-3.3 | regulator | GND/ADJ | OUT | IN | OUT | S17 |
| LM1117 | regulator | ADJ/GND | OUT | IN | OUT | S18 |
| LM317 (DCY) | regulator | ADJ | OUT | IN | OUT (not stated; consistent with pin 2) | S20 |
Package-specific values: BCP56 RthJA 192 / 125 / 93 K/W (standard footprint, 1 cm2, 6 cm2 collector pad), Ptot 0.65 to 1.35 W, VCEO 80 V, 1 A; LM1117 61.6 K/W, LM317 59.6 K/W, LM2940 59.3 K/W (TI, new chip, JEDEC board), AMS1117 45-80 K/W by copper. A SOT-223 regulator at 8.7 V drop and 0.8 A needs 6.96 W: the 61.6 K/W part reaches thermal shutdown. Land pattern per 3D spec (tab pad 3.30 x 1.60).
Defaults: AMS1117-3.3 (`LDO_R6` with the AMS parameter set, GND/ADJ pin 1, OUT pin 2 and tab 4, IN pin 3), `.nodeset v(OUT)=3.3`. Polarity: tab opposite the leads; pin 1 left of the three leads.
Notes: The tab is the output for every regulator opened and the collector for the BJT, so the board copper under the tab carries the output (or collector) net: the copper pour that cools the part is not ground. The BCP56 and the regulators agree that pin 2 and pin 4 are the same net, so one electrical net serves both terminals. The 4th terminal must be tied to pin 2 in the netlist (one pin map entry with two package terminals).
Status: partial (pin maps verified for four parts; no MOSFET in SOT-223 researched; BCP56 has no fitted card).

## [OHM-097] TO-126 transistor -> BEH-TRN-BJT

Package facts (3D spec OHM-097): THT, body 7.6 x 2.6 x 10.8 mm, three flat leads at 2.28 mm, metal back plate with mounting hole (pin 2 tied to the plate). Aliases TO-126, SOT-32.
Binding: BD135/BD137/BD139 (ST, S7): pin 1 emitter, pin 2 collector (plate), pin 3 base; no other part opened (the PNP BD136/138/140 mirror the function but no PNP data opened).
Package-specific values: BD139 VCEO 80 V (BD135 45 V), IC 1.5 A, Ptot 12.5 W at Tc = 25 C (125 K / 10 K/W = 12.5 W reproduces the datasheet), Tj max 150 C, RthJC 10 K/W, RthJA 100 K/W, hFE 40-250 at 150 mA and 2 V, VCE(sat) 0.5 V at 0.5 A/50 mA; no fT in the datasheet. Free-air Ptot is 1.25 W (125/100), a factor of 10 below the case-referenced value.
Defaults: BD139, model DERIVED (BF = 100 geometric mean of 40-250, IS 1e-14; status partial). Polarity: the metal plate faces away from the marked face; the plate is the collector, so a heat sink at ground needs an insulating pad (standard practice; the plate is pin 2 per the 3D spec and S7).
Notes: do not use the free-air RthJA for a TO-126 mounted on a sink and do not use RthJC without one.
Status: partial (pin map and ratings verified; no fitted model; no SOA chart).

## [OHM-098] TO-220 transistor/MOSFET -> BEH-TRN-MOSFET, BEH-REG-LINEAR (power BJTs possible, not researched)

Package facts (3D spec OHM-098): THT, plastic 10.1 x 3.18 x 9.03 mm with a metal tab on +Y rising 6.22 mm above the plastic and a 3.8 mm hole, leads at 2.54 mm pitch, pin 2 tied to the tab; isolated TO-220F variant has no exposed metal. Aliases TO-220AB, SOT78, TO-220-3.
Binding:

| Functional part | Class | Pin 1 | Pin 2 (tab) | Pin 3 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| IRFZ44N, IRF540N, IRLB8721 | N-MOSFET | G | D | S | S10, S11, S12 |
| L7805 (ST) | regulator | IN | GND | OUT | S19 (tab aligns with pin 2 = GND) |
| LM317 | regulator | ADJ | OUT | IN | S20 (tab not stated) |
| LM1117 | regulator | GND | OUT | IN | S18 (tab not stated for TO-220) |
| LM2940 | regulator | IN | GND | OUT | S21 (tab not stated) |
So the tab is the drain for MOSFETs, GND for the L78 family and, by pin position, the output for LM317/LM1117 (an inference). A heat sink bolted to the tab therefore carries drain, ground or output potential, a classic wiring surprise.
Package-specific values: MOSFETs: RthJC 1.5 (IRFZ44N), 1.15 (IRF540N), 2.3 (IRLB8721) K/W; RthJA 62 K/W; RthCS 0.5 K/W greased (IRFZ44N); regulators: L7805 RthJC 5, RthJA 50 K/W; TI regulators 23.3-23.8 K/W (JEDEC board). Tj max 175 C for the MOSFETs, 125 C for the L78 'C' versions and new-chip LM317, 150 C absolute for LM1117 and LM2940.
Defaults: IRFZ44N (`IRFZ44N_R6`, G-D-S). Polarity: the tab and pin 1 at the left when facing the marked front.
Notes: The Vgs(th) of logic-level IRLB8721 is 1.35-2.35 V, IRFZ44N/IRF540N 2-4 V: a 3.3 V gate drive is marginal for the latter (bench B9 principle). The L7805 at 12 V in and 1 A out dissipates 7 W: 50 K/W free air gives 350 K of rise, so a sink is mandatory.
Status: partial (three MOSFETs and four regulators verified from datasheets; fitted cards for the three MOSFETs; regulator cards use datasheet-based parameters; tab for LM317/LM1117/LM2940 inferred; power BJTs in TO-220 not researched).

## [OHM-099] TO-247 power transistor -> BEH-TRN-MOSFET

Package facts (3D spec OHM-099): THT, body 15.9 x 5.02 mm, height 20.95 mm, leads at 5.45 mm pitch, metal tab on +Y with a 3.6 mm hole, pin 2 = tab. Aliases TO-247-3, TO-247AC/AD, SOT429.
Binding: IRFP260N (S13): drain, gate, source order as printed in the extract appears garbled; the TO-247AC convention is G-D-S like TO-220 (tab = drain) but this is UNRESOLVED from the opened document: keep G=pin 1, D=pin 2 and tab, S=pin 3 with status research_required for the pin order.
Package-specific values: VDS 200 V, ID 50 A, IDM 200 A, PD 300 W (150 K / 0.50 K/W = 300 W reproduces it), VGS +/-20 V, EAS 560 mJ, Tj -55..175 C, RthJC 0.50, RthCS 0.24 (greased), RthJA 40 K/W, Rds(on) max 40 mohm at 10 V and 28 A, Vgs(th) 2-4 V, Qg max 234 nC, Ciss 4057 pF, body diode 1.3 V max, trr 268-402 ns. The model carries only a lumped Cgs = Ciss (no Crss, Coss data in the extract).
Defaults: IRFP260N, level-1 card from `IRFP260N_R6` (KP = 4.197, VTO = 3.0 assumed). Polarity: pin 1 at -X from the marked face, tab at the back.
Notes: the gate charge of 234 nC means a 1 A gate driver needs 234 ns at the plateau start; the lumped Cgs model will understate switching time. 0.5 K/W is a case-referenced number; with a 1 K/W sink and 0.24 K/W interface the practical limit is about (175 - 25)/(0.5 + 0.24 + 1) = 86 W.
Status: partial (ratings verified, pin order unresolved, no vendor model).

## [OHM-100] DPAK / TO-252 -> BEH-TRN-MOSFET, BEH-REG-LINEAR

Package facts (3D spec OHM-100): SMD, plastic 6.10 x 6.58 x 2.29 mm, two gull-wing leads (pin 1 at -X, pin 3 at +X), the middle lead cropped (pin 2), exposed tab on +Y = pin 2/4, standoff 0.08 mm, optional stub to 1.0 mm. Aliases DPAK, TO-252, TO-252AA, SOT428.
Binding:

| Functional part | Class | Pin 1 | Pin 2 (cropped lead and tab) | Pin 3 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| IRLR8721, IRLR3410 | N-MOSFET | G | D (tab = drain) | S | S14, S15 |
| LM1117 (TO-252) | regulator | ADJ/GND | OUT (tab) | IN | S18 |
| L78 (DPAK) | regulator | IN | GND | OUT (tab not stated; assumed GND like TO-220) | S19 |
The cropped middle lead is physically absent in the default 3D model but its net is the tab, so the pin-2 net still reaches the board through the tab and the copper pour; only the lead stub is missing.
Package-specific values: IRLR8721 RthJA 50 K/W (1 in2 copper) vs 110 K/W (minimum footprint), RthJC 2.3 K/W with PD 33 W (extracts conflict: 150/2.3 = 65 W); IRLR3410 RthJC 1.9, RthJA 50 (PCB mount), PD 79 W; ST AN1703: junction-to-PCB 62 K/W at 0.45 cm2 and 50 K/W at 6 cm2 (2 oz, FR-4), 2.4-3 W at 150 K; L78 DPAK RthJC 8, RthJA 100 K/W; LM1117 TO-252 45.1 K/W; onsemi AND9008: DPAK constant-current regulators 0.92 W (300 mm2, 1 oz) to 1.82 W (1000 mm2, 3 oz) at 85 C ambient.
Defaults: IRLR8721 (`IRLB8721_R6` card is the closest fitted card but a different part; ASSUMPTION that the IRLR8721 shares the IRLB8721 die: Rds(on) 8.4/11.8 mohm vs 8.7/16 mohm shows they differ, so no card is shipped for IRLR8721: status research_required for the card). Polarity: tab at +Y, pin 1 at -X.
Notes: the copper under the tab is the heat path (S24, S25); the pour carries the drain (or output) net and must not be assumed ground. A DPAK at minimum footprint can dissipate only about 1.1 W at 125 K rise (110 K/W).
Status: partial.

## [OHM-101] D2PAK / TO-263 -> BEH-TRN-MOSFET (not opened), BEH-REG-LINEAR

Package facts (3D spec OHM-101): SMD, plastic 10.0 x 9.0 x 4.3 mm, 1.4 mm copper tab with exposed underside extending 1.5 mm past the +Y edge, two gull-wing leads at +/-2.54 mm, middle lead cropped, 5-lead variant at 1.7 mm pitch exists. Aliases D2PAK, TO-263, TO-263AB, SOT404.
Binding:

| Functional part | Class | Pin 1 | Pin 2 (cropped, tab) | Pin 3 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LM317 (TO-263 KTT) | regulator | ADJ | OUT | IN | S20 |
| LM2940 (TO-263 KTT) | regulator | IN | GND | OUT | S21 |
| L78 (D2PAK) | regulator | IN | GND | OUT | S19 |
| power MOSFETs in D2PAK | MOSFET | G | D | S | no D2PAK MOSFET datasheet opened: research_required |
Package-specific values: L78 D2PAK RthJC 3, RthJA 62.5 K/W; LM317 TO-263 41 K/W; LM2940 TO-263 40.9 K/W (TI, new chip); ST AN1703 junction-to-PCB 42 K/W at 1.2 cm2 and 34 K/W at 6 cm2 (3.5-4.4 W at 150 K).
Defaults: L7805 in D2PAK (IN pin 1, GND pin 2/tab, OUT pin 3), `LDO_R6` with the L7805 parameter set, RTH 62.5 or the area-table value. Polarity: tab at +Y, pin 1 at -X.
Notes: the tab and the middle terminal are GND for L78 and LM2940 but OUT for LM317: copper pour polarity differs per part. LM317 5-lead D2PAK variants are not researched.
Status: partial.

## [OHM-102] PowerPAK SO-8 MOSFET -> BEH-TRN-MOSFET

Package facts (3D spec OHM-102): SMD, molded body 5.89 x 4.90 x 1.04 mm, 8 flat leads at 1.27 mm pitch on the two long sides protruding about 0.13 mm, exposed drain pad 3.76 x 3.66 mm underneath, pins 1-3 source, pin 4 gate, pins 5-8 drain. Aliases PowerPAK SO-8, PPAK SO-8. Not SO-8FL, DFN5x6, LFPAK or PowerPAK SO-8L; the dual version is not modelled.
Binding: Si7898DP (Vishay, S16): S, S, S, G, D, D, D, D (pins 1-8): agrees exactly with the 3D spec.
Package-specific values: VDS 150 V, VGS +/-20 V, ID 4.8 A (25 C) and 3.8 A (70 C), IDM 25 A, PD 5 W (25 C), 3.2 W (70 C), Tj -55..150 C, RthJA 20/25 K/W (typ/max, t <= 10 s) and 52/65 K/W (steady state) on 1 in x 1 in FR4, RthJC (drain) 2.1/2.6 K/W; Rds(on) 68 mohm typ and 85 mohm max at 10 V and 3.5 A, 76/95 mohm at 6 V and 3 A; Qg 17/21 nC; VSD 0.75/1.2 V; trr 45/70 ns. The datasheet power of 5 W corresponds to the 10 s thermal resistance (125 K / 25 K/W = 5 W); steady state is 125/65 = 1.9 W.
Defaults: Si7898DP (`SI7898DP_R6`, level-3 card with THETA 1.84 and a lumped Cgs of 1.7 nF derived from Qg/10 V), `Rth` steady state 65 K/W max. Polarity: pin 1 dot at the top-left; the drain pad must be soldered to a copper pour for the datasheet thermal numbers to apply.
Notes: the drain pad is the heat path (RthJC to the pad 2.1-2.6 K/W); the leads alone are not. The 2 to 4 V Vgs(th) means 3.3 V logic is marginal. Package-level rows from the Vishay extract are consistent with the 3D spec dimensions (extracted thickness 1.07 mm on the product page vs 1.04 mm in the 3D spec: a 0.03 mm difference, no action).
Status: partial (single part verified; no vendor SPICE model; Qg only for dynamics).

# SOURCE CONFLICTS, GAPS AND DECISIONS FOR THE COORDINATOR

Conflicts between opened documents (all kept visible):
1. TO-92 BJT pin order: 2N3904 and PN2222A are E-B-C, BC546/547/548 are C-B-E (same package).
2. 78L05: ST L78L TO-92 IN-GND-OUT vs TI LM78L TO-92 OUT-GND-IN; SOT-89 ST GND-VI-VO vs TI VOUT-GND-VIN; TO-92 RthJA 200 (ST) vs 158.7 (TI), quiescent current 6 mA (ST) vs 3.6-4.7 mA (TI), maximum input 20 V (ST) vs 30 V (TI), dropout 2 V (ST) vs 1.4-1.8 V at 40 mA (TI).
3. SOT-89 L78L: the extract says the tab is GND and also that pin 2 is VI; cannot both be "tab = pin 2".
4. IRFZ44N: PD = 94 W with derating 0.63 W/K (1.59 K/W) vs RthJC 1.5 K/W (100 W).
5. 2N7002 (Nexperia): Ptot 0.83 W vs Rth(j-a) 350 K/W (0.357 W).
6. IRLR8721: PD 33 W at Tc = 25 C vs RthJC 2.3 K/W (65 W); the 2.3 may have been carried over from the IRLB8721 table.
7. TO-220 regulator RthJA: ST L7805 50, Infineon MOSFETs 62, TI regulators 23.3-23.8 (different test boards).
8. DPAK minimum footprint RthJA: ST AN1703 62 K/W junction-to-PCB vs Infineon IRLR8721 110 K/W.
9. IRFP260N pinout order printed as "drain, gate, source" (probable extraction error).
10. Si7898DP package height: 1.07 mm on the Vishay product page, 1.04 mm in the 3D spec (trivial).
11. Infineon extracts carry 2026 revision stamps and the TI LM78L extract says "Revision O (August 2026)"; I cannot confirm them.

3D spec versus electrical reality (no hard disagreement found; these need a decision):
- "Pin 2 = tab" holds for BJT (collector), MOSFET (drain), LM317/LM1117/AMS1117 (output) and L78/LM2940 (ground) in every opened case, so the 3D spec's tab rule is right, but the tab FUNCTION must come from the part binding, not from the package.
- SOT-89 L78L (ST) as extracted would break "pin 2 = tab" (unresolved).
- OHM-100/101 default to a cropped middle lead; for a 3-lead regulator the middle terminal is the same net as the tab, so no electrical change is needed, but a 3-lead variant (no cropping) may be needed for through-hole-like pin maps and for LM2940/LM317 5-lead TO-263 (not researched).
- OHM-093 TO-92: pin 1 is the left lead looking at the flat face; for BC547 that lead is the collector, for 2N3904 the emitter, so the package symbol alone cannot define the pin names.
- OHM-098: nothing contradicts the 3D spec; the TO-220F (isolated) variant mentioned in the spec has no exposed tab and a different RthJC (not researched).

Layer decisions: everything is L1. The regulator behavioural subcircuit is a pure L1 B-source model (no XSPICE). Thermal runs through an electrical analogy network (L1). No L2 or L3 content.

Compatibility with the OHMNI runner: every model ships `.model`/`.subckt` so the runner would label it `behavioural_approximation`; none may be labelled `vendor_model`. The runner parses only `.op` tables, so transient, ac and thermal results are available only if the runner is extended. The regulator needs a `.nodeset` per instance. The MOSFET and regulator subcircuits use B sources, charge capacitors (`q=`), `tanh` and `sqrt`, all in stock ngspice 42.

What is NOT done: no vendor SPICE models (Infineon, Vishay, TI, onsemi publish some; none opened); no PNP, P-channel or depletion fits; no MMBT3904, MCP1700, MC78L05 verification; no Zth(t) curves; no SOA charts for the small-signal BJTs; no Rds(on)-vs-Tj or Vth-vs-Tj curves; no D2PAK MOSFET datasheet; hFE typical curves were guessed from min/max bands (labelled).

<!-- BEGIN R7A -->
# GROUP R7A: IC packages DIP, SOIC, TSSOP, SSOP, MSOP, SOT-23-5/6 (OHM-103 to OHM-121)

Author: research agent R7A. ngspice 42 (stock build, XSPICE enabled) run locally. Every bench netlist is under `/home/claude/behavior/bench/<class-dir>/`, the raw output of the last full run is `results_ngspice42.txt` in each directory, and `/home/claude/behavior/tmp_R7A_runall.sh` re-runs all of them.

## 0. Reading guide

The 19 entries of this group are PACKAGES. A DIP-8, a SOIC-14 or a SOT-23-5 has no electrical behaviour by itself. What a user places on the board is "an 8-pin DIP", and the behaviour is whatever functional part the part binding puts in it. The deliverable therefore has two layers.

1. **BEH-IC-PKGBIND** (class 1): how a functional part is bound to a package. It defines the pin-number-to-function map convention (pin 1 first, counter-clockwise), the thermal resistance table by package with sources, the lead parasitics (inductance, capacitance) by package with sourced ranges, and the role of the package in power dissipation and in the absolute-maximum junction temperature check. It applies to all 19 entries.
2. **A researched reference set** of real, common parts that live in these packages (classes 2 to 12), each with a behaviour model and at least two validation benches. The per-entry sections (Part B) say which reference parts bind to which package and give the pin map in that package's terminal numbers.

| # | Class | Reference parts (datasheets actually opened) | Layer | Fidelity | Benches (matched / run) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | BEH-IC-PKGBIND | package binding, thermal, parasitics | L1 | behavioural_approximation | 3 / 3 |
| 2 | BEH-IC-OPAMP | LM358 (DIP-8/SOIC-8/TSSOP-8/MSOP-8), LM324 (DIP-14/SOIC-14/TSSOP-14), TLV9061 and MCP6001 (SOT-23-5) | L1 | behavioural_approximation | 5 / 5 |
| 3 | BEH-IC-COMPARATOR | LM393 | L1 | behavioural_approximation | 3 / 3 |
| 4 | BEH-IC-TIMER555 | NE555 | L1 (behavioural latch) | behavioural_approximation | 5 / 5 (one with a documented 3 % formula difference, explained) |
| 5 | BEH-IC-LOGIC-HC | 74HC00, 74HC04-class inverter, 74HC14 Schmitt, 74HC245 interface numbers | L2 | behavioural_approximation | 5 / 5 |
| 6 | BEH-IC-LOGIC-SEQ | 74HC595, 74HC138 | L2 (XSPICE) | behavioural_approximation | 2 / 2 |
| 7 | BEH-IC-DIGITAL-IO | ATmega328P (DIP-28), ATtiny85 (DIP-8), 25LC256 (DIP-8/SOIC-8), W65C02S (DIP-40) | L2 pad model, L3 firmware/protocol | behavioural_approximation (pad only) | 2 / 2 |
| 8 | BEH-IC-LDO-SOT235 | TLV70033 (TLV700 family) | L1 | behavioural_approximation | 5 / 5 |
| 9 | BEH-IC-CHARGER-SOT235 | MCP73831 | L1 | behavioural_approximation | 3 / 3 (parameters partly ASSUMED) |
| 10 | BEH-IC-DRIVER-DIP16 | ULN2003A, L293D | L1 | behavioural_approximation | 3 / 4 (B2 is a self-consistency run that missed its rough hand estimate; explained in 10.10) |
| 11 | BEH-IC-RS232-DIP16 | MAX232 | L1 | behavioural_approximation | 3 / 3 |
| 12 | BEH-IC-OPTO-DIP6 | 4N35 | L1 | behavioural_approximation | 2 / 2 |

Layer decisions: classes 1 to 4, 8 to 12 are L1 (analog), classes 5 and 6 are L2 (logic levels, thresholds, delay, supply current vs frequency), class 7 is an L2 pad model plus an explicit L3 requirement (nothing about firmware, SPI command execution or EEPROM contents is simulated). Class 6 needs XSPICE (`adc_bridge`, `dac_bridge`, `d_dff`, `d_inverter`); every other class runs on the stock B-source/T-line/diode/switch primitives. The existing runner `src/ohmni/eda/simulation.py` labels a deck `behavioural_approximation` if it contains `.model`, `.subckt`, `.include` or `.lib`, otherwise `ideal_components`; it never emits `vendor_model` and neither does anything in this file.

### Honesty notes that apply to the whole file

1. The page-fetch tool returns a model-written extract of each PDF, not the raw PDF. Tables are usually right, but I found concrete extraction errors, listed here so nobody trusts them silently. (a) LM358 `VIO` shows "3 / 7" in min/typ columns; it is typical 3 mV, maximum 7 mV (my reading, labelled MEDIUM). (b) SN74HC00 input leakage shows "+-100 uA / +-1000 uA", which is a units error (nA); ICC "2 .. 20 uA" mixes the 25 C and full-temperature columns. (c) The ULN2003A extract's input-current rows (0.35 to 0.5 mA at 5 V) are consistent with the 10.5 k ULN2004A input, not the 2.7 k ULN2003A. (d) The MCP73831 SparkFun mirror extract printed pin 4 as "NC"; the repo annotation transcribed from DS20001984H page 11 says VDD, and I use that. (e) The W65C02S pin table has duplicated pin names (D4, D5 twice, RESB at pin 1), so it was NOT used for a pin map. (f) The MCP6001 SOT-23-5 pin order differs between three mirror extracts (details in class 2), so it is marked UNVERIFIED. (g) Two Vishay 4N35 copies disagree on pins 5 and 6 and on minimum CTR (details in class 12). (h) The AN-1205 package R/L/C table lost column alignment in the extract (details in class 1).
2. No vendor SPICE model was opened or attached anywhere. Every model is `behavioural_approximation`. Many "datasheet fits" calibrate a model to a typical value and then a bench reproduces that value; such benches prove the netlist implements the intent, not that the model is physically right, and they are labelled "calibration check" below.
3. Where a number came only from my own engineering knowledge it is labelled ASSUMPTION with confidence L. Typical values were taken only from documents I opened.
4. Microchip pages (ww1.microchip.com, microchip.com) refused the fetch tool (robots.txt). Microchip numbers therefore come from third-party mirrors of the same datasheets (SparkFun, radiolocman, ciiva, alldatasheet, upenn, components.ru, colorado.edu, soselectronic) and from the repo's own transcription. Mirrors are labelled as such in the source list.

# PART A. BEHAVIOR CLASSES

## 1. BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-IC-PKGBIND

### 1.1 Purpose and real-world use

An IC package does three jobs that matter to a simulator and a rules checker. It maps the die's bond pads to numbered leads in a fixed order, so the same function lands on different pin numbers in different packages. It is the thermal path from the junction to the board and air, which sets how much power the part may dissipate. And its leads add small series inductance, shunt capacitance and resistance that matter above a few MHz and for fast edges (ground bounce, supply-pin resonance, input loading). A "DIP-8 IC" in the OHMNI inventory is therefore a footprint plus a binding: a list of terminal numbers and the functional part (or the pin-function map of a family) assigned to them.

Typical uses: choosing between a through-hole DIP for prototyping and an SMD SOIC/TSSOP/SSOP/MSOP/SOT-23 for production; checking that power dissipated in an LDO, a Darlington array, a motor driver or an MCU stays below the junction limit in that package; estimating supply-pin and ground-pin inductance when many outputs switch.

### 1.2 What it is and how it works

Construction. A plastic dual-in-line package (DIP, JEDEC MS-001 narrow 7.62 mm row spacing for 6/8/14/16/20 pins, MS-011 wide 15.24 mm for 28/40) or a gull-wing SMD package (SOIC MS-012 narrow 3.9 mm body for 8/14/16 pins and MS-013 wide 7.5 mm body for 20 pins; TSSOP MO-153; SSOP MO-150/MO-137; MSOP MO-187; SOT-23-5/6 MO-178) holds a die on a copper lead frame. Gold or copper bond wires connect die pads to the inner ends of the leads. The geometry is in the 3D spec (OHM-103 to OHM-121); this class does not repeat dimensions.

Pin-number convention (all 19 entries, per the 3D spec "Orientation Markings"). Pin 1 is at the top-left at rotation 0 for dual-row packages (DIP and SO families), numbering runs counter-clockwise seen from the top: down the left row (pins 1..N/2), then up the right row (N/2+1..N). So pin N is at the top-right and the function of pin k and pin N+1-k are opposite each other. For SOT-23-5/6 pin 1 is the bottom-left lead, pins 1, 2, 3 run left to right along the bottom, then the remaining leads go right to left along the top (SOT-23-5: pin 4 top-right, pin 5 top-left, no lead at top-centre; SOT-23-6: pin 4 top-right, 5 top-centre, 6 top-left). Pin 1 is marked by a notch/dimple (DIP, SO) or by the lead position under upright text (SOT-23). Verified against datasheet pin tables for every reference part below; the 3D spec numbering agrees with every datasheet table I could read.

Electrical effect of the package.

* Series lead inductance L_p and resistance R_p, shunt capacitance C_p per pin to the board ground plane (AN-1205 assumes the plane 0.5 mm below the seating plane). Resonance of the lead with the pad plus load capacitance: f0 = 1/(2 pi sqrt(L C)). Ground bounce: V = L_g N dI/dt for N outputs switching through one ground lead.
* Thermal path. Steady state: Tj = Ta + P theta_JA (SPRA953 defines theta_JA, notes it is board dependent and "the most often misused" metric; JEDEC high-K 2s2p and low-K 1s boards differ by about 50 %; 70 to 95 % of the heat leaves through the board, not the package surface). For a more accurate estimate from a measured board or case temperature: Tj = T_board + P psi_JB or Tj = T_case + P psi_JT. Transient: a Foster network of R-C stages (see R6 BEH-PWR-PKGTHERMAL, which this class re-uses; its bench B1 proves the network).
* The maximum power in a package is Pmax = (Tjmax - Ta)/theta_JA with Tjmax = 150 C for every reference part opened here (TI abs-max "operating junction temperature 150 C" in NE555, LM358, LM393, 74HC, ULN2003A, L293D, MAX232, TLV9061; Microchip MCP6001/MCP1700 extracts 150 C).

### 1.3 How it connects

A package binding is a table: terminal number -> {function name, electrical_type, net role, absolute-maximum relative to a supply pin}. For the reference parts below the binding is given verbatim in Part B. Common mistakes: reading a pin map from a different package of the same part (the MCP73831 DFN and SOT-23-5 numbers differ; the MCP1700 SOT-23A, SOT-89 and TO-92 orders differ), assuming dual op-amps and comparators put V- on the same pin in every part (LM358 V- is pin 4; MCP6002 differs), mounting a DIP rotated by 180 degrees (VCC and GND swap places), floating unused CMOS inputs, forgetting that SOT-23-5 LDOs do not all share one order (TLV700 IN-GND-EN-NC-OUT versus MCP73831 STAT-VSS-VBAT-VDD-PROG).

### 1.4 Electrical model for simulation

Layer L1. Fidelity: `behavioural_approximation` for the typical-value parasitics and thermal defaults (nothing here is a vendor model); the thermal and RLC networks use only R, L, C, I, V primitives and no `.model`, so the existing runner would label a deck containing only them `ideal_components`: a deck must also carry the part's `.subckt` to be labelled correctly.

Pin parasitic network per signal pin (placed between the package terminal and the die pad node of the part's subcircuit):

```
* pin k of package, die node = {k}_die
R{ref}_p{k} {k}_term {k}_x {Rp}
L{ref}_p{k} {k}_x {k}_die {Lp}
C{ref}_p{k} {k}_die 0 {Cp}
```

Ideal mode: Rp = 0, Lp = 0 (a tiny 1 pH keeps matrix solvable if needed), Cp = 0. Realistic mode: values from the table in 1.5, applied to every pin including supply and ground pins (GND lead inductance produces the bounce of bench B3).

Thermal network (one per instance, node `tj`):

```
Ipd 0 tj {P_W}          ; 1 W = 1 A
Rth tj tamb {theta_JA}  ; 1 degC = 1 V
Cth tj tamb {C_th}      ; optional, ASSUMPTION; C_th unknown, 1e-3 .. 0.1 J/K per package
Vta tamb 0 {Ta}
```

with the power injected by the part's own behavioural model (sum over supply pins of V*I minus power delivered to the load). Valid analyses: op, dc, tran (thermal and RLC), ac (RLC). Valid range: Ta -40 to 125 C, board-dependent theta; parasitics meaningful below roughly 1 GHz.

Known limitations: theta_JA depends on the test board, copper area, airflow and neighbouring heat sources; the table below is a spread across different dies in the same package, not a package property (SOIC-8 124.7 to 148.5 C/W across three parts). Lead R/L/C values are typical ranges for lead-frame packages from one 2004 application note and cover only some package types; SOT-23 has no sourced value. No thermal coupling between devices. Parasitics are lumped; mutual coupling between adjacent leads (M, CM in AN-1205) is not modelled.

### 1.6 Ratings and limits

| Quantity | Value | Condition | Check expression |
|---|---|---|---|
| Max junction temperature | 150 C | TI abs-max for all opened TI parts; Microchip extracts 150 C | `Tj = Ta + P*theta_JA <= 150` |
| Max package power | (150 - Ta)/theta_JA | table in 1.5 | `P_total = sum(Vsupply*Isupply) - P_load <= (Tjmax-Ta)/theta_JA` |
| Recommended Tj for reliability | no sourced value | | simulators should WARN above 125 C (ASSUMPTION) |
| Storage temperature | -65 to 150 C | TI parts | static |

Derating rule: linear, `Pmax(Ta) = Pmax(25)*(Tjmax-Ta)/(Tjmax-25)`. When a part model supplies its own theta (thermal pad, heat-spreading ground pins like L293D) it overrides the package default. Total package power includes quiescent supply power (VCC*ICC) and load-dependent power; for logic add `Cpd*Vcc^2*f` summed over outputs.

### 1.7 Failure and misuse behavior

| Event | Physical effect | Simulator response | Permanence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tj > 150 C (Pd beyond Pmax) | accelerated wear-out, parametric drift; plastic and bond-wire damage if sustained far above; part-specific thermal shutdown only if the die has it (TLV700 about 160 C, MCP73831 150 C extract) | FLAG error when Tj > Tjmax; if the part model has a thermal limiter use it, else keep the simulation running but mark the part "overheated" | permanent if exceeded for long, recoverable for brief excursions |
| Reversed orientation (DIP/SO rotated 180 deg) | supply and ground at the wrong pins, ESD diodes forward biased, destruction | design-rule error: pin 1 marker versus footprint pin 1 | permanent |
| Missing bypass capacitor with large lead L | supply droop, ringing | WARN in realistic mode if L_p*dI/dt exceeds 10 % of Vcc | recoverable |
| Pin capacitance on high-impedance nodes | input loading | included via C_p and the part's own Cin | n/a |
| Mechanical (SMD reflow, DIP lead bend) | outside electrical model | none | n/a |

### 1.8 Thermal behaviour

See 1.2 and 1.4. The thermal network is a single-pole R-C per package with a DC solution Tj = Ta + P theta_JA (bench B2). For fast pulses use the Foster extension from R6 (BEH-PWR-PKGTHERMAL). Spread warning: because the table is a spread over different dies, the simulator should use the datasheet theta of the bound part when available and the package default only otherwise; use the range ends for a worst-case warning.

### 1.9 Appearance summary

DIP entries are long black blocks on two rows of 2.54 mm-pitch through-hole leads (narrow 7.62 mm or wide 15.24 mm row spacing) with an end notch and a pin-1 dimple. SO-family entries are small black bodies with gull-wing leads on both long sides and a round pin-1 dimple; SOT-23-5/6 are 2.9 x 1.6 mm bodies with three leads along one edge. See OHM-103 to OHM-121 in the 3D spec.

  valid_analyses: [op, dc, ac, tran]

  - {name: max package power, symbol: Pmax, value: "(150-Ta)/theta_ja", unit: W, condition: "table 1.5", check: "P_total <= (150-Ta)/theta_ja", source_ref: S27}

  - {id: reversed_orientation, trigger: "pin 1 marker not at footprint pin 1", effect: "supplies on wrong pins", sim_response: "design-rule error", permanence: permanent}

  - {id: B3, file: bench/ic-pkgbind/B3_ground_bounce.cir, expected: [{measure: V bounce, value: "32.0/12.8 mV", tolerance: "1 %", basis: "L dI/dt"}], measured_in_ngspice: "32.0/12.8 mV", ngspice_version: "42"}

Unresolved: theta_JA for DIP-6, DIP-28, DIP-40; any sourced lead L/C for SOIC-8/14/16, TSSOP, MSOP, SOT-23 specifically (only SSOP-28 and Mini SOIC-8 rows); psi_JT, psi_JB values; JESD51 board definitions (read only via SPRA953); transient Zth curves.

## 2. BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-IC-OPAMP

### 2.1 Purpose and real-world use

An operational amplifier is a high-gain differential voltage amplifier used in feedback to build amplifiers, filters, buffers, integrators, level shifters and active rectifiers. Reference parts: LM358 (dual) and LM324 (quad) are the classic low-cost single-supply bipolar parts (3 to 30 V supply, input range includes ground, output swings to ground but only to about V+ - 1.5 V at the top); MCP6001 (single, 1.8 to 5.5 V, 1 MHz, rail-to-rail input and output) and TLV9061 (single, 1.8 to 5.5 V, 10 MHz, rail-to-rail) are the SOT-23-5 CMOS examples. Typical applications: sensor signal conditioning, ADC drivers, voltage followers, current-sense amplifiers, active filters, simple oscillators.

### 2.2 What it is and how it works

A differential input stage drives a high-impedance gain node that sets the open-loop gain Aol and, with the internal compensation capacitor, a single dominant pole at f_p = GBW/Aol. Beyond f_p the gain falls at 20 dB/decade until it reaches 1 at the gain-bandwidth product GBW. In a feedback amplifier with feedback factor beta the closed-loop bandwidth is about GBW*beta (single-pole approximation) and the closed-loop gain error is 1/(1+Aol beta). The compensation capacitor charged by the input-stage tail current limits the output slew rate: SR = I_tail/C_c (bench B2). The output stage is a push-pull or class-A/AB follower that cannot reach the rails: LM358 top swing V+ - 1.5 V (the extract's output-high rail row is "1.5" with a V+ reference, interpreted as dropout; HIGH confidence that it is a dropout figure, MEDIUM on exact load condition), bottom swing about 20 mV max at 5 V with 10 k load (the NPN sinks to the negative rail). MCP6001 and TLV9061 outputs get within about 25 mV and 20 mV of the rails at 10 k. Input stage: PNP pair for LM358 so the bias current flows OUT of the pins (extract shows negative input bias, -20 nA typical, -250 nA maximum) and common-mode range includes V-; CMOS parts have pA bias.

Key equations: closed-loop f_-3dB ~ GBW/G (noninverting gain G, single pole); SR = dV/dt max; Vout = Aol (V+ - V-) between the rails; full-power bandwidth = SR/(2 pi Vpeak).

### 2.3 How it connects

Pins (package terminal numbers in Part B): non-inverting input IN+, inverting input IN-, output OUT, positive supply V+, negative supply V- (ground in single-supply use). Duals and quads repeat the three signal pins per amplifier and share V+/V-. Typical circuits: buffer, inverting and non-inverting amplifier, difference amplifier. Mistakes: exceeding the input common-mode range (LM358 top is V+ - 1.5 V, so a 5 V follower cannot track 4 V), driving a capacitive load without an isolation resistor, using an LM358 as a rail-to-rail part, floating unused channels of a dual or quad (tie IN+ to a safe voltage and make it a follower), exceeding the supply limits of the specific variant (LM358 32 V, LM358B 40 V, MCP6001 7 V), assuming an op-amp can be used as a comparator without hysteresis.

### 2.4 Electrical model for simulation

Layer L1. ngspice primitives: R, C, B (behavioural V and I sources), V, I. Fidelity: `behavioural_approximation`. No vendor SPICE file was opened. File: `bench/ic-opamp/opamp_gp.lib`.

Structure: input offset source in series with IN+ (`vos`), input bias current sources from V+ into each input (`ib +- ios/2`), differential resistance `rid` and per-input capacitance `cin`; a transconductance stage `gm = 2 pi GBW C1` (C1 = 1 nF internal choice) with a tanh limit `Imax = SR*C1` (gives slew limiting), into a node with `R1 = Aol/gm` and `C1`; a smooth switch-off of the gm current once the node passes the rails +-0.5 V (prevents wind-up and gives fast saturation recovery); an output clamp to `[V- + vol, V+ - vdrop]` followed by `rout`; a constant supply current `iq`; the load current sourced by the output is drawn from V+ (bench B5).

Netlist template (call):

```
X{ref} {INP} {INM} {VPLUS} {VMINUS} {OUT} opamp_gp aol={aol} gbw={gbw} sr={sr} vos={vos} ib={ib} ios={ios} vol={vol} vdrop={vdrop} rout={rout} iq={iq} cin={cin} rid={rid}
```

Parameter-to-datasheet mapping and per-part sets:

| Parameter | meaning | LM358 (S2) | LM324 (S9) | MCP6001 (S18) | TLV9061 (S11) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| aol | open-loop gain V/V | 100e3 (100 V/mV typ) | 100e3 (assumed same die class, L) | 398e3 (112 dB) | 316e3 (datasheet 104..130 dB: 110 dB used, L) |
| gbw | Hz | 0.7e6 (typ) | 1.0e6 (ASSUMPTION L, not in opened extract; extract only gives 4-amp Icc) | 1.0e6 | 10e6 |
| sr | V/s | 0.3e6 | 0.3e6 (ASSUMPTION L) | 0.6e6 | 6.5e6 |
| vos | V | 3e-3 typ (7 mV max, M) | 3e-3 (L) | 1e-3 ASSUMED typ (max 4.5 mV or 7 mV, mirrors disagree) | 0.3e-3 typ (2 mV max) |
| ib | A (out of pin) | 20e-9 (250 nA max) | 20e-9 (L) | 1e-12 | 0.5e-12 |
| ios | A | 2e-9 typ (50 nA max, M) | 2e-9 (L) | 0 | 0 |
| vol | V above V- | 5e-3 typ (20 mV max) | 5e-3 | 25e-3 (mirror swing) | 20e-3 |
| vdrop | V below V+ | 1.5 | 1.5 | 25e-3 | 20e-3 |
| rout | ohm | 50 (ASSUMPTION L: not in opened extracts) | 50 | 100 (ASSUMPTION L) | 50 (L) |
| iq | A per package | 350e-6 typ (dual, M; max 600 uA) | 0.7e-3 (4 amps at 5 V, typ, S9) | 100e-6 | 538e-6 |
| cin, rid | | 2 pF, 2 Meg (ASSUMPTION L) | same | same | same |

Ideal mode: ib = ios = vos = 0, rout = 1 m, vol = vdrop = 0, aol 1e9, gbw 1e12, sr 1e12. Realistic mode: the set above. Temperature and noise are not modelled. Valid analyses: op, dc, ac, tran. Valid range: supply within the part's recommended range (LM358 3 to 30 V; MCP6001 1.8 to 5.5 V; TLV9061 1.8 to 5.5 V), input common mode inside the stated range.

Known limitations (where the model is wrong): single dominant pole, so phase margin is about 90 degrees (MCP6001 extract says 90 degrees typical, TLV9061 55 degrees typical: its capacitive-load peaking is NOT reproduced); no second pole or output impedance vs frequency; no input-stage phase reversal or crossover distortion; open-loop output resistance is an assumption; Aol, GBW and SR do not vary with supply, temperature or load; no CMRR or PSRR (a DC-offset term could be added from CMRR 80 dB LM358 and 76 dB MCP6001); no noise; the constant `iq` does not rise with load or output state; input protection diodes and abs-max are checked outside the netlist.

Check expressions (evaluated by the simulator each timestep or at the operating point):
`V(V+)-V(V-) <= Vsupply_max`; `abs(V(IN+)-V(IN-)) <= Vdiff_max`; `V(IN) >= V(V-)-0.3 and V(IN) <= Vinmax`; `abs(I(OUT)) <= Isc`; `Tj = Ta + P*theta_ja <= 150` with `P = Iq*Vs + (V+ - Vout)*Iout_source + (Vout - V-)*Iout_sink`.

Derating: output current beyond +-20 mA at 15 V reduces swing (LM358 min source 20 mA, min sink 10 mA); no sourced temperature derating of GBW or Aol.

### 2.7 Failure and misuse behavior

| Event | Physical result | Simulator response | Permanence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Supply above abs max | breakdown of the process, destroyed | ERROR at the first violation, mark part failed (outputs open) | permanent |
| Supply reversed | substrate diode conducts, large current | ERROR; model keeps working only if the netlist includes a reverse diode (not modelled) | permanent |
| Input below V- by more than 0.3 V (LM358) or beyond VSS-1.0/VDD+1.0 (MCP6001) | ESD or parasitic diode conducts, possible latch or output inversion | WARN; clamp the input with a diode network if current exceeds 1 mA | recoverable if current limited, else permanent |
| Input beyond recommended common mode | gain collapse, output stuck, LM358 top: output cannot follow above V+ - 1.5 V | model clamps via the output limits, WARN on CM violation (`V(IN) > V+ - 1.5`) | recoverable |
| Output shorted to a rail | current limit about +-40..60 mA (LM358) heats the part | WARN when |I(OUT)| > Isc; if sustained compute Tj via theta | recoverable unless Tj > 150 C |
| Capacitive load | peaking or oscillation | not modelled; warn when CL > 100 pF with unity gain | recoverable |
| Overpower (Pd > Pmax of package) | thermal damage | FLAG using BEH-IC-PKGBIND | permanent |

### 2.8 Thermal behaviour

Pd = (V+ - V-)*Iq + output stage losses; Tj = Ta + Pd*theta_JA (Part B gives theta per package: LM358 DIP-8 80.9, SOIC-8 124.7, TSSOP-8 171.7, VSSOP-8 181.4 C/W; LM324 DIP-14 83.5, SOIC-14 99.3, TSSOP-14 124.7; TLV9061 DBV 221.7; MCP6001 SOT-23-5 256 (mirror)). Example: LM358 at 30 V, 0.6 mA max plus a sourcing load 10 mA with 5 V drop: Pd = 0.018 + 0.05 = 0.068 W, Tj rise 8.5 K in SOIC-8, negligible; a 40 mA short at 30 V (1.2 W) would exceed the SOIC-8 limit (0.64 W at 70 C) within seconds.

### 2.9 Appearance summary

In DIP-8/DIP-14 these are black epoxy blocks with a semicircular notch; SOIC/TSSOP/MSOP versions are small black bodies with a dot at pin 1; the MCP6001 and TLV9061 are tiny SOT-23-5 bodies with the dot or lead 1 at bottom-left. Markings carry the part number (3D spec entries OHM-104, 105, 110, 111, 114, 115, 119, 120).

## 3. BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-IC-COMPARATOR

### 3.1 Purpose and real-world use

A comparator turns "which of two voltages is higher" into a logic level. The LM393 is a dual open-collector comparator used for threshold detection, window comparators, zero-crossing detectors, level shifting (the output pulls up to any supply up to 36 V), relaxation oscillators and wired-AND outputs (several open collectors on one pull-up).

### 3.2 What it is and how it works

A PNP-input differential stage drives a high-gain stage whose output is an open NPN collector to ground. When IN+ is above IN- (beyond the offset) the output transistor is off and the pull-up resistor takes the output high. When IN- is above IN+ the transistor saturates and sinks current; the saturation voltage rises with current. The input stage needs headroom, so the input common-mode range is 0 to VCC - 1.5 V (extract; recommended 0 to VCC - 2 V). Response time depends on overdrive: TI quotes 1.3 us for a 100 mV step with 5 mV overdrive and 0.3 us for a TTL-level step (typical, VCC = 5 V, RL = 5.1 k, CL = 15 pF). No internal hysteresis: add positive feedback for noisy inputs. The extract text says that inputs more than 0.3 V below the negative supply cause excessive input current and wrong output.

### 3.3 How it connects

Pins per channel: IN+, IN-, OUT; shared VCC and GND. OUT needs a pull-up resistor to the logic supply (common mistake: no pull-up, output never goes high; or a pull-up so small that IOL or the 20 mA limit is exceeded). Hysteresis: Rhys from OUT to IN+. Unused channel: tie IN- above IN+ range or both inputs to a defined level.

### 3.4 Electrical model for simulation

Layer L1. B sources, V, I, C, T line (transport delay). `behavioural_approximation`; file `bench/ic-comparator/lm393.lib`, subcircuit `comp_oc inp inm vcc gnd out`.

```
X{ref} {INP} {INM} {VCC} {GND} {OUT} comp_oc vos={vos} ib={ib} ios={ios} ron={ron} isat={isat} a={a} vs={vs} tau={tau} td={td} icc={icc} ioh={ioh}
```

Offset source in series with IN+, bias currents out of both inputs (PNP), a clipped gain `a*vd` charging a dominant-pole node (time constant `tau`, clamped to +-`vs`), a transport delay `td` through a matched T line, and an output sink `I = Isat*tanh(Vout/(Ron*Isat))` gated by a smooth switch. Output off-state leakage `ioh`.

Response calibration: crossing time t = td + tau*ln(1 + Vs/(A*vod)); with td = 0.3 us, tau = 1.44 us, A = 200, Vs = 1 V it gives 1.30 us at 5 mV overdrive and 0.30 us at TTL-level overdrive, matching the two TI typical points. Ron = 33 ohm from VOL = 130 mV (typical, extract) at 4 mA.

Ideal mode: vos = ib = ios = 0, td = tau = 0 (replace the delay path with a step), ron = 1 m, ioh = 0. Valid analyses: op, dc (static only: dynamics behave as an integrator), tran. The op solve of this model prints gmin/source-stepping warnings in ngspice 42 for some netlists but converges (B1b); see limitation list.

Known limitations: a single delay law calibrated at two points; output rise is set by the external RC only; no input protection model; no hysteresis; no CMRR/PSRR; no temperature dependence; output sink current is a smooth tanh so the stated VOL min/max band is not reproduced separately; the model accepts input common-mode violations without erroneous output (the simulator must warn instead).

### 3.7 Failure and misuse behavior

| Event | Result | Simulator | Permanence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Output sink current above 20 mA | overheating, bond wire stress | WARN above 16 mA, ERROR above 20 mA, clamp not applied (the real part keeps conducting) | permanent if sustained |
| Output pulled above 36 V | collector breakdown | ERROR | permanent |
| Input below GND by > 0.3 V | input current, incorrect output | WARN, output state undefined flag | recoverable |
| Input above VCC-1.5 V | input stage loses headroom, output unpredictable | WARN (CM violation) | recoverable |
| No pull-up | OUT floats | netlist check "open-collector output has no pull-up" | n/a |
| Reversed supply | destroyed | ERROR | permanent |

### 3.8 Thermal behaviour

Pd = VCC*ICC + VOL*IOL for each saturated channel. Packages (theta): PDIP-8 114.9, SOIC-8 148.5, TSSOP-8 200.6, VSSOP-8 193.7, SOT-23-8 197.9, WSON-8 96.9 C/W (TI extract). Example: 2 channels each sinking 20 mA at 0.4 V plus 5 V*1 mA = 0.021 W, negligible. The package limit matters only at VCC 30 V and high ICC.

### 3.9 Appearance summary

Standard 8-pin dual-in-line or SO-8 body (OHM-104 DIP-8, OHM-110 SOIC-8, OHM-114 TSSOP-8, OHM-119 MSOP-8), pin 1 at the dot or notch; the same footprints as LM358 and NE555.

| B2_response | falling output, RL 5.1 k, CL 15 pF; 5 mV and TTL-level overdrive | td + tau ln(1+Vs/(A vod)): 1.30 us and ~0.31 us (TI typ 1.3 and 0.3 us) | 5 % | 1.3004 us and 0.3169 us (calibration check) |

All 3 match. B2 is a calibration check of the two TI typical points.

## 4. BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-IC-TIMER555

### 4.1 Purpose and real-world use

The 555 timer produces precisely timed pulses (monostable) or a free-running square-ish wave (astable) from one resistor and one capacitor, and also serves as a Schmitt trigger, a PWM generator, a debouncer and a missing-pulse detector. NE555 (0 to 70 C), SA555, SE555 and CMOS variants exist; here the bipolar NE555 as documented by TI (SLFS022K). Packages: PDIP-8 (OHM-104), SOIC-8 (OHM-110), SO-8 PS, TSSOP-8 (OHM-114).

### 4.2 What it is and how it works

A resistor divider of three 5 k resistors from VCC sets reference levels at 2/3 VCC and 1/3 VCC. The THRESHOLD comparator trips when THRES exceeds the CONT voltage (2/3 VCC with CONT open); the TRIGGER comparator trips when TRIG falls below half of CONT (1/3 VCC). They drive an SR flip-flop whose output (reset dominant) drives the OUT stage and the base of the DISCHARGE transistor, an open-collector NPN to ground that is on when the output is low. RESET (active low) forces output low and discharges.

Astable (TRIG and THRES tied to the capacitor, R1 from VCC to DISCH, R2 from DISCH to the capacitor): charge through R1+R2 from VCC/3 to 2VCC/3: tH = (R1+R2) C ln 2 = 0.693 (R1+R2) C; discharge through R2 into the transistor: tL = 0.693 R2 C. Period T = 0.693 (R1+2R2) C, f = 1.44/((R1+2R2)C), duty (R1+R2)/(R1+2R2) (TI formulas, S1). Monostable: width t = R C ln 3 = 1.0986 R C (TI quotes 1.1 RC). With CONT forced to Vc: thresholds Vc and Vc/2, monostable width t = R C ln(VCC/(VCC - Vc)). Real deviations: comparator input currents, the saturation of the discharge transistor, ln(2) rather than 0.693 (0.01 % effect), supply sensitivity 0.3 %/V astable, temperature coefficient 150 ppm/C astable and 50 ppm/C monostable (TI typical).

### 4.3 How it connects

Pins (package order 1..8): GND, TRIG, OUT, RESET, CONT, THRES, DISCH, VCC (TI, same for D, P, PS, PW). Typical circuits: astable (R1, R2, C plus 10 nF on CONT recommended in practice), monostable (R, C, trigger pulse low), PWM with CONT modulated. Mistakes: leaving RESET floating, trigger pulse longer than the output pulse in monostable mode, R1 too small (discharge transistor current limit, VCE(sat), duty cannot go below 50 %), forgetting that R1 below about 1 k makes tL longer than 0.693 R2 C (see B1), supply below 4.5 V on the bipolar NE555.

### 4.4 Electrical model for simulation

Layer L1 with a behavioural latch (no XSPICE). File `bench/ic-timer555/ne555.lib`, subckt `ne555 gnd trig out rst cont thr dis vcc` (pins in package order).

Elements: three 5 k resistors; threshold and trigger decisions as 1 mV tanh B sources on `v(cont)` and `v(cont)/2`; SR latch as `C=1F` node with `I = k*(set*(1-reset)*(1-q) - reset*q)`, k = 1e8 (reset dominant; RESET asserted below 0.7 V, ASSUMED); output Thevenin source `Vcc - voh0` behind `rout`; discharge as a voltage-controlled switch with `ron`, `roff = 100 Meg`; THRES input current 100 nA sinking, TRIG input current 500 nA sourcing; supply current `icc0 + icck*(Vcc-5)`.

Fit of the output stage to TI (S1) at 25 C, NE555: VOH(-100 mA) = 13.3 V typical at 15 V and 12.5 V minimum at -200 mA give R = 8 ohm and an unloaded drop 0.9 V (check 5 V: 5 - 0.9 - 0.8 = 3.3 V, TI typical 3.3 V). VOL(10 mA) 0.1 V typ, VOL(50 mA) 0.4 V typ both give about 8 to 10 ohm; at 100 mA TI gives 2.0 to 2.5 V because the sink saturates, which this linear fit does NOT reproduce (model gives 0.8 V): limitation. Discharge ron = 30 ohm from VCE(sat) 0.15 to 0.4 V at 8 mA (mid 0.25 V); at the small currents of a timing network the real saturation voltage is lower, so ron over-estimates tL when R1 is a few kohm (bench B1).

Parameters: `rdiv=5k voh0=0.9 rout=8 ron=30 ithr=100n itrg=500n klatch=1e8 rstth=0.7 icc0=2m icck=0.7m`.

Ideal mode: ron = 0, rout = 0, voh0 = 0, ithr = itrg = 0, icc0 = 0. Valid analyses: tran (needs `uic` for the free-running case), op for static levels. Valid range: VCC 4.5 to 16 V, output |I| <= 200 mA, f up to about 500 kHz (not specified in the extract; model has no explicit f limit; the real NE555 astable is limited by the comparator and discharge delays, ASSUMPTION).

Known limitations: no propagation delay between trigger and output (a few tens of ns real), no supply-current spikes during output transitions (real 555 draws a current spike at switching), no temperature or supply dependence of timing, symmetrical thresholds exactly 1/3 and 2/3 (TI gives THRES 3.3 V typ at 5 V and 10 V typ at 15 V, 2.4..4.2 V and 8.8..11.2 V over the unit range, so +-15 % unit-to-unit spread of the tap is NOT modelled; ratiometric spread is a Monte Carlo item), VOL at high current wrong (above).

### 4.7 Failure and misuse behavior

| Event | Result | Simulator | Permanence |
|---|---|---|---|
| VCC > 18 V | destroyed | ERROR | permanent |
| Output current > 225 mA (short to a rail) | overheating | ERROR above 225 mA; the model's 8 ohm resistive output limits at 15 V to ~1.9 A, so the simulator must flag, not rely on the model | permanent if sustained |
| Pin above VCC or below GND | ESD structure conducts | WARN | recoverable |
| RESET floating | random resets | netlist check for floating input | n/a |
| Missing timing capacitor | oscillation at parasitic C | none | n/a |
| Discharge pin shorted to VCC | discharge transistor overloaded | WARN if I(DISCH) exceeds 200 mA (ASSUMPTION; no TI figure in the extract) | permanent |

### 4.8 Thermal behaviour

Pd = VCC*ICC + output losses; see the table above and BEH-IC-PKGBIND. The NE555 has no thermal protection.

### 4.9 Appearance summary

Eight-lead package (OHM-104 DIP-8 black body with notch, OHM-110 SOIC-8, OHM-114 TSSOP-8), pin 1 at the dot, marked NE555 plus the manufacturer logo.

## 5. BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-IC-LOGIC-HC

### 5.1 Purpose and real-world use

High-speed CMOS (HC) logic gates are the glue of digital boards: inverters (74HC04), NAND gates (74HC00), Schmitt-trigger inverters (74HC14, used for switch debouncing, RC oscillators and cleaning slow edges) and bus transceivers (74HC245). They run from 2 to 6 V, drive about 4 mA at 4.5 V per output with TTL-compatible loading, and draw almost no static current. Packages here: DIP-14 (OHM-105), SOIC-14 (OHM-111), TSSOP-14 (OHM-115) for HC00, HC04, HC14; DIP-20 (OHM-107), SOIC-20 wide (OHM-113), TSSOP-20 (OHM-117) for HC245.

### 5.2 What it is and how it works

Each gate is a complementary MOS pair per input. The output is pulled to VCC through a PMOS network or to GND through an NMOS network, so the output impedance is tens of ohms and the static supply current is the leakage of the junctions (microamps). Input switching threshold is near VCC/2 (HC; the HCT family shifts it to TTL levels). The Schmitt trigger (HC14) adds positive feedback inside the input stage so the rising threshold VT+ is above the falling threshold VT-; hysteresis 0.9 V typical at 4.5 V. Dynamic supply current: each output transition charges and discharges the internal and load capacitance, giving average ICC = ICC0 + (Cpd + CL) VCC f per switching output (Cpd is the TI "power dissipation capacitance": 20 pF in the HC00 extract (stated for the device, no load; the model applies it per switching output), 85 pF HC138, 40 pF HC245, 400 pF HC595). Propagation delay tpd is dominated by output resistance times load: TI typical 18 ns at 4.5 V, CL = 50 pF for the HC00 (HC00 extract: 90 ns typ at 2 V, 18 ns at 4.5 V, 15 ns at 6 V; the HC14 extract gives 25 ns typ at 4.5 V because of its Schmitt input). Input ESD diodes to VCC and GND clamp overvoltage; they conduct for inputs beyond VCC + 0.5 V or below -0.5 V and absolute-maximum input clamp current is 20 mA.

### 5.3 How it connects

Every input must be driven (floating CMOS inputs oscillate, draw supply current and can latch); unused gate inputs go to GND or VCC, unused gates are tied to a defined state. Bypass 100 nF at the supply pins, close to pins 14 and 7. Output loading: keep to about 4 mA at 4.5 V for the specified levels (the loaded levels quoted here are at 4 mA); do not connect outputs together unless the device has tri-state. Mixed voltages: an HC input must not be driven above VCC + 0.5 V without a series resistor to limit the clamp current; the driven input of a 5 V HC part from a 3.3 V output needs VIH = 0.7 VCC = 3.15 V, which 3.3 V CMOS outputs do not guarantee (use HCT). Pin maps (package order): HC00: 1A 1B 1Y 2A 2B 2Y GND 3Y 3A 3B 4Y 4A 4B VCC. HC14 (and HC04): 1A 1Y 2A 2Y 3A 3Y GND 4Y 4A 5Y 5A 6Y 6A VCC. HC245: 1 DIR, 2..9 A1..A8, 10 GND, 11..18 B8..B1, 19 OE (active low), 20 VCC.

### 5.4 Electrical model for simulation

Layer L2 implemented with L1 primitives only (B sources, R, C, D, a lossless T line used as a pure delay), so stock ngspice 42 is enough and no XSPICE is needed. File `bench/ic-logic-hc/hc_gates.lib`: `hc_nand2 a b y vcc gnd`, `hc_inv a y vcc gnd`, `hc_inv_st a y vcc gnd` (Schmitt). Fidelity `behavioural_approximation`.

Structure of each cell: input capacitance `ci` (5 pF, ASSUMPTION M-L; datasheet CI 3..10 pF class), ESD clamp diodes to both rails (`.model dclamp d(is=1e-14 n=1 rs=5)`, ASSUMPTION; only the clamp-current/voltage circuit consistency was checked), decision at `vtfrac*VCC` with 50 mV tanh smoothing, logic value through a matched T line of delay `td` (10.4 ns), a single-pole edge shaper `taue` (6.4 ns), and one Thevenin output (`roh` 50 ohm, `rol` 65 ohm, blended with the logic level). The supply source takes only the positive part of the output current (no crowbar current, so Cpd is not counted twice) plus `icc0 + 0.5 Cpd VCC |d(logic)/dt|`, whose average is Cpd VCC f. Schmitt cell: hysteresis implemented in the decision with thresholds 2.5 V and 1.6 V at 4.5 V (TI typical, extract).

```
X{ref} {A} {B} {Y} {VCC} {GND} hc_nand2 vtfrac=0.5 roh=50 rol=65 td=10.4n taue=6.4n ci=5p cpd=20p icc0=2u
```

Parameter basis: roh/rol from VOH = 4.30 V at -4 mA and VOL = 0.26 V at +4 mA (typical, SCLS181H extract, VCC 4.5 V): 50 ohm and 65 ohm. td and taue tuned so that the inverter bench gives tpd = 18 ns and tt = 15 ns (TI typical at 4.5 V, CL 50 pF). This is calibration, not independent evidence (B2 comment). The ratio td/taue is a design choice (ASSUMPTION).

Ideal mode: roh = rol = 1 mohm, td = taue = 0 (use 1 ps), ci = 0, cpd = 0, no clamp diodes. Valid analyses: op (static truth table), tran. dc sweeps work for the Schmitt branch (history-dependent hysteresis is implemented as a smooth state with latch memory only in tran).

Known limitations: levels are scaled linearly with VCC (real roh/rol rise at lower VCC; delay law is not VCC-dependent unless parameters are re-fitted); one delay for both edges (the real tpLH and tpHL differ by a few ns); no input-threshold spread (VIH min 3.15 V, VIL max 1.35 V at 4.5 V as limits, typical threshold near VCC/2); no simultaneous-switching ground bounce unless the package parasitics from class 1 are bound; no meta-stable behaviour; no temperature dependence; at 2 V the HC family is slow and weak, not reproduced. 74HC245 tri-state and direction logic are documented in the L2 class 6 style (hcout with `en`) but not benched.

### 5.6 Ratings and limits

| Quantity | Value (TI HC family, extract) | Check |
|---|---|---|
| Supply voltage | -0.5..7 V abs max (HC00, HC14, HC138, HC595, HC245 extracts agree) | `V(VCC)-V(GND) <= 7` |
| Input voltage | -0.5..VCC+0.5 V | `V(in) <= V(VCC)+0.5 and V(in) >= V(GND)-0.5` |
| Input clamp current | +-20 mA | `abs(I(clamp_in)) <= 20e-3` |
| Output clamp current | +-20 mA | `abs(I(clamp_out)) <= 20e-3` |
| Continuous output current | +-25 mA per output (HC00, HC14, HC138); +-35 mA (HC595, HC245) | `abs(I(out)) <= 25e-3` |
| Continuous ICC / GND current | +-50 mA (HC00, HC14, HC138); +-70 mA (HC595, HC245) | `I(VCC) <= 50e-3` |
| Recommended VCC | 2..6 V | warn outside |
| Junction | 150 C | `Tj = Ta+P*theta_JA <= 150` |

Check expression for dynamic power: `P = VCC*(ICC0 + sum_k (Cpd + CL_k) VCC f_k) + sum_k Iout_k^2 Ro` (the last term is the output-stage loss).

### 5.7 Failure and misuse behavior

| Event | Result | Simulator | Permanence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Input above VCC+0.5 V (no series R) | ESD diode current, possible latch-up | clamp diodes conduct in the model; ERROR if I > 20 mA, WARN above 5 mA | permanent when sustained |
| Output shorted to rail | current limited only by the output resistance (about 90 mA at 4.5 V in the model), beyond 25 mA abs max | ERROR above 25 mA | permanent if sustained |
| Floating input | undefined level, shoot-through current, oscillation | netlist check: input net without driver or pull | recoverable |
| VCC > 7 V | oxide breakdown | ERROR | permanent |
| Reverse supply | ESD diodes conduct, destruction | ERROR | permanent |
| Slow input edge on HC (non-Schmitt) | output oscillates, excess ICC | WARN when input slew below about 500 ns/V (ASSUMPTION L; datasheet gives an input transition-time limit in the extract that was not read) | recoverable |

### 5.8 Thermal behaviour

Self-heating is dominated by dynamic power. Example: HC00 at 4.5 V, four gates at 1 MHz with 50 pF: P = 4.5 V x (4 x 70 pF x 4.5 V x 1 MHz) = 5.7 mW; DIP-14 (60.7 C/W) rises 0.34 K. Not a thermal concern except for a 245 driving large buses at high frequency. theta_JA per package from class 1.

### 5.9 Appearance summary

Standard black plastic DIP or SO bodies with a pin-1 notch or dot, marked 74HC00 or 74HC14 with the manufacturer logo (3D spec entries OHM-105, 107, 111, 113, 115, 117).

## 6. BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-IC-LOGIC-SEQ

### 6.1 Purpose and real-world use

Sequential and decoding logic that expands a few microcontroller pins into many: the 74HC595 (8-bit serial-in, parallel-out shift register with output latch and tri-state outputs: LED rows, relays, display segments) and the 74HC138 (3-to-8 line decoder/demultiplexer: chip selects, address decoding). Packages here: DIP-16 (OHM-106), SOIC-16 (OHM-112), TSSOP-16 (OHM-116), SSOP-16 (OHM-118).

### 6.2 What it is and how it works

HC595: SER data is clocked into an 8-stage shift register on the rising edge of SRCLK. A separate storage register copies the shift register on the rising edge of RCLK. SRCLR (active low) clears the shift register (asynchronously); OE (active low) enables the three-state outputs QA..QH; QH' is the unlatched serial output for cascading. The extracted datasheet gives a maximum clock frequency of 21 to 31 MHz at 4.5 V (SCLS041J extract). HC138: with G1 high and G2A, G2B low exactly one of Y0..Y7 goes low (active low), selected by C B A (A is the LSB); any enable inactive makes all outputs high. Outputs are CMOS-type totem pole with the same drive as the gates in class 5.

### 6.3 How it connects

HC595 package order: 1 QB, 2 QC, 3 QD, 4 QE, 5 QF, 6 QG, 7 QH, 8 GND, 9 QH', 10 SRCLR, 11 SRCLK, 12 RCLK, 13 OE, 14 SER, 15 QA, 16 VCC. Note that QA is on pin 15, not pin 1. Cascading: QH' of the first device to SER of the next, SRCLK and RCLK in common. Typical mistakes: SRCLR left floating, OE left floating (outputs random), assuming all 8 outputs can source the full 25 mA together (total VCC/GND current is limited to +-70 mA for the 595, not the 50 mA of the gates; SCLS041J extract), pulse the RCLK before the last SRCLK so that latched data is one bit short. HC138 package order: 1 A, 2 B, 3 C, 4 G2A, 5 G2B, 6 G1, 7 Y7, 8 GND, 9 Y6, 10 Y5, 11 Y4, 12 Y3, 13 Y2, 14 Y1, 15 Y0, 16 VCC. Tie unused enables to their active level.

### 6.4 Electrical model for simulation

Layer L2 with XSPICE digital primitives (needs XSPICE: ngspice 42 here is built with it; a build without XSPICE cannot run this class). File `bench/ic-logic-seq/hc_seq.lib`, subcircuits `hc595` and `hc138`, pin order = package pin order 1..16. Input conditioner `hcin` (5 pF, clamp diodes, normalised decision at VCC/2 through `adc_bridge`), digital core (`d_dff`, `d_inverter`, further XSPICE digital primitives where needed), output cell `hcout` (the class 5 delay/edge/Thevenin cell with a normalised enable `en` that blends to a high-impedance leakage `gz` = 1 nS at OE high). Delays: 12 ns flip-flop clock-to-Q (`clk_delay`), plus the `hcout` delay of 10.4 ns, giving RCLK-to-Q about 30 ns at 4.5 V. Supply current: `cpd` = 400 pF for the 595 (SCLS041J extract; stated for the whole device, no load) and static `icc0` = 8 uA.

Ideal mode: zero delays, roh = rol = 1 mohm. Valid analyses: tran only (the XSPICE core has no meaningful ac or dc). The decoder is combinational but still requires XSPICE for the same reason.

Known limitations: no setup/hold timing checks (the model samples at the clock edge; violation is not flagged), no metastability, no minimum pulse-width checks, SRCLR modelled as asynchronous reset only, a single tpd per path, undefined input (X) levels are not propagated (adc_bridge maps mid-rail to a defined level with a warning), the clock-to-Q numbers are not individually fitted to the datasheet tpd table.

### 6.7 Failure and misuse behavior

As class 5, plus: OE floating or high leaves outputs undefined (the model marks them Hi-Z with a 10 k divider in the bench); output sum above 70 mA overheats the bond wires (ERROR); clock above 21 MHz is a WARN (not a failure); data/clock edges violating setup are not modelled (flag RESEARCH_REQUIRED).

### 6.8 Thermal behaviour

P = VCC ICC + Cpd VCC^2 f + output losses. Example: 595 driving 8 LEDs at 5 mA, Vf 2 V from a 5 V part: output loss about 8 x 5 mA x 0.2 V = 8 mW; negligible against DIP-16 (60.6 C/W) 2 W. The TSSOP-16 limit (about 1.1 W at 25 C) is again far above the dissipation.

### 6.9 Appearance summary

16-pin dual-row bodies (OHM-106 DIP-16, 112 SOIC-16, 116 TSSOP-16, 118 SSOP-16), pin 1 at the notch, marked 74HC595 or 74HC138.

| B2_hc138 | address 0..7, G1 = 1, G2A = G2B = 0; then enable tests | exactly one low output at Y[addr] for each address; G1 = 0 gives all high; G2A = 1 gives all high | exact | all 8 addresses correct; enable checks correct |

2 of 2 match (logic exactness). The RCLK-to-Q figure is consistent with the sum of the modelled delays, not with a datasheet-fitted number.

### 6.13 Research confidence

(a) M. (b) H (595 and 138 abs-max tables agree with the extracts). (c) M for logic function, M-L for timing (RCLK to Q falls inside the 17..45 ns band; setup/hold of 20..30 ns and pulse width 16..24 ns at 4.5 V are in the extract but not modelled). (d) M. Unresolved: setup and hold checks, tpd by path, the CD4017 counter (named in the brief, not researched; 74HC138 chosen instead as allowed), SRCLR timing.

## 7. BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-IC-DIGITAL-IO

### 7.1 Purpose and real-world use

Microcontrollers, serial memories and processors in DIP and SO packages are programmable or protocol-driven. Their useful behaviour (firmware, SPI transactions, bus cycles) cannot be simulated by SPICE. What a board-level simulator and the rule checker can do is model the electrical interface of every pin: output drive strength, input thresholds, pull-ups, tri-state, clamp diodes and absolute-maximum checks, and require a higher layer (L3) for everything else. Reference parts: ATmega328P (PDIP-28, OHM-108), ATtiny85 (PDIP-8, OHM-104; SOIC-8 OHM-110), 25LC256 (PDIP-8 and SOIC-8, OHM-104/110), W65C02S (PDIP-40, OHM-109).

### 7.2 What it is and how it works

A CMOS I/O pad is a push-pull output stage, an input buffer with a Schmitt-like threshold, ESD diodes to both rails, and optionally a weak pull-up transistor. Output drive is limited by the stage resistance: the ATmega328P extract (8161D) gives VOL <= 0.4 V at IOL = 20 mA and VOH >= 4.2 V at IOH = -20 mA with VCC = 5 V (datasheet limits, worst case; typical pins are stronger). Input levels: VIL up to 0.3 VCC and VIH from 0.6 VCC for the ATmega328P extract; input leakage up to +-1 uA and pin capacitance 4 pF (same extract); between those levels the logic state is undefined and a simulator must flag it. The internal pull-up is 20 to 50 kohm (ATmega328P extract; 35 kohm used). The 25LC256 SO pin is tri-state: it drives only while CS is low; VOL <= 0.4 V at 2.1 mA (VCC 4.5 V) and VOH >= VCC - 0.5 V at -400 uA; VIH >= 0.7 VCC, VIL <= 0.3 VCC (DS20001822H mirror extract, M).

L3 requirement (explicit): the following are NOT electrical and are NOT simulated here, and a design that depends on them must be handled by firmware or protocol simulation (outside this repository's SPICE runner): ATmega328P and ATtiny85 program execution, clock fuse and reset behaviour, the ADC, timers and UART/SPI/I2C peripherals; 25LC256 instruction decoding (READ, WRITE, WREN, status polling, 64-byte page boundary, write cycle time); W65C02S bus cycles, address decode and memory timing. The pad model exposes `din`, `und`, `dout`, `oe`, `pu` nodes so that an L3 engine can drive and sample the pins.

### 7.3 How it connects

ATmega328P PDIP-28 (the ATmega package of the Arduino Uno class): 1 PC6/RESET, 2 PD0, 3 PD1, 4 PD2, 5 PD3, 6 PD4, 7 VCC, 8 GND, 9 PB6/XTAL1, 10 PB7/XTAL2, 11 PD5, 12 PD6, 13 PD7, 14 PB0, 15 PB1, 16 PB2, 17 PB3, 18 PB4, 19 PB5, 20 AVCC, 21 AREF, 22 GND, 23..28 PC0..PC5. Pins 7/8 and 22 supply and ground; AVCC (20) must be connected to VCC even when the ADC is unused, with 100 nF decoupling on each supply pair. ATtiny85 PDIP-8: 1 PB5/RESET, 2 PB3, 3 PB4, 4 GND, 5 PB0, 6 PB1, 7 PB2, 8 VCC. 25LC256: 1 CS, 2 SO, 3 WP, 4 VSS, 5 SI, 6 SCK, 7 HOLD, 8 VCC (agrees with the repo catalog record 25LC256-I_SN.json: same terminal numbers; catalog electrical types CS, WP, HOLD, SI, SCK input, SO tri_state, VSS and VCC power; abs max for I/O is VCC + 1.0 V and -0.6 V; CS, WP, HOLD are flagged "must not float"). Typical mistakes: CS floating at power-up (catalog rule: a CS pull-up), HOLD and WP left open (the catalog requires them tied high when unused), SO of several SPI devices driven simultaneously, 5 V MCU outputs into a 3.3 V memory (25LC256 abs max VCC + 1.0 V), unconnected AVCC, ISP programming header connected to pins that also load the lines.

W65C02S PDIP-40: pin map UNVERIFIED. The datasheet extract from westerndesigncenter.com (W65C02S, 8 April 2022) is self-contradictory (D4 appears at pins 18 and 38, D5 at pins 17 and 40, address pins listed as A11 down to A0 on pins 22 to 33 with a missing A12 to A15 group), so I could not obtain a reliable 40-pin table. No pin map is given here. Status research_required for that entry's binding.

### 7.4 Electrical model for simulation

Layer L2 (pad) plus L3 (everything else, not simulated). File `bench/ic-digital-io/dio.lib`, `dio_pin pad din und dout oe pu vcc gnd params: vilf=0.3 vihf=0.6 roh=40 rol=20 cpin=4p ileak=1u rpu=35k`. Elements: pin capacitance, clamp diodes (ASSUMPTION, same diode as class 5), input decision `din` (0..1, tanh centred at the midpoint of VIL and VIH), undefined-region flag `und` (1 between VIL and VIH), output Thevenin source `v(oe) * (pad - level)/(roh*d + rol*(1-d))` with the data node `dout`, supply current taken only when sourcing, and a pull-up from VCC to the pad when `oe` = 0 and `pu` = 1. The leakage source is present but multiplied by 0 in the file as run: Hi-Z leakage is NOT modelled (ileak = 1 uA matches the ATmega328P maximum input leakage of +-1 uA, but the term is switched off in the library; enabling it is a one-line change).

Fits: roh = (5 - 4.2)/0.02 = 40 ohm, rol = 0.4/0.02 = 20 ohm (limits, so the pad is deliberately weak). For the 25LC256 SO pad use rol = 190 ohm and roh = 1250 ohm (0.4 V at 2.1 mA; 0.5 V at 0.4 mA). Parameter sets per part:

| part | roh | rol | vilf | vihf | pull-up | basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ATmega328P (5 V) | 40 | 20 | 0.3 | 0.6 | 20..50 k (35 k) | extract limits, S16 |
| ATtiny85 | RESEARCH_REQUIRED | RESEARCH_REQUIRED | RESEARCH_REQUIRED | RESEARCH_REQUIRED | RESEARCH_REQUIRED | the ATtiny25/45/85 extracts opened (preliminary 2586AS-AVR-02/05 via the soselectronic mirror, and a 2586Q-AVR-08/2013 reference) do not show DC characteristics, absolute maximums, pull-up or pin capacitance; only supply range (2.7-5.5 V, 1.8-5.5 V for the V parts), speed (0-20 MHz at 4.5-5.5 V; 0-10 MHz at 1.8-5.5 V V parts) and 450 uA active at 1 MHz, 1.8 V are available. Using the ATmega328P pad set is ASSUMPTION L (same AVR family, not a sourced equality) |
| 25LC256 (4.5 V) | 1250 | 190 | 0.3 | 0.7 | none | DS20001822H mirror extract: VIL max 0.3 VCC, VIH min 0.7 VCC, VOL 0.4 V at 2.1 mA, VOH VCC-0.5 V at -0.4 mA, S19 |
| W65C02S (5 V) | RESEARCH_REQUIRED | RESEARCH_REQUIRED | VIL max VSS+0.4 V (0.08 VDD), VIH min 0.7 VDD | | none | extract DC table (M-L; the same extract's pin table is corrupted, so the DC numbers also need a second source): IOL 1.6 mA min, IOH 700 uA min, leakage +-20 nA?, IDD 1.5 mA/MHz max, 14 MHz at 5 V, S23 |

Ideal mode: roh = rol = 1 mohm, no clamps, cpin = 0. Valid analyses: op and tran; ac is not meaningful for the decision nodes.

Known limitations: no input leakage, no temperature or VCC dependence of drive, no hysteresis at the pad (real pins have about 0.5 V of Schmitt hysteresis on digital inputs, not recorded), no analog pin function (ADC input, AREF), no oscillator, reset or brown-out behaviour, no ESD structures beyond the diodes, the pin-current limits are listed in 7.6 but are checks for the simulator, not part of the library; the injected-current limit of the clamps was not in the extract.

### 7.7 Failure and misuse behavior

| Event | Result | Simulator | Permanence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Input above VCC + 1.0 V (25LC256) or VCC + 0.5 V (ATmega328P, W65C02S is +0.3 V) | clamp conduction, damage | clamp diode model; ERROR beyond the sourced abs max (25LC256) | permanent |
| Input in the undefined band | indeterminate logic state | flag from `und` node | recoverable |
| Two outputs driving one net | contention current limited by roh/rol | netlist check; report current | permanent if sustained |
| CS, HOLD, WP floating (25LC256) | spurious selection, write protection undefined | netlist check using the catalog `must_not_float` flag | recoverable |
| Output beyond 20 mA | outside VOL/VOH limits | WARN above 20 mA, ERROR above 40 mA (ATmega328P abs max) | permanent if sustained |
| AVCC unconnected | ADC reference undefined; part may not behave | netlist check (ATmega328P) | recoverable |

### 7.8 Thermal behaviour

Self-heating from I/O is small: 8 pins at 20 mA with 0.4 V drop is 64 mW; MCU core current is firmware-dependent (L3). No sourced thermal resistance for DIP-28 and DIP-40 (class 1 marks them RESEARCH_REQUIRED, default 50 C/W ASSUMPTION).

### 7.9 Appearance summary

Black plastic DIP bodies with a pin-1 notch or dot and a marking such as ATMEGA328P-PU or 25LC256-I/P; DIP-28 and DIP-40 are the wide 15.24 mm row spacing (3D spec entries OHM-104, 108, 109, 110).
