## 8. BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-IC-LDO-SOT235

### 8.1 Purpose and real-world use

A low-dropout linear regulator makes a stable lower voltage from a higher one using a pass transistor and feedback, with low quiescent current (microamps), small area and no inductor. The SOT-23-5 is the usual package for 150 to 300 mA fixed-output LDOs in portable designs (3.3 V from a Li-ion cell, 1.8 V cores). Reference part: TI TLV70033 (3.3 V option of the TLV700 family, 200 mA, orderable TLV70033DDCR in SOT-23 DDC, SLVSA00E). Brief note: MCP1700 (Microchip) is NOT SOT-23-5; its SOT-23A package has three terminals (the repo catalog `MCP1700T-3302E-TT.json` lists 1 VOUT, 2 GND, 3 VIN; the mirror datasheet for SOT-23A reads 1 GND, 2 VOUT, 3 VIN, see Part C conflicts). MCP1700 is therefore not bound to OHM-120.

### 8.2 What it is and how it works

An error amplifier compares a divided output with an internal reference and drives a PMOS or PNP pass element in series with the input. Output voltage is regulated while Vin - Vout > dropout; below that the pass device is fully on and Vout = Vin - Iload x Rdo (Rdo about 0.86 ohm in the model from VDO = 85 mV at 100 mA for the 2.8 V option). The current limit protects against short circuits; thermal shutdown disables the pass element near 160 C with hysteresis (TI extract: about 160 C off, 140 C on). Dissipation: Pd = (Vin - Vout) Iout + Vin Iq. In SOT-23-5 (theta_JA 235.9 C/W for TLV700 DDC in the TI table) the dissipation limit at Ta = 25 C is (150 - 25)/235.9 = 0.53 W, and just 0.34 W at 70 C.

### 8.3 How it connects

TLV700 DDC SOT-23-5: 1 IN, 2 GND, 3 EN, 4 NC, 5 OUT (TI table; verified). Input and output capacitors: TI recommends 1 uF ceramic on IN and OUT; the output needs at least 0.1 uF effective capacitance and an ESR of at most 200 mohm. EN above 0.9 V enables, below 0.4 V shuts down; tie EN to IN for always-on. NC pin 4 may be tied to ground for thermal improvement (TI). Mistakes: using another SOT-23-5 LDO pinout (MCP73831 is STAT VSS VBAT VDD PROG; TLV9061 is OUT V- IN+ IN- V+; LDOs from other makers put EN or GND elsewhere), EN left floating, load current beyond the limit or beyond the thermal limit at high Vin, output capacitor ESR out of the stability range (not modelled).

### 8.4 Electrical model for simulation

Layer L1. `bench/ic-ldo/tlv700.lib`, subckt `tlv700 in gnd en out params: vnom=3.3 acc=0 rdo=0.86 rout=0.04 icl=0.43 iq=31u ign200=270u ven_hi=0.9 ven_lo=0.4 rth=235.9 ta=25 tsd_hi=160 cth=0.05`. Pass element: a current source from IN to OUT, `I = enable * (1 - shutdown) * icl * tanh(Iraw/icl)` with `Iraw = a b/(a+b)`, `a = (Vreg - Vout)/rout` (regulation branch) and `b = (Vin - Vout)/rdo` (dropout branch), both passed through a soft positive-part function (eps 1e-8), so the knee is smooth and a hard-knee solution differs by at most 2.5 mV. Ground current: `iq + (ign200 - iq) * min(Iout/0.2 A, 1)`. Thermal: node `tj` in volts (1 V = 1 C) with `rth`, `cth` to an ambient source; memoryless limiter `1 - 0.5(1 + tanh((Tj - tsd_hi)/2))` scales the pass current; the real hysteresis (160 off, 140 on) is not modelled because a latch has no unique DC solution. A 1 Mohm internal feedback load (ASSUMPTION; about 3 uA) keeps the output node non-singular.

Needs `.nodeset v(out)=...` (and `tj`) in some benches because the op solve depends on the initial guess; loads must be resistive when shutdown is possible.

Ideal mode: rdo = rout = 1 mohm, icl = 100 A, iq = 0, rth = 0. Valid analyses: op, dc, tran. Not valid: ac, noise (no loop dynamics; PSRR, noise and transient load response are not modelled).

Known limitations: no PSRR (68 dB at 1 kHz in the datasheet), no output-capacitor stability, no startup soft-start, no reverse-current behavior (a real pass PMOS conducts backwards through the body diode when Vout > Vin), no enable hysteresis, current limit is ASSUMED (430 mA between TI min 220 mA and max 860 mA of the TLV700 extract), 3.3 V dropout proxied from the 2.8 V option, no line regulation, no temperature dependence.

| Output capacitor missing | oscillation | WARN (not modelled) | recoverable |

### 8.8 Thermal behaviour

Tj = Ta + theta_JA (Vin - Vout) Iout + Vin Iq. Example bench: Vin = 5.5 V, 3.29 V, 199 mA: Pd = 0.442 W, Tj = 129.3 C at 25 C ambient; at 70 C ambient the same dissipation would reach 174 C, so the part limits itself near 160 C. The recommended design practice is to hold Pd below (150 - Ta)/theta. Cross-reference: R6 BEH-REG-LINEAR is the generic linear regulator class; this class is the SOT-23-5 fixed-output instance with the packaged thermal network.

### 8.9 Appearance summary

Small 5-lead SOT-23 body, 2.9 x 1.6 mm class, pin 1 at the bottom-left, marking code on top (3D spec entry OHM-120).

## 9. BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-IC-CHARGER-SOT235

### 9.1 Purpose and real-world use

A single-cell Li-ion/Li-polymer linear charger: it charges at a programmed constant current until the cell reaches the regulation voltage (4.2 V for the -2 option), holds that voltage while the current tapers, and stops at termination. Used in USB-powered gadgets, wearables and small power banks. Reference part: Microchip MCP73831 (SOT-23-5 "OT", also DFN-8; 15 to 500 mA programmable; regulation options 4.20, 4.35, 4.40, 4.50 V at +-0.75 %), orderable MCP73831T-2ACI/OT as in the repo corpus recording. Package: OHM-120.

### 9.2 What it is and how it works

A linear pass element charges the cell from VDD. Phases: preconditioning at 7.5 to 50 % of the fast-charge current (factory-selectable) while the cell is deeply discharged, constant current Ireg = 1000 V / Rprog (the datasheet formula IREG(mA) = 1000/RPROG(kohm) from the mirror extract: 10 kohm gives 100 mA, 2 kohm 500 mA), constant voltage at Vreg, then termination at 3.75 to 25 % of the programmed current (factory-selectable). VDD range 3.75 to 6 V; standby current 25 to 50 uA with PROG floating; reverse discharge current from the battery below 2 uA when disabled. STAT is an open-drain-like status output (low while charging, high impedance or high at termination, depending on variant). Thermal regulation reduces the charge current as the die heats; extract mentions a 150 C shutdown with 10 C hysteresis.

### 9.3 How it connects

SOT-23-5 pins: 1 STAT, 2 VSS, 3 VBAT, 4 VDD, 5 PROG (Microchip DS20001984H page 11 as transcribed in the repo annotation `tests/corpus/annotations/MCP73831_SOT23-5.json`; the DFN numbering differs: STAT 5, VSS 6, VBAT 3, VDD 1). The SparkFun mirror extract printed pin 4 as "NC"; this is an extraction error against the repo transcription and is not used. Layout: VDD input capacitor (typical 4.7 uF class, ASSUMPTION M), VBAT capacitor (typical 4.7 uF), PROG resistor to VSS, STAT to an LED with a series resistor or to a logic input with a pull-up. Mistakes: PROG resistor too small for the source (USB 500 mA limit), charging without a battery (output capacitor only), thermal design: at 500 mA and a 5 V input the dissipation is (5 - 3.7) x 0.5 = 0.65 W, above SOT-23-5 capability (theta 230 C/W gives 174 C), so the thermal regulation reduces the current.

### 9.4 Electrical model for simulation

Layer L1. `bench/ic-charger/mcp73831.lib`, subckt `chg_cc_cv vdd vss prog vbat stat params: vreg=4.2 vptrh=3.0 pre=0.1 term=0.075 rcv=0.3 rdo=1.0 rth=230 ta=25 tsd=150 cth=0.05 iqs=50u uvlo=3.75`. PROG is held at 1.0 V by an internal source; the current through Rprog times 1000 sets the regulation current node. Charge current: `Ib = UVLO gate * (1 - thermal) * min(Ireg * phase(Vbat) * tanh((Vreg - Vbat)/(rcv * Ireg)), (Vdd - Vbat)/rdo)`, where `phase` applies `pre` below `vptrh`. STAT is pulled low through 100 ohm while Ib is above `term * Ireg` and to VDD through 1 kohm at termination. The thermal limiter is memoryless at `tsd` with Tj = Ta + rth Pd.

ASSUMPTION list (confidence L, not found in the opened extracts; `pre`, `term`, `iqs` lie inside sourced ranges): `vptrh` 3.0 V, `pre` 0.1, `term` 0.075, `rcv` 0.3 ohm (CV loop sharpness), `rdo` 1.0 ohm, `uvlo` 3.75 V, STAT resistances, `cth` 0.05 J/C. Sourced: Ireg formula, 4.2 V regulation for the -2 option, 150 C thermal threshold (extract), theta 230 C/W (SOT-23-5, 4-layer board, Microchip mirror), pin map (repo annotation).

Ideal mode: rcv small (1e-3), rdo = 1 mohm, thermal off (rth = 0.001). Valid analyses: op, dc, tran.

Known limitations: no timer or safety timer, no battery-detect or charge-inhibit logic, no thermistor, no recharge threshold (Vrech) hysteresis, no precondition timer, no PROG-fault behaviour, no thermal hysteresis, no reverse-battery or short behaviour, termination is only a status flag (the model keeps charging with the tanh taper rather than stopping).

### 9.7 Failure and misuse behavior

| Event | Result | Simulator | Permanence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Overheating (high Vin, high Ireg) | charge current reduced | thermal limiter in the model | recoverable |
| PROG shorted to VSS | Ireg beyond the 500 mA rating | ERROR when I(VBAT) > 0.5 A | possible damage |
| PROG open | charge stops (standby) | model gives Ireg = 0 | recoverable |
| Battery reversed | destructive | ERROR | permanent (safety: Li-ion hazard; the simulator must treat reversed battery as fatal) |
| Charging a deeply discharged or damaged cell | Li-ion safety hazard | out of model; WARN | n/a |
| VDD below UVLO | no charging | model gate | recoverable |

Safety note: Li-ion cells can vent or burn if overcharged, charged below 0 C or short-circuited; charge current, voltage and temperature limits come from the cell datasheet, not this model.

### 9.8 Thermal behaviour

Pd = (VDD - VBAT) Ibat + VDD Iq. Bench B3: Rprog 2 kohm (500 mA), VDD 5 V, VBAT 3.7 V: unlimited Tj would be 174.5 C; the model limits Ibat to 0.4126 A, Tj = 148.4 C (analytic estimate 0.418 A, since quiescent power is included). Real silicon uses a datasheet-specific regulation; only the 150 C shutdown figure is documented in the opened extract.

### 9.9 Appearance summary

5-lead SOT-23 body with a marking code; pin 1 at the bottom-left (3D spec OHM-120; repo annotation: pads in rows 1-2-3 and 5-4, first pad bottom-left, counter-clockwise).

## 10. BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-IC-DRIVER-DIP16

### 10.1 Purpose and real-world use

Load drivers let a logic pin switch loads it cannot drive directly. The ULN2003A is seven open-collector Darlington channels with common flyback clamp diodes (relays, solenoids, stepper-motor coils, lamps, LED strips up to 50 V and 500 mA peak per channel). The L293D is four push-pull half-H drivers (two full H-bridges) for small DC motors and unipolar/bipolar steppers at 4.5 to 36 V, 600 mA continuous per channel, with internal clamp diodes. Packages: DIP-16 (OHM-106), SOIC-16 (OHM-112), TSSOP-16 (OHM-116, ULN2003A only in the sources opened).

### 10.2 What it is and how it works

ULN2003A channel: 2.7 kohm series base resistor into a Darlington pair (TI schematic), an internal base pulldown (value NOT in the extract: 3 kohm assumed here), the collector to the output pin, and a clamp diode from the output to COM. The Darlington gives a collector-emitter saturation voltage of 0.9..1.1 V at 100 mA, 1.0..1.3 V at 200 mA and 1.2..1.6 V at 350 mA (TI SLRS027T extract), so the dissipation is about 1 V x current: this is the main thermal limit. The clamp diode VF is 1.7..2.0 V at 350 mA. Propagation delay 0.25..1 us. L293D channel: totem-pole output with Darlington source and saturated sink; output high is VCC2 - 1.4 to 1.8 V at 1 A and output low is 1.2..1.8 V at 1 A (L293 conditions in the extract), clamp diode drop about 1.3 V. VCC1 (4.5..7 V) supplies the logic, VCC2 (VCC1 to 36 V) the outputs. An enable pin per pair switches the outputs to a high-impedance state. The four middle pins (4, 5, 12, 13) are the ground and the heat-sinking path: theta_JA 36.4 C/W for PDIP-16, far lower than other DIP-16 parts (class 1).

### 10.3 How it connects

ULN2003A (package order): 1..7 = 1B..7B (inputs), 8 E (emitter, to ground), 9 COM (common clamp cathode, to the load supply), 10..16 = 7C..1C (outputs). Outputs are in reverse order to inputs: 1B is pin 1 and its output 1C is pin 16. The load goes between the supply and the output; COM goes to the supply that feeds the inductive loads. Mistakes: COM tied to ground (the clamp diodes then conduct the load current: B1b bench note), load supply above 50 V, inputs driven above 30 V, expecting the 500 mA peak as a continuous rating with seven channels loaded (total emitter current -2.5 A and the thermal limit apply), forgetting the output polarity (open-collector outputs pull low when on).

L293D (PDIP-16): 1 1,2EN, 2 1A, 3 1Y, 4/5/12/13 GND, 6 2Y, 7 2A, 8 VCC2, 9 3,4EN, 10 3A, 11 3Y, 14 4Y, 15 4A, 16 VCC1. Typical H-bridge: motor between 1Y and 2Y, inputs 1A and 2A opposite for forward or reverse, both equal to brake (low) or both low-side fast stop, EN for PWM. Mistakes: VCC1 missing (outputs disabled, the model gates the enable at VCC1 above 4.5 V), motor supply connected to VCC1 above 7 V, stall current above 1.2 A peak, no motor supply decoupling, reversing direction without a dead time.

### 10.4 Electrical model for simulation

Layer L1. `bench/ic-driver/drivers.lib`.

* `uln_ch in out com e params: rb=2.7k`: Rb 2.7 k in series with a two-transistor Gummel-Poon Darlington (Q1 `q1uln` is=1e-14 bf=50 rb=20 rc=2 ikf=0.05; Q2 `q2uln` is=1e-13 bf=100 rb=3 rc=0.3 re=1.5 ikf=0.5), a 3 kohm base pulldown (ASSUMED from schematic memory, not confirmed in the extract) and a clamp diode `duln` (is=1e-11 rs=3.4 bv=60) from OUT to COM. The transistor parameters were fitted by `bench/ic-driver/fit_uln.py` to the middle of the three VCE(sat) bands. `fit_uln.py` is a fit script (python), not a runtime dependency.
* `l293d_ch a en y vcc1 vcc2 gnd params: roh=1.6 rol=1.5 vih=2.3 vil=1.5`: logic threshold at 1.9 V, enable gated by VCC1 > 4.5 V, output Thevenin source to VCC2 (roh) or ground (rol) when enabled, high-impedance otherwise, clamp diodes (`dl293` is=1e-10 n=1.5 rs=0.8) to VCC2 and ground. roh and rol are LINEAR fits to one datasheet point each (VOH = VCC2 - 1.6 V and VOL = 1.5 V at 1 A, middle of the printed ranges), so the model is only valid near 1 A: at 100 mA the real saturation voltages are lower than the linear model (it gives 0.15 V).

Parameter mapping: ULN VCE(sat) bands, input resistor 2.7 k, clamp VF 1.7..2.0 V at 350 mA; L293D VOH/VOL at 1 A, VIH 2.3 V min, VIL 1.5 V max, VF 1.3 V, delays 400..800 ns (L-H) and 200..400 ns (H-L) are not modelled (transport delay absent).

Ideal mode: ULN: replace the Darlington with a 1 mohm switch controlled by the input threshold; L293D: roh = rol = 1 mohm. Valid analyses: op, dc, tran (switching times not calibrated).

Known limitations: Darlington storage time and turn-off tail (the 0.25..1 us delay) is not calibrated; input current of the ULN2003A is NOT sourced (see B2); no thermal derating of VCE(sat); clamp reverse recovery not modelled (tt = 100 ns placeholder); L293D linear Ron wrong far from 1 A; L293D has no shoot-through protection; ULN2003A needs COM at a supply above the output voltage; temperature coefficient ignored.

### 10.7 Failure and misuse behavior

| Event | Result | Simulator | Permanence |
|---|---|---|---|
| ULN output above 50 V | breakdown | ERROR | permanent |
| ULN channel above 500 mA or sum above 2.5 A | overheating, bond wire | ERROR | permanent |
| ULN COM grounded | clamp diode carries the current | netlist check on COM (must be at or above the load supply) | recoverable until overload |
| Inductive load without a path | flyback voltage above 50 V | the internal clamp prevents it only if COM is wired | permanent if unclamped |
| L293D above 600 mA continuous | overheating | WARN 600 mA, ERROR 1.2 A | permanent |
| L293D input above 7 V | input breakdown | ERROR | permanent |
| L293D VCC1 missing | outputs disabled | model gate | recoverable |
| Overpower | dissipation above (150 - Ta)/theta_JA | flag | permanent when sustained |

### 10.8 Thermal behaviour

ULN2003A: seven channels at 200 mA, VCE(sat) 1.15 V: 1.6 W; the PDIP-16 limit is (150 - 70)/66.7 = 1.2 W at 70 C ambient, SOIC-16 0.9 W, TSSOP-16 0.7 W: the part cannot run all channels at 200 mA in surface-mount packages. L293D: two motors at 600 mA, each through one source and one sink drop of about 1.6 + 1.5 V, dissipate about 3.7 W; the PDIP limit is 125/36.4 = 3.4 W at 25 C and 80/36.4 = 2.2 W at 70 C, so full load needs copper heat sinking on pins 4/5/12/13 and the 600 mA limit cannot be used on both channels continuously.

### 10.9 Appearance summary

16-pin dual-row bodies (3D spec OHM-106 DIP-16, OHM-112 SOIC-16, OHM-116 TSSOP-16); L293D PDIP has four centre pins fused to the lead frame for heat sinking; pin 1 notch.

B1, B1b, B3 match their analytic or band expectation (3 of 4). B2 does NOT match its rough pre-bench estimate: the fitted Darlington has a base-emitter drop sum of about 1.8 V at these currents (3.85 V - 0.764 mA x 2.7 k), not 1.4 V, so the input currents are 16 % to 11 % lower than the estimate, and the flyback peak is 0.15 V below the guessed band because the model's clamp VF at 0.22 A is 1.35 V. Neither estimate is datasheet data; the extract row for II belongs to the 10.5 kohm ULN2004A, so the ULN2003A input current stays RESEARCH_REQUIRED. B2 is reported as a self-consistency run, not a pass against the datasheet.

## 11. BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-IC-RS232-DIP16

### 11.1 Purpose and real-world use

An RS-232 level shifter converts 5 V logic into the plus/minus 5 to 15 V swing of EIA-232 and back, using an on-chip charge pump so a single 5 V supply is enough. The MAX232 (TI SLLS047N) has two drivers and two receivers and needs four external 1 uF capacitors. Packages: DIP-16 (OHM-106), SOIC-16 narrow and wide (OHM-112), TSSOP-16 is not listed for this part in the extract (SOP-NS 88.5 C/W is). Common in serial consoles, instruments and legacy-port adapters. Data rate up to 120 kbit/s.

### 11.2 What it is and how it works

Voltage doubler: C1 charges to VCC and is stacked on VCC to give VS+ about 2 VCC - losses (+8.5 V from 5 V in the bench). Inverter: C2 pumps VS- = -VS+ roughly (-9 V unloaded in the bench, -8.5 V loaded). Drivers are inverting level translators from VS- to VS+ with an output resistance of about 300 ohm typical and a slew-rate limit near 30 V/us (extract). With a 3 kohm RS-232 load the output is 5..7 V (high) and -7..-5 V (low) typical. Receivers have a 3..7 kohm input resistance and a Schmitt trigger with VT+ = 1.7..2.4 V and VT- = 0.8..1.2 V (hysteresis 0.2..1.0 V), inverting (RIN high gives ROUT low). Supply current 8 mA typical. Output short circuit to ground is unlimited in duration (extract).

### 11.3 How it connects

Package order (TI): 1 C1+, 2 VS+, 3 C1-, 4 C2+, 5 C2-, 6 VS-, 7 T2OUT, 8 R2IN, 9 R2OUT, 10 T2IN, 11 T1IN, 12 R1OUT, 13 R1IN, 14 T1OUT, 15 GND, 16 VCC. Capacitors: C1 between 1 and 3, C2 between 4 and 5, C3 from VS+ (pin 2) to VCC or ground, C4 from VS- (pin 6) to ground; four 1 uF in the TI table (the connection of C3 and C4 as I describe is the common one and is not stated in the extract: ASSUMPTION M). Mistakes: omitting a capacitor (no pump, no swing), connecting TX to TX instead of crossing in a null-modem, driving T1IN above VCC, loading the VS+ rail for another purpose, using polarised capacitors backwards, connecting RS-232 to a 3.3 V MCU directly (the 5 V part drives 5 V into the MCU: use a 3.3 V variant).

### 11.4 Electrical model for simulation

Layer L1 (behavioural charge pump). `bench/ic-rs232/max232.lib`, `max232 c1p vsp c1m c2p c2m vsm t2out r2in r2out t2in t1in r1out r1in t1out gnd vcc params: vdrop=1.0 rpump=200 ro=300 vsat=1.0 sr=30e6 icc0=8m vtp=2.0 vtm=1.0 rrx=5k`, pins in package order.

Pump: `VS+ = 2 (VCC - GND) - vdrop - rpump (Ips1 + Ips2)` and `VS- = -(2 (VCC - GND) - vdrop) + rpump (Ims1 + Ims2)` (voltage sources whose output droops with the driver currents, so loading is represented); supply current `icc0 + 2 x (sum of driver pump currents)`. Driver: Schmitt-like input at GND + 1.4 V, inverting target `VS- + vsat` (input high) or `VS+ - vsat` (input low), slew-limited node (current source `sr x 1 nF`), output resistance `ro` 300 ohm, current-reporting nodes `ips`, `ims`. Receiver: 5 kohm to ground, Schmitt thresholds `vtp` 2.0 V and `vtm` 1.0 V (middle of the extract ranges), inverting, logic output with roh = rol = 100 ohm (ASSUMED). The four external capacitors are NOT simulated: the pump pins `c1p c1m c2p c2m` are left as stubs and the netlist checker must require the four capacitors.

Ideal mode: vdrop = 0, rpump = 0, ro = 1 ohm. Valid analyses: op, tran. Valid range: VCC 4.5..5.5 V, f below 120 kbit/s.

Known limitations: pump is a voltage source (no start-up, ripple, or capacitor-value dependence), pump droop uses a 200 ohm resistance chosen to give about -6.9 V at 3 kohm (the extract gives only the range 5..7 V), no short-circuit current limit, no ESD, VS+/VS- are not allowed to be loaded externally beyond the driver currents, receiver thresholds ignore the VCC dependence, propagation delay (500 ns max for the receiver in the extract) not modelled, slew rate effective value 27 V/us.

### 11.8 Thermal behaviour

Pd = VCC x ICC + driver output losses: 5 V x 8 mA = 40 mW typical, more with the drivers loaded (3 kohm: 7 V/3 k = 2.3 mA per driver, doubled on the supply). Package theta from the extract (PDIP 60.6) gives about 2.4 K rise at 40 mW: negligible.

## 12. BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-IC-OPTO-DIP6

### 12.1 Purpose and real-world use

A phototransistor optocoupler passes a signal or switching state across an isolation barrier with an LED on the input side and a phototransistor on the output side (galvanic isolation, level shifting, noise rejection, microcontroller I/O isolation). The 4N35 (Vishay Rev. 1.2/1.8, document 83717) is the classic DIP-6 device with a base connection. Package DIP-6 (OHM-103), the only entry in this group with six leads.

### 12.2 What it is and how it works

An infrared LED (forward voltage 1.2..1.5 V at 10 mA) illuminates the base region of an NPN phototransistor. The collector current is the current transfer ratio times the LED forward current, IC = CTR x IF, as long as the transistor is not saturated. CTR (minimum 40 % at IF = 10 mA, -55..100 C, per the Rev 1.8 extract; minimum 100 % at VCE = 10 V, IF = 10 mA per the Rev 1.2 extract; see conflict below) varies strongly with IF, temperature and ageing. In saturation VCE(sat) is about 0.3..0.4 V (Rev 1.8 extract; 0.4 V in the Rev 1.2 graphs). Rise and fall times about 10 us typical: slow, suitable for kilohertz switching only. Isolation test voltage 5000 VRMS; input-output coupling capacitance below 0.5 pF. The base pin is optional: leaving it open gives the full CTR; a resistor from base to emitter speeds up the response and reduces CTR.

### 12.3 How it connects

DIP-6 pin map: 1 anode, 2 cathode, 3 NC, 4 emitter, 5 collector, 6 base (Vishay Rev. 1.2 copy; matches the usual 4N35 convention). The Rev. 1.8 extract printed 5 = base and 6 = collector, which contradicts Rev. 1.2 and is treated as an extraction error until a human checks the original PDF (status: CONFLICT, kept in Part C). Typical circuits: LED in series with a resistor from the logic supply to pin 1 with pin 2 to the driver, the collector to a pull-up on the secondary side and the emitter to the secondary ground (output inverts when the transistor pulls the collector low). Mistakes: confusing pins 5 and 6, driving the LED above 60 mA (Rev 1.8) or 50 mA (Rev 1.2), connecting base pin to a supply, using the CTR minimum as a typical value and thus underdriving the LED, expecting fast edges, isolation voltage exceeded by PCB creepage.

### 12.4 Electrical model for simulation

Layer L1. `bench/ic-opto/opto4n35.lib`, `opto_pt an cat c e params: ctr=1.0 vsat=0.15 ioff=5n`. LED diode `dled` (is=1.5e-13, n=1.8, rs=4, cjo=30p) and a collector current source `Ic = ctr x max(IF,0) x tanh(max(Vce,0)/vsat) + ioff`. Base pin 6 is not modelled (left open in the typical circuit). Default CTR = 1.0 (100 %) is a typical-class number between the Rev 1.2 minimum (100 %) and the Rev 1.8 minimum (40 %); the right choice for a design is the minimum 40 % (conservative) or a measured value: documented as a user parameter, not a fact. Ideal mode: ctr = 1, ioff = 0, vsat = 1 mV. Valid analyses: op, dc, tran (no speed limit modelled).

Known limitations: constant CTR (no IF, temperature, aging dependence), no 10 us rise/fall time (add a capacitor on the collector), no base pin, no isolation breakdown, no coupling capacitance, dark current fixed at 5 nA (extract: ICEO 5..50 nA at 10 V), VCE(sat) from a tanh, so the saturation level in B1 is 0.37 V against 0.3..0.4 V typical (inside).

### 12.6 Ratings and limits

| Quantity | Rev 1.8 extract | Rev 1.2 extract | Check (conservative) |
|---|---|---|---|
| LED forward current | 60 mA | 50 mA | `I(LED) <= 50e-3` |
| LED reverse voltage | 6 V | not recorded | `V(LED reverse) <= 6` |
| VCEO | 30 V | 70 V | `V(C)-V(E) <= 30` (conservative choice) |
| VEBO | 7 V | not recorded | |
| Output power | 150 mW | not recorded (input and output 70 mW listed) | `Vce*Ic <= 70e-3` conservative |
| Isolation | 5000 VRMS | 5000 VRMS | informational |
| Operating ambient | -55 to 100 C | -55 to 100 C | |

### 12.7 Failure and misuse behavior

| Event | Result | Simulator | Permanence |
|---|---|---|---|
| LED current above rating | LED degradation, open | WARN above 50 mA, ERROR above 60 mA | permanent |
| VCE above rating | breakdown | ERROR | permanent |
| Isolation voltage exceeded | barrier breakdown (safety hazard) | out of model: design-rule check on creepage | permanent |
| LED reverse above 6 V | junction breakdown | ERROR | permanent |
| Base pin left to noise | false triggering | WARN not modelled | recoverable |

Safety: opto-couplers on mains side must meet the creepage and clearance required by the application standard, not the datasheet isolation test voltage alone; the model does not check this.

### 12.8 Thermal behaviour

Output dissipation (collector current x VCE) is limited to a few tens of mW: 70 mW is the conservative figure. No sourced theta_JA for DIP-6 (class 1: RESEARCH_REQUIRED).

### 12.9 Appearance summary

Black 6-lead DIP with a pin-1 dot or notch, marking 4N35 (3D spec OHM-103).

| B1_ctr_sat | 5 V, RL 470 ohm; (a) IF about 2 mA via 1.9 kohm, (b) IF about 10 mA via 380 ohm | (a) IF = (5 - VF)/1.9k = 2.05 mA with VF = 1.095 V, Vc = 5 - 470 x 2.05 mA x CTR 1 = 4.04 V; (b) saturated: Vc inside the Vishay VCE(sat) band 0.3..0.4 V | 1 % for (a); band for (b) | (a) VF 1.0949 V, Vc 4.034 V; (b) VF 1.200 V (inside 1.2..1.5 V), Vc 0.369 V |
| B2_ctr_linear | LED current sources 1, 2, 5 mA, RL 100 ohm to 5 V (unsaturated); CTR 1.0 and 0.4 | Ic = CTR x IF + 5 nA: 1, 2, 5 mA; 0.4, 0.8 (not run), 2.0 mA | 0.1 % | 1.000, 2.000, 5.000 mA; 0.400005, 2.000 mA; VF at 5 mA 1.148 V |

2 of 2 match. B2 adds the CTR proportionality check on the unsaturated branch. B1 (b) saturates at 0.369 V, inside the Vishay 0.3..0.4 V typical band but outside my own pre-bench guess of 0.07..0.2 V (written in the bench header): the datasheet band governs.

## 13. SOT-23-6 BINDING EXAMPLE: TPS3808 (no behavior model)

The only SOT-23-6 reference part opened is the TI TPS3808 supervisor (SBVS050N, May 2004 to August 2026 as printed in the extract; the document date is as printed and is not independently checked). It is bound to OHM-121 as a pin-map and thermal example only. No behavior model or bench exists; the behavior class for supervisors is RESEARCH_REQUIRED (status partial for the binding).

Pins (DBV SOT-23-6): 1 RESET (open-drain, active low), 2 GND, 3 MR (manual reset, active low), 4 CT (reset-delay programming), 5 SENSE, 6 VDD. Absolute maximum: VDD and signal pins -0.3 to 7 V, junction -40 to 150 C. Recommended supply 1.7 to 6.5 V, supply current 2.4 uA typical at 3.3 V. Reset delay: 20 ms with CT open, 300 ms with CT to VDD through 40..200 kohm, programmable 1.25 ms to 10 s with a capacitor. RESET output VOL 0.4 V maximum at 1 mA; external pull-up 10 kohm to 1 Mohm. SENSE hysteresis 1 % to 2.5 % depending on variant. theta_JA (DBV) 180.9 C/W. The RESET pin is an open-drain output and, like the LM393 output, needs an external pull-up (a netlist check rule).

# PART B. PER-ENTRY SECTIONS

Every entry is a package. Terminal numbers below are the numbers of the 3D spec (pin 1 top-left, counter-clockwise for dual-row packages; pin 1 bottom-left for SOT-23). They agree with every datasheet pin table opened. Thermal values are copied from class 1 (section 1.5): the default is the median of the observations from opened datasheets, derating slope = 1/theta, Pmax = (150 - Ta)/theta. Lead parasitics are the class 1 defaults for the package family. Dissipation check for every entry: `Tj = Ta + P*theta_JA <= 150` with P the total package power (supply power minus power delivered to the load outside the package).

## C.2 Source conflicts (shown, not resolved by guess)

1. MCP6001 SOT-23-5 pin order: the three mirrors give different pin tables for VIN+/VIN-. Unresolved; no map is bound to OHM-120 (the TLV9061 map is the verified alternative).
2. 4N35: Rev 1.2 pins 5 = collector, 6 = base; Rev 1.8 extract 5 = base, 6 = collector (the usual convention and Rev 1.2 agree; the Rev 1.8 extract is probably wrong). CTR minimum 100 % (Rev 1.2) versus 40 % (Rev 1.8). VCEO 70 V (Rev 1.2) versus 30 V (Rev 1.8). IF maximum 50 mA versus 60 mA. The model uses the conservative minimum of each.
3. MCP73831 SOT-23-5 pin 4: SparkFun mirror extract printed NC; the repo annotation of DS20001984H page 11 gives VDD (pins: STAT, VSS, VBAT, VDD, PROG). The repo annotation is used.
4. MCP1700 SOT-23A: mirror datasheet 1 GND, 2 VOUT, 3 VIN (SOT-89 and TO-92: 1 GND, 2 VIN, 3 VOUT) versus repo catalog `MCP1700T-3302E-TT.json` 1 VOUT, 2 GND, 3 VIN. The catalog disagrees with the mirror; to be checked by a human against the original PDF.
5. AN-1205 table: two extracts of the same table give different C values (SSOP-28: 0.6/0.35 pF versus 0.27 to 0.10 pF; mini SOIC-8: 0.15/0.08 versus 0.04 pF) and the lead-count column lost alignment. Class 1 uses the first reading; if the second is right, the SO-family C default (0.45 pF) is about 2x to 4x too high. Effect on the benches is nil (they use the DIP values).
6. 74HC00 extract: VOL(4 mA, 4.5 V) 0.17 / 0.26 / 0.33 V typ-max labelled, VOH(-4 mA) row has max below min (extraction error); the HC138 extract gives 0.26 V as maximum. The model uses 0.26 V.
7. W65C02S extract: D4 appears twice (pins 18 and 38) and D5 twice (17 and 40): pin table unusable.
8. ULN2003A extract: input-current row 0.35..0.5 mA at 5 V belongs to the 10.5 kohm ULN2004A, not the 2.7 kohm ULN2003A; the model's input current (1.19 mA at 5 V) is not datasheet-checked.
9. LM358 VIO columns (min/typ shifted: "3 / 7"), LM393 VIO/ICC columns, 555 ICC "3, 6": read as typical/maximum; labelled M.
10. MCP6001 absolute-maximum input voltage differs between mirrors (class 2 section 2.13).
11. Document dates: several TI revisions are dated after the knowledge cut of this agent (for example SBVS050N August 2026); dates are as printed by the extracts and were not independently verified.

## C.3 Gaps (RESEARCH_REQUIRED)

- theta_JA for DIP-6 (OHM-103), DIP-28 (OHM-108), DIP-40 (OHM-109): no opened source; 50 C/W is an assumption (L).
- Lead parasitics: no sourced value for SOT-23-5/6 and for DIP-28/40; defaults are assumptions (L); AN-1205 table ambiguity (C.2 item 5).
- ATtiny85 DC characteristics and absolute maximums; W65C02S pin map (second source needed) and a second source for its DC characteristics; MCP6001 SOT-23-5 pin order; ATmega328P I/O hysteresis.
- L3 layer (firmware, SPI command execution, 6502 bus cycles, ADC and timers) is not simulated and no L3 model is provided.
- CD4017 counter named in the brief: not researched (74HC138 chosen); 74HC04 datasheet not opened (cell calibrated to HC00 and HC14 numbers, pin map assumed equal to HC14).
- MCP73831 internal values (vptrh, exact precondition/termination fractions, CV loop, UVLO, abs max); TLV70033 3.3 V option dropout and current limit specifically; LM324 GBW and slew rate; MCP6001 offset and slew.
- TPS3808: no behavior model (section 13); supervisor class not defined.
- No vendor SPICE model was obtained for any part: all fidelity labels are `behavioural_approximation`.
- Setup/hold and minimum pulse-width checks for the 595; tpLH versus tpHL; VCC dependence of the HC cell.

## C.4 Disagreements between the 3D spec and electrical reality

None found in pin order or polarity: every datasheet table opened (NE555, LM358, LM393, LM324, HC00, HC14, HC138, HC595, HC245, ULN2003A, L293D, MAX232, 25LC256, ATmega328P, ATtiny85, TLV700, TLV9061, MCP73831 annotation, TPS3808, 4N35 Rev 1.2) uses the same counter-clockwise numbering from pin 1 as the spec, and the SOT-23-5/6 lead layout of the spec (3 leads on the bottom row, pin 4 top-right, pin 5 top-left or centre for the 6-lead) matches TLV700, TLV9061, MCP73831 and TPS3808. Notes: (a) the repo catalog (not the 3D spec) disagrees with the MCP1700 mirror datasheet (C.2 item 4); (b) the spec's DIP-14 and DIP-16 bodies share one length (19.3 mm), which is a dimension question outside this group; (c) the spec's SOIC-16 default is the narrow body and the wide variant is selected by body_class, so wide-body parts (74HC595 DW, MAX232 DW) must request it; thermal defaults differ (85.9 versus 64.3 C/W).

# GROUP R7B: IC packages QFP, QFN, DFN, PLCC, BGA, WLCSP (OHM-122 to OHM-140)

Author: research agent R7B. ngspice 42 run locally. Bench files and raw results (`results_ngspice42.txt`) are in `/home/claude/behavior/bench/pkg-ic-binding/`, `ic-digital-if/`, `mem-spinor/`, `reg-buck-dcs/`, `pwr-loadswitch/`.

## 0. Reading guide and honesty notes

These 19 entries are PACKAGES. A QFP-32 or a BGA-256 has no electrical behavior of its own. What the user places is "a QFP-32", and what it does is whatever functional device the part binding puts in it. So this file does two things:

1. It defines a **package binding** class (BEH-PKG-IC-BINDING): how a functional part is bound to a package (pin or ball function map, exposed pad rule, thermal resistance, lead parasitics, junction temperature and power limits, failure behavior when the binding is wrong).
2. It documents a **reference set of real parts** that live in these packages, each with the electrical interface the simulator can honestly model, and, where a part is not SPICE-simulable (MCU, FPGA, flash, SoC), a clear statement of what a higher layer (L3) must provide.

| Class | What it models | Layer | Entries |
|---|---|---|---|
| BEH-PKG-IC-BINDING | package binding, pin/ball maps, exposed pad, Rth, parasitics, Tj/P limits | L1 (parasitics, thermal network) + metadata | all 19 |
| BEH-IC-DIGITAL-IF | electrical interface of MCUs, FPGAs, PLDs, RTCs, bridges and audio ICs (rails, I/O thresholds, drive, leakage, abs max, reset, power sequencing) | L1/L2 interface only; behavior of the firmware or bitstream is L3 | 122-126, 128-131, 135, 137-139 |
| BEH-MEM-SPINOR | SPI NOR flash and parallel EPROM electrical interface plus the command timing an L3 model must obey | L1/L2 interface; command set and array are L3 | 133, 134 (flash), 135 note (EPROM) |
| BEH-REG-BUCK-DCS | small synchronous buck (TPS62160 WSON-8, TPS62130 QFN-16): constant on-time behavioural switching model | L1 (ngspice, no XSPICE) | 127, 134 |
| BEH-PWR-LOADSWITCH | load switch / power switch (TPS22810 DFN-6/DRV, NX5P3290 WLCSP-16) | L1 | 132, 140 |

Linear regulators in these packages (for example the TPS7A80 in VSON-8) reuse BEH-REG-LINEAR from `parts/R6.md`; only the package binding, Rth and Tj check are added here (bench P1 case c).

Fidelity label for everything in this file: **behavioural_approximation** (or `ideal_components` for pure RLC/thermal networks). **No vendor SPICE model was opened or attached, so nothing here may be labelled `vendor_model`.** A simulation that did not run is never a pass: the checks below must return `unbound` / `not_simulated` rather than `ok` when a binding or model is missing.

### Honesty notes that apply to the whole file

1. **Datasheet access limits.** The page-fetch tool returns a model-written extract of a PDF, cut off after roughly the first 40 to 60 pages. Tables later than that (electrical characteristics of large MCU datasheets) were NOT visible for ST (STM32F103, STM32F407), Microchip ATmega328P (and Microchip, Winbond and ST host direct-PDF fetches were refused by robots.txt), Lattice electrical tables partly, and Winbond W25Q electrical tables. I did not paper over this: where a number is not from an opened document the row says so, and sibling-device numbers are marked as such.
2. **Extracts can be wrong, and I found examples.** The first ST extract of the STM32F103 gave thermal resistances (LQFP100 about 80 K/W, LQFP64 about 90) that a verbatim table page contradicts (46 and 45 K/W). The TQFP-32 pin list returned for the ATmega328P was in text-flow order, not pin-number order, and is NOT used. Values below are used only when repeated by a second query or by a table page, or they are flagged.
3. **Pin maps.** Pin tables I could actually verify: CP2104 QFN-24, P89LPC935 PLCC-28, TPS62160 WSON-8, TPS62130 VQFN-16, TPS7A80 VSON-8, TPS22810 WSON-6, NX5P3290 WLCSP-16, MAX98357A WLP-9, W25Q128JV 8-pad, ESP32-C3 QFN-32 (extract, M), plus a handful of STM32F103 rows. Everything else (ATmega328P TQFP-32 numbering, ATmega32U4, ATF22V10C PLCC-28, STM32F407 LQFP-144, Artix-7 FTG256 ball map) is `RESEARCH_REQUIRED` for a verified pin-number map. Where I give the commonly known ATmega328P pin numbers it is labelled ASSUMPTION / confidence L.
4. **The brief's hint "27C256 EPROM in PLCC-28" is not true.** The Atmel AT27C256R is offered in a 28-pin PDIP and a **32-pin PLCC** (S23). A 28-pin PLCC family that does exist and was opened: NXP P89LPC935FA (SOT261-2), and the GAL22V10 / ATF22V10C PLDs.
5. **ngspice 42 facts found by running** (matter for implementers):
   - This ngspice build has **no XSPICE** (`a`-devices fail with "Scalar connection expected"). Everything uses only B sources, R, L, C, switches, diodes.
   - `S` switch hysteresis: the device turns ON at `Vt + Vh` rising and OFF at `Vt - Vh` falling. A state-dependent `S` switch whose control depends on a current it carries caused "timestep too small" failures; smooth B-source conductances do not.
   - `.control` blocks do not expand `{param}`; use a template substitution (`@RL@` in B2) or numeric literals.
   - A regenerative latch built from a capacitor and a B source needs a bistability term (`0.5*q*(1-q)*(2q-1)`) or it stalls at a partial state.
   - `meas ... when vp(node)=0` finds an AC resonance if a few milliohm of series R keep the phase continuous.
   - `.tran ... uic` with `Cout ic=` is needed for the switching regulators; they do not start from a plain `.op`.
6. Compatibility with the OHMNI repository: pin electrical types use KiCad vocabulary (`power_in`, `input`, `bidirectional`, `passive`, ...); the repo already has `TerminalKind.EXPOSED_PAD` and a pin-number pattern `^[A-Z]?\d{1,4}$` (one row letter plus digits: covers BGA rows A..T used here, not two-letter rows such as AA). `Unit` has no K/W: thermal resistance needs a new unit or a `ratio`-style dimensionless field with a unit string. The package `name` strings in part records ("SOIC-8") are free text; the binding below keys on OHM-ID.

## 2. BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-PKG-IC-BINDING

Applies to: OHM-122 to OHM-140 (all 19 entries). Layer L1 for the numbers (parasitic RLC, thermal network) and pure metadata for the pin map.

### 2.1 Purpose and real-world use
A package is the mechanical and thermal carrier of a die: it fixes where each signal comes out, how much power can leave as heat, and how much inductance and capacitance sit between the die pad and the board land. In a design flow the package matters in four ways: (a) **pin or ball numbering** (which terminal number is which function; the same package number carries different functions in different parts), (b) **exposed pad** (QFN, DFN, WSON: it is both the main heat path and, for some parts, a required electrical connection, for others it is deliberately unconnected), (c) **thermal limit** (junction temperature Tj = Ta + RthJA x P, with RthJA depending on the package and on the copper and vias under it), (d) **parasitics** (lead inductance limits supply decoupling above some MHz and sets ground bounce).

Typical applications per family: QFP/TQFP/LQFP for microcontrollers and FPGAs (hand solderable at 0.5 to 0.8 mm), QFN for small MCUs, USB bridges and power ICs, DFN/WSON for SPI flash, LDOs, load switches and buck converters, PLCC for legacy logic, PLDs and 8051-class MCUs (socketable), BGA for large MCUs, FPGAs and memories, WLCSP for tiny sensors, power switches and audio amps.

### 2.2 What it is and how it works
Physics that justifies the numbers:
- **Lead inductance** of a wire-bonded leadframe package is roughly the wire plus lead length times about 1 nH/mm (S30 Table 7: a 1 mm wire is 0.78 nH, 2 mm 1.83 nH, 5 mm 5.50 nH; "effective" values including return are about 1.4 times higher). Corner leads are longer than center leads (S30: QFP-28 corner 4.5 nH, center 2.4 nH). QFN and BGA shorten the path; WLCSP removes the wire completely (bump only).
- **Thermal path.** Heat flows die -> die attach -> leadframe or substrate -> (a) board through the exposed pad or balls, and (b) mold compound and leads to ambient. For a QFN or DFN with a soldered pad, the board path dominates: S2 gives RthJC(bottom) = 4.5 K/W for the 3x3 VQFN-16 versus RthJC(top) = 53.6, and S1 gives 8.6 K/W bottom versus 61.3 K/W top for WSON-8. RthJA is then set mostly by the board: S27 models a 20-pin QFN at 46.8 K/W with no thermal vias and 30.8 K/W with four vias on a JESD51-5 card, and S28 gives 3.25 W (PowerPAD SSOP-20) against 0.75 W (standard) at 150 C junction and 80 C ambient, i.e. about 21.5 K/W against 93 K/W.
- Steady state: `Tj = Ta + RthJA * P`. Transient: a multi-stage Foster network (see BEH-PWR-PKGTHERMAL in `parts/R6.md` for the tested form and its honesty notes: the capacitances are assumptions).

Key equations: `Tj = Ta + RthJA*P`; `Pmax = (Tjmax - Ta)/RthJA`; lead self-resonance with a decoupling capacitor `f0 = 1/(2*pi*sqrt(L*C))`; first droop on a step `dV = dI*sqrt(L/C)` (ideal step, damped by series R); ground bounce `dV = L*di/dt`.

### 2.3 How it connects: binding rules
A binding is a record that attaches a functional part to a package entry:

```yaml
package_binding:
  package: OHM-130            # package library entry (physical spec)
  part_id: "ESP32-C3"
  pin_map:                    # package terminal -> part pin; terminal ids as in the 3D spec numbering
    "1": {pin: LNA_IN, electrical_type: passive}
    "33": {pin: GND, kind: exposed_pad, must_connect: GND, thermal: true}
  thermal: {theta_ja: {value: , unit: "K/W", conditions: ""}, tj_max: {value: 125, unit: degC}}
  parasitics: {lead_l_nH: , lead_c_pF: , lead_r_mOhm: , basis: ""}
```

Rules the implementer must enforce:
1. **Terminal numbering.** QFP, QFN, DFN, WSON, PLCC: numbers follow the 3D spec convention (counter-clockwise from top view; QFP/QFN/DFN pin 1 at the top of the left side, PLCC pin 1 at the center of the top side). BGA and WLCSP: ball names are a row letter plus a column number, A1 at the top-left corner **in the top view**, letters increase toward -Y, numbers toward +X. Manufacturer ball maps are often **bottom views** (mirror image); NXP NX5P3290 states "transparent top view" (S5), which equals the OHMNI convention. The row-letter skip rule (I, O, Q, S, X, Z omitted) is confirmed by real parts: LPC1768 TFBGA100 balls A2, D5, J2 (S9) and STM32F103 LFBGA100 balls up to K10 (S10) fit a 10-row array of A-H, J, K.
2. **The exposed pad is a terminal.** Model it with `kind: exposed_pad` (the repo's `TerminalKind.EXPOSED_PAD`). It is not numbered in the 3D spec (the footprint nets it as N+1). **What it must connect to depends on the part, not the package.** Evidence from opened documents:
   | Part (package) | Exposed pad rule | Source |
   |---|---|---|
   | TPS62160 (WSON-8) | "Must be connected to AGND. Must be soldered ..." | S1 |
   | TPS6213x (VQFN-16) | connected to AGND, PGND and the ground plane | S2 |
   | TPS7A80 (VSON-8) | pad is GND (pin 4 and pad) | S3 |
   | ATmega328P (QFN/MLF-32, 28) | "Bottom pad should be soldered to ground" | S13 |
   | ESP32-C3 (QFN32) | EPAD listed as GND (pin 33 in the extract) | S16 |
   | FT231XQ (QFN-20) | centre pad internally connected to ground | S26 |
   | CP2104 (QFN-24) | center pad not captured (GND pin 2 is a separate pin) | S25 (RESEARCH_REQUIRED) |
   | **MAX98357A (TQFN-16)** | **"The exposed pad is not internally connected"** | S6 |
   So the model must carry `must_connect: GND | float_ok | not_connected` per part, and the verifier must treat an unconnected EP differently for those cases: for the TPS62160 an unsoldered or unconnected EP is a design error (thermal and AGND), for the MAX98357A it is merely a mechanical/thermal choice.
3. **Gang pins.** Several package terminals can be the same function: TPS62130 SW = pins 1, 2, 3; PVIN = 11, 12; PGND = 15, 16 (S2); NX5P3290 VIN = A1, A2; VCP = B1, B2, C1; VBUS = C2, D1, D2; GND = B3, C3, D3 (S5). The model must tie ganged terminals together and check that all of them are connected on the board (high current).
4. **Unbound = no behavior.** A package with no `package_binding` produces `status: unbound` and must not be reported as passing any simulation or rule.
5. **Pin electrical types** use the repo vocabulary. Supply pins `power_in`, ground pins `power_in` (the repo has no dedicated ground type), the exposed pad `passive` with `kind: exposed_pad`, no-connect `no_connect`.

Common mistakes: wrong ball map mirror (bottom versus top view), treating the EP as optional on a power IC, tying the MAX98357A-style "not connected" pad to a noisy rail, leaving ganged power pins partly unconnected, using a QFN 4x4 footprint for a 5x5 part of the same pin count, expecting the same function at the same pin number in another part (for example VDD is pin 17 on the P89LPC935 PLCC-28 and pin 2/3 on the ESP32-C3's QFN).

### 2.4 Electrical and thermal model for simulation
Layer: L1. Fidelity: `ideal_components` for the passive RLC (it is exactly R, L, C), `behavioural_approximation` for the thermal network.

Per-terminal parasitic subcircuit (realistic mode only; default ideal mode omits it):
```
* terminal ref: package pin node 'pin' (board side), die pad node 'die'
R{ref}_lead pin n1 {Rlead}
L{ref}_lead n1 die {Llead}
C{ref}_pad  die 0 {Cpad}     ; lead-to-ground capacitance; place at the die node
```
Thermal network (steady state and transient):
```
Ip{ref} 0 tj dc {P_watts}          ; power into the junction node, 1 W = 1 A
Rjc{ref} tj tc {RthJC}             ; optional split when RthJC and RthCA are known
Rca{ref} tc ta {RthCA}
Cj{ref} tj 0 {Cth_j}               ; ASSUMPTION unless a Zth curve is sourced
Vta ta 0 {Ta}
```
With only `RthJA` known: a single resistor `Rja tj ta {RthJA}`.
Thermal-via option: parallel path `Rvia tj_pad ta {Rvia}` calibrated to a sourced point (bench P2).

Parameter-to-datasheet map: `RthJA` = "thermal resistance junction-ambient" (JEDEC board; the board is part of the value), `RthJC(bot)` for QFN/DFN/WSON/VSON pads, `Tjmax` = "operating junction temperature" (recommended) and the absolute maximum junction temperature (150 C for most parts opened).

Valid analyses: op (steady Tj), tran (thermal transient with assumed Cth), ac (lead resonance). Valid range: board-level frequencies up to about 1 GHz for lumped lead models; above that need transmission-line or S-parameter models (not provided).
Known limitations: lead parasitics are per-package averages (corner versus center spread of 2 to 3 times); mutual inductance and mutual capacitance (M12, CM) are NOT modeled (S30 lists them and they dominate crosstalk in BGAs); RthJA from a datasheet applies to its JEDEC board, not to the user's board (error can be a factor of 2); there is no air-flow term; the thermal-via model is a calibrated parallel path, not a spreading-resistance model.

### 2.7 Ratings and limits (what the simulator checks)

| Check | Expression | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| junction temperature | `Tj = Ta + RthJA*P` must be `<= Tj_max_operating`; flag WARN above `Tj_max_operating - 10 K`, FAIL above `Tj_max_abs` | Tj_max values from the bound part (125 C or 150 C in the parts opened). |
| power limit | `Pmax = (Tjmax - Ta)/RthJA` | e.g. TPS7A80: (125-25)/47.8 = 2.09 W; 1.7 W LDO case gives Tj = 106.3 C (bench P1 c). |
| EP connection | if `exposed_pad.must_connect = GND` then the EP terminal must be on the GND net; if `thermal: true` and `RthJA` was taken with a soldered pad then the EP must be soldered (assembly note) | verifier rule, not SPICE |
| ganged pins | all terminals of a gang must share a net | high-current pins |
| binding present | `status == bound` | otherwise `unbound` |
| land pattern fit | EP land and paste coverage within 50 to 80 percent paste, vias 0.3 mm on 1.0 to 1.5 mm pitch under the pad | S27-S29, advisory |

### 2.8 Failure and misuse behavior

| Mode | Trigger | Physical effect | Simulator response | Permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| over-temperature | Tj above Tjmax_abs | die damage, shutdown if the part has thermal shutdown (TPS62160 160 C typ, TPS7A80 160 C, NX5P3290 140 C, TPS22810 160 C with 30 C hysteresis) | flag; if the bound part has a thermal shutdown model, open the output until Tj falls by the hysteresis; otherwise FAIL | recoverable (shutdown) or permanent (beyond abs max) |
| EP not soldered | assembly | RthJA rises toward the leaded figure (TPS62160: 184.3 K/W VSSOP-8 versus 61.8 K/W with pad as a scale) | multiply RthJA by a user-selected factor (advisory only; no sourced factor), warn | recoverable by rework |
| EP on the wrong net | design | for TPS62160/TPS6213x EP must be AGND; a pad tied to a different rail shorts the die substrate path or injects noise | verifier ERROR if `must_connect` violated | permanent if powered |
| ball map mirrored | library or import error | functions swapped (VIN on VOUT etc.) | the binding is the single source of truth; a mismatch between the datasheet bottom view and the OHMNI top view must be caught at import with a mirror flag | permanent in hardware |
| lead L too large for decoupling | supply droop | bench P3/P4 | none (analysis only): flag if first droop `dI*sqrt(L/C)` exceeds the rail tolerance | n/a |
| unbound | no part | no behavior | `unbound`, never pass | n/a |

### 2.9 Thermal behavior
Above (2.2, 2.6). The simple model: steady state with the RthJA of the table; transient with assumed Cth. RthJA values are not additive between a datasheet board and a user board: when the user board has less copper, RthJA is larger. S27: 20-pin QFN RthJA 46.8 to 30.8 K/W with four 0.30 mm vias at 1.2 mm pitch; S28: five to nine vias suit a small die. Heat spreading through the pad copper is not parallel, so adding more vias saturates (the extrapolation in P2 is labelled unverified).

### 2.10 Appearance summary
Each entry is a plastic or wafer-level body with the pin or ball pattern defined in its 3D spec section (OHM-122 to OHM-140). QFP and TQFP have gull-wing leads on four sides, QFN/DFN/WSON have flush underside terminals and a central pad, PLCC has J-leads folded under a square body, BGA has a ball array under the body, WLCSP has bumps directly on a bare die with a dark back-side coat. Pin 1 is a molded dimple (QFP/QFN/DFN), a bevel and dimple (PLCC), or the A1 corner (BGA, WLCSP).

### 2.12 Canonical YAML

```yaml
behavior_id: BEH-PKG-IC-BINDING
applies_to: [OHM-122, OHM-123, OHM-124, OHM-125, OHM-126, OHM-127, OHM-128, OHM-129, OHM-130, OHM-131, OHM-132, OHM-133, OHM-134, OHM-135, OHM-136, OHM-137, OHM-138, OHM-139, OHM-140]
layer: L1
category: ic
pins:
  - {name: terminal_N, role: terminal, electrical_type: passive, package_terminal_rule: "numbered per 3D spec (ccw from pin 1) for QFP/QFN/DFN/WSON/PLCC; row letter + column number for BGA/WLCSP; function comes from the bound part"}
  - {name: exposed_pad, role: thermal_pad, electrical_type: passive, package_terminal_rule: "kind=exposed_pad, un-numbered; must_connect per bound part (GND | float_ok | not_connected)"}
parameters:
  RthJA: {unit: "K/W", default: null, min: 18, max: 184.3, tolerance: board dependent, basis: MFR_DATASHEET, confidence: M, source_ref: "S1-S6,S11"}
  Tj_max_operating: {unit: degC, default: 125, min: 100, max: 150, tolerance: , basis: MFR_DATASHEET, confidence: M, source_ref: "S1,S2,S3"}
  lead_L: {unit: nH, default: 0, min: 0.011, max: 12.0, tolerance: "+/-30 percent per package, corner vs center 2-3x", basis: MFR_DATASHEET, confidence: M, source_ref: "S27,S30"}
  lead_C: {unit: pF, default: 0, min: 0.012, max: 0.35, tolerance: "+/-50 percent", basis: MFR_DATASHEET, confidence: M, source_ref: "S27,S30"}
  lead_R: {unit: ohm, default: 0, min: 0.001, max: 1.2, tolerance: wide, basis: MFR_DATASHEET, confidence: M, source_ref: "S27,S30"}
model:
  fidelity: ideal_components
  spice_primitives: [R, L, C, I, V]
  netlist_template: |
    R{ref}_lead {pin} n{ref} {lead_R}
    L{ref}_lead n{ref} {die} {lead_L}
    C{ref}_pad {die} 0 {lead_C}
    Ip{ref} 0 tj{ref} dc {P_watts}
    Rja{ref} tj{ref} ta {RthJA}
    Vta ta 0 {Ta}
  valid_analyses: [op, ac, tran]
  valid_range: "lumped model, below about 1 GHz; RthJA valid on the vendor board only"
  known_limitations: ["no mutual L or C", "RthJA board dependent", "no airflow", "thermal capacitance assumed", "thermal-via model calibrated not predictive"]
ratings:
  - {name: junction_temperature, symbol: Tj, value: 125, unit: degC, condition: "operating, parts opened", check: "Ta + RthJA*P <= Tj_max", source_ref: S1}
  - {name: power_limit, symbol: Pmax, value: null, unit: W, condition: "per bound part", check: "(Tj_max - Ta)/RthJA", source_ref: "S1,S3"}
failure_modes:
  - {id: overtemp, trigger: "Tj > Tj_max_abs", effect: "shutdown or die damage", sim_response: "flag; open output if part has thermal shutdown", permanence: recoverable}
  - {id: ep_wrong_net, trigger: "EP not on must_connect net", effect: "thermal/AGND error", sim_response: "verifier ERROR", permanence: permanent}
  - {id: unbound, trigger: "no package_binding", effect: "no behavior", sim_response: "status unbound, never pass", permanence: recoverable}
bench:
  - {id: P1, file: bench/pkg-ic-binding/P1_tj_steady.cir, expected: [{measure: Tj, value: "70.0, 55.9, 106.26, 43.396, 89.5, 54.2", tolerance: "0.1 percent", basis: "Tj = Ta + Rth*P"}], measured_in_ngspice: "70.000, 55.900, 106.260, 43.396, 89.500, 54.200", ngspice_version: "42"}
  - {id: P2, file: bench/pkg-ic-binding/P2_thermal_via_parallel.cir, expected: [{measure: theta_4vias, value: 30.8, tolerance: "0.5 percent", basis: "calibration of S27 Fig.16"}], measured_in_ngspice: "30.80 (9-via extrapolation 21.58 unverified)", ngspice_version: "42"}
  - {id: P3, file: bench/pkg-ic-binding/P3_lead_resonance.cir, expected: [{measure: f0_MHz, value: "7.5026, 7.5874, 15.0454, 12.2066, 25.1646", tolerance: "0.5 percent", basis: "1/(2 pi sqrt(LC))"}], measured_in_ngspice: "7.5026, 7.5874, 15.0454, 12.2066, 25.1646", ngspice_version: "42"}
  - {id: P4, file: bench/pkg-ic-binding/P4_supply_droop.cir, expected: [{measure: peak_droop_mV, value: "42.43, 21.16, 12.65", tolerance: "2 percent", basis: "dI*sqrt(L/C)"}], measured_in_ngspice: "42.42, 21.15, 12.64", ngspice_version: "42"}
sources: [S1, S2, S3, S4, S5, S6, S11, S13, S16, S25, S26, S27, S28, S29, S30, S31]
confidence: {parameters: M, ratings: M, model: M, failure: M}
status: complete
```

### 2.13 Sources and research confidence
Sources: S1-S6, S11, S13, S16, S25-S31 (table in section 1).

Research confidence: (a) parameters M (parasitics come from a 2004 National app note and a 2004 TI note, for packages of that era; only one QFN size and one PLCC and no QFP at the library's body sizes); (b) ratings M; (c) model fidelity M (lumped RLC and RthJA only); (d) failure behavior M.

Unresolved items:
1. S30 lists QFN-like "LLP" with L = 0.008 nH, while S27 lists QFN-20 at 1.119 nH: a factor of 140. The LLP row is physically implausible for a leaded-pad package and is not used as a default (listed as a conflict, per the "show conflicts" rule).
2. No parasitic value is sourced for QFP-144, QFP-100, TQFP-44/64 at the library body sizes (only a 28-pin 12 x 8 mm and a 208-pin 28 x 20 mm QFP): use 4.5 nH (corner) / 2.4 nH (center) as a floor and up to 12 nH for QFP-144, labelled ASSUMPTION L.
3. WLCSP values come from National "micro SMD" (S30), the same technology as TI DSBGA; the figures (0.011 nH) are very small; trace and via inductance on the board dominate.
4. RthJA for QFP-32/44, LQFP-144, PLCC-28, BGA-256: not opened.
5. The brief's "thermal resistance with and without thermal vias" per package is only sourced for a 20-pin QFN (S27) and as two PowerPAD contrast points (S28); other packages need vendor thermal tables.

---

## 3. BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-IC-DIGITAL-IF

Applies to: parts bound to OHM-122 to OHM-126 (QFP family), OHM-128 to OHM-131 (QFN), OHM-135 (PLCC-28), OHM-137 and OHM-138 (BGA), OHM-139 (WLCSP-9). Layer: **L1/L2 for the electrical interface only. The behavior of an MCU (firmware execution, peripherals, memories), an FPGA (bitstream), a PLD (fuse map), an RTC (time keeping) or a bridge/codec (protocol) is L3 and is NOT SPICE-simulable.** This class defines the part of those devices that a netlist can honestly contain and lists exactly what an L3 model has to add.

### 3.1 Purpose and real-world use
Digital ICs connect a board to the logic world: they read input levels, drive output levels, take supply current that depends on activity, must be powered in a safe order and reset into a known state. The electrical interface decides whether two parts can talk (VOH versus VIH, VOL versus VIL, 5 V into 3.3 V), whether a rail can supply them (current versus frequency), and whether the board survives mistakes (absolute maximum ratings, injection current, latch-up).

### 3.2 What it is and how it works
- **CMOS input cell:** a buffer with a switching threshold (a fraction of VDD for CMOS parts: 0.2/0.7 x VDD for the P89LPC935 (S8), 0.25/0.75 x VDD for the ESP32-C3 (S16)), optional hysteresis (iCE40: 200 mV typical, S19), a small input capacitance (iCE40: 6 pF typical, S19) and leakage (iCE40: up to 10 uA, S19; P89LPC935: +/-10 uA, S8). Protection clamp diodes to VDD and VSS conduct when the pin leaves the rails by about 0.6 V: injected current must be limited by a series resistor (bench D2).
- **Output cell:** a complementary driver with an on-resistance, modelled as a Thevenin source `Ron` fitted to the specified (VOL, IOL) and (VOH, IOH) points (bench D1). Real drivers are not linear and the datasheet points are worst-case limits.
- **Supply current:** `Idd = Istatic + Ceff*VDD*f` (dynamic switching of the digital core) with a floor from leakage; ESP32-C3-class parts add large RF bursts (335 mA peak transmit, S16).
- **Power-on reset (POR)** threshold detectors hold the core in reset until the rails exceed a trip level (iCE40: VCC rising trip 0.55 to 0.75 V, S19).
- **Absolute maximum ratings** limit the pin voltage relative to the rails (P89LPC935 tolerates 5 V pins at 2.4-3.6 V supply: "5 V tolerant I/O" S8; STM32F103 only on pins marked FT; ATmega-family pins are limited to VCC + 0.5 V, S15 sibling).

### 3.3 How it connects (rail and pin types)
- Supply pins `power_in`; each VDD/VSS pair needs a local ceramic capacitor (100 nF is common practice, ASSUMPTION L; the exact count per part is in each datasheet, not captured here for ST).
- GPIO `bidirectional`; reset `input` (open-drain-like on STM32 NRST), clock/crystal pins `passive`/`input`.
- Analog supply pins (AVCC, VDDA, VREF) must be powered even if the ADC is unused (ATmega328P note S13: "AVCC is the supply voltage pin for the A/D Converter, PC3:0, and ADC7:6").
- Mistakes: 5 V on a non-tolerant pin (D2), floating inputs on CMOS parts (shoot-through current and noise), forgetting the thermal pad, driving the reset pin from a weak source, mixing 1.8 V and 3.3 V banks (iCE40 VCCIO per bank 1.71-3.46 V, S19), removing LRCLK while BCLK runs on the MAX98357A (large DC output offset, S6), unpowered I/O supply while another rail is up.

### 3.4 Electrical model for simulation
Layer L1 (analog interface) plus L2 logic-level semantics. Fidelity `behavioural_approximation` (it is datasheet-point fitting, not a vendor IBIS or SPICE model; an IBIS model would be the next fidelity step and was not available).

Pin subcircuit template (one per GPIO), parameters named for the datasheet quantity:

```
.subckt DIGIF_IO pad vdd vss dout oe din_unused params: VDDN=3.3 RONH=33 RONL=20 CPIN=6p ILEAK=1u VIL_F=0.2 VIH_F=0.7 DCLAMP_IS=1e-14
* pad capacitance and leakage
Cpad pad vss {CPIN}
Bleak pad vss I = {ILEAK}*tanh(v(pad)-v(vss))      ; sign-symmetric leakage to the rail
* clamp diodes: injection current flows when pad goes beyond the rails
.model DCL D(Is={DCLAMP_IS} N=1 Rs=0)
Dh pad vdd DCL
Dl vss pad DCL
* output stage: dout is a logic level 0..1 (L2), oe enables drive
Bdh vdd pad I = v(oe)*v(dout)*(v(vdd)-v(pad))/{RONH}
Bdl pad vss I = v(oe)*(1-v(dout))*(v(pad)-v(vss))/{RONL}
.ends
```
Input logic reading (L2): `logic1 = v(pad) > VIH_F*VDD`, `logic0 = v(pad) < VIL_F*VDD`, undefined between (flag, never silently resolve). Supply: `Bidd vdd vss I = Istatic + Ceff*v(vdd)*f` (bench D4). POR: threshold switch on VDD (bench D3).

Valid analyses: op, dc, tran (digital edges slow compared with ~ns), ac (small-signal pin impedance). Valid range: quasi-static and edge rates of ns and slower; no simultaneous switching noise, no IBIS-style nonlinear driver. Known limitations: linear Ron fit (real VOH/VOL curves bend), no slew-rate control (STM32 has selectable output speeds), no pad-capacitance dependence on bias, injection-induced rail pumping not modelled, no latch-up model, no analog functions (ADC, comparators, PLL), no clock tree.

**What L3 must provide (per part type):**
- MCU: instruction execution and the peripheral set (GPIO registers, timers, UART/SPI/I2C controllers, ADC/DAC, flash, SRAM), reset and boot sequencing (boot pins, fuses), clock tree and PLL, low-power modes with their current. The L1/L2 interface above only sees pins and the supply current an L3 model reports.
- FPGA: the bitstream-defined logic, configuration process (iCE40: CRESET_B low then SPI master load; CDONE goes high when configured, S19), PLL and block RAM.
- PLD (ATF22V10C): the JEDEC fuse map; L2 supplies tPD, tCO, setup and hold per speed grade (S24 gives them, extract M-L).
- RTC (PCF8564A): calendar and alarm registers, I2C slave logic at address A2h write / A3h read (S7), 32.768 kHz oscillator.
- Bridge (CP2104, FT231X): USB device stack and UART engine.
- Audio amp (MAX98357A): I2S decode and class-D modulator; BCLK must be 32, 48 or 64 x LRCLK, LRCLK in {8, 16, 32, 44.1, 48, 88.2, 96} kHz (S6).

### 3.6 Ratings and limits (checks the simulator evaluates)
For each bound part, from its table:
- `v_pin <= VDD + 0.3 V` (or the tolerant limit) and `v_pin >= -0.3 V` (use the part's value; ATmega family -0.5 V per S15).
- `|i_pin_inject| <= I_inj_max` (ST standard I/O 5 mA, first extract only) when the pin exceeds a rail.
- `|i_pin| <= I_pin_max` and `sum(i_vdd) <= I_vdd_max` (STM32F103: 150 mA verified; CP2104: 500 mA verified).
- Supply within the recommended range; ramp rate within limits (iCE40 0.40 to 10 V/ms as stated, extract formatting ambiguous).
- Logic compatibility between a driver and a receiver: `VOH_min >= VIH_min` and `VOL_max <= VIL_max` at the actual load, using the datasheet-point linear fit; otherwise report `level_mismatch`.
- Tj = Ta + RthJA*(VDD*Idd + sum of I/O dissipation) from the package binding.

### 3.7 Failure and misuse behavior

| Mode | Trigger | Physical effect | Simulator response | Permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| input overvoltage above abs max | e.g. 5 V on a non-tolerant 3.3 V pin without series R (D2: pin sits at 3.96 V, 1.04 mA injected through 1 kohm) | clamp diode conducts, rail pumped up, then oxide damage or latch-up | flag when injection exceeds the limit; treat above abs max as FAIL (part damaged) | permanent |
| supply above abs max | e.g. VDD > 4.0 V on STM32F103, > 3.6 V on ESP32-C3, > 1.42 V on iCE40 VCC | gate oxide breakdown | FAIL; do not continue the simulation silently | permanent |
| reverse supply | VDD below VSS | internal diodes conduct heavily | FAIL | permanent |
| output short | pin driven against the driver | current limited by Ron only (about 3.3/20 = 165 mA per D1 numbers, above the 20-25 mA ratings) | FAIL if above `I_pin_max`; report as overcurrent | permanent if sustained |
| floating input | unconnected CMOS input | undefined level, extra supply current | flag `floating_input` (never silently choose 0 or 1) | recoverable |
| reset/POR violated | ramp too slow or too fast, brown-out | undefined logic state | flag; hold outputs undefined until POR release (bench D3) | recoverable |
| latch-up | injection above limit | high-current SCR path | cannot be modelled in SPICE here; flag from injection check | permanent risk |
| ESD | human body model events | latent damage | not simulated; rating only (AT27C256R 2 kV) | permanent |
| thermal | Tj above limit | shutdown or damage | via BEH-PKG-IC-BINDING | per part |

### 3.8 Thermal behavior
Power dissipated: `P = VDD*Idd + sum(VOL/VOH drops times pin currents)`. Example: ESP32-C3 peak transmit 335 mA at 3.3 V is 1.1 W in bursts; with a QFN32 whose RthJA was not obtained, a continuous Tj estimate cannot be made (RESEARCH_REQUIRED). Use BEH-PKG-IC-BINDING for Tj.

### 3.9 Appearance summary
See the 3D spec entries of the bound package (QFP 122-126, QFN 128-131, PLCC 135, BGA 137-138, WLCSP 139). The marking and pin-1 mark are in those entries; the part is identified by the printed part number, not by shape.

| ID | File | Analytic expected | Measured | Match |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | `D1_gpio_drive.cir` | VOL = 5 mA x 20 ohm = 0.100 V; VOH = 3.3 - 5 mA x 33 ohm = 3.135 V | 0.1000, 3.1350 | yes (exact); fit to P89LPC935 worst-case points, prediction at a second load, NOT a datasheet validation |
| D2 | `D2_input_injection.cir` | Shockley fixed point with Is = 1e-14: I = 1.0438 mA, Vpin = 3.9562 V (python iteration) | 1.04377 mA, 3.95623 V | yes (< 0.01 %) |

### 3.12 Sources
See section 1: S6-S19, S23-S26.

### 3.13 Research confidence
(a) Parameters: **L to M**. The big MCU datasheets (ST, Microchip) were largely unreadable past their first pages, so for the ATmega328P, STM32F103, STM32F407 and LPC1768 the VIL/VIH/VOL/VOH tables, per-pin current limits and supply-current-versus-frequency tables are NOT obtained; the P89LPC935 and ESP32-C3 values are from extracts and may contain extraction errors. (b) Ratings: M for STM32F103 supply limits, CP2104, ATF22V10C, iCE40; L elsewhere. (c) Model fidelity: M for the interface model (honest, simple), none for L3. (d) Failure: M (standard CMOS mechanisms, not part-specific tests).

Unresolved items (RESEARCH_REQUIRED): ATmega328P DC table and per-pin limits; STM32F103 I/O static characteristics and Idd-vs-frequency; STM32F407 and LPC1768 electrical tables; Artix-7 abs max and I/O standards (DS181 not opened); RP2040 electrical chapter; nRF52832 and ESP32 (original) specifics; ATF22V10C PLCC-28 pin numbers; DRAM interface (no BGA DRAM datasheet opened).

## 4. BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-MEM-SPINOR

Applies to: OHM-133 (DFN-8) and OHM-134 (WSON-8) as the electrical map for 8-pad SPI NOR flash (plus SOIC-8 and others outside this group); EPROM note for OHM-135. Layer: **L1/L2 for pins, rail and timing; L3 for the command set, the memory array, the status register and the erase/program state machine.**

### 4.1 Purpose and real-world use
Serial NOR flash holds firmware and data for MCUs, FPGAs (iCE40 boots from SPI flash, S19) and ESP-class SoCs (the ESP32-C3 has dedicated SPIHD, SPIWP, SPICS0, SPICLK, SPID, SPIQ pins and a VDD_SPI pin for its flash, S16). Typical parts: Winbond W25Q series (W25Q128JV: 128 Mbit), Microchip SST25VF016B (16 Mbit, EOL). Typical packages: SOIC-8, WSON-8 (6x5), USON/UDFN (2x3, 3x2).

### 4.2 What it is and how it works
Floating-gate NOR cells in sectors (4 KB), blocks (32 KB, 64 KB) and pages (typically 256 bytes). Reads are random access through a serial opcode + 24-bit address; programming can only change 1 to 0 and an erase returns a sector to all ones. A Write Enable latch must be set before program, erase or status-register write; a Write-In-Progress bit is polled through Read Status Register (opcode 05h in both opened datasheets). Program and erase take microseconds to tens of milliseconds, during which the part draws a program/erase current (30 mA max, S22).

### 4.3 How it connects (8-pad map)
W25Q128JV 8-pad WSON (S21, same order as SOIC-8): 1 /CS (input), 2 DO (IO1, output/bidirectional), 3 /WP (IO2), 4 GND, 5 DI (IO0), 6 CLK (input), 7 /HOLD or /RESET (IO3), 8 VCC. In plain SPI mode /WP and /HOLD are control inputs and must be tied to a defined level (pull-up) when unused (general practice, ASSUMPTION M; the datasheet text on internal pull-ups was not visible). The same pin order is used by SOIC-8 versions; the library's DFN-8 (3x3, 0.65 pitch) and WSON-8 (2x2, 0.5 pitch) outlines are **not** the outline of the W25Q WSON (6 x 5 mm, 1.27 pitch), so a footprint mismatch must be flagged when this map is bound to OHM-133 or OHM-134 (see 4.9).
Mistakes: floating /HOLD or /WP, 5 V logic on a 3 V part, two SPI slaves driving DO at the same time (DO is high impedance only when /CS is high: TCHZ 7 ns after CE# high in S22), cutting power during a program or erase, clocking at more than the opcode's maximum (READ 03h: 25 MHz, high-speed read 0Bh: 80 MHz for the SST25VF016B, S22).

### 4.4 Electrical model for simulation
Fidelity `behavioural_approximation`. L1/L2 interface subcircuit (the memory itself is not modeled):

```
.subckt SPINOR_IF cs_n sck di do wp_n hold_n vcc gnd params: CIN=6p VOLMAX=0.4 IOLTEST=1.6m RO=250 oe=1 dout=0
Cin1 cs_n gnd {CIN}
Cin2 sck gnd {CIN}
Cin3 di gnd {CIN}
* DO driver: dout, oe come from the L3 model as 0/1 levels
Bdo_h vcc do I = v(oe)*v(dout)*(v(vcc)-v(do))/{RO}
Bdo_l do gnd I = v(oe)*(1-v(dout))*(v(do)-v(gnd))/{RO}
* supply current by state (the L3 model sets the level of node 'idd_ma')
Bidd vcc gnd I = v(idd_ma)*1e-3
.ends
```
`CIN` is an ASSUMPTION (about 6 pF is common, not sourced). `RO` (250 ohm) is the worst-case fit to VOL <= 0.4 V at IOL = 1.6 mA (S22), which is a limit, not the real driver strength; a typical driver is much stronger (RO about 20-50 ohm, ASSUMPTION L). Valid analyses: tran for pin-level edges, op. Known limitations: no memory array, no command decode, no status register, no timing violation detection (an L3 monitor must do it), no power-loss corruption.

**L3 model requirements (what a higher layer must implement), cited from the opened datasheets:**
1. Command decode in SPI mode 0/3, MSB first. Opcode set (S21 for W25Q128JV Rev F, S22 for SST25VF016B):

   | Function | W25Q128JV (S21) | SST25VF016B (S22) |
   |---|---|---|
   | Write Enable | 06h | 06h (WREN) |
   | Write Disable | 04h | 04h |
   | Read Status Register | 05h (SR-1) | 05h (RDSR) |
   | Write Status Register | 01h | 01h (after EWSR 50h) |
   | Read | 03h | 03h (max 25 MHz; 3 address bytes, 0 dummy) |
   | Fast / High-speed read | 0Bh | 0Bh (1 dummy byte, up to 80 MHz) |
   | Page / byte program | 02h Page Program | 02h Byte-Program (one byte); ADh AAI word program |
   | Sector erase 4 KB | 20h | 20h |
   | Block erase 32 KB / 64 KB | 52h / D8h | 52h / D8h |
   | Chip erase | C7h or 60h | 60h or C7h |
   | JEDEC ID | 9Fh (ID bytes not captured) | 9Fh (ID bytes not captured) |
   | Read ID | not captured | 90h or ABh |
2. Write-enable latch (set by WREN, cleared after program/erase/WRDI), Write-In-Progress flag in the status register, ignoring all but status reads while busy.
3. Timing monitor from S22 (80 MHz table): SCK high/low >= 6 ns, CE# active setup (TCES) >= 5 ns, CE# active hold (TCEH) >= 5 ns, CE# not-active setup/hold (TCHS, TCHH) >= 5 ns, CE# high time (TCPH) >= 50 ns, data setup TDS >= 2 ns, data hold TDH >= 4 ns, output valid TV <= 6 ns, output hold TOH >= 0, CE# high to output Hi-Z TCHZ <= 7 ns, HOLD# setup/hold 5 ns. **The column headings in the extract read "Min" for TV and "Max" for TSE etc.; the physical meaning (TV is a maximum delay) is inferred, not read.** W25Q128JV timing: **not obtained**.
4. Program/erase durations: SST25VF016B sector erase 25 ms max, block erase 25 ms max, chip erase 50 ms max, byte program 10 us max (S22). W25Q128JV: not obtained.
5. Transaction length: CS# low for `(8 + 24 + 8*N)` clocks for a 03h read of N bytes, `(8 + 24 + 8 + 8*N)` for 0Bh (bench F1).
6. Power-up: a read must not start before the part is ready (SST25VF016B TPU-READ not obtained; W25Q VWI/tVSL not obtained).

### 4.6 Ratings and limits
Absolute maximum ratings: **not captured** for the SST25VF016B supplement ("no explicit Absolute Maximum Stress Ratings table is present") and not visible for the W25Q128JV extract; RESEARCH_REQUIRED. Operating: VCC 2.7-3.6 V (S22). Checks: `vcc_ok = 2.7 <= vcc <= 3.6`; `fsck <= 25 MHz for 03h, 80 MHz for 0Bh`; `CS# high >= 50 ns between commands`; `no command except status read while WIP`.

### 4.7 Failure and misuse behavior
| Mode | Trigger | Effect | Simulator response | Permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| power loss during program/erase | VCC drops below the operating range while busy | the sector contents become undefined | L3 marks the affected page/sector `corrupt`; never pretend it completed | permanent data loss, device usable after re-erase |
| VCC out of range | below 2.7 V or above 3.6 V | out of spec, abs max not captured | flag; above abs max (unknown) FAIL | unknown |
| clock too fast for opcode | 03h above 25 MHz | wrong data | L3 returns undefined data and a warning | recoverable |
| /HOLD or /WP floating | open pins | spurious pause or write protection toggling | verifier flag `floating_control_pin` | recoverable |
| bus contention on DO | two drivers active | current in both outputs | flag when DO is driven while CS# is high by another device | possible damage |
| CS# not asserted correctly | CS# glitch | partial command | timing monitor (TCES, TCPH) | recoverable |

### 4.8 Thermal behavior
Negligible for read (20 mA x 3.3 V = 66 mW); program/erase 30 mA x 3.3 V = 99 mW. RthJA not obtained; use the package binding.

### 4.9 Appearance summary
See OHM-133/134 (and SOIC-8 elsewhere). 8-pad WSON has two rows of four pads and a central pad on the underside, pin 1 dimple at the top-left. Library mismatch: W25Q WSON is 6 x 5 mm at 1.27 mm pitch (S21 lists "8-pad WSON"; the 6 x 5 body size comes from distributor listings returned by search, not from the opened datasheet text) versus the library's 3 x 3 and 2 x 2 bodies.

Unresolved: W25Q128JV VCC range, AC timing, program/erase times, JEDEC ID (EF 40 18 is widely quoted but was NOT in an opened document), power-up timing; abs max for both; exposed-pad connection rule for 8-pad WSON/USON flash; QPI/dual-quad opcodes.

### 4.14 Note: parallel EPROM in a PLCC (not 28 pins)
AT27C256R (S23): 32K x 8 OTP EPROM, 45 ns access, 5 V +/-10 %, 20 mA active max at 5 MHz, 100 uA CMOS standby, packages 28-pin PDIP and **32-pin PLCC**. Its L2 interface is the classic asynchronous memory read: address in, CE#/OE# low, data out after tACC (45 to 70 ns grade dependent), outputs Hi-Z when CE# or OE# is high. A 32-pin PLCC does not fit OHM-135 (28 leads). The PLCC-32 pin map was not captured; do not bind it to OHM-135.
