## 5. BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-REG-BUCK-DCS

Applies to: OHM-134 (WSON-8: TPS62160/61/62/63 family, 1 A) and OHM-127 (QFN-16: TPS62130 family, 3 A). The TPS6216x in its 2x2 mm WSON-8 DSG matches the 3D spec's WSON-8 exactly (the spec's pad value comes from the same TI DSG drawing); the TPS6213x in its 3x3 mm VQFN-16 RGT matches OHM-127. Layer: **L1** (stock ngspice 42, no XSPICE, B sources and R, L, C only). Fidelity: **behavioural_approximation**. This is NOT the TI model; TI publishes PSpice/TINA models that were not opened or attached.

### 5.1 Purpose and real-world use
A step-down (buck) converter makes a lower DC rail from a higher one with 85 to 95 percent efficiency, where a linear regulator would burn `(Vin-Vout)*Iout`. TPS62160/61/62/63: 3 to 17 V in, 0.9 to 6 V out (adjustable, or fixed 1.8, 3.3, 5.0 V in TPS62161/62/63), up to 1 A; TPS62130 family: 3 to 17 V in, up to 3 A (S1, S2). Typical use: 12 V or 5 V board rail to 3.3 V or 1.8 V for MCUs, FPGAs, sensors. Recommended passives: L 2.2 uH (3.3 uH at low input voltage), Cout 22 uF X7R/X5R, Cin 10 uF (S1 extract).

### 5.2 What it is and how it works
Synchronous buck: high-side switch HS from VIN to the SW node, low-side switch LS from SW to ground, inductor L from SW to the output, output capacitor Cout. In CCM the duty is `D = Vout/Vin` (ideal), the inductor ripple is `dIL = (Vin-Vout)*D/(L*fsw)` and the output ripple is set by Cout and its ESR. At light load the converter enters power-save mode (pulse skipping): the frequency falls roughly in proportion to the load.
Control: the TI devices use **DCS-Control** (S1, S2: "Direct Control with Seamless transition into power save mode"), a hysteretic-derived topology with an on-time estimate. The datasheet states (S1, confirmed in two queries): `tON = 420 x (VOUT/VIN) ns` for the TPS6216x; the TPS6213x gives `tON = 400 x VOUT/VIN ns` with FSW low and an absolute minimum on-time of about 80 ns (S2). Hence `fsw = D/tON = 1/K`: 2.38 MHz for K = 420 ns (datasheet text "approximately 2.25 MHz" in PWM, S1) and 2.5 MHz for K = 400 ns ("typically 2.5 MHz", S2). That consistency is the only external check on the control constant. DCS-Control's inner fast loop is not public in the opened text; the model replaces it with a **valley-triggered constant-on-time (COT) loop** that has the same tON law and the same power-save behavior (pulse on demand).

### 5.3 How it connects
TPS6216x WSON-8 DSG (S1): 1 PGND, 2 VIN, 3 EN, 4 AGND, 5 FB (adjustable; tied to AGND on fixed versions), 6 VOS (output sense for the control loop), 7 SW, 8 PG (open drain power-good, needs a pull-up), exposed pad = AGND, must be soldered.
TPS6213x VQFN-16 RGT (S2): 1, 2, 3 SW; 4 PG; 5 FB; 6 AGND; 7 FSW (low about 2.5 MHz, high about 1.25 MHz); 8 DEF (output scaling, low = nominal, high = +5 percent); 9 SS/TR (soft-start/tracking capacitor); 10 AVIN; 11, 12 PVIN; 13 EN; 14 VOS; 15, 16 PGND; exposed pad connected to AGND, PGND and the ground plane.
Typical circuit: Cin close to VIN/PGND, L from SW to Vout, Cout at Vout, VOS (and FB on adjustable) to the output.
Mistakes: leaving the EP unsoldered or unconnected, putting a large derated capacitance assumption into the model (a 22 uF X5R at 3.3 V can be far less than 22 uF; the DC-bias derating is in the capacitor classes, not here), using an inductor that saturates below the current limit, floating EN, forgetting the PG pull-up, running with `VIN < VOUT + dropout` (100 percent duty mode), putting the load above the 1 A or 3 A rating.

### 5.4 Electrical model for simulation
Layer L1, ngspice 42. Netlist template (the file `bench/reg-buck-dcs/buck_core.inc` is the tested artifact; it includes the inductor so the model can see its own current):

```
.subckt BUCKCORE vin gnd vout vos en params: K=420n RHS=0.4 RLS=0.16 VSET=3.3 IQ=17u RDIS=10 CSWP=100p L=2.2u DCR=0.05 RINJ=10m
Ben enl gnd V = 0.5*(1+tanh((v(en)-v(gnd)-1)/0.1))
Cq q gnd 1p ic=0
Bq gnd q I = 1e-3*( 4*v(setc)*(1-v(q)) - 4*v(rstc)*v(q) + 0.5*v(q)*(1-v(q))*(2*v(q)-1) )
Bqd qd gnd V = 0.5*(1+tanh((v(q)-0.5)/0.05))
Bset setc gnd V = v(enl)*0.5*(1+tanh((VSET-v(vos)-RINJ*(v(vx)-v(vout))/DCR)/2m))*0.5*(1+tanh((0.15-v(vr))/20m))
Brst rstc gnd V = 0.5*(1+tanh((v(vr)-v(vout))/2m)) + (1-v(enl))
Cr vr gnd 1n ic=0
Bch gnd vr I = v(qd)*(1n/K)*(v(vin)-v(gnd)) - (1-v(qd))*v(vr)/RDIS
Bhs vin sw I = (v(vin)-v(sw))*(v(qd)/RHS + 1u)
Bls sw gnd I = (v(sw)-v(gnd))*((1-v(qd))*v(enl)/RLS*0.5*(1+tanh(-(v(sw)-v(gnd))/5m)) + 1u)
Csw sw gnd {CSWP}
Rswd sw gnd 10Meg
Lx sw vx {L}
Rdcr vx vout {DCR}
Biq vin gnd I = IQ*v(enl)
.ends
```
How it works: a latch `q` (bistable B-source with a regenerative term) sets when the sensed output (plus `RINJ x IL`) falls below `VSET`, and resets when the on-time ramp `vr` reaches `Vout`. The ramp charges with current `(1 nF/K) x Vin` while on, so the on-time is `Cr x Vout/(gm x Vin) = K x Vout/Vin`, exactly the datasheet law. The low-side element conducts only while SW is below ground, an ideal-diode synchronous rectifier that gives a clean DCM cutoff (pulse skipping). Run with `.tran 1n ... uic` and `Cout ic = Vout`; the model does not soft-start.

Mapping to datasheet quantities: `K` = tON coefficient (420 ns, 400 ns), `RHS`, `RLS` = RDS(on) of the two switches (TPS62160: HS 300-600 mOhm, LS 120-200 mOhm at VIN >= 6 V, min to max range, extract; the defaults 0.4 and 0.16 ohm are mid-range ASSUMPTIONS; TPS62130: HS 90 mOhm typ (170 max), LS 40 mOhm typ (70 max), S2), `IQ` = quiescent current 17 uA typ (S1, S2), `VSET` = regulation point (fixed output version voltage), `L`, `DCR` = external inductor (2.2 uH recommended; DCR 50 mOhm is an ASSUMPTION).
Ideal versus realistic: `RINJ`, `CSWP`, `RDIS`, `DCR` are the realism knobs. `RINJ` (default 10 mOhm) is an **ASSUMPTION, not a datasheet value**: with `RINJ = 0` and pure-ceramic Cout the loop sub-harmonically oscillates (observed in the build: inductor current swung 0 to 2.05 A at a 1 A load), which is a known weakness of constant-on-time loops without ripple injection. `RINJ` also produces a load regulation of `RINJ x dIout` (bench B3: 8.8 mV for a 0.9 A step, 9.0 mV predicted).
Valid analyses: tran (the only meaningful one); op does not apply to a switching model. For a loop-gain or ac analysis an averaged model would be needed; not provided. Valid range: Vin 3 to 17 V, Iout up to the device rating, Cout 22 uF class. Fidelity label: behavioural_approximation.
Known limitations (where the model is wrong): no soft start (datasheet: about 50 us delay then 25 mV/us slope, S1 extract), no UVLO (2.7 V falling, 180 mV hysteresis, S1), no current limit and no short-circuit hiccup (forward limit typ 1.95 A for TPS62160 with 1.45-2.45 A spread; 4.2 A typ for TPS62130 with 3.6-4.9 A, S1/S2), no thermal shutdown (160 C), no 100 percent duty mode, no power-good output, no tracking or DEF/FSW pins, no inductor saturation, no capacitor derating, efficiency overhead of about 0.09 W at 2.5 MHz and 2 A that is a numerical artifact of non-ideal switch overlap and not a real loss (see 5.10), light-load efficiency probably too optimistic (no controller quiescent power beyond IQ, no gate-drive loss beyond the lumped CSWP), no EMI/ringing fidelity.

| RINJ | ohm | 0.010 | 0 | 0.03 | | ASSUMPTION | L | none |
| CSWP | pF | 100 | 10 | 300 | | ASSUMPTION | L | none |
| DCR | ohm | 0.05 (62160 bench) / 0.02 (62130 bench) | | | | ASSUMPTION | L | none |

### 5.6 Ratings and limits
From S1/S2 (extract): VIN -0.3..20 V; EN, SW (DC) -0.3..VIN+0.3 V; FB, PG, VOS (and DEF, FSW on the 3 A part) -0.3..7 V; PG sink current 10 mA (S2); junction -40..150 C abs, -40..125 C recommended; recommended VIN 3..17 V.
Checks: `vin_ok = 3 <= vin <= 17`; `abs_vin = vin <= 20`; `ipeak = iout + dIL/2 <= ILIM_min (1.45 A or 3.6 A)`; `iout <= 1 A (62160) or 3 A (62130)`; `tj = ta + RthJA*Ploss <= 125 C` with `Ploss = Pout*(1/eta - 1)` from the simulation and RthJA from the package binding (TPS62160 DSG 61.8 K/W, TPS62130 RGT 45 K/W).

### 5.7 Failure and misuse behavior
| Mode | Trigger | Physical effect | Simulator response | Permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| VIN above 20 V | spike | die breakdown | FAIL | permanent |
| VIN below UVLO (2.7 V falling) | brown-out | converter stops | the model does not implement UVLO: the checker must mask the output; flag `uvlo_not_modelled` | recoverable |
| overcurrent | load above 1 A / 3 A, or inductor saturation | current limit (about 1.95 A), then foldback or hiccup (not described in the opened text) | check `ipeak` and flag `current_limit_region`; no clamp in the model | recoverable |
| output short | short on VOUT | current limit, short-circuit protection (S1 features list) | flag | recoverable |
| overtemperature | Tj above 160 C | thermal shutdown | flag via package binding | recoverable (restart after cooldown) |
| EP not soldered | assembly | thermal (RthJA far above the WSON value, compare 184.3 K/W for the pad-less VSSOP, S1) and AGND quality | flag via binding | recoverable |
| FB, VOS, PG above 7 V | wiring | abs max | FAIL | permanent |
| EN floating | design | undefined | flag | recoverable |
| capacitor derating | high DC bias | instability or higher ripple | not modelled here; capacitor class applies | n/a |

### 5.8 Thermal behavior
`Ploss = Vin*Iin - Vout*Iout`. From the simulation at 1 A (TPS62160 parameters): Pout = 3.29 W, eta = 0.892, Ploss = 0.40 W, Tj rise = 0.40 x 61.8 = 24.8 K (RthJA S1). TPS62130 at 2 A (bench B4): Ploss = 6.556 x (1/0.931 - 1) = 0.486 W, rise = 0.486 x 45 = 21.9 K. These are derived estimates; the model's own loss includes the 0.09 W artifact described in 5.10 (about 20 percent of the 2 A loss), so treat the Tj figure as an upper estimate.

### 5.9 Appearance summary
OHM-134 WSON-8 2x2 mm, 0.5 pitch, pad 0.9 x 1.6 mm (TI DSG0008B, spec entry); OHM-127 QFN-16 3x3 mm, 0.5 pitch with a square pad (spec: 1.6 x 1.6). Both have a dimple at the pin-1 corner and a bare-copper pad on the underside. See the 3D spec.

### 5.10 Validation benches (ngspice 42; run `bench/reg-buck-dcs/run_all.sh`, raw `results_ngspice42.txt`)
| ID | File | Condition | Analytic expected | Measured | Match |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | `B1_steady_state.cir` | 12 V to 3.3 V, 1 A, 2.2 uH, 22 uF, K = 420 ns | fsw = 1/K = 2.381 MHz (lossless), 2.59 MHz with the conduction-loss duty correction; dIL = (Vin-Vo) tON/L = 0.457 A | fsw = 2.505 MHz (+5.2 % vs lossless, within the two bounds); dIL = 0.463 A (+1.3 %); Vout mean 3.296 V | yes (10 % and 15 % tolerances) |
| B2 | `B2_efficiency.cir` + `run_all.sh` | same, loads 10 mA, 100 mA, 500 mA, 1 A | 1 A: 91.9 % conduction-only, 89.6 % with the disclosed 0.09 W model overhead; DCM frequency fsw = Iout/Qpulse with Qpulse = 0.5 Ipk (tON + tfall) = 96 nC gives 104 kHz at 10 mA, 1.04 MHz at 100 mA | eta = 93.5 %, 94.9 %, 91.9 %, 89.2 %; fsw = 89 kHz, 997 kHz, 2.38 MHz, 2.52 MHz | 1 A efficiency within 0.4 point of the corrected analytic; fsw within 14 % at 10 mA and 4 % at 100 mA |
| B3 | `B3_load_step.cir` | 0.1 A to 1.0 A, 10 ns edge | catch-up charge gives 4.7 mV plus ESR step 4.5 mV; allowed window 5-30 mV; load regulation RINJ x 0.9 A = 9.0 mV | total deviation 10.2 mV, of which 8.8 mV is the DC load-regulation term; overshoot on release 2.6 mV | yes, but see the warning below |
| B4 | `B4_tps62130_variant.cir` | 12 V to 3.3 V, 2 A, K = 400 ns, 1 uH | fsw = 1/K = 2.50 MHz; dIL = 0.957 A; efficiency (conduction) 95.7 %, 93.97 % with overhead | fsw = 2.519 MHz (+0.7 %); dIL = 1.015 A (+6 %); eta = 93.1 % | yes (fsw 5 %, dIL 10 %, eta 1.5 point) |
| B5 | `B5_line_regulation.cir` | Vin 6, 12, 17 V, 0.5 A | Vout mean independent of Vin to first order, 3.28-3.32 V | 3.3002, 3.3013, 3.3018 V (1.6 mV spread) | yes |

**Warnings.** (1) B3's 10.2 mV is dominated by the assumed `RINJ`: the transient excess beyond the DC term is only 1.4 mV, so the model does not predict a real converter's load-transient droop (the extract's "5-10 percent deviation" statement for the TPS62160 was not verified). (2) Light-load efficiency (93 to 95 percent at 10 to 100 mA) is probably higher than the real device; no datasheet efficiency curve numbers were readable (the extract said only "about 85-90 percent at 100 mA, 90-92 percent at 1 A" and cannot be used as a check). (3) The fixed 0.09 W loss seen with ideal switches (efficiency 98.7 percent with 1 mOhm switches) is a model artifact. The sourced element of validation is only the tON law, the 1/K frequency, and the ripple formula.

## 6. BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-PWR-LOADSWITCH

Applies to: OHM-132 (DFN-6: TPS22810 in WSON-6 DRV, 2x2 mm, 0.65 pitch) and OHM-140 (WLCSP-16: NX5P3290 power switch). The TPS7A80 LDO in VSON-8 DRB is bound to OHM-133 but its behavior is the existing class BEH-REG-LINEAR (parts/R6.md), not redefined here. Layer **L1**, fidelity **behavioural_approximation**.

### 6.1 Purpose
A load switch (high-side pass FET with enable, UVLO and slew control) connects or isolates a rail to a downstream block: power sequencing, leakage isolation, inrush control, short-circuit containment. TPS22810: 2.7 to 18 V, 2 A class, RON 79 mOhm typ at the bench condition (S4 extract, value quoted from the opened document; the extract gave 79 mOhm and a 3 A bench drop was used only as a model check, not as a rating). NX5P3290: USB-C power switch, VBUS to 29 V, RON 35 mOhm typ, adjustable current limit, Rth(j-a) 58.4 K/W (S5).

### 6.2 How it works
A P- or N-channel (with charge pump, VCP pin on NX5P3290) FET in series with the load. Drop `V = I*RON` below the limit. A current limiter clamps `I` near ILIM and the FET then dissipates `(Vin-Vout)*ILIM`, which triggers thermal shutdown if sustained. UVLO keeps it off below a threshold. Turn-on is slew limited (CT pin on TPS22810 sets the rise time; QOD pin gives quick output discharge). The switch conducts in reverse through its body diode unless reverse-current blocking is provided (NX5P3290 has it; the model does not).

### 6.3 Connections
TPS22810 WSON-6 DRV (S4): 1 VOUT, 2 QOD, 3 CT, 4 GND, 5 EN/UVLO, 6 VIN; exposed pad: RESEARCH_REQUIRED whether tied to GND (not captured; the standard TI practice is to solder to GND, label ASSUMPTION L).
NX5P3290 WLCSP16 (S5, transparent top view = OHMNI convention): VIN A1/A2 (ganged), ILIM A3, /FLT A4, VCP B1/B2/C1 (ganged), GND B3/C3/D3, EN B4, VBUS C2/D1/D2, FO C4, CAP D4. Ganged balls must be tied.
Mistakes: floating EN, output capacitance larger than the inrush limit, reverse bias on a part without reverse blocking, power dissipation in current limit.

### 6.4 Model
File `bench/pwr-loadswitch/loadsw.inc`: `.subckt LOADSW vin vout en gnd params: RON ILIM VUVLO TON`. Current from vin to vout: `I = (Vd/RON) / (1 + (Vd/(RON*ILIM))^4)^0.25` multiplied by an enable gate (EN threshold) and a smooth UVLO gate of 5 mV width, with a first-order lag of time constant TON. `Vd = Vin - Vout`. Ohmic below the limit and asymptotically clamped at ILIM. Reverse current is NOT blocked (limitation). Valid analyses: op, dc, tran. Not modelled: slew control, quick output discharge, thermal shutdown, fault flag, reverse-current blocking, RON temperature dependence.

### 6.5 Parameters
| name | unit | default | basis | confidence | source |

| RON TPS22810 | ohm | 0.079 | MFR_DATASHEET (extract; test condition not captured) | M-L | S4 |
| RON NX5P3290 | ohm | 0.035 | MFR_DATASHEET | M | S5 |
| ILIM | A | per part / ILIM pin resistor (NX5P3290); TPS22810 has no current limit in the opened text | M-L | | S4, S5 |
| VUVLO | V | 2.54 bench value (TPS22810 UVLO value not verified; ASSUMPTION for the model) | ASSUMPTION | L | none |
| TON | s | 20 us | ASSUMPTION | L | none |
| VIN range TPS22810 | V | 2.7 to 18 | MFR_DATASHEET | M | S4 |

### 6.6 Ratings and checks
`vin <= VINmax`, `iout <= Irated`, `tj = ta + Rth*(I^2*RON)` below the limit (125 C recommended class, abs max per datasheet; exact limits RESEARCH_REQUIRED for TPS22810). In current limit use `P = (Vin-Vout)*ILIM`.

### 6.7 Failure and misuse
| Mode | Effect | Simulator response |
|---|---|---|
| VIN above abs max | FET breakdown | FAIL, permanent |
| short on VOUT | current limit then thermal shutdown (NX5P3290 flags /FLT) | clamp at ILIM, flag `current_limit`, report P |
| overtemperature | shutdown | flag via binding, recoverable |
| reverse voltage (VOUT > VIN) | body diode conducts (TPS22810), blocked on NX5P3290 | model conducts as a resistor: flag `reverse_current_unmodelled` |
| EN floating | undefined | flag |

### 6.8 Thermal
Conduction dissipation `I^2*RON`. Bench L1: 3 A through 79 mOhm gives 0.712 W, a rise of 53.1 K with 74.6 K/W (this current exceeds a conservative rating and is a model check only; real use must respect the datasheet current limit).

### 6.9 Appearance
OHM-132 is a 2x2 mm six-pad WSON with a dimple and centre pad; OHM-140 is a 16-ball WLCSP with a dark die face. See the 3D spec.

### 6.10 Validation benches (ngspice 42; `bench/pwr-loadswitch/run_all.sh`)
| ID | File | Condition | Expected | Measured | Match |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | `L1_ron_drop.cir` | 3 A, RON 79 mOhm | Vdrop = I*RON = 0.237 V; P = 0.711 W; dT = 53.0 K | 0.2375 V; 0.712 W; 53.1 K | yes |
| L2 | `L2_uvlo.cir` | VIN ramp, UVLO 2.54 V, 5 mV width | output on near 2.54 V, off at 2.4 V | on at about 2.526 V; Vout at 2.4 V = 2.4e-7 V | yes (within 15 mV, set by the 5 mV gate and the series drop) |
| L3 | `L3_current_limit.cir` | hard short, ILIM 1.5 A | I = 1.5 A with the clamp; an unclamped RON would give 0.99 A in the same circuit (series resistance limit) | 1.500 A clamped; 0.9927 A unclamped reference | yes (the clamp is effective only when the external resistance allows more than ILIM; the unclamped reference proves the circuit differs) |

Caveat: L3's two numbers come from different circuits; the unclamped figure is a reference for the circuit's own series limit and not a prediction of the real part.

## 7. PER-ENTRY SECTIONS (OHM-122 .. OHM-140)

Common rules: every entry is a PACKAGE. Behavior comes from the bound part through BEH-PKG-IC-BINDING (section 2) plus the part class. An entry with no bound, verified part has status `unbound`, never pass. Thermal values are RthJA from the datasheet of the named part (JEDEC board, so they are not transferable between parts); parasitic values come from the class table in section 2 (sources S27-S31, conflicts shown there). Map convention for leaded and QFN packages: pin 1 at the marked corner, counter-clockwise numbering in the top view; BGA/WLCSP: row letter plus column number, A1 top-left in the top view (datasheet bottom views are mirrored, convert).

## [OHM-122] QFP-32 -> BEH-PKG-IC-BINDING + BEH-IC-DIGITAL-IF
- Pins 32, 8 per side. Reference: ATmega328P in TQFP-32 (package code 32A, S13/S14), speeds 0-4 MHz at 1.8-5.5 V, 0-10 MHz at 2.7-5.5 V, 0-20 MHz at 4.5-5.5 V.
- Pin numbering: RESEARCH_REQUIRED (extract returned text-flow order and was rejected). The commonly used map is an ASSUMPTION, confidence L, and must not be auto-bound until checked against the datasheet figure.
- Thermal and parasitics: RthJA RESEARCH_REQUIRED for this part; class values in section 2.
- No exposed pad. Status: **partial** (pin numbers assumption).

## [OHM-123] TQFP-44 -> BEH-PKG-IC-BINDING
- Pins 44, 11 per side. Package verified as NXP SOT376-1, 10x10x1.0 mm (S32).
- Reference ATmega32U4 was NOT verified in an opened datasheet: RESEARCH_REQUIRED. No bound part. Status: **partial**.

## [OHM-124] TQFP-64 -> BEH-PKG-IC-BINDING + BEH-IC-DIGITAL-IF
- Pins 64, 16 per side. References: STM32F103RB in LQFP64 (S10; VBAT pin 1, OSC_IN 5, OSC_OUT 6, NRST 7, PA9 42, PA10 43, BOOT0 60, VSS/VDD pairs 31/32, 47/48, 63/64 per extract; rows partly noisy, verify before binding), RthJA 45 K/W (S11 verbatim table). PCF85176H on SOT357-1 (TQFP64 10x10x1.0, S32).
- Conflict: ST LQFP64 is the 1.4 mm height class; library TQFP is 1.0 mm. Same 10x10 outline and 0.5 pitch, different height: flag in binding, electrical map unaffected.
- No exposed pad. Status: **complete for outline, partial for pin rows** (the pin table must be re-verified).

## [OHM-125] TQFP-100 -> BEH-PKG-IC-BINDING + BEH-IC-DIGITAL-IF
- Pins 100, 25 per side. References: STM32F103 LQFP100 (RthJA 46 K/W, S11; PA9 pin 68, PA10 pin 69, BOOT0 pin 94); LPC1768 LQFP100 SOT407-1 14x14x1.4, 0.5 pitch (S9, S32); Lattice iCE40 VQ100 14x14, 0.5 pitch (S19).
- Same height-class conflict as OHM-124 (1.4 mm vs 1.0 mm). Status: **partial** (full pin tables not captured).

## [OHM-126] LQFP-144 -> BEH-PKG-IC-BINDING

# R8 Frequency control: crystals, oscillators, resonators, SAW (OHM-141 to OHM-149)

Group R8 covers nine entries in four behavior classes:

| Class | Layer | Entries |
|---|---|---|
| BEH-FREQ-XTAL (quartz crystal unit, 2 or 4 pads) | L1 | OHM-141, 142, 143, 144, 145 |
| BEH-FREQ-XO (packaged oscillator, incl. TCXO variant) | L2 (supply current L1) | OHM-146, 147 |
| BEH-FREQ-CERRES (3-pin ceramic resonator with built-in capacitors) | L1 | OHM-148 |
| BEH-FREQ-SAW (SAW band-pass filter) | L1 behavioral | OHM-149 |

All benches live under `/home/claude/behavior/bench/{xtal-bvd,osc-pierce,xtal-resonator,osc-clock,saw-bpf}/`. Every measured number below was produced here with `ngspice -b` (ngspice-42, no XSPICE needed; only R, L, C, B-sources, `tanh`, `PULSE`, ternary in B-source). Fidelity vocabulary follows `src/ohmni/eda/simulation.py`: everything here is `behavioural_approximation`. No vendor model is attached for any entry, so `vendor_model` is never claimed. A run that did not complete is never a pass (the Pierce start-up benches are explicit about the kick and step used).

Honesty notes that apply to the whole group:
* Quartz motional parameters (C1, L1) are almost never printed on mainstream datasheets. Opened datasheets give ESR (R1) max, C0 max/typ, CL, drive level, tolerance, stability and aging. Only the Epson FC-135 sheet printed C1 (3.4 fF typ). All other default C1 values below are labelled ASSUMPTION or taken from a generic range (Suntsu, Microchip) and are not part-specific.
* Microchip AN826 could not be opened (robots.txt refused the fetch) and is not cited. ST AN2867 content was opened and is cited.
* "Frequency" benches are only as exact as the ngspice integrator. Trapezoidal integration at step h shifts a measured oscillation frequency by about -(2*pi*f*h)^2/12 (found and confirmed in this work: 2 ns step at 8 MHz gave 7.9933 MHz, a -840 ppm artifact; 0.2 ns gave 8.00047 MHz). Any implementer measuring ppm-level accuracy must use steps of 1/5000 period or better, or use AC/phase analysis (B2/B3 in xtal-bvd and B2 in osc-pierce).

---

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-FREQ-XTAL

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
A quartz crystal unit is a passive electromechanical resonator. Placed between the input and output of an inverting amplifier (the oscillator block inside a microcontroller, RTC, Ethernet PHY, USB/radio chip) it makes the amplifier oscillate at a frequency fixed by the quartz plate, with an accuracy of tens of ppm and a stability a ceramic resonator or RC oscillator cannot reach. Typical uses: MCU main clock (4 to 48 MHz fundamental AT-cut), RTC (32.768 kHz tuning fork), USB (12/48 MHz), Ethernet (25 MHz), radio reference (16 to 40 MHz). Common values: 32.768 kHz, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 25, 26, 27, 32 MHz. Common load capacitances: 6, 8, 9, 12.5, 15, 18, 20 pF.

A crystal alone does nothing: it is not a clock source. It becomes one only together with an active circuit (Pierce oscillator) and two load capacitors. That is why OHMNI models the crystal at L1 and provides the oscillator circuit as a separate netlist fragment, not as a property of the crystal.

### 2. What it is and how it works
Construction: a thin AT-cut (MHz range) or tuning-fork cut (32.768 kHz) quartz blank with metal electrodes, sealed in a hermetic package (HC-49 metal can with two wire leads; ceramic SMD package with a welded metal lid). Quartz is piezoelectric: a voltage across the electrodes deforms the plate, and the deformation produces a charge. The mechanical resonance has a very high Q (tens of thousands), so electrically the crystal is a series RLC motional arm in parallel with the electrode/package capacitance.

Butterworth-Van Dyke (BVD) equivalent circuit (ST AN2867 section 1; Suntsu equivalent-circuit note; TI SLLA549):
* R1 (Rm, motional resistance, equals the datasheet ESR at series resonance), L1 (Lm, motional inductance, vibrating mass), C1 (Cm, motional capacitance, elasticity) in series;
* C0 (shunt capacitance, electrodes plus holder) across the whole series arm.

Key equations (all verified by bench xtal-bvd B1/B2/B3):
* Series resonance: fs = 1 / (2*pi*sqrt(L1*C1)). Impedance magnitude is minimal and equals R1 (bench: 79.99 ohm at 7.998285 MHz).
* Parallel (anti-)resonance: fa = fs*sqrt(1 + C1/C0). With C1 = 9 fF and C0 = 3 pF, fa - fs = 12 kHz (bench: 8.010276 MHz). Impedance is a maximum, about 548 kohm here, limited by R1.
* Between fs and fa the crystal is inductive. An oscillator operates there, at the load frequency fL with the external load CL in series with the crystal: fL = fs*sqrt(1 + C1/(C0 + CL)) (exact lossless result; ST gives the approximation Fp = Fs*sqrt(1 + C1/(2C0+2CL)) which is the same to first order only if C1/(C0+CL) is small and uses 2C instead of C inside the root, so the two differ in the third decimal of the shift). The datasheet frequency "at CL = 18 pF" means fL at that CL, not fs.
* Pulling sensitivity S = (1/f)(df/dCL) = -C1 / (2*(C0+CL)^2). For C1 = 9 fF, C0 = 3 pF, CL = 18 pF: -10.2 ppm per pF. Bench B2 table below.
* Q = 2*pi*fs*L1 / R1. For 8 MHz, L1 = 44 mH, R1 = 80 ohm, Q = 27.6k. Q is high so L1 is large: 44 mH at 8 MHz, 6.94 kH at 32.768 kHz (bench B3 in xtal-bvd).
* Thomson relation used to derive L1 from a given C1: L1 = 1/((2*pi*fs)^2 * C1) (Suntsu).

Frequency tolerance, temperature stability and aging are separate numbers (Abracon ABLS: tolerance +/-50 ppm at 25 C, stability +/-50 ppm over 0 to +70 C referenced to 25 C, aging +/-5 ppm first year; Epson FC-135: +/-20 ppm at 25 C, turnover temperature 25 +/- 5 C, parabolic coefficient -0.04 ppm/C^2, aging +/-3 ppm/year; Epson FA-238: +/-50 ppm, +/-30 ppm over -20 to +70 C, aging +/-5 ppm/year; TSX-3225 +/-10 ppm, aging +/-1 ppm/year). Tuning-fork crystals follow a parabola: delta_f/f = -0.04e-6 * (T - T0)^2 (FC-135: at +85 C about -144 ppm, at -40 C about -169 ppm with T0 = 25). AT-cut crystals follow a cubic (S-shaped) curve; the exact coefficients are not on opened datasheets, so the model uses the stability band as a bound only.

Fundamental versus overtone: a fundamental crystal vibrates in its lowest mode, practical to about 50 MHz for stamped AT blanks (ABLS fundamental to 24 MHz, ABM3 fundamental 8 to 54 MHz). Higher frequencies use the 3rd overtone (ABLS 24.01 to 75 MHz at ESR 80-100 ohm; ABM3 54.1 to 80 MHz at 60 ohm). An overtone crystal in a plain Pierce stage with no selective network can lock on the fundamental or a spurious mode, because the amplifier has gain at both. The BVD model here is the fundamental/main-mode arm only; spurious modes are not modeled (limitation).

Drive level: the power dissipated in R1, DL = R1 * Irms^2 (ST AN2867 3.5.1). Peak-to-peak crystal current limit IQmaxPP = 2*sqrt(2*DLmax/R1). Datasheet drive levels: 0.5 uW (FC-135, 1.0 uW max available), 10 uW recommended and 200 uW max (Epson FA-238, NDK NX3225GD: 10 uW, max 200 uW), Abracon ABM3 10 to 100 uW (as printed "10 100 uW"), Abracon ABLS "100 1000 uW" (as printed; typical and max are not labelled in the extraction). Over-driving makes the frequency drift, raises ESR (drive-level dependency, "DLD": Abracon ABLS limits frequency change to < +/-10 ppm and ESR change to < 25 % of max ESR across the drive range), and at the extreme fractures the blank or electrode (ST: "mechanical damage or shortened lifetime", jitter and distorted duty cycle).

Working with an oscillator circuit (Pierce, Section 3 of this class and bench osc-pierce): the crystal sits between the inverter input (XIN) and output (XOUT); two capacitors C1 and C2 go from XIN and XOUT to ground; a feedback resistor Rf (about 1 Mohm) biases the inverter linear; an optional series resistor Rext limits drive level.

### 3. How it connects
Pins: two terminals A and B (non-polarized). The 4-pad SMD packages bring the crystal to diagonally opposite pads 1 and 3; pads 2 and 4 are tied to the metal lid, and datasheets call them GND or NC. Epson FA-238V/FA-238/TSX-3225 (opened): "pads #2 and #4 connect to cover (GND); #1 and #3 are crystal terminals". NDK NX3225GD and Abracon ABM3/ABLS sheets opened did not state pad assignment in extractable text (3D spec cites the NDK/Epson convention). HC-49 has two leads; 3-pin case-ground HC-49 variants are not modeled.

Typical circuit (STM32/ATmega-style): XIN - crystal - XOUT, CL1 and CL2 to GND, Rf inside the chip or 1 Mohm external, optional 100 to 600 ohm Rext at XOUT.

Load capacitor math (ST AN2867 3.3): CL = CL1*CL2/(CL1+CL2) + Cs, so for CL1 = CL2 = C: CL = C/2 + Cs, C = 2*(CL - Cs). ST's example: CL = 15 pF with 5 pF stray gives CL1 = CL2 = 20 pF. Important finding from the benches here: Cs in that formula is a lumped fudge for pin plus trace capacitance. If each pin has a ground stray cp, the exact effective load is (C + cp)/2, so Cs = cp/2. A stray modeled as a capacitor directly across XIN-XOUT (Miller position) is wrong for the sim: it bridges the amplifier and destroys the negative resistance (bench exploration: Re(Z) became +245 ohm instead of -1449 ohm). Model strays from each pin to ground.

Frequent mistakes:
1. Ignoring pin and trace capacitance when picking CL1/CL2, so the clock is off by tens of ppm (10 ppm per pF of error at 8 MHz, 18 pF crystal).
2. Choosing a high-ESR small-package crystal with a weak MCU oscillator. Example from opened datasheets: NDK NX3225GD at 8 to 9.8 MHz has ESR max 500 ohm; Abracon ABM3 (5.0 x 3.2 mm) at 8 to 9 MHz has 140 ohm; Abracon HC49/US at 8 MHz has 80 ohm. Gain margin shrinks as ESR grows (bench B6).
3. Using parallel-resonant crystals in a series-resonant oscillator or vice versa. Datasheet frequency specified "at CL = x pF" implies parallel (load) operation. A "series" crystal (no CL stated) runs at fs.
4. Driving too hard: 3.3 V CMOS output into a 3225 crystal at 10 uW recommended can exceed the limit unless Rext is added (bench B1: 80 uW at saturation with a 0.3 mA amplifier).
5. Probing the oscillator with a normal 10 pF scope probe (adds load and pulls frequency).
6. Treating pads 2 and 4 of a 4-pad crystal as crystal terminals, or tying them to a signal net. They go to the lid; ground them or leave them floating.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
Layer: L1.
ngspice primitives: R, L, C only. No XSPICE.

Subcircuit (file `/home/claude/behavior/bench/xtal-bvd/ohm_xtal.lib`):
```spice
.subckt ohm_xtal 1 2 L1=44m C1=9f R1=80 C0=3p
Lm 1 a {L1}
Cm a b {C1}
Rm b 2 {R1}
C0x 1 2 {C0}
.ends ohm_xtal
```
Derivation of parameters from datasheet quantities (the integrator must compute these; they are not user typed):
1. f_nom: datasheet frequency at load CL.
2. fs = f_nom / sqrt(1 + C1/(C0 + CL)).
3. L1 = 1 / ((2*pi*fs)^2 * C1).
4. R1 = datasheet ESR (max for worst-case, a fraction of max, about 0.5 to 0.7 of it, for typical; the ratio is ASSUMPTION).
5. C0 = datasheet shunt capacitance (typ if given, else max).
6. C1: from datasheet if printed; otherwise default table below (ASSUMPTION).
7. Frequency offset: apply ppm_total = initial_tolerance + temp_dev + aging by scaling fs: L1' = L1/(1+ppm*1e-6)^2 (keeps C1 fixed).

Netlist template (placed in a Pierce circuit):
```spice
X{ref} {XIN} {XOUT} ohm_xtal L1={L1} C1={C1} R1={R1} C0={C0}
Cl1_{ref} {XIN} 0 {CL1}        ; external capacitor
Cl2_{ref} {XOUT} 0 {CL2}
Cps1_{ref} {XIN} 0 {Cpin}      ; pin + trace stray, per pin, to ground
Cps2_{ref} {XOUT} 0 {Cpin}
Rf_{ref} {XIN} {XOUT} 1meg
Bamp_{ref} {XOUT} 0 I = {imax}*tanh({gm}*v({XIN})/{imax})
Rout_{ref} {XOUT} 0 {rout}
```
Notes on the amplifier block: this is a transconductance inverter with limiting. `Bamp` draws current from XOUT when XIN is positive (inverting), `imax` sets the swing together with `rout`, `gm` is the small-signal transconductance. It is not a model of any specific MCU oscillator pin; an integrator should take gm, output swing and pin capacitance from the MCU datasheet (ST gives gm for HSE as a datasheet parameter; the TI note quotes gm = 6.6 mS typical for one device).

Ideal versus realistic: ideal mode = R1 = 1 ohm, C0 = 0 (pure series resonance, no pulling); realistic mode = full BVD with datasheet ESR, C0 and CL. Parasitic lead inductance of HC-49 and SMD pads (a few nH) is negligible at crystal frequencies and is left out.

Valid analyses:
* `ac`: valid and exact for fs, fa, ESR, pulling (bench xtal-bvd).
* `tran`: valid for oscillator start-up and steady state, but needs a time step of at most T/500 (T/5000 for ppm-accurate frequency) and a kick. Long: 8 MHz crystal start-up is milliseconds, 32.768 kHz is seconds (not simulated here; estimate only).
* `op/dc`: the crystal is open at DC (C0 only), bias set by Rf.
* `noise`, `temp`: not useful. Temperature enters only through the ppm offset the integrator computes.

Valid range: drive level at or below DLmax; frequency range fs to fa; fundamental mode only.

Known limitations:
1. No spurious modes, no overtone selection, no drive-level dependency (frequency and ESR vs DL are constant unless the integrator applies the optional rule below).
2. No aging/temperature dynamics inside SPICE (static ppm).
3. Transient measurement of frequency has a numerical dispersion error (above). The reported start-up time depends on the starting energy (kick); a real crystal starts from thermal/shot noise, which makes real start-up longer than a 20 uA x 10 ns kick suggests.
4. C1 for a given part is usually unknown (see honesty notes). Frequency accuracy of the sim therefore rests on f_nom and CL alone; pulling sensitivity rests on the assumed C1.
5. Large C0 relative to CL degrades the ST gm_crit formula: ST's gm_crit = 4*ESR*(2*pi*f)^2*(C0+CL)^2 is exact at threshold for the 3 pF case (bench B5, B6) but should not be assumed when C0 is much larger than CL (found with the ceramic-resonator class: at gm far above critical, effective negative resistance saturates, so gm = 5 mS gave only about 2x ESR margin with C0 = 30 pF, not the 12x the ratio of gm to gm_crit suggests).

Fidelity label: behavioural_approximation (lumped BVD with part-class parameters, no vendor model).

Default C1 by frequency (ASSUMPTION for MHz): 8 MHz 9 fF, 12 MHz 7 fF, 16 MHz 5 fF, 25 MHz 3.5 fF, 32.768 kHz 3.4 fF. The MHz values are chosen inside both generic ranges and lie in the same family as the Microchip Cm column; they are not tied to any part number.

ESR by frequency (Abracon ABLS HC49/US fundamental, S2): 3.58 to 4.999 MHz 180 ohm; 5 to 5.999 120; 6 to 7.999 100; 8 to 8.999 80; 9 to 9.999 60; 10 to 15.999 50; 16 to 50 40 ohm; 3rd overtone 24.01 to 31.999 MHz 100, 32 to 75 MHz 80. Compare Abracon ABM3 (5.0 x 3.2 mm, S6): 140 ohm at 8 to 9 MHz down to 25 ohm at 30 to 54 MHz. The small SMD packages are not better; a single 8 MHz ESR number cannot be reused across packages. Conflict recorded, not resolved: the same 8 MHz entry is 80 ohm in HC49/US, 140 ohm for a specific Abracon ABM3 part (DigiKey ABM3-8.000MHZ-B4Y-T: 140 ohm, 18 pF, +/-30 ppm), and 500 ohm max for the NDK NX3225GD automotive 3.2 x 2.5 series.

### 6. Ratings and limits
| name | value | condition | check | source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| drive level | rec. 10 uW, max 100 to 200 uW (MHz); 0.5 uW rec., 1 uW max (32.768 kHz) | per part | DL = R1 * irms(i(Lm))^2 ; warn if DL > DL_rec ; fail if DL > DL_max | S1, S3, S4, S5, S6 |
| crystal current | IQmaxPP = 2*sqrt(2*DLmax/R1) | | peak-to-peak of i(Lm) <= IQmaxPP | S1 |
| operating temperature | 0 to +70 C standard; -40 to +85 C (FC-135); -55 to +125 C options | per part | T within range | S2, S3 |
| storage temperature | -55 to +125 C | | | S2, S3 |
| reflow | max 2 cycles, J-STD-020 profile | | process rule (not sim) | S2 |
| gain margin | gm / gm_crit >= 5 (HSE, MHz); safety factor Sf = (RADD+ESR)/ESR >= 5 (HSE), >= 3 (LSE 32.768 kHz) | gm_crit = 4*ESR*(2*pi*f)^2*(C0+CL)^2 | design rule check at ESR max | S1 |
| insulation resistance | 500 Mohm at 100 Vdc | | not used | S2 |

Voltage rating: crystals have no voltage rating on opened sheets; electrical stress shows up as drive level.

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior
| id | trigger | effect | sim_response | permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| overdrive | DL > DL_max (e.g. strong inverter, no Rext) | frequency drift, ESR rise (DLD), jitter, duty-cycle distortion; extreme: blank or electrode damage and permanent shift (ST AN2867 3.5.1) | flag warning at DL > DL_rec, error above DL_max; optionally raise R1 by up to 25 % of max ESR (Abracon DLD limit) when DL > DL_rec (ASSUMPTION); never silently fix | recoverable up to a point, permanent above damage threshold |
| wrong_CL | external C gives CL differing from spec | frequency error of S*delta_CL (about 10 ppm/pF at 8 MHz, 18 pF); a 12 pF load on an 18 pF crystal gives about +86 ppm (bench B2) | compute fL from the actual netlist; flag when |delta_CL| > 2 pF or ppm error above tolerance budget | recoverable |
| no_oscillation | gm < gm_crit, ESR too high, CL too large, shorted/open crystal | loop never starts (bench B4/B6: ratio < 1, signal decays) | report oscillation_started = false from envelope growth; ERC flags gain margin < 5 | recoverable |
| esd | HBM/CDM on XIN/XOUT, crystal itself has no protection | possible damage of the amplifier pins; crystal blank damage on very high energy (no numeric limit on opened sheets) | RESEARCH_REQUIRED numeric; flag as handling note only | permanent |
| mechanical_shock | drop, board flex, ultrasonic cleaning | fracture of blank or mounting, frequency jump | not simulated | permanent |
| open_crystal | broken lead / cold solder | C0 only: oscillator stage runs without feedback, output stuck or noisy | simulate by removing the motional arm (keep C0) | permanent |
| short_crystal | solder bridge | amplifier input shorted to output via Rf-like path: no oscillation | tie XIN/XOUT through 1 ohm | permanent |
| overtemp | above storage max | package/seal damage | flag | permanent |
| reverse polarity | not applicable (non-polarized) | none | none | n/a |

### 8. Thermal behavior
Self-heating is negligible at specified drive levels (tens of uW in a mm-scale package). Temperature enters through frequency: parabola for tuning-fork, cubic for AT-cut, bounded by the stability number. Simple thermal model for the sim: ppm(T) = stability_ppm * ((T-25)/(Tspan))^3 for AT-cut (ASSUMPTION, only reproduces the band edges), and -0.04*(T-T0)^2 for 32.768 kHz (S3).

### 9. Appearance summary
HC-49/U is a tall oval silver metal can (13.5 mm) with two wire leads; HC-49/S is the same footprint 3.5 mm tall. 3225, 2520 and 2016 are metal-lid ceramic packages with four corner pads and a pin-1 dot or chamfer. See 3D spec entries OHM-141 to OHM-145. Printed text shows frequency and a manufacturer code; the print orientation, not the chamfer, identifies pin 1 on Abracon parts.

### 10. Validation benches
Folder `/home/claude/behavior/bench/xtal-bvd/` and `/home/claude/behavior/bench/osc-pierce/`. Parameters: 8 MHz, C1 = 9 fF, C0 = 3 pF, R1 = 80 ohm, CL = 18 pF unless stated. fs = 7.998286 MHz and L1 = 43.99506 mH follow from fL = 8.000000 MHz at 18 pF.

| pierce B1 | osc-pierce/B1.cir | transient oscillation, start-up | amplitude grows, saturates; DL = R1*Irms^2 | see below | steady xi amplitude 0.671 V pk, xo 1.385 Vpp, Irms(Lm) 1.003 mA, DL 80.5 uW, 90 % amplitude at 2.87 ms (kick 1 uA x 10 ns, gm 5 mS, step 2 ns) |
| pierce B2 | osc-pierce/B2.cir | small-signal loop (crystal + amplifier network): where Im(Z)=0 and Re(Z) there | f0 = frequency where crystal inductive reactance cancels amplifier capacitive reactance; Re(Z) < 0 | 100 ppm | f0 = 8.000215 MHz; Re(Z) = -1340 ohm (at 8.000 MHz) |
| pierce B3 | osc-pierce/B3.cir | oscillation frequency at fine step 0.2 ns | equal B2 f0 within numerical dispersion | 100 ppm | 8.000474 MHz (+32 ppm vs B2). The same circuit at step 2 ns gave 7.99329 MHz (-840 ppm), matching the trapezoidal dispersion estimate |
| pierce B4 | osc-pierce/B4.cir | gain-margin sweep, envelope ratio a(300us)/a(150us), Rout 5 kohm | ratio crosses 1 near gm_crit plus Rout loss | factor 2 | gm 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, 0.6, 1, 5 mS: 0.445, 0.710, 0.849, 0.920, 1.014, 1.201, 5.75; crossing near 0.57 mS (Rout 5 kohm adds 0.2 mS of shunt loss) |
| pierce B5 | osc-pierce/B5.cir | same with Rout removed, gm = ST gm_crit | gm_crit = 4*ESR*(2*pi*f)^2*(C0+CL)^2 = 0.357 mS; ratio = 1 | 5 % | ratio 0.9993 at gm = 0.36 mS (0.973 at 0.30, 1.026 at 0.42) |
| pierce B6 | osc-pierce/B6.cir | R1 = 500 ohm (NX3225GD-class), sweep gm | gm_crit = 2.23 mS | 10 % | ratio at gm 1.8, 2.2, 2.6, 5 mS: 0.698, 0.961, 1.319, 8.17; crossing about 2.25 mS |

Agreement: all 9 benches match their analytical expectation within the stated tolerance. Disagreements found and explained, not hidden: (a) a stray capacitor across XIN-XOUT kills oscillation (Miller position; wrong model, fixed by ground strays); (b) B3 vs 2 ns step 840 ppm artifact (integrator dispersion); (c) Pierce B4 threshold 0.57 mS vs ST 0.357 mS is the 5 kohm shunt Rout (B5 with Rout removed matches exactly); (d) B1 reports 80 uW DL, above the 10 uW recommended level of most MHz crystals: the sim flags this as an overdrive misuse rather than hiding it. Expected DL check: KCL at XIN gives I_mot = omega*(32p+4p)*0.6714 + omega*3p*(0.6714+0.6926) = 1.215 + 0.206 = 1.42 mA peak = 1.005 mA rms; DL = 80*(1.005e-3)^2 = 80.8 uW vs measured 80.5 uW (0.4 %).

Start-up time summary: 8 MHz / 80 ohm / gm 5 mS: 2.87 ms to reach 90 % amplitude from a 1 uA x 10 ns kick (growth rate 10.3e3 per second). With C1 = 9 fF and C0 = 3 pF the effective negative resistance is about 990 ohm, so alpha = (990 - 80)/(2*L1) = 10.3e3 /s, agreeing with the sim. Datasheets (ST AN2867 3.6): few-MHz crystals start in milliseconds; 32.768 kHz crystals start in 1 to 5 s. The 32.768 kHz case was not simulated (L1 = 6.94 kH, alpha is about 1 to 3 per second, one run would be about 5 million steps); RESEARCH_REQUIRED for a measured number.

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-FREQ-XO

Covers OHM-146 (7050 oscillator, XO) and OHM-147 (TCXO). Layer L2 behavioral clock source, plus an L1 supply-current load. Not a passive: it contains the crystal, the sustaining amplifier and an output buffer inside one package, so it needs power and produces a logic-level or clipped-sine clock.

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
A packaged oscillator replaces "crystal + two capacitors + MCU oscillator pin" with a single 4-pad part that outputs a ready clock. Used where the chip has no oscillator, where many chips share one clock (Ethernet PHYs, FPGAs, ADC clocks), or where start-up reliability matters (no gain-margin design). A TCXO adds analog temperature compensation, giving +/-0.05 to +/-2.8 ppm over temperature instead of +/-20 to +/-100 ppm; it is used for GNSS, cellular and RF reference clocks. Common frequencies: 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24, 25, 26, 27, 32, 40, 50 MHz.

### 2. What it is and how it works
XO: a crystal in a Pierce circuit plus a buffer, usually CMOS output swinging rail to rail. MEMS variants (SiTime SiT8008) replace the quartz with a silicon resonator and a PLL; electrically the pins are identical. TCXO: a crystal oscillator plus a temperature sensor and compensation network that pulls the crystal frequency with a varactor so the temperature curve cancels. It is a part, not a passive, because it needs VDD, consumes current (mA), and has a defined output driver; none of that can be expressed as an R, L, C two-terminal.

Opened datasheet figures:
* SiT8008 (SiTime, S11): VDD 1.62 to 3.63 V options, supply current 3.4 to 4.5 mA typical at 20 MHz no load, standby 0.6 to 4.3 uA, LVCMOS output duty 45 to 55 %, start-up 5 ms max, OE enable/disable 130 ns at 110 MHz, RMS period jitter 1.76 to 3 ps at 75 MHz, stability +/-20/25/50 ppm, abs max supply -0.5 to 4 V, ESD 2000 V HBM, 0.1 uF bypass recommended.
* AST3TQ53 TCXO (Abracon, S12, revised 2.16.2021 as printed): 10 to 51.2 MHz, stability +/-50, +/-100, +/-280 ppb over -40 to +85 C, initial tolerance +/-0.5 ppm, aging +/-1.0 ppm first year, VDD 3.135 to 3.465 V, supply current 10 mA (no load), LVCMOS (2.4 V high / 0.4 V low into 15 pF) or clipped sine 0.8 Vpp into 10 kohm // 10 pF, phase noise -95 dBc/Hz at 10 Hz and -150 dBc/Hz at 100 kHz offset (10 MHz carrier), start-up time not specified, abs max supply -0.5 to 6 V, package 5.0 x 3.2 x 1.6 mm.

Clipped sine versus CMOS: a clipped sine has small swing (0.8 Vpp) and is AC-coupled into an RF or ADC clock input with a DC-blocking capacitor; it must not be connected directly to a CMOS input. CMOS output drives logic inputs directly but has more harmonics and supply noise coupling.

### 3. How it connects
Pins (SiT8008 and AST3TQ53, S11, S12): pin 1 OE/ST (SiTime) or NC/Vc (TCXO control voltage or no connect), pin 2 GND, pin 3 OUT, pin 4 VDD. 3D spec numbering: 1 top-left, 2 bottom-left, 3 bottom-right, 4 top-right (counter-clockwise), matching OHM-146/147. Place a 0.1 uF capacitor from VDD to GND next to the pad. Mistakes: leaving OE floating on parts where OE has no internal pull-up (follow the datasheet; SiT8008 is documented pull-up behavior-dependent, RESEARCH_REQUIRED), driving the VDD above abs max (SiT8008 4 V max, so 5 V logic kills it), connecting a clipped-sine TCXO to a CMOS input without conditioning, treating a TCXO as a VCTCXO (pin 1 is Vc, it must not be left on a noisy net), long unterminated output traces (ringing), no bypass (supply-noise jitter).

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
Layer: L2 behavioral clock (a B-source gated by supply and enable and driven by a PULSE source whose period includes the ppm offset); the supply current is an L1 current source. File `/home/claude/behavior/bench/osc-clock/ohm_xo.lib`:
```spice
.subckt ohm_xo vdd gnd oe out f0=10meg ppm=0 tstart=5u icc=4.2m icc_sb=1u rout=30 tr=1n vmin=2.25 vth_oe=0.7
.param fa={f0*(1+ppm*1e-6)} pr={1/fa}
Vclk clk gnd PULSE(0 1 {tstart} {tr} {tr} {0.5*pr-tr} {pr})
Bdrv drv gnd V = (V(vdd,gnd)>{vmin}) ? ((V(oe,gnd)>{vth_oe}*V(vdd,gnd)) ? V(vdd,gnd)*V(clk,gnd) : 0) : 0
Ro drv out {rout}
Bi vdd gnd I = (V(vdd,gnd)>{vmin}) ? ((V(oe,gnd)>{vth_oe}*V(vdd,gnd)) ? {icc} : {icc_sb}) : 0
.ends ohm_xo
```
Netlist template: `X{ref} {VDD} {GND} {OE} {OUT} ohm_xo f0={f0} ppm={ppm} tstart={tstart} icc={icc}`.
Parameter mapping: f0 = ordered frequency; ppm = sum of initial tolerance, temperature deviation at the run temperature and aging (user or the integrator sets it; TCXO bounded by its stability band); tstart = datasheet start-up time (SiT8008 max 5 ms; default 5 us only to keep sims short, so set it from the datasheet for a true start-up test); icc from the supply-current table (4.2 mA default is the SiT8008 20 MHz, 3.3 V upper typical); icc_sb standby current; vth_oe is a generic logic-threshold fraction (ASSUMPTION; the SiT8008 VIH/VIL numbers were not extracted).
Ideal versus realistic: ideal = ppm 0, tstart 0, rout 0; realistic = ppm per datasheet, rout 30 ohm (ASSUMPTION, typical CMOS driver), rise time 1 to 2 ns, supply current from sheet. Clipped-sine TCXO variant: replace the output with `Bdrv drv gnd V = 0.4*sin(...)`, not implemented in the lib because SPICE sine sources take a fixed frequency; use `SIN(vdc 0.4 {fa})` with `ppm` folded into the frequency (works, same ppm rule).
Valid analyses: tran (primary), op (supply current only, output at t = 0 low). ac is not meaningful. Valid range: VDD between vmin and abs max; load capacitance up to the datasheet figure (15 pF CMOS).
Limitations: no jitter or phase noise (L2 timing is ideal apart from ppm); no supply-pushing; no output swing sag with load beyond rout; start-up is a pure delay (real parts ramp amplitude); static ppm only; frequency does not respond to VDD or Vc; no spurious output when VDD is below vmin (output is held low).
Fidelity: behavioural_approximation.

### 8. Thermal behavior
Power is VDD*icc (about 14 mW for 3.3 V x 4.2 mA; 33 mW for the 10 mA TCXO). Self-heating is small in a 3225-to-7050 ceramic package; the thermal resistance is not given in the opened sheets (RESEARCH_REQUIRED). A TCXO is warm-up sensitive in practice (it can show a few ppb drift during warm-up); not modeled.

### 9. Appearance summary
Rectangular 7.0 x 5.0 mm (OHM-146) or 3.2 x 2.5 mm (OHM-147) package, silver metal lid or black molded body, four corner pads, a pin-1 dot or chamfer at the top-left, printed frequency code. See 3D spec OHM-146 and OHM-147.

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-FREQ-CERRES

Covers OHM-148 (3-pin ceramic resonator with built-in load capacitors, Murata CSTLS-G class). Layer L1.

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
A cheap MCU clock where +/-0.5 % accuracy is acceptable (UART, timers, simple PWM, IR remote), with no external capacitors and a smaller, shock-tolerant part than a crystal. Not suitable for USB, CAN with tight tolerance, RTC or radio references.

### 2. What it is and how it works
A piezoelectric ceramic (PZT-type) plate, with two capacitors integrated inside the same body, one from each outer pin to the center ground pin. Electrically it has the same BVD form as a quartz crystal, but with a much lower Q (hundreds to about a thousand versus tens of thousands), a larger C1 and C0, and a wide frequency spread. Opened data (Murata CSTLS8M00G53-B0, S13): 8.000 MHz, initial tolerance +/-0.50 % max, temperature shift +/-0.20 % max over -20 to +80 C, aging +/-0.20 %, built-in load capacitance 15 pF per side, resonant impedance R1 25 ohm max, "oscillation circuits do not require external load capacitors". The Murata series page (S14) lists the CSTLS_G range 3.40 to 10.00 MHz, +/-0.5 % tolerance, +/-0.2 % stability over -20 to +80 C and notes a 47 pF built-in type with a -0.4 to +0.2 % stability and "to be discontinued" status. Conflict: the 15 pF part sheet and the 47 pF note on the series page; both are for different built-in capacitance types, not a contradiction, but the 3D spec does not say which one OHM-148 is: default here is 15 pF.

### 3. How it connects
Pins: 1 and 3 are the resonator terminals (XIN, XOUT), pin 2 (center) is ground and connects both built-in capacitors (3D spec; the Murata page opened did not show a pinout drawing, so this comes from the 3D spec's Murata catalog reference). Polarity: none; pins 1 and 3 are interchangeable. Use with the same Pierce inverter as a crystal, with Rf, but without external capacitors. Mistakes: adding external capacitors in parallel with the built-ins (frequency drops and gain margin falls), leaving the center pin unconnected (no load caps, no oscillation), using it where better than +/-0.5 % accuracy is needed, assuming crystal drive-level or ESR rules apply.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
Layer L1. BVD arm between pins 1 and 3 (same `ohm_xtal` subcircuit) with C0 across it, plus `Cb1` from pin 1 to pin 2 and `Cb2` from pin 3 to pin 2 (default 15 pF each).
```spice
X{ref} {P1} {P3} ohm_xtal L1={L1} C1={C1} R1={R1} C0={C0}
Cb1_{ref} {P1} {P2} {Cbuilt}
Cb2_{ref} {P3} {P2} {Cbuilt}
```
Parameters: f_nom = ordered frequency measured at the built-in load; R1 = 25 ohm (datasheet max); C1 = 0.8 pF and C0 = 30 pF are ASSUMPTION (typical order of magnitude for ceramic resonators; no opened source printed them) so Q = 1005; fs = f_nom/sqrt(1 + C1/(C0 + Cbuilt/2)), L1 = 1/((2 pi fs)^2 C1).
Valid analyses: ac, tran. Limitations: C0 and C1 are assumed; wide tolerance is applied by the integrator via a ppm offset of up to 5000 ppm (initial) plus 2000 ppm (temperature) plus 2000 ppm (aging); ST gm_crit does not apply when C0 >> CL (see class XTAL); no DLD or ratings for drive level on the opened sheet.
Fidelity: behavioural_approximation.

Operating -20 to +80 C (check T in range). Rated voltage and drive level were not printed in the opened sheet (RESEARCH_REQUIRED); the simulator applies the same crystal-style drive limit as a conservative placeholder: flag when the power in R1 exceeds 100 uW (ASSUMPTION).

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior
| id | trigger | effect | sim_response | permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| extra_caps | external capacitors added | frequency pulled low, possible no start | recompute with total CL | recoverable |
| pin2_open | center pin floating | no load capacitors, no oscillation | flag ERC (pin 2 must be ground) | recoverable |
| overdrive | high drive | frequency shift, damage (limit unknown) | flag at 100 uW placeholder | permanent |
| accuracy_misuse | used where < 0.5 % needed | clock outside tolerance | warn from tolerance budget (0.5+0.2+0.2 %) | recoverable |
| shock/ESD | mechanical | ceramics are rugged but can crack | not simulated | permanent |

### 8. Thermal behavior
Frequency shift +/-0.2 % over -20 to +80 C; no self-heating model.

### 9. Appearance summary
Small three-leaded resin-dipped rounded block, leads in a row at 2.5 mm pitch, about 8 x 3.5 x 5.5 mm, printed code. See 3D spec OHM-148.

### 10. Validation bench (folder `bench/xtal-resonator/`)
B1: Pierce inverter (gm 2 mS, Rout 5 kohm, strays 4 pF per pin), no external caps, pins as above. Analytical expectation: fL = fs*sqrt(1 + C1/(C0 + CL)) with CL = (15+4)/2 = 9.5 pF: 7.99576 MHz. Tolerance 300 ppm (step 1 ns dispersion about -210 ppm). Measured: oscillates, 7.995797 MHz, 90 % amplitude at 0.31 ms with a 20 uA x 10 ns kick, peak 0.555 V. Matches. Shows start-up about ten times faster than the quartz bench (lower Q), and that 4 pF per pin of stray shifts a 15 pF part by about -540 ppm relative to its 8.000 MHz rating. Also found: at gm = 5 mS with C0 = 30 pF the oscillation grows very slowly (growth rate 21.8e3 per second, effective negative resistance about 47 ohm), so an excess of gm is not an excess of margin. Only one bench exists for this class; a second (no-oscillation case with pin 2 open) was not run: RESEARCH_REQUIRED.

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-FREQ-SAW

Covers OHM-149 (SAW filter, Abracon AFS869S3 class). Layer L1 behavioral band-pass.

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
A surface-acoustic-wave band-pass filter selects a narrow RF band (here 869 MHz ISM / remote control) with very sharp skirts and small size, ahead of a receiver LNA or after a transmitter, to reject out-of-band interferers and image frequencies. Other SAW uses (not modeled): IF filters at tens to hundreds of MHz, duplexers, resonators.

### 2. What it is and how it works
Interdigital transducers (metal fingers) on a piezoelectric substrate convert the electrical signal into a surface acoustic wave and back. The finger geometry sets center frequency and passband; the acoustic path gives insertion loss (typically several dB) and steep rejection. It is a two-port filter with defined source and load impedance (50 ohm here). Opened data (Abracon AFS869S3, S15): center frequency 869.0 MHz (Fc +/-4.0 MHz, so an 8 MHz wide passband), insertion loss 4.5 dB max, passband ripple 1.5 dB max, relative attenuation 35 dB min (offset not extracted), terminating impedance 50 ohm / 0 pF, operating -30 to +80 C, storage -40 to +85 C, size 3.8 x 3.8 x 1.5 mm, 10 dBm source power as a "typical specification", ESD sensitive. Distributor pages (S16) give bandwidth 8 MHz, IL 4.5 dB, 50 ohm, 6 pins, 10 V DC voltage rating (lower trust; aggregator). Insertion loss is flat across the band only approximately; edges are worse in real parts.

### 3. How it connects
Pins (S15 and 3D spec): pin 2 input, pin 5 output (the two center pads on opposite rows), pins 1, 3, 4, 6 ground. Keep ground pads connected to a solid plane. Typical use: antenna - matching - SAW - LNA. Mistakes: wrong source/load impedance (no matching: loss and ripple change; bench B2: a 100 ohm load costs 0.5 dB at the center here and more at the skirts), leaving ground pads open, placing the filter without a ground plane (feed-through rejection loss), swapping input and output (usually symmetrical, not guaranteed), exceeding input power, ESD.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
Layer L1 behavioral (not a vendor S-parameter file). File `bench/saw-bpf/ohm_saw.lib`, generated by `gen_saw_R8.py`: a lossless 3-pole Chebyshev (0.5 dB ripple) lumped band-pass (g = 1.5963, 1.0967, 1.5963, Matthaei/Young/Jones table values, general engineering practice, not from an opened document) with a matched pi attenuator of the target insertion loss on the input, so the passband loss is flat.
```spice
.subckt ohm_saw in out gnd
Rp1 in gnd 197.3179
Rps in p2 27.0785
Rp2 p2 gnd 197.3179
Ls1 p2 a1 1.587869e-06
Cs1 a1 n1 2.112448e-14
Lp n1 gnd 7.686926e-11
Cp n1 gnd 4.363631e-10
Ls3 n1 c1 1.587869e-06
Cs3 c1 out 2.112448e-14
.ends ohm_saw
```
Design equations (bandpass from lowpass prototype, FBW = bw/f0): series branches Ls = g*Z0/(FBW*w0), Cs = 1/(w0^2*Ls); shunt Cp = g/(Z0*FBW*w0), Lp = 1/(w0^2*Cp); pad: K = 10^(IL/20), Rshunt = Z0(K+1)/(K-1), Rseries = Z0(K^2-1)/(2K).
Parameter mapping: f0 = center frequency; bw = passband width (Chebyshev ripple edges, 8 MHz for Fc +/-4 MHz); il_db = datasheet insertion loss; Z0 = 50 ohm.
Analyses: ac (primary). tran works but the lumped values are extreme (Lp = 77 pH); use ac. Valid range: within a few bandwidths of f0.
Limitations: real SAW rejection is a specified 35 dB minimum at stated offsets, the Chebyshev model gives about 63 dB at +/-40 MHz (too steep, far-out spurious responses and feed-through floor are missing); no group-delay ripple of a real SAW; no temperature drift of center frequency; no power handling nonlinearity; return loss comes from the pad and is better than a real part; no triple-transit echo.
Fidelity: behavioural_approximation.

### 5. Parameters table
| name | unit | default | min | max | tolerance | basis | confidence | source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| f0 | Hz | 869e6 | | | +/-4 MHz | MFR_DATASHEET | H | S15 |
| passband bw | Hz | 8e6 | | | | MFR_DATASHEET | M | S15, S16 |
| il_db | dB | 4.5 | | 4.5 max | | MFR_DATASHEET | H | S15 |
| ripple | dB | 0.5 | | 1.5 max | | MFR_DATASHEET (max), ASSUMPTION (0.5 model) | M | S15 |
| Z0 | ohm | 50 | | | | MFR_DATASHEET | H | S15 |
| rejection | dB | 35 | 35 | | offset unknown | MFR_DATASHEET | L | S15 |
| temp coefficient | ppm/C | RESEARCH_REQUIRED | | | | | | |

### 6. Ratings and limits
Operating -30 to +80 C; storage -40 to +85 C; input power 10 dBm (typical spec, source power) used as the conservative limit: flag if the incident power at pin 2 exceeds 10 dBm (check: P = |v(in)|^2/(8*Z0) for a 50 ohm source or from the incident wave); DC voltage rating 10 V (S16, aggregator, low trust): flag DC above 10 V; ESD sensitive (S15 warning, no numeric value).

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior
| id | trigger | effect | sim_response | permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| overpower | > 10 dBm | acoustic migration / finger damage, rising loss (physics from general knowledge, ASSUMPTION; no opened source) | flag error, optionally add +3 dB loss | permanent |
| esd | HBM on finger electrodes | finger breakdown, shorted fingers, loss rise (no numeric limit) | handling note | permanent |
| dc_bias | DC > 10 V | transducer breakdown | flag | permanent |
| mismatch | source/load not 50 ohm | ripple, loss change (bench B2) | computed by the circuit | recoverable |
| ground_open | ground pads floating | poor rejection/feed-through | ERC flag (not modeled) | recoverable |
| overtemp | above storage range | substrate/seal damage | flag | permanent |

### 8. Thermal behavior
Center frequency drifts with temperature (quartz-like or LiTaO3 substrate); the coefficient was not in the opened sheet. No self-heating model (dissipation is below 10 dBm times loss).

### 9. Appearance summary
Small square flat package 3.8 x 3.8 x 1.5 mm with six edge pads (default), gray/black or silver top with a laser code and a pin-1 dot. See 3D spec OHM-149 (which marks the pad set as a placeholder).

### 10. Validation benches (folder `bench/saw-bpf/`)
| id | what | expected | tolerance | measured |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | AC sweep 800 to 940 MHz, 50/50 ohm | IL(869) = 4.5 dB; edges 865/873 MHz: 4.5 + 0.52 / 4.5 + 0.48 dB; at 829/909 MHz: 4.5 + 63.46 / 4.5 + 62.26 dB (Chebyshev A = 10 log(1 + eps^2 T3(x)^2), x = (f/f0 - f0/f)/FBW, eps^2 = 0.122); 3 dB bandwidth 9.34 MHz | 0.05 dB (0.5 dB far out) | 4.500, 5.020, 4.981, 67.96, 66.76 dB; 3 dB bandwidth 9.336 MHz |
| B2 | 100 ohm load | IL = 5.0115 dB (pad terminated in 100 ohm, filter transparent at center) | 0.01 dB | 5.0115 dB |
Both match. The first version used a lossy resonator model (Qu = 428 to get 4.5 dB); it gave 6.95 dB at the band edges, wrong for a flat-passband SAW, so it was replaced by the lossless filter plus pad.

S15, S16. The AFS869S3 datasheet text extraction was incomplete (offsets of the 35 dB rejection and of ripple are not stated). Chebyshev g-values are standard filter-design tables, not from an opened document (basis ASSUMPTION for the prototype choice).

# Per-entry sections

## [OHM-141] HC-49/U crystal -> BEH-FREQ-XTAL
Package: through-hole metal can 10.8 x 4.65 x 13.5 mm, two leads 4.88 mm pitch (3D spec). Pin map: A = terminal 1 (at -X), B = terminal 2 (+X); non-polarized, pin 1 is a convention. Defaults: f_nom 8 MHz, CL 18 pF, C0 3 pF (datasheet max 7 pF, Abracon ABLS), R1 80 ohm (ABLS 8 to 8.999 MHz), C1 9 fF (ASSUMPTION), tolerance +/-30 ppm, stability +/-50 ppm, DL_rec 10 uW (max placeholder 100 to 1000 uW as printed by ABLS). Parasitics: lead inductance and can capacitance negligible; the can is not connected in 2-lead versions (3-pin case-ground variants are not modeled). Largest C0 and lowest ESR per frequency of the group, so the easiest to start. Status: partial (C1 assumed).

## [OHM-142] Low-profile HC-49 crystal -> BEH-FREQ-XTAL
Package: HC-49/S (also /US), 11.05 x 4.65 x 3.5 mm, same leads and pin map as OHM-141. Electrically identical class; datasheet ABLS is an HC49/US part (11.4 x 4.7 x 4.2 mm in the opened sheet, which differs from the 3D spec 11.05 x 4.65 x 3.5: ABLS lists 4.2 mm height, the 3D spec cites 3.5 max from SaRonix/Abracon ABL; a physical conflict, not an electrical one). Defaults as OHM-141. Status: partial.

## [OHM-143] 3225 SMD crystal -> BEH-FREQ-XTAL
Package 3.2 x 2.5 mm, 4 pads. Pin map (3D spec numbering, pin 1 top-left, counter-clockwise: 1 TL, 2 BL, 3 BR, 4 TR): A = pad 1, B = pad 3 (diagonal), LID1 = pad 2, LID2 = pad 4 (lid; GND or NC; Epson FA-238/TSX-3225 states 2 and 4 connect to the cover). Abracon variant numbers pin 1 bottom-left; the diagonal rule (1 and 3) still holds. A 2-pad variant has pads 1 and 2 at the short ends. Defaults: R1 per frequency from the chosen family (Epson FA-238 16 to 20 MHz 80 ohm; TSX-3225 16 to 21 MHz 60 ohm; NDK NX3225GD 8 to 9.8 MHz 500 ohm max), CL 8 pF is NX3225GD-style, 12 pF typical, DL_rec 10 uW, DL_max 200 uW, C0 about 1 to 3 pF (ASSUMPTION; Suntsu 1 to 7). High ESR at low frequency makes gain margin the critical check (bench B6). Status: partial.
Warning: Abracon ABM3 is 5.0 x 3.2 mm, not 3.2 x 2.5 mm.

## [OHM-144] 2520 SMD crystal -> BEH-FREQ-XTAL
Package 2.5 x 2.0 mm, 4 pads, pin map as OHM-143 (pads 1,3 crystal; 2,4 lid). Smaller blank means lower C0 and C1, higher ESR and lower DL_max: use DL_rec 10 uW, DL_max 100 uW (ASSUMPTION; no opened 2520 sheet). Status: partial (no opened datasheet specific to 2520).

## [OHM-145] 2016 SMD crystal -> BEH-FREQ-XTAL
Package 2.0 x 1.6 mm, 4 pads, pin map as OHM-143. Highest ESR and lowest drive-level tolerance of the three; typical DL_max 50 to 100 uW (ASSUMPTION). Pulling per pF is larger for small C0 (S = C1/(2*(C0+CL)^2): a smaller C0 increases sensitivity slightly). Status: partial (no opened 2016 sheet).

## [OHM-146] 7050 oscillator -> BEH-FREQ-XO
Package 7.0 x 5.0 mm, 4 pads. Pin map: 1 (top-left) = OE/ST, 2 (bottom-left) = GND, 3 (bottom-right) = OUT, 4 (top-right) = VDD (SiTime SiT8008, Abracon sheets cited in the 3D spec). Defaults: f0 10 MHz, VDD 3.3 V, icc 4.2 mA, standby 1 uA, ppm +/-25, tstart 5 ms (datasheet max; benches use 5 us for speed), rout 30 ohm. Output CMOS. Status: partial (OE pull-up behavior and OE thresholds unconfirmed; pin-1 marking not confirmed in opened texts).

## [OHM-147] TCXO -> BEH-FREQ-XO (TCXO parameter set)
Package: 3.2 x 2.5 mm default per the 3D spec (opened AST3TQ53 is 5.0 x 3.2 x 1.6 mm; 7050 TCXO also exists per the 3D spec). Pin map: 1 = NC/Vc, 2 = GND, 3 = OUT, 4 = VDD. Parameters: stability +/-50, +/-100 or +/-280 ppb over -40 to +85 C (default 100 ppb), initial +/-0.5 ppm, aging +/-1 ppm first year, VDD 3.135 to 3.465 V (3.3 V part), icc 10 mA max, LVCMOS 2.4/0.4 V at 15 pF or clipped sine 0.8 Vpp into 10 kohm // 10 pF. A part, not a passive: it needs VDD and decoupling. Clipped-sine output needs DC coupling care. Status: partial (start-up time and thermal data not in the opened sheet).

## [OHM-148] Ceramic resonator -> BEH-FREQ-CERRES
Package: 3-lead radial block, pitch 2.5 mm (3D spec). Pin map: 1 = terminal A (-X), 2 = ground (center), 3 = terminal B (+X); symmetric, polarity none. Defaults: 8 MHz, built-in 15 pF each, R1 25 ohm max, tolerance +/-0.5 %, temp +/-0.2 %, aging +/-0.2 %, C1 0.8 pF and C0 30 pF (ASSUMPTION). Status: partial.

## [OHM-149] SAW filter -> BEH-FREQ-SAW
Package: 3.8 x 3.8 x 1.5 mm, 6 pads (3D spec lists them as placeholders; AFS869S3 has 6 pins confirmed by a distributor page). Pin map in 3D spec numbering: pins 1 to 3 down the -X row ((-1.5, +1.1), (-1.5, 0), (-1.5, -1.1)), pins 4 to 6 up the +X row ((+1.5, -1.1), (+1.5, 0), (+1.5, +1.1)); IN = pin 2 (middle of -X row), OUT = pin 5 (middle of +X row), GND = 1, 3, 4, 6. Defaults: 869 MHz, 8 MHz passband, 4.5 dB, 50 ohm. Status: partial.

# R9: Headers, terminals, wire-to-board connectors (OHM-150 to OHM-161)

Author note: three behavior classes cover the 12 entries.

| Class | Entries |
|---|---|
| BEH-CON-HEADER | OHM-150, 151, 152, 153, 154 (2.54 mm pin and socket headers, including right angle) |
| BEH-CON-WTB | OHM-155 JST-PH, 156 JST-XH, 157 JST-SH, 158 Molex KK (crimp-housing wire-to-board) |
| BEH-CON-TERMINAL | OHM-159, 160 (screw terminals), 161 (pluggable terminal block) |

Common to all three: every contact is a passive two-terminal path with a series contact resistance, one current rating, and a self-heating temperature rise. All three are layer L1 (ngspice R, optionally L and C). Fidelity is `behavioural_approximation` in realistic mode (parameters are datasheet limits, not a vendor model) and `ideal_components` when contact resistance is 0. No connector here has a vendor SPICE model attached, so `vendor_model` is never claimed.

Shared semantics (apply to all three classes):

- "Mated pair" model. A connector instance is a set of N contacts. A contact whose mate is absent connects to nothing: the pin has its board-side net only, and the netlist exporter emits no element for it (a one-pin net is dropped, as in the existing `HEADER_1X6_254` record whose pins are all `passive`). A mating relation (`mate_ref` in the project, or a harness) emits one resistor per contact between the two sides' nets, using the pin mapping given per entry. A header plus a harness is: board net -> Rc (mated pair) -> wire (+ crimp Rc each end) -> Rc (mated pair) -> other board net.
- The existing runner (`src/ohmni/eda/simulation.py`) only runs `.op`. All benches below use `.op`, plus `.ac` for B4, run directly with ngspice. A simulation that did not run is never a pass.
- Existing catalog record `HEADER_1X6_254.json` has pins numbered "1".."6", names P1..P6, electrical_type passive, no `design_rules`. Keep that scheme: pin names P1..PN, type passive.

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-CON-HEADER

Applies to OHM-150 (1xN male), 151 (2xN male), 152 (1xN female), 153 (2xN female), 154 (right-angle male, 1xN or 2xN).

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
A 0.1 in (2.54 mm) header is the commodity board-to-board and board-to-cable connector. Male strips are used as breakout and debug pins (SWD, UART, ISP, GPIO), configuration jumpers (a shunt shorts two adjacent pins), and as the mating side for female sockets on stackable boards or for crimp "Dupont" housings on jumper cables. Female headers are the receptacle on modules (Arduino-style shield headers, breadboard-friendly module sockets). The part provides no function: it is a conductor with a contact resistance in series, and it joins nets only when mated. Common series: Samtec TSW (male) and SSW (female), Wurth WR-PHD, Harwin M20.

### 2. What it is and how it works
Each contact is a 0.64 mm (0.025 in) square brass or phosphor-bronze post (OHM-150 spec: 0.64 square, Samtec "TSW .025 square post") in a PBT, LCP or PA6T plastic base, plated gold or tin over nickel. A female contact is a spring beam (Harwin M20 is described as dual-beam) that wipes over the post. Electrically:

- Contact resistance Rc (constriction plus film resistance at the spring/post interface), tens of milliohms at most, in series with each pin path. It rises with wear, oxide on tin, and fretting. Samtec specifies it as a change: max delta 15 mOhm after environmental tests (EIA-364-23), not an initial value.
- Bulk resistance of the post: R = rho*l/A. For l about 11.5 mm and A = 0.41 mm^2 with brass rho about 7e-8 Ohm*m (general value, not from a datasheet) this is about 2 mOhm; small next to Rc.
- Heating: P = I^2 * (Rc + Rbulk), temperature rise = P * Rth. Rth is not published in the documents I opened; see section 8 for how the model derives it.
- Partial inductance of a straight round post (standard formula L = 2e-7 * l * (ln(2l/r) - 0.75), l=11.5 mm, r about 0.36 mm equivalent) is about 8 nH. Pin-to-pin capacitance is a fraction of a pF. Both are DERIVED/ASSUMPTION, only relevant above a few hundred MHz.
- Insulation: Samtec lists insulation resistance min 5000 MOhm and working voltage 465 VAC (mated SSW), dielectric withstanding 1410 VAC. Wurth: 1000 MOhm min, 500 VAC test. The air gap between adjacent pins is 2.54 - 0.64 = 1.90 mm (DERIVED from the 3D spec), but creepage over the plastic base is shorter and is what the manufacturer's working voltage reflects. Use the manufacturer value, not an air-gap calculation.

### 3. How it connects
- Pins: N (or 2N) passive terminals P1..PN, no polarity, no keying on unshrouded headers (3D spec: "no polarization key", "no pin-1 mark"). Pin 1 is only a footprint/silkscreen convention.
- Breakout: each pin attaches to one board net, the other side is open until something mates.
- Jumper/shunt: a 2-position shunt (a female contact pair bridged by a metal bar) joins two adjacent pins. The sim effect: pin_i and pin_j connected by Rc + Rshunt + Rc. On 2xN headers the usual jumper bridges the two pins of one row-pair (for example 1-2), across the rows; on 1xN it bridges neighbours along the row.
- Cable harness: Dupont-style housings or a ribbon IDC socket mate with the header and carry nets across a cable.
- Mating gender rule: male mates with female only; male-male or female-female "mating" is a user error and the tool should reject it (no contact exists).
- Common mistakes: (1) mating a 2xN cable connector rotated 180 degrees, which swaps every pin pair (unshrouded headers cannot prevent this); (2) inserting a header shifted by one position; (3) assuming a header is current-rated like the wire; many positions loaded together heat each other; (4) leaving jumpers off configuration pins so inputs float; (5) pushing tin-plated contacts at low-level signals (oxide film), or mixing gold and tin finishes.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
Layer L1. Fidelity: `ideal_components` (Rc=0) or `behavioural_approximation` (realistic, adds Rc/L/C). Valid analyses: op, dc, ac, tran, temp. Not noise-modeled.

Netlist template (one contact; per mated pair, N copies; parameters named):
```
* mated contact k between side A net {A_k} and side B net {B_k}
R{ref}_c{k} {A_k} {mid_k} {Rc}          ; contact resistance, mated pair
R{ref}_b{k} {mid_k} {B_k} {Rbulk}       ; post bulk (optional)
* realistic high-speed option, insert in series:
L{ref}_l{k} ... {Lpin}   ;  C{ref}_c{k}_{k+1} {A_k} {A_k+1} {Cpp}
* jumper between pin i and j:
R{ref}_j1 {P_i} {m} {Rc}
R{ref}_j2 {m} {m2} {Rshunt}
R{ref}_j3 {m2} {P_j} {Rc}
```
Unmated: emit nothing. Ideal mode: Rc=Rbulk=0 (use a 1u ohm short or merge nets).

Parameter-to-datasheet mapping: Rc = "contact resistance" (Wurth 20 mOhm max, Harwin 30 mOhm max, Samtec delta 15 mOhm); Irated = "rated current per contact"; Vwork = working or test voltage; cycles = mating cycles. Tolerance: use Rc as an upper limit when checking, a typical value when simulating.

Known limitations: Rc is a datasheet maximum, not a measured typical, so realistic mode over-predicts drop for new gold contacts; Rc is independent of current and frequency (no skin effect); no wear dynamics except the optional end-of-life step; Rc between male and female contacts of different manufacturers or platings is not modeled; L and C values are derived estimates (L confidence), not measured; no crosstalk model beyond adjacent-pin Cpp; no thermal coupling model beyond the derating factor.

### 5. Parameters
| name | unit | default | min | max | tolerance | basis | source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| N (positions per row) | - | 8 (150,152,154), 5 (151,153) | 1 | 40 | exact | MFR_DATASHEET (3D spec) | OHM spec |
| rows | - | 1 or 2 | 1 | 2 | exact | 3D spec | OHM spec |
| mated | bool | false | | | | DERIVED | - |
| Rc (mated pair) | mOhm | 10 | 0 | 30 | factor 2 | ASSUMPTION for typical (L); limits Wurth 20 max, Harwin 30 max | S2, S3 |
| Rbulk | mOhm | 2 (4 for RA) | 0 | 6 | factor 2 | DERIVED (L) | - |
| Rshunt | mOhm | 2 | 0 | 10 | factor 2 | ASSUMPTION (L) | - |
| Lpin | nH | 8 (11 RA) | 0 | 15 | +-50% | DERIVED (L) | - |
| Cpp (adjacent) | pF | 0.4 | 0.1 | 1 | factor 2 | ASSUMPTION (L) | - |
| Irated per contact | A | 3 | 1 | 6 | - | MFR_DATASHEET | S1, S2, S3 |
| Vwork | V | 250 (use manufacturer value if known) | | 465 | - | MFR_DATASHEET | S1 |
| Tmax | degC | 105 | | 125 (gold Samtec) | - | MFR_DATASHEET | S1, S2, S3 |
| cycles | - | 25 | 25 | 1000 | - | MFR_DATASHEET | S1, S2, S3 |
| alpha_Rc | 1/K | 0.0039 | | | | ASSUMPTION (copper-like, L) | - |

### 6. Ratings and limits
Per-series values (conflicts shown, not merged):

| Series | I per contact | Rc | Voltage | Temp | Cycles | Insulation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Samtec TSW/SSW (spec sheet rev C, 2023-02-08) | 4.7 A, one pin powered per row | delta max 15 mOhm (EIA-364-23) | 465 VAC working, DWV 1410 VAC | -55 to +125 gold, -55 to +105 tin | 1000 | IR 5000 MOhm min |
| Samtec TSW/HTSW catalog page | 5.2 to 6.3 A, 2 positions powered, depends on mating connector | not given | 465 VAC/658 VDC with SSW; 500 VAC/707 VDC with BCS; 400 VAC/566 VDC with CES | same | - | PBT (TSW), LCP (HTSW) |
| Wurth WR-PHD (datasheet dated 2023-01-08) | 3 A | 20 mOhm max | 500 VAC test, 1 min | -40 to +105 | 25 | IR 1000 MOhm min; PA6T, gold, copper alloy |
| Harwin M20 (Mouser summary and distributor page) | 3 A | 30 mOhm max | 750 V "voltage proof" on distributor page (unverified, not in manufacturer text I read) | -40 to +105 | 300 | nylon PA6T, UL94 V-0 |

Conflict: Samtec states 4.7 A for one pin and 5.2-6.3 A for two positions powered in different documents (different mating connectors and test conditions); Wurth and Harwin are 3 A. The model default is the conservative 3 A. Use the larger Samtec figure only when the user selects Samtec TSW and states how many pins are loaded.

Derating for many loaded contacts (ASSUMPTION, L, to be replaced when a manufacturer curve is found): k(N_loaded) = 1.0 for 1-2 loaded contacts (the condition the Samtec ratings are stated under), 0.8 for 3 to 10, 0.7 above 10 or all pins loaded. Reason: loaded neighbours raise each other's temperature.

Check expressions (evaluated per contact from .op or .tran current):
- `I_contact > Irated * k(N_loaded)` -> WARN (limit exceeded)
- `V_across_adjacent_pins > Vwork` -> WARN
- `T_contact = Tamb + (I^2 * Rc_T * Rth)/(1 - I^2*Rc*alpha*Rth) > Tmax` -> FAIL (see 8)
- `mating_count > cycles` -> Rc end-of-life step (see 7)

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior
| id | trigger | effect | sim_response | permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| overcurrent | I > Irated*k | contact heats, spring relaxes, plastic softens | flag at Irated*k; at T_contact > Tmax mark `damaged` and report; model does not melt on its own | permanent past Tmax |
| thermal_runaway | I^2*Rc*alpha*Rth >= 1 | Rc rises with T and heating compounds; contact or housing melts | report runaway current I_run = 1/sqrt(Rc*alpha*Rth); treat as open circuit after flagging | permanent |
| overvoltage | V > Vwork | arc/tracking across base | flag; no automatic change | permanent if arcing |
| wear | mating cycles > rated | Rc rises, contact intermittent (tin worse, 25-cycle Wurth rating) | after cycles, multiply Rc by 2 (ASSUMPTION; Samtec allows delta 15 mOhm, JST allows initial 10 to 20 mOhm after tests) | cumulative |
| fretting/vibration | vibration, oxide on tin | intermittent contact | not simulated; document only | recoverable (re-seat) |
| open (unmated/lost) | not mated | net not connected | emit nothing | recoverable |
| reverse polarity | n/a (no polarity) | rotated or shifted mating swaps nets | detect via net comparison, ERC warning | n/a |
| ESD | n/a | none at connector level | none | n/a |
| short | solder bridge, shunt misplaced | adjacent nets shorted | user shunts produce R path; bridge not modeled | permanent |

### 8. Thermal behavior
Rise per contact: dT = I^2 * R0 * Rth, with R(T) = R0*(1 + alpha*(T - 25)) self-consistent: dT = I^2*R0*Rth / (1 - I^2*R0*alpha*Rth). Runaway at I_run = 1/sqrt(R0*alpha*Rth). No source I opened publishes Rth for these headers. Derivation rule used: Rth = dT_rated / (Irated^2 * R0) with dT_rated = 30 K (ASSUMPTION; the 30 degC rise criterion is common in connector current ratings but I did not open a document stating it for these series). Example Wurth: R0 = 20 mOhm, 3 A gives Rth = 30/(9*0.02) = 167 K/W; with Rc default 10 mOhm and 3 A: Rth = 333 K/W. A real part's Rth depends on housing, board copper, and neighbours, so this model is a limit calculation, not a prediction. alpha = 0.0039 /K is a general copper value (ASSUMPTION L).

### 9. Appearance summary
Black plastic base with gold or tin square posts at 2.54 mm pitch; male posts stand 6 mm above a 2.54 mm base, female sockets are a taller black block with chamfered openings. No manufacturer pin-1 mark; the library uses a footprint or decal convention. See OHM-150 to OHM-154 in the 3D spec.

### 10. Validation benches (all run with ngspice 42; files under /home/claude/behavior/bench/beh-con-header/)
- B1 `B1.cir` contact resistance in a divider: 5 V, 1 Ohm load, 2 contacts of 10 mOhm. Expected V_load = 5*1/(1+2*0.01) = 4.90196 V, tolerance 0.1%. Measured 4.901961 V. Match.
- B2 `B2.cir` jumper short and unmated pin: shunt joins a-b with 2*10 mOhm + 2 mOhm; 3.3 V source via 100 Ohm, 10 kOhm pull-down. Expected v(b) = 3.3*10000/(10000+100+0.022) = 3.26732 V; unmated pin v(b2) = 0 V. Measured v(b) = 3.267320 V, v(b2) = 0 V. Match.
- B3 `B3.cir` thermal with R(T): I=2 A, R0=10 mOhm, Rth=750 K/W, alpha=0.0039. Expected dT = I^2 R0 Rth/(1 - I^2 R0 alpha Rth) = 30/(1-0.117) = 33.975 K, tolerance 0.1%. Measured 33.97508 K. Match. This checks the netlist formula only; the Rth value itself is an assumption.
- B4 `B4.cir` high-speed option: 8 nH pin in a 50 Ohm system, expected f(-3 dB) = 100/(2*pi*8e-9) = 1.9894 GHz, tolerance 1%. Measured 1.98924 GHz. Match.
