## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-CON-WTB

Applies to OHM-155 (JST PH, 2.0 mm), 156 (JST XH, 2.5 mm), 157 (JST SH, 1.0 mm, SMD side entry), 158 (Molex KK 254, 2.54 mm).

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
Crimp-housing wire-to-board connectors: a plastic housing with crimped terminals on the cable (the mating "plug") mates a polarized header on the board. Used for batteries (PH, XH), sensor and I2C cables (SH, as in Qwiic/STEMMA QT-style 4-pin 1.0 mm cables per the 3D spec alias), fan and motor harnesses, front-panel and power leads (KK). Sizes by current: SH 1.0 A (AWG 28), PH 2 A (AWG 24), XH 3 A (AWG 22), KK 4.0 A (AWG 22).

### 2. What it is and how it works
A tin-plated copper-alloy post in the board header mates a crimped receptacle terminal in the cable housing (JST PH: "copper alloy, tin plated", housing PA natural for through-hole). Electrically each position is: wire resistance + crimp (wire to terminal) + mated-contact interface + post and solder tail. JST specifies the mated-pair contact resistance (10 mOhm initial max for PH and XH, 20 mOhm for SH; after environmental tests 20, 20, 40 mOhm). Molex KK spec PS-99020-0088: 10 mOhm max initial for mated connectors and 2 mOhm max for the wire termination (crimp). Heating, derating and runaway are the same physics as BEH-CON-HEADER. Current rating is tied to wire gauge: JST states "2 A AC/DC (AWG #24)", "3 A (AWG #22)", "1.0 A (AWG #28)", and the Molex KK table gives 22 AWG 4.0 A, 24 AWG 3.75 A, 26 AWG 3.5 A, 28 AWG 3.0 A.

### 3. How it connects
- Pins: N passive terminals, numbered along the housing. JST marks the "No. 1 circuit" on drawings (JST PH datasheet mentions the "Mark of No. 1 circuit"); the 3D spec places pin 1 at the +Y end with a decal, which is a library convention for display.
- Keying: housings are polarized (a housing cannot be mated rotated 180 degrees), but the assignment of supply versus ground to a pin number is NOT standardized. Which of pin 1 or pin 2 is positive differs between products and vendors. Cable wire color (red = +, black = -) is a convention that is not followed by all vendors. The tool must never infer polarity from a connector type; the user assigns nets to pins and the tool should warn when a connector in a power role connects to a harness whose far-end pin assignment is not confirmed. It is commonly reported that batteries from different sellers fitted with JST-PH plugs have opposite polarity; this is general knowledge, I have no primary source for it, treat as L.
- Wire gauge limits (applicable wire): PH AWG 32-24 (insulation OD 0.5-1.5 mm); XH AWG 30-22 (OD 0.9-1.9 mm); SH AWG 32-28 (OD 0.4-0.8 mm); KK 22-30 AWG per the Molex housing sheet (22-28 AWG per PS-99020-0088 with pull-out force 22 AWG 44 N, 24 AWG 35 N, 26 AWG 26 N, 28 AWG 17 N).
- Mistakes: reversed polarity from mismatched cables; crimping the wrong gauge (poor retention, high crimp resistance); exceeding the rating because the housing fits a larger gauge; pulling on wire instead of housing; thin SH wire plus 1 A load drops significant voltage; using a header for hot-plug of a charged battery (arc on pin ordering).

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
Layer L1, fidelity `behavioural_approximation` (realistic) or `ideal_components` (Rc=0). Template per position k:
```
* board-side header pin Pk to cable far end Wk
R{ref}_m{k} {Pk} {mid} {Rmate}         ; mated pair, JST/Molex spec value
R{ref}_x{k} {mid} {Wk} {Rcrimp}        ; wire crimp (Molex: 2 mohm max)
* the cable itself is a separate resistor: Rwire = rho_per_m(AWG) * length
```
Unmated: no element; the pin has only its board-side net. Valid analyses: op, dc, ac (low frequency), tran, temp. Parameter maps: Rmate = JST "contact resistance" or Molex "contact resistance mated"; Rcrimp = Molex "wire termination"; Irated = rating at the stated AWG. Limitations: ratings apply at the stated gauge only; a thinner wire lowers the usable current (wire dominates); wire resistance per metre is general AWG table practice (AWG24 about 84.2 Ohm/km at 20 C) not read from a source here (ASSUMPTION M); inductance and capacitance are not modeled (cables are slow-signal only here; L2/L3 interface behavior is out of scope).

| N | positions | 2 (SH: 4) | 2 | 16 (UNCERTAIN, 3D spec) | 3D spec | OHM spec |
| Rmate (initial, max) | mOhm | PH 10, XH 10, SH 20, KK 10 | 0 | PH/XH 20, SH 40, KK 20 (after tests/assumed) | MFR_DATASHEET | S1, S2 |
| Rmate default for sim | mOhm | PH 6, XH 6, SH 12, KK 6 (0.6 x spec max) | | | ASSUMPTION (L) | - |

### 6. Ratings and limits
Conflicts: Molex KK voltage is 250 V in PS-99020-0088 but 500 V on the product page for 22232021; operating temperature is 0 to +75 degC in the spec and -40 to +80 degC on the product page. Use the more conservative (250 V, 0-75 degC) until the part-specific product spec PS-47053-001-001 is read. JST temperature ranges "include temperature rise in applying electrical current", so the T limit is on the contact, not the ambient, which the check expression honors. Checks: `I > Irated(AWG)` WARN; `Tamb + dT > Tmax` FAIL; `V > Vwork` WARN; wire gauge outside the AWG range for the housing WARN; `I > ampacity(AWG)` WARN (Molex table above for KK only).

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior
Overcurrent: housing softens, contact spring loses force, plastic can melt (nylon/PA housing); sim: flag at Irated, `damaged` at Tmax exceed, runaway open. Reverse polarity from cable mismatch: the sim connects whatever nets the user wired; a polarity-sensitive load (diode, electrolytic, IC protection) then fails by its own model (see bench B1); the connector only transmits. Overvoltage beyond Vwork: arcing risk (SH only 50 V). Mating cycles: KK 25 cycles; JST allows 10-20 mOhm after tests. Wrong gauge: add pull-out or high-resistance warning. Hot-plug: not modeled. ESD: none. Permanent versus recoverable: overheated housing is permanent; unmated is recoverable.

### 8. Thermal behavior
Same equations as BEH-CON-HEADER (section 8), with Rth = 30 K / (Irated^2 * R0) using the spec max R0 and dT = 30 K assumed (ASSUMPTION). Example PH: R0 = 10 mOhm, 2 A: Rth = 750 K/W, dT = 34.0 K with R(T) feedback (B3 of the header class). JST's stated ranges explicitly include the self-heating allowance, so a PH contact at 2 A in 75 degC ambient is at the +105 limit if dT is 30 K.

### 9. Appearance summary
White/ivory plastic shrouded housings; PH 5.9 x 4.5 x 6.0, XH taller 7.4 x 5.75 x 7.0, SH tiny low ivory SMD housing, Molex KK with friction-lock ramp and partial shroud. See OHM-155 to OHM-158.

### 10. Validation benches (/home/claude/behavior/bench/beh-con-wtb/)
- B1 `B1.cir` harness polarity: straight harness lets a diode load conduct (about 0.043 A, expected approximately (5 - 0.75 V)/100 = 0.0425 A, tolerance 5%), crossed harness (+ on - pin) leaves the diode reverse biased, v(c2) = 5.000 V with no load current. Measured straight_i = 0.04244 A, v(c2) = 5.0 V. Match.
- B2 `B2.cir` 0.3 m AWG24 harness with KK values: per conductor 2*10 + 2*2 mOhm + 25.26 mOhm wire = 49.26 mOhm; V_load = 5*1/(1+0.09852) = 4.55158 V, tolerance 0.1%. Measured 4.551578 V. Match.

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-CON-TERMINAL

Applies to OHM-159 (2-pos screw terminal), 160 (3-pos), 161 (pluggable terminal block, header plus plug).

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
Field wiring for power and I/O: supply input, motor and relay outputs, sensor cables, mains-adjacent or 24 V industrial wiring. Screw clamp terminals (Phoenix MKDS family, 5.0/5.08 mm) hold a stripped wire under a screw clamp; pluggable blocks (MSTB/MSTBA, 5.08 mm) put the header on the PCB and a screw plug on the cable so the harness can be disconnected.

### 2. What it is and how it works
A tin-plated brass/copper clamp and solder pin per position in a PA (polyamide) body (Phoenix MSTB: "PA, UL94 V0"). The wire-to-clamp interface is a gas-tight screw joint; its resistance depends on torque and strand condition (too low torque is high resistance, too high crushes strands). The pluggable version adds a mated contact between header pin and plug socket. Phoenix does not publish contact resistance in the datasheets I opened. Ratings are given as nominal current at the maximum conductor size, plus rated voltage with overvoltage category and pollution degree (III/2 means overvoltage category III, pollution degree 2), and a rated surge voltage (4 kV).

### 3. How it connects
- Pins: N passive terminals, one per position; no polarity, no keying on screw terminals (3D spec). The pluggable block's polarity is mechanical coding only (coding can be added to prevent wrong plug/header pairing but the electrical polarity of each position is chosen by the user).
- Wire sizes: MKDS 1,5/2-5,08: AWG 26-14, 0.14-1.5 mm^2 stranded or 2.5 solid (MKDSP sheet); torque 0.5-0.6 Nm. MSTB 2,5/2-ST-5,08: AWG 24-12, 0.2-2.5 mm^2, torque 0.5-0.6 Nm (M3 screw).
- Typical circuits: DC supply entry with reverse-protection downstream; motor and relay load outputs; sensor 2- and 3-wire (3-position: supply, signal, ground, order set by the user).
- Mistakes: miswired polarity (nothing mechanical prevents it); wire gauge too small for the load, so the wire overheats before the terminal; insulation clamped under the screw (open or high-resistance joint); loose screw; stranded wire without ferrule spreading; using the terminal rating for a thinner wire; exceeding rated voltage category in mains work.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
Layer L1, `behavioural_approximation` realistic, `ideal_components` when Rc=0. Template per position k:
```
R{ref}_cl{k} {Wk} {Pk} {Rclamp}        ; screw clamp joint, ASSUMPTION
R{ref}_mt{k} {Pk} {Hk} {Rmate}         ; only for OHM-161 header/plug mated pair
```
Unmated pluggable: no elements; header pins exist as board nets, plug side has only its wires. Valid analyses: op, dc, ac low frequency, tran, temp. Limitations: no source gives a contact resistance for Phoenix terminals in the documents I opened, so Rclamp (3 mOhm default) is an ASSUMPTION L and may be wrong by several x; the current limit is the lesser of terminal rating and wire ampacity; no inductance model.

### 5. Parameters

| N | positions | 2 (159), 3 (160), 2 (161) | 2 | 12 (screw), 22 (pluggable) per 3D spec | 3D spec | OHM spec |
| Rclamp | mOhm | 3 | 0 | 10 | ASSUMPTION (L) | - |
| Rmate (161 only) | mOhm | 3 | 0 | 10 | ASSUMPTION (L) | - |
| Irated | A | MKDS 17.5; MSTB 12; derate below | | | MFR_DATASHEET | S1, S2 |
| Vrated | V | MKDS 400 (III/2) or 250 (MKDSP sheet), RS lists 160 V for 5.0 mm MKDS 1,5/2; MSTB 320 (III/2) | | | MFR_DATASHEET (conflict shown) | S1, S2 |
| AWG range | AWG | MKDS 26-14; MSTB 24-12 | | | MFR_DATASHEET | S1, S2 |
| torque | Nm | 0.5 to 0.6 | | | MFR_DATASHEET | S1, S2 |
| Tmax | degC | 100 (MSTBA, distributor listing; "subject to derating") | | | MFR_DATASHEET (distributor) | S3 |

### 6. Ratings and limits
Values: MKDS 1,5/2-5,08 (Phoenix datasheet dated 2014-08-13, distributor copy): 17.5 A, 400 V (III/2), 1.5 mm^2, AWG 26-14. MKDSP 1.5/2-5.08 (1730120, dated 2011-01-19): 17.5 A nominal, "maximum load current 22 A", 250 V, surge 4 kV, AWG 26-14, 0.5-0.6 Nm. RS Components lists MKDS 1.5/2 (5 mm, 1715022): 10 A, 160 V, a different variant, pitch 5 mm. MSTB 2,5/2-ST-5,08 (1757019, 2014-06-12): 12 A (with 2.5 mm^2), 320 V (III/2), 4 kV surge, AWG 24-12. MSTBA 2,5/2-G-5,08 (1757242, distributor): 12 A, 320 V, -40 to +100 degC (subject to derating). Do not trust the 17.5 A figure for AWG 26 wires; the wire carries less than the terminal. Rule: `I_allowed = min(Irated_terminal, ampacity(AWG))` with ampacity left as RESEARCH_REQUIRED (the only wire-current source I opened is Molex KK for AWG 22-28 crimp). Derating many loaded positions: the Phoenix datasheets do not give a curve in the text read; assume 0.8 for all positions loaded (ASSUMPTION L). Checks: `I > I_allowed` WARN; `V > Vrated` WARN; `AWG outside range` WARN; `torque` informational.

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior
Overcurrent: clamp and wire heat, PA body softens or discolors (UL94 V0, but thermal limit by rating); sim flags at I_allowed, `damaged` at Tmax exceed. Loose clamp: Rclamp rises (a user can set 100 mOhm to see the heating, P = I^2*R, e.g. 10 A, 0.1 Ohm gives 10 W, which is the classic terminal fire). Reverse polarity: not detected by the connector. Overvoltage above rated: creepage failure, permanent. Plug not inserted (OHM-161): open circuit, recoverable. Open: unterminated screw is the same as unmated. ESD: none.

### 8. Thermal behavior
dT = I^2*Rc*Rth with the same self-consistent R(T) and runaway form. Derived Rth = 30/(Irat^2 * Rc): for R0 = 3 mOhm and Irat = 12 A this is 69.4 K/W, dT = 33.98 K at 12 A and runaway current 35.1 A (benches). Rth is ASSUMPTION; the real limit is the Phoenix rating at the stated conductor and the 100 degC listing.

### 9. Appearance summary
Green PA block with screw heads on top and wire openings on the side (159, 160, 5.08 mm); the pluggable block is a two-piece green assembly, taller plug with screws and a shrouded header. See OHM-159 to OHM-161.

### 10. Validation benches (/home/claude/behavior/bench/beh-con-terminal/)
- B1 `B1.cir` overcurrent flag: 10 A through a 6 mOhm contact pair, Irated 12 A, derate 0.8 (limit 9.6 A). Expected flag = 1, P = 100*0.006 = 0.6 W. Measured flag = 1, P = 0.6 W. Match. (A B-source with a conditional expression was accepted by ngspice 42; no XSPICE needed.)
- B2 `B2.cir` thermal and runaway: R0 = 3 mOhm, Rth from 30 K at 12 A, alpha 0.0039. Expected dT = 33.975 K and I_run = 35.08 A. Measured 33.97508 K and 35.08232 A. Match.

## Per-entry sections

## [OHM-150] 1xN male pin header -> BEH-CON-HEADER
- Defaults: N = 8, 1 row, gold (Wurth WR-PHD style), Rc 10 mOhm, Rbulk 2 mOhm, Lpin 8 nH, Irated 3 A, Tmax 105 degC, cycles 25 (conservative), mated=false.
- Pin map: P1..PN = terminals 1..N; pin 1 at +Y end ("(0, +(N-1)/2 x 2.54)"), numbering toward -Y (3D spec). Existing catalog analogue: `HEADER_1X6_254` (pins 1..6, passive).
- Polarity: none; no keying. Silkscreen pin 1 is a footprint convention.
- Mated pair: a mate with OHM-152 or a Dupont housing; N contacts each Rc. A shunt connects adjacent P_i, P_i+1.
- Notes: current derating per class; header series (Samtec 4.7 to 6.3 A, Wurth/Harwin 3 A) selectable. Status: partial (Rc typical and Rth assumed).

## [OHM-151] 2xN male pin header -> BEH-CON-HEADER
- Defaults: N = 5 (10 pins), 2 rows; same electrical values as OHM-150.
- Pin map: 2N pins, odd pins on -X row, even pins on +X row, pairs descending in -Y; pin 1 at (-1.27, +(N-1)/2 x 2.54) (3D spec). Pins 1-2 are a row pair; the usual jumper positions are 1-2, 3-4, ...
- Polarity: none. A 2xN IDC or Dupont housing can be mated 180 degrees rotated, which swaps pin pairs; the sim should warn that unshrouded headers do not prevent it.
- Derating: k = 0.7 when all 2N loaded. Status: partial.

## [OHM-152] 1xN female header -> BEH-CON-HEADER
- Defaults: N = 8, female contacts (spring beams), Rc 10 mOhm (Rc for a female/male interface; no separate contact in the pin path), Irated 3 A (Samtec SSW and Wurth female not read separately; SSW listed in S1 with TSW: 4.7 A).
- Pin map: P1..PN = contacts 1..N; pin 1 at +Y end; numbering toward -Y (3D spec). Tail 0.64 square "UNCERTAIN".
- Polarity: none. Mates only with a male pin; male-male is rejected.
- Notes: female socket sets mated count to mate_ref; the 25-cycle Wurth rating is the conservative default; Samtec 1000 cycles. Status: partial (female-specific datasheet not read).

## [OHM-153] 2xN female header -> BEH-CON-HEADER
- Defaults: N = 5 (10 contacts); same electrical values as OHM-152.
- Pin map: 2N contacts, odd on -X row, even on +X row, pairs descending -Y; pin 1 at (-1.27, +(N-1)/2 x 2.54) (3D spec).
- Polarity: none; unkeyed. Status: partial.

## [OHM-154] Right-angle pin header -> BEH-CON-HEADER
- Defaults: N = 8, 1 row (2xN supported), Rc 10 mOhm, Rbulk 4 mOhm (longer elbow path, DERIVED, L), Lpin 11 nH (DERIVED, L), Irated 3 A, cycles 25.
- Pin map: 1xN pin 1 at +Y end; 2xN pin 1 at (-1.27, +(N-1)/2 x 2.54) with odd pins on the upper row, descending toward -Y (3D spec). Tail depth 3.0 below board top.
- Polarity: none. Row stacking staggers tails; electrically identical.
- Notes: mechanical stress at the elbow and cable pull is not an electrical effect; same ratings as straight. Status: partial.

## [OHM-155] JST-PH connector -> BEH-CON-WTB
- Defaults: B2B-PH-K-S style, N = 2, 2.0 mm pitch. Irated 2 A (AWG24), Vwork 100 V, Tmax 105 degC (includes rise), Rmate spec 10 mOhm initial max (20 after tests), sim default 6 mOhm, AWG 32-24.
- Pin map: pins 1..N, pin 1 at (0, +(N-1)/2 x 2.0) = (0, 1.0) for N = 2, numbering toward -Y (3D spec). JST marks "No. 1 circuit".
- Polarity: housing is polarized (cannot be reversed) but nothing says which pin is positive; battery packs and cables from different vendors differ. The tool must make the user assign nets and show a warning for a power role.
- Notes: side-entry S2B-PH-K-S and SMT variants not modeled. Status: partial.

## [OHM-156] JST-XH connector -> BEH-CON-WTB
- Defaults: B2B-XH-A, N = 2, 2.5 mm pitch. Irated 3 A (AWG22), Vwork 250 V, Tmax 85 degC (includes rise), Rmate 10 mOhm initial max (20 after tests), sim default 6 mOhm, AWG 30-22.
- Pin map: pin 1 at (0, +(N-1)/2 x 2.5) = (0, 1.25), toward -Y (3D spec). Marked "No. 1 circuit".
- Polarity: polarized housing; positive pin not standardized (same warning). Common for balance leads: N may be larger and positions carry different cell taps; not a power-pair assumption.
- Status: partial.

## [OHM-157] JST-SH connector -> BEH-CON-WTB
- Defaults: SM04B-SRSS-TB, N = 4, 1.0 mm pitch, SMD side entry. Irated 1.0 A (AWG28), Vwork 50 V, Tmax 85 degC, Rmate 20 mOhm initial max (40 after tests), sim default 12 mOhm, AWG 32-28, IR 100 MOhm min.
- Pin map: pin 1 at (+2.0, +1.5) for SM04B, numbering toward -Y; top-entry BM04B pin 1 at (-1.325, +1.5) (3D spec). No housing pin-1 mark confirmed.
- Polarity: polarized housing; signal order is defined by the application (I2C-style 4-pin cables, per the 3D spec alias) and is not set by JST. No pin-assignment is implied. 4 positions with 1 A each is a conservative limit; use derating 0.8 if all loaded.
- Notes: the thin AWG28 wire drops about 0.2 Ohm/m at 1 A (AWG28 about 213 Ohm/km, general table, unsourced).
- Status: partial.

## [OHM-158] Molex KK connector -> BEH-CON-WTB
- Defaults: 22-23-2021 style, N = 2, 2.54 mm, friction-lock ramp. Irated 4.0 A (AWG22), 3.75 A (24), 3.5 A (26), 3.0 A (28); Vwork 250 V (conflict: 500 V on part page); temperature 0 to +75 (spec) vs -40 to +80 (part page); Rmate 10 mOhm initial max, Rcrimp 2 mOhm max; cycles 25.
- Pin map: pin 1 at (0, +(N-1)/2 x 2.54) = (0, 1.27), toward -Y (3D spec). Pin 1 mark not read; polarized lock features identify orientation.
- Polarity: positive pin is not standardized; cables vary.
- Notes: Molex housing sheet for 0470541000 refers to terminals 2759 for 22-30 AWG; I did not open PS-47053-001-001. Status: partial.

## [OHM-159] 2-position screw terminal -> BEH-CON-TERMINAL
- Defaults: Phoenix MKDS 1,5/2-5,08 style, N = 2, 5.08 mm. Irated 17.5 A at 1.5 mm^2 (derate to wire), Vrated 400 V (III/2) per 2014 datasheet (conflict: 160 V on RS for a 5 mm variant; 250 V MKDSP), AWG 26-14, torque 0.5-0.6 Nm, Rclamp 3 mOhm (assumed).
- Pin map: P1 at (0, 2.54), P2 at (0, -2.54), solder pins 0.9 x 0.9, toward -Y (3D spec).
- Polarity: none; user assigns + and -.
- Notes: wire is the limiting element for small AWG; user is warned. Status: partial.

## [OHM-160] 3-position screw terminal -> BEH-CON-TERMINAL
- Defaults: N = 3, 5.08 mm, same values as OHM-159; derating 0.8 if all three carry current.
- Pin map: P1 at (0, 5.08), P2 (0, 0), P3 (0, -5.08) (3D spec).
- Polarity: none; typical use supply/signal/ground, but the assignment is the user's.
- Status: partial.

## [OHM-161] Pluggable terminal block -> BEH-CON-TERMINAL
- Defaults: Phoenix MSTBA 2,5/2-G-5,08 header plus MSTB 2,5/2-ST-5,08 plug, N = 2. Irated 12 A, Vrated 320 V (III/2), 4 kV surge, AWG 24-12, torque 0.5-0.6 Nm, Tmax 100 degC (header listing), Rclamp 3 mOhm and Rmate 3 mOhm (assumed).
- Pin map: header pins 1..N at +Y end first, (0, +(N-1)/2 x 5.08) (3D spec); the plug has no PCB pins and is a separate mating object with the same positions. Unmated plug: header pins exist but connect nowhere.
- Polarity: mechanical coding only; electrical polarity is the user's.
- Notes: model state `mated` toggles the header/plug path; cycles RESEARCH_REQUIRED. Status: partial.

- All 12 entries: pin numbering and pin 1 location used exactly as the 3D spec states.
- 3D spec says JST pin 1 is at the +Y end as a decal convention; JST's own documents mark a "No. 1 circuit", which is consistent but not the same as polarity. KK pin-1 mark was not read in either source.
- 3D spec headers 1x6 existing catalog record lists pins as "P1".."P6" (passive), consistent with this behavior.
- 3D spec lists solder pins "0.9 x 0.9" for MKDS; no electrical conflict.

# GROUP R10A: I/O connectors, USB, HDMI, RJ, audio (OHM-162 to OHM-171)

Output of the R10A research agent. Bench netlists are in `bench/beh-con-usb/`, `bench/beh-con-hdmi/`, `bench/beh-con-modjack/`, `bench/beh-con-audio/` (paths relative to `/home/claude/behavior/`). Every benchmark number in this file was produced by `ngspice -b` (ngspice-42) in this environment.

## 0. Group overview and conventions

Four behavior classes cover the 10 entries.

| Class | Entries | Layer | Core idea |
|---|---|---|---|
| BEH-CON-USB | OHM-162, 163, 164, 165, 166 | L1 body, L3 protocol | one resistor per mated contact, net list per variant, optional pair parasitics; CC resistors are NOT in the connector |
| BEH-CON-HDMI | OHM-167, 168 | L1 body, L3 protocol | 19 contacts, 100 ohm TMDS pairs (current-mode link, 50 ohm to AVcc at the sink), DDC/CEC/HPD side channels |
| BEH-CON-MODJACK | OHM-169, 170 | L1 body, L3 protocol | 8P8C and 6P4C/6P6C jack contacts, optional integrated magnetics (magjack) and LEDs |
| BEH-CON-AUDIO | OHM-171 | L1 | TRS/TRRS contact set plus normally closed switch contacts that open on plug insertion |

Fidelity for every class: `ideal_components` when contact resistance is 0, `behavioural_approximation` in realistic mode (datasheet maximum contact resistance, optional pair C and L). No vendor SPICE model exists or is attached for any of these, so `vendor_model` is never claimed. All classes follow the mated-pair convention of `parts/R9.md` (BEH-CON-HEADER): a contact whose mate is absent emits no element; a mating relation emits one resistor (Rc) per contact between the two sides' nets; pin names and the existing catalog record scheme are kept (`USB_C_RECEPTACLE_16P.json` uses A1..B12 numbering, `passive` for power/ground/SBU, `bidirectional` for CC and D+/D-).

Layer split (decision for the coordinator): the connector body is L1 only. USB, HDMI (TMDS, DDC, CEC, HPD) and Ethernet link protocols are L3. This file documents the electrical interface that an L3 layer must drive or sense, and states what the protocol layer must supply. Nothing here claims a protocol simulates in SPICE.

Cross-class rules:
1. **Connectors are not circuits.** The CC resistors (Rd, Rp, Ra), the D+ pull-up, the ESD diodes, the common-mode choke on a USB data pair, the HDMI DDC pull-ups and TMDS terminations, the Ethernet magnetics (unless a magjack), the audio detect pull-up, are board or IC circuitry. They get their own parts, or a "helper subcircuit" in `bench/beh-con-usb/usb_io.lib` that the design generator inserts on request. A design that omits them must be flagged by DRC (the existing `usbc.rd_required` rule), not silently fixed by the connector model.
2. **Ratings are per contact or per group of contacts**, taken from the datasheet; the check expression is evaluated per contact (or per power group for USB-C VBUS/GND).
3. **Case-insensitive node names (ngspice trap).** ngspice treats `vB` and `vb` as the same node. The first version of bench B5 silently shorted a load output to the supply this way (output read 5.000 V instead of 0 when the VBUS switch was open). Generated nets must be unique after lowercasing.
4. **Method caveat.** Pages were read through the WebFetch tool, which returns a model-written summary, not raw PDF text. Numbers marked "(summarizer)" below were not read from the page by eye. The USB-IF specifications (USB 2.0, USB Type-C R2.0) were requested but the tool returned only a table-of-contents excerpt for them, so no number below is attributed to USB-IF text; USB 2.0 and Type-C numbers that I could not confirm from a manufacturer document are labelled as recalled and have confidence L or M.

Source IDs are global to this file (S1..S22 at the end).

---

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-CON-USB

Applies to OHM-162 (USB-A receptacle), OHM-163 (USB-B), OHM-164 (Micro-USB Micro-B), OHM-165 (USB Type-C), OHM-166 (Mini-USB Mini-B). Layer L1 (body, VBUS/GND contacts, optional pair model); L3 (USB protocol, Type-C CC state machine, Power Delivery, OTG role switching).

### 1. Purpose and real-world use

A USB receptacle is the board-side half of a cable connection that carries power (VBUS and GND) and, in USB 2.0, one differential data pair (D+ and D-). Typical uses: device power input (5 V sink), host port (5 V source with current limiting), data link to a microcontroller or USB-UART bridge, battery charging, and (Type-C) role and power negotiation. Variants and typical use:

- **Standard-A receptacle (OHM-162):** host side of the cable (PC ports, hubs, chargers). 4 contacts: VBUS, D-, D+, GND.
- **Standard-B receptacle (OHM-163):** device side of larger peripherals (printers, instruments). 4 contacts.
- **Micro-B receptacle (OHM-164) and Mini-B (OHM-166):** device side of small devices; 5 contacts including ID (S9 lists 5 circuits for the Molex 105017; S10 lists 5 positions for Wurth 65100516121). ID is used by On-The-Go (OTG).
- **Type-C receptacle (OHM-165):** reversible, host or device, up to 24 contacts (A1..A12, B1..B12); 16-pin variants are USB 2.0 only; 6-pin variants are power only (S4).

### 2. What it is and how it works

Construction: stamped copper-alloy spring contacts (phosphor bronze, gold plated; S11 lists "Phosphor Bronze" with gold plating for the Molex 67643) in a plastic housing inside a nickel-plated steel shell. The shell is a shield and is also the mechanical anchor (PTH or SMD legs). Electrically a mated contact is a low resistance: the constriction resistance at the spring wipe plus film resistance, tens of milliohms (S1: 40 mOhm max initial, 50 mOhm after test for the GCT USB4105; S10: 20 mOhm max for the Wurth mini-B; S15 shows the same order for modular jacks).

**USB 2.0 electrical interface (what the connector carries; numbers marked R are recalled, USB-IF text not opened):**

| item | value | basis | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| VBUS at a device | 4.75 to 5.25 V | S8 (a TI power-switch datasheet restating the USB requirement for downstream ports) | host port supply range |
| unit loads | 100 mA is one unit load; low-power function <= 100 mA, high-power function up to 500 mA after enumeration | S8 ("It must power up with less than 100 mA", "can draw up to 500 mA after enumeration") | 500 mA = 5 unit loads (R) |
| inrush rule | a function whose load is larger than 44 ohm in parallel with 10 uF at power up must limit inrush | S8 | limits bulk capacitance behind the connector |
| USB 3.x (SuperSpeed) | 900 mA | R (brief; not confirmed) | needs the 9-pin A or the Type-C SS pairs |
| D+/D- full-speed idle/identification | device pulls D+ to 3.0 to 3.6 V with 1.5 kohm (full speed); low speed pulls D- | S7 (D+ 1.5 kohm to 3.0..3.6 V); S11 not needed; low-speed rule R | host has 15 kohm pull-downs on both lines (R) |
| signal levels | full-speed swing about 0 to 3.3 V single-ended; high-speed 400 mV differential into 45 ohm per line | R (brief and general knowledge) | not in an opened document |
| differential impedance | 90 ohm +-15 % | S6 ("differential impedance 90 +-15 %") | routing and connector transition |
| ESD | put ESD devices close to the connector; must be USB 2.0 compliant (low capacitance) because they load the line | S7, S6 | |
| ID pin (Micro/Mini-B, Micro-AB) | identifies A-device vs B-device role for OTG: ID grounded (via plug) = A-device (host); floating = B-device | S7 states ID identifies the role in micro-AB; the grounded/floating rule is R | a micro-B plug leaves ID floating; micro-A plug grounds it |
| shield | connected to chassis/ground; DC to GND or through RC (design choice) | S6, S4 (shell = GND in S1 table) | the shield is not a signal |

**USB Type-C additions** (S1, S2, S3, S4):

- Contact set: A1/B1/A12/B12 GND (4), A4/B4/A9/B9 VBUS (4), A5 CC1, B5 CC2 (VCONN on the one CC pin not used for communication), A6/B6 D+, A7/B7 D-, A8 SBU1, B8 SBU2, plus the SuperSpeed lanes A2/A3 TX1+/TX1-, A10/A11 RX2-/RX2+, B2/B3 TX2+/TX2-, B10/B11 RX1-/RX1+ (the lane assignments are recalled; S1 and S4 confirm the pins that carry USB 2.0, CC, VBUS, GND and SBU, S1 lists A5/B5, A6/B6, A7/B7, A8/B8).
- **Rd (sink termination):** each CC pin of a sink is pulled to GND with 5.1 kohm. S2: "UFP's Rd value is fixed at 5.1 kOhm". S4: "CC1 and CC2 need to be pulled down with 5.1 kOhm resistors". The Type-C spec tolerance quoted in the existing catalog record is +-20 % (record `usbc.rd_required`, not machine verified); S3 (summarizer) quotes 5.1 kOhm +-10 % for the power-capability detection table. The two numbers differ; keep both (5.1 k nominal, 10 to 20 % tolerance).
- **Rp (source current advertisement):** S2 and S3 agree (pull-up resistor option): default USB power Rp = 56 kohm +-20 % to 4.75..5.5 V (36 kohm +-20 % to 3.3 V); 1.5 A @ 5 V Rp = 22 kohm +-5 % (12 kohm +-5 % to 3.3 V); 3.0 A @ 5 V Rp = 10 kohm +-5 % (4.7 kohm +-5 % to 3.3 V). The same advertisement can be made with a current source: 80 uA +-20 %, 180 uA +-8 %, 330 uA +-8 % (S3, summarizer).
- **Sink detection voltages (S3, summarizer, with a Type-C 5.1 kohm Rd):** attach window 0.25 to 2.04 V; vRd-USB 0.25 to 0.61 V (decision threshold 0.66 V); vRd-1.5 0.70 to 1.16 V (threshold 1.23 V); vRd-3.0 1.31 to 2.04 V. Bench B2 shows the three resistor values land inside these windows (0.417 V, 0.941 V, 1.689 V at 5 V).
- **Orientation:** the source (DFP) pulls both its CC pins up with Rp; the cable connects exactly one CC wire end to end, so the DFP sees Rd on exactly one of CC1/CC2; that tells it the plug orientation. The other CC pin of the plug carries Ra (800 to 1200 ohm to GND, S2) in a cable that needs VCONN, which tells the DFP to apply VCONN to that pin. The mux that swaps D+/D- and SuperSpeed lanes is a board circuit.
- **VCONN:** 5 V supply on the CC pin that is not used for communication, for e-marker or active cables. S1 gives B5 a higher current rating (1.25 A) than A5 (0.25 A), consistent with B5 being the pin that carries VCONN on this receptacle, but the A5/B5 assignment is orientation-dependent; the connector rating is per physical pin, not per role.
- **Why a USB-C device needs Rd on the receptacle even on an A-to-C cable:** a legacy Type-A host has no CC logic. The A-to-C cable carries Rp (56 kohm to VBUS) inside the Type-C plug, so a cable plug presents Rp to the device's CC pin and the device's Rd closes the divider; the device then reads "default USB power". A device with no Rd works (by luck) on an A-to-C cable because an A host powers VBUS unconditionally, but is dead on a C-to-C cable, because a Type-C host keeps VBUS off until it sees Rd. This is the commonest USB-C mistake in hobby boards. Another is one resistor shared by both CC pins: with the cable's Ra on the other pin the shared node is Rd || Ra, which pulls vCC to 0.074 V in bench B2/B5, below the 0.25 V attach threshold (S3), so the host never turns on VBUS.
- **Receptacle variants:** 24-pin (full), 16-pin and 12-pin (USB 2.0: GND, VBUS, CC1, CC2, D+, D-, SBU as available), 6-pin (power and CC only) (S4). In 16-pin parts A6/B6 and A7/B7 are both present and are tied together on the board (S4: "A6 is tied to B6 as D+ and A7 is tied to B7 as D-"). SBU1/SBU2 are not used by a USB-2 sink and are left unconnected.

Key quantities:
- Contact drop: V = I * Rc_eff, with Rc_eff = Rc/n_parallel for n parallel contacts of one net (Type-C: VBUS n = 4, GND n = 4).
- CC divider: vCC = Vp * Rd / (Rd + Rp).
- Self-heating: P = I^2 * Rc_eff, DeltaT = P * Rth (Rth is an assumption, see section 8).

### 3. How it connects

Electrical pins by variant (map by NAME; the OHM numbering is the 3D spec's, see per-entry sections):

| function | USB-A / USB-B | Micro-B / Mini-B | Type-C (24-pin) | electrical type |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| VBUS | 1 | 1 | A4, A9, B4, B9 (all one net) | power_in (device) or power_out (host) |
| D- | 2 | 2 | A7, B7 | bidirectional |
| D+ | 3 | 3 | A6, B6 | bidirectional |
| ID | none | 4 | none (CC replaces it) | input |
| GND | 4 | 5 | A1, A12, B1, B12 | passive/power |
| CC | none | none | A5 (CC1), B5 (CC2/VCONN) | bidirectional |
| SBU | none | none | A8 (SBU1), B8 (SBU2) | passive |
| SuperSpeed | none (9-pin A only) | none | A2 A3 A10 A11 B2 B3 B10 B11 | bidirectional |
| SHELL | 2 legs | 4 shell pads/pegs | 4 shell legs | passive |

The existing catalog record `USB_C_RECEPTACLE_16P.json` has the 16 non-SuperSpeed contacts and no shell pin; the 3D entry OHM-165 has 24 contacts (see per-entry notes). Neither record has a shell/SHELL pin, so the shield cannot currently be connected in a design. Recommend adding a `SHELL` (passive) pin to each connector record.

Typical circuits:
- **Device powered from USB (sink):** VBUS -> (ESD TVS to GND, ferrite or fuse optional) -> input protection/regulator; D+/D- via ESD array to the MCU PHY (with 1.5 kohm D+ pull-up if the MCU lacks one internal, S7); Type-C: 5.1 kohm from each of CC1 and CC2 to GND; shield to GND (direct, or RC).
- **Host port (source):** current-limited power switch on VBUS (S8: "up to 500 mA"), 15 kohm pull-downs on D+/D- (R), 120 uF bulk capacitance recommended by the standard (R; not found in S8's text).
- **Type-C source:** Rp from a supply to CC1 and CC2 (value sets advertised current), a VBUS switch that closes only when a sink Rd is detected.

Common mistakes: Type-C Rd missing or shared (above); D+ and D- swapped on a 16-pin part that is wired as a 24-pin; CC pins shorted to VBUS by a solder bridge or contamination (see failure modes); micro-B ID pin tied to GND on a device receptacle (device then believes it is a host); shield and GND confusion; no ESD protection near the connector; connector pin 1 reversed because the footprint was mirrored; assuming both A-row and B-row VBUS pins of a Type-C connector are separate nets on a single-row (16-pin) part.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation

**Layer:** L1 for the connector. L3 for everything protocol. Valid analyses: op, dc, ac, tran, temp (resistive model is frequency independent).

**Connector netlist template (one net group of mated contacts; mated pair convention of R9):**
```
* contact k: board-side net {BOARD_k}  ->  cable-side net {CABLE_k}
R{ref}_c{k}  {BOARD_k} {CABLE_k} {Rc}
* VBUS group (Type-C: four contacts) is simply four of these in parallel
* shield: one contact from the shell pin to the shield net
R{ref}_sh {SHELL} {SHIELD_NET} {Rshell}
* realistic pair option (high-speed only): per leg series L, line-to-ground C
L{ref}_dp {DP_board} {dp_mid} {Lcon}
C{ref}_dp {dp_mid} 0 {Ccon}
```
If the connector is unmated, emit nothing. In ideal mode Rc = 1 uOhm (never 0; ngspice replaces R = 0 by 1 mOhm: see R1.md).

**Helper subcircuits (NOT part of the connector), file `bench/beh-con-usb/usb_io.lib`, tested in bench B5:**
```
.subckt CON_CONTACT a b Rc=40m
.subckt USBC_SINK_RD cc gnd Rd=5.1k       ; sink pull-down, one per CC pin
.subckt USBC_SRC_RP cc vp Rp=56k          ; DFP pull-up (56k / 22k / 10k)
.subckt USBC_DFP_EN cc vbus_in vbus_out gnd vlo=0.25 vhi=2.04 Ron=10m
```
`USBC_DFP_EN` is a behavioural (B source + voltage-controlled switch) stand-in for the source-side CC detector: it closes the VBUS switch when `vlo < v(cc) < vhi`. It is a model of the attach window, not of the Type-C state machine (no debounce tCCDebounce, no VCONN, no PD, no orientation detect).

**Ideal vs realistic:**
- Ideal: Rc = 0 (1 uOhm), no L, no C.
- Realistic: Rc per contact = datasheet maximum (Type-C 40 mOhm, mini-B 20 mOhm, HDMI 20 to 30 mOhm; a new gold contact is usually lower, so the realistic mode overestimates drop), shell resistance, per-contact L and C as optional high-speed parameters.

**Fidelity:** `ideal_components` (Rc = 0) or `behavioural_approximation` (any non-zero Rc, L, C, or the behavioural helper). Never `vendor_model`.

**Known limitations:** Rc is a datasheet maximum, not a typical; no current dependence (heating changes Rc); no wear; the pair model has no mode conversion, no skin effect, no connector discontinuity profile (a real receptacle is a stub-and-bend, not a lumped C); the CC detector does not time anything; SuperSpeed lanes are listed as nets but no SS electrical model is provided (RESEARCH_REQUIRED); Power Delivery (BMC signalling on CC at 300 kHz, 20 V and higher VBUS) is L3 and not modelled.

Derating (ASSUMPTION, general practice): current rating is for a 30 C rise; above 60 C ambient derate linearly to zero at Tmax. Datasheets read here do not state it.

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior

| id | trigger | effect | sim response | permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| over_current_contact | I > rated per contact or per group | contact heating, plating wear, housing softening; at a few times rating, melted housing | flag at I > Irated; if P = I^2 Rc_eff * Rth gives T > Tmax flag overtemperature; do not open the contact | permanent if sustained |
| over_voltage_vbus | VBUS above the connector rating (Molex micro/mini 30 V rms; PD 20 V on a micro-B is out of design intent) | arc/creepage failure, not instantaneous | flag at v > rating; no behavioural change | permanent |
| vbus_to_cc_leak | contamination, liquid or solder bridge between A4/B4 and A5/B5, adjacent pins | CC pin sees 5 to 20 V; unprotected CC input and Rd fail | flag when `abs(v(cc)) > 5.5`; optional model: resistor Rleak between VBUS and CC (default open) | permanent for the IC pin |
| missing_rd | no Rd on a Type-C sink | a Type-C source never closes VBUS; A-to-C cable still works | DRC `usbc.rd_required` (exists) plus the B5 behaviour (vCC > 2.04 V means no attach) | design error |
| shared_rd | one resistor for both CC pins | vCC = Rd || Ra on a cable with Ra: 0.074 V < 0.25 V | flag as detach (B2/B5 case C) | design error |
| reverse_polarity | VBUS and GND swapped | Type-C and A/B plugs are keyed, so only by wiring error: reverse supply to the load | not a connector effect; downstream device model handles | n/a |
| esd | cable plug discharge to shell, D+, D-, CC | gate-oxide damage of an unprotected PHY; connector itself survives | flag any D+/D-/CC/VBUS net on this connector with no TVS/ESD part within the same net; ESD part is a board component (the diode TVS behavior class of R5) | permanent for the IC |
| short_vbus_gnd | cable or board short | host current limit trips (500 mA/900 mA/Type-C advertised) | not connector; the source/power-switch model limits | recoverable |
| open_contact | broken solder joint or worn contact | open net | set Rc to 1e9 ohm | permanent until reflow |
| hot_plug_inrush | plugging a large capacitor on VBUS | VBUS dip and arc across contacts | check `C_vbus <= 10 uF` or limiter (S8 rule: 44 ohm || 10 uF) | recoverable |
| overheating_shell | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a |

### 8. Thermal behavior

Contact heating is P = I^2 * Rc_eff. For a Type-C connector with 4 VBUS and 4 GND contacts at 40 mOhm (worst case initial) and 5 A: Rc_eff = 10 mOhm + 10 mOhm = 20 mOhm, P = 25 A^2 * 0.02 = 0.5 W; at 3 A, 0.18 W. Temperature rise DeltaT = P * Rth with Rth about 100 K/W per connector (ASSUMPTION, L; no datasheet figure was found). A single-pin path (D+, CC, B5) gets its own I^2 * Rc and its own much smaller current rating. Simple model: one node `tcon` with Rth to ambient and a current source of value P; a temperature coefficient for copper Rc (about +0.4 % per K, general value) is optional. Do not use it to hide an over-rating: the ratings table above is the compliance test.

### 9. Appearance summary

All five receptacles are metal shells with a plastic tongue or insulator carrying gold contacts; sizes and shapes differ (USB-A 13.1 x 5.8 mm rectangle, USB-B square with chamfered corners, Micro-B and Mini-B trapezoids, Type-C rounded oval 8.94 x 3.26 mm with a centre tongue and two rows of contacts). See the 3D spec entries OHM-162..OHM-166 for dimensions and recognition features; not re-researched.

### 10. Validation benches

All run with `ngspice -b` from the bench directory (B5 includes `usb_io.lib` relative to its own folder, so run it from `bench/beh-con-usb/`).

| id | file | circuit | expected (formula) | tolerance | measured |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | `bench/beh-con-usb/B1_vbus_drop.cir` | Type-C 4 VBUS + 4 GND contacts at 40 mOhm, sweep load current 0..5 A at 5 V | V_load = 5 - I*(Rc/4 + Rc/4) = 5 - I*0.02: 4.98 (1 A), 4.94 (3 A), 4.90 (5 A) | 0.1 % | 4.980, 4.940, 4.900 V. Match. |
| B2 | `bench/beh-con-usb/B2_cc_rd_divider.cir` | Rp (56k, 22k, 10k to 5 V; 36k, 12k, 4.7k to 3.3 V) with Rd 5.1k; plus shared-Rd case and open-Rd case | vCC = Vp*5.1/(5.1+Rp): 0.4173, 0.9410, 1.6887; 0.4095, 0.9842, 1.7173; shared with Ra 1k: 5*(1/(1/5.1+1/1)=0.8361)/(0.8361+56)=0.07355; open: 5*1G/(1G+56k)=4.99972 | 0.1 % | 0.41735, 0.94096, 1.68874, 0.40949, 0.98421, 1.71735, 0.07355, 4.99972 V. Match. All three Rp cases fall inside the S3 windows (0.25 to 0.61, 0.70 to 1.16, 1.31 to 2.04 V). |
| B3 | `bench/beh-con-usb/B3_pair_term.cir` | 90 ohm differential pair as 2 x 45 ohm per leg: 45 ohm source, 100 ps T line 45 ohm, 1 pF connector pad C per leg, 45 ohm termination; AC | DC gain = 45/(45+45) = 0.5; f(-3 dB) = 1/(2 pi * 22.5 ohm * 1 pF) = 7.074 GHz (45 || 45 = 22.5 ohm) | 1 % | 0.499999 and 7.0737 GHz. Match. |
| B4 | `bench/beh-con-usb/B4_fs_id.cir` | FS device: 1.5k from 3.3 V to D+, host 15k pull-downs | V(D+) = 3.3*15/(15+1.5) = 3.000 V; V(D-) = 0 | 0.1 % | 3.000000 V and 0 V. Match. The model assumes the 15 kohm host value, which is recalled, not sourced; the bench tests the arithmetic only. |
| B5 | `bench/beh-con-usb/B5_dfp_vbus_enable.cir` | DFP behaviour using `usb_io.lib`: A sink with Rd, B no Rd, C shared Rd + Ra | A: VBUS on, 5*100/(100+0.01) = 4.9995 V; B: off (CC at 5 V > 2.04 V), 5*100/(1e9) = 5e-7 V; C: off (CC 0.0736 V < 0.25 V), 5e-7 V | 0.1 % on, absolute 1e-6 off | A 4.99950 V, B 5.0e-7 V, C 5.0e-7 V. Match after a bug fix: the first run read 5.000 V in case B because the output node `vB` collided with the supply node `vb` (ngspice node names are case-insensitive). |

All 5 benches matched their analytical expectation. B3 and B4 verify arithmetic and the netlist idiom; they do not validate the real USB electrical behavior.

### 12. Sources

See the global table at the end (S1 to S11 are used here).

### 13. Research confidence

- (a) Parameters: MEDIUM. Type-C Rc and ratings are from one maker (GCT) drawing; mini-B from one distributor listing; Rd/Rp from two manufacturer documents that agree on the resistor values (S2, S3) and differ on the Rd tolerance; A/B/Micro-B Rc is an assumption.
- (b) Ratings: MEDIUM. Per-pin ratings are from GCT and Molex; Standard-B has no rating.
- (c) Model fidelity: MEDIUM for the resistive contact model, LOW for the pair parasitics.
- (d) Failure behavior: MEDIUM (general, not source-confirmed for VBUS-CC leak).
- Unresolved: USB-IF USB 2.0 and Type-C R2.0 text not obtainable through the tool (only a table-of-contents excerpt returned); USB 2.0 signal levels, host pull-down value and tolerance, USB 3.x 900 mA, 120 uF bulk capacitance, A2/A3/A10/A11 lane assignments are recalled; Type-C contact resistance and VCONN limits per Type-C spec not confirmed; Standard-A/B/Micro-B Rc not found; SuperSpeed and PD not modelled; a 3D-spec shell-pin mapping needs a design decision; whether OHM-165 is the 16-pin or 24-pin Amphenol 12401610E4 part is unresolved (3D spec lists 24 contacts, the catalog record is 16 pins).

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-CON-HDMI

Applies to OHM-167 (HDMI Type A, 19-pin) and OHM-168 (Mini-HDMI Type C, 19-pin). Layer L1 body; L3 for TMDS link, DDC/EDID, CEC and HPD protocols.

### 1. Purpose and real-world use

HDMI carries uncompressed digital video and audio from a source (set-top box, SBC, GPU) to a sink (TV, monitor). Type A is the full-size connector on TVs and boards (OHM-167); Type C ("mini") is on cameras and compact boards (OHM-168). The connector is a 19-contact transfer path for four high-speed differential pairs (three TMDS data pairs and a TMDS clock pair), a DDC (I2C) channel for EDID, a CEC single-wire control line, a hot-plug-detect line and a +5 V supply pin.

### 2. What it is and how it works

**Pin table, Type A (S12; S13 confirms the subset it lists):**

| pin | signal | pin | signal |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | TMDS Data2+ | 11 | TMDS Clock Shield |
| 2 | TMDS Data2 Shield | 12 | TMDS Clock- |
| 3 | TMDS Data2- | 13 | CEC |
| 4 | TMDS Data1+ | 14 | Utility (reserved) |
| 5 | TMDS Data1 Shield | 15 | SCL (DDC clock) |
| 6 | TMDS Data1- | 16 | SDA (DDC data) |
| 7 | TMDS Data0+ | 17 | DDC/CEC Ground |
| 8 | TMDS Data0 Shield | 18 | +5 V Power |
| 9 | TMDS Data0- | 19 | Hot Plug Detect |
| 10 | TMDS Clock+ | shell | shield (mates first) |

S12 gives the mating sequence: shell first, +5 V pin third (last), everything else second. S13 lists the same signals (its summary omits some pins). The 3D spec (OHM-167) places odd pins on one row and even pins on the other, consistent with this table.

**Electrical behavior of the link (recalled values; HDMI Licensing specification not opened):** TMDS is current-mode logic. The source steers a constant current (about 10 mA) into one leg of each pair; the sink terminates each leg with 50 ohm to AVcc (3.3 V), so the single-ended swing is about 0.5 V (400 to 600 mV) and the differential impedance is 100 ohm. Bench B1 checks the arithmetic: 10 mA * 50 ohm = 0.5 V. Because the termination is at the sink and is part of the sink IC, the connector model contains no termination; a netlist that wants to simulate the link adds the 50 ohm to 3.3 V terminations as sink-side parts.

Side channels (L3, values recalled, RESEARCH_REQUIRED against the HDMI specification):
- DDC: I2C, 100 kHz, EDID at address 0x50 (0x50 is the standard EDID address, general knowledge); pull-ups are on the source side to the +5 V rail.
- CEC: single wire, open-drain, shared bus with a pull-up in each device (about 3.3 V logic, high impedance when not driving).
- HPD: sink output, high (about 2.4 to 5.3 V) when the sink is ready to be read; the source treats low as "unplugged".
- +5 V pin: source supplies it for the sink's EDID/DDC power-on (the brief gives "up to 50 mA"; the HDMI source requirement is recalled as a minimum of 55 mA available).

**Contact data (S12, S13, S14):** rated current 0.5 A per contact, 40 Vac, contact resistance 20 mOhm (HD12-19-SMT, S12) or 30 mOhm dry-circuit and 50 mOhm shell (HD01-19-RA-TH, S13), insulation resistance 100 MOhm, withstand 500 Vac unmated and 300 Vac mated (S13), 5,000 to 10,000 mating cycles, -40/-20 to 85/100 C. The TE mini-HDMI listing (S14) gives 0.5 A, 40 VAC, 100 MOhm, opening 10.42 x 2.42 mm, and states that the 19-pin assignment of Type C differs from Type A.

### 3. How it connects

- **TMDS pairs (pins 1/3, 4/6, 7/9, 10/12):** AC- or DC-coupled to the HDMI PHY or an ESD array; route as 100 ohm differential (each leg about 50 ohm); the "shield" pins 2, 5, 8, 11 are grounds for each pair and must connect to ground, not left floating, at both ends of the connector.
- **DDC SCL/SDA (15, 16):** to the I2C of the source (3.3 V or 5 V according to design) or to the EDID EEPROM on a sink; level and pull-up are a board concern.
- **CEC (13):** to a CEC controller or tied through a diode/resistor; unused CEC may be left open.
- **Pin 14 (Utility/reserved):** leave unconnected unless using the optional Ethernet/ARC channel (a later version); not modelled.
- **HPD (19):** sink: drive from +5 V through a resistor when ready; source: sense input with pull-down (value RESEARCH_REQUIRED).
- **+5 V (18):** source: switched supply with current limit; sink: powers the EDID memory only, with a series diode against back-power.
- **Type C (OHM-168):** the signal set is the same 19 signals, but the pin order differs from Type A (S14). The 3D spec itself flags the assignment as unresolved. Map by signal name, not by Type A pin numbers.
- Mistakes: skipping the pair shields to ground; unprotected HPD and DDC pins on a hot-plug connector; back-powering the source through +5 V; routing TMDS with stubs.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation

Layer L1. Per-contact resistor Rc between board net and cable net; shell via Rshell. Optional high-speed model: each TMDS pair is a 100 ohm differential line (two 50 ohm lines for a single-ended model, one 100 ohm line for a differential-equivalent model) with C per pad; the sink termination 2 x 50 ohm to AVcc is a separate part.
```
R{ref}_c{n}  {BOARD_n} {CABLE_n} {Rc}                  ; n = 1..19
R{ref}_sh    {SHELL} {SHIELD_NET} {Rshell}
* optional pair parasitics (per TMDS leg)
C{ref}_p{n}  {BOARD_n} 0 {Cpad}
```
Fidelity: `ideal_components` (Rc = 0) or `behavioural_approximation`. Analyses: op, dc, ac, tran. Limitations: no frequency-dependent loss or crosstalk between the four pairs; the connector impedance discontinuity is a lumped C only; TMDS encoding, HDCP, EDID content, CEC and HPD sequencing are L3 and not modelled; the 5 V I2C pull-ups and the HPD thresholds are RESEARCH_REQUIRED.

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior

| id | trigger | effect | sim response | permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| overcurrent_5v | > 0.5 A on pin 18 or any contact | contact heating | flag; source power switch model limits | permanent if sustained |
| back_power | sink +5 V pin driven while the source is off | damage to source-side supply | flag current into pin 18 from the cable side | permanent |
| esd_hotplug | live plug/unplug, cable discharge | TMDS/HPD/DDC input damage | flag HDMI nets with no ESD array | permanent |
| pair_open | broken solder joint on a TMDS contact | link lost | Rc = 1e9 ohm; L3 shows "no signal" | permanent |
| shield_floating | pair shield pins 2, 5, 8, 11 not grounded | impedance/EMI degradation | flag | design error |
| wrong_map_type_c | Type A numbering used for Type C | wrong signals | refuse mapping by number for OHM-168 | design error |

### 8. Thermal behavior

Contact heating P = I^2 Rc per contact; at 0.5 A and 20 mOhm P = 5 mW, which is negligible. The shell and pair do not carry heat. No thermal model beyond a flag is needed.

### 9. Appearance summary

OHM-167 is a wide, flat, trapezoid-opening metal shell about 14 mm wide with two rows of 19 contacts visible and four shield tabs. OHM-168 is a smaller flat opening about 10.4 x 2.4 mm with fine contacts. See the 3D spec entries OHM-167 and OHM-168.

### 10. Validation benches

| id | file | circuit | expected | tolerance | measured |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | `bench/beh-con-hdmi/B1_tmds_term.cir` | sink terminates each leg 50 ohm to 3.3 V, source steers 10 mA into one leg, Rc 20 mOhm in each leg | V(dp) = 3.3 V; V(dn) = 3.3 - 0.01*(50 + 0.02) = 2.7998 V; Vdiff = 0.5002 V | 0.1 % | 3.3000, 2.7998, 0.50020 V. Match. |
| B2 | `bench/beh-con-hdmi/B2_tline_mismatch.cir` | 100 ohm line (1 ns), matched 100 ohm source, 85 ohm termination | gamma = (85-100)/185 = -0.08108; load first arrival 0.5*(1+gamma) = 0.45946 V; source end after round trip 0.45946 V; before 0.5 V | 0.5 % | 0.459459, 0.459459, 0.500000 V. Match. |

Both matched; these test the arithmetic and the T-line idiom (single-ended equivalent of a differential 100 ohm pair), not a real HDMI eye.

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-CON-MODJACK

Applies to OHM-169 (RJ45 8P8C jack, default plain shielded jack; magjack variant with LEDs) and OHM-170 (RJ11 6P4C jack). Layer L1 body; L3 for the link (Ethernet PHY/MAC, auto-negotiation, auto-MDI-X; telephone line signalling).

### 1. Purpose and real-world use

An 8P8C modular jack ("RJ45") terminates twisted-pair Ethernet cable. A plain jack passes the eight conductors to the board, where the magnetics (a separate transformer part, see OHM-055 and `parts/R3.md` BEH-MAG-ETHMAG) provide isolation; a "magjack" (RJ45 jack with integrated magnetics and LEDs, for example the Amphenol RJHSE538X family named in the 3D spec) has the transformers and common-mode chokes inside the housing. A 6P4C/6P6C jack ("RJ11"/"RJ12") is the telephone connector: line 1 on the centre pair, line 2 on the next pair outward in a 6P4C. These are legacy-style connectors; here the RJ11 entry is covered only as a connector.

### 2. What it is and how it works

Eight (RJ45) or four to six (RJ11) phosphor-bronze spring contacts in a plastic housing, usually inside a metal shield, gold over nickel (S15: "Phosphor Bronze; Gold over Nickel"). Rated values from an Amphenol modular jack sheet (S15): "1,5 Amps DC maximum" current, contact resistance "20 milliohms maximum", insulation resistance 500 MOhm min, voltage rating 125 V AC. The RJmag series with integrated magnetics: 500 MOhm min at 500 V DC insulation, 1000 V AC for 1 minute, operating temperature 0 to +70 C, storage -40 to +105 C (S15).

**RJ45 / 8P8C pin table and wiring (standard knowledge, ANSI/TIA-568 not opened):**

| pin | T568A | T568B | 10/100BASE-T | 1000BASE-T | PoE Alt A | PoE Alt B |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | white/green | white/orange | TD+ (TX+) | BI_DA+ | + or - on pair 1,2 (data pair) | not used |
| 2 | green | orange | TD- (TX-) | BI_DA- | same | not used |
| 3 | white/orange | white/green | RD+ (RX+) | BI_DB+ | pair 3,6 (data pair) | not used |
| 4 | blue | blue | unused | BI_DC+ | not used | spare pair |
| 5 | white/blue | white/blue | unused | BI_DC- | not used | spare pair |
| 6 | orange | green | RD- (RX-) | BI_DB- | pair 3,6 | not used |
| 7 | white/brown | white/brown | unused | BI_DD+ | not used | spare pair |
| 8 | brown | brown | unused | BI_DD- | not used | spare pair |

Pair usage for 10/100: S17 (TE magjack spec 114-161364): 10/100BASE-T uses pair 1 = J1/J2 (TX+/TX-), pair 2 = J3/J6 (RX+/RX-), pairs 3 and 4 unused; for 1000BASE-T and above all four pairs are used (J4/J5, J7/J8). The linux kernel PSE documentation (S18) states: Alternative A uses conductors 1, 2, 3 and 6 (the data pairs; for 10/100 and gigabit); Alternative B uses conductors 4, 5, 7 and 8 (spare pairs without data in 10/100; in gigabit it uses the data pairs, with two polarity variants). PoE power (IEEE 802.3af/at: about 48 V nominal; 350 mA per pair for af, 600 mA for at, recalled) is therefore injected through the transformer centre taps of the magnetics, which is why a magjack's centre taps and a plain-jack-plus-magnetics design need current-capable centre taps.

**Magjack pin mapping, example (S16, Pulse PulseJack 1x1 tab-up with LEDs, summarizer):** pin 1 (TX+) to TD+, pin 2 (TX-) to TD-, pin 3 (RX+) to RD+, pin 6 (RX-) to RD-; pins 4 and 5 centre tap/common (as written in the summary: "Pins 4, 5 (Center Tap/CT) -> Common ground"), pin 8 chassis ground; transformer ratio 1CT:1 (transmit and receive), insertion loss about -1.0 dB, hipot 1500 Vrms at 60 Hz, 0 to +70 C, LED forward voltage 2.1 to 2.5 V typical. These numbers also match the standalone magnetics class in `parts/R3.md` (hipot 1500 Vrms min, 1CT:1CT). The magjack pad numbering differs between manufacturers; use the per-part drawing.

**RJ11/RJ12 telephone pinouts (consensus, no document opened; S19 only for the line voltages):** 6P2C (RJ11): centre positions 3 and 4 = line 1 (position 3 = ring, position 4 = tip); 6P4C (RJ14): positions 2 and 5 = line 2 in addition; 6P6C (RJ12): positions 1 to 6 populated. Line signalling (S19, a UBC lecture): the on-hook line voltage is -48 V DC (tip about 0 V, ring about -48 V); off-hook loop current is typically 20 to 120 mA; the ringing waveform in North America is 20 Hz at about 86 V (the 90 Vrms value in the research brief is the usual round figure) with a 2 s on, 4 s off cadence. The ring signal rides on the -48 V DC, so the peak voltage on the pair is -48 V minus 1.414 * Vrms at the negative peak (about -175 V for 90 Vrms; bench B2). That is the only L1 fact about a telephone jack that matters to the connector: its voltage rating must cover about 175 V peak, and an Ethernet-class jack (125 V AC rating, S15) would be only just adequate in rms (peak 177 V).

### 3. How it connects

- **Plain RJ45 + discrete magnetics:** pins 1/2 to the magnetics' TX line side, 3/6 to RX, 4/5 and 7/8 to the Bob Smith termination or PoE circuit (75 ohm to a 1 nF/2 kV capacitor to chassis, general practice); shield to chassis ground; the PHY side is a separate transformer part (OHM-055).
- **Magjack:** PHY pins on the board side per the vendor pin table (TD+, TD-, RD+, RD-, centre taps, LED anodes and cathodes); the magnetics are inside, so no OHM-055 is placed; centre taps are biased from the PHY's supply; chassis shield pins to chassis.
- **Mistakes:** placing OHM-055 and a magjack on the same port; using a plain jack without magnetics; swapping TD and RD (auto-MDI-X usually forgives this at the PHY); a missing chassis connection; plugging an RJ11 plug into an RJ45 jack bends the outer contacts (general knowledge, not source-confirmed); treating an RJ11 jack as safe on a PSTN line (ring voltage and DC are real hazards).
- **RJ11:** pin positions for 6P4C: use positions 2..5; for 6P6C use 1..6.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation

Layer L1. Same mated-pair resistor model as BEH-CON-USB: `R{ref}_c{n} {BOARD_n} {CABLE_n} {Rc}`, 8 contacts for RJ45 and 4 or 6 for RJ11, plus a shell resistor. The magnetics of a magjack are an integrated model reused from OHM-055 (`bench/mag_ethmag/ethmag.lib`, `ETH_CH`), applied inside the part: `[TD+ TD- TDCT]` PHY side to `[pin1 pin2 centre]` line side. The model fidelity and limitations then follow BEH-MAG-ETHMAG (behavioural_approximation, no vendor model). LEDs on a magjack are ordinary diodes (green/orange pairs); apply BEH-LED rules with Vf 2.1 to 2.5 V typical (S16).

Ideal vs realistic: ideal Rc = 0; realistic Rc = 20 mOhm per contact (S15). Optional pair C (about 1 pF between adjacent contacts, ASSUMPTION L) for high-frequency studies. Valid: op, dc, ac, tran, temp. Limitations: no near-end crosstalk between pairs, no frequency-dependent plug/jack compensation (the jack is part of the category-rated channel in a real system), RJ11 line signalling is L3.

| lightning/surge | coupled via cable | PHY, magnetics damage | flag no surge protection (TVS or gas tube) | permanent |
| ring_voltage_on_ethernet | RJ11 plug into RJ45 jack on a live telephone line | 175 V peak into PHY | flag if RJ45 pair 4/5 carries a voltage over the PHY rating | permanent |
| open_contact | worn contact, cold joint | open conductor | Rc = 1e9 ohm; link falls back (10/100 uses 1,2,3,6 only) | permanent until repair |
| shorted pair | cable short | PHY driver or PoE current limit | not connector | recoverable |

### 8. Thermal behavior

Contact heating P = I^2 Rc. For PoE at 600 mA on a 20 mOhm contact pair: P = 7 mW. Negligible. Magjack magnetics heating belongs to BEH-MAG-ETHMAG.

### 9. Appearance summary

OHM-169 is a rectangular opening about 11.7 x 7 mm with a latch notch, eight gold contacts, locating posts and (default) a shield; the magjack variant adds LED windows and a larger shell. OHM-170 is a narrower opening (about 10 mm) with fewer contacts and no LEDs. See the 3D spec entries OHM-169 and OHM-170.

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-CON-AUDIO

Applies to OHM-171 (3.5 mm audio jack, 5-pin TRS with switch contacts, default Ledino KB3SPRS; alternates SJ1-3535NG and PJ-307). Layer L1.

### 1. Purpose and real-world use

A 3.5 mm jack takes headphones, line-in/out cables and headsets. A stereo (TRS) jack has tip (left), ring (right) and sleeve (ground). Jacks with switches add normally closed contacts that tell the board a plug is present or reroute the signal (mute an internal speaker when headphones are inserted, change a line input from internal source to external).

### 2. What it is and how it works

The plug is a three-conductor (TRS) or four-conductor (TRRS) stack; the jack has a spring contact for each plug segment. A **switched contact** is a spring pair: when no plug is inserted the spring touches a second terminal (the switch terminal), forming a closed contact; inserting the plug lifts the spring and opens the contact. On the SJ1-353xNG family the models differ by switch: SJ1-3533NG no switch, SJ1-3534NG tip switch, SJ1-3535NG tip and ring switch (S21, pins: sleeve, tip, ring, tip switch, ring switch). Switchcraft mono jacks list a "shunt terminal" (S20), the same idea. That the switch contact is closed with the plug out and opens on insertion is the usual convention; the datasheets read here do not state it in words (S20 lists no switch description; S21 describes the models only), so it is labelled CONSENSUS and must be checked on the specific drawing (some jacks have the opposite, a make-on-insertion contact).

**TRRS (4-pole) standards:** CTIA (also called AHJ, used by Apple and most modern phones): tip = left, ring 1 = right, ring 2 = ground, sleeve = microphone; OMTP (older): tip = left, ring 1 = right, ring 2 = microphone, sleeve = ground (S22). A CTIA headset in an OMTP jack has the ground and microphone swapped (no sound or no microphone). The default OHM-171 is a 3-pole jack; a TRRS jack would need a fourth contact and is a variant (PJ320D 4-pole is named in the 3D spec).

Plug effects: a mono (TS) plug shorts ring to sleeve (the right channel is shorted to ground, which the jack cannot see); a TRS plug in a TRRS jack shorts the second ring to sleeve; the plug and cable are part of the harness, not the jack.

**Contact ratings (S20 Switchcraft 3.5 mm family; S21 Same Sky SJ1-353xNG):** contact resistance 20 mOhm max (mono), 20 mOhm max initial and 100 mOhm after life (stereo), 30 mOhm max initial and 100 mOhm after life (non-threaded stereo); insulation resistance 100 MOhm min at 500 V DC (some models 50 MOhm); dielectric withstanding 250 V AC (500 V AC non-threaded); life 5000 cycles minimum (S20). S21: 12 V DC rated, 1 A rated current, plug-contact resistance 50 and switch (closed circuit) 30 (the summary printed the unit as "MOhm"; a milliohm unit is physically the only plausible reading for a closed spring contact, so this is recorded as 30 mOhm with LOW confidence), insulation 100 MOhm at 500 V DC, 500 V AC dielectric, 5000 cycles, -25 to 85 C.

### 3. How it connects

- Tip -> left channel (output: through a DC-blocking capacitor of about 100 to 220 uF for a single-supply amplifier; input: AC-coupled); ring -> right channel; sleeve -> audio ground (and CTIA microphone in TRRS).
- Tip switch (TN) and ring switch (RN): normally closed to tip and ring respectively. Typical use: the amplifier output goes to the tip *switch* terminal pair so that the internal speaker is fed from the amplifier when no plug is present, and the headphone is fed from tip when a plug is present (an SJ1-3535NG type switch); or the switch terminal is a plug-detect input pulled up by a resistor (the logic level the MCU reads depends on how the switch terminal is wired; the simulator evaluates the netlist, not an assumed convention).
- Typical mistakes: confusing TN with T (TN is the switch, the other side of the contact); using CTIA wiring in an OMTP headset; leaving the sleeve unconnected; tying TN and RN to the amplifier outputs without current limiting; DC offset into the headphone (no coupling capacitor); not decoupling long cables from the jack (ESD).

### 4. Electrical model for simulation

Layer L1. The jack is a set of contacts and switches with an `inserted` state (mated pair convention): 
```
* plug in: signal contacts closed to the cable, switch contacts open
R{ref}_t  {T_board}  {T_cable}  {Rc}       ; tip to plug tip   (only if inserted)
R{ref}_r  {R_board}  {R_cable}  {Rc}       ; ring to plug ring (only if inserted)
R{ref}_s  {S_board}  {S_cable}  {Rc}       ; sleeve to plug sleeve
* tip switch TN: normally closed contact to T; opens when inserted
S{ref}_tn {T_board} {TN} {ctl_inserted} 0 SWNC
.model SWNC SW(vt=-0.5 vh=0.1 ron={Rsw} roff=1G)
* DC/op: set the state with a parameter instead of a source:  Rtn = {inserted ? 1G : Rsw}
```
Two ways to use it: for `.op`/`.dc`/`.ac`, the state is a fixed parameter (`inserted` 0 or 1) and the switch is a resistor with value `Rsw` or `1G`; for `.tran` the state is a control source (PWL or pulse) driving a voltage-controlled switch. Bench B1 demonstrates the transient form. The ngspice `SW` model with control polarity inverted (`S1 t tn 0 plug SWNC` with `vt=-0.5`) gives a normally closed contact; hysteresis `vh=0.1` avoids chatter. Plug type (TS, TRS, TRRS CTIA/OMTP) is a harness property: it decides which cable nets are shorted together; the jack exposes the contacts.

Fidelity: `ideal_components` (Rc = 0, ideal switch Ron small, Roff 1G) or `behavioural_approximation`. Valid: op, dc, ac, tran, temp. Limitations: no contact bounce on insertion (the real contact bounces for about milliseconds during insertion; a model can add a PWL control), no plug-insertion transient where the tip passes across the ring contact (the left channel briefly shorts to the right and to ground as the plug slides; audible pop), no capacitance or inductance, no shield effect; no thermal model needed.

Audio signal levels are far below any rating (a headphone output is volts at most; speaker-level signals through the switch contact of a small jack can reach amps at 8 ohm and 5 V; these are the real stress case, so the check on I matters for the switch contact).

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior

| id | trigger | effect | sim response | permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| switch_overcurrent | speaker-level current through the TN/RN contact, over 1 A | contact welding or burning | flag | permanent |
| plug_short | TS plug in a TRS jack | ring shorted to sleeve | harness model sets R-S short; amplifier overcurrent check on the board's output | recoverable |
| wrong_standard | CTIA headset in OMTP jack (or reverse) | ground and microphone swapped; bias on the ground rail | netlist driven by `plug_type`; flag MIC bias voltage on a ground pin | recoverable |
| esd | plug static discharge | audio IC input damage | flag audio nets without protection | permanent |
| worn_contact | beyond 5000 cycles | Rc up to 100 mOhm or intermittent | set Rc = 100 mOhm; optionally add noise | permanent |
| dc_into_headphone | no coupling capacitor | DC current in the transducer | not connector | permanent |

### 8. Thermal behavior

Negligible at line and headphone levels. At speaker-level through a switch contact use P = I^2 Rsw (1 A, 30 mOhm: 30 mW).

### 9. Appearance summary

OHM-171 is a black block about 11.6 x 14.3 mm with a 6 mm wide nose and a round aperture; five flat solder pins on the underside in an asymmetric pattern, no printed pin 1. See the 3D spec entry OHM-171.

# PER-ENTRY SECTIONS

Pin numbering is the 3D spec's; "map by name" means the library pin names below shall be used in netlists and the footprint terminal is looked up from the 3D spec.

## [OHM-162] USB-A receptacle -> BEH-CON-USB

- Package PKG-USB_A.RA_THT (Molex 67643 style). Terminals 1..4 along -X at the rear (pin 1 at +X end, 3D spec): **1 = VBUS, 2 = D-, 3 = D+, 4 = GND**. 3D spec pitch 2.5 / 2.0 / 2.5 mm: the inner close pair (2-3, 2.0 mm) is the data pair, outer pins are power, consistent with the standard USB-A contact order (physical order from standard knowledge; the 3D spec marks the function RECALLED_UNVERIFIED). 2 shield legs (nickel) = SHELL (no electrical pin in the current spec; add SHELL1, SHELL2).
- Ratings: 1.5 A, 30 V, -40..85 C (Molex 67643-3910 listing, S11). Rc: ASSUMPTION 30 mOhm (no figure found).
- USB interface: VBUS 4.75..5.25 V, 100/500 mA unit-load rule (S8); host side has 15 kohm pull-downs on D+/D- (recalled); blue tongue variant = USB 3.0 (9-pin, SuperSpeed, 900 mA recalled; not this default).
- Polarity: none, keyed by shape. Defaults: Rc 30 mOhm (realistic), 1 uOhm (ideal). Notes: add ESD and a power switch with current limit on the host side. Status: partial.

## [OHM-163] USB-B receptacle -> BEH-CON-USB

- Package PKG-USB_B.RA_THT (Lumberg 2411 02 style). 4 pins in a 2 x 2 rectangle, 3D spec FCO coordinates: pin 1 (-1.25, -2.43), 2 (1.25, -2.43), 3 (1.25, -0.43), 4 (-1.25, -0.43). Function: **1 = VBUS, 2 = D-, 3 = D+, 4 = GND** (standard contact order; the numbering runs round the rectangle, so the physical placement (VBUS and D- in the rear row) agrees with the usual Standard-B layout; the chirality has not been checked against a drawing). 2 shield posts = SHELL.
- Ratings: no Standard-B receptacle rating found: RESEARCH_REQUIRED; use 1.0 A, 30 V as a conservative placeholder (ASSUMPTION, aligned with the Mini-B and Micro-B figures S9, S10). Rc ASSUMPTION 30 mOhm.
- Device side connector: VBUS is `power_in`; the device must not back-feed VBUS. Status: partial.

## [OHM-164] Micro-USB receptacle (Micro-B) -> BEH-CON-USB

- Package PKG-USB_MICRO.AMPH_10118194. 5 SMD contacts at 0.65 mm pitch, pin 1 at +X (1.3, -1.35) running to pin 5 at -X (3D spec). Function: **1 = VBUS, 2 = D-, 3 = D+, 4 = ID, 5 = GND**; matches the Molex 105017 "5 circuits, 0.65 mm pitch" (S9). Shell: 4 SMD pads and 4 THT shell legs = SHELL (the 3D spec describes 2 rear TH ovals and 2 side TH ovals plus SMD pads).
- Ratings: Molex 105017-0002 (a different part from the Amphenol 10118194 default): 1.8 A and 1 A per contact, 30 V AC rms, 10,000 mating cycles, -30..+85 C (S9). Contact resistance not given in the sheet read; ASSUMPTION 30 mOhm.
- ID: for a device-only (B) receptacle leave ID unconnected (floating); a micro-AB or OTG host function reads ID: grounded = A-device (S7 notes the ID pin identifies the role; the grounded/floating convention is recalled). VBUS at 20 V (USB-PD) is outside the 30 V AC rating margin and outside the micro-B design intent: flag if `v(vbus) > 5.5`.
- Status: partial.

## [OHM-165] USB-C receptacle -> BEH-CON-USB

- Default Amphenol 12401610E4-2A style, SMD contacts + 4 THT legs. 3D spec: 24 SMD tails A1..A12, B1..B12 at 0.5 mm pitch; A row on the rear line (A1 at (2.75, -3.93)), B row 1.7 mm closer to the front and offset 0.25 mm; pin 1 = A1. Four shell legs (front pair at (+-4.49, +3.93), rear pair at (+-4.13, -2.02)) and two NPTH pegs = SHELL.
- Full pin table (map by name): A1 GND, A2 TX1+, A3 TX1-, A4 VBUS, A5 CC1, A6 D+, A7 D-, A8 SBU1, A9 VBUS, A10 RX2-, A11 RX2+, A12 GND; B1 GND, B2 TX2+, B3 TX2-, B4 VBUS, B5 CC2, B6 D+, B7 D-, B8 SBU2, B9 VBUS, B10 RX1-, B11 RX1+, B12 GND. Confirmed by S1: GND A1/B1/A12/B12, VBUS A4/B4/A9/B9, CC A5/B5, D+ A6/B6, D- A7/B7, SBU A8/B8; the SuperSpeed pins are recalled (consensus).
- **Compatibility with the existing catalog record** (`USB_C_RECEPTACLE_16P.json`, HRO TYPE-C-31-M-12, 16 pins): that record's pins (A1,A12,B1,B12 GND; A4,A9,B4,B9 VBUS; A5,B5 CC; A8,B8 SBU; A6,A7,B6,B7 D+/D-) are the 24-pin set minus the eight SuperSpeed pins (A2, A3, A10, A11, B2, B3, B10, B11), so the 16-pin part is a strict subset. If OHM-165 is placed as the 24-pin Amphenol, the eight SuperSpeed pins are `passive` no-connects for a USB 2.0 design. Neither record has a SHELL pin.
- Mating sequence (S1): GND and VBUS first, then CC, D+, D-, SBU (second); shell GND. Ratings (S1): 5.00 A collectively VBUS, 6.25 A collectively GND, 1.25 A on B5, 0.25 A per other pin; Rc 40 mOhm max initial, 50 mOhm after test; insulation 100 MOhm; 100 V AC withstand; 10,000 cycles. The A5/B5 rating asymmetry is real and is modeled per physical pin.
- Sink circuit (board, not connector): Rd 5.1 kohm from A5 to GND and from B5 to GND (two resistors, never one shared); D+ A6 and B6 tied, D- A7 and B7 tied; ESD array near the connector; SBU left open. Source: Rp per advertisement. Orientation detect and VCONN supply are IC functions.
- Polarity: none (reversible); A1 is the pin-1 reference for geometry only. Status: partial (24-pin vs 16-pin identity unresolved, SuperSpeed not modelled).

## [OHM-166] Mini-USB receptacle (Mini-B) -> BEH-CON-USB

- Package PKG-USB_MINI.WURTH_65100516121. 5 SMD tails 0.5 x 2.5 mm at 0.8 mm pitch, pin 1 at +X (1.6, -2.75) to pin 5 at -X (3D spec). Function: **1 = VBUS, 2 = D-, 3 = D+, 4 = ID, 5 = GND**. 4 shell SMD pads and 2 NPTH pegs = SHELL.
- Ratings (Wurth 65100516121 via Farnell listing, S10): 1 A, 30 VAC, contact resistance 20 mOhm max, 5 positions. Mating cycles and insulation not in the listing.
- ID as in OHM-164. Mini-B is obsolete for new designs (general knowledge). Status: partial.

## [OHM-167] HDMI receptacle -> BEH-CON-HDMI

- Package PKG-HDMI.CT_19APL2, SMT right angle. 19 contacts, pad centres x = 4.5 - 0.5(n-1), pin 1 at +X (4.5, -0.05); odd pins on the top layer, even pins on the bottom layer; 4 shield SMD pads at (+-6.775, +0.05) = SHELL.
- Pin map by number: 1 D2+, 2 D2 shield, 3 D2-, 4 D1+, 5 D1 shield, 6 D1-, 7 D0+, 8 D0 shield, 9 D0-, 10 CK+, 11 CK shield, 12 CK-, 13 CEC, 14 Utility, 15 SCL, 16 SDA, 17 DDC/CEC GND, 18 +5 V, 19 HPD (S12). The odd-on-one-row layout (1,3,..,19 top, 2,..,18 bottom) is consistent with the 3D spec's two-layer pads.
- Ratings (Same Sky HD12-19-SMT-TR, S12): 0.5 A, 40 Vac, 20 mOhm, 100 MOhm, 500 Vac, 5,000 cycles, -40..100 C. A through-hole sibling (HD01-19-RA-TH, S13) reads 30 mOhm and 50 mOhm shell; the part in the 3D spec (CT_19APL2) is a different manufacturer, no datasheet opened.
- Defaults: Rc 20 mOhm. Differential impedance 100 ohm. Status: partial.

## [OHM-168] Mini-HDMI receptacle (Type C) -> BEH-CON-HDMI

- Package PKG-HDMI_MINI, SMT right angle. 19 contacts at 0.4 mm pitch (TE 2013978-1 listing); the 3D spec position formula x = 3.6 - 0.4(n-1) is DERIVED and whether the contacts are one row or two staggered rows is RESEARCH_REQUIRED.
- Pin map: **RESEARCH_REQUIRED.** S14 says the 19-pin assignment of Type C differs from Type A and does not give the table. The 19 signals are the same as Type A (3 TMDS pairs, clock pair, shields/grounds, CEC, DDC clock/data, DDC/CEC ground, +5 V, HPD, utility). Do not reuse Type A numbering; map by signal name once a per-part pin table is opened.
- Ratings (TE Mini HDMI Type C, S14): 0.5 A, 40 VAC, 100 MOhm min, opening 10.42 x 2.42 mm; temperature printed garbled ("-250 C - +700 C"), probably -25 to +70 C; Rc not given: ASSUMPTION 30 mOhm.
- Status: partial (pin map missing).

## [OHM-169] RJ45 Ethernet jack -> BEH-CON-MODJACK

- Package PKG-RJ45.AMPH_54602, THT, tab-down. 8 pins in two staggered rows: OHMNI pin n at x = 4.445 - 1.27(n-1), odd pins y = -1.905, even pins y = -4.445; pin 1 at (4.445, -1.905); 2 NPTH locating holes.
- Pin map (jack position n = pin n): 1 TD+, 2 TD-, 3 RD+, 4, 5, 6 RD-, 7, 8. Pins 4,5 and 7,8 are unused for 10/100 and are the PoE Alternative B spare pairs; pins 1,2,3,6 carry data and PoE Alternative A (S17, S18). 10/100 pair use per TE magjack spec 114-161364 (S17). T568A and T568B differ only in the colours of pairs 2 and 3 (TD and RD), not in the pin numbers.
- Magjack variant (RJHSE538X-type, 3D spec): pins 1..8 at x = -3.56 + 1.016(n-1); LED pins 9, 10 (left) and 11, 12 (right); two shield legs; two NPTH pegs. Pin names beyond 1..8 (LED anode/cathode, centre taps, chassis) follow the vendor sheet: **RESEARCH_REQUIRED** (the Amphenol RJHSE538X sheet itself was not opened; S15 is a family sheet; S16 is a different maker's magjack).
- **Transformer/magnetics link:** in the plain-jack default there is no magnetics in this part; place OHM-055 (BEH-MAG-ETHMAG, `parts/R3.md`, 1CT:1CT with line-side CMC) between this jack's 1/2 and 3/6 and the PHY. For a magjack the magnetics are inside the part: use the `ETH_CH` model from `bench/mag_ethmag/ethmag.lib`, TX pair on pins 1/2, RX on 3/6; do not also place OHM-055.
- Ratings: S15 1.5 A DC, 20 mOhm, 125 V AC, 500 MOhm; RJmag: 1000 V AC / 1 min, 0 to +70 C; PulseJack hipot 1500 Vrms (S16).
- Defaults: Rc 20 mOhm. Status: partial.

## [OHM-170] RJ11 jack -> BEH-CON-MODJACK

- Package PKG-RJ11 (variant of PKG-RJ45), THT, tab-down. 3D spec placeholder: 4 pins at x = 1.53, 0.51, -0.51, -1.53 (pitch 1.02) in alternating rows, pin 1 at +X; 6P6C would be 6 pins. Pin positions flagged UNCERTAIN in the 3D spec.
- Pin map (jack positions of a 6P4C jack, consensus): OHM pins 1..4 = jack positions 2, 3, 4, 5; line 1 on positions 3 (ring) and 4 (tip); line 2 on positions 2 and 5. Whether the vendor numbers the four contacts 1..4 or 2..5 and which end is pin 1 is RESEARCH_REQUIRED. A 6P2C jack populates only positions 3 and 4. Document the tip/ring names, not the colors.
- Electrical (connector only): telephone line -48 V DC on hook, 20 to 120 mA off hook, ring 20 Hz at about 86 V (S19; 90 Vrms common figure) superimposed on -48 V: peak about -175 V (bench B2). Hazard: this is far above SELV levels; the model's job is to flag, not protect. No RJ11 rating was found: use the RJ45 125 V AC figure only as a comparison, not as a rating.
- Defaults: Rc 30 mOhm (ASSUMPTION). Status: partial (pin numbering and rating research required).

## [OHM-171] 3.5 mm audio jack -> BEH-CON-AUDIO

- Package PKG-AUDIO_JACK.LEDINO_KB3SPRS (default), THT right-angle. 5 pins, map by NAME: T (-4.9, +1.7) = pin 1, TN (-4.4, -5.6), RN (+2.2, -1.2), R (+4.9, -2.4), S (-0.3, +5.6) (3D spec, KiCad names). Alternates: SJ1-3535NG (S (-1.0, 5.8), T (1.0, 3.4), R (1.0, -2.1), TN (-1.0, -5.8), RN (-1.0, -0.3)), and PJ-307 whose pin positions are unresolved (do not reuse the KB3SPRS pads).
- Behavior: TN = tip switch terminal: closed to T when no plug, opens on insertion; RN likewise for R (SJ1-3535NG is "tip and ring switch" per S21). Ratings from the SJ1 family (S21): 12 V DC, 1 A, -25 to 85 C, 5000 cycles; Switchcraft 3.5 mm family (S20): 20 to 30 mOhm initial, 100 mOhm after life. The default KB3SPRS ratings are not known: RESEARCH_REQUIRED.
- Polarity: none; pin identity by name. Plug type (TS/TRS/TRRS) is a harness parameter. Status: partial.
