# GROUP R10B: Power, RF, FFC and card connectors (OHM-172 to OHM-180)

Author: research agent R10B. ngspice 42 (stock build with KLU) run locally. All benches are in `/home/claude/behavior/bench/beh-con-dcjack/`, `beh-con-xt/`, `beh-con-rf/`, `beh-con-ffc/`, `beh-con-sd/`; each folder holds a `results_ngspice42.txt` with the raw output of the last full run.

## 0. Reading guide

| Class | What it models | Entries |
|---|---|---|
| BEH-CON-DCJACK | 2.1 / 2.5 mm barrel jack, 3 contacts incl. plug-sense switch | OHM-172 |
| BEH-CON-XT | Amass XT30 / XT60 high-current power connectors (self-heating, safety) | OHM-173, OHM-174 |
| BEH-CON-RF | 50 ohm coax connectors: U.FL, vertical SMA, edge-launch SMA (transmission line plus parasitics) | OHM-175, OHM-176, OHM-177 |
| BEH-CON-FFC | 0.5 mm pitch FFC/FPC ZIF, N contacts | OHM-178 |
| BEH-CON-SDSOCKET | SD (9 contact) and microSD (8 contact) sockets with card-detect and write-protect switches; SD protocol L3 | OHM-179, OHM-180 |

Layer decision: every connector body is L1 (R, L, C, T line, S switch, B source). The SD card interface protocol (command/response, CRC, initialisation, SPI-mode framing) is L3 and is NOT simulable here. What is documented for L3 is the electrical interface (pins, levels, pull-ups, supply, current) plus the requirement a higher layer must provide. Nothing here needs XSPICE.

### Honesty notes for the whole file

1. The page-fetch tool returns a model-written extract of each PDF, not raw bytes. Numbers in tables were taken from those extracts and are tagged with the document they came from. Where two documents disagree both values are shown.
2. No vendor SPICE model, S-parameter file or EM model was opened or attached. Everything is `ideal_components` (DC and contact-resistance behavior) or `behavioural_approximation` (thermal feedback, lumped RF parasitics, supply sag). Nothing may be labelled `vendor_model`.
3. The SD Association Physical Layer Simplified Specification was NOT opened: the download link returned only the license terms page. All SD electrical numbers below come from a Transcend SDXC card datasheet and a Cactus Technologies white paper, which are secondary to the SD spec. Marked accordingly.
4. Datasheets for these connectors do not publish thermal resistance, so connector temperature rise is a model (ASSUMPTION, confidence L) calibrated to a 30 K rise at rated current. That calibration is general engineering practice for connector current rating; the IEC/EIA test standard behind it was not opened.
5. Polarity, which jack terminal the plug-sense switch connects, the tail assignment of XT60, the SD detect/WP switch pad locations and the XT30/XT60 + / - convention were NOT established from an opened document. They are RESEARCH_REQUIRED and are exposed as parameters or rules so the implementer does not hard-code a guess.
6. ngspice 42 findings relevant to the implementer: `T` lines work in `.ac` (lossless, Z0/TD); `ac lin 1 f f` works for a single frequency; a `B` current source `B n1 n2 I=expr` injects current from n1 through the source to n2, so `B 0 t I=...` pushes current INTO node t (used for the thermal node); `meas ... when` fails with "out of interval" if the run ends before the crossing (the XT thermal tran must run past about 5 time constants).

---

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-CON-DCJACK

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
The DC barrel jack is the common low-voltage external power inlet for wall adapters, bench supplies and battery packs on hobby, test-equipment and appliance boards. The mating plug has a 5.5 mm outer diameter barrel with a 2.1 mm or 2.5 mm center bore (S2 gives the jack center pin as 2.0 mm copper, with a 9.0 mm plug insertion depth). The 2.1 mm plug on a 5.5 mm barrel is the most common size. The third terminal is a sense switch that opens (or closes) when a plug is inserted. It is used to disconnect an internal battery when an adapter is present, or to let a microcontroller detect the adapter.

### 2. What it is and how it works
Construction: an insulating housing holds three contacts. (1) A center pin contacts the inside of the plug's center bore. (2) A leaf-spring sleeve contact touches the plug barrel outside. (3) A switch spring touches one of those contacts while no plug is inserted and is pushed away by the plug. The 3D spec calls the terminals P1 center pin, P2 sleeve, P3 switch (OHM-172).

Physics: the DC path is only series contact resistance (S1: 30 mohm; S2 lists 50 mohm min between terminal and mating plug, 30 mohm closed circuit, an ambiguous mix of limits that the extract cannot disambiguate). Current rating is thermal: I^2 R heating in the contact and leads. Equations:
- Drop: V = I (Rtip + Rsleeve), each contact about half of the spec value if only the total is given.
- Heating: P = I^2 R_contact; steady rise dT = P Rth / (1 - P alpha Rth) with R(T) = R0 (1 + alpha dT), alpha about 0.0039 /K for copper alloys (physics, ASSUMPTION for the plated alloy).
Spec values: 24 Vdc, 2.5 A (S1 rev 1.07, 03/11/2025). SOURCE CONFLICT: S2 (older copy of the same part number) says 16 Vdc, 2.5 A. The simulator uses the newer 24 V as the limit and records the conflict. Jacks rated at higher current exist (the task brief mentions 2 to 5 A) but no 5 A document was opened, so 5 A is RESEARCH_REQUIRED.

### 3. How it connects
Three terminals. Convention: center pin positive, sleeve ground ("center positive") is the most common choice but is NOT universal; center-negative and AC-output adapters exist. The jack has no markings (OHM-172 Orientation Markings), so polarity is a schematic net decision, and the library must not attach a polarity to the part. Typical circuit: center pin to a series protection element (Schottky or P-FET reverse-polarity protection, TVS, fuse) and then the board rail; sleeve to GND. The switch terminal P3 connects with either the sleeve or the center pin when unplugged; which one varies by part and was not established from an opened document (the S1/S2 extracts list the third terminal but not its switch partner). Common mistakes: wrong plug size (a 2.5 mm plug does not fit a 2.0 mm pin jack; a 2.1 mm plug on a 2.5 mm pin is loose and intermittent; general knowledge, not sourced), assuming polarity from the adapter label, no reverse-polarity protection, hot-plug inrush spike (long adapter cable inductance plus a low-ESR cap can ring above the adapter voltage), and using the jack as a high-current path above the 2.5 A rating.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
Layer L1. Fidelity: `ideal_components` in ideal mode, `behavioural_approximation` in realistic mode (thermal feedback).

Primitives: R (contact), S (plug-sense switch, `.model SW`), B (thermal feedback, R(T)), L and C for optional realistic parasitics.

Template (realistic mode):
```
* DC jack, pins: TIP(P1) SLV(P2) SW(P3), SWPARTNER = TIP or SLV (parameter, default RESEARCH_REQUIRED -> TIP)
.param Rtip={Rc_total/2} Rslv={Rc_total/2} Rsw=50m
R{ref}_tip  PLUG_TIP  P1  {Rtip}
R{ref}_slv  PLUG_SLV  P2  {Rslv}
.model SWNC_{ref} SW(Vt=0.5 Vh=0.1 Ron={Rsw} Roff=1G)
* plug present flag: control voltage 1 when a plug source drives the jack, else 0
S{ref}_sw P3 {SWPARTNER_NODE} PLUGINV 0 SWNC_{ref}
Bplug_inv PLUGINV 0 V = 1 - v(PLUG)
* thermal node T{ref}: volts = temperature rise in K
B{ref}_th 0 T{ref} I = i_tip^2*Rc_total*(1+alpha*v(T{ref}))
R{ref}_th T{ref} 0 {Rth}
```
Netlist file with working values: `bench/beh-con-dcjack/B1.cir` (heating) and `B2.cir` (switch).

Parameter mapping: Rc_total = datasheet contact resistance (S1 30 mohm); Rth derived (see 8); Rsw = ASSUMPTION 50 mohm (no switch spec in S1 or S2). Ideal mode: Rc = 1 mohm (kept nonzero for solver conditioning), switch ideal, no thermal node.

Valid analyses: op, dc, tran (thermal node), ac (resistive only). Valid range: DC to a few kHz for ac; the jack is not modeled as inductive (pin inductance on the order of nH is ASSUMPTION L and irrelevant below MHz).

Known limitations: no contact resistance growth with wear (the S1/S2 5,000 cycle life is stated without a resistance limit), no intermittent contact on plug wiggle, no inductive kick or arc on live unplug, switch bounce not modeled.

### 5. Parameters

| V_rated | V | 24 | 0 | 24 | n/a | MFR_DATASHEET (S1; S2 says 16) | M | S1,S2 |
| I_rated | A | 2.5 | 0 | 2.5 | n/a | MFR_DATASHEET | M | S1,S2 |
| insulation_R | ohm | 100e6 | 100e6 | inf | min | MFR_DATASHEET at 500 Vdc | M | S1,S2 |

| center_pin_dia | mm | 2.0 | 2.0 | 2.5 | | 3D spec parametric variant; S2 gives 2.0 | M | S2 |

### 6. Ratings and limits
- Current: `I <= 2.5 A` continuous (S1,S2). Check: `abs(i(contact)) <= I_rated`. Warn at 100%, fail at 120% (the 120% is a policy choice, not a datasheet value).
- Voltage: `V(P1,P2) <= 24 V` (S1). Use 16 V as the warning level on the older-revision conflict (S2).
- Contact heating check: `Tamb + dT <= 85 degC` where dT from the thermal node (S1 85 degC limit; S2 lists -25 to 85 degC).
- Derating: the datasheet gives no current derating curve; RESEARCH_REQUIRED. Rule used: linear derating from 100% at 25 degC to 0% at 85 degC is a conservative placeholder only (ASSUMPTION).
- Source conflict to expose in the UI: voltage 24 V (S1) vs 16 V (S2); contact resistance 30 mohm (S1) vs 50 mohm / 30 mohm (S2).

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior
| id | trigger | effect | sim response | permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| overcurrent | I > 2.5 A sustained | contact heating, plating degradation, eventual plastic softening | flag at 100%, model R rising 20% per 10 K above the 30 K design rise; open at dT where Tamb+dT > 85 C is only flagged, not opened | permanent if long |
| overvoltage | V > 24 V | dielectric margin shrinks; the part is not a protection device | flag only | recoverable |
| reverse polarity | plug polarity opposite to board assumption | the jack itself is undamaged; downstream ICs may be | no part-level failure; ERC rule: jack has no polarity, the board needs reverse protection | n/a |
| plug short | plug center touches sleeve (damaged plug) | adapter short | flag short via ideal supply current | recoverable |
| intermittent / worn | beyond 5000 cycles | resistance rises, noise | optional parameter Rc multiplier up to 10x (ASSUMPTION) | permanent |
| open (no plug) | no plug | center and sleeve open; switch contact in its resting state | S switch closed per parameter | n/a |
| hot-plug inrush | live plug into a capacitive load | voltage overshoot above adapter voltage | requires realistic cable L model: add 1 to 2 m cable L ~ 1 uH/m (ASSUMPTION L) | recoverable |

### 8. Thermal behavior
P = I^2 R_contact: 2.5 A through 30 mohm is 0.1875 W, drop 75 mV (bench B1). Rth is not published; calibration: Rth = 30 K / (I_rated^2 R0) = 160 K/W, so dT = 30 K without feedback and 33.98 K with R(T) feedback (measured bench B1). ASSUMPTION L: the real number depends on lead heatsinking into PCB copper. First-order thermal capacity Cth about 1 to 2 J/K (ASSUMPTION L). Thermal runaway threshold current of the R(T) loop: I_run = 1/sqrt(R0 alpha Rth), far above the rated current for this calibration.

### 9. Appearance summary
Black rectangular plastic block with a round 5.5 mm bore on the front face, a 2.0 mm metal pin in the bore and three flat tails (3D spec OHM-172). No markings and no polarity symbol on the part.

### 10. Validation benches
| id | file | expected | tolerance | measured |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | bench/beh-con-dcjack/B1.cir | drop 75 mV (= 2.5 A x 30 mohm), dT = 30/(1-0.0039*30) = 33.975 K | 0.1% | 75.000 mV, 33.975 K: match |
| B2 | bench/beh-con-dcjack/B2.cir | unplugged Vload = 9*100/(100+0.1+0.05) = 8.9865 V; plugged Vload = 12*100/(100+0.03) = 11.9964 V; battery current to leakage level when plugged | 0.01% | 8.98652 V, 11.9964 V, battery current 3 nA: match |

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-CON-XT

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
XT30 and XT60 (Amass) are two-pole polarized nylon connectors with gold-plated brass bullet contacts. They are the standard battery and power connectors on RC models, drones, e-bikes, robots and bench-power projects, where a LiPo or Li-ion pack connects to an ESC or a power board. XT30 is the small one (15 A continuous), XT60 the mid one (30 A continuous). The PCB versions XT30PW-M and XT60PW-M are right-angle male parts for the controller side (the Amass XT60 sheet labels XT60-F as the "battery" side and XT60-M as the "controller" side).

### 2. What it is and how it works
Construction: two gold-plated brass contacts in a PA (nylon) housing; the mating shroud has two chamfered corners that make the connector fit only one way (mechanical keying; the + / - assignment relative to the chamfer is a wiring convention, not documented in the opened sheets). Spring-less bullet-and-socket contacts rely on the female socket's slotted cylinder for contact force.

Published values:
| quantity | XT30PW-M | XT60 (-F/-M) | source |
|---|---|---|---|
| continuous current | 15 A | 30 A | S4, S3 |
| peak (instantaneous) current | 30 A | 60 A | S4, S3 |
| contact resistance | 0.80 mohm | 0.55 mohm | S4, S3 |
| rated voltage | DC 500 V | DC 500 V | S4, S3 |
| temperature | -20 to 120 degC | -20 to 120 degC | S4, S3 |
| mating cycles ("recommended use times") | 1000 | 1000 | S4, S3 |
| housing / contact | PA / brass gold plated | PA / brass gold plated (UL94 V0) | S4, S3 |
| recommended cable | n/a | 12 AWG | S3 |

Self-heating at rated current (computed, bench B1): P = I^2 R. XT60 at 30 A: 900 x 0.55 mohm = 0.495 W for the mated pair and 16.5 mV drop. XT30 at 15 A: 225 x 0.8 mohm = 0.18 W, 12 mV. At peak: XT60 60 A gives 1.98 W and 33 mV; XT30 30 A gives 0.72 W. With the 30 K-at-rated-current calibration these produce 33.98 K with positive-temperature-coefficient feedback. Real values: published contact resistance is a new-part value (the extract does not say max or typical); wear, oxidation, the solder joint and the cable crimp each add and the PCB tail soldered into copper is usually the hotter point. At 30 A through a 2 oz outer layer a narrow trace is the real limit: trace sizing (IPC-2221 style) was not opened here and is not computed; design rule only: use a copper pour, not a 1 mm trace.

Polarity: keyed mechanically only. Which pin is + is not in the opened sheets (3D spec says RESEARCH_REQUIRED). The model therefore exposes pin A/B as symmetric passive terminals and a `polarity_rule` that the board annotation (net names) fills in.

### 3. How it connects
Two power pins, no signal pins. Typical circuit: battery + through a fuse or reverse-protection element into the load; large bulk capacitance close to the connector. Mistakes: 
- Mating a pack with the wrong + / - wiring convention (the connector cannot stop it if cables are crimped backwards).
- Hot-plug into a capacitive load (ESC, DC-DC input caps): connecting a charged pack to uncharged low-ESR capacitance draws a current spike limited only by the pack impedance and contact resistance (I_peak about V/(R_pack + R_contact + R_wiring)). The spark at the first touch damages the gold plating. Anti-spark (precharge resistor) designs exist; none was opened.
- Battery short: a LiPo or Li-ion pack can source hundreds of amps into a short (physics). The connector's 30 A / 60 A limit is thousands of times below the available fault energy, so the connector is NOT a protective device; it will weld, melt the nylon and ignite the pack. Fuse or active current limit is mandatory.
- Under-sized PCB copper or no strain relief of the right-angle tail (mechanical stress cracks solder joints).

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
Layer L1. Fidelity: `ideal_components` (series R) plus `behavioural_approximation` (thermal feedback).

Template (see bench `B1.cir`, `B2.cir`):
```
R{ref}_c   A   Aint  {Rc/2}       * contact resistance split per pole
R{ref}_c2  B   Bint  {Rc/2}
* thermal node T{ref}, volts = dT in K
B{ref}_th 0 T{ref} I = i(V{ref}_s)^2 * {Rc} * (1+{alpha}*v(T{ref}))
R{ref}_th T{ref} 0 {Rth}
C{ref}_th T{ref} 0 {Cth}
```
In a full netlist the current is measured with a zero-volt source in series, V{ref}_s.

Parameters: Rc from datasheet (0.80 / 0.55 mohm); Rth = 30 K/(Irated^2 R0): XT60 60.6 K/W, XT30 167 K/W (ASSUMPTION, calibrates to a typical 30 K rise at rated current); Cth = 2 J/K for XT60 (ASSUMPTION; XT30 smaller, 1 J/K, ASSUMPTION); alpha 0.0039 /K (ASSUMPTION).

Valid analyses: op (heating), dc, tran (thermal and current pulse). ac: resistive plus an ASSUMPTION L series inductance of about 10 to 20 nH per pole, only relevant above MHz.

Known limitations: ignores arcing on live hot-plug, contact wear, and the PCB trace temperature; the thermal model is a single lump.

### 5. Parameters
| name | unit | default XT60 / XT30 | min | max | basis | conf | src |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rc (mated pair) | ohm | 0.55e-3 / 0.80e-3 | 0.1e-3 | 5e-3 (aged) | MFR_DATASHEET (new value; whether max or typical not stated) | M | S3,S4 |
| I_cont | A | 30 / 15 | | | MFR_DATASHEET | M | S3,S4 |
| I_peak | A | 60 / 30 | | | MFR_DATASHEET ("instantaneous"; duration not stated) | L | S3,S4 |
| V_rated | V | 500 / 500 | | | MFR_DATASHEET (DC) | M | S3,S4 |
| T_range | degC | -20..120 | -20 | 120 | MFR_DATASHEET | M | S3,S4 |
| cycles | count | 1000 / 1000 | | | MFR_DATASHEET | M | S3,S4 |
| Rth | K/W | 60.6 / 167 | | | ASSUMPTION | L | none |
| Cth | J/K | 2 / 1 | | | ASSUMPTION | L | none |
| alpha | 1/K | 0.0039 | | | ASSUMPTION | L | none |
| L_series | H | 15e-9 | | | ASSUMPTION | L | none |

### 6. Ratings and limits
- Continuous: `abs(i) <= I_cont` with default 30 A (XT60), 15 A (XT30). Recommended design margin: a derating policy such as 80% is ASSUMPTION (not from the datasheet); apply as a warn level, fail at 100%.
- Peak: `abs(i) <= I_peak` only for a short pulse; duration is not given (RESEARCH_REQUIRED). Simulator rule: evaluate the thermal tran; fail if Tamb + dT_pulse > 120 degC.
- Temperature: `Tamb + dT <= 120 degC` (S3,S4; nylon).
- Voltage: 500 V DC rating is a dielectric rating, not a battery system rating; the application voltage is limited by arcing at unmating under load (not quantified here).

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior
| id | trigger | effect | sim response | permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| overcurrent | I > 30 A (XT60), 15 A (XT30) continuous | contact and housing heating, softening of the PA, higher Rc | flag at 100%; R(T) feedback; fail at Tamb+dT > 120 C | permanent |
| peak overcurrent | I > 60 / 30 A | melting, welding | fail immediately (open the part in sim and flag a fire hazard) | permanent |
| battery short | short across the pack with no fuse | hundreds of amps, arc, fire | flag CRITICAL: current limit element missing when a Li source is connected | permanent, hazard |
| hot-plug arc | connect into uncharged C | inrush, arc pits on plating | tran flag when peak current > I_peak | permanent (wear) |
| wrong polarity (cables crossed) | reversed wiring | reverse supply on the board | no part-level failure; ERC polarity rule on the nets | n/a |
| aging | > 1000 cycles, oxidation | Rc rises | Rc multiplier (ASSUMPTION) | permanent |
| open | unmated or broken tail | no current | A and B isolated | n/a |

### 8. Thermal behavior
Bench B1: 33.975 K with R(T) feedback versus 30 K at constant R (XT60 and XT30 both calibrated to 30 K at rated current). Bench B2 transient: tau = Rth Cth / (1 - P alpha Rth) = 137.3 s for XT60; measured t63 = 137.23 s. A 60 A peak pulse (1.98 W) heats about 1 K/s with Cth = 2 J/K, so a pulse of a few seconds adds only a few kelvin; this is a model consequence of an assumed Cth and not a datasheet allowance.

### 9. Appearance summary
Keyed nylon shroud with two chamfered corners and two gold pins in the mating face (OHM-173 pitch 5.0, 9.9 mm wide; OHM-174 pitch 7.2, 15.5 mm wide). The 3D spec has no polarity symbol; XT parts are usually yellow but the library's color is NATURAL.

| B2 | bench/beh-con-xt/B2.cir | tau = Rth Cth/(1-alpha P Rth) = 137.26 s (t63 of final 33.975 K) | 1% | t63 = 137.23 s: match (run length 800 s; final value 33.875 K reached after 5.8 tau, 0.3% below asymptote) |

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-CON-RF

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
Coaxial RF connectors bring a 50 ohm signal between a PCB trace and a cable or antenna. U.FL (Hirose; I-PEX MHF is mechanically compatible) is a tiny board-to-antenna connector inside phones, Wi-Fi/BLE modules and GPS boards. SMA is the threaded lab/antenna connector, vertical through-hole for panel or antenna mounting, and edge-launch (straddle) mounted on the board edge so the center pin lands directly on the surface trace.

### 2. What it is and how it works
A coaxial connector is a short length of 50 ohm transmission line: a center conductor, a dielectric (PTFE for SMA) and an outer shell connected to the board ground. Its electrical behavior is: characteristic impedance 50 ohm, delay set by the physical length and dielectric, attenuation from skin-effect (rises roughly with sqrt(f), general physics) and the reflection at the discontinuities where the line meets the PCB (pad capacitance and pin inductance). The usable bandwidth is set by those discontinuities, not by the 50 ohm section.

Equations (textbook transmission line theory, checked in benches):
- Reflection coefficient from load: Gamma = (ZL - Z0)/(ZL + Z0); VSWR = (1+|Gamma|)/(1-|Gamma|); return loss RL = -20 log10 |Gamma| dB; mismatch loss = -10 log10 (1 - |Gamma|^2).
- Input impedance of a line section: Zin = Zc (ZL + j Zc tan(theta)) / (Zc + j ZL tan(theta)). A quarter-wave section of Zc into 50 ohm presents Zc^2/50.
- Lumped parasitics in a matched 50 ohm system: shunt C gives |Gamma| = x/sqrt(4+x^2) with x = w C Z0; series L gives the same with x = w L/Z0; |S21| = 2/sqrt(4+x^2).

Published values:
| quantity | U.FL (S5) | SMA (S6 panel mount, S7, S8) |
|---|---|---|
| impedance | 50 ohm | 50 ohm |
| frequency | DC to 6 GHz | DC to 18 GHz (S6, S7, S8) |
| VSWR | 1.3 max to 3 GHz; 1.3 to 1.5 max from 3 to 6 GHz (cable dependent) | 1.15 max (S6, panel-mount SMA, "except solder cup"); Molex 73251-1150 VSWR not published in the opened page |
| mating durability | 30 cycles | 500 cycles min (S6, S7) |
| contact resistance | center 20 mohm max (25 after durability); outer 10 mohm max (15 after) | 2.0 mohm (S6, panel mount) |
| insulation resistance | 500 Mohm min dry | 5000 Mohm (S6) |
| voltage | 100 V DC; 200 V AC 1 min; 10 mA max | 500 to 1000 Vrms (S6); 500 Vrms at sea level for Molex 73251-1150 (S8) |
| current | 10 mA max | not a power connector |
| temperature | -40 to +90 degC operating | -65 to 165 degC (S7 distributor listing) |
| mating torque | n/a (snap-on) | 7 to 10 in-lb stainless; 3 to 5 in-lb brass (S6); SV Microwave edge launch 7 to 10 in-lb SMA, board mount 12 in-oz (S9) |

Derived: VSWR 1.3 means |Gamma| 0.130, return loss 17.7 dB; VSWR 1.5 means 0.200, 14.0 dB (mismatch loss 0.177 dB); VSWR 1.15 means 0.0698, 23.1 dB. These are computed from the published VSWR with the formulas above, not additional datasheet values.

Insertion loss: NOT published in any opened U.FL or SMA document. The model uses mismatch loss from VSWR (derived) plus a skin-effect term of ASSUMPTION L (about 0.05 dB for an SMA at a few GHz, 0.1 to 0.2 dB for U.FL with its thin cable; general practice only). Do not present insertion loss as a datasheet value.

Edge-launch geometry: the center pin lies on the trace and the shell straddles the board, so the pad-to-pin geometry sets the launch impedance. The pin must be small and flat; a large pad adds fringing capacitance and spoils return loss (S10). In coplanar-with-ground form, the gap between trace and ground becomes critical below about 10 mil and the ground-via pitch should be below a quarter wavelength at the highest frequency (S10). S9 shows full-path VSWR of 1.0 to 2.0 across 50 GHz bands depending on connector family, for an optimized launch on 10 mil Rogers 3003. Bench B3 shows how a 40 ohm section (oversized pad) 50 ps long gives VSWR 1.56 at 5 GHz, which is the mechanism: pad width mismatched from 50 ohm acts as a short low-Z line.

### 3. How it connects
- U.FL: 3 terminals on the 3D model: SIG pad and two ground pads (OHM-175). The mated connector takes SIG as the center contact. U.FL is rated for about 30 mating cycles only, so it is a "fit once" connector, not a test port. Mistakes: pulling the cable instead of using a tool (it detaches at the pad), routing a 50 ohm trace that is not width-matched to the SIG pad, and placing SIG and ground pads with reference plane cutouts missing.
- Vertical SMA: 5 pins, center and four grounds (OHM-176). Antenna or panel lead. Mistake: leaving the ground legs unstitched.
- Edge-launch SMA: 5 terminals: SIG and four ground legs (two top, two bottom, OHM-177). Mistake: the pad pattern assumes a board thickness (3D spec 1.57 mm slot); a different thickness changes pin height versus the trace and the footprint must be re-tuned.
- All: 50 ohm trace or CPWG on the PCB, short and with solid return path; matching network (pi pad) footprint recommended between connector and radio.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
Layer L1. Fidelity `behavioural_approximation` (lumped parasitics plus lossless line) for AC; DC uses `ideal_components` (connector is a short with contact resistance).

Template:
```
* pins: SIG GND (ground pins tied)
* contact R at DC, line + parasitics for AC/tran
R{ref}_c  SIG  n1  {Rc_center}
C{ref}_p  n1   GND {Cpad}
L{ref}_s  n1   n2  {Lpin}
T{ref}    n2 GND  OUT GND  Z0=50 TD={td}
```
Use the lossless `T` element for the connector body and add `R` series loss only if needed (a lossy `LTRA` line is possible in ngspice but not benched here). For sourced behavior, the model can be driven from the published VSWR bound: select Cpad or Lpin so that |Gamma| equals the worst-case bound at the band edge using |Gamma| = x/sqrt(4+x^2) (bench B2).

Parameter mapping: Rc_center from the published center resistance (U.FL 20 mohm max; SMA panel 2.0 mohm); Cpad, Lpin and td have NO sourced typical values (ASSUMPTION L); default 0 in ideal mode, tuned to the VSWR bound in realistic mode.

Valid analyses: op/dc (as resistance), ac, tran (reflections), no noise. Valid range: U.FL DC to 6 GHz, SMA DC to 18 GHz. Beyond the band edge the lumped model is not valid.

Known limitations: frequency-dependent loss not modeled; no radiation; no PCB footprint EM (the launch geometry needs a 3D EM solver; the lumped step is a stand-in); no mode conversion.

### 6. Ratings and limits
- Frequency: `f <= f_max` (6 GHz U.FL; 18 GHz SMA). Warn above.
- Power: not published for U.FL (current 10 mA max, voltage 100 V DC, 200 V AC (S5)); implement as a DC bias limit: `abs(v_dc) <= 100` and `abs(i_dc) <= 10 mA`. RF power handling is RESEARCH_REQUIRED.
- Mate cycles: U.FL 30, SMA 500 (counted as a lifetime metadata, not simulated).
- Return loss check: `VSWR(f) <= VSWR_max(f)` evaluated from the AC solution (bench B1 shows the extraction).
- SMA torque: 7 to 10 in-lb (stainless, S6) or 3 to 5 in-lb (brass); informational, over-torque damages the PTFE.

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior
| id | trigger | effect | sim response | permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| overcycled | U.FL mated more than 30 times | pad lift, contact wear, higher VSWR | derate: increase Cpad by 0.05 pF per 10 cycles beyond 30 (ASSUMPTION) | permanent |
| overfrequency | f beyond band | VSWR rises | flag | recoverable |
| DC overvoltage (U.FL) | > 100 V DC | breakdown | flag | permanent |
| ESD | static on antenna input | damages the radio, not the connector | flag: no ESD element in the part | n/a |
| unterminated | open SMA | VSWR infinity at the radio PA | model open end, flag PA protection | recoverable |
| over-torque | beyond 10 in-lb | dielectric deformation | informational | permanent |
| bad launch | wrong pad geometry or board thickness | VSWR step like bench B3 | add the step to the netlist; flag footprint check | n/a |

### 8. Thermal behavior
RF dissipation is a small fraction of transmitted power (skin loss, tens of mdB). Not modeled; negligible below the power published for the part, which is not available in the opened sources.

### 9. Appearance summary
U.FL: tiny ring-shaped top on a 3.0 x 2.6 body with a signal tab and two ground legs (OHM-175). Vertical SMA: hex barrel with thread, white dielectric ring, four-peg square flange (OHM-176). Edge-launch SMA: hex barrel pointing off the board edge with a straddle slot and center tab (OHM-177).

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-CON-FFC

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
A ZIF (zero insertion force) FFC/FPC connector terminates a flat flexible cable or flex circuit in a PCB, typically for display panels, camera modules, touch panels and inter-board links. Pitch is 0.5 mm in this entry. Typical lane counts N = 6 to 60.

### 2. What it is and how it works
The housing holds N flat spring contacts along one row. A flip-lock actuator (bar) opens to allow the cable in with no force and closes to press the cable conductors against the contacts. Contact is on the bottom or top of the cable: the 3D spec default is bottom contact (OHM-178, Hirose FH12-10S-0.5SH-like).

Published values (Hirose FH12 series sheet 2010.9, S11): current 0.5 A DC per contact, with a note to use 70% when passing current through all contacts; voltage 50 V AC; contact resistance 50 mohm max at 1 mA; insulation 500 Mohm min; withstand 150 V AC for 1 min; 20 insertion/withdrawal cycles; temperature -40 to +85 degC (includes rise from current flow); FPC thickness 0.3 +/- 0.05 mm (0.18 mm for the F variant). So the part is a signal and low-power connector; it is not a power connector.

Physics: each contact is a small series resistance; with all contacts loaded, heating from neighboring contacts adds, which is why the 70% rule exists. The signal behavior at speed (tens to hundreds of MHz for MIPI or LVDS) needs per-lane impedance that the datasheet extract does not give (RESEARCH_REQUIRED).

### 3. How it connects
N signal pins, pin 1 at -X by library convention (OHM-178, KiCad FH12 same). The cable's contact side must match the connector: bottom-contact connectors need the cable's exposed conductors facing down; a cable made for a top-contact connector is a mirror image. Same-contact-type connectors at both ends need a cable whose conductors are on opposite sides at each end (general practice, not verified here; confidence L). Two retaining tab pads (mechanical). Mistakes: pin 1 mirrored (wrong cable type), inserting too short, not closing the lock fully, using a cable of the wrong thickness, hot plugging a powered display, and using power lanes beyond 0.5 A per contact.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
Layer L1. Fidelity `ideal_components`: each contact a series resistance; optional L parasitic.
```
* N contacts, pin k -> cable k
R{ref}_k  P{k}_board  P{k}_cable  {Rc}
```
Parameter mapping: Rc = 50 mohm max (S11) used as the worst-case default; typical is lower but not published (use 20 mohm as an ASSUMPTION L for typical mode). Multiple contacts can be paralleled for power: current sharing follows the resistance spread (bench B2). Thermal: single-contact P = I^2 R = 12.5 mW at 0.5 A / 50 mohm; thermal coupling between contacts is not modeled, so the 70% N-contact derate is applied as a rule in the checker.

Valid analyses: op, dc, tran, ac (resistive). Valid range: DC to a few MHz in this model; above that insertion loss, crosstalk and impedance discontinuity are not modeled (honest limit).

### 5. Parameters
| name | unit | default | min | max | basis | conf | src |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| N | count | 10 | 4 | 60 | CONSENSUS (3D spec parametric by N) | M | 3D spec |
| pitch | mm | 0.5 | | | MFR_DATASHEET | H | S11, 3D spec |
| Rc | ohm | 0.050 worst / 0.020 typical | 0.01 | 0.05 | MFR_DATASHEET worst; typical ASSUMPTION | M/L | S11 |
| I_contact | A | 0.5 | | | MFR_DATASHEET | M | S11 |

| contact_side | enum | bottom | | | 3D spec | M | 3D spec |

### 6. Ratings and limits
- Per contact: `abs(i_k) <= 0.5 A`. When more than one contact carries current: `abs(i_k) <= 0.35 A` if all contacts are loaded (70%, S11).
- Voltage: `abs(v) <= 50 V` AC (S11); DC rating not stated in the opened sheet.
- Cycles: 20 (S11). Informational lifetime counter; the library should warn that FFC connectors are not for repeated plug cycles.
- Temperature: `Tamb + rise <= 85 degC` (S11 includes the self-heating).

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior
| id | trigger | effect | sim response | permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| overcurrent per contact | > 0.5 A | contact heating, flip-lock plastic limit | flag at 100%; fail at 150% | permanent |
| uneven sharing | parallel contacts with unequal Rc | one contact carries more than average (bench B2: the 20 mohm contact carries 0.568 A of 1.75 A, above the 0.5 A rating) | flag per-contact overcurrent | permanent if sustained |
| half-latched | lock not closed | intermittent open | optional random open (needs L3 or a manual open parameter) | recoverable |
| mirrored cable | wrong contact side or flipped pin 1 | pins reversed | ERC: pin 1 side check; no part model failure | n/a |
| overvoltage | > 50 V AC | breakdown | flag | permanent |
| wear | > 20 cycles | contact resistance increases | multiplier (ASSUMPTION) | permanent |

### 8. Thermal behavior
At 0.5 A / 50 mohm one contact dissipates 12.5 mW (bench B1). The sheet states the 85 degC limit includes temperature rise; no thermal resistance is published. The 70% rule is the datasheet's way of handling mutual heating. No explicit thermal model is added; the check is `i_k <= rating * factor`.

### 9. Appearance summary
Low rectangular housing about 2 mm high with a flip-lock bar at the rear and a row of N tiny contacts at 0.5 mm pitch, with end tabs (OHM-178). No polarity marking in the 3D spec; pin 1 at -X by convention.

| B2 | bench/beh-con-ffc/B2.cir | share I_k = I (1/Rk)/sum(1/Rj): I1 = 0.5677 A, I5 = 0.2271 A, drop 11.354 mV | 0.01% | 0.567714, 0.227086, 11.3543 mV: match |

### 12. Sources
- S11: Hirose, "FH12 Series" FPC/FFC connector sheet dated 2010.9, hosted at the University of Toronto link above (file name FH12-16S-1SV(55), 1.0 mm pitch variant of the same series sheet). Took: 0.5 A DC (70% when all contacts loaded), 50 V AC, 50 mohm max at 1 mA, 500 Mohm, 150 V AC 1 min, 20 cycles, -40 to +85 degC, FPC t = 0.3 mm. NOTE: that copy is the 1.0 mm pitch file name; the specification table is the series table, so applying it to 0.5 mm pitch is MEDIUM confidence. The opened sheet did not state a per-pitch difference.
- Not opened: Hirose FH12-10S-0.5SH specific drawing, any FFC high-speed S-parameter data.

### 13. Research confidence
(a) parameters M, (b) ratings M, (c) model M for DC, none for HF, (d) failure L.
Unresolved: top versus bottom contact confirmation on the 3D part (Hirose naming not opened), per-pitch rating differences, current rating at 0.5 mm pitch specifically, high-speed behavior, flip-lock actuation force, the exact cable side convention.

## BEHAVIOR CLASS: BEH-CON-SDSOCKET

### 1. Purpose and real-world use
SD and microSD sockets hold removable flash cards on data loggers, cameras, single-board computers and embedded products. The socket is a passive interface; the card is the active device. A push-push socket latches on first insertion and releases on the second push; push-pull sockets use a slide.

### 2. What it is and how it works
Contacts: the full-size SD socket has 9 signal/power contacts (OHM-179); microSD has 8 (OHM-180). The socket also has mechanical switches. The full-size socket has a card-detect switch and a write-protect switch (S13: card removed OPEN, card inserted CLOSE; write protect CLOSE, write enable OPEN). The microSD socket has a card-detect switch (Hirose DM3 series: normally open, closes when a card is inserted, S12); microSD cards have no write-protect slider in the opened material and none was found in S12, so a WP switch is not part of the 8-pin microSD interface (general knowledge: adapters carry the slider).

Contact ratings of the sockets (S12 DM3, S13 WERI, S14 Molex): 0.5 A per contact; voltage 100 to 125 V AC (S13: 100 VAC; S12: 125 V AC; S14: 500 V AC dielectric); contact resistance limit 40 mohm (S12, change from initial), 100 mohm max (S13, S14); insulation resistance 100 Mohm min (S12) or more than 1000 Mohm (S13); durability 10,000 cycles (S12 DM3AT; S13 WERI), 500 to 10,000 depending on part (S14); temperature -25 to +85 degC (S12, S13) or -40 to +85 degC (S14).

Pin tables.

SD (full size), S15 and S16:
| pin | SD mode | SPI mode | type |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | CD/DAT3 | CS | I/O |
| 2 | CMD | DI | PP (push-pull) |
| 3 | VSS1 | VSS | S |
| 4 | VDD | VDD | S |
| 5 | CLK | SCLK | I |
| 6 | VSS2 | VSS2 | S |
| 7 | DAT0 | DO | I/O/PP |
| 8 | DAT1 | RSV | I/O/PP |
| 9 | DAT2 | RSV | I/O/PP |

microSD (8 pin), S12: 1 DAT2, 2 CD/DAT3, 3 CMD, 4 VDD, 5 CLK, 6 VSS, 7 DAT0, 8 DAT1. SPI mode for microSD follows the same function mapping as the SD table: pin 2 CS, pin 3 DI, pin 5 SCLK, pin 7 DO, pins 1 and 8 reserved (derived from S12 plus S16, not read as a single table).

Card supply and current (S16, Transcend SDXC datasheet Rev 1.0): supply 2.7 to 3.6 V (S15 states 2.7 to 3.3 V for standard SD cards: a source conflict in the upper limit); current before the first command 15 mA max; initialization and default mode 100 mA max; high-speed mode 200 mA max; other functions 500 mA max; all given as 1-second averages. Real peaks (write bursts, erase) are higher than the average and a 1 second average hides them; the opened sheet does not give an instantaneous peak. 1.8 V signaling for UHS-I cards is NOT in the opened documents; treat as RESEARCH_REQUIRED (the 3.3 V default is what the library models).

Pull-ups (S16): CMD and DAT lines need 10 to 100 kohm pull-ups on the bus to prevent floating; the card pin 1 (CD/DAT3) has an internal 10 to 90 kohm pull-up that is used for card detection. The SD simplified specification was not opened, so these values are from a card vendor's datasheet and not from the standard. In SPI mode DI and CS also need defined idle levels (pull-up on CS; confidence L).

Card-detect and write-protect switches are mechanical, floating contacts: they are not connected to the card. The socket's switch pads are separate terminals (the 3D spec does not model them: OHM-179 notes "detect/write-protect switch pads not modeled"; OHM-180 lists two shield/detect pads at +X with mirrored positions assumed). Typical use: host pull-up to VDD, switch to GND; a closed switch reads low. Bench B1 shows the numbers.

### 3. How it connects
Wire VDD to a 3.3 V rail (with 10 uF-class bulk close to the socket as general practice; value ASSUMPTION), VSS to GND, CLK, CMD and DAT0..3 to the host (SDIO) or CS/DI/DO/SCLK to an SPI port. Series 22 to 33 ohm resistors on CLK are common practice (ASSUMPTION L), ESD protection array on the lines. Mistakes: using the LDO that powers the MCU with 100 mA headroom only (a card write can pull 100 to 200 mA, S16, so the rail sags and the card or MCU resets, see bench B2), missing pull-ups on CMD/DAT (floating bus), leaving DAT1/DAT2 unterminated in 1-bit mode, treating card-detect as the DAT3 line and the mechanical switch interchangeably, SPI CS floating during power-up, and shorting card-detect to the wrong polarity. Also: card hot-plug into a rail with large bulk capacitance.

### 4. Electrical model for simulation
Layer: the socket body is L1. The SD card protocol is L3 (see the L3 requirement below). The card itself is modeled in L1 only as a supply load.

L1 model (socket):
```
* Contacts: R per pin (contact resistance)
R{ref}_k  Pk_board  Pk_card  {Rc}
* Card-detect: SPST normally open, closes on card insertion
.model SWCD_{ref} SW(Vt=0.5 Vh=0.1 Ron={Rsw} Roff=1G)
S{ref}_cd CD_A CD_B CARD_PRESENT 0 SWCD_{ref}
* Write-protect (full-size SD only): closes when the slider is in the lock position
S{ref}_wp WP_A WP_B WP_LOCK 0 SWCD_{ref}
```
Card-supply load (for rail analysis), see bench B2: `Bload vcc 0 I = {Iload}*min(1, v(vcc)/Vknee)` with Iload = 100 mA (default) or 200 mA (high-speed) and Vknee an ASSUMPTION of the load model.

Parameter mapping: Rc = 100 mohm max (S13, S14) or 40 mohm change (S12), default 50 mohm ASSUMPTION; Rsw = 100 mohm max (same contact resistance limit, applied to the switch: ASSUMPTION since the switch contact has no separate spec in the opened sheets); Iload from S16.

Valid analyses: op, dc, tran. Valid range: DC to a few tens of MHz for the SD clock path; the SD clock reaches 25 MHz default or 50 MHz high speed (general knowledge; UHS higher, none opened), where the contacts' inductance and trace matching matter and are not modeled.

Fidelity: `ideal_components` for contacts and switches; `behavioural_approximation` for the card current load.

L3 requirement: the SD protocol is not simulable in ngspice. A higher layer must supply (a) a card state machine: identification clock, CMD0/CMD8/ACMD41 initialization, command and response framing with CRC, block read/write, busy signalling on DAT0 (SD mode) or DO (SPI mode); (b) the voltage and speed negotiation, including the UHS 1.8 V switch if supported; (c) SPI vs SD bus mode selection by the CS level at the first command; (d) a card-present flag that drives the CARD_PRESENT node of the L1 switch. These requirements are written from general knowledge of the protocol and from S15 (which states that the command/response sequences are protocol-level); the SD simplified specification was not opened, so command numbers and init clock limits above are NOT verified in this research and are RESEARCH_REQUIRED.

Known limitations: no signal integrity, no card capacitance (typical input capacitance of the card pins is not in any opened document), no inrush model beyond the constant-current load, the socket's own hot-plug bounce not modeled, switch bounce not modeled.

### 6. Ratings and limits
- Per contact: `abs(i) <= 0.5 A` (S12, S13, S14).
- Switch: assume contact rating equal to the connector's 0.5 A, 100 V AC; the switch is for logic-level detect only (ASSUMPTION L, no separate switch rating was in the opened extracts).
- Card supply: `2.7 V <= Vcc <= 3.6 V` (S16); S15 gives 3.3 V as the upper bound for standard cards. Use 3.6 V as the error level, 3.3 V +5% as the warning. Check: `vcc_min >= 2.7`.
- Card current: `I_load <= I_regulator_limit` and `vcc_droop <= 3.3 - 2.7`; use 200 mA as the minimum recommended rail capability (100 mA default mode, 200 mA high speed, S16; 500 mA for "other functions") and flag a regulator with a smaller limit.
- Cycles: 10,000 typical.

### 7. Failure and misuse behavior
| id | trigger | effect | sim response | permanence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| weak regulator | card load 200 mA vs regulator limit 150 mA | rail collapses (bench B2: 1.125 V) or droops by I x Rout (3.2 V at 0.5 ohm and 200 mA); card resets and file corruption | flag SUPPLY_COLLAPSE when vcc < 2.7 V during a card current step | recoverable (data may be corrupt) |
| missing pull-ups | CMD/DAT floating | undefined bus states, no initialization | flag NO_PULLUP on CMD/DAT in SD mode | recoverable |
| overvoltage | Vcc > 3.6 V | card damage (not quantified in the opened sheets) | flag | permanent |
| reverse polarity | VDD/VSS swapped | card ESD structure conducts | flag | permanent |
| contact overcurrent | > 0.5 A | contact heating | flag | permanent |
| card removed hot | removal during write | file corruption (L3) | L3 requirement: abort transactions when CD goes open | recoverable |
| switch bounce | insertion bounce | CD glitches for ms | optional debounce note | recoverable |
| ESD | handling | card or host damage | flag: add TVS on the lines | permanent |

### 8. Thermal behavior
Contact heating is negligible (a 100 mohm contact at 100 mA dissipates 1 mW). Card self-heating is a function of the card, not the socket. No thermal model.

### 9. Appearance summary
OHM-179: flat steel box with an open +Y slot and a contact row at the rear. OHM-180: very thin steel box with an open +Y slot and a contact row. Neither has a polarity mark in the 3D spec; pin 1 is at the outer pad on the card side listed in the per-entry pin map.

### 10. Validation benches
| id | file | expected | tolerance | measured |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | bench/beh-con-sd/B1.cir | open: 3.3 x 1e9/(1e9+47k) = 3.29984 V; closed: 3.3 x 0.1/(47000.1) = 7.021 uV, 70.21 uA | 0.01% | 3.299845 V, 7.0213e-6 V, 70.213 uA: match |
| B2 | bench/beh-con-sd/B2.cir (and B2b.cir) | Ilim 500 mA, Rout 0.5 ohm, load 200 mA: V = 3.3 - 0.2 x 0.5 = 3.2 V. Ilim 150 mA (B2b): v = Ilim x 1.5 V / Iload = 1.125 V | 0.1% | 3.200000 V; 1.124999 V: match |

- S12: Hirose, "DM3 Series microSD Card Connectors" (hosted by Purdue ECE477 at the URL above, no date seen). Took: pins 1 DAT2, 2 CD/DAT3, 3 CMD, 4 VDD, 5 CLK, 6 VSS, 7 DAT0, 8 DAT1; 0.5 A; 125 V AC; 40 mohm change; 100 Mohm; 10,000 cycles for DM3AT/DM3B (5,000 for DM3C/DM3D); -25 to +85 degC; card detection switch normally open, closes on card insertion.

Took: 0.5 A, 100 VAC, 100 mohm max, more than 1000 Mohm, 10,000 cycles, -25 to 85 degC; CD: removed OPEN, inserted CLOSE; WP: protect CLOSE, enable OPEN; 9 pins. The extract names neither the pins of the switches nor the pin table.
- S14: Molex memory card sockets 987652-0671. Took: 0.5 A max, 500 V AC, 100 mohm max, 500 to 10,000 cycles, -40 to 85 degC, card detect available on most models; no pin table, no WP info.
- S15: Cactus Technologies white paper. Took: SD mode pin 1 DAT3/CS, 2 CMD/DI, 3 Vss1, 4 Vcc, 5 CLK, 6 Vss2, 7 DAT0/DO, 8 DAT1, 9 DAT2; supply 2.7 to 3.3 V; refers readers to the SD Association simplified specification for electrical details.

- Not opened: SD Association Physical Layer Simplified Specification (terms page only), Kyocera/Attend/Amphenol/Molex 67600 or 104031 drawings, any card-detect pad pin map, UHS-I 1.8 V timing.

# PER-ENTRY SECTIONS

## [OHM-172] DC Barrel Jack -> BEH-CON-DCJACK
- Package: PKG-DC_JACK, member PJ-102A-like (CUI). Default 2.1 mm center pin / 5.5 mm barrel, right-angle THT; variant 2.5 mm center pin (parameter center_pin_dia). The opened S2 gives the jack's center pin as 2.0 mm copper (the library's `center_pin_dia` default 2.0 matches it; the 2.5 mm variant is a library parameter and was not found in an opened document).
- Pin map (3D spec): P1 center pin (TIP), P2 sleeve, P3 switch. KiCad PJ-102AH coordinates: P1 (0,0), P2 (0,6.0), P3 (4.7,3.0).
- Ratings: 24 Vdc / 2.5 A / 30 mohm (S1); conflict 16 Vdc (S2).
- Polarity: NONE on the part. Do not assume center positive; the schematic net names decide.
- Defaults: Rc_total 30 mohm, switch partner TIP (placeholder), thermal Rth 160 K/W calibrated (ASSUMPTION).
- Notes: sleeve-switch versus tip-switch variants exist; flag in UI that the switch pairing is unverified.
- Status: partial.

## [OHM-173] XT30 PCB Connector -> BEH-CON-XT
- Package PKG-XT, member XT30PW-M (Amass), right-angle male THT. Pitch 5.0.
- Pin map: pin 1 at -X (OHMNI), pin 2 at +X; the KiCad footprint numbers the square pad (pad 1) at +X (mirror delta: map by pad name). Polarity (+ / -) RESEARCH_REQUIRED.
- Ratings: 15 A continuous, 30 A peak, 0.80 mohm, 500 V DC, -20 to 120 degC, 1000 cycles (S4).
- Thermal defaults: Rth 167 K/W, Cth 1 J/K, alpha 0.0039 (ASSUMPTION); P at rated = 0.18 W, drop 12 mV.
- Hazard note: battery pack short-circuit current can exceed the 30 A peak by orders of magnitude; a fuse or current limit is required.
- Status: partial.

## [OHM-174] XT60 PCB Connector -> BEH-CON-XT
- Package PKG-XT, member XT60PW-M (Amass). Pitch 7.2.
- Pin map: pin 1 at -X, pin 2 at +X (3D spec: (-3.6,0), (+3.6,0)). Polarity RESEARCH_REQUIRED. 3D spec also leaves the tail assignment (0.6 x 1.7 slot versus dia 2.7 hole) unresolved.
- Ratings: 30 A continuous, 60 A peak, 0.55 mohm, DC 500 V, -20 to 120 degC, 1000 cycles, 12 AWG (S3). Mated pair P at rated = 0.495 W, drop 16.5 mV.
- Thermal defaults: Rth 60.6 K/W, Cth 2 J/K, alpha 0.0039 (ASSUMPTION).

## [OHM-175] U.FL/I-PEX RF Connector -> BEH-CON-RF
- Package PKG-UFL, member U.FL-R-SMT-1 (Hirose). SMD receptacle.
- Pin map (3D spec): SIG (-1.05, 0) 1.05 x 1.0; GND1 (+0.475, +1.475) and GND2 (+0.475, -1.475) 2.2 x 1.05. Electrical: SIG is the center contact, GND1 and GND2 tied to the shell. No polarity.
- Ratings: 50 ohm; DC to 6 GHz; VSWR 1.3 max to 3 GHz, 1.3 to 1.5 from 3 to 6 GHz; 30 cycles; 100 V DC; 10 mA max; contact resistance center 20 mohm, outer 10 mohm max (S5).
- Defaults: Cpad 0, Lpin 0 (ideal); realistic mode tunes parasitics to |Gamma| of 0.2 at 6 GHz (derived from VSWR 1.5). Insertion loss RESEARCH_REQUIRED.
- Notes: mated height 1.9 mm or 2.4 mm depends on cable (S5); the library uses 3.0 x 2.6 body.

## [OHM-176] Vertical SMA Connector -> BEH-CON-RF
- Package PKG-SMA_RF, member Cinch 142-0701-201 / Amphenol 132134 aliases. Vertical THT jack (female).
- Pin map: center signal pin at (0,0) (hole 1.5); four ground legs at (+-2.54, +-2.54) (hole 1.7). Electrical: SIG = center, GND = four legs tied.
- Ratings: 50 ohm; DC to 18 GHz; 500 cycles; VSWR 1.15 max is from the SMA panel-mount family (S6), so apply with confidence L; BeCu gold center, PTFE (S7).

## [OHM-177] Edge-Launch SMA Connector -> BEH-CON-RF
- Package PKG-SMA_EDGE, member Molex 73251 series (EWR-2074 drawing). Mounting smd_edge.
- Pin map: SIG center pad 1.78 x 4.19 on top; two ground pads top and bottom at (+-3.4925, ...); small ground tabs and via-style ground pads. Terminal order per 3D spec: SIG then 4 grounds (2 top legs, 2 bottom legs). All grounds tied. No polarity.
- Ratings: 50 ohm; 18 GHz; 500 Vrms at sea level (S8); VSWR not published in the opened Molex page; torque 7 to 10 in-lb for SMA, board mount 12 in-oz (S9).
- Notes: board thickness slot 1.57 mm (2.13 mm on another Molex part); launch impedance depends on that thickness. Use the step model (bench B3) for launch sensitivity. The 3D spec leaves the barrel axis height RESEARCH_REQUIRED.
- Status: partial.

## [OHM-178] FFC/FPC ZIF Connector -> BEH-CON-FFC
- Package PKG-FFC_ZIF, parametric by N; default FH12-10S-0.5SH-like, bottom contact, flip-lock, pitch 0.5.
- Pin map: pad k (k = 1..N) at x = -A/2 + 0.5 (k-1), y = +1.85, pad 0.3 x 1.3; pin 1 at -X. Two retaining-tab pads 1.8 x 2.2 (mechanical; may be tied to GND at the schematic level, not a datasheet requirement).
- Ratings: 0.5 A per contact (70% = 0.35 A when all loaded), 50 V AC, 50 mohm max, 20 cycles, -40 to +85 degC (S11).
- Defaults: N = 10, Rc 50 mohm worst.
- Notes: Top versus bottom contact is a mechanical property that flips cable orientation; FPC thickness 0.3 mm.
- Status: partial.

## [OHM-179] SD Card Socket -> BEH-CON-SDSOCKET
- Package PKG-SD_SOCKET, Molex 67600-8001 default (the 3D spec notes that Molex 5031821852 is a microSD part). Push-push SMD.
- Pin map (3D spec numbering, X = -7.065, -4.565, -1.265, +0.435, +2.935, +5.435, +7.865, +9.565, -9.565): pad 1 DAT3/CS, 2 CMD/DI, 3 VSS1, 4 VDD, 5 CLK/SCLK, 6 VSS2, 7 DAT0/DO, 8 DAT1, 9 DAT2 (S15, S16). The 3D spec says pad 9 is the outer pad on the -X side and the pad positions are an exemplar from a Kyocera footprint (confidence L). Detect and write-protect switch pads are NOT modeled in the 3D spec (RESEARCH_REQUIRED); the electrical model carries CD_A, CD_B, WP_A, WP_B as extra terminals so the schematic is complete.
- Switch behavior: CD open when no card, closes on insertion (S13); WP closes when write-protect is set (S13). A host pull-up to VDD with the switch to GND reads high with no card and low with a card (bench B1).
- Defaults: Rc 50 mohm, 0.5 A per contact, 10,000 cycles, supply 3.3 V, card current 100 mA (200 mA high speed).
- Layers: socket L1; protocol L3.
- Status: partial.

## [OHM-180] MicroSD Card Socket -> BEH-CON-SDSOCKET
- Package PKG-MICROSD_SOCKET, Molex 104031-0811 default (alternates 503398-1892, 503182-1852, 47352, DM3AT). Push-pull SMD.
- Pin map (3D spec: 8 contacts at pitch 1.10, pin 1 at +X, pad 8 narrower): pad 1 DAT2, 2 CD/DAT3 (SPI: CS), 3 CMD (SPI: DI), 4 VDD, 5 CLK (SPI: SCLK), 6 VSS, 7 DAT0 (SPI: DO), 8 DAT1 (S12). Shield/detect pads 1.2 x 1.0 at (+5.74, +1.25) and (+5.74, +4.95); mirrored positions at -X assumed (L). Which of the two pads pairs with the card-detect switch is RESEARCH_REQUIRED.
- Switch: card-detect only, normally open, closes on card insertion (S12). No write-protect switch.
- Ratings: 0.5 A, 125 V AC, 40 mohm change, 100 Mohm, 10,000 cycles for DM3AT (S12).
- Defaults: Rc 50 mohm, supply 3.3 V, card 100 mA default mode.
- Layers: socket L1; protocol L3.
- Status: partial.
